...of the sacrifice. And they shall offer

### And he shall slaughter the calf before the Lord. And the sons of Aaron the priests shall offer its blood, pouring it around the altar that is before the door of the tabernacle. And having stripped the hide of the victim, they shall cut the limbs into joints; and they shall put fire on the altar, piling a heap of wood above. And they shall place the limbs that were cut above, specifically the head and all things that cling to the liver. Once the intestines and feet are washed with water, the priest shall burn them upon the altar as a burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total dedication</note> and a sweet aroma to the Lord. If his offering is from the flocks—either from the sheep or from the goats—for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without blemish. And he shall slaughter it at the side of the altar that looks toward the north, before the Lord. The sons of Aaron shall pour its blood upon the altar all around. And they shall divide the limbs, the head, and all that clings to the liver, and place them upon the wood where the fire is to be laid on the altar. But the intestines and the feet they shall wash with water. And the priest shall burn all that is offered upon the altar as a burnt offering and a most sweet aroma to the Lord. If the burnt offering to the Lord is of birds—namely of turtledoves or young pigeons—the priest shall offer them at the altar. And with the head twisted back to the neck and the place of the wound broken, he shall make the blood run down upon the edges of the altar. But the crop of the throat and the feathers he shall cast near the altar toward the east, in the place where the ashes are usually thrown. And he shall break its wings, but not cut them, nor divide it with an iron blade; and he shall burn it upon the altar, with wood placed under the fire. It is a burnt offering and an oblation of most sweet aroma to the Lord. When a soul <note>original: "Anima"; here used to mean a person or individual</note> offers an offering of sacrifice to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense, and bring it to the sons of Aaron the priests. One of them, taking a handful of the flour and oil and all the frankincense, shall place it as a memorial upon the altar for a most sweet aroma to the Lord. But what remains of the sacrifice shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is the Most Holy of the offerings of the Lord. Moreover, when he offers a sacrifice baked in an oven of fine flour—namely, loaves without leaven mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil—if your offering is from a frying pan, of fine flour mixed with oil and without leaven, you shall divide it into tiny parts and pour oil over it. But if the sacrifice is from a griddle, the flour shall likewise be mixed with oil. Offering this to the Lord, you shall deliver it into the hands of the priest. When he has offered it, he shall take a memorial from the sacrifice and burn it upon the altar for an aroma of sweetness to the Lord. But whatever is left shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is the Most Holy of the offerings of the Lord. Every offering that is offered to the Lord shall be made without leaven, nor shall any leaven or honey be burned in the sacrifice of the Lord. You shall offer only their firstfruits and gifts, but they shall not be placed upon the altar for an aroma of sweetness. Whatever sacrifice you offer, you shall season with salt. Nor shall you take away the salt of the covenant of your God from your sacrifice. In every offering of yours, you shall offer salt. But if you offer gifts of the firstfruits of your crops to the Lord—ears of grain still green, toasted with fire and broken in the manner of meal—you shall thus offer your firstfruits, pouring oil upon them and putting on frankincense, because it is an offering of the Lord. From which the priest shall burn, in memory of the gift, a part of the broken meal and the oil, and all the frankincense. If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings <note>original: "hostia pacificorum"; a voluntary sacrifice to signify fellowship or gratitude</note>, and he wishes to offer from the cattle—whether male or female—he shall offer them immaculate before the Lord. And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his victim, which shall be slaughtered at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony. And the sons of Aaron the priests shall pour the blood around the altar. And they shall offer from the victim of peace offerings as an oblation to the Lord: the fat that covers the vitals and whatever fat is within. The two kidneys with the fat by which the flanks are covered, and the caul of the liver with the kidneys. And the sons of Aaron shall burn them upon the altar as a burnt offering, with wood placed under the fire for a most sweet aroma to the Lord. If his offering for a peace sacrifice is from the sheep—whether male or female—he shall offer them immaculate. If he offers a lamb before the Lord, he shall lay his hand upon its head and slaughter it in the vestibule of the tabernacle of testimony. And the sons of Aaron shall pour the blood around the altar. And they shall offer from the peace victim a sacrifice to the Lord: the fat and the whole tail, and he shall take it with the fat of the kidneys that covers the vitals, and both kidneys with the fat that is near the flanks, and the caul of the liver with the kidneys. And the priest shall burn it upon the altar as food for the fire and an offering of the Lord. If a goat is his offering and he offers it to the Lord, he shall lay his hand upon its head and slaughter it at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony. And the sons of Aaron shall pour the blood around the altar. And they shall take away all the fat that covers the vitals, and the two kidneys with the fat that is above the flanks, and the caul of the liver with the kidneys, as was said above. And the priest shall burn them upon the altar as food for the fire and a most sweet aroma. All the fat shall belong to the Lord, by a perpetual law throughout your generations and in all your dwellings. You shall eat absolutely no fat nor blood. ### If a soul sins through ignorance and does one of all the commands of the Lord which ought not to be done: if the priest who is anointed sins, making the people to offend, he shall offer for his sin an immaculate calf to the Lord. And he shall bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord, and he shall lay his hand upon its head, and slaughter it to the Lord. He shall also take some of the blood of the calf and carry it into the tabernacle of testimony. And having dipped his finger in the blood, he shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord against the veil of the sanctuary. And he shall put some of the same blood upon the horns of the altar of most pleasing incense to the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of testimony. But all the remaining blood he shall pour at the base of the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the tabernacle. And he shall take away the fat of the calf for the sin: both that which covers the vitals and all things that are within. The two kidneys, and the caul of the liver with the kidneys, and the fat that is near the flanks, just as it is taken from the calf of the victim of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn them upon the altar of burnt offerings. But the skin and all the meat, with the head and feet and intestines and dung, and the rest of the body, he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are usually poured out; and he shall burn them upon a pile of wood, which shall be consumed in the place of the ashes. But if the whole assembly of Israel is ignorant and through imprudence does what is against the command of the Lord, and afterward understands its sin, it shall offer a calf for the sin, and they shall bring it to the door of the tabernacle. And the elders of the people shall lay their hands upon its head before the Lord. Once the calf is slaughtered in the sight of the Lord, the priest who is anointed shall carry some of its blood into the tabernacle of testimony. With his finger dipped, he shall sprinkle it seven times against the veil. And he shall put some of the same blood on the horns of the altar that is before the Lord in the tabernacle of testimony; but the rest of the blood he shall pour near the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which is at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony. And he shall take all its fat and burn it upon the altar. So he shall do with this calf as he did before; and the priest praying for them, the Lord will be merciful. He shall carry the calf itself outside the camp and burn it, just as the former calf, because it is for the sin of the multitude. If a leader <note>original: "princeps"; a tribal chief or ruler</note> sins and does one of many things through ignorance which is forbidden by the law of the Lord, and afterward understands his sin, he shall offer as a victim to the Lord a female goat from the flocks, without blemish. And he shall lay his hand upon its head. When he has slaughtered it in the place where the victim of the burnt offering is usually slain before the Lord, because it is for sin, the priest shall dip his finger in the blood of the victim for sin and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and the rest he shall pour at its base. But the fat he shall burn above, just as is usually done in the peace victims. And the priest shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him. But if a soul from the people of the land sins through ignorance, so as to do any of those things which are forbidden by the law of the Lord, and recognizes his sin, he shall offer an immaculate female goat. He shall lay his hand upon the head of the victim and slaughter it in the place of the burnt offering. And the priest shall take some of the blood on his finger and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and the rest he shall pour at its base. But all the fat he shall take away, as it is usually taken away from the peace victims, and he shall burn it upon the altar for an aroma of sweetness to the Lord. And the priest shall pray for him, and it shall be forgiven him. But if he offers a victim for sin from the sheep, an immaculate ewe, he shall lay his hand upon its head and slaughter it in the place where the victims of burnt offerings are usually slain. And the priest shall dip some of its blood with his finger and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering; the rest he shall pour at its base. All the fat also he shall take away, as the fat of the ram that is slaughtered for peace offerings is usually taken away, and he shall burn it upon the altar as an incense of the Lord. And the priest shall pray for her and for her sin, and it shall be forgiven her. If a soul sins and hears the voice of one swearing, and is a witness because he either saw it himself or is aware of it; unless he indicates it, he shall bear his iniquity. A soul that touches anything unclean—whether what was killed by a beast, or what died of itself, or any other reptile—and has forgotten its uncleanness, is guilty and has offended. And if he touches anything of the uncleanness of a man according to all the impurity by which one is usually polluted, and has forgotten it, and afterward recognizes it, he shall be subject to the offense. A soul that swears and utters with its lips, whether to do evil or to do good, and confirms that very thing with an oath and speech, and has forgotten it, and afterward understands his offense, let him do penance for the sin and offer from the flocks a lamb or a goat; and the priest shall pray for her and for her sin. But if he is not able to offer a beast, let him offer two turtledoves or two

<column-break/>

young pigeons to the Lord: one for sin, and the other for a burnt offering. And he shall give them to the priest. He, offering the first for sin, shall twist back its head to the wings, so that it clings to the neck and is not entirely broken off. And he shall sprinkle some of its blood on the wall of the altar. But whatever is left over, he shall make to drip at its foundation, because it is for sin. But the other he shall burn as a burnt offering, as is usually done. And the priest shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him. If his hand does not find enough to offer two turtledoves or 

two young pigeons, he shall offer for his sin the tenth part of an ephah <note>An ephah is an ancient dry measure, roughly equal to 22 liters or a large bucket.</note> of fine flour. He shall not put oil into it, nor frankincense, because it is for sin. When he has delivered it to the priest, he shall take a handful from it and burn it upon the altar as a monument to him who offered it; praying for him, and having made atonement, he shall have the rest as a gift. If a soul sins against the ceremonies through error in those things which are sanctified to the Lord, he shall offer for his offense an immaculate ram from the flocks, which can be bought for two shekels <note>A shekel was a standard weight for silver, roughly 11 grams.</note> according to the weight of the sanctuary. Also, the damage which he caused, he shall restore, and put a fifth part above it, delivering it to the priest, who shall pray for him, offering the ram, and it shall be forgiven him. If a soul sins through ignorance and does one of these things which are forbidden by the law of the Lord, and being guilty of the sin understands his iniquity, he shall offer an immaculate ram from the flocks to the priest, according to the measure and estimation of the sin. The priest shall pray for what he did unknowingly, and it shall be forgiven him, because he erred through ignorance against the Lord. A soul that sins and, despising the Lord, denies a deposit to his neighbor which had been committed to his trust, or extorts anything, or commits a slander, or finds a lost thing and, denying it, furthermore swears falsely, or does any other of many things in which men are accustomed to sin; being convicted of the offense, he shall restore all things which he wished to obtain through fraud, in full, and a fifth part besides to the lord to whom he brought the damage. On the day of his sin, he shall offer to the Lord for his offense an immaculate ram from the flock, according to the estimation and measure of the offense, and shall deliver it to the priest, who shall pray for him before the Lord. And it shall be forgiven him for each of the things he sinned in doing.

### And the Lord spoke 
to Moses, saying: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering. It shall be burned on the altar all nights until morning; the fire shall be from the same altar. The priest shall be clothed in a tunic and linen breeches. And he shall take the ashes which the devouring fire burned up and, placing them near the altar, he shall be stripped of his former clothes; and being clothed in others, he shall carry them outside the camp to a most clean place and make them be consumed to a spark. Therefore, the fire shall always burn on the altar, which the priest shall nourish, putting wood under it every morning; and having placed the burnt offering above, he shall burn the fat of the peace offerings. This is the perpetual fire which shall never fail on the altar. This is the law of the sacrifice and of the libations <note>original: "libaminum"; liquid offerings, though here used in context of grain offerings</note> which the sons of Aaron shall offer before the Lord and before the altar. The priest shall take a handful of the fine flour which is mixed with oil, and all the frankincense that is placed upon the flour; and he shall burn it as a memorial for a most sweet aroma to the Lord. But the remaining part Aaron shall eat with his sons, without leaven; and he shall eat it in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle. For this reason it shall not be leavened, because a part of it is offered as the Lord's incense. It shall be the Most Holy, just as for sin and for offense. Only the males of the lineage of Aaron shall eat it. It is a legitimate and eternal law in your generations concerning the sacrifices of the Lord. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they ought to offer to the Lord on the day of their anointing. They shall offer the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour as a perpetual sacrifice: half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening. Which, being prepared with oil in a frying pan, shall be fried. But the priest who succeeds his father by right shall offer it hot for a most sweet aroma to the Lord. And it shall be entirely burned on the altar. For every offering of the priests shall be consumed by fire, nor shall anyone eat of it.

<margin>9.</margin>
### The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and
his sons. This is the law of the victim for sin. In the place where the burnt offering is offered, it shall be slaughtered before the Lord. It is the Most Holy. The priest who offers it shall eat it in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle. Whatever touches its meat shall be sanctified. If a garment is splashed with its blood, it shall be washed in the holy place. An earthen vessel in which it was cooked shall be broken. If it was a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and washed with water. Every male of the priestly race shall eat of its meat, because it is the Most Holy. For the victim that is cooked for sin, whose blood is carried into the tabernacle of testimony in the most clean place, shall not be eaten, but shall be burned with fire.

<margin>10.</margin>
### The Lord spoke to
Moses, saying: This also is the law of the victim for an offense; it is the Most Holy. Therefore, where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the victim for the offense shall also be slain. Its blood he shall pour around the altar. They shall offer for it the fat: the tail and the fat that covers the vitals; the two kidneys and the fat that is near the flanks; the caul of the liver with the kidneys. And the priest shall burn them upon the altar. It is the incense of the Lord for the offense. Every male of the priestly race shall eat of this meat in the holy place, because it is the Most Holy. As a victim is offered for sin, so also for an offense. There shall be one law for both; it shall belong to the priest who offered it. The priest who offers the victim of the burnt offering shall have its skin. And every sacrifice of fine flour that is baked in an oven, and whatever is prepared in a frying pan or on a griddle, shall be that priest's by whom it is offered. Whether the offering is mixed with oil or is dry, it shall be divided by equal measure among all the sons of Aaron. This is the law of the victim of peace offerings which is offered to the Lord. If the offering is for thanksgiving, they shall offer loaves without leaven mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and cooked fine flour, and rolls mixed with an addition of oil. Also, leavened bread with the victim of thanks which is slaughtered for peace offerings. From which one shall be offered to the Lord for the firstfruits, and it shall be the priest's who pours the blood of the victim. Its meat shall be eaten on the same day, nor shall anything of it remain until morning. If someone offers a victim by a vow or spontaneously, it shall likewise be eaten on the same day; but also if anything remains until the morrow, it is permitted to eat it. But whatever the third day finds, fire shall consume. If anyone eats of the meat of the victim of peace offerings on the third day, the offering shall become void; nor shall it benefit the one offering. Rather, whatever soul contaminates itself with such food shall be guilty of transgression. Meat that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten, but shall be burned with fire. He who is clean shall eat of it. A polluted soul that eats of the meat of the victim of peace offerings which was offered to the Lord shall perish from its people. And whoever touches the uncleanness of a man, or of a beast, or of any thing that can pollute, and eats of meat of this kind, shall perish from his people.

### The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel.
You shall not eat the fat of an ox, or a sheep, or a goat. The fat of a carcass that died of itself, and of that animal which was caught by a beast, you shall have for various uses. Just as the fat is offered for the incense of the Lord, whoever wishes to eat of it shall perish from his people. You shall not eat the blood of any animal in all your dwellings, whether of birds or of beasts. Every soul that eats blood shall perish from its people. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel: He who offers a victim of peace offerings to the Lord, let him offer at the same time a sacrifice, that is, its libations. He shall hold in his hands the fat of the victim and the small breasts. And when he has consecrated both as offerings to the Lord, he shall deliver the fat upon the altar; but the small breast shall fall to the use of Aaron and his sons. The right shoulder also from the peace victims shall fall to the firstfruits of the priest. He of the sons of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat shall have the right shoulder as his portion. For I have taken the breast of elevation and the shoulder of separation from the sons of Israel from their peace victims, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons by a perpetual law from all the people of Israel.

<margin>vii</margin>
This is the portion of the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the ceremonies of the Lord on the day when Moses offered them to perform the office of the priesthood: and what the Lord commanded to be given to the children of Israel by a perpetual ordinance throughout their generations. This is the law of the burnt offering <note>original: "holocausti"</note> and of the sacrifice for sin and for trespass, and for the consecration, and for the peace offerings <note>original: "pacificorum"</note> which the Lord appointed to Moses on Mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their oblations to the Lord in the desert of Sinai.

<margin>viii</margin>
He also brought Aaron and his sons. And when he had washed them, he clothed the high priest with the hyacinth-colored <note>likely referring to a deep blue or violet dye</note> tunic and girded him with the belt, and clothed him with the white tunic. Then, having placed the ephod <note>original: "superhumerali"; a vest-like garment worn by the high priest</note> over it, he girded him with the sash. And he fitted to him the breastplate <note>original: "rationale"</note> in which were "Doctrine and Truth" <note>Latin: "doctrina & veritas"; these represent the Urim and Thummim, sacred lots used to discern the divine will</note>. He also covered his head with a miter; and upon the miter, over against his forehead, he placed the golden plate, consecrated in sanctification, just as the Lord had commanded him. He also took the oil of unction, with which he anointed the tabernacle with all its furniture. And when he had sprinkled the altar seven times, he anointed it and all its vessels; and the basin with its base he sanctified with the oil. Pouring it upon Aaron's head, he anointed and consecrated him. He also clothed Aaron's sons, who were presented, in linen tunics, and girded them with belts, and placed turbans on them as the Lord had commanded. And when Aaron and his sons had laid their hands upon the head of the victim, he sacrificed it, drawing the blood; and dipping his finger, he touched the horns of the altar round about. Once it was expiated and sanctified, he poured the remaining blood at its base. He burned the fat that was upon the vital organs, and the membrane of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, upon the altar anointed with oil. But the meat and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded.

He also brought the burnt offering and placed it upon the altar anointed with oil. Drawing its blood, he poured it round about the altar. And cutting the ram itself into pieces, he burned its head, and limbs, and fat with fire, having first washed the intestines and the feet; and he burned the whole ram together upon the altar, because it was a burnt offering of most sweet aroma to the Lord, just as He had commanded him. He also offered the second ram for the consecration of the priests, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon its head. When he had sacrificed it, Moses, taking some of its blood, touched the tip of Aaron’s right ear and the thumb of his right hand, and likewise of his foot. He also presented Aaron's sons. And when he had touched the tip of each of their right ears and the thumbs of their right hands and right feet with the blood of the sacrifice, he poured the rest upon the altar round about. But the fat, and the tail, and all the grease that covers the intestines, and the membrane of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fats, and the right shoulder, he set apart. Taking from the basket of unleavened bread that was before the Lord one loaf without leaven and a cake tempered with oil and a wafer, he placed them upon the fats and the right shoulder, delivering them all together to Aaron and his sons. After they had lifted them up before the Lord, Moses received them back from their hands and burned them upon the altar of the burnt offering, because it was an offering of consecration for a sweet-smelling aroma to the Lord. And he took the breast, elevating it before the Lord from the ram of consecration as his own portion, as the Lord had commanded. And taking the ointment and the blood that was on the altar, he sprinkled it upon Aaron and his garments, and upon his sons and their garments. And when he had sanctified them in their vestments, he commanded them, saying: "Boil the meat before the doors of the tabernacle and eat it there. Also eat the loaves of consecration in the basket, as the Lord commanded me, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them. But whatever remains of the meat and the loaves, the fire shall consume. You shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle for seven days, until the day that the time of your consecration is fulfilled. For in seven days the consecration is finished, as has been done this day, so that the rite of the sacrifice might be completed. Day and night you shall remain in the tabernacle, keeping the watches of the Lord, lest you die. For so it has been commanded to me."

<margin>ix</margin>
And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel, and he said to Aaron: "Take from the herd a calf for sin and a ram for a burnt offering, both without blemish, and offer them before the Lord. And you shall speak to the children of Israel: Take a he-goat for sin, and a calf and a lamb of a year old and without blemish for a burnt offering; an ox and a ram for peace offerings, and sacrifice them before the Lord in the sacrifices of each one, offering fine flour tempered with oil; for today the Lord will appear to you." Therefore, they brought all things that Moses had commanded to the door of the tabernacle. When the whole multitude stood there, Moses said: "This is the word which the Lord has commanded; do it, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you." And he said to Aaron: "Approach the altar and sacrifice for your sin; offer the burnt offering and pray for yourself and for the people." And when he had slain the victim of the people, he prayed for their salvation as the Lord had commanded. And the sons of Aaron approached and offered him the blood, in which dipping his finger, he touched the horns of the altar and poured the remainder at its base. The fat and the kidneys and the membrane of the liver which are for sin, he burned upon the altar as the Lord had commanded Moses. But the meat and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp. He also sacrificed the burnt offering; and his sons offered him its blood, which he poured around the altar. They also offered the victim itself cut into pieces, with the head and each limb. All these he burned upon the altar, having first washed the intestines and the feet with water. And offering for the sin of the people, he slew the he-goat for sin, making the altar a burnt offering and adding in the sacrifice the libations <note>drink offerings</note> which are likewise offered, and burning them upon the altar without the ceremonies of the morning burnt offering. He also sacrificed the ox and the ram, the peace offerings for the people. And his sons offered him the blood, which he poured upon the altar round about. But the fat of the ox and the tail of the ram and the kidneys with their fats and the membrane of the liver they placed upon the breasts. And when the fats were burned on the altar, Aaron set apart the breasts and the right shoulder, elevating them before the Lord, as Moses had commanded. And stretching out his hand to the people, he blessed them. And thus, having completed the victims for sin and the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he descended. And Moses and Aaron entered the tabernacle of the testimony, and afterwards coming out, they blessed the people.

And the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole multitude. And behold, a fire coming out from the Lord devoured the burnt offering and the fats that were upon the altar. When the crowds saw this, they praised the Lord, falling on their faces.

<margin>x</margin>
And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, taking their censers, put fire and incense in them, offering before the Lord "strange fire" <note>unauthorized or profane fire not taken from the sacred altar</note>, which was not commanded of them. And fire coming out from the Lord devoured them, and they died before the Lord. And Moses said to Aaron: "This is what the Lord spoke: I will be sanctified in those who approach me, and in the sight of all the people I will be glorified." Hearing this, Aaron remained silent. And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said to them:

<column-break/>

"Go and carry your brothers from the sight of the sanctuary, and bear them outside the camp." And going immediately, they took them as they lay, clothed in linen tunics, as had been commanded them. And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying: "Wine and everything that can make one drunk, you and your sons shall not drink when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony, lest you die; for it is a perpetual commandment throughout your generations. This is so that you may have the knowledge to discern between the holy and the profane, between the polluted and the clean, and that you may teach the children of Israel all my laws which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand of Moses."

And Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons who remained: "Take the sacrifice that remained of the oblation of the Lord, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is the Holy of Holies. And you shall eat it in a holy place, which is given to you and your sons of the offerings of the Lord, as he commanded me. The breast also which was offered, and the shoulder which was set apart, you shall eat in a most clean place: you, and your sons, and your daughters with you. For they are reserved for you and your children from the saving victims of the children of Israel. Because they elevated the shoulder and the breast and the fats to be burned on the altar before the Lord, and they belonged to him and his sons by a perpetual law, as the Lord commanded." Meanwhile, when Moses sought the he-goat that had been offered for sin, he found it had been burned up. Being angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who remained, he said: "Why did you not eat the victim for sin in the holy place, which is the Holy of Holies, and was given to you that you might bear the iniquity of the multitude and pray for it in the sight of the Lord? Especially since its blood was not carried into the sanctuary; you ought to have eaten it in the holy place as was commanded me." Aaron answered: "Behold, today the sacrifice for sin and the burnt offering have been offered before the Lord; but what you see has happened to me. How could I eat it or please the Lord in ceremonies with a mourning mind?" When Moses heard this, he was satisfied with the explanation.

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

<margin>xi</margin>
This is the food which you shall eat of all the living things of the earth. Everything that has a divided hoof and chews the cud among the cattle, you shall eat. But that which chews the cud and has a hoof but does not divide it, like the camel, you shall not eat it; and you shall count it among the unclean. The rock hyrax <note>original: "chero grillus"; a small, herbivorous mammal</note> which chews the cud but does not divide the hoof, is unclean. The hare also chews the cud, but does not divide the hoof. The pig also, though it divides the hoof, does not chew the cud. Of their meat you shall not eat, nor shall you touch their carcasses, because they are unclean to you. These are the things that are produced in the waters and which it is lawful to eat. Everything that has fins and scales, as well in the sea as in the rivers and pools, you shall eat. But whatever has not fins and scales, of those things that move and live in the waters, shall be an abomination and execrable to you. You shall not eat their meat, and you shall avoid their carcasses. All things that have not fins and scales in the waters shall be polluted. Of birds, these are the ones which you shall not eat and are to be avoided by you: The eagle, and the griffon-vulture <note>original: "gripem"</note>, and the osprey. The kite and the vulture according to its kind. And every kind of raven in its likeness. The ostrich, and the night-owl, and the seagull, and the hawk according to its kind. The eagle-owl, and the cormorant <note>original: "mergulum"</note>, and the ibis. And the swan, and the pelican <note>original: "onocrotalum"</note>, and the purple waterhen <note>original: "porfirionem"</note>. The heron and the plover according to its kind, the hoopoe also, and the bat. Everything among winged insects that goes upon four feet shall be an abomination to you. But whatever goes upon four feet, and has longer legs behind by which it hops upon the earth, you shall eat: such as the cricket <note>original: "bruchus"</note> in its kind, and the bald locust <note>original: "attacus"</note>, and the beetle <note>original: "ophiomachus"</note>, and the locust, each according to its kind. Whatever other winged insect has only four feet shall be execrable to you. And whoever touches their carcasses shall be polluted and shall be unclean until evening. And if it be necessary that he carry any of their dead, he shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the sun sets. Every animal that has a hoof but does not divide it, nor chews the cud, shall be unclean; and whoever touches it shall be contaminated. That which walks upon its paws among all the animals that go on four legs shall be unclean. He who touches their carcasses shall be polluted until evening. And he who carries such carcasses shall wash his clothes and be clean, for all these things are unclean to you. These also shall be counted polluted among the things that move upon the earth: the weasel, and the mouse, and the crocodile, each according to its kind. The shrew <note>original: "mygale"</note>, and the chameleon, and the gecko <note>original: "stellio"</note>, and the lizard, and the mole. All these are unclean. He who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening. And that upon which any of their carcasses falls shall be polluted: whether it be a wooden vessel or a garment, or skins or hair-cloth; and in whatever work it is used, it shall be dipped in water, and it shall be polluted until evening, and so afterwards it shall be cleansed. But the earthen vessel into which any of these falls shall be polluted and must be broken. Every food which you eat, if water be poured upon it, shall be unclean; and every liquid that is drunk from any vessel that is unclean, whatever of such carcasses falls upon it shall be unclean, whether ovens or pots, they shall be destroyed and be unclean. Furthermore, every collection of waters shall be clean, but he who touches their carcass shall be polluted. If it falls upon seed, it shall not pollute it. But if any man pours water upon the seed, and afterwards it be touched by the carcasses, it shall be immediately polluted. If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies, he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening. And he who eats of it anything, or carries it, shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. Everything that creeps upon the earth shall be an abomination to you; it shall not be taken for food. Whatever goes upon its breast on four feet and has many feet, or is dragged on the ground, you shall not eat, because it is an abomination. Do not contaminate your souls nor touch any of them, lest you be unclean. For I am the Lord your God. Be holy because I am a fountain <note>likely a poetic reference to God as the source of holiness; often translated as "I am holy"</note>. Do not pollute your souls with any creeping thing that moves upon the earth. For I am the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God. You shall be holy, because I also am holy. This is the law of animals and birds and of every living soul that moves in the water and creeps on the earth, that you may know the difference between the clean and the unclean, and know what you ought to eat and what to refuse.

<margin>xii</margin>
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: If a woman has conceived seed and given birth to a male, she shall be unclean seven days, according to the days of the separation of her flowers <note>menstrual period</note>. And on the eighth day the infant shall be circumcised. But she shall remain thirty-three days in the blood of her purification. She shall not touch anything holy, nor shall she enter into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed. But if she gives birth to a female, she shall be unclean for two weeks according to the rite of her menstrual flow, and...

## And when the days of her purification are fulfilled, for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring a yearling lamb for a burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"</note> and a young pigeon or a turtle dove for a sin offering to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall deliver it to the priest. He shall offer it before the Lord and pray for her, and she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood. This is the law for her who gives birth to a male or a female. But if her hand cannot find nor is she able to offer a lamb, she shall take two turtle doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering; and the priest shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed.

## The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: The man in whose flesh and skin there shall arise a different color or a pustule, or something like a bright spot—that is, the plague of leprosy <note>The biblical term "leprosy" (tzara'at) refers to a variety of skin conditions, molds, and mildews that rendered a person or object ritually "unclean," rather than just modern Hansen’s disease.</note>—shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to any one of his sons. When the priest sees the leprosy in the skin and the hair turned white, and the appearance of the leprosy itself is deeper than the rest of the skin and flesh, it is the plague of leprosy; and at his judgment he shall be separated. But if there is a bright whiteness in the skin and it is not deeper than the rest of the flesh, and the hair is of its original color, the priest shall shut him up for seven days. And on the seventh day he shall examine him. And if the leprosy has not grown further, nor spread across the skin within its former boundaries, he shall shut him up again for another seven days. And on the seventh day he shall examine him: if the leprosy is darker and has not grown in the flesh, he shall declare him clean, because it is a scab; and the man shall wash his clothes and be clean. But if, after he was seen by the priest and restored to cleanliness, the leprosy grows again, he shall be brought to him and shall be condemned of uncleanness.

## If the plague of leprosy is in a man, he shall be brought to the priest and he shall see him. And when the color in the skin is white, and has changed the appearance of the hair, and the raw flesh itself appears, it shall be judged as a very old leprosy that has grown into the skin. Therefore the priest shall declare him contaminated and shall not shut him up, because he is clearly unclean. But if the leprosy flourishes and spreads in the skin, covering all the flesh from head to foot, whatever falls under the sight of the eyes, the priest shall consider him and judge that he is held by a very clean leprosy, because it has all turned into whiteness; and therefore the man shall be clean. But when raw flesh appears in him, then by the judgment of the priest he shall be contaminated and shall be counted among the unclean. For raw flesh, if the leprosy has sprinkled it, is unclean. But if it turns again into whiteness and covers the whole man, the priest shall consider him and decree him clean. In the flesh and skin where an ulcer was born and healed, and in the place of the ulcer a white scar appears, or a white-reddish spot, the man shall be brought to the priest. When he sees the place of the leprosy lower than the rest of the flesh and the hair turned into whiteness, he shall contaminate him. For the plague of leprosy has arisen in the ulcer.

### But if the hair is of its original color, and the scar is somewhat dark, and is not lower than the living flesh, he shall shut him up for seven days. And if it has indeed grown, he shall adjudge it to be leprosy. But if it stays in its place, it is the scar of an ulcer, and the man shall be clean. In the flesh and skin which the fire has burned, if it has a white or red scar when healed, the priest shall consider it; and behold, if it has turned into whiteness and its place is lower than the rest of the skin, he shall contaminate him, because the plague of leprosy has arisen in the scar.

### But if the color of the hair has not changed, nor the plague is lower than the rest of the flesh, and the appearance of the leprosy itself is somewhat dark, he shall shut him up for seven days, and on the seventh day he shall examine it. If it has grown in the skin, he shall then judge him; for he shall be contaminated. But if the whiteness stays in its place and the plague is not bright enough, it is a burn, and therefore he shall be cleansed, because it is the scar of a burning.

### A man or woman on whose head or beard leprosy has germinated, the priest shall see them. And if the spot is deeper than the rest of the flesh, and the hair is yellow and thinner than usual, he shall contaminate them, because it is the leprosy of the head and beard. But if he sees the place of the spot equal to the neighboring flesh, and the hair is black, he shall shut him up for seven days, and on the seventh day he shall look upon the finding. If the spot has not grown and the hair is not yellow, and the place of the plague is equal to the rest of the flesh, the man shall shave his beard at the place of the spot, and he shall be shut up for another seven days. If on the seventh day the spot is seen to have stayed in its place and is not lower than the rest of the flesh, he shall cleanse him; and having washed his clothes, he shall be clean. But if after the cleansing the spot is again in the skin, he shall no longer seek whether the hair is changed to a yellow color, because he is openly unclean <note>The scribe likely meant "unclean" here, as the symptoms indicate the disease is active.</note>. Furthermore, if the spot has stayed and the hair is black, let him know the man is healed, and he shall confidently pronounce him clean.

### In whatever garment, whether woolen or linen, there is a spot of leprosy, green or red, it shall be shown to the priest. When he has seen it, he shall shut it up for seven days. And on the seventh day, looking again, if the leprosy has grown, it is a persistent leprosy; he shall judge the garment polluted, and everything in which it was found, whether it be woolen or linen or made of skins, therefore it shall be burned with flames.

### But if he sees that it has not grown, he shall command and they shall wash that in which the leprosy is, and he shall shut it up for another seven days. And when he sees that the former appearance has not returned, yet the leprosy has not grown, he shall judge it unclean and burn it with fire, because it is infused on the surface of the garment or throughout. But if the place of the leprosy is darker after the vessel <note>The text likely refers to the "garment" or material here.</note> is washed, he shall tear it off and separate it from the rest of the garment.

### If, however, there appears in those places which were previously untainted a flying and wandering leprosy, it must be burned with fire. If it has departed, he shall wash the parts that are pure a second time, and they shall be clean. This is the law of the leprosy of a woolen or linen garment, of the warp and the woof, and of all leather furniture, how it should be cleansed or contaminated.

## The Cleansing of Leprosy.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: This is the ritual of the leper when he is to be cleansed. He shall be brought to the priest, who, going out of the camp, when he finds the leprosy to be healed, shall command him who is being purified to offer for himself two living sparrows which it is lawful to eat, and cedar wood, and a scarlet thread <note>original: "uermiculum"; literally 'little worm', referring to the kermes insect used to produce scarlet dye</note>, and hyssop. And he shall command one of the sparrows to be sacrificed in an earthen vessel over living waters. Then, taking the other living sparrow with the cedar wood and the scarlet and the hyssop, dipping them in the blood of the sacrificed sparrow, he shall sprinkle him who is to be cleansed seven times, that he may be rightly purified; and he shall let the living sparrow fly away into the field. And when the man has washed his clothes, he shall shave all the hair of his body and be washed with water; and being purified, he shall enter the camp, provided that he remains outside his tent for seven days. And on the seventh day he shall shave the hair of his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and the hair of his whole body. And having washed his clothes and his body again, on the eighth day he shall bring two immaculate lambs and

<column-break/>

one yearling ewe without blemish, and three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and separately a sextary <note>A Roman unit of liquid measure, roughly a pint.</note> of oil. And when the priest purifying the man has presented him and all these things before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, he shall take the lamb and offer it for a trespass offering, with the sextary of oil; and having been offered before the Lord, he shall sacrifice the lamb where the victim for sin and the burnt offering is accustomed to be sacrificed—that is, in the holy place. For just as for sin, so also for a trespass offering the victim belongs to the priest; it is the holy of holies. And the priest, taking some of the blood of the victim that was sacrificed, shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him who is being cleansed, and upon the thumbs of his right hand and right foot. And of the sextary of oil, he shall pour some into his own left hand, and in it dip his right finger and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord. And if any of the oil remains in his hand, he shall pour it upon the tip of the right ear of him who is being cleansed, and upon the thumbs of his right hand and right foot, and upon the blood which was shed for the trespass, and upon his head. And he shall pray for him before the Lord, and shall make a sacrifice for sin. Then he shall sacrifice the burnt offering and place it on the altar with its libations, and the man shall be rightly cleansed. But if he is poor and his hand cannot find what was said, he shall take one lamb for a trespass offering as an oblation, that the priest may pray for him, and a tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and a sextary of oil, and two turtle doves or two young pigeons, of which one shall be for sin and the other for a burnt offering. And he shall offer them on the eighth day of his purification to the priest at the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord. He, taking the lamb for the trespass and the sextary of oil, shall offer them together. And having sacrificed the lamb, he shall put some of its blood upon the tip of the right ear of him who is being cleansed, and upon the thumbs of his right hand and right foot. Truly, he shall pour part of the oil into his left hand, in which, dipping the finger of his right hand, he shall sprinkle seven times before the Lord. And he shall touch the tip of the right ear of him who is being cleansed, and the thumbs of his right hand and foot, in the place of the blood which was shed for the trespass. Moreover, the remaining part of the oil which is in his left hand he shall put upon the head of the purified person, that the Lord may be merciful to him. And he shall offer one turtle dove or young pigeon for sin, and the other for a burnt offering with its libation. This is the sacrifice of a leper who cannot have all things for his purification.

## The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: When you have entered the land of Canaan, which I will give you for a possession, if there is a plague of leprosy in the houses, he whose house it is shall go and tell the priest, saying: It seems to me there is something like a plague of leprosy in my house. And he shall command that they carry everything out of the house before he enters it to see whether it is leprosy, lest all things that are in the house become unclean; and afterwards he shall enter to examine the house. And if he sees in its walls as it were little hollows, deformed with paleness or redness and lower than the rest of the surface, he shall go out the door of the house and immediately shut it for seven days. And returning on the seventh day, he shall examine it. If he finds that the leprosy has grown, he shall command the stones in which the plague was to be cast out of the city into an unclean place. But the house itself he shall scrape on the inside round about, and sprinkle the dust of the scraping outside the city in an unclean place. And he shall replace other stones for those which were taken away, and the house shall be plastered with other mortar. But if, after the stones were pulled out and the dust carried away and other earth plastered, the priest enters again and sees the leprosy regerminating in the walls, it appears to be a persistent leprosy and the house is unclean. They shall immediately destroy it, and cast the stones and the wood and all the dust outside the town into an unclean place. He who enters the house while it is shut shall be unclean until evening; and he who sleeps in it and eats anything shall wash his clothes. If the priest finds that the leprosy has not grown, he shall not cleanse it <note>This likely means he shall declare it clean but still perform the ritual.</note>, but for its purification he shall take the smoke of a sacrifice: two sparrows and cedar wood and scarlet thread and hyssop. And having sacrificed one sparrow in an earthen vessel over living waters, he shall take the cedar wood and hyssop and the scarlet and the living sparrow, and dip them all in the blood of the sacrificed sparrow and in the living water, and sprinkle the house seven times. And he shall purify it as much with the blood of the sparrow as with the living water, and with the living sparrow and the cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet thread. And when he has let the sparrow fly away into the field freely, he shall pray for the house, and it shall be rightly cleansed. This is the law of every leprosy and stroke of leprosy, of the garments and houses, of a scar and of erupting papules, of a shining spot, and of various species changed into colors, so that it may be known at what time something is clean or unclean.

## The Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: A man who suffers a flow of seed shall be unclean. And he shall then be judged to be subject to this vice when at every moment it clings to his flesh and a foul humor grows thick. Every bed on which he sleeps shall be unclean, and where he sits. If any man touches his bed, he shall wash his clothes, and being himself washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. If he sits where that man sat, he also shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. He who touches his flesh shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. If the spit of such an unclean man falls upon one who is clean, he shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. The saddle <note>original: "sagum"; can refer to a saddlecloth or a coarse cloak</note> upon which he sits shall be unclean; and whoever touches anything that was under him shall be unclean until evening. He who carries any of these things shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. Everyone whom such a person touches without having washed his hands first shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. An earthen vessel which he touches shall be broken; but a wooden vessel shall be washed with water. If the man who suffers this kind of passion is healed, he shall count seven days after his cleansing; and having washed his clothes and his whole body in living waters, he shall be clean. And on the eighth day he shall take two turtle doves or two young pigeons, and shall come into the sight of the Lord to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and give them to the priest. He shall make one for sin and the other for a burnt offering; and he shall pray for him before the Lord, and he shall be cleansed from the flow of his seed. A man from whom the seed of intercourse goes out shall wash his whole body with water and be unclean until evening. The garment and skin which he had on he shall wash with water, and it shall be unclean until evening.

### The woman with whom a man has slept shall be washed with water and shall be unclean until evening. The woman who, when her month returns, suffers a flow of blood, shall be separated for seven days. Everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening; and that in which she sleeps or sits shall be separated. He who touches her bed shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. Every vessel upon which she sits, whoever touches it shall wash his clothes, and being washed with water, he shall be polluted until evening. If a man comes to her at the time of her menstrual blood, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he sleeps shall be polluted. A woman who suffers a flow of blood for many days...

...[she who suffers] a monthly discharge for a long period, or who begins to flow with blood after her menstruation, when she is subject to this suffering, she shall be unclean, just as during the time of her menstruation. Every bed in which she sleeps and every vessel in which she sits shall be defiled. Whoever touches them shall wash his clothes, and being himself washed with water, he shall be unclean until evening. If the blood flows and then stops, she shall count seven days for her purification, and on the eighth day she shall offer for herself to the priest two turtledoves or two young pigeons at the door of the tabernacle of testimony <note>The "tabernacle of testimony" refers to the portable earthly dwelling place of God during the Exodus.</note>. He shall offer one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"</note>. And he shall pray for her before the Lord regarding the flow of her uncleanness.

## You shall therefore teach the children of Israel to beware of uncleanness, so that they do not die in their filthiness by defiling my tabernacle which is among them. This is the law for him who suffers a flow of seed, and who is defiled by sexual intercourse, and for her who is separated during the times of menstruation, and for him who suffers a perpetual flow of blood, and for the man who sleeps with her.

---

## The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they were killed while offering strange fire <note>referring to Nadab and Abihu, who died for using "unauthorized fire" in their censers (Leviticus 10).</note>. And he commanded him, saying: Speak to your brother Aaron, that he should not enter at all times into the sanctuary which is within the veil before the mercy seat <note>original: "propitiatorio"; the gold lid of the Ark of the Covenant.</note> with which the ark is covered, so that he does not die; for I will appear in a cloud over the oracle—unless he has first done these things. He shall offer a calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. He shall be clothed in a linen tunic and shall use linen breeches to cover his flesh. He shall be girded with a linen sash and a linen miter <note>A liturgical headdress or turban.</note> shall be placed on his head. For these are the holy vestments. He shall be clothed in all of them after he has been washed. And he shall receive from the whole multitude of the children of Israel two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.

## And when he has offered the calf and prayed for himself and his household, he shall make the two goats stand before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony. Casting lots over each, one for the Lord and the other for the scapegoat <note>original: "capro emissario"; literally the "emissary goat" sent into the wilderness.</note>. The one whose lot falls to the Lord, he shall offer for a sin offering. But the one whose lot is for the scapegoat, he shall set him alive before the Lord, that he may pour out prayers over him and send him out into the wilderness.

## When these things are rightly celebrated, he shall offer the calf, and praying for himself and his household, he shall immolate it. And taking a censer which he had filled with burning coals from the altar, and drawing with his hand the finely ground incense of spices into the area within the veil, he shall place the incense upon the fire: so that its cloud and vapor may cover the oracle which is over the testimony, and he might not die. He shall also take some of the blood of the calf and sprinkle it with his finger seven times against the mercy seat toward the east. And when he has slaughtered the goat for the sin of the people, he shall carry its blood within the veil, just as was commanded concerning the blood of the calf: so that he may sprinkle it opposite the oracle, and cleanse the sanctuary from the uncleanness of the children of Israel and from their transgressions and all their sins.

## According to this rite he shall do in the tabernacle of testimony, which is placed in the midst of their dwelling places. Let no man be in the tabernacle when the high priest enters the sanctuary to pray for himself, for his household, and for the entire multitude of Israel, until he comes out. But when he has gone out to the altar which is before the Lord, let him pray for himself; and taking the blood of the calf and of the goat, let him pour it upon its horns all around. And sprinkling with his finger seven times, let him cleanse it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel. For after he has cleansed the sanctuary, the tabernacle, and the altar, then let him offer the living goat. And having placed both hands upon its head, let him confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel and all their offenses and sins. Praying these over its head, he shall send it out by a man prepared for the task into the desert.

## And when the goat has carried all their iniquities into a solitary land, and has been released in the desert, Aaron shall return to the tabernacle of testimony. And having taken off the garments in which he was previously clothed when he entered the sanctuary, he shall leave them there. He shall wash his flesh in a holy place and be clothed in his own garments. After he has come out and offered his burnt offering and that of the people, he shall pray both for himself and for the people; and the fat which was offered for the sin, he shall burn upon the altar. But he who let go of the scapegoat shall wash his clothes and his body with water, and so enter the camp. But the calf and the goat which were immolated for sin, and whose blood was carried into the sanctuary so that the atonement might be completed, they shall carry outside the camp; and they shall burn with fire both their skins and their flesh and their dung. And whoever burns them shall wash his clothes and his flesh with water, and so enter the camp. And this shall be for you an everlasting statute: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls. You shall do no work, whether a native or a stranger who sojourns among you. On this day shall be your atonement and cleansing from all your sins: before the Lord you shall be cleansed. For it is a Sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls by a perpetual religion.

## And the priest who has been anointed, and whose hands have been consecrated to function in the priesthood in place of his father, shall make atonement. He shall be clothed in the linen robe and holy garments, and he shall cleanse the sanctuary, the tabernacle of testimony, and the altar, as well as the priests and all the people. And this shall be an everlasting statute: that you pray for the children of Israel and for all their sins once a year. He did, therefore, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

<margin>M</margin>
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel; you shall say to them: This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying: Any man of the house of Israel who kills an ox or a sheep or a goat in the camp or outside the camp, and does not offer it at the door of the tabernacle as an offering to the Lord, shall be guilty of blood: for he has shed blood; thus he shall perish from the midst of his people. Therefore, the children of Israel ought to bring to the priest their victims which they kill in the field, so that they may be sanctified to the Lord before the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and they shall immolate those as peace offerings to the Lord. And the priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall burn the fat as a sweet odor to the Lord. And they shall no longer immolate their victims to demons <note>original: "demonibus"; likely referring to goat-idols or nature spirits.</note> with whom they have fornicated. This shall be an everlasting statute for them and their descendants.

<margin>E</margin>
You shall also say these things to them: Any man of the house of Israel or of the strangers who sojourn among you, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice, and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony to offer it to the Lord, his soul shall perish from his people.

<margin>H</margin>
Any man of the house of Israel or of the strangers who sojourn among them, if he eats blood, I will set my face against his soul, and I will destroy it from among his people. Because the life <note>original: "anima"; literally "soul."</note> of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you so that upon the altar you may make atonement for your souls with it: and let the blood be for the expiation of the soul. Therefore I said to the children of Israel: Every soul among you shall not eat blood, nor any of the strangers who sojourn among you. Any man of the children of Israel or of the strangers who sojourn among you, if by hunting or fowling he catches a wild beast or a bird which it is lawful to eat: let him pour out its blood and cover it with earth. For the life of all flesh is in the blood: wherefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of the flesh is in the blood; and whoever eats it shall perish. The soul that eats that which has died of itself or was caught by a beast, whether of the natives or of the strangers, shall wash his clothes and himself with water; and he shall be unclean until evening, and in this order he shall become clean.

<column-break/>

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: I am the Lord your God. You shall not do according to the custom of the land of Egypt in which you dwelt; and you shall not act according to the manner of the region of Canaan into which I will lead you, nor shall you walk in their ordinances. You shall perform my judgments and keep my precepts, and walk in them. I am the Lord your God. Keep my laws and judgments: which if a man does, he shall live in them. I am the Lord. No man shall approach anyone near of his own blood to reveal her nakedness <note>original: "turpitudinem"; literally "disgrace" or "shame," a euphemism for sexual relations.</note>. I am the Lord. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother: you shall not reveal her nakedness. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father's wife, for it is the nakedness of your father. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your sister by your father or by your mother, who was born at home or abroad. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because it is your own nakedness. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father's wife's daughter whom she bore to your father, for she is your sister. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father's sister, because she is your father's flesh. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your mother's sister, because she is your mother's flesh. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father's brother, nor shall you approach his wife, who is joined to you by affinity. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, because she is your son's wife: nor shall you uncover her shame. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife, nor reveal it: because it is the nakedness of your brother. You shall not reveal the nakedness of a wife and her daughter. You shall not take his son's daughter or his daughter's daughter to reveal her nakedness, because they are her flesh, and such intercourse is incest. You shall not take your wife's sister as a concubine <note>original: "pellicatu"; referring to taking a second wife while the first is alive.</note>, nor reveal her nakedness while she is still living. You shall not approach a woman who is suffering her menstruation, nor reveal her uncleanness. You shall not sleep with your neighbor's wife, nor be defiled by the mixing of seed. You shall not give of your seed to be consecrated to the idol Moloch <note>An ancient deity associated with child sacrifice.</note>, nor shall you pollute the name of your God. I am the Lord. You shall not lie with a male as with a woman, because it is an abomination. You shall not lie with any beast, nor be defiled with it. A woman shall not lie down before a beast nor be joined to it, because it is a crime. Do not be polluted in any of these things in which all the nations have been contaminated, which I will cast out before your sight, and by which the land is defiled; whose crimes I will visit, so that it vomits out its inhabitants. Keep my statutes and judgments, and do not perform any of these abominations, whether a native or a resident who sojourns among you. For the inhabitants of the land who were before you performed all these execrations and defiled it. Beware, therefore, lest it vomit you out in like manner when you do the same, as it vomited out the nation that was before you. Every soul that does any of these abominations shall perish from among his people. Keep my mandates and do not do what those who were before you have done, and do not be polluted by them. I am the Lord your God.

<margin>C</margin>
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the whole assembly of the children of Israel and say to them: Be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy. Let every one fear his mother and his father. Keep my Sabbaths. I am the Lord your God. Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molten gods. I am the Lord your God. If you immolate a peace offering to the Lord so that it may be acceptable, you shall eat it on the same day it was immolated and on the next day. But whatever remains on the third day shall be burned with fire. If anyone eats of it after two days, he shall be profane and guilty of impiety; he shall bear his iniquity because he has polluted the holy thing of the Lord, and that soul shall perish from his people. When you reap the corn of your land, you shall not cut it down to the very ground, nor shall you gather the remaining ears; nor shall you gather the clusters and fallen grapes in your vineyard, but you shall leave them for the poor and the strangers to take. I am the Lord your God. You shall not steal, nor shall you lie, nor shall anyone deceive his neighbor. You shall not perjure yourself in my name, nor pollute the name of your God. I am the Lord. You shall not bring false accusations against your neighbor, nor oppress him by force. The work of your hired laborer shall not remain with you until morning. You shall not curse the deaf, nor place a stumbling block before the blind: but you shall fear the Lord your God, because I am the Lord. You shall not do what is unjust, nor judge unrighteously. You shall not consider the person of the poor, nor honor the face of the powerful. Judge your neighbor justly. You shall not be a slanderer, nor a whisperer among the people. You shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the Lord. You shall not hate your brother in your heart, but publicly rebuke him, lest you have sin because of him. You shall not seek revenge, nor be mindful of the injury of your citizens: You shall love your friend as yourself. I am the Lord. Keep my laws. You shall not make your cattle breed with animals of another kind. You shall not sow your field with diverse seed. You shall not wear a garment woven of two types of thread <note>Ancient law prohibited the mixing of wool and linen.</note>. If a man sleeps with a woman and has intercourse, who is a handmaid also betrothed to a nobleman, and yet not redeemed nor given her freedom: they shall both be flogged, but they shall not die, because she was not free. For his offense, however, he shall offer a ram to the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony. And the priest shall pray for him and for his sin: and the Lord will be propitiated toward him, and his sin shall be forgiven him.

<margin>Q</margin>
When you have entered the land and have planted fruit-bearing trees in it, you shall remove their first-fruits <note>original: "preputia"; literally "foreskins," referring to the fruit of the first three years.</note>. The fruits that grow shall be unclean to you, nor shall you eat of them. In the fourth year all their fruit shall be sanctified, praiseworthy to the Lord. But in the fifth year you shall eat the fruits, gathering the abundance which they produce. I am the Lord your God. You shall not eat meat with blood. You shall not practice augury, nor observe dreams. You shall not cut your hair in a circle, nor shave your beard. And for the dead you shall not cut your flesh, nor make any figures or marks <note>tattoos</note> on yourselves. I am the Lord. Do not prostitute your daughter, lest the land be contaminated and filled with crime. Keep my Sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. I am the Lord. Do not turn to magicians, nor seek anything from soothsayers, lest you be polluted by them. I am the Lord your God. Rise up before the hoary head <note>gray hair</note> and honor the person of the aged, and fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord. If a stranger dwells in your land and stays among you, do not upbraid him: but let him be among you like a native, and you shall love him as yourselves. For you also were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God. Do not do anything unjust in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure. Let the scales be just and the weights equal, a just bushel and an equal quart. I am the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt. Keep all my precepts and all my judgments and do them. I am the Lord.

If anyone commits adultery with the wife of another, and rushes into adultery with the wife of his neighbor, let both the adulterer and the adulteress die the death. He who sleeps with his stepmother and reveals the shame <note>original: "ignominiam"</note> of his father: let both die the death. Their blood be upon them. If anyone sleeps with his daughter-in-law: let both die, because they have committed a crime; their blood be upon them. He who sleeps with a male in the manner of a woman <term>coitu femineo: sexual intercourse as with a woman</term>: both have committed a foul deed; let them die the death. Their blood be upon them. He who, besides his wife, takes her daughter and her mother: it is a crime; he shall be burned alive with them, nor shall such a great wickedness remain in the midst of you. He who copulates with a beast or cattle: let him die the death. Kill the beast as well. A woman who lies down with any beast shall be killed together with it; her blood be upon her. If anyone takes his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother, and sees her nakedness: they have committed an illicit crime. For this wicked thing they are killed in the sight of their people, because they have revealed each other's nakedness, and they shall bear their iniquity. He who sleeps with a woman in her menstrual flow and reveals her nakedness, and she opens the fountain of her blood: both shall be killed from the midst of their people. You shall not reveal the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister; he who does this reveals his own kin. Both shall be childless. He who copulates with his brother’s wife does an illicit thing. He has revealed his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.

Keep my laws and judgments and do them, lest the land into which you are to be led and in which you are to dwell vomit you out. Do not walk in the laws of the nations which I am about to drive out before you. For they have done all these things, and I have detested them. But I speak to you: possess their land, which I will give to you as an inheritance—a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God who has separated you from other peoples. Therefore, separate the unclean animals from the clean, and all birds. You shall know how to distinguish them so you are not defiled. They shall be overwhelmed with stones; their blood be upon them.

**T**he Lord also said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say to them: A priest shall not be defiled by the deaths of his fellow citizens, except only for his closest kin: that is, for father and mother, and for a sister who is a virgin not yet married to a man. But neither shall he be contaminated as a leader of his people. They shall not shave their heads nor their beards, nor shall they make incisions in their flesh. They shall be holy to their God, and shall not pollute his name; for they offer the incense of the Lord and the bread of the Lord, and therefore they shall be holy. He shall not take as a wife a harlot or a common prostitute, nor her who has been divorced by her husband, because he is consecrated to his God and offers the <term>bread of proposition: the twelve loaves of sacred bread kept in the Tabernacle</term>. Let him therefore be holy, because I, the Lord who sanctifies you, am holy. If the daughter of a priest is caught in debauchery and violates the name of her father, she shall be burned with flames. The Pontiff, that is the High Priest <note>original: "sacerdos maximus"</note> among his brothers, upon whose head the oil of unction has been poured, and whose hands were consecrated in the priesthood, and who is clothed in holy garments: he shall not uncover his head, nor shall he tear his clothes. He shall not enter at all to any dead person. He shall not be contaminated even for his father or mother, nor shall he go out of the holy places, lest he pollute the sanctuary of the Lord, because the oil of the holy unction of his God is upon him. I am the Lord. He shall take a virgin as a wife. A widow, a divorcee, a defiled woman, or a harlot he shall not take, but a girl from his own people. Let him not mix the stock of his family with the common crowd of his nation, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
