**A**nd the Lord said to Moses: Speak to Aaron. A man of your seed through your families who has a blemish shall not offer bread to his God, nor approach his ministry. If he be blind or lame; if he has a nose too small or too large or crooked; if he has a broken foot or hand; if he is a hunchback or bleary-eyed <note>original: "lippus"</note>; if he has a white film in his eye; if he has a chronic itch, a skin disease, or a hernia. Anyone of the seed of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall not approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor bread to his God. He may nevertheless eat of the bread which is offered in the sanctuary, provided that he does not enter within the veil nor approach the altar, because he has a blemish, and he must not contaminate my sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctifies them. **A**nd so Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons, and to all Israel, regarding what had been commanded him.

**A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they beware of those things which are consecrated by the children of Israel, and that they do not contaminate the name of my holiness in what they offer to me. I am the Lord. Say to them and to their descendants: Every man of your stock who approaches those things which are consecrated and which the children of Israel have offered to the Lord, in whom there is uncleanness, shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord. A man of the seed of Aaron who is a leper or suffers a flow of seed shall not eat of the things that are sanctified until he is healed. He who touches anything unclean by a dead body, or from whom seed of intercourse goes out, or who touches any unclean creeping thing, by whose touch he is defiled... or anything else that is filthy... he who has done this shall be [unclean] until evening, but when he has washed his flesh with water and the sun has set, then he shall be clean and may eat of the sanctified things, because it is his food. That which dies of itself or is caught by a beast they shall not eat, nor be polluted by them. I am the Lord. Let them keep my precepts, lest they fall into sin and die in the sanctuary when they have polluted it. I am the Lord who sanctifies you. No stranger shall eat of the sanctified things; a guest of the priest or a hired servant shall not eat of them. But he whom the priest has bought, and he who is a servant born in his house, these shall eat of them. If the daughter of a priest marries a commoner, she shall not eat of the sanctified things or the firstfruits. But if she is a widow or divorced and returns childless to her father’s house, she shall live as a girl was accustomed to live, on her father’s food. No stranger has the power to eat of these. He who eats of the sanctified things through ignorance shall add a fifth part to that which he ate and give it to the priest in the sanctuary. They shall not contaminate the sanctified things of the children of Israel which they offer to the Lord, lest they bear the iniquity of their offense when they eat the sanctified things. I am the Lord who sanctifies them. **A**nd Moses spoke about the solemnities of the Lord to the children of Israel.

**T**he Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When a bull, a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall be seven days under the udder of its mother. **T**he Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: These are the festivals of the Lord, which you shall call holy. **F**or six days you shall do work; the seventh day, because it is the rest of the Sabbath <note>original: "sabbati"</note>, shall be called holy. In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the Lord’s Passover <note>original: "phase"</note>. The first day shall be most celebrated for you and called holy; you shall do no servile work on it. You shall offer a sacrifice by fire to the Lord for seven days. **A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give to you and have reaped the harvest, you shall offer sheaves of grain, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest. He shall lift the bundle before the Lord so it may be acceptable for you, according to the custom of the next day, that is, the Sabbath, and he shall sanctify it. On the same day that the sheaf is consecrated, a yearling lamb without blemish shall be slaughtered as a burnt offering to the Lord. And libations shall be offered with it: two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for an incense of the Lord of most sweet odor; and libations of wine, a fourth part of a <term>hin: an ancient measure of liquid, roughly one gallon</term>. You shall not eat bread or parched grain or pottage from the harvest until the day you offer it to your God. It is an everlasting precept in your generations and in all your dwellings. You shall count therefore from the day after the Sabbath on which you offered the sheaf of firstfruits, seven full weeks, until the day after the completion of the seventh week, that is, fifty days; and thus you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord from all your dwellings: two loaves of firstfruits made of two-tenths of fine flour, which you shall bake with honey as the firstfruits to the Lord. You shall offer with the loaves seven yearling lambs without blemish, and one calf from the herd, and two rams; and they shall be a burnt offering with their libations, as a most sweet odor to the Lord. You shall also make a goat for sin, and two yearling lambs as peace offerings. When the priest has lifted them with the loaves of firstfruits before the Lord, they shall fall to his use. And you shall call this day most celebrated and most holy. You shall do no servile work on it. It shall be a perpetual law in all your dwellings and generations. After you have reaped the harvest of your land, you shall not shave it to the ground, nor shall you gather the remaining ears; but you shall leave them for the poor and for strangers. I am the Lord your God.

**T**he Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel. In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be for you a memorial Sabbath with the blaring of trumpets, and it shall be called holy. You shall do no servile work on it, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord. **A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the most celebrated Day of Atonement <note>original: "dies expiationis"</note>, and it shall be called holy. You shall afflict your souls on it and offer a burnt offering to the Lord. You shall do no servile work during the time of this day, because it is the day of propitiation, that the Lord your God may be propitious to you. Every soul that is not afflicted on this day shall perish from his people; and whoever does any work, I will destroy him from his people. For you shall do no work on it. It shall be a perpetual law in your generations and in your dwellings. You shall rest on the Sabbath; you shall afflict your souls. From the evening of the tenth day of the month until evening, you shall celebrate your Sabbaths.

**A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel. These are the festivals of the Lord, which you shall call most celebrated and most holy, and you shall offer in them oblations to the Lord: burnt offerings and libations according to the ritual of each day, except for the Sabbaths of the Lord, and your gifts, and those things which you offer by vow, or which you give spontaneously to the Lord. From the fifteenth day therefore of the seventh month, when you have gathered all the fruits of your land, you shall celebrate the festivals of the Lord for seven days. You shall celebrate his solemnity seven days throughout the year. It shall be a perpetual law in your generations. Behold, the son of an Israelite woman, whom she had borne to an Egyptian man, went out among the children of Israel, and he quarreled in the camp with an Israelite man. And when he had blasphemed the name of the Lord and cursed it, he was brought to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. And they put him in prison until they might know what the Lord would command. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Bring the blasphemer outside the camp; and let all who heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let the whole people stone him. And you shall speak to the children of Israel: The man who curses his God shall bear his sin; and he who blasphemes the name of the Lord shall die the death. The whole multitude of the people shall overwhelm him with stones. Whether he be a citizen or a stranger, he who blasphemes the name of the Lord shall die the death. He who strikes and kills a man shall die the death. He who strikes an animal shall restore a substitute, that is, a life for a life <note>original: "animam pro anima"</note>. If anyone inflicts a blemish upon any of his citizens, as he has done, so shall it be done to him: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth shall he restore. Whatever blemish he has inflicted, such shall he be compelled to suffer. He who strikes a beast shall restore another; he who strikes a man shall be punished. Let there be equal judgment among you, whether a stranger or a citizen has sinned, because I am the Lord your God. And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and they led him who had blasphemed outside the camp and overwhelmed him with stones. And the children of Israel did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give to you, keep a sabbath <note>original: "sabbatizate"; to rest or keep a holy day</note> to the Lord. Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its fruits. But in the seventh year, there shall be a sabbath of rest for the land of the Lord's resting. You shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard. What the ground produces of its own accord you shall not reap, and the grapes of your first-fruits you shall not gather after the harvest, as if in a vintage; for it is a year of rest for the land. But they shall be for food for you: for you and your servant, your handmaid and your hired worker, and the stranger who lives with you, for your cattle and your beasts; everything that is born shall provide food. You shall also count seven weeks of years, that is, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years; and the trumpet shall sound in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, at the time of atonement <note>original: "propitiationis"; referring to Yom Kippur</note>, in all your land.

Also the fiftieth year: and you shall proclaim a release <note>original: "remissionem"</note> to all the inhabitants of the land. For it is the Jubilee <note>original: "iubileus"</note>. A man shall return to his possession, and everyone shall return to his former family. Because it is the Jubilee, and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor reap what grows of its own accord in the field, and you shall not gather the first-fruits of the vintage because of the sanctification of the Jubilee; but you shall eat the things offered at once. In the year of the Jubilee, all shall return to their possessions. <margin>In turn. 1.</margin> When you sell anything to your citizen, or buy from him, do not distress your brother. But according to the number of years of the Jubilee you shall buy from him, and according to the calculation of the crops he shall sell to you. The more years that remain after the Jubilee, the more the price shall increase; and the less time you count, the less the purchase shall cost. For he shall sell to you the time of the crops. Do not afflict your fellow countrymen, but let each one fear his God, because I am your Lord. Perform my precepts and keep my judgments and fulfill them, so that you may dwell in the land without any fear, and the ground may yield its fruits for you, which you may eat until you are full, fearing no one's attack. But if you should say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year if we have not sown nor gathered our crops?" I will give my blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce the fruit of three years. And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat the old crops until the ninth year. Until the new ones grow, you shall eat the old. The land also shall not be sold forever, because it is mine, and you are my strangers and settlers. Therefore, the whole region of your possession shall be sold under the condition of redemption. If your brother, being impoverished, sells his small possession, and his kinsman wishes, he can redeem what the other had sold. But if he has no near kinsman, and he himself is able to find the price for redeeming it, the fruits shall be counted from the time he sold it, and what remains he shall restore to the buyer, and thus receive his possession back. But if his hand does not find the means to restore the price, the buyer shall have what he bought until the Jubilee year. For in that year, every sale shall return to its lord and to the former possessor. He who sells a house within the walls of a city shall have the liberty of redeeming it until one year is completed. But if the circle of a year has passed and he has not redeemed it, the buyer shall possess it and his descendants forever, nor shall it be redeemed even in the Jubilee. But if the house is in a village that has no walls, it shall be sold by the law of the fields of the countryside. If it has not been redeemed, it shall return to the lord in the Jubilee. The houses of the Levites which are in cities can always be redeemed. If they are not redeemed, they shall return to the lords in the Jubilee, because they are the houses of the cities of the Levites among the possessions of the children of Israel. But their suburbs cannot be sold, because it is an everlasting possession. If your brother is impoverished and weak in hand, and you receive him like a stranger and a pilgrim and he lives with you, do not take interest <note>original: "usuras"</note> from him, nor more than you gave. Fear your God, that your brother may be able to live with you. You shall not give him your money for interest, nor <margin>Grain.</margin> shall you demand an abundance of food above what you gave. I am the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your Lord. If your brother, compelled by poverty, sells himself to you, you shall not oppress him with the service of slaves, but he shall be with you like a hired man and a settler until the Jubilee year. He shall work for you, and afterward he shall go out with his children and return to his kindred and to the possession of his fathers. For they are my servants, and I led them out of the land of Egypt.

They shall not be sold under the condition of slaves, nor shall you afflict them by power, but fear your Lord, your God.

Let your male and female slaves be from the nations that are around you, and from the strangers who travel among you, and from those who were born in your land. These you shall have as servants, and by hereditary right you shall transmit them to your descendants, and you shall possess them forever. But your brothers, the children of Israel, you shall not oppress by power. If the hand of a stranger or pilgrim prevails among you, and your brother, being impoverished, sells himself to him or to anyone of his lineage, after the sale he can be redeemed. Whoever of his brothers wishes shall redeem him: both the uncle, and the uncle's son, and the kinsman, and the relative. But if he himself is able to redeem himself, the years shall be calculated from the time of his sale until the Jubilee year, and the money for which he was sold according to the number of years and the rate of a hired man being calculated. If there are more years remaining until the Jubilee, according to these he shall also restore the price. If few, he shall settle the account with him according to the number of years, and he shall restore to the buyer what remains of the years, with the wages for which he served before being imputed. He shall not afflict him violently in your sight. But if he cannot be redeemed by this, he shall go out in the Jubilee year with his children. For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I led out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

<column-break/>

You shall not make for yourselves an idol or a carved image, and you shall not set up titles <note>original: "titulos"; likely referring to standing stones or pillars</note>, nor shall you place a notable stone in your land to adore it. For I am the Lord your God. Keep my sabbaths and fear my sanctuary. I am the Lord. If you walk in my precepts and keep my commandments and do them, I will give rain in its seasons, and the land shall yield its fruit, and the trees shall be filled with apples. The threshing of the harvest shall reach until the vintage, and the vintage shall occupy the sowing time; and you shall eat your bread until you are full, and you shall dwell in your land without fear. I will give peace in your borders; you shall sleep, and there will be no one to terrify you. I will take away evil beasts, and the sword shall not pass through your borders. You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you. Five of yours shall pursue a hundred foreigners, and a hundred of you ten thousand. Your enemies shall fall in your sight by the sword. I will look upon you and make you grow; you shall be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you. You shall eat the oldest of the old, and when the new comes, you shall cast away the old. I will set my tabernacle in your midst, and my soul shall not cast you off. I will walk among you and be your Lord, and you shall be my people. I am the Lord your God who led you out of the land of the Egyptians, so that you would not serve them, and who broke the chains of your necks so that you might walk upright. But if you do not hear me, nor do all my commandments, but despise my laws and contemn my judgments, so that you do not do those things which were established by me, and you make my covenant void: I also will do this to you. I will visit you quickly with poverty and burning heat, which shall waste your eyes and consume your souls. In vain shall you sow your seed, which shall be devoured by enemies. I will set my face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies, and you shall be made subject to those who hate you; you shall flee when no one pursues. But if even so you do not obey me, I will add a sevenfold correction for your sins, and I will break the pride of your hardness. I will give you the sky above like iron and the earth like bronze. Your labor shall be consumed in vain. The land shall not bring forth its sprout, nor shall the trees provide fruit. If you walk contrary to me and will not hear me, I will add your plagues up to sevenfold for your sins. I will send out the beasts of the field among you, which shall consume you and your cattle, and reduce everything to a small number, and your ways shall become deserted. But if even so you will not receive discipline, but walk contrary to me, I also will walk contrary to you and I will strike you seven times for your sins. I will bring upon you the sword, the avenger of my covenant. And when you flee into the cities, I will send a pestilence into your midst, and you shall be delivered into the hands of enemies, after I have broken the staff of your bread, so that ten women shall bake bread in one oven and deliver them by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied. But if even after these things you do not hear me, but walk against me, I also will walk against you in a contrary fury and I will correct you seven times with plagues for your sins, so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and your daughters <note>A stark depiction of the desperation of siege and famine</note>. I will destroy your high places and break your idols. You shall fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you, so that I will reduce your cities to a wilderness and make your sanctuaries deserted, nor will I receive further the sweetest odor. I will destroy your land, and your enemies shall be astonished over it when they become its inhabitants. But I will scatter you among the nations, and I will unsheathe the sword after you; your land shall be deserted and your cities destroyed. Then the land shall enjoy its sabbaths all the days of its desolation. When you are in an enemy land, it shall keep sabbath and rest in the sabbaths of its desolation, because it did not rest in your sabbaths when you dwelt in it. And those of you who remain, I will give fear in their hearts in the regions of the enemies. The sound of a flying leaf shall terrify them, and they shall flee as if from a sword. They shall fall with no one pursuing, and each one shall fall upon his brothers as if fleeing from war. None of you will dare to resist enemies. You shall perish among the nations, and the hostile land shall devour you. But if some of these remain, they shall waste away in their iniquities in the land of their enemies; and because of the sins of their fathers and their own, they shall be afflicted until they confess their iniquity and that of their ancestors, with the great reverence by which they transgressed against me and walked contrary to me. I also will walk against them and will lead them into a hostile land until their uncircumcised mind is ashamed. Then they shall pray for their impieties, and I will remember my covenant which I made with Jacob and Isaac and Abraham. Surely I will be mindful of the land which, when it is left by them, shall please itself in its sabbaths, and suffer desolation because of them. They indeed shall pray and receive their sins, because they rejected my judgments and despised my laws. And yet, even when they were in a hostile land, I did not entirely cast them off, nor did I so despise them that they should be consumed, and I make void my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God. And I will remember my former covenant, when I led them out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their Lord. I am the Lord. These are the judgments and precepts and laws which the Lord gave between himself and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: A man who has made a vow and vowed his soul to God shall give the price according to the valuation <note>original: "estimatione"</note>. If it is a male, from the twentieth to the sixtieth year, he shall give fifty shekels <note>original: "siclos"</note> of silver according to the measure of the sanctuary. If a woman, thirty. From the fifth until the twentieth, a male shall give twenty shekels, a female ten. From one month until the fifth year, for a male five shekels shall be given, for a female three. A sixty-year-old and above: a male shall give fifteen shekels, a female ten. If he is poor and unable to pay the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and as much as he shall estimate and see that he can pay, so much he shall give. But an animal that can be sacrificed to the Lord, if anyone vows it, it shall be holy and he cannot change it, that is, neither a better for a worse, nor a worse for a better. But if he changes it, both that which was changed and that for which it was changed shall be consecrated to the Lord. An unclean animal that cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, if anyone vows it, he shall bring it to the priest. Who, judging whether it be good or bad, shall establish the price. But if he who offers it wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth part above the valuation.

If a man vows his house and sanctifies it to the Lord, the priest shall consider it, whether it be good or bad, and according to the price established by him, it shall be sold. But if he who had vowed it wishes to redeem it, he shall give a fifth part of the valuation above it, and he shall have the house. If he vows a field of his possession and consecrates it to the Lord, the price shall be estimated according to the measure of the seed. If the land is sown with eighty bushels <note>original: "modii"</note> of barley, it shall be sold for fifty shekels of silver. If he vows immediately from the year of the Jubilee, as much as the field can be worth, so much it shall be estimated. But if after some time, the priest shall calculate the money according to the number of years that remain until the Jubilee, and he shall deduct from the price. But if he who vowed it wishes to redeem the field, he shall add a fifth part of the estimated money and possess it. If he will not redeem it, but it is sold to another, he who vowed it can no longer redeem it; because when the day of the Jubilee comes, it shall be...

<meta>This page concludes the final laws of Leviticus regarding vows and tithes and transitions directly into the opening of the Book of Numbers (Vagedaber). ...it shall be sanctified to the Lord. As a consecrated possession, it belongs to the right of the priest. If a field is bought and is not from his ancestral possession, and it has been sanctified to the Lord, the priest shall calculate the price according to the number of years until the Jubilee; and he who had vowed it shall give that amount to the Lord. In the Jubilee, however, it shall return to the previous owner who had sold it and who had it as his allotted possession. Every valuation shall be weighed according to the sanctuary shekel <note>A unit of weight used for temple currency</note>. A shekel has twenty obols <note>original: "obolos"; small units of currency or weight, often called gerahs</note>.

The firstborn which belong to the Lord: no one may sanctify them; whether it be an ox or a sheep, they are the Lord’s. But if it is an unclean animal, he who offered it shall redeem it according to its valuation, and shall add a fifth part to the price. If he does not wish to redeem it, it shall be sold to another for whatever price it was valued. Everything that is vowed to the Lord, whether it be a human, a beast, or a field, shall not be sold, nor can it be redeemed. Whatever has been once consecrated shall be the holy of holies to the Lord. And every consecration offered by a man shall not be redeemed, but shall surely die.

All tithes of the land, whether from grain or from the fruits of trees, belong to the Lord and are sanctified to Him. If anyone wishes to redeem his tithe, he shall add a fifth part to it. Of all the tithes of oxen and sheep and goats that pass under the shepherd's rod, every tenth one that comes shall be sanctified to the Lord. It shall not be chosen for being good or bad, nor shall it be exchanged for another. If anyone does change it, both that which was changed and that for which it was changed shall be sanctified to the Lord and shall not be redeemed. These are the precepts which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai. **Leviticus ends.**

# The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
"Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from the midst of the Levites, by their families and houses, from the thirtieth year and upward even to the sixtieth year, of all who enter in to stand and minister in the Tabernacle of the Covenant. This is the service of the sons of Kohath: in the Tabernacle of the Covenant and in the Holy of Holies, Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp is to be moved, and they shall take down the veil that hangs before the doors, and wrap the Ark of the Testimony in it, and cover it again with a covering of violet skins <note>original: "ianthinarum pellium"; likely referring to the skins of sea-cows or leather dyed a specific violet-blue</note>, and shall spread over it a cloth entirely of violet, and shall put in the carrying bars. They shall also wrap the Table of Showbread in a violet cloth, and put with it the censers and little mortars, the cups and bowls for pouring libations; the bread shall always be upon it. And they shall spread over it a scarlet cloth, which they shall again cover with a covering of violet skins, and shall put in the carrying bars. The golden altar also they shall wrap in a violet cloth, and spread over it a covering of violet skins, and put in the bars. All the vessels with which they minister in the sanctuary they shall wrap in a violet cloth, and spread over it a covering of violet skins, and put in the bars. But they shall also cleanse the altar of ashes, and wrap it in a purple cloth, and put with it all the vessels which they use in its ministry, that is, the fire-receptacles, the flesh-hooks, the forks, and the shovels. They shall cover all the vessels of the altar with a covering of violet skins, and put in the bars. And when Aaron and his sons have wrapped up the sanctuary and all its vessels in the moving of the camp, then the sons of Kohath shall enter to carry the things wrapped; and they shall not touch the vessels of the sanctuary, lest they die. These are the burdens of the sons of Kohath in the Tabernacle of the Covenant. Over them shall be Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, to whose care pertains the oil for preparing the lamps, and the composition of incense, and the sacrifice which is always offered, and the oil of unction, and whatever pertains to the service of the Tabernacle, and of all the vessels that are in the sanctuary."

# And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
"Command the children of Israel that they cast out of the camp every leper, and whosoever has an issue of seed and is polluted, and anyone defiled by the dead. Both male and female you shall cast out of the camp, lest they contaminate them while they dwell with us." And the children of Israel did so, and they cast them out of the camp, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

<margin>L</margin>
# And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
"Speak to the children of Israel: When a man or woman shall have committed any of all the sins that are wont to happen to men, and by negligence have transgressed the commandment of the Lord and have offended, they shall confess their sin, and shall restore the principal itself, and a fifth part besides, to him against whom they have sinned. But if there be no one to receive the restitution, it shall be given to the Lord, and it shall belong to the priest, except for the ram

<column-break/>

which is offered for atonement, that it may be an appeasing sacrifice. All the firstfruits also which the children of Israel offer belong to the priest; and whatever is offered by the mouths of individuals and delivered into the hands of the priests shall be their own."

<margin>L</margin>
# And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
"Speak to the children of Israel and you shall say to them: If a man's wife has gone astray and, despising her husband, has slept with another man, and the husband cannot discover this, and the adultery is hidden and cannot be proven by witnesses because she was not caught in the act; if the spirit of jealousy stirs up the man against his wife, who is either defiled or is attacked by a false suspicion, he shall bring her to the priest. And he shall offer an oblation for her, the tenth part of a measure <note>original: "sate"; a seah, about 7-13 liters</note> of barley flour; he shall not pour oil upon it, nor put frankincense on it, because it is a sacrifice of jealousy and an oblation investigating adultery. The priest shall therefore offer her and set her before the Lord. And he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and he shall cast a little earth from the floor of the Tabernacle into it. And when the woman stands in the sight of the Lord, he shall uncover her head, and shall put the sacrifice of remembrance and the oblation of jealousy upon her hands; but he himself shall hold the most bitter waters, in which he has heaped curses with a malediction. And he shall adjure her, and shall say: 'If no strange man has slept with you, and if you are not defiled by deserting your husband, these most bitter waters, into which I have heaped curses, shall not harm you. But if you have turned away from your husband and are defiled, and have lain with another man, you shall be subject to these maledictions: May the Lord make you a curse and an example to all among His people; may He make your thigh to rot and your belly to swell and burst. Let the cursed waters enter into your belly, and as your womb swells, may your thigh rot.' The woman shall answer, 'Amen, Amen.' <note>original: "am̄ am̄"; a Hebrew formula of solemn agreement</note> And the priest shall write these curses in a book, and shall wash them out with the bitter waters into which he heaped the curses, and shall give them to her to drink. When she has drained them, the Lord will do thus: if the wife was unfaithful—and if thereafter the wife is defiled and has trespassed against her husband by adultery—the waters of the curse shall enter her, and as her womb swells her thigh shall rot; and the woman shall be a curse and an example to all the people. But if she has not been defiled, but is clean, she shall be unharmed and shall bear children. This is the law of jealousy: if a woman turns away from her husband and is defiled, and the spirit of jealousy stirs up the husband, he shall bring her into the sight of the Lord, and the priest shall do to her according to all that is written. The husband shall be without fault, and she shall receive her iniquity."

<margin>L</margin>
# And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
"Speak to the children of Israel and you shall say to them: When a man or woman shall make a vow to be sanctified, and wish to be consecrated to the Lord, they shall abstain from wine and everything that can make one drunk. They shall not drink vinegar made from wine or any other drink, nor anything squeezed from the grape. They shall not eat fresh or dried grapes all the days they are consecrated to the Lord by vow. They shall eat nothing that can come from the vineyard, from the raisin to the stone, during the whole time of their separation. A razor shall not pass over their head until the day is fulfilled for which they are consecrated to the Lord. They shall be holy, the hair of their head growing long. All the time of their consecration they shall not go in to a dead body, nor shall they be contaminated even at the funeral of a father or mother, brother or sister, because the consecration of the Lord their God is upon their head. All the days of their separation they shall be holy to the Lord. But if anyone dies suddenly near them, the head of their consecration shall be defiled, and they shall shave it immediately on the day of their purification, and again on the seventh day. On the eighth day, however, they shall offer two turtles or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the Tabernacle of Testimony. And the priest shall make one for sin and the other for a holocaust <note>A burnt offering</note>, and shall pray for them, because they sinned over the dead. And he shall sanctify their head on that day, and shall consecrate to the Lord the days of their separation, offering a lamb of a year old for sin; yet so that the former days be made void, because their sanctification was defiled. This is the law of consecration when the days which they determined by vow shall be fulfilled: they shall bring him to the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and he shall offer his oblation to the Lord: a male lamb of a year old without blemish for a holocaust, and a ewe lamb of a year old without blemish for sin, and a ram without blemish for a peace offering, and a basket of unleavened bread tempered with oil, and wafers without leaven anointed with oil, and the libations of each. These the priest shall offer before the Lord, and shall perform both for sin and for a holocaust. But the ram he shall immolate as a peace offering to the Lord, offering at the same time the basket of unleavened bread and the libations which are due by custom. Then the Nazarite shall be shaved before the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant of the hair of his consecration; and he shall take the hair and put it upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of the peace offerings. And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall deliver them into the hands of the Nazarite. After his head is shaved, the priest shall take them back and elevate them before the Lord; and being sanctified they shall belong to the priest, like the breast which was commanded to be separated, and the thigh. After these things the Nazarite may drink wine. This is the law of the Nazarite when he has vowed his oblation to the Lord for the time of his separation, besides those things which his hand shall find. According to that which he had vowed in his mind, so shall he do for the perfection of his sanctification."

<margin>L</margin>
# And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
"Speak to Aaron and his sons: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'The Lord bless you and keep you. The Lord make His face shine upon you and be merciful to you. The Lord turn His countenance toward you and give you peace.' And they shall invoke my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them." And on the day that Moses had finished the setting up of the Tabernacle, and had erected it, and had anointed and sanctified it with all its vessels, the altar likewise and all its vessels:

<margin>O</margin>
# The leaders of Israel offered,
the heads of the families who were over each tribe, the prefects of those who had been numbered. They brought their gifts in the sight of the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen—one ox for every leader and one wagon for every two leaders—and they offered them in the sight of the Tabernacle. And the Lord said to Moses: "Receive them from them that they may serve in the ministry of the Tabernacle, and deliver them to the Levites according to the order of their ministry." Therefore, when Moses had received the wagons and the oxen, he delivered them to the Levites. Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to what they needed. Four other wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their offices and service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. But to the sons of Kohath he gave no wagons or oxen, because they serve in the sanctuary and carry their burdens on their own shoulders. Likewise the leaders offered at the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed, their offering before the altar. And the Lord said to Moses: "Let each leader on his own day offer his gifts for the dedication of the altar."

And the Lord spoke to Moses from the Tabernacle of the Covenant so that he might consult the oracle, and he heard the voice of one speaking to him from the propitiatory <note>The "mercy seat" or covering of the Ark</note> that was over the Ark of the Testimony between the two cherubim, from where he spoke to him.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you place the seven lamps, let the candlestick be set up in the southern part."
<margin>Numbers 8</margin>
### This is the precept, that the lamps should look toward the table of the bread of presence, directly opposite the area where the candlestick was meant to shine. And Aaron did so, and placed the lamps upon the candlestick, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Now, the workmanship of the candlestick was of beaten gold, both the shaft itself and whatever was produced from the gold, according to the pattern which the Lord had shown to Moses; so he fashioned the candlestick. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Take the Lev-

<column-break/>

### -ites from the midst of the children of Israel and purify them according to this rite.
Let them be sprinkled with the water of lustration <note>Water used for ritual cleansing</note>, and let them shave all the hair of their flesh when they have washed their clothes. And being cleansed, let them take an ox from the herds and its drink offering, fine flour mixed with oil; but you shall take another ox from the herd for a sin offering. And you shall bring the Levites before the Tabernacle of the Covenant, having called together the whole multitude of the children of Israel. And when the Levites are before the Lord, let the children of Israel lay their hands upon them, and let Aaron offer the Levites as a gift in the sight of the Lord from the children of Israel, so that they may serve in his ministry. The Levites shall also lay their hands upon the heads of the oxen, of which you shall make one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering of the Lord, to pray for them. And you shall stand the Levites in the sight of Aaron and his sons, and you shall consecrate them as offered to the Lord. And you shall separate them from the midst of the children of Israel so that they may be mine; and afterward they shall enter the Tabernacle of the Covenant to serve me. Thus you shall purify and consecrate them as an offering to the Lord, because they were given as a gift to me by the children of Israel; for every male who opens every womb in Israel, I have taken them. All the firstborn of the children of Israel are mine, both of men and of beasts; from the day that I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them to myself. But I took the Levites for the firstborn of the children of Israel; and I gave them as a gift to Aaron and his sons from the midst of the people, to serve me for Israel in the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and to pray for them, lest a plague come upon the people if they should dare to approach the sanctuary." And Moses and Aaron and the whole multitude of the children of Israel did to the Levites what the Lord had commanded Moses. And they were purified and washed their clothes.
And Aaron raised them in the sight of the Lord and prayed for them so that, being purified, they might enter their duties in the Tabernacle of the Covenant before Aaron and his sons. So the Lord had commanded Moses, and the Levites did so.
### The Lord also spoke to Moses, saying: "This is the law of the Levites: from twenty-five years and upward, they shall enter to minister in the Tabernacle of the Covenant. And when they have completed the fiftieth year of their age, they shall cease to serve and shall be ministers of their brothers in the Tabernacle of the Covenant to guard what has been entrusted to them, but they shall not perform the work itself. Thus you shall arrange the Levites in their watches."
<margin>Numbers 9</margin>
### The Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai, in the second year after they had gone out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying: "Let the children of Israel perform the Passover <note>original: "Phase"; the Hebrew word for Passover</note> in its time, on the fourteenth day of this month at evening, according to all its ceremonies and justifications." And Moses commanded the children of Israel to perform the Passover. They did so at its time, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, at Mount Sinai; according to all that the Lord had commanded Moses, the children of Israel did.
### But behold, certain men who were unclean because of a human soul <note>original: "super anima hominis"; meaning they had touched a dead body</note> and could not perform the Passover on that day, coming to Moses and Aaron, said to them: "We are unclean because of a human soul; why are we cheated so that we may not offer the offering to the Lord in its time among the children of Israel?" To whom Moses replied: "Stand still, that I may consult what the Lord commands concerning you."
### And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Speak to the children of Israel: The man who shall be unclean because of a soul, or far away on a journey in your nation, let him perform the Passover to the Lord in the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening. They shall eat it with unleavened bread <note>original: "azimis"</note> and wild lettuce. They shall not leave anything of it until morning, and they shall not break a bone of it. They shall observe the whole rite of the Passover. But if anyone is both clean and was not on a journey, and yet did not perform the Passover, that soul shall be cut off from his people, because he did not offer the sacrifice to the Lord in its time; he shall bear his own sin. The traveler and the stranger also, if he be among you performing the Passover of the Lord according to its ceremonies and justifications, the same precept shall be among you, for the stranger as well as for the native." Therefore, on the day the Tabernacle was erected, a cloud covered it; and from evening over the tent there was as it were the appearance of fire until morning. So it happened always: by day a cloud covered it, and by night as it were the appearance of fire. And when the cloud that protected the Tabernacle was taken up, then the children of Israel set out; in the place where the cloud had stood, there they pitched their tents. At the command of the Lord they set out, and at his command they pitched the tent. All the days that the cloud stood over the Tabernacle, they remained in the same place. And if it happened that it remained for a long time over it, the children of Israel were in the watches of the Lord and did not set out for however many days the cloud was over the Tabernacle. At the command of the Lord they erected their tents, and at his command they took them down. If the cloud had been from evening until morning, and immediately in the morning it left, they set out. And if after a day and a night it withdrew, they struck their tents. If for two days or a month or a longer time it had been over the Tabernacle, the children of Israel remained in the same place and did not set out. But as soon as it withdrew, they moved camp. By the word of the Lord they pitched their tents, and by his word they set out; and they were in the watches of the Lord according to his command by the hand of Moses.
<margin>Numbers 10</margin>
<margin>10.</margin>
### The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Make for yourself two silver trumpets of beaten work, with which you may call together the multitude when the camps are to be moved. And when you sound the trumpets, all the crowd shall gather to you at the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant. If it sounds once, the princes and the heads of the multitude of Israel shall come to you. But if a longer and broken blast sounds, those who are on the eastern side shall move camp first. At the second sound and similar wailing of the trumpet, those who dwell to the south shall lift their tents; and according to this manner the rest shall do as they wail in departure. But when the people are to be gathered, there shall be a simple sounding of the trumpets, and not a broken wailing. The sons of Aaron the priests shall sound the trumpets, and this shall be a perpetual law in your generations. If you go out to war from your land against the enemies who fight against you, you shall sound with wailing trumpets, and there shall be a remembrance of you before the Lord your God, that you may be rescued from the hands of your enemies. If whenever you have a feast and festival days, and the new moons, you shall blow the trumpets over the burnt offerings and peace victims, that they may be to you for a memorial of your God. I am the Lord your God."
### In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant. The last of all the camps to the north were the sons of Dan, whose prince was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. This was the order of the camps and the companies of the children of Israel. Under the first standards were the sons of Judah, who held the lead for the march and for their companies.

And Moses said to Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite <note>original: "raguel madianite"; Moses' father-in-law or brother-in-law</note>, his kinsman: "We are journeying to the place which the Lord will give to us. Come with us, that we may do you good, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel." But he answered him: "I will not go with you, but I will return to my own land where I was born." And Moses said: "Do not leave us, I pray you. For you know in which places we should camp in the desert, and you shall be our guide. And when you come with us, whatever is the best of the riches which the Lord shall give to us, we will give to you."

They departed from the mountain of the Lord a journey of three days, and the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord went before them for those three days, providing a place for the camp. The cloud of the Lord was also over them by day when they marched. And when the Ark was lifted up, Moses would say: "Arise, O Lord, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee from before your face." And when it was set down, he would say:
<margin>Numbers 10:35</margin> "Return, O Lord, to the multitude of the army of Israel."

Meanwhile, there arose a murmuring among the people, as of those grieving over their labor against the Lord. When Moses heard this, he was angry, and the fire of the Lord was kindled and devoured the furthest part of the camp. When the people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire was swallowed up. And he called the name of that place "Burning" <note>original: "incensio"; known as Taberah</note>, because the fire of the Lord had been kindled against them. 

The mixed crowd that had come up with them also burned with desire, sitting and weeping, joined by the children of Israel, saying: "Who will give us meat to eat? We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for free. The cucumbers come to our minds, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic. Our soul is dry; our eyes see nothing else but manna." 

Now the manna was like coriander seed, of the color of bdellium <note>original: "bdellii"; a yellowish, transparent resin</note>. The people went about and gathered it, and ground it in a mill or beat it in a mortar, cooking it in a pot and making small cakes from it, with a taste like bread made with oil. And when the dew fell upon the camp at night, the manna fell along with it. 

Therefore, Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, each man at the door of his tent. And the fury of the Lord was greatly kindled; the matter seemed intolerable to Moses, and he said to the Lord: "Why have you afflicted your servant? Why do I not find grace before you, and why have you laid the weight of all this people upon me? Did I conceive all this multitude or give birth to them, that you should say to me: 'Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse is wont to carry a little infant,' and bring them into the land for which you swore to their fathers? Where can I get meat to give to such a great multitude? They weep against me, saying: 'Give us meat that we may eat.' I cannot sustain all this heavy people alone; it is too much for me. But if it seems otherwise to you, I beseech you to kill me, that I may find grace in your eyes and not be afflicted by such great evils."

And the Lord said to Moses: "Gather for me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders and masters of the people, and lead them to the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and make them stand there with you. And I will descend and speak to you; and I will take of your spirit and give it to them, so that they may sustain the burden of the people with you, and you may not be burdened alone. You shall also say to the people: 'Sanctify yourselves; tomorrow you shall eat meat. For I have heard you saying: "Who will give us food of flesh? We were well off in Egypt." The Lord will give you meat, and you shall eat—not for one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, but even for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and turns into nausea, because you have rejected the Lord who is in your midst, and have wept before him, saying: "Why did we go out of Egypt?"'"

And Moses said to the Lord: "There are six hundred thousand footmen of this people, and you say: 'I will give them food of flesh for a whole month'? Shall a multitude of sheep and oxen be slaughtered to suffice for food, or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together to satisfy them?" 

The Lord answered him: "Is the hand of the Lord weakened? You shall see now whether my word shall be fulfilled in deed."

Moses went out and told the people the words of the Lord, gathering seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom he made to stand around the Tabernacle. And the Lord descended in a cloud and spoke to him, taking from the spirit that was in Moses and giving it to the seventy men. And when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease thereafter. 

But two men had remained in the camp, one called Eldad and the other Medad, upon whom the spirit rested. For they also had been enrolled, but had not gone out to the Tabernacle. And when they prophesied in the camp, a young man ran and told Moses, saying: "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp." Immediately Joshua, the son of Nun, the minister of Moses and chosen from many, said: "My lord Moses, forbid them." But he said: "Why are you jealous on my account? Who would grant that all the people might prophesy, and that the Lord would give them his spirit?" 

And Moses and all the elders of Israel returned to the camp. Then a wind went out from the Lord and brought quails from across the sea, and sent them into the camp for as far as a day’s journey could be made on every side around the camp. They flew in the air at a height of two cubits <note>original: "duobus cubitis"; about three feet</note> above the ground. The people rose up all that day and night and the next day, and gathered the quails, ten homers <note>original: "choros"; a large dry measure</note> per person, and they dried them around the camp. While the meat was still between their teeth and such food had not yet failed, behold, the fury of the Lord was kindled against the people, and he struck them with a very great plague. And that place was called "The Graves of Lust" <note>original: "sepulchra concupiscentiarum"; Kibroth-hattaavah</note>, for there they buried the people who had desired meat. 

Departing from the Graves of Lust, they came to Hazeroth and stayed there. And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of his Ethiopian wife <note>original: "uxorem ethyopissam"; likely referring to Zipporah or a second wife from Cush</note>, and they said: "Has the Lord spoken only through Moses? Has he not likewise spoken to us?" When the Lord heard this, he was angry. Now Moses was a man most meek, above all men who dwelt upon the earth. 

And immediately he spoke to him, and to Aaron and Miriam: "Go out, just you three, to the Tabernacle of the Covenant." And when they had gone out, the Lord descended in a column of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle, calling Aaron and Miriam. When they had gone forward, he said to them: "Hear my words. If there is a prophet of the Lord among you, I will appear to him in a vision, or I will speak to him through a dream. But it is not so with my servant Moses, who is most faithful in all my house. For I speak to him mouth to mouth, and plainly; and not through riddles and figures does he see the Lord. Why then did you not fear to detract from my servant Moses?" 

And being angry against them, he departed. The cloud also withdrew which was over the Tabernacle, and behold, Miriam appeared white with leprosy like snow. When Aaron looked back and saw her covered in leprosy, he said to Moses: "I beseech you, my lord, do not impose upon us this sin which we have foolishly committed, lest she become as one dead, and like an abortion that is cast out from its mother's womb. Behold, already

<column-break/>

half of her flesh is devoured by leprosy." And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying: "O Lord, I beseech you, heal her." The Lord answered him: "If her father had spit in her face, should she not have been covered in shame for at least seven days? Let her be separated for seven days outside the camp, and afterwards she shall be called back." So Miriam was shut out for seven days outside the camp, and the people did not move from that place until Miriam was called back.

The people set out from Hazeroth and pitched their tents in the desert of Paran. There the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Send men to view the land of Canaan, which I will give to the children of Israel, one from each tribe, from among the princes." 

Moses sent the leading men from the desert of Paran according to the command of the Lord, whose names are these:
<margin>Numbers 13</margin> From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur. From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori. From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh. From the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph. From the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea <note>original: "ossee"; later renamed Joshua</note> son of Nun. From the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu. From the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi. From the tribe of Joseph, of the scepter of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi. From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli. From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael. From the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi. From the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi. 

These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to view the land; and Moses called Hoshea, the son of Nun, Joshua. Moses sent them to view the land of Canaan and said to them: "Go up by the southern region. And when you come to the mountains, consider the land, what it is like, and the people who are its inhabitants: whether they are strong or weak, few in number or many; whether the land itself is good or bad; what kind of cities they are, walled or without walls; whether the soil is rich or barren, wooded or without trees. Be of good courage, and bring us some of the fruits of the land." 

Now it was the time when the first-ripe grapes could be eaten. And when they had gone up, they explored the land from the desert of Zin as far as Rehob, as one enters Hamath. And they went up to the south and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the sons of Anak, were. For Hebron was built seven years before Zoan, a city of Egypt. 

Proceeding as far as the Valley of the Cluster <note>original: "torrentem botri"; Eshcol</note>, they cut off a branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs from that place, which was called Nehelle Escol, that is, the Valley of the Cluster, because the children of Israel had carried a cluster of grapes from there. 

The explorers of the land returned after forty days, having circled the whole region. They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole assembly of the children of Israel in the desert of Paran, which is in Kadesh. 
<margin>Numbers 13:27</margin> They spoke to them and to the whole multitude, showed them the fruit of the land, and told their story, saying: "We came to the land to which you sent us, which truly flows with milk and honey, as can be known from these fruits. But it has very fierce inhabitants, and the cities are great and walled. We saw the race of Anak there. Amalek dwells in the south; the Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the mountains; while the Canaanite stays by the sea and around the streams of the Jordan."

Amidst this, Caleb, quieting the murmuring of the people that was rising against Moses, said: "Let us go up and possess the land, for we shall be able to obtain it." But the others who had been with him said: "By no means are we able to go up against this people, because they are stronger than we." And they spoke ill of the land they had viewed among the children of Israel, saying: "The land which we passed through devours its inhabitants; and the people whom we beheld are of tall stature. There we saw certain monsters, the sons of Anak of the race of giants, compared to whom we seemed like locusts."

Therefore the whole crowd, crying out, wept that night. And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: "Would that we had died in Egypt, and not in this vast wilderness! Would that we might perish, and that the Lord would not lead us into this land, lest we fall by the sword, and our wives and children be led away as captives. Is it not better to return to Egypt?" And they said to one another: "Let us appoint a leader for ourselves and return to Egypt."

Hearing this, Moses and Aaron fell prone on the ground before the whole multitude of the children of Israel. But Joshua, the son of Nun, and Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, who had also surveyed the land, tore their garments and spoke to the whole multitude of the children of Israel: "The land which we circled is very good. If the Lord is favorable, he will lead us into it and give us a soil flowing with milk and honey. Do not be rebellious against the Lord, nor fear the people of this land, for we can devour them like bread. All protection has departed from them; the Lord is with us, do not fear."

When the whole multitude cried out and wanted to overwhelm them with stones, the glory of the Lord appeared over the Tabernacle of the Covenant to all the children of Israel. And the Lord said to Moses: "How long will this people detract from me? How long will they not believe me, despite all the signs I have performed before them? I will strike them with a pestilence and consume them; but I will make you a prince over a great nation, and one stronger than this is." 

<margin>Numbers 14:13</margin> And Moses said to the Lord: "That the Egyptians may hear, from whose midst you led out this people, and the inhabitants of this land, who have heard that you, O Lord, are among this people, and are seen face to face, and that your cloud stays over them, and that you go before them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of fire by night; if you kill such a great multitude as if they were one man, they will say: 'He could not lead the people into the land for which he had sworn; therefore he killed them in the wilderness.' Let the strength of the Lord be magnified, as you have sworn, saying: 'The Lord is patient and of great mercy, taking away iniquity and crimes, and leaving no one innocent, who visits the sins of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.' Forgive, I beseech you, the sin of this people according to the greatness of your mercy, just as you have been favorable to them from their departure from Egypt until this place."

And the Lord said: "I have forgiven according to your word. As I live, and as the glory of the Lord shall fill the whole earth, yet all those men who have seen my majesty and the signs which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now ten times, and have not obeyed my voice, they shall not see the land for which I swore to their fathers; nor shall anyone from those who spoke ill of me see it. My servant Caleb, who, being full of another spirit, has followed me, I will lead into this land which he circled, and his seed shall possess it. Because the Amalekites and Canaanites dwell in the valleys, tomorrow move the camp and return to the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea."

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: "How long does this wicked multitude murmur against me? I have heard the complaints of the children of Israel. Say therefore to them: 'As I live, says the Lord, just as you have spoken in my hearing, so will I do to you. In this wilderness shall your carcasses lie. All of you who were numbered from twenty years and upwards, and have murmured against me, shall not enter the land over which I lifted my hand to make you dwell, except for Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, of whom you said they would be a prey for the enemies, I will lead in, that they may see the land which displeased you. Your carcasses shall lie in the wilderness; your children shall be wanderers in the desert for forty years, and shall bear your wandering <note>original: "fornicationem"; often used biblically to describe unfaithfulness or spiritual wandering</note> until the carcasses of their fathers are consumed in the desert. According to the number of the forty days in which you viewed the land, a year shall be counted for a day, and for forty years you shall receive your iniquities, and you shall know my vengeance. For as I have spoken, so will I do to all this wicked multitude which has risen up against me.'"

<summary>This page recounts the Israelites' journey from Sinai to the borders of Canaan, marked by divine guidance and human rebellion. It details the complaints about food, the appointment of seventy elders, the scouting of the Promised Land, and God's judgment sentencing the generation to forty years in the wilderness.</summary>

**T**he Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land of your habitation which I will give you, and make an offering to the Lord as a burnt offering <term>holocaustum: a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire</term> or a peace offering, fulfilling vows, or spontaneously offering gifts, or in your solemnities burning a sweet aroma to the Lord from the oxen or from the sheep: whoever immolates the victim shall offer a similar sacrifice: a tenth part of an ephah <note>about 2.2 liters</note> of flour sprinkled with oil that has the measure of a fourth part of a hin <note>about 1 liter</note>; and he shall give wine for the libations to be poured of the same measure for the burnt offering or for the victim. For every lamb and ram, there shall be a similar sacrifice of two-tenths of flour sprinkled with oil of a third part of a hin; and he shall offer wine for the libations, a third part of the same measure, as a sweet aroma to the Lord. When, however, he makes a burnt offering or a victim from the oxen to fulfill a vow or peace offerings, he shall give for each ox a similar offering of three-tenths <note>original: "cerei decimam" likely a scribal error for "tres decimas"</note> of flour sprinkled with half a measure of a hin of oil; and wine for the libations of the same measure as a sweet aroma to the Lord. **T**he Lord spoke to Aaron: "Behold, I have given you the guard of my firstfruits. All things that are sanctified by the children of Israel I have delivered to you and your sons for the priestly office as a perpetual law. These things therefore you shall receive from those which are sanctified and have been offered to the Lord. Every offering and sacrifice, and whatever is rendered to me for sin and offense and yields to the holy of holies, shall be yours and your sons'. You shall eat it in the sanctuary. Only males shall eat of it, because it is consecrated to you. But the firstfruits which the children of Israel have vowed and offered, I have given to you and your sons and your daughters by a perpetual right. Whoever is clean in your house shall eat them. All the marrow of oil and wine and grain, and whatever firstfruits they offer to the Lord, I have given to you. All the firstfruits of the crops which the ground produces and are brought to the Lord shall yield to your uses. Whoever is clean in your house shall eat them. Everything that the children of Israel render by vow shall be yours. Whatever first breaks from the womb of all flesh which they offer to the Lord, whether it be of men or of cattle, shall be your right; provided that for a firstborn man you receive a price, and every animal that is unclean you cause to be redeemed; the redemption of which shall be after one month for five shekels <note>original: "siclis"</note> of silver, by the weight of the sanctuary. A shekel has twenty obols <note>original: "obolos"; here meaning gerahs</note>. But the firstborn of an ox and a sheep and a goat you shall not cause to be redeemed, because they are sanctified to the Lord. Only their blood shall you pour upon the altar, and the fat you shall burn as a most sweet aroma to the Lord. But the flesh shall fall to your use, just as the consecrated breast and the right shoulder shall be yours. All the firstfruits of the sanctuary which the children of Israel offer to the Lord, I have given to you and your sons and daughters..."

# **T**he Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: This is the religious rite of the victim which the Lord has established for his brother.

<margin>
Command the children of Israel that they bring to you a red heifer <term>red heifer (vacca rufa): a rare animal used in a purification ritual to cleanse those who had come into contact with the dead</term> of full age, in which there is no blemish, and which has not borne a yoke. You shall give her to Eleazar the priest, who, having led her outside the camp, shall immolate her in the sight of all. And dipping his finger in her blood, he shall sprinkle it against the doors of the tabernacle seven times. And he shall burn her while all are watching, her skin and flesh as well as her blood and dung being delivered to the flames. The priest shall also cast cedar wood, hyssop, and twice-dyed scarlet into the flame that devours the heifer. And then at last, having washed his clothes and his body, he shall enter the camp, and he shall be unclean until evening. But he also who burned her shall wash his clothes and body and shall be unclean until evening. A clean man shall collect the ashes of the heifer and pour them outside the camp in a very clean place, so that they may be for the multitude of the children of Israel for safekeeping and for the water of sprinkling, because the heifer was burned for sin. And when he who carried the ashes of the heifer has washed his clothes, he shall be unclean until evening. The children of Israel and the strangers who dwell among them shall have this as a perpetual right. Whoever touches the corpse of a man shall be unclean for seven days. He shall be sprinkled with this water on the third and seventh day, and he shall be cleansed. If he is not sprinkled on the third day, he cannot be cleansed on the seventh. Everyone who touches the dead body of a human soul and is not sprinkled with this water pollutes the tabernacle of the Lord and shall perish from Israel. Because the water of expiation was not sprinkled on him, he shall be unclean and his filthiness shall remain upon him. This is the law for a man who dies in a tabernacle: all who enter his tent and all the vessels that are there shall be polluted for seven days. A vessel that has no lid or fastening upon it shall be unclean. If anyone in a field touches the corpse of a slain man, or one who died of himself, or his bone, or a grave, he shall be unclean for seven days. They shall take of the ashes of the burning for sin and put living waters upon them in a vessel. In which, when a clean man has dipped hyssop, he shall sprinkle from it the whole tent and all the furniture and the men polluted by such contagion; and in this way he shall purify the unclean on the third and seventh day. And having been expiated on the seventh day, he shall wash himself and his clothes, and he shall be unclean until evening. If anyone has not been expiated by this rite, his soul shall perish from the midst of the church, because he has polluted the sanctuary of the Lord and the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him. This shall be a legitimate and everlasting precept. Also he who sprinkles the water shall wash his clothes. Everyone who touches the water of expiation shall be unclean until evening. Whatever an unclean person touches, he shall make unclean; and the soul that touches any of these things shall be unclean until evening.

Moses also spoke to the princes of the tribes of the sons of Israel: "This is the word which the Lord has commanded. If any man vows a vow to the Lord, or binds himself by an oath, he shall not make his word void, but shall fulfill all that he promised. If a woman in her father's house and in the age of girlhood vows a vow to the Lord or binds herself by an oath, if her father hears the vow she promised and the oath by which she bound her soul, and remains silent, she shall be liable for the vow; whatever she promised and pledged by oath she shall fulfill. But if immediately as he hears it he contradicts her, both her vows and her oaths shall be void, nor shall she be held liable to the promise, because her father contradicted it. If she has a husband and vows something, and once the word has gone out of her mouth binding her soul by an oath, if the husband hears and does not contradict it, she shall be liable for the vow and shall render what she promised. But if as soon as he hears it he contradicts it and makes her promises void, and the words by which she bound her soul, the Lord will be merciful to her.

Widows and divorced women shall render whatever they have vowed. A wife in the house of a husband, when she has bound herself by a vow and an oath, if the husband hears and remains silent and does not contradict the promise, she shall render whatever she promised. But if he immediately contradicts it, she shall not be held liable for the promise, because the husband contradicted it, and the Lord will be merciful to her. If they have vowed and bound themselves by an oath to afflict the soul through fasting or other abstinence from things, it shall be in the choice of the husband whether she should do it or not do it. But if the husband hears and remains silent and defers his judgment to another day, she shall render whatever she had vowed and promised, because as soon as he heard it, he was silent. But if he contradicts it after he has known of it, he himself shall bear her iniquity." These are the laws which the Lord established for Moses between a husband and wife, and between a father and daughter who is still in the age of girlhood or who remains in the father's house.
