Moses answered them: "Shall your brothers go to the battle while you sit here? Why do you subvert the minds of the children of Israel, so they do not dare to cross into the place which the Lord will give them? Did not your fathers do the same when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to explore the land? When they came to the Valley of the Cluster <note>original: "uallem botri"; referring to Eshcol</note> and surveyed the whole region, they discouraged the hearts of the children of Israel so they would not enter the borders the Lord had given them. The Lord swore in His anger on that day: 'If these men who came up from Egypt from twenty years old and upward shall see the land which I promised under oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—for they have not followed me, except for Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua the son of Nun; these have fulfilled my will.' And the Lord, being angry against Israel, led them through the desert for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in His sight was consumed. And behold," he said, "you have risen up in place of your fathers, an increase and offspring of sinful men, to increase the fury of the Lord against Israel. If you will not follow Him, He will leave the people in the wilderness, and you will be the cause of the death of all."

But they, approaching closer, said: "We will build folds for the sheep and stables for the cattle, and fortified cities for our little ones. But we ourselves will proceed armed and girded to the battle before the children of Israel until we bring them into their places. Our little ones shall stay in fortified cities because of the ambushes of the inhabitants. We will not return to our houses until the children of Israel possess their inheritance; nor will we seek anything beyond the Jordan, since our possession is already here in the eastern region."

Moses said to them: "If you do what you promise—equipped before the Lord for battle, and every armed warrior crosses the Jordan until the Lord subverts His enemies and all the land is subjected to Him—then you shall be blameless before the Lord and before Israel, and you shall obtain the regions you desire before the Lord. But if you do not do what you say, there is no doubt that you sin against the Lord; and know that your sin shall find you out. Build therefore cities for your little ones, and folds and stables for your sheep and cattle, and fulfill what you have promised." And the children of Gad and Reuben said to Moses: "We are your servants; we will do what our lord commands. Our little ones, wives, flocks, and cattle we will leave in the cities of Gilead; but we your servants, all equipped, will proceed to war as you, our lord, speak." <margin>10.</margin>

**M**oses commanded Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the princes of the families of the tribes of Israel, saying to them: "If the children of Gad and 

<column-break/>

the children of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed for war before the Lord, and the land is subjected to you, give them Gilead as a possession. But if they will not cross with you into the land of Canaan, let them receive places to dwell among you." The children of Gad and Reuben answered: "As the Lord has spoken to His servants, so we will do. We will proceed armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and let our possession be confirmed to us across the Jordan."

So Moses gave to the children of Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and that land with its cities all around. The children of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, Sophan, Jaser, Jogbehah, Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran: fortified cities and folds for their flocks. The children of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim, Nebo, and Baal-meon (their names being changed), and Sibmah; they gave names to the cities they built. Furthermore, the children of Machir son of Manasseh went into Gilead and wasted it, killing the Amorite inhabitant there. Moses gave the land of Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, who dwelt in it. Jair the son of Manasseh went and occupied its villages, which he called Havoth-jair, that is, the villages of Jair. Nobah also went and captured Kenath with its villages, and called it Nobah after his own name.

These are the stations <note>original: "mansiones"; the resting places or stages of a journey</note> of the children of Israel who went out of Egypt by their ranks under the hand of Moses and Aaron, which Moses described according to the places of their camps. Having set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the month, on the day after the Passover, the children of Israel went out with an uplifted hand, in the sight of all the Egyptians who were burying their firstborn whom the Lord had struck. For the Lord had also executed vengeance upon their gods. They camped in Succoth; and from Succoth they came to Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness. From there they went toward Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol. Having set out from Pi-hahiroth, they passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness; and walking for three days through the desert of Etham, they camped in Marah. Setting out from Marah, they came to Elim, where there were twelve fountains of water and seventy palm trees; and there they camped.

But setting out from there, they pitched their tents by the Red Sea. Setting out from the Red Sea, they camped in the wilderness of Sin. From there they went to Dophkah. Setting out from Dophkah, they camped in Alush. Leaving Alush, they pitched their tents in Rephidim, where the people lacked water to drink. Setting out from Rephidim, they camped in the wilderness of Sinai. Leaving the wilderness of Sinai, they came to the Graves of Lust <note>original: "sepulcra concupiscentie"; Kibroth-hattaavah</note>. Setting out from the Graves of Lust, they camped in Hazeroth; and from Hazeroth they came to Rithmah. Setting out from Rithmah, they camped in Rimmon-perez. Leaving there, they came to Libnah; and from Libnah they camped in Rissah. Leaving Rissah, they came to Kehelathah. In that place they camped at Mount Shepher. Leaving Mount Shepher, they came to Haradah. From there they set out and camped in Makheloth. Setting out from Makheloth, they came to Tahath; from Tahath they camped in Terah. Leaving there, they pitched tents in Mithcah. From Mithcah, they camped in Hashmonah. Setting out from Hashmonah, they came to Moseroth; and from Moseroth they came to Bene-jaakan. Setting out from Bene-jaakan, they came to Mount Gidgad. From there they set out and camped in Jotbathah; and from Jotbathah they came to Abronah. Leaving Abronah, they camped in Ezion-geber. From there they set out and came to the wilderness of Zin; this is Kadesh. And setting out from Kadesh, they camped at Mount Hor on the edge of the borders of Edom.

And Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor at the command of the Lord, and there he died in the fortieth year of the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month, when he was one hundred and twenty-three years old. And the Canaanite king Arad, who dwelt to the south in the land of Canaan, heard that the children of Israel had come. Setting out from Mount Hor, they camped in Zalmonah; from there they went to Punon. Setting out from Punon, they camped in Oboth; and from Oboth they came to Iye-abarim, which is on the borders of the Moabites. Setting out from Iye-abarim, they pitched tents in Dibon-gad. Leaving there, they camped in Almon-diblathaim. And from Almon-diblathaim they came to the mountains of Abarim facing Nebo. Setting out from the mountains of Abarim, they came to the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho; and there they camped from Beth-jeshimoth even to Abel-shittim in the level places of the Moabites. <insert>2</insert>

**T**he Lord spoke to Moses: "Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land of Canaan, you shall drive out all the inhabitants of that region, breaking their statues and destroying all their high places. You shall lay waste to the land and dwell in it. For I have given it to you as a possession by lot. To the more numerous you shall give a wider portion, and to the fewer a narrower one. As the lot falls to each, so shall the inheritance be granted; the possession shall be divided by tribes and families. But if you will not kill the inhabitants, those who remain will be like nails in your eyes and spears in your sides; and they shall oppose you in the land of your habitation. And whatever I had thought to do to them, I will do to you," says the Lord. <margin>10.</margin>

**T**he Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you enter the way of Canaan, and it falls to you as a possession by lot, it shall be enclosed by these borders. The southern part shall begin from the wilderness of Zin which is next to Edom, and it shall have as its boundary the Salt Sea to the east, which shall curve to the southern side by the ascent of the Scorpion <note>original: "ascensum scorpionis"; Maaleh-acrabbim</note>, so that it passes into Zin and reaches the south at Kadesh Barnea. From there the borders shall go out to the village named Addar and extend to Azmon. From Azmon the boundary shall go in a circle to the Torrent of Egypt and finish at the shore of the Great Sea. The western region begins from the Great Sea and is enclosed by that limit. Furthermore, to the northern side, the borders shall begin from the Great Sea reaching to the highest mountain, coming into Hamath as far as the borders of Zedad. The boundaries shall go as far as Ziphron and the village of Enan. These shall be the limits in the north. From there you shall measure the border to the eastern side from the village of Enan to Shepham; and from Shepham the boundaries shall descend into Riblah facing the fountain of Daphne. From there they shall reach toward the east to the Sea of Chinnereth <note>Sea of Galilee</note>, and finally to the Jordan, and at last be enclosed by the Salt Sea. You shall have this land by its borders all around."

Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: "This shall be the land which you shall possess by lot, and which the Lord commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe. For the tribe of the sons of Reuben by their families, and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to the number of their kinships, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—that is, two and a half tribes—have received their portion across the Jordan across from Jericho toward the east." Moses said: "These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and one prince from each tribe, whose names are these..."

**T**hese are the cities which shall be given to the Levites from the possessions of the children of Israel, along with their suburbs. Their dimensions shall be measured as follows: from the city walls outward toward the east there shall be two thousand cubits, and toward the south two thousand. Toward the west also and toward the north the same measure shall be set. These shall be cities for habitation and their suburbs. Among those you give to the Levites, six shall be designated as refuges for fugitives, so that anyone who has shed blood may flee to them; and besides these, forty-eight other suburban towns. Of those given from the possessions of the children of Israel, more shall be taken from those who have more, and fewer from those who have less; each shall give towns to the Levites according to the measure of their inheritance. 35.

**R**egarding redemption, the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When you have entered the land of Canaan, determine which cities ought to be refuges for fugitives who have unintentionally shed blood. In these, when the fugitive arrives, the kinsman of the slain <note>the "Avenger of Blood"</note> shall not be able to kill him until he stands before the multitude and his case is judged. Of the cities separated for the refuge of fugitives, three shall be across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They are for the children of Israel as well as for strangers and pilgrims, so that whoever has shed blood unintentionally may flee to them. 35.

**I**f anyone strikes with an iron tool and the one struck dies, he is guilty of murder and shall himself die. If he throws a stone and the person dies from the blow, he shall be punished similarly. If he strikes with wood and death follows, he shall pay with his blood. The relative of the slain shall kill the murderer; as soon as he catches him, he shall strike him. If out of hatred someone pushes a person, or lays any trap, or throws something at him, and the person dies, the striker is guilty of murder. The kinsman of the slain shall kill him as soon as he finds him. But if by chance, and without hatred or enmity, he does any of these things, and this is proven before the people, and the question is debated between the striker and the relative of the blood, the innocent man shall be delivered from the hand of the avenger and brought back to the city to which he fled; and he shall remain there until the High Priest, who was anointed with the holy oil, dies. If he is found outside the borders of the cities separated for exiles and is struck down by the seeker of blood, it shall be without guilt; however, when the High Priest dies, the fugitive shall then return to his own land. After the High Priest dies, the manslayer shall return to his land. These shall be everlasting and legal statutes in all your dwellings. A murderer shall be punished only on the evidence of witnesses. No one shall be condemned on the testimony of only one person. You shall not accept a price <note>a ransom</note> from him who is guilty of blood, for he himself must die. Those born there and those in exile cannot return to their own city before the death of the High Priest. Do not pollute the house of your dwelling; the land is defiled by the blood of the innocent, and it cannot be expiated for the blood shed except by the blood of the one who shed it. Thus your possession shall be cleansed while I dwell with you. For I am the Lord who dwells among the children of Israel. 35.

**T**hen the heads of the families of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the stock of the sons of Joseph, approached and spoke before the leaders of Israel, saying: The Lord commanded you, our lord, to divide the land by lot to the children of Israel and to give the possession of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters. If men of another tribe take them as wives, their possession will follow them, and being transferred to another tribe, our inheritance will be diminished. And so it will happen that when the Jubilee—that is, the fiftieth year of remission—arrives, the division of all will be confused and the possession of some will pass to others. Moses answered the children of Israel, as the Lord commanded, saying: The daughters of Joseph have spoken rightly. This is the law promulgated by the Lord regarding the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whom they wish, provided it is to men of their own tribe, so that the possession of the children of Israel does not shift from tribe to tribe. For all men shall take wives from their own tribe and kinship, and all women shall take husbands from the same tribe, so that the inheritance remains within families and the tribes do not mix, but remain as they were established by the Lord. And the daughters of Zelophehad did as had been commanded. Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah married the sons of their uncles from the family of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph; and the possession assigned to them remained in the tribe and family of their father. These are the commandments and judgments which the Lord commanded through the hand of Moses to the children of Israel in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.

But you would not go up; instead, being incredulous of the word of the Lord your God, you murmured in your tents and said: "The Lord hates us, and therefore he led us out of the land of Egypt to deliver us into the hand of the Amorite and destroy us. The messengers have terrified our hearts, saying: 'The multitude is very great and taller in stature than we are; the cities are large and fortified up to heaven; we saw the sons of Anak there.'" And I answered you: Do not fear, nor be afraid of them. The Lord your God, who is your leader, will himself fight for you just as he did in Egypt before your eyes. And in the wilderness you yourselves saw how he carried you through the whole way you walked until you came to this place. Yet even so, you did not believe the Lord your God, who went before you on the way and marked out the place where you should pitch your tents, showing you fire by night and a pillar of cloud by day. To Machir also I gave Gilead; and to the tribes of Reuben and Gad I gave the land of Gilead as far as the torrent Arnon, the middle of the torrent and the border, even to the torrent Jabbok which is the border of the children of Ammon; and the plain of the wilderness and the Jordan, and the borders of Chinnereth <note>Latin: Ienereth</note> even to the sea of the desert, which is most salt, at the foot of mount Pisgah <note>Latin: Phasga</note> toward the east. I spoke to you at that time, saying: "The Lord your God has given you this land for an inheritance. You men of strength, go prepared before your brothers, the children of Israel, all of you, except for your wives and little ones and cattle. For I know that you have much livestock; and they ought to remain in the cities I have given you, until the Lord gives rest to your brothers as He has given to you, so that they also may possess the land which He is about to give them across the Jordan. Then each one shall return to his possession which I have given you." I also commanded Joshua at that time: "Your eyes have seen what the Lord your God did to these two kings; so shall He do to all the kingdoms into which you are about to pass. Do not fear them, for the Lord your God will fight for you."

**I** prayed to the Lord at that time, saying: "Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your most powerful hand. For there is no other God in heaven or on earth who can do your works and compare to your strength. Let me cross over, therefore, and see this excellent land across the Jordan, and this extraordinary mountain, and Lebanon." But the Lord was angry because of you and did not hear me, but said to me: "It is enough for you; do not speak to me further about this matter. Go up to the top of Pisgah and cast your eyes around to the west and the north, the south and the east, and look. For you shall not cross this Jordan. Command Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he himself shall go before this people, and he shall divide for them the land which you see." And we stayed in the valley opposite the temple of Peor <note>Latin: Phogor</note>.

And you shall know that the Lord your God himself is the strong and faithful God, keeping covenant and mercy for those who love him and for those who keep his precepts for a thousand generations: and repaying those who hate him immediately, so that he destroys them, and delays no further, immediately repaying what they deserve.

**The** commandment which I command you today is not above you, nor placed far off, as if one might say frequently: no one can possess the losses which are not even placed in heaven. So that you could say: Who of us can ascend to heaven that he may bring it to us, so that we may hear it and complete it in work? Nor is it placed beyond the sea, that you should say again: Who of us can cross the sea entering or... and bring it back to us, so that we may hear and do what is commanded? And the people being gathered together, as well men as women, children and strangers who are within your gates: that hearing they may learn and fear the Lord your God, and keep and fulfill all the words of this law. Their children also who are now ignorant, that they may be able to hear and fear the Lord their God all the days in which you live in the land to which you shall go, crossing the Jordan, to possess it. All evils <margin>verse 31e.</margin> and afflictions shall find them, so that they say in that day: Truly because God is not with me, these evils have found me. Now therefore write for yourselves this song, and teach it to the children of Israel, that they may hold it in memory and sing it with their mouth. Give magnificence to our God. The works of God are perfect, and all his ways are judgments. A faithful God, and without any iniquity, just and right. They have sinned against him, and not his sons in filthiness: a wicked and perverse generation. Do you thus repay the Lord, O foolish and unwise people? When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam: he appointed the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. But the Lord's part is his people: Jacob the line of his inheritance. He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror and of vast solitude. He led him about, and taught him, and kept him as the apple of his eye. As an eagle provoking her young to fly, and hovering over them, he expanded his wings, and took him, and carried him on his shoulders. The Lord alone was his leader, and there was no foreign god with him. He set him upon <margin>verse 32e.</margin> the high land, that he might eat the fruits of the fields: that he might suck honey from the rock, and oil from the hardest stone. Butter from the herd, and milk from the sheep with the fat of lambs, and of rams of the sons of Bashan, and goats with the marrow of wheat: and that he might drink the purest blood of the grape. The beloved was grown fat, and kicked. Fat, thick, and expanded. He forsook God his maker, and departed from God his savior. They provoked him in foreign gods, and in abominations they stirred him to anger. They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know. New and recent ones came, whom their fathers did not worship. You have forsaken the God who begot you, and have forgotten the Lord your creator. The Lord saw, and <margin>verse 32e.</margin> was stirred to anger, because his sons and daughters provoked him. And he said: I will hide my face from them, and I will consider their last end. For it is a perverse generation, and unfaithful children. They have provoked me in that which was not a god, and have irritated me in their vanities. And I will provoke them in that which is not a people, and in a foolish nation I will irritate them. A fire is kindled in my fury, and shall burn even to the lowest hell. And it shall devour the earth with its growth, and shall burn the foundations of the mountains. <margin>verse 32e.</margin> I will gather evils upon them, and I will complete my arrows in them. They shall be consumed with famine, and birds shall devour them with a most bitter bite. I will send the teeth of beasts upon them, with the fury of those dragging upon the earth and of serpents. Outside the sword shall waste them, and inside terror. The young man and the virgin together, the suckling with the old man. I said: Where are they? I will make the memory of them to cease from men. But because of the wrath of the enemies <margin>verse 32e.</margin> I deferred it: lest perhaps their enemies should be proud and say: Our high hand, and not the Lord, has done all these things. A nation without counsel it is, and without prudence. Would that they were wise and understood, and provided for their last end. How should one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Is it not because their God sold them, and the Lord shut them up? For our God is not as their gods, and our enemies are the judges. Their vine is of the vine of the Sodomites, and of the suburbs of Gomorrah. Their grape is a grape of gall, and most bitter clusters. Their wine is the gall of dragons, and the incurable poison of asps. Are not these things stored up with me, and sealed in my treasures? Revenge is mine, and I will repay them in time, so that their foot may slide. The day of perdition is at hand, and the times hasten to be present. The Lord will judge his people, and will have mercy on his servants. He shall see <margin>verse 32e.</margin> that the hand is weakened, and the shut up also have failed, and the residue are consumed. And he shall say: Where are their gods in whom they had confidence? Of whose victims they ate the fat, and drank the wine of libations. <margin>verse 32e.</margin> Let them rise up and help you, and protect you in necessity. See that I am alone, and there is no other god besides me. I will kill, and I will make to live. I will strike, and I will heal. And there is no one who can deliver out of my hand. I will lift up my hand to heaven, and I will say: I live forever. <margin>verse 32e.</margin> If I whet my sword as the lightning, and my hand take hold on judgment: I will render vengeance to my enemies, and will repay those who hate me. <margin>verse 32e.</margin> I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and from the captivity, of the naked <margin>verse 32e.</margin> head of the enemies. Praise his people, O nations: because he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance upon their enemies, and will be merciful to the land of his people.

...two stone tablets like the first ones. And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, except that you fear the Lord your God, walk in his ways, love him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul? For the Lord your God himself is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, powerful, and terrible God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes. He brings justice to the orphan and the widow; he loves the foreigner <note>Original: "peregrinum," referring to a resident alien or traveler.</note> and gives him food and clothing. And you, therefore, must love foreigners, because you yourselves were strangers in the land of Egypt. You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him alone; you shall cling to him and swear by his name. He is your praise and your God, who performed for you these great and terrible things which your eyes have seen. With seventy souls your fathers went down into Egypt; and behold, now the Lord your God has multiplied you like the stars of heaven. Therefore, love the Lord your God, and observe his precepts and ceremonies, his judgments and commandments at all times. Recognize today what your children do not know—those who did not see the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, his strong hand and outstretched arm, the signs and works he did in the midst of Egypt to Pharaoh the king and to all his land, and to the entire army of the Egyptians, to their horses and chariots; how he covered them with the waters of the Red Sea when they were pursuing you, and how he destroyed them to this day; and what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place; and to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, whom the earth swallowed with its mouth open, along with their houses and tents and all the substance they had in the midst of Israel. Your eyes have seen all the great works the Lord has done, so that they might keep all his commandments which I command you today, that you may be able to enter and possess the land into which you are going, and live in it for a long time—the land which the Lord promised under oath to your fathers and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey. For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, where, after the seed was sown, waters were brought in to irrigate it like a garden. But it is a land of mountains and plains, waiting for rain from heaven, which the Lord your God always watches over; his eyes are upon it from the beginning to the end of the year. If, therefore, you obey my commandments which I command you today, to love the Lord your God and serve him with all your heart and all your soul, I will give rain to your land in its season, the early and the late rain, so that you may gather your grain, wine, and oil; and hay from the fields to feed your cattle, and that you yourselves may eat and be satisfied. Beware lest perhaps your heart be deceived and you turn away from the Lord to serve foreign gods and worship them; and the Lord, being angry, closes the heaven so that rain does not fall, and the earth does not give its sprout, and you perish quickly from the excellent land which the Lord is about to give to you. Place these words in your hearts and in your souls; hang them as a sign on your hands and place them between your eyes. Teach them to your children so they may meditate on them when you sit in your house, walk on the path, lie down, and rise up. Write them upon the posts and doors of your house, so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give them as long as the heaven hangs over the earth. For if you keep the commandments I command you and do them—to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, clinging to him—the Lord will scatter all these nations before your face, and you shall possess those who are greater and stronger than you. Every place your foot treads shall be yours. From the desert and Lebanon, from the great river Euphrates to the western sea shall be your borders. No one shall stand against you. The Lord your God shall put the terror and fear of you upon all the land you are to tread, just as he spoke to you. Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse. A blessing if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you; a curse if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God and turn away from the path I show you, following foreign gods you do not know. When the Lord your God has brought you into the land you are going to inhabit, you shall place the blessing upon Mount Gerizim and the curse upon Mount Ebal, which are across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the setting sun in the land of the Canaanite who lives in the plains, opposite Gilgal, which is near the valley stretching far away. For you shall cross the Jordan to possess the land the Lord your God is giving you, to have and possess it. See therefore that you fulfill the ceremonies and judgments which I set before you today.

<margin>Deuteronomy 8</margin>
**When** you have eaten and are satisfied, bless the Lord your God for the excellent land he has given you. Beware that you never forget the Lord your God, and neglect his commandments, judgments, and ceremonies which I command you today; lest after you have eaten and are satisfied, have built beautiful houses and lived in them, and have herds and flocks of sheep, and an abundance of silver and gold and all things, your heart be lifted up and you do not remember the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt and the house of slavery. He was your leader in the great and terrible wilderness, in which there was the serpent with the burning breath, and the scorpion, and the parched land <note>Original: "dipsas," a type of serpent whose bite was thought to cause intense thirst.</note> where there was no water at all. He brought streams out of the hardest rock and fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know. And after he afflicted and tested you, in the end he had mercy on you. Do not say in your heart: "My own strength and the power of my hand have provided all these things for me." But remember the Lord your God, that he himself provided strength for you, to fulfill his covenant which he swore to your fathers, as this present day shows.

<margin>Deuteronomy 12</margin>

Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat them; the clean and the unclean shall eat together. Only beware that you do not eat the blood. For their blood is the life <note>Original: "anima," meaning soul or life-force.</note>. Therefore you must not eat the life with the meat; but pour it upon the earth like water. Do not drink it, so that it may be well with you and your children after you, if you do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord. Nevertheless, your sacred things and what you have vowed to the Lord, you shall take and come to the place the Lord chooses; and you shall offer your oblations, meat, and blood upon the altar of the Lord your God. You shall pour the blood of the sacrifices on the altar, but you yourself shall eat the meat. Observe and hear all that I command you, so that it may be well with you and your children after you forever, when you do what is good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God. When the Lord your God has destroyed before your face the nations you are entering to possess, and you possess them and live in them, beware that you do not imitate them after they have been overthrown. Do not seek their ceremonies, saying: "As these nations worshipped their gods, so I will also worship." You shall not do likewise to the Lord your God. For they have done to their gods all the abominations which the Lord hates, even offering their sons and daughters and burning them with fire. What I command you, do this only for the Lord; do not add anything or take anything away.

<margin>Deuteronomy 13</margin>
**If** there arises among you a prophet or one who has seen a dream, and he predicts a sign or a wonder, and what he spoke comes to pass, and he says to you: "Let us go and follow foreign gods whom you do not know, and let us serve them," you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer. For the Lord your God is testing you, to make it clear whether you love him or not with all your heart and all your soul. Follow the Lord your God. Fear him, keep his commandments, and hear his voice; serve him and cling to him. But that prophet or fabricator of dreams shall be put to death, because he spoke to turn you away from the Lord your God who led you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to make you wander from the way the Lord your God commanded you. Thus you shall remove the evil from your midst. If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife in your bosom, or the friend whom you love as your own soul, tries to persuade you secretly, saying: "Let us go and serve foreign gods," whom you and your fathers do not know—of any of the nations around you, whether near or far, from one end of the earth to the other—do not yield to him or listen to him; nor shall your eye spare him to have mercy or protect him. But you shall kill him immediately. Let your hand be the first upon him, and afterward the hand of all the people. He shall be killed, overwhelmed by stones, because he wanted to pull you away from the Lord your God who led you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. So all Israel may hear and fear, and never again do anything like this. If you hear in one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you to inhabit, some saying: "Sons of Belial <note>Original: "filii belial," meaning wicked or worthless men.</note> have gone out from your midst and turned away the inhabitants of their city, saying 'Let us go and serve foreign gods whom you do not know,'" inquire diligently. And if, after the truth of the matter has been carefully looked into, you find it certain that this abomination was committed, you shall immediately strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, and destroy it and all that are in it, even the cattle. Whatever furniture is there, you shall gather into the middle of its streets and burn it with the city itself, so that you consume everything for the Lord your God, and it shall be an everlasting mound. It shall not be built again, and nothing of that curse <note>Original: "anathemate," something set apart for destruction.</note> shall stay in your hand, so that the Lord may turn from the heat of his fury and have mercy on you, and multiply you as he swore to your fathers; when you hear the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his precepts which I command today, that you may do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.

<margin>Deuteronomy 14</margin>
**Everyone** indeed who offers an offspring, the Lord shall kill him and make an idol... <note>This sentence appears to be a corrupt or mixed reading of the text.</note> so the Lord swore to your fathers concerning the land he would give you, so that you might love the Lord your God. The Lord your God is God, and you are the children of the Lord your God. Do not cut yourselves or make a bald spot for the dead. For you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord has chosen you to be his peculiar people out of all the nations on the earth. You shall not eat anything that is unclean. This is the animal you should eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat; the deer, the gazelle, the wild goat, the pygarg, the antelope, the camel, and the giraffe <note>Original: "camelopardalem."</note>. Every animal that has a divided hoof in two parts and chews the cud, you shall eat. But those that chew the cud but do not have a divided hoof, you must not eat: the camel, the hare, and the rock-badger <note>Original: "choirigillium," usually the hyrax or coney.</note>, because they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof; they shall be unclean to you. The pig also, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, shall be unclean. You shall not eat their meat or touch their carcasses. These you shall eat of all that live in the waters: eat all that have fins and scales. Those without fins and scales you shall not eat, for they are unclean. You may eat all clean birds.

...give it to him that he may eat it, or to whatever stranger <unclear>is within...</unclear> to the Lord. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk. But when the way is too long and the place which the Lord your God has chosen—where he has blessed you—is too far for you to carry all these things, you shall sell them all and turn them into money. You shall carry the money in your hand and go to the place which the Lord your God has chosen. There you may buy with that same money whatever pleases you, whether from the herds or sheep, wine also, and strong drink <note>original: "sicera"; refers to fermented liquor other than wine</note>, and everything that your soul desires. And you shall eat before the Lord your God, and you and your household shall feast,
<margin>A</margin> and also the Levite who is within your gates. Take care not to abandon him, because he has no other portion in your possession.

2. 
In the third year, you shall set aside another tithe from all that grows for you at that time, and you shall store it within your gates. And the Levite shall come, who has no other part or possession of your own, as well as 
<margin>S</margin> the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates, and they shall eat and be satisfied, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands which you shall do.

2. 
In the seventh year, you shall grant a remission <note>A "remission" or release, where debts were canceled and slaves were often freed.</note>, which shall be celebrated in this order:
<margin>C</margin> He to whom anything is owed by his friend or neighbor or brother shall not be able to demand it back, because it is the year of the Lord's remission. From the foreigner and the newcomer he may demand it, but over a citizen and kinsman you have no power of demanding it back, so that there may be no needy person or beggar among you—that the Lord may bless you in the land which he is about to give you as a possession.

2. 
<margin>O</margin> If, however, you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep all the things he has commanded, and which I command to your fathers, he has spoken well; and do not let it be a promise only. You shall lend to many nations, and you yourself shall receive a loan from no one.
<margin>D</margin> You shall rule over many nations, and no one shall rule over you. If one of your brothers who dwells within your gates is in need... if you are about to enter the land which the Lord your God is giving to you, you shall not harden your heart nor close your hand if the poor lack bread, and to all the needy 
<margin>O</margin> who neighbor you, you shall provide. But when the prescribed times come, let not the thought in your heart say: "the year of remission is approaching," and you turn your eyes away from your poor brother, refusing to lend him what he asks, lest he cry out against you to the Lord and it become 
<margin>S</margin> a sin to you. Instead, you shall give to him, nor shall you act craftily in succoring his necessities, so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times and in all things to which you set your hand. The poor will not be lacking in the land of your dwelling; therefore I command you to open your hand to your needy and poor brother who lives with you in the land.

2. 
When a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman is sold to you, they shall serve you for six 
<margin>I</margin> years; in the seventh year you shall let them go free. And when you grant them freedom, you shall by no means let them go empty-handed, but you shall give them provisions for the journey from your flocks and your barns and from your winepresses with which the Lord your God has blessed you. Remember that you yourself served in Egypt <note>This serves as a moral reminder that the Israelites were once slaves themselves.</note> under pressure, and the Lord your God liberated you; and therefore I command this to you now. But if he says, "I do not wish to leave," because he loves you and your house and feels that it is well with him in your service, you shall take an awl and pierce his ear against the door of your house, and he shall serve you forever. You shall do likewise for your maidservants. Do not turn your eyes away from them when you set them free, for they have served you for six years for the double wages of a hired hand; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works. Of the firstborn that are born in your herds and sheep, whatever is of the male sex you shall sanctify to the Lord your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of a bull, and you shall not shear the firstborn of the sheep. In the sight of the Lord your God you shall eat them every year in the place which the Lord chooses, both you and your household. But if it has a blemish, or is lame, or blind, or in any part deformed or weak, it shall not be sacrificed to the Lord your God, but you shall eat it within the gates of your city. Both the clean and the unclean shall eat of them alike, just as they eat the roe deer. Only observe this: that you do not eat their blood, but pour it out on the earth like water.

2. 
Observe diligently the month of new fruits and of the springtime, so that you may perform the Passover <note>original: "phase"; the Passover festival commemorating the exodus from Egypt</note> to the Lord your God, because in that month the Lord your God led you out of Egypt by night. You shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God from the sheep and the cattle in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that his name may dwell there. You shall not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat it without leaven, the bread of affliction, so that you may remember the day of your departure from Egypt all the days of your life. No leaven shall appear in all your borders for seven days, and nothing of the meat that was sacrificed in the evening of the first day shall remain until morning. You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the neighboring places which the Lord your God is giving to you, but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose so that his name may dwell there. You shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at the setting of the sun, the time when you went out from Egypt. You shall cook and eat it in the place which the Lord your God himself shall choose; and in the morning you shall return to your tents. For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day, because it is the assembly of the Lord your God, you shall do no work.

2. 
You shall count seven weeks for yourself from the day you first put the sickle to the harvest, and you shall celebrate the feast day of weeks to the Lord your God, a spontaneous offering of your hand which you shall offer according to the blessing of the Lord your God. And you shall feast before the Lord your God: you, and your son, and your daughter, and your servant, and your maidservant, and the Levite who is within your gates, and the newcomer, the orphan, and the widow who dwell with you in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that his name may dwell there. And you shall remember that you were a servant in Egypt, keeping and doing what has been commanded. You shall also celebrate the solemnity of Tabernacles <note>The Feast of Booths or Sukkot, a harvest festival.</note> for seven days when you have gathered your fruits from the threshing floor and the winepress. And you shall feast in your festival: you, and your son, and your daughter, and your servant, and your maidservant; the Levite also, and the newcomer, the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates. For seven days you shall celebrate the feast to the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all your fruits and in every work of your hands, and you shall be in joy. Three times a year all your males shall appear in the sight of the Lord your God in the place he shall choose: in the solemnity of unleavened bread, and in the solemnity of weeks, and in the solemnity of Tabernacles. They shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed, but each one shall offer according to what he has, according to the blessing which the Lord your God has given to you.

2. 
You shall appoint judges and masters in all your gates which the Lord your God shall give you throughout your individual tribes, so that they may judge the people with a just judgment, nor should they lean to one side. You shall not show favoritism to any person, nor accept bribes, because bribes blind the eyes of the wise and change the words of the just. You shall justly pursue what is just, so that you may live and possess—

<column-break/>

<margin>N</margin> the land which the Lord your God is about to give to you. You shall not plant a grove or any tree near the altar of the Lord your God, nor shall you make or set up for yourself a statue <note>Specifically, a cultic pillar or idol.</note>, which the Lord your God hates.

2. 
You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a sheep or an ox in which there is a blemish or any defect, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God. When there is found among you in one of your gates which the Lord your God is about to give to you, a man or a woman who does evil in the sight of the Lord your God, so as to transgress his covenant, going and serving strange gods and adoring them—the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which I did not command—and this is reported to you, and hearing it you investigate diligently and find it to be true: that such an abomination has been done in Israel; you shall bring the man or woman who has perpetrated this impious thing to the gate of your city, and they shall be overwhelmed with stones from the Lord. 
<margin>I</margin> By the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he who is to be killed perish. Let no one be killed on the testimony of only one person speaking against him. The first hand in the execution shall be yours to put him to death, and the hands of the rest of the people shall be the last, so that you may take away the evil from your midst.

2. 
If a judgment appears difficult and ambiguous to you between blood and blood, case and case, leprosy and non-leprosy, 
<margin>Q</margin> and you see the judgment within your gates varies, rise and go up to the place which the Lord your God shall choose. And you shall come to the priests of the Levitical stock and to the judge who is there at that time; and you shall seek from them, and they will show you the truth of the judgment. You shall do whatever they say—those who preside over the place which the Lord has chosen—and they shall teach you according to his law. You shall follow their decree, nor shall you turn to the right or to the left. 
<margin>U</margin> But if anyone in their pride refuses to obey the command of the priest who at that time ministers to the Lord your God, and the decree of the judge, that man shall die, and you shall take away the evil from Israel. All the people, hearing it, shall fear, so that pride may no longer swell within them.

2. 
When you have entered the land which the Lord your God will give to you, and you possess it and dwell in it, 
<margin>O</margin> and you say, "I will set a king over me, just as all the nations round about have," you shall appoint him whom the Lord your God chooses from among the number of your brothers. You cannot make a man of another nation a king, one who is not your brother. And when he is appointed, he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor lead the people back into Egypt... especially since the Lord your God commanded you that you should by no means return by that same way again. He shall not have many wives to entice his soul, nor immense weights of silver and gold. 
<margin>S</margin> After he sits upon the throne of your kingdom, he shall write for himself this second law <note>original: "deutronomium"; literally 'the second law' or a copy of the law</note> in a volume, taking a copy from the priests of the Levitical tribe. He shall have it with him and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God and keep his words and ceremonies which are commanded in the law. Nor let his heart be lifted up in pride above his brothers, nor turn to the right or to the left, so that he and his sons may rule for a long time over Israel.

2. 
The priests and Levites, and all who are of the same tribe, shall have no part or inheritance with the rest of the people of Israel, because they eat the sacrifices of the Lord and his offerings; they shall receive nothing else from the possession of their brothers. For the Lord is their inheritance, just as he spoke to them. This shall be the right of the priests from the people and from those who offer victims: whether they sacrifice an ox or a sheep, they shall give to the priest the shoulder and the stomach, the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil, and of the wool from every shearing. For the Lord your God has chosen him from all your tribes, that he may stand and minister in the name of the Lord, both he and his sons forever. If a Levite goes out from one of your cities in all Israel where he dwells, and wishes to come, desiring the place which the Lord has chosen, he shall minister in the name of the Lord your God, just like all his brother Levites who stand at that time before the Lord. He shall receive the same portion of food as the others, except for what is due to him in his city from his paternal succession.

2. 
<margin>O</margin> When you enter the land which the Lord your God will give you, beware that you do not choose to imitate the abominations of those nations. Let there not be found among you anyone who purifies his son or daughter by leading them through fire, or who consults soothsayers, or observes dreams and omens; let there be no sorcerer, nor enchanter, nor one who consults spirits or diviners, seeking the truth from the dead. For the Lord 
<margin>Q</margin> abominates all these things, and because of these wicked deeds he will destroy them at your entry. You shall be perfect and without blemish before the Lord your God. These nations whose land you will possess listen to soothsayers and diviners, but you have been instructed otherwise by the Lord your God. A prophet from your own nation and from your 
<margin>U</margin> brothers—one like me—the Lord your God will raise up for you; him you shall hear, just as you requested from the Lord your God at Horeb when the assembly was gathered, and you said: "Let me not hear the voice of the Lord my God again, nor see this great fire anymore, lest I die." And the Lord said: "They have spoken well. I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers like you, and I will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak to them all that I command him. But whoever will not hear his words which he speaks in my name, I will be the avenger. But a prophet who, corrupted by arrogance, wishes to speak in my name things which I did not command him to say, or speaks in the name of foreign gods, shall be put to death. If you answer in your silent thought, 'How can I understand the word which the Lord has not spoken?'— 
<margin>S</margin> this is the sign: if the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord and it does not happen, the Lord has not spoken this; but the prophet has devised it through the swelling of his own mind. Therefore, you shall not fear him." When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose land he is about to give you, and you possess it and dwell in its cities and houses, you shall separate three cities in the middle of the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession. You shall prepare the way diligently and divide the whole area of your land into three equal parts, so that he who has fled from nearby because he killed someone by accident may have a place to go. 

<margin>S</margin> And this shall be the law of the fleeing manslayer whose life is to be saved: Whoever kills his neighbor unknowingly, and who is proved to have had no hatred against him yesterday or the day before <note>original: "nudius tertius"; an idiom for "the day before yesterday" or "previously"</note>, but went into the woods with his friend to cut wood, and in the cutting of the wood the iron axe-head slipped from his hand and struck his friend and killed him—he shall flee to one of the above-mentioned cities and live. Lest perhaps the kinsman of him whose blood was shed, being moved by grief, should pursue and overtake him—if the way is too long—and strike his soul when he is not guilty of death, because it is shown he had no previous hatred against the one who was killed. Therefore I command 
<margin>Q</margin> you that you separate three equal cities. **I**f a thief is found breaking into a house or digging under it, and having received a wound he dies, the one who struck him shall not be guilty of blood-guilt. **I**f a man is found with the wife of another, both shall die; that is, the adulterer and the adulteress: and you shall take away the evil from Israel. But if a man finds a betrothed girl in a field, and taking hold of her he lies with her, he alone shall die: the girl shall suffer nothing, nor is she guilty of death; for just as a robber rises up against his brother and kills him, so it was with this girl: she was alone in the field; she cried out, and there was no one there to rescue her.

**O**bserve quite diligently that you do not fall into the plague of leprosy, but you shall do whatever the priests of the Levite lineage <note>The tribe of Levi was designated for priestly duties and the interpretation of the Law.</note> shall teach you according to what I have commanded them, and fulfill it carefully. **Y**ou shall not deny the wages of your needy and poor brother, or of the stranger who stays with you in the land. **I**f you gather the fruit of your olives, whatever remains on the trees you shall not return to gather, but you shall leave it for the stranger and the orphan and the widow.

**I**f, however, he does not wish to take his brother's wife, whom he owes by law, the woman shall go to the gate of the city and appeal to the elders, saying: "My husband's brother does not wish to raise up his brother's name in Israel, nor take me in marriage." **I**f you hear the voice of the Lord your God to do and keep all his mandates which I command you today, the Lord your God will make you higher than all the nations that dwell on the earth, and all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if only you hear his precepts. The Lord will set you as the head and not as the tail, and you shall always be above and not beneath, if only you hear the mandates of the Lord your God which I command you today and keep and perform them, and do not decline from them neither to the right nor to the left, nor follow alien gods nor worship them.

**I**f, however, you will not hear the voice of the Lord your God to keep and perform all his mandates and ceremonies which I command you today, all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you. Cursed shall you be in the city, cursed in the field. Cursed your barn and cursed your remains. Cursed the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, the herds of your oxen and the flocks of your sheep. Cursed shall you be entering and exiting. The Lord will send upon you famine and hunger and rebuke in all the works you do until he crushes you and destroys you quickly because of your most wicked inventions in which you have left me. May the Lord join pestilence to you until he consumes you from the land into which you enter to possess. May the Lord strike you with poverty, fever and cold, burning and heat, and with corrupted air and rust, and pursue you until you perish. Let the heaven that is above you be brazen, and the earth which you tread be iron. May the Lord give dust as rain in your land, and from heaven may ruin descend upon you until you are crushed. May the Lord deliver you falling before your enemies. By one way you shall go out against them and by seven you shall flee and be dispersed through all the kingdoms of the earth, and may your corpse be food for all the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, and let there be no one to drive them away. May the Lord strike you with the ulcer of Egypt and the part of the body through which dung is cast out <note>Reference to hemorrhoids or similar afflictions.</note>, and with scab and itch so that you cannot be cured. May the Lord strike you with madness and blindness and fury of mind, and may you grope at midday as a blind man is accustomed to grope in the dark, and may you not direct your ways. At all times may you suffer slander and be oppressed by violence, nor have anyone who may free you. May you take a wife and another sleep with her. May you build a house and not live in it. May you plant a vineyard and not harvest it. May your ox be slaughtered before you and you not eat of it. May your donkey be seized in your sight and not returned to you. May your sheep be given to your enemies and there be no one to help you. May your sons and your daughters be delivered to another people while your eyes see and fail at the sight of them all day long, and let there be no strength in your hand. May a people whom you do not know eat the fruit of your land and all your labors, and may you always be suffering slander and oppressed all your days, and stunned at those things which your eyes shall see. May the Lord strike you with a most evil ulcer in the knees and in the calves, and may you not be able to be healed from the sole of your foot to the top of your head. The Lord will lead you and your king whom you have set over you into a nation which you and your fathers do not know, and there you shall serve alien gods of wood and stone, and you shall be lost in proverb and fable to all the peoples to whom the Lord shall lead you. You shall cast much seed into the land and gather little, because locusts shall devour everything. You shall plant a vineyard and dig, and you shall not drink the wine nor gather anything from it, because it shall be laid waste by worms. You shall have olives in all your borders, and you shall not be anointed with oil, because they shall drop off and perish. You shall beget sons and daughters and you shall not enjoy them because they shall be led into captivity. Rust shall consume all your trees and the fruits of your land. The stranger who is with you in the land shall rise above you and be superior. You, however, shall descend and be inferior.

...these [curses] shall come upon you and overtake you. Great and various persecutions shall invade, and all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God, nor did you keep his commandments and the ceremonies which he commanded you. And there shall be signs and wonders upon you and your descendants forever, because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart. Despite the abundance of all things, you shall serve your enemy, whom the Lord will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and the lack of all things. And he shall place an **iron yoke** <note>original: "iugū ferreū"; a metaphor for harsh, inescapable slavery</note> upon your neck until he crushes you. The Lord will bring against you a nation from afar and from the furthest ends of the earth, like an eagle flying with an impulse, whose language you cannot understand—a most arrogant nation that shows no respect to the elderly nor mercy to the young—and it shall devour the fruit of your cattle and the crops of your land until you perish. It shall leave you no wine, oil, herds, oxen, or flocks of sheep until it destroys you and crushes you in all your cities, and your firm and high walls, in which you placed your trust, are destroyed throughout all your land. You shall be besieged within your gates in all your land which the Lord your God has given you. And you shall eat the fruit of your own womb, and the flesh of your sons and daughters, whom the Lord your God has given you, in the distress and devastation with which your enemy shall oppress you. The man who is delicate among you and very luxurious will begrudge his own brother and the wife who lies in his bosom... <note>original: "uxori quæ cubat i ſinu"; the text here describes the extreme horrors of a siege leading to cannibalism.</note> the flesh of his sons whom he eats, because he has nothing else left in the siege and the poverty with which all your enemies have devastated you within all your gates. The tender and delicate woman, who could not even step upon the ground or fix a foot because of her extreme softness and delicacy, will begrudge the husband who lies in her bosom, and her sons and daughters, and the flesh of the afterbirth that comes out from between her thighs, and the children born in that same hour. For they shall eat them secretly because of the lack of all things in the siege and the devastation with which your enemy shall oppress you within your gates. If you do not keep and perform all the words of this law that are written in this volume, and if you do not fear his glorious and terrible name—that is, the Lord your God—the Lord will increase your plagues and the plagues of your descendants, great and persistent plagues, and the worst and perpetual sicknesses. And he will bring back upon you all the afflictions of Egypt which you feared, and they shall cling to you. Moreover, the Lord will bring upon you every languor and every plague that is not written in the volume of this law, until he crushes you. And you shall remain few in number, you who were previously as numerous as the stars of heaven, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God. And just as the Lord previously rejoiced over you, doing good to you and multiplying you, so shall he rejoice in destroying and overthrowing you, so that you are taken away from the land which you are entering to possess. The Lord will scatter you among all peoples from the summit of the earth to its furthest bounds, and there you shall serve alien gods, whom both you and your fathers did not know—gods of wood and stone. Among those nations you shall have no rest, nor shall there be any repose for the sole of your foot. For the Lord will give you a trembling heart there, failing eyes, and a soul consumed by grief. And your life shall be as if hanging before you; you shall fear night and day, and you shall not trust in your own life. In the morning you shall say, "Who will give me evening?" and in the evening, "Who will give me morning?" because of the dread of your heart with which you shall be terrified, and because of those things which you shall see with your eyes. The Lord will bring you back in ships to Egypt by the way of which he said to you, "You shall see it no more." There you shall be sold to your enemies as male and female slaves, and there shall be no one to buy you, etc.

<margin>Deuteronomy 29</margin>
## These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to strike with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides that covenant which he made at Horeb <note>original: "oreb"; Mount Sinai.</note>. And Moses called all Israel and said to them: "You have seen everything that the Lord did before you in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and to all his land—the great trials which your eyes saw, those signs and great wonders. Yet the Lord has not given you an understanding heart, eyes that see, and ears that could hear until this present day. He led you for forty years through the wilderness; your clothes were not worn out, nor were the shoes on your feet consumed by age. You did not eat bread, nor did you drink wine or strong drink <note>original: "sicera"; any intoxicating beverage other than wine.</note>, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God. And you came to this place. And Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we struck them and took their land, and gave it as a possession to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Therefore, keep the words of this pact and fulfill them, so that you may understand all that you do. You all stand here today before the Lord your God—your leaders, your tribes, your elders, and your teachers, and all the people of Israel, your children and your wives, and the stranger who dwells with you in the camps (excepting the wood-cutters and those who carry water)—so that you may pass into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into the oath which today the Lord your God strikes with you, so that he may raise you up as a people for himself, and that he himself may be your Lord God, just as he spoke to you and as he swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Nor do I make this covenant and confirm these oaths with you alone, but with all who are present and absent. For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations. As you passed through, you saw their abominations and filth, their idols of wood and stone, silver and gold, which they worshipped. Let there not be among you a man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart is turned away from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations; and let there not be among you a root sprouting gall and bitterness. And when such a person hears the words of this oath, let him not bless himself in his heart, saying, 'Peace shall be mine even if I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,' so that the drunken may consume the thirsty. The Lord will not indulge him, but then his fury and his zeal shall smoke against that man, and all the curses written in this volume shall settle upon him, and the Lord shall blot out his name from under heaven. He shall consume him in destruction from all the tribes of Israel, according to the curses contained in the book of this law and covenant. And the following generation—the sons born hereafter and the foreigners who come from afar—seeing the plagues of that land and the sicknesses with which the Lord has afflicted it, burning it with sulfur and the heat of salt, so that it can no longer be sown, nor any green thing sprout (as an example of the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger and fury), all nations shall say: 'Why has the Lord done this to this land? What is this immense heat of his fury?' And they shall respond: 'Because they abandoned the pact of the Lord which he made with their fathers when he led them out of the land of Egypt, and they served alien gods, whom they did not know and who had not been assigned to them. Therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against this land, to bring upon it all the curses written in this volume. And he cast them out of their land in his fury and in the greatest indignation, and threw them into an alien land, as it is proven today.' Secret things belong to the Lord our God; those things that are manifest belong to us and our children forever, that we may perform all the words of this law's commandments."

## And Moses addressed all Israel and said to them:

<column-break/>

<margin>Deuteronomy 30</margin>
"And when all these words come upon you, whether the blessing or the curse which I have set before you, and you are moved by repentance in your heart among all the nations into which the Lord your God has dispersed you, and you return to him and obey his commands just as I command you today—you and your children with all your heart and all your soul—the Lord your God will bring you back from your captivity and will have mercy on you. He will gather you again from all the peoples among whom he previously scattered you. Even if you have been scattered to the furthest reaches of heaven, the Lord your God will bring you back from there; he will take you and lead you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall obtain it. And blessing you, he will make you greater in number than your fathers were. The Lord your God will **circumcise your heart** <note>original: "Circūcidet... cor tuū"; a spiritual metaphor for removing stubbornness and opening the heart to God.</note> and the heart of your descendants, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, that you may live. But all these curses he will turn upon your enemies and those who hated and persecuted you. You, however, shall return and listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and you shall perform all the commandments which I command you today. And the Lord your God will make you abound in all the works of your hands, in the offspring of your womb, and in the fruit of your cattle, in the fertility of your land, and in the abundance of all things. For the Lord your God will return to rejoice over you in all good things, just as he rejoiced over your fathers—if, however, you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep his precepts and ceremonies written in this law, and return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul. This commandment which I command you today is not above you, nor far off, nor placed in heaven so that one might say, 'Who of us can go up to heaven to bring it to us, that we may hear and fulfill it in work?' Nor is it placed across the sea, so that you might excuse yourself and say, 'Who of us can cross the sea and bring it to us, so that we might hear and do what is commanded?' But the word is very near to you, and in your heart, so that you may do it. Consider that today I have set before your sight life and good, and on the contrary, death and evil—that you may love the Lord your God, walk in his ways, and keep his commandments, ceremonies, and judgments, so that you may live and multiply, and he may bless you in the land you are entering to possess. But if your heart is turned away and you are unwilling to listen, and being deceived by error you adore alien gods and serve them, I declare to you today that you shall perish, and you shall dwell for only a short time in the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

## I invoke heaven and earth as witnesses today, that I have set before you life and death, good and evil, blessing and curse. Therefore, **choose life** <note>original: "Elige g̃ uitam"; a famous exhortation to moral agency.</note>, so that both you and your descendants may live, and that you may love the Lord your God, obey his voice, and cling to him. For he is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—to give to them. So Moses went and spoke all these words to all Israel, and said to them: "I am one hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in, especially since the Lord has said to me: 'You shall not cross this Jordan.' Therefore the Lord your God himself will cross before you; he will destroy all these nations in your sight, and you shall possess them. And this Joshua shall cross before you, just as the Lord has spoken. And may the Lord do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their lands, and destroy them. Since he will deliver them to you, you shall do to them just as I have commanded you. Act manfully and be strengthened; do not fear nor be terrified at their sight, because the Lord your God himself is your leader, and he will not fail you nor forsake you, etc."

<margin>Deuteronomy 31</margin>
## And Moses called Joshua and said to him before all Israel: "Be strengthened and be robust. For you shall introduce this people into the land which the Lord swore to give to their fathers, and you shall divide it by lot. Moreover, the Lord who is your leader will himself be with you; he will not fail you nor forsake you; do not fear nor be terrified." So Moses wrote this law and delivered it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel. And he commanded them, saying: "After seven years, in the year of remission, at the solemnity of Tabernacles, when all Israel comes together to appear in the sight of the Lord your God in the place which the Lord shall choose, you shall read the words of this law before all Israel in their hearing—the whole people being gathered into one, both men and women, children and the strangers who are within your gates—so that hearing they may learn and fear the Lord your God, and keep and fulfill all the words of this law. And let their children, who are now ignorant, be able to hear and fear the Lord your God all the days they live in the land to which you are going, having crossed the Jordan, to obtain it."

## And the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, the days of your death are near. Call Joshua and stand in the Tabernacle of Testimony <note>original: "tabernaculo teſtimonī"; also known as the Tent of Meeting.</note>, that I may give him a charge." So Moses and Joshua went and stood in the Tabernacle of Testimony. And the Lord appeared in the pillar of a cloud, which stood at the entrance of the tabernacle. And the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, you shall sleep with your fathers, and this people, rising up, will play the harlot after alien gods in the land they are entering, and they will dwell in it. And there they will forsake me, and make void the covenant which I struck with them. And my fury shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them. They shall be devoured; all evils and afflictions shall find them, so that they say in that day: 'Truly, because God is not with me, these evils have found me.' But I will hide and conceal my face because of all the evils they have done, because they followed alien gods. Now therefore, write for yourselves this song and teach it to the children of Israel, so that they keep it in memory and sing it with their mouths; and let this song be a witness for me among the children of Israel. For I will lead them into the land flowing with milk and honey, which I swore to their fathers. And when they have eaten and are satisfied and grown fat, they will turn to alien gods and serve them, and they will disparage me and make my pact void. After many evils and afflictions have found them, this song shall respond as a testimony, which no forgetfulness shall erase from the mouth of your descendants. For I know their thoughts and what they are about to do today, before I lead them into the land which I promised them." So Moses wrote the song and taught it to the children of Israel. And the Lord commanded Joshua the son of Nun and said: "Be strengthened and be robust. For you shall lead the children of Israel into the land which I promised, and I will be with you."

## After Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a volume and completed it, he commanded the Levites who carried the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, saying: "Take this book and place it in the side of the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord your God, so that it may be there against you as a testimony. For I know your contention and your very stiff neck. While I am still living and entering with you, you have always acted rebelliously against the Lord; how much more so when I am dead? Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your teachers, and..."
