...let him hear; these words. And I will call heaven and earth against them. For I know that after my death you will act wickedly and will quickly turn aside from the way I commanded you. Evils will come upon you in the end times, when you do evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking him to anger through the works of your hands.

Let the earth hear the words of my mouth. Let my doctrine gather like the rain: let my speech flow like the dew. Like a shower upon the grass, and like drops upon the herbs. For I will call upon the name of the Lord: give greatness to our God. The works of God are perfect, and all his ways are judgments. A faithful God, without any iniquity, just and upright. They have sinned against him, and they are not his children in their filth: a wicked and perverse generation. Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and senseless people? Is he not your father who possessed you, and made you, and created you? Remember the days of old, consider every generation: ask your father, and he will declare it to you, your elders, and they will tell you. When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam: he appointed the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. But the Lord’s portion was his people, Jacob the lot of his inheritance. He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror and vast solitude. He led him about, and taught him, and kept him as the apple of his eye. Like an eagle enticing her young to fly, and hovering over them. He spread his wings, and took them, and carried them on his shoulders. The Lord alone was his leader: and there was no strange god with him. He set him over the high places of the earth, so that he might eat the fruits of the fields: that he might suck honey from the rock, and oil from the hardest stone. Butter from the herd, and milk from the sheep: with the fat of lambs, and of rams of the breed of Bashan. And goats with the marrow of wheat, and that he might drink the purest blood of the grape. The beloved <note>original: "dilectus"; often interpreted as Jeshurun, a poetic name for Israel</note> grew fat and kicked: grown fat, thick, and bloated. He forsook God his maker, and departed from God his savior. They provoked him with strange gods, and stirred him to anger with abominations. They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods they did not know. New and fresh ones came, whom their fathers did not worship. You forsook the God who fathered you, and you forgot the Lord your creator. The Lord saw and was stirred to anger: because his sons and daughters provoked him. And he said: I will hide my face from them: and I will consider their end. For it is a perverse generation, and unfaithful children. They have provoked me with that which was not a god: and have irritated me with their vanities: and I will provoke them with a people that is not a nation: and I will irritate them with a foolish nation. A fire is kindled in my wrath, and it shall burn even to the lowest depths of hell: it shall devour the earth with its growth, and shall burn the foundations of the mountains. I will heap evils upon them, and I will spend my arrows among them. They shall be consumed with famine, and birds shall devour them with a most bitter bite. I will send the teeth of beasts upon them: with the fury of those that trail upon the ground and of serpents. Outside, the sword shall lay them waste, and within there shall be fear: the young man and the virgin alike, the suckling with the old man. And I said: where are they? I will make the memory of them cease from among men. But I delayed because of the wrath of the enemies: lest perhaps their foes should wax proud, and say: Our high hand, and not the Lord, has done all these things. A nation without counsel and without wisdom. If only they were wise and understood and provided for their end. How should one pursue a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Was it not because their God sold them, and the Lord shut them up? For our God is not like their gods: even our enemies are judges. Their vine is of the vineyard of Sodom, and of the suburbs of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of gall, and their clusters are most bitter. Their wine is the gall of dragons, and the incurable venom of asps. Are these things not stored up with me, and sealed in my treasures? Revenge is mine, and I will repay them in due time: so that their foot may slide. The day of destruction is at hand, and the times hasten to arrive. The Lord will judge his people, and will have mercy on his servants. He will see that their hand is weakened, and that those shut up have failed, and the remaining are consumed. And he will say: where are they? The gods in whom they trusted? Of whose victims they ate the fat, and drank the wine of their libations? Let them arise, and help you, and protect you in your need. See that I alone am: and there is no other god besides me. I will kill, and I will make to live. I will strike, and I will heal. And there is no one who can deliver out of my hand. I will lift up my hand to heaven, and I will say: I live forever. If I whet my sword like lightning, and my hand takes hold on judgment: I will render vengeance to my enemies, and I will repay those who hate me. I will make my arrows drunk with blood: and my sword shall devour flesh. From the blood of the slain, and from the captivity of the bared head of the enemies. Praise his people, you nations: for he will avenge the blood of his servants: and will render vengeance to their enemies, and will be merciful to the land of his people.

Moses came, therefore, and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people: he and Joshua the son of Nun. And he finished all these words, speaking to all Israel, and he said to them: Set your hearts on all the words which I testify to you today: so that you may command your children to observe and do and fulfill all things that are written in the volume of this law: for I did not command you in vain: but so that each one might live by them: that doing them you may continue for a long time in the land which you are entering to possess after crossing the Jordan. And the Lord spoke to Moses on that same day, saying: Ascend this mountain Abarim <note>original: "abarim id est transitum"; the name means 'the regions beyond' or 'the crossings'</note>, that is, the crossing, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan which I will deliver to the children of Israel to possess, and die on the mountain which you ascend; you shall be joined to your people, just as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people. Because you transgressed against me in the midst of the children of Israel at the waters of contradiction <note>original: "aquas contradictionis"; referring to Meribah</note> in Kadesh of the desert of Zin, and you did not sanctify me among the children of Israel. You shall see the land from a distance, and you shall not enter into it, the land which I will give to the children of Israel.

### ->THE WORDS OF BLESSING OF THE SERVANT OF GOD<-

The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up to us from Seir. He appeared from Mount Paran, and with him were thousands of saints. In his right hand was a fiery law. He loved the people. All the saints are in his hand: and those who approach his feet shall receive of his doctrine. Moses commanded a law to us, the inheritance of the multitude of Jacob. He shall be king with the most upright, when the princes of the people are gathered together with the tribes of Israel. Let Reuben live, and not die: and let him be small in

<column-break/>

number. This is the blessing of Judah. Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him in to his people. His hands shall fight for him: and he shall be his helper against his adversaries. To Levi also he said: Your perfections <note>original: "perfectiones"; likely translating the Hebrew 'Thummim'</note>, and your doctrine are for your holy man, whom you tested in temptation, and judged at the waters of contradiction. Who said to his father and his mother: I do not know you; and to his brothers: I am ignorant of them; and they did not know their own children. These have kept your word, and have preserved your covenant. Your judgments, O Jacob, and your law, O Israel. They shall place incense in your wrath, and a holocaust upon your altar. Bless, O Lord, his strength, and receive the works of his hands. Strike the backs of his enemies: and let those who hate him not rise up. And to Benjamin he said: The most beloved of the Lord shall dwell confidently in him: as in a bridal chamber he shall stay all the day: and he shall rest between his shoulders. Of Joseph also he said: His land is of the blessing of the Lord: of the fruits of heaven, and the dew, and the deep that lies beneath, of the fruits of the sun and the moon, of the tops of the ancient mountains, of the fruits of the eternal hills, and of the riches of the earth, and of its fullness. Let the blessing of him who appeared in the bush come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarene <note>original: "nazarei"; here meaning one set apart or consecrated</note> among his brothers. His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull, his horns are the horns of a rhinoceros. With them he shall push the nations, even to the ends of the earth. These are the multitudes of Ephraim: and these the thousands of Manasseh. And to Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tabernacles. They shall call the people to the mountain: there they shall sacrifice victims of justice. They shall suck the abundance of the sea like milk, and the hidden treasures of the sands. And to Gad he said: Blessed is Gad in his breadth. He rested like a lion, and seized the arm and the crown. He saw his preeminence, that in his portion the teacher was laid up: who was with the princes of the people, and did the justices of the Lord, and his judgment with Israel. To Dan also he said: Dan is a lion's whelp: he shall flow largely from Bashan. And to Naphtali he said: Naphtali shall enjoy abundance, and shall be full of the blessings of the Lord: he shall possess the sea and the south. To Asher also he said: Blessed is Asher among sons: let him be pleasing to his brothers: and let him dip his foot in oil. Iron and brass shall be his shoe. As the days of your youth, so also shall be your old age. There is no other god like the God of the most upright. He is the rider upon the heaven: your helper. By his magnificence the clouds run about: his dwelling is above, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He shall cast out the enemy from before your face, and shall say: Be crushed. Israel shall dwell confidently, and alone. The eye of Jacob is in a land of corn and wine: the heavens also shall be misty with dew. Blessed are you, Israel. Who is like you, O people who are saved in the Lord? The shield of your help, and the sword of your glory. Your enemies shall deny you, and you shall tread upon their necks.

Moses therefore went up from the plains of Moab upon Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah opposite Jericho: and the Lord showed him all the land of Gilead as far as Dan, and all of Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim, and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the furthest sea, and the south part, and the breadth of the plain of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Zoar. And the Lord said to him: This is the land, for which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: I will give it to your seed. You have seen it with your eyes: and you shall not cross over to it. And Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, by the command of the Lord. And he buried him in a valley of the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor: and no man has known his sepulcher until the present day. Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dimmed, nor were his teeth loosened. And the children of Israel wept for him in the plains of Moab for thirty days. And the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were finished. Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom: because Moses had laid his hands upon him. And the children of Israel obeyed him: and did as the Lord commanded Moses. And there has not arisen a prophet in Israel since then like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face. In all the signs and wonders: which the Lord sent by him to do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land: and all the mighty hand: and the great wonders which Moses did before all Israel.

he found Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe 
of Judah. And Joshua said to Achan: "My son, give glory to the Lord God of Israel and 
confess. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it." Achan answered 
Joshua and said to him: "Truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and thus 
and thus I have done. For I saw among the spoils a very good scarlet cloak, 
and two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar of fifty shekels. And 
desiring them, I took them and hid them in the earth in the middle of my tent, 
and I covered the silver in a dug hole." So Joshua sent ministers 
who, running to his tent, found everything hidden in that same 
place, along with the silver. And taking them from the tent, 
they brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel, and they threw them before the Lord. 
Then Joshua, taking Achan son of Zerah, and the silver shekels, 
the cloak and the gold bar, and his sons and daughters, oxen and donkeys and sheep, 
and the tent itself and all the furniture, and all Israel with him, 
led them to the **Valley of Achor** <note>Achor means "trouble" or "disturbance"</note>, where Joshua said: "Because you have disturbed us, 
the Lord shall disturb you on this day." And all Israel stoned him, and 
all that was his was consumed by fire. And they gathered 
over him a great heap of stones, which remains even to the present 
day. And the fury of the Lord God was turned away from them. And the name 
of that place was called the Valley of Achor even until today.

And with the warriors' minds changed, he chose thirty thousand strong men 
and sent them by night, commanding them: "Place an ambush behind the

rest of the multitude who are with me will approach against the city

until we draw the pursuers far from the city. For they will 
think we are fleeing, just as before. While we are fleeing and they are left 
behind, you shall rise from the ambush and lay waste to the city. The 
Lord God will deliver it into your hands. And when you have taken it, set it on fire. 
You shall do everything just as I have ordered." Those who were sent went 
to the place of ambush and sat between Bethel and Ai to the west.
<margin>Joshua 8</margin>

Now he had chosen five thousand men and placed them in ambush between

Joshua went that night and stood in the middle of the valley. When the

But they, shouting together and encouraging one another, pursued

The adversaries gave way on both sides, so that no one from the multitude

Therefore, after all were killed who had pursued Israel into the desert,

<margin>a</margin>
They came into their cities on the third day, the names of which are these: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim. And the children of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders had sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel. Therefore, all the common people murmured against the princes. But they answered them: "We have sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel, and therefore we cannot touch them.
**But** this we will do to them: let them be reserved indeed so that they may live, lest the vengeance of the Lord be stirred up against us if we should commit perjury. But let them live in such a way that they serve the needs of the whole multitude, cutting wood and carrying water." While they were saying these things, Joshua called the Gibeonites and said to them: "Why did you wish to deceive us with fraud, saying 'we live very far from you,' when you dwell in our very midst? Therefore, you shall be under a curse, and there shall never fail to be from your offspring those who cut wood and carry water for the house of my God." They answered: "It was told to us, your servants, that the Lord your God had promised His servant Moses that He would deliver to you all the land and destroy all its inhabitants. We were greatly afraid and feared for our lives, compelled by the terror you inspire; thus we took this counsel. But now we are in your hand: do to us what seems good and right to you." Joshua did as he had said, and delivered them from the hands of the children of Israel so they would not be killed. And he decreed on that day that they should be in the service of all the people and of the altar of the Lord, cutting wood and carrying water even unto the present time, in the place which the Lord should choose.

<margin>b</margin>
And when Adoni-zedek <note>original: "adonisedech," the Canaanite king of Jerusalem</note>, king of Jerusalem, had heard that Joshua had taken Ai and destroyed it—for just as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he had done to Ai and its kings—and that the Gibeonites had fled to Israel as fugitives and entered a treaty, he was greatly afraid. For Gibeon was a great city, one of the royal cities, and greater than the town of Ai, and all its warriors were very brave. Therefore, Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent to Hoham, king of Hebron, and to Piram, king of Jarmuth, and to Japhia, king of Lachish, and to Debir, king of Eglon, saying: "Come up to me and bring help, so that we may conquer Gibeon, because it has gone over to Joshua and the children of Israel." Therefore, the five kings of the **Amorites** <note>a general term for the inhabitants of Canaan</note> gathered and went up: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, together with their armies, and they camped around Gibeon, attacking it. But the inhabitants of the city of Gibeon sent word to Joshua, who was then staying in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him: "Do not withdraw your hands from helping your servants. Come up quickly and deliver us, and bring aid. For all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the mountains have gathered against us." And Joshua went up from Gilgal, and all the army with him, the bravest men. And the Lord said to Joshua: "Do not fear them. For I have delivered them into your hand; none of them shall be able to resist you." **Coming** therefore upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal, the Lord threw them into a panic at the sight of Israel, and he crushed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and pursued them along the way of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah. And as they fled from the children of Israel and were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord sent great stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and many more died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel struck with the sword.

<margin>c</margin>
**Then** Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day that He delivered the Amorite into the sight of the children of Israel, and he said to them: "Sun, do not move against Gibeon, and moon, against the valley of Ajalon." And the sun and the moon stood still until the nation had avenged itself upon its enemies. Is this not written in the **Book of the Just**? <note>original: "libro iustor." (Book of Jasher), a lost non-canonical book mentioned in the Bible</note> So the sun stood in the midst of heaven and did not hasten to set for the space of one day. There was never before nor after so long a day, when the Lord obeyed the voice of a man and fought for Israel. And Joshua returned with all Israel into the camp of Gilgal. For the five kings had fled and hidden themselves in a cave of the city of Makkedah. And it was told to Joshua that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave of Makkedah; he commanded his companions and said: "Roll great stones to the mouth of the cave, and station industrious men to keep them shut in. But you, do not stay here; pursue the enemies and cut down the rearmost of the fugitives. Do not let them enter the defenses of their cities, for the Lord your God has delivered them into your hand." And after the adversaries had been struck with a great slaughter and consumed almost to total destruction, those who were able to escape from Israel entered the fortified cities. And all the army returned to Joshua in Makkedah, where the camp then was, healthy and in full number; and no one dared to mutter a word against the children of Israel.

<margin>d</margin>
**Pursuing** this, Joshua said: "Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out to me the five kings who are hiding in it." The servants did as they had been commanded, and they led out the five kings to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon. And when they had been led out to him, he called all the men of Israel and said to the leaders of the army who were with him: "Go and place your feet upon the necks of these kings." When they had gone and trampled their necks with their feet, he said to them again: "Do not fear, nor be dismayed; be comforted and be strong. For so shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom you fight." And Joshua struck and killed them, and hanged them upon five poles; and they were hanging until evening. And when the sun was setting, he commanded his companions to take them down from the gibbets. Having taken them down, they cast them into the cave in which they had hidden, and placed great stones over its mouth, which remain until the present.

<margin>e</margin>
**On that day** Joshua also took Makkedah and struck it with the edge of the sword, and killed its king and all its inhabitants. He did not leave even small remnants in it. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho. He passed then from Makkedah to Libnah, and fought against it. Which the Lord delivered, with its king, into the hand of Israel; and he struck the city with the edge of the sword and all its inhabitants. They left no remains in it, and did to the king of Libnah just as they had done to the king of Jericho. From Libnah he passed to Lachish, and having positioned the army all around, he attacked it. And the Lord delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he took it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword and every soul that was in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

<margin>f</margin>
**And** at that time Horam, king of Gezer, came up to help Lachish. Joshua struck him with all his people until total destruction. He passed from Lachish to Eglon and surrounded it; he conquered it on the same day and struck with the edge of the sword every soul that was in it, according to all that he had done to Lachish. He also went up with all Israel from Eglon to Hebron, and fought against it; he took it and struck it with the edge of the sword, both its king and all the towns of that region, and all the souls that were staying in it. He left no remnants in it. As he had done to Eglon, so he did to Hebron, consuming with the sword everything he found.

Returning at that time, he took Hazor, and struck its king and all the towns with the edge of the sword. For that city formerly held the leadership of the other kingdoms. For tomorrow at this same hour, I will deliver all these to be wounded in the sight of Israel. You shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."

<margin>A</margin>
**Coming** therefore, Joshua and all the army with him against them at the waters of Merom, they rushed suddenly upon them. And the Lord delivered them into the hand of Israel. They struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon and the waters of Misrephoth-maim, and the field of Mizpah which is to the east part of them. Thus he struck all, so that he left no remnants. He did as the Lord had commanded him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots. And returning immediately, he took Hazor and struck its king with the sword. For Hazor anciently held the leadership among all these kingdoms. And all the souls that stayed there fell; he left no remains in it, but devastated everything to total destruction, and burned the city itself with fire. And he took all the cities and their kings and struck their kings with the edge of the sword and destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded. Except for the cities situated on hills and mounds, Israel did not burn them. Only Hazor, the most fortified, was consumed by flame. And the children of Israel divided all the plunder of these cities and the cattle among themselves, after all the men were killed. So the Lord had commanded Moses His servant; so Moses commanded Joshua, and he fulfilled everything. Not one word of all the commands that the Lord had ordered Moses passed away.

<margin>B</margin>
Joshua therefore took all the mountain land and the south, and the land of Goshen, and the plain, and the western region, and the mountain of Israel and its lowlands, and the part of the mountain that goes up to Seir as far as Baal-gad in the plain of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He took all their kings, struck them, and killed them. Joshua fought for a long time against these kings. There was no city that delivered itself to the children of Israel except the Hivite who dwelt in Gibeon; he conquered all those and cast them out in victory. For it was the will of the Lord that their hearts should be hardened and they should fight against Israel and fall, and not deserve any indulgence, but perish as the Lord had commanded Moses. At that time Joshua came and killed the **Anakim** <note>original: "enachim," a race of giants</note> from the mountains of Hebron, and Debir, and Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah and Israel; and he destroyed their cities. He left no one of the race of the Anakim in the land of the children of Israel, except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod. Joshua took the whole land, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses, and he delivered it as a possession to the children of Israel according to their parts and tribes; and the land rested from battles.

Sihon, king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, ruled from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent Arnon, and the middle part of the valley and half of Gilead as far as the torrent Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon; and from the wilderness to the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and to the Sea of the Desert, which is the Salt Sea, on the south side... <note>The text continues listing the conquered territories of Og, king of Bashan, and the total of 31 kings</note> ...Moses the servant of the Lord and the children of Israel struck them, and Moses gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. As the Lord had commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel, and they divided the land.

**Then** the children of Judah came to Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite spoke to him: "You know what the Lord said to Moses the man of God concerning me and you in Kadesh-Barnea. I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to survey the land, and I reported to him what seemed true to me. But my brothers who had gone up with me discouraged the heart of the people; and nonetheless I followed the Lord my God. And Moses swore on that day, saying: 'The land which your foot has trodden shall be your possession and your children's forever, because you have followed the Lord my God.' The Lord has therefore preserved my life as he promised, even to the present day. It is forty and five years since the Lord spoke this word to Moses, when Israel walked through the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old, as strong as I was at that time when I was sent to explore. The strength of that time remains in me until today, as much for fighting as for walking. Give me therefore this mountain which the Lord promised, while you were listening, in which are the Anakim <note>A race of legendary giants</note> and great and fortified cities; if perhaps the Lord be with me and I shall be able to destroy them as he promised me."

**And Joshua** blessed him, and delivered Hebron to him as a possession. And from that time Hebron belonged to Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite even to the present day, because he followed the Lord the God of Israel. The name of Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-Arba. Adam, the greatest among the giants, was laid there <note>original: "Adam maximus ibi inter enachim situs est." This is a unique interpretation found in the Latin Vulgate; modern versions usually read "Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim."</note>; and the land ceased from battles.

**Therefore** the lot of the sons of Judah by their families was this: From the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin toward the south, and to the farthest part of the southern region. Its beginning was from the top of the Salt Sea, from the tongue of it that looks toward the south. And it goes out toward the ascent of the Scorpion <note>original: "ascensum scorpionis," often called Maaleh-acrabbim</note>, and passes into Zin, and goes up into Kadesh-Barnea, and reaches Hezron, ascending to Addar, and circling Karka, and from there passing into Azmon, and reaching the torrent of Egypt; and its borders shall be the Great Sea. This shall be the end of the southern region. But from the east the beginning shall be the Salt Sea as far as the ends of the Jordan, and those parts which look toward the north, from the tongue of the sea as far as the same river Jordan. And the border goes up into Beth-Hoglah, and passes from the north into Beth-Arabah, ascending to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, and stretching to the borders of Debir from the valley of Achor toward the north, looking toward Gilgal, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim on the south side of the torrent. And it crosses the waters which are called the Fountain of the Sun, and its exits shall be at the Fountain of Rogel. And it goes up through the valley of the son of Hinnom by the side of the Jebusite to the south—this is Jerusalem—and from there raising itself to the top of the mountain which is opposite the valley of Hinnom to the west, at the top of the valley of the Rephaim <note>The Valley of the Giants</note> toward the north. And it passes from the top of the mountain to the fountain of the waters of Nephtoah, and reaches to the villages of mount Ephron; and it inclines into Baalah, which is Kiriath-Jearim, that is, the city of forests. And it circles from Baalah toward the west as far as mount Seir; and it passes by the side of mount Jearim to the north in Chesalon, and descends from there into Beth-Shemesh. And it passes into Timnah, and reaches opposite the north part of Ekron by the side; and it inclines to Shikkeron, and passes Baalah, and reaches Jabneel, and is closed by the end of the Great Sea toward the west. These are the borders of the sons of Judah round about in their families. But to Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part in the midst of the sons of Judah, as the Lord had commanded Joshua: Kiriath-Arba, the father of Anak, which is Hebron. And Caleb destroyed from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, of the race of Anak. And ascending from there he came to the inhabitants of Debir, which was first called Kiriath-Sepher. And Caleb said: "Whoever strikes Kiriath-Sepher and takes it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as a wife." And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb, took it; and he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife. And as they were going

<column-break/>

together, her husband persuaded her to ask a field from her father. And she sighed as she sat on the donkey. To whom Caleb said: "What is it?" he asked. And she replied: "Give me a blessing. You have given me a southern and dry land; join to it also a watered land." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower watered land.

**This** is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Judah by their families. And the cities from the farthest parts of the sons of Judah near the borders of Edom from the south were: Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur, and Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan, Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth, and Hazor-Hadattah, and Kerioth-Hezron. This is Hazor, Amam, Shema, and Moladah, and Hazar-Gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-Pelet, and Hazar-Shual, and Beersheba, and Biziothiah, and Baalah, and Iim, Ezem, and Eltolad, and Chesil, and Hormah, and Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah, and Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and En-Rimmon; all the cities are twenty-nine, and their villages. In the plains: Eshtaol, and Zorah, and Ashnah, and Zanoah, and En-Gannim, Tappuah, and Enam, and Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah, and Shaaraim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities and their villages. Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-Gad, and Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel, and Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon, and Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish, and Gederoth, and Beth-Dagon, and Naaman, and Makkedah; sixteen cities and their villages. Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan, and Iphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib, and Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities and their villages. Ekron with its towns and its villages, from Ekron to the sea, all that turn toward Ashdod and its villages. Ashdod with its villages, Gaza with its towns and villages, as far as the torrent of Egypt, and the Great Sea is its border. And in the mountain: Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh, and Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah—this is Debir—Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim, Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities and their villages. Arab, and Dumah, and Eshan, and Janum, and Beth-Tappuah, and Aphekah, and Humtah, and Kiriath-Arba—this is Hebron—and Zior; nine cities and their villages. Maon, and Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah, and Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities and their villages. Halhul, and Beth-Zur, and Gedor, Maarath, and Beth-Anoth, and Eltekon; six cities and their villages. Kiriath-Baal—this is Kiriath-Jearim, the city of forests—and Rabbah; two cities and their villages. In the desert: Beth-Arabah, Middin, and Secacah, and Nibshan, and the City of Salt, and En-Gedi; six cities and their villages. But the Jebusite inhabitant of Jerusalem the sons of Judah could not destroy; and the Jebusite lived with the sons of Judah in Jerusalem even to the present day.

**And the lot** of the sons of Joseph went forth from the Jordan opposite Jericho, and its waters from the east; the wilderness which ascends from Jericho to the mountains of Bethel. And it goes out from Bethel to Luz, and passes the border of Archi-Ataroth, and descends to the west near the border of Japhleti as far as the borders of Lower Beth-Horon and Gezer; and its regions are ended by the Great Sea. And the sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, possessed it. And the border of the sons of Ephraim was made by their families; and their possession toward the east was Ataroth-Addar as far as Upper Beth-Horon. And the border goes out to the sea. Michmethath looks to the north; and the border circles toward the east in Taanath-Shiloh, and passes from the east of Janoah. And it descends from Janoah into Ataroth and Naarah, and reaches Jericho, and goes out to the Jordan. From Tappuah it passes toward the sea into the Valley of Reeds, so that its end is in the Salt Sea. This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim by their families.

**And this lot** fell to the tribe of Manasseh—for he is the firstborn of Joseph—to Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he was a man of war; and he had the possession of Gilead and Bashan. And to the rest of the sons of Manasseh according to their families: the sons of Abiezer, and the son of Helek, and the son of Asriel, and the son of Shechem, and the son of Hepher, and the son of Shemida. These are the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph by their families. But to Zelophehad the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, there were no sons but only daughters, whose names are these: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah. And they came into the presence of Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the princes, saying: "The Lord commanded Moses to give us a possession in the midst of our brothers." And a possession was given to them according to the command of the Lord in the midst of their father's brothers. And ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan. For the daughters of Manasseh possessed an inheritance among his sons.

**And the border** of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which looks toward Shechem; and the boundary goes to the right near the inhabitants of En-Tappuah. For in the lot of Manasseh fell Tappuah, which is on the borders of Manasseh, belonging to the sons of Ephraim. And the border descends to the Valley of Reeds in the south of the torrent of the cities of Ephraim, which are in the midst of the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh is from the north of the valley, and its exit is to the sea; so that the north belongs to Manasseh, and the south to Ephraim, and the sea closes both. And they are joined to each other in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east. And the inheritance of Manasseh in Issachar and in Asher was Beth-Shean and its villages, and Ibleam with its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor with its towns, also the inhabitants of Endor with its villages, and likewise the inhabitants of Taanach with its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages, and the third part of the city of Nopheth. Nor could the sons of Manasseh overthrow these cities, but the Canaanite began to dwell in his land. But after the children of Israel had grown strong, they subjected the Canaanites and made them tributaries, but did not kill them.

**And the sons of Joseph** spoke to Joshua, saying: "Why have you given me as a possession one lot and one portion, when I am of such a great multitude, and the Lord has blessed me?" To whom Joshua said: "If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest, and cut out spaces for yourself in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim; because the possession of Ephraim is too narrow for you." To which the sons of Joseph replied: "We shall not be able to go up to the mountains, since the Canaanites use iron chariots, both those who dwell in the land of the valley in which Beth-Shean is situated with its villages, and those who possess the middle part of Jezreel." And Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh: "You are a numerous people and of great strength; you shall not have only one lot, but you shall pass to the mountain and cut out spaces for yourself to dwell in; and you shall be able to proceed further when you have overthrown the Canaanite, whom you say has iron chariots and is very strong."

**And the whole multitude** of the children of Israel was gathered together in Shiloh, and there they fixed the tabernacle of the testimony; and the land was subjected to them. There remained of the children of Israel seven tribes which had not yet received their possessions. To whom Joshua said: "How long will you wither away in sloth, and not enter to possess the land which the Lord the God of your fathers has given you?"

Describe the land between these in seven parts; and you shall come here to me so that I may cast lots for you here before the Lord our God. Because there is no portion for the Levites among you, but the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. But Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their possessions across the Jordan toward the eastern side, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave to them.

And when the men had risen to go and describe the land, Joshua commanded them, saying: Go, travel through the land and describe it; then return to me so that here, before the Lord in Shiloh, I may cast lots for you. And so they went out and, surveying it, divided it into seven parts, writing them in a book; and they returned to Joshua in the camp at Shiloh. He cast lots before the Lord in Shiloh. And the lot came out by their families between the borders of the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph. And its border was toward the north: starting from the Jordan near the northern side of Jericho; and from there it goes up toward the west into the mountains and reaches the wilderness of Beth-aven; and it passes along near Luz to the south, which is Bethel; and it descends into Ataroth-addar on the mountain that is to the south of lower Beth-horon. And it inclines and circles toward the sea, south of the mountain that looks toward Beth-horon toward the southwest <note>original: "affricum," referring to the southwest wind</note>; and its exits are in Kiriath-baal, which is called Kiriath-jearim, a city of the sons of Judah. This is the side toward the sea and the west. But from the south, from the side of Kiriath-jearim, the border goes out toward the sea and reaches as far as the spring of the waters of Nephtoah. And it descends into the part of the mountain that looks toward the valley of the sons of Hinnom.

**D**escending toward the edge of the mountain that looks toward the valley of the sons of Hinnom; and it is toward the northern side at the edge of the valley of Rephaim <note>The Valley of Rephaim was known as the "Valley of Giants"</note>; and it descends into Gehenna, that is, the valley of Hinnom, near the side of the Jebusite to the south; and it reaches the spring of Rogel. Passing to the north and going out to En-shemesh, which is the "Spring of the Sun"; and it passes through to the mounds that rise in the ascent of Adummim; and it descends to Eben-bohen, that is, the "Stone of Bohen" the son of Reuben, and it passes from the northern side to the plains; and it descends into the flatland and passes over toward Beth-hoglah; and its exits are in the tongue of the Salt Sea from the north at the end of the Jordan at the southern side, which is its border from the east. This is the possession of the sons of Benjamin by their borders in circuit and by their families. And its cities were Jericho and Beth-hoglah, and the valley of Keziz. Beth-arabah and Zemaraim and Bethel. Avvim and Ephrathah and Ophrah, the village of Ammona, and Ophni and Geba—twelve cities and their villages. Gibeon and Ramah and Beeroth and Mizpah. Kephirah and Mozah, and Rekem and Irpeel, and Taralah, Zela, and Haeleph, and Jebus, which is Jerusalem. Gibeath and Kiriath—fourteen cities and their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Benjamin according to their families.

**S**econd, the lot came out for Simeon according to their kindreds: and his inheritance was in the midst of the possession of the sons of Judah. Beersheba and Sheba, and Moladah, and Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem, and Eltolad, Bethul and Hormah, and Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah, and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities and their villages. Ain and Rimmon and Ether and Ashan—four cities and their villages. All the hamlets around the villages as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah toward the southern side. This is the inheritance of the sons of Simeon according to their kindreds within the territory and possession of the sons of Judah, because it was too large; and therefore the sons of Simeon possessed land in the midst of their inheritance.

**T**he third lot came out for the sons of Zebulun according to their kindreds: and the border of their possession was as far as Sarid. And it ascends from the sea and Maralah; and it reaches to Dabbesheth as far as the torrent that is opposite Jokneam. And it returns from Sarid toward the east into the borders of Chisloth-tabor; and it goes out to Daberath and ascends toward Japhia; and from there it passes toward the eastern side which is called Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin and goes out into Rimmon-methoar and Neah and circles to the north of Hannathon. And its exits are Nephthal-el and Kattath and Nahalal, and Shimron, and Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve cities and their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun according to their kindreds, their cities and hamlets.

**T**he fourth lot came out for Issachar according to their kindreds: and its inheritance was Jezreel and Chesulloth and Shunem and Hapharaim. Shion and Anaharath and Rabbith and Kishion, Ebez and Remeth and En-gannim and En-haddah and Beth-pazzez. And its border reaches as far as Tabor and Shahazumah and Beth-shemesh; and its exits shall be the Jordan—sixteen cities and their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Issachar according to their kindreds, their cities and hamlets.

**T**he fifth lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Asher according to their kindreds: and its border was Helkath and Hali and Beten and Achshaph, and Allammelech and Amad and Mishal. And it reaches as far as Carmel by the sea and Shihor-libnath. And it returns toward the east to Beth-dagon; and it passes through to Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el toward the north into Beth-emek and Neiel. And it goes out to the left of Cabul, and Ebron and Rehob and Hammon and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon. And it returns to Ramah as far as the most fortified city of Tyre and as far as Hosah; and its exits shall be into the sea from the region of Achzib. And Ummah and Aphek and Rehob—twenty-two cities and their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Asher according to their kindreds, their cities and hamlets.

**T**he sixth lot came out for the sons of Naphtali according to their families: and the border extended from Heleph and Elon and Zaanannim and Adami, which is Nekeb, and Jabneel as far as Lakkum; and their exit is as far as the Jordan. And the border returns toward the west into Aznoth-tabor and from there goes out into Hukkok and passes into Zebulun toward the south, and into Asher toward the west, and into Judah at the Jordan toward the rising of the sun. The most fortified cities are Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, and Rakkath and Chinnereth, and Adamah and Ramah, Hazor and Kedesh and Edrei and En-hazor and Iron and Migdal-el, Horem and Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh—nineteen cities and their villages. This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali according to their kindreds, their cities and hamlets.

**T**he seventh lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their families: and the border of his possession was Zorah and Eshtaol and Ir-shemesh, and Shaalabbin and Aijalon and Ithlah and Elon and Timnah and Ekron, and Eltekeh and Gibbethon and Baalath and Jehud and Bene-berak and Gath-rimmon, and the waters of Jarkon and Rakkon with the border that looks toward Joppa and is concluded by that boundary. And the sons of Dan went up and fought against Leshem and captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword. And they possessed it and lived in it, calling its name Leshem Dan from the name of Dan their father. This is the possession of the tribe of the sons of Dan

according to their kindreds, their cities and hamlets.

**A**nd when they had finished dividing the land for each by their tribes, the sons of Israel gave a possession to Joshua the son of Nun in their midst: according to the command of the Lord, the city which he asked for, Timnath-serah in the mountain of Ephraim; and he built the city and lived in it. These are the possessions which Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the princes of the families and tribes of the sons of Israel divided by lot in Shiloh before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony; and they partitioned the land.

<margin>L. <note>likely abbreviation for "Liber" (Book) or "Lex" (Law)</note></margin>
**A**nd the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: Set aside the cities of the fugitives <note>These are the "Cities of Refuge"</note> of which I spoke to you through the hand of Moses: so that anyone who has struck down a person unknowingly may flee to them, so that he may escape the wrath of the next of kin, the avenger of blood. And when he has fled to one of these cities, he shall stand before the gate of the city; and he shall speak to the elders of that city those things which prove him innocent; and so they shall receive him and give him a place to live. And when the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not deliver him into his hands, because he struck his neighbor in ignorance and is not proven to have been his enemy yesterday or the day before. And he shall live in that city until he stands before the judgment to give an account of his deed; and until the high priest who is in that time dies. Then the manslayer shall return and enter the city and his own house from which he had fled. And they met and sanctified Kedesh in Galilee on the mountain of Naphtali, and Shechem in the mountain of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba (this is Hebron) on the mountain of Judah. And across the Jordan toward the east of Jericho, they gave Bezer, which is situated in the plain of the wilderness from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh. These cities were established for all the sons of Israel and the strangers who live among them: so that anyone who unknowingly struck a soul might flee to them and not die by the hand of the next of kin to shed blood, until he stood before the people to explain his cause.

And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites from their possessions, according to the command of the Lord, cities and their suburbs.

**A**nd the Lord gave to Israel all the land which he had sworn to their fathers; and they possessed it and lived in it. And peace was given by him on every side among the nations; and none of their enemies dared to resist them, but all were brought under their dominion. Not even one word that the Lord had promised he would provide for them failed, but all things that were expected were fulfilled.

<margin>xxv</margin>
**A**t the same time Joshua called the Reubenites and Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh; and he said to them: You have provided all things that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you; in which matters you also obeyed me. Nor have you left your brothers for a long time even until the present day, keeping the command of the Lord your God. Because therefore the Lord your God has given rest and peace to your brothers as he spoke: return and go into your tents and into the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of the Lord delivered to you across the Jordan.

...servant of the Lord, confirming <note>The Latin text here appears to have some scribal variations or glosses regarding the visibility of the altar.</note> as long as you lived, or they might see the altar. You have fulfilled the commandment and the law which Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you: that you should love the Lord your God, walk in His ways, keep His commandments, cling to Him, and serve Him with all your heart and all your soul. Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they returned to their tents. Now, to the half-tribe of Manasseh, Moses had given a possession in Bashan; and therefore to the other half, Joshua gave a lot among their brothers across the Jordan toward the western side. And when he sent them away to their tents and had blessed them, he said to them: "Return to your homes with great substance and riches, with silver and gold, bronze and iron, and many-colored clothing. Divide the spoils of the enemies with your brothers." So the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned from the children of Israel at Shiloh, which is situated in Canaan, to enter Gilead, the land of their possession, which they had obtained according to the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

When they came to the banks of the Jordan in the land of Canaan, they built an altar of immense size near the Jordan. When the children of Israel heard this, and certain messengers brought word to them that the sons of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar in the land of Canaan upon the banks of the Jordan against the children of Israel, they all gathered at Shiloh to go up and fight against them. In the meantime, they sent to them in the land of Gilead Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, and ten princes with him, one from each tribe. They came to the sons of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said: "Thus says all the people of the Lord: What is this transgression? Why have you forsaken the Lord your God, building a sacrilegious altar and departing from His worship? Is the sin of <note>original: "beelphedor"</note> Baal-peor <note>A reference to an incident where the Israelites worshipped a local deity, leading to a plague.</note> too little for you, the stain of which remains on us even to this day, and many of the people fell? You also have forsaken the Lord today, and tomorrow His wrath will rage against all Israel. But if you think the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land in which the tabernacle of the Lord is, and dwell among us: only do not depart from the Lord and from our company by building an altar other than the altar of the Lord our God. Did not <note>original: "acham"</note> Achan the son of Zerah <note>Achan took forbidden spoils from Jericho, causing God's anger to fall on the whole community.</note> violate the command of the Lord, and His wrath fell upon all the people of Israel? He was but one man; would that he alone had perished in his crime."

The sons of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the princes of the embassy of Israel: "The Lord, the most powerful God, He knows, and Israel itself shall understand: if we built this altar with a spirit of transgression, may He not protect us but punish us now. If we did it with the intent to place <term>holocausts</term> <note>A religious animal sacrifice that is completely consumed by fire.</note> and sacrifices and peace offerings upon it, let Him seek it out and judge. We did this rather with the thought and plan that we should say: 'Tomorrow your children will say to our children: What have you to do with the Lord God of Israel? The Lord has placed the Jordan river as a boundary between us and you, O sons of Reuben and Gad; therefore you have no part in the Lord.' And by this occasion, your children might turn our children away from the fear of the Lord. Therefore we thought it better and said: Let us build an altar for ourselves, not for burnt offerings or for offering sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you, and our offspring and your progeny, that we may serve the Lord and have the right to perform burnt offerings and victims and peace offerings. Never let your children say to our children: You have no part in the Lord. If they should want to say this, they will answer them: Behold the altar of the Lord which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifice, but as a witness for you and for us. Far be it from us to commit this crime of departing from the Lord and leaving His footsteps by building an altar for burnt offerings and victims besides the altar of the Lord our God which is built before His tabernacle."

When Phinehas the priest and the princes of the embassy of Israel who were with him heard these things, they were appeased; and they most willingly accepted the words of the sons of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said to them: "Now we know that the Lord is with you, because you are innocent of this transgression, and you have delivered the children of Israel from the hand of the Lord." And he returned with the princes from the sons of Reuben and Gad, from the land of Gilead in the borders of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and reported to them. The word pleased all who heard it, and the children of Israel praised God; and they said no more about going up against them to fight and destroy the land of their possession. The sons of Reuben and Gad called the altar they had built "Our Witness," because "the Lord Himself is God."

After a long time had passed, and the Lord had given peace to Israel by subjecting all the nations round about, and Joshua being now elderly and of advanced age, he called all Israel, their elders, princes, judges, and officers, and said to them: "I have grown old and am of a more advanced age. You see all that the Lord your God has done to all the nations round about: how He Himself has fought for you. And now, because He has divided to you by lot all the land from the part of the Jordan to the Great Sea <note>The Mediterranean Sea.</note>, and many nations still remain: the Lord your God will destroy them and take them away from before your face, and you shall possess the land as He promised you. Only be strengthened and be careful to keep all things that are written in the book of the law of Moses, and do not decline from them to the right or to the left: lest after you have entered among the nations that will be among you, you swear in the name of their gods, and serve them, and adore them. But cling to the Lord your God, as you have done until this day. And then the Lord will take away from your sight great and very strong nations, and no one will be able to resist you. One of you shall pursue a thousand men of the enemy, because the Lord your God Himself will fight for you as He promised. Take great care for this one thing: that you love the Lord your God. But if you wish to cling to the errors of these nations that dwell among you, and join with them in marriage, and unite in friendships: know even now that the Lord your God will not destroy them before your face, but they shall be a pit and a snare to you, and a stumbling block at your side, and thorns in your eyes, until He takes you away and destroys you from this excellent land which He has given to you. Behold, today I enter the way of all the earth <note>A poetic way of saying he is about to die.</note>: and you shall know with all your soul that of all the words the Lord promised to provide for you, not one has passed in vain. Therefore, as He has fulfilled in deed what He promised and all prosperous things have come, so He will bring upon you whatever evils He has threatened, until He takes you away and destroys you from this excellent land which He has given to you, because you have transgressed the covenant of the Lord your God which He made with you, and have served foreign gods and adored them. For quickly and speedily His anger shall rise against you..."

<margin>24</margin>
**J**oshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem, and called the elders, the princes, the judges, and the officers: and they stood in the presence of the Lord. He spoke thus to the people: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Your fathers dwelt across the river from the beginning—Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor—and they served foreign gods. Therefore I took your father Abraham from the borders of Mesopotamia and led him into the land of Canaan. I multiplied his seed and gave him Isaac. And to him again I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau, I gave Mount Seir to possess; but Jacob and his sons descended into Egypt. I also sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with many signs and wonders. I brought you and your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and cavalry as far as the Red Sea. But the children of Israel cried out to the Lord, who placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. And you dwelt in the wilderness for a long time. I introduced you into the land of the Amorites who lived across the Jordan. When they fought against you, I delivered them into your hands, and you possessed their land and killed them. Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel; he sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you. But I would not listen to him; on the contrary, I blessed you through him and delivered you from his hand. You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The men of that city fought against you—the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite—and I delivered them into your hands. I sent hornets before you and drove them out from their places, even the two kings of the Amorites; it was not by your sword or your bow. And I gave you a land in which you did not labor, and cities which you did not build, that you might dwell in them: vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant. Now therefore, fear the Lord and serve Him with a perfect and most true heart. Put away the gods which your fathers served in Mesopotamia and in Egypt, and serve the Lord. But if it seems evil to you to serve the Lord, you are given a choice. Choose today what pleases you, whom you ought most to serve: whether the gods your fathers served in Mesopotamia, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord."

The people answered and said: "Far be it from us that we should leave the Lord and serve foreign gods. The Lord our God Himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. He performed great signs in our sight and kept us in all the way in which we walked, and among all the people through whom we passed. He drove out all the nations—the Amorites, the inhabitants of the land we entered. Therefore we will serve the Lord, for He is our God." And Joshua said to the people: "You will not be able to serve the Lord. For God is holy and a powerful jealous one; He will not forgive your crimes and sins. If you leave the Lord and serve foreign gods, He will turn and afflict you, and overthrow you after He has provided good things for you." But the people said to Joshua: "It shall not be so; but we will serve the Lord." And Joshua said to the people: "You are witnesses against yourselves, that you yourselves have chosen the Lord to serve Him." And they answered: "We are witnesses." "Now therefore," he said, "put away the foreign gods from your midst and incline your hearts to the Lord God of Israel." The people said to Joshua: "We will serve the Lord our God, and we will be obedient to His commands."

So Joshua made a covenant on that day and set before the people precepts and judgments in Shechem. He also wrote all these words in the volume of the law of the Lord; and he took a very large stone and placed it under the oak tree that was in the sanctuary of the Lord. He said to all the people: "Behold, this stone shall be a witness to you: for it has heard all the words of the Lord which He spoke to you, lest perhaps afterward you should want to deny it and lie to the Lord your God." Then he dismissed the people, each to his own possession. After these things, Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being one hundred and ten years old. They buried him in the borders of his possession in Timnath-serah, which is situated on Mount Ephraim, on the north side of Mount Gaash. And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and of the elders who lived for a long time after Joshua, and who knew all the works of the Lord which He had done in Israel. Also the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel had brought out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in the part of the field which Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred young sheep; and it was in the possession of the sons of Joseph. Eleazar the son of Aaron also died, and they buried him in Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which was given to him on Mount Ephraim. <note>The 'F.' likely stands for 'Finit', meaning 'It ends'.</note>

And the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy upon him, and he became a tributary to them. Now the border of the Amorite was from the Ascent of the Scorpion, from the Rock and the places above.

**C**umque <note>meaning "And when"</note> the Angel of the Lord had gone up from Gilgal to the place of the weeping ones, he said: "I led you out of Egypt and brought you into the land for which I swore to your fathers; and I promised that I would not make void my covenant with you forever, provided that you would not strike a treaty with the inhabitants of this land, and would overturn their altars. And you would not hear my voice. Why have you done this? Wherefore, I would not destroy them from before your face, so that you may have enemies, and their gods may be a ruin to you." And when the Angel of the Lord spoke all these words to all the sons of Israel, they lifted up their voice and wept. And the name of that place was called "of the weeping ones" or "of tears" <note>Bochim</note>. And they sacrificed victims there to the Lord. Therefore, Joshua dismissed the people, and the sons of Israel went away, each to his own possession, to obtain it. And they served the Lord all the days of his life, and of the elders who lived for a long time after him and knew all the works of the Lord which he had done with Israel. Now Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at one hundred and ten years of age. And they buried him in the borders of his possession in Timnath-heres, in the mountain of Ephraim, on the north side of Mount Gaash. And all that generation was gathered to their fathers. And others arose who did not know the Lord, nor the works which he had done for Israel. And the sons of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they served the Baals <note>original: "baalim"</note> and abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had led them out of the land of Egypt. And they followed alien gods, the gods of the peoples who dwelt round about them, and they adored them; and they provoked the Lord to anger, abandoning him and serving Baal and Ashtoreth <note>original: "astaroth"</note>. And the Lord, being angry against Israel, delivered them into the hands of plunderers, who took them and sold them to the enemies who dwelt round about; nor could they resist their adversaries. But wherever they wished to go, the hand of the Lord was upon them, just as he had spoken and sworn to them; and they were vehemently afflicted. And the Lord raised up judges who would deliver them from the hands of the wasters; but they would not listen even to them, fornicating with alien gods and adoring them. They quickly deserted the way in which their fathers had entered, and hearing the commandments of the Lord, they did all things to the contrary. And when the Lord raised up judges, in their days his mercy was moved, and he heard the groaning of the afflicted and delivered them from the slaughter of the wasters.

**P**ostquam <note>meaning "After"</note> however the judge was dead, they returned and did much worse things than their fathers had done, following alien gods, serving them, and adoring them. They did not abandon their own inventions and the very hard way through which they were accustomed to walk. And the fury of the Lord was angry against Israel, and he said: "Because this nation has made void my covenant which I had established with their fathers, and has despised hearing my voice, I also will not destroy the nations which Joshua left when he died, so that in them I may test Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord and walk in it, as their fathers kept it, or not." So the Lord left all these nations and [intended] to exercise Israel in them, nor did he deliver them into the hands of Joshua.

<margin>iii.</margin>
**H**ae <note>meaning "These"</note> are the nations which the Lord left, that by them he might instruct Israel and all who did not know the wars of the Canaanites; and that afterward their sons might learn to fight with enemies and have a custom of warring: the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites and Sidonians, and the Hivites who dwelt on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath. And the land rested for forty years, and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

**A**ddiderunt <note>meaning "They added" or "They continued"</note> moreover the sons of Israel to do evil in the sight of the Lord. And he strengthened against them Eglon, the king of Moab, because they did evil in the sight of the Lord. And he joined to him the sons of Ammon and Amalek. He went and struck Israel and possessed the City of Palms. And the sons of Israel served Eglon, the king of Moab, for eighteen years. And afterward they cried to the Lord, who raised up for them a savior named Ehud <note>original: "aioth"</note>, the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, who used both hands as the right <note>meaning he was ambidextrous or left-handed</note>. And the sons of Israel sent gifts by him to Eglon, the king of Moab. He made for himself a double-edged sword, having a handle in the middle the length of a palm, and he was girded with it under his garment on his right thigh. And he offered the gifts to Eglon, king of Moab. Now Eglon was exceedingly fat. And when he had offered him the gifts, he followed the companions who had come with him, and returning from Gilgal where the idols were, he said to the king: "I have a secret word for you, O king." And he commanded silence; and all who were around him having gone out, Ehud entered to him. Now he was sitting alone in a cool summer chamber. And he said: "I have a word of God for you." He immediately rose from his throne. And Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly so strongly that the handle followed the blade into the wound, and it was held fast by the thick fat. Nor did he draw out the sword, but left it in the body as he had struck. And immediately, through the secret parts of nature, the dung of the bowels erupted. But Ehud, having very diligently closed the doors of the chamber and secured them with a bolt, went out through a back door. The servants of the king, entering, saw the doors of the chamber closed and said: "Perhaps he is purging his bowels in the summer bedroom." And waiting for a long time until they were ashamed, and seeing that no one opened, they took the key, and opening it, they found their lord lying dead on the ground. But Ehud, while they were in confusion, escaped; and passing the place of the idols from where he had returned, he came to Seirah. And immediately the trumpet sounded in the mountain of Ephraim. And the sons of Israel descended with him, he himself walking at the front. He said to them: "Follow me. For the Lord has delivered our enemies, the Moabites, into our hands." And they descended after him and occupied the fords of the Jordan that cross into Moab, and they did not let anyone pass. But they struck down of the Moabites at that time about ten thousand, all robust and strong men; not one of them could escape. And Moab was humbled that day under the hand of Israel, and the land rested for eighty years.

**A**biit <note>meaning "He went" or "He departed"</note> after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with a plowshare <note>original: "uomere" - an ox-goad or part of a plow</note>; and he also defended Israel.

<margin>iiii.</margin>
**P**ostquam <note>meaning "After"</note> however Ehud was dead, the sons of Israel continued to do evil in the sight of the Lord. And the Lord delivered them into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and he had a commander of his army named Sisera, and he dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. And the sons of Israel cried to the Lord. For he had nine hundred scythed chariots, and for twenty years he had vehemently oppressed them. Now Deborah was a prophetess, the wife of Laphidoth, who judged the people at that time. And she sat under a palm tree, which was called by her name, between Ramah and Bethel in the mountain of Ephraim. For the sons of Israel went up to her for every judgment. She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali. And she said to him: "The Lord God of Israel has commanded you: Go, and lead the army to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand fighting men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zebulun. And I will lead to you at the place of the torrent Kishon, Sisera, the prince of Jabin's army, and his chariots and all the multitude, and I will deliver them into your hand." And Barak said to her: "If you come with me, I will go; if you will not come with me, I will not proceed."

**S**i <note>meaning "If"</note> indeed she said to him: "I will go with you, but in this instance the victory shall not be reputed to you, because Sisera shall be delivered into the hand of a woman." And so Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh. He, having called together Zebulun and Naphtali, went up with ten thousand fighting men, having Deborah in his company. And entering secretly and silently, she placed the peg upon the temple of his head and struck it.

**A**nd the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, who delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years, and they were greatly oppressed by them. **W**hile it was yet evening in Ophrah, which belongs to the family of Abiezer, on that night the Lord said to him: "Take your father's bull, and another bull of seven years, and you shall destroy the altar of Baal which is your father's, and cut down the grove <note>A sacred grove or Asherah pole associated with pagan worship</note> that is around the altar. **S**o the people took food and trumpets, and he commanded all the rest of the multitude to go to their tents, and he gave himself to the battle with the three hundred men. And he divided the three hundred men into three parts, and gave trumpets into their hands, and empty jars, and lamps in the middle of the jars. And he said to them: "What you see me do, do the same. I will enter a part of the camp, and follow what I do. When the trumpet sounds in my hand, you also sound them around the camp and cry out: 'To the Lord and to Gideon!'"

**G**ideon and the hundred men who were with him entered a part of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch of the night; and the guards having been awakened, they began to sound the trumpets and to clash the jars together. And when they sounded in three places around the camp and had broken the vessels, they held the lamps in their left hands and the sounding trumpets in their right hands, and they cried out: "The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!" Each man stood in his place around the enemy camp. And so all the camp was troubled, and wailing and howling, they fled. And nevertheless, the three hundred men persisted in sounding the trumpets. And the Lord sent the sword throughout all the camp, and they struck one another in mutual slaughter, and they fled as far as Beth-shittah and the border of Abel-meholah in Tabbath. And the men of Israel, shouting together from Naphtali and Asher and all Manasseh, pursued Midian. And the Lord gave victory to the people of Israel on that day. And Gideon sent messengers into all the mountain of Ephraim, saying: "Come down to meet Midian and occupy the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan." And all Ephraim cried out and occupied the waters as far as Beth-barah. And they pursued Midian, carrying the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the currents of the Jordan.

Which responded: 'Can I desert my fatness, which both gods and men use, and come to be promoted among the trees?' And the trees said to the fig tree: 'Come and accept the kingdom over us.' Which responded to them: 'Can I desert my sweetness and my most sweet fruits, and go to be moved among the trees?' The trees also spoke to the vine: 'Come and command us.' Which responded: 'Can I desert the wine that cheers God and men, and go to be moved among the trees?' And all the trees said to the buckthorn <note>original: "ramnum"; a thorny shrub</note>: 'Come and command us.' And so Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
