<margin>Isaiah 44</margin>
Thus says the Lord: your maker and your former from the womb, your helper: Do not fear, my servant Jacob: and you, most upright one, whom I have chosen. For I will pour out waters upon the thirsty land, and rivers upon the dry ground. I will pour out my spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring. And they shall spring up among the grass, like willows by the streams of water. This one shall say: I am the Lord’s. And that one shall call himself by the name of Jacob. And this one shall write with his hand to the Lord: and he shall take the name of Israel. I am the first and I am the last: and besides me there is no God. Who is like me? Let him call and announce it: and let him set it out in order for me. Since I established the ancient people: let him announce to them the things that are coming and what shall be in the future. Do not fear, and do not be troubled. From that time I made you hear it, and I announced it. You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me: or any maker whom I do not know? The makers of idols are all nothing: and the things they love most shall not profit them. They themselves are their own witnesses: for they do not see nor understand, so that they may be put to shame. Who has formed a god, or cast a carved image that is useful for nothing? Behold, all its participants shall be put to shame: for the craftsmen are but men. Let them all gather together; let them stand and fear; and let them be put to shame together. The ironsmith worked with his file: he fashioned it in the coals and with hammers: and he worked it with the strength of his arm. He grew hungry and fainted; he drank no water and grew weary. The wood-worker stretched out his rule; he fashioned it with a plane <note>original: "runcina", a carpenter's tool for smoothing wood</note>. He made it with corners, and turned it with a compass: and he made the image of a man like a beautiful person dwelling in a house. He cut down cedars, he took the holm-oak and the oak that stood among the trees of the forest: he planted a pine which the rain nourished: and it became fuel for men. He took part of them and warmed himself: and he kindled a fire and baked bread. But from the rest he made a god and worshipped it: he made a carved image and bowed down before it. Half of it he burned in the fire, and with that half he ate meat: he cooked a meal and was satisfied; he warmed himself and said: "Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire." But from the remainder he made a god, a carved image for himself: he bows down before it, and worships it, and prays to it saying: "Deliver me, for you are my god." They did not know nor understand. For their eyes were covered so they could not see, and their hearts so they could not understand. They do not reflect in their minds: nor do they have the knowledge or sense to say: "Half of it I burned in the fire, and I baked bread over its coals; I cooked meat and ate it; and shall I make the rest of it into an idol? Shall I fall down before a block of wood?" Part of it is ashes. A foolish heart has worshipped it, and he did not deliver his soul, nor did he say: "Perhaps there is a lie in my right hand." Remember these things, Jacob and Israel: for you are my servant. I formed you, you are my servant, Israel: do not forget me. I have wiped away your iniquities like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you. Praise, O heavens, for the Lord has shown mercy; shout, you ends of the earth. Resound with praise, you mountains, the forest and every tree in it: for the Lord has redeemed Jacob, and Israel shall be glorified.

<margin>Isaiah 43</margin>
Thus says the Lord your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and have brought down all the bars, and the Chaldeans boasting in their ships. I am the Lord your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your king.

<margin>Isaiah 43</margin>
Thus says the Lord: who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the rushing waters. Who brought out the chariot and the horse, the army and the strong. They lay down together and shall not rise. They are crushed like flax and extinguished. Do not remember former things, and do not look at the things of old. Behold, I am doing new things: and now they shall spring forth. Surely I will make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the pathless land. The beasts of the field shall glorify me, the dragons and the ostriches: because I have given waters in the wilderness and rivers in the pathless land, to give drink to my most chosen people. This people I have formed for myself: they shall declare my praise. You have not called upon me, Jacob, nor have you labored for me, Israel. You have not offered me the ram of your burnt offering: and you have not glorified me with your victims. I did not make you serve with offerings, nor did I weary you with incense. You did not buy me sweet cane with silver, nor did you fill me with the fat of your sacrifices. Yet you have made me serve with your sins; you have given me labor with your iniquities. I am he, I am he himself, who wipes away your iniquities for my own sake: and I will not remember your sins. Put me in remembrance, and let us be judged together: if you have anything to say to justify yourself. Your first father sinned: and your interpreters <note>meaning the mediators or priests</note> have transgressed against me. And I have profaned the holy princes: I have given Jacob to destruction, and Israel to reproach. And now hear, my servant Jacob, and Israel whom I have chosen.

<column-break/>

I the Lord speak righteousness, announcing what is right. Assemble yourselves and come: and draw near together, you who have been saved from the nations. Those who lift up the sign of their carving have no knowledge: and they pray to a god that cannot save. Announce it and come: and take counsel together. Who made this heard from the beginning? From that time I foretold it. Was it not I, the Lord? And there is no other God besides me: a just God and a savior, there is none except me. Be converted to me and you shall be saved, all you ends of the earth: for I am the Lord and there is no other. I have sworn by myself; the word of righteousness shall go out from my mouth and shall not return: for every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall swear. Therefore they shall say in the Lord: "Righteousness and power are mine." To him they shall come: and all who resist him shall be put to shame. In the Lord all the seed of Israel shall be justified and praised. Bel is broken, Nebo is crushed <note>Bel and Nebo were primary deities of the Babylonian pantheon</note>. Their idols are placed upon beasts and cattle. Your burdens were assembled with a heavy weight even unto weariness: and they were crushed together. They could not save the one carrying them: and their soul shall go into captivity.

<margin>Isaiah 43</margin>
Bring out the people who are blind, yet have eyes; who are deaf, yet have ears. All the nations are gathered together, and the peoples are collected. Who among you is there to announce these things, and make us hear the first things? Let them produce their witnesses and be justified: let them hear and say, "It is true." You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen. So that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed: and after me there shall be none. I am, I am the Lord: and besides me there is no savior. I announced and saved: I made it heard, and there was no stranger among you. You are my witnesses, says the Lord: and I am God. And from the beginning I am he: and there is no one who can rescue from my hand. I will work: and who shall turn it away?

<margin>Isaiah 43</margin>
Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. I am the Lord your Holy One: the creator of Israel, your king. Who made a way in the sea, and a path in the rushing waters. Who brought out the chariot and the horse, the army and the strong. They lay down together and shall not rise. They are crushed like flax and extinguished. Do not remember former things, and do not look at the things of old. Behold, I am doing new things: and now they shall spring forth. Surely I will make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the pathless land. The beasts of the field shall glorify me, the dragons and the ostriches: because I have given waters in the wilderness and rivers in the pathless land, to give drink to my most chosen people. This people I have formed for myself: they shall declare my praise.

Remember these things, and be ashamed: return, you transgressors, to your heart. Remember the former age: that I am God, and there is no God besides me, nor any like me, announcing the end from the beginning, and from the start those things that are not yet done, saying: "My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done." Calling a bird from the east, and from a far-off land a man of my will. And I have spoken and I will bring it to pass; I have created and I will do it. Hear me, you hard-hearted, who are far from righteousness. I have brought my righteousness near, it shall not be far off: and my salvation shall not delay. I will give salvation in Zion: and my glory in Israel. Descend, sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground. There is no throne for the daughter of the Chaldeans: because you shall no longer be called soft and tender. Take the millstone and grind flour; uncover your shame, lay bare your shoulder, reveal your legs, cross the rivers. Your nakedness shall be revealed, and your reproach shall be seen. I will take vengeance, and no man shall resist me.

Hear these things, O house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel: and you came out from the waters of Judah, you who swear in the name of the Lord, and remember the God of Israel—but not in truth nor in righteousness. For they are called from the holy city: and they are founded upon the God of Israel. The Lord of hosts is his name. The former things I announced from that time, and they went out from my mouth: and I made them heard. Suddenly I acted and they came to pass. For I knew that you are stubborn: and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead is bronze. I foretold it to you then, before they came I showed you: lest perhaps you should say: "My idols did these things, and my carvings and my cast images commanded these things which you heard." See it all. But did you not announce it? I have made you hear new things from this time: and things are preserved which you do not know. They are created now, and not from of old: and before this day you did not hear them, lest perhaps you should say: "Behold, I knew it." You neither heard, nor knew, nor was your ear opened back then. For I know that you will surely transgress: and I have called you a transgressor from the womb. For my name’s sake I will put my fury far away: and for my praise I will curb you, lest you perish. Behold, I have refined you: but not like silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of my poverty <note>original: "camino paupertatis mee", often translated elsewhere as the "furnace of affliction"</note>. For my own sake I will do it: so that I may not be blasphemed: and I will not give my glory to another. Hear me, Jacob, and Israel whom I call. I am he, I am the first, and I am the last. My hand also founded the earth: and my right hand measured the heavens. I will call them: and they shall stand together. Gather yourselves all together and hear. Who among them has announced these things? The Lord loved him: he will do his will in Babylon: and his arm against the Chaldeans. I, even I, have spoken: and I called him: I brought him, and his way was made straight. Draw near to me and hear this. I have not spoken in secret from the beginning. From the time before it happened, I was there. And now the Lord and his spirit have sent me.

Thus says the Lord your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel. I am the Lord your God, teaching you useful things, governing you in the way you walk. If only you had attended to my commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea. And your seed would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your womb like its pebbles. His name would not have perished: nor would it have been worn away from before my face. Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans. Announce it with a voice of exultation, make this heard: and carry it even to the ends of the earth. Say: "The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob." They did not thirst in the desert when he led them out. He brought forth water from the rock for them: and he split the rock and the waters flowed.

<summary>This page contains several pivotal prophecies from Isaiah, including a famous satire on the folly of carving idols from the same wood used for firewood, and promises of redemption from Babylon. It emphasizes God's unique sovereignty ("I am the first and the last") and the historical inevitability of Israel's deliverance.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Book of Isaiah, moving from Chapter 48 into the famous "Servant Songs." The text transitions from the promise of return from exile to the specific mission of a chosen Servant who will be a light to the Gentiles and a sufferer for the people's sins.</meta>

<margin>Chapter 49</margin>
There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord. Listen, you islands, and pay attention, you people from afar. The Lord called me from the womb; from my mother’s body he remembered my name. And he made my mouth like a sharp sword. In the shadow of his hand he protected me, and he made me like a chosen arrow. In his quiver he hid me. And he said to me: You are my servant Israel, for in you I will be glorified. And I said: I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength without cause and for nothing. Therefore, my judgment is with the Lord, and my work is with my God. And now says the Lord, who formed me from the womb to be his servant, that I might bring Jacob back to him, and Israel shall be gathered. And I am glorified in the eyes of the Lord, and my God has become my strength. And he said: It is a small thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to convert the dregs <note>original: "feces," referring to the remnants or the lowliest survivors</note> of Israel. Behold, I have given you as a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation even to the ends of the earth. Thus says the Lord, the redeemer of Israel, his Holy One, to the contemptible soul, to the abhorred nation, to the servant of lords: Kings shall see and princes shall rise up and worship because of the Lord, for he is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel who chose you.

**T**hus says the Lord: In an acceptable time I have heard you, and in the day of salvation I have helped you. And I have preserved you and given you as a covenant for the people, so that you might raise up the earth and possess the scattered heritages; so that you might say to those who are bound: "Come out," and to those who are in darkness: "Be revealed." They shall feed along the pastures, and their pastures shall be in all the plain places. They shall not hunger nor thirst, and the heat and the sun shall not strike them, for he who has mercy on them shall lead them, and he shall give them drink at the fountains of waters. And I will make all my mountains into a road, and my paths shall be exalted. Behold, these shall come from afar; and behold, those from the north and from the sea, and these from the southern land. Praise, O heavens, and rejoice, O earth; let the mountains shout with praise, because the Lord has comforted his people and will have mercy on his poor. And Zion <note>The personified city of Jerusalem</note> said: The Lord has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me. Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have mercy on the son of her womb? And even if she should forget, yet I will not forget you. Behold, I have carved you into my hands; your walls are always before my eyes. Your builders have come; those who destroy you and scatter you shall depart from you. Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these are gathered together, they have come to you. As I live, says the Lord, you shall be clothed with all these as an ornament, and you shall put them around you like a bride. For your deserted places and your solitudes and the land of your ruin shall now be too narrow for the inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up shall be driven far away. The children of your barrenness shall yet say in your ears: "The place is too narrow for me; make space for me so that I may dwell." And you shall say in your heart: "Who has fathered these for me? I was barren and not bearing, an exile and a captive; and who has nourished these? I was destitute and alone; and where were these?"

**T**hus says the Lord God: Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and I will raise my signal to the peoples. And they shall bring your sons in their arms, and carry your daughters upon their shoulders. And kings shall be your foster fathers, and queens your nursing mothers. With faces bowed down to the earth they shall worship you, and lick the dust of your feet. And you shall know that I am the Lord, for those who wait for him shall not be put to shame. Shall the prey be taken from the strong man, or can that which was captured by the robust be saved? For thus says the Lord: Even the captivity shall be taken from the strong, and that which was snatched by the robust shall be saved. Indeed, I will judge those who judged you, and I will save your sons. And I will feed your enemies with their own flesh, and they shall be drunk with their own blood as if with new wine; and all flesh shall know that I am the Lord who saves you, and your redeemer, the Strong One of Jacob.

<margin>Chapter 50</margin>
Thus says the Lord: Where is this bill of your mother's divorce by which I dismissed her? Or who is my creditor to whom I sold you? Behold, you were sold for your iniquities, and for your crimes your mother was dismissed. For I came and there was no man; I called and there was no one who would hear. Has my hand been shortened and made small, so that I cannot redeem? Or is there no strength in me to deliver? Behold, with my rebuke I will make the sea a desert, I will turn rivers into dry land. The fish shall rot without water and die of thirst. I will clothe the heavens with darkness, and I will make sackcloth their covering. The Lord has given me a learned tongue, so that I might know how to sustain the one who is weary with a word. He awakens me morning by morning; he awakens my ear so that I might listen as a student <note>original: "quasi magistrum," literally "as to a master," but meaning as one who is being taught</note>. The Lord God has opened my ear, and I do not contradict him; I have not turned back. I gave my body to those who strike me, and my cheeks to those who pluck out the hair; I have not turned my face away from those who rebuke and spit on me. The Lord God is my helper, and therefore I am not disgraced. For this reason, I have set my face like the hardest rock, and I know that I shall not be put to shame. He who justifies me is near. Who is he that would contradict me? Let us stand together. Who is my adversary? Let him approach me. Behold, the Lord God is my helper; who is he that would condemn me? Behold, they shall all wear out like a garment; the moth shall eat them. Who among you fears the Lord, listening to the voice of his servant? He who has walked in darkness and has no light, let him hope in the name of the Lord and lean upon his God.

**A**ll you who kindle a fire, girded with flames: Walk in the light of your fire and in the flames which you have kindled. This has been done to you by my hand; you shall sleep in sorrows.

<margin>Chapter 51</margin>
Listen to me, you who follow what is just and seek the Lord. Look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry of the pit from which you were cut. Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for I called him when he was but one, and I blessed him and multiplied him. Therefore the Lord will comfort Zion, and he will comfort all her ruins. And he will make her desert like a place of delights, and her solitude like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness shall be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of praise. Pay attention to me, my people, and listen to me, my tribe; for a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest as a light to the peoples. My Just One is near, my Savior has gone forth, and my arms shall judge the peoples. The islands shall wait for me.

**A**rise, arise, put on strength, O arm of the Lord! Arise as in the days of old, in the generations of ages past. Have you not struck the proud one and wounded the dragon? Have you not dried up the sea, the water of the vast abyss? You who made the depth of the sea a path, so that the liberated might pass over. And now those who have been redeemed shall return to the Lord, and they shall come into Zion with praise; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads. They shall obtain joy and gladness; sorrow and mourning shall flee away. I

<column-break/>

myself, I am the very one who will comfort you. Who are you, that you should be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man who shall wither like grass? And you have forgotten the Lord your maker, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth. And you have trembled continually all day long before the face of the fury of him who afflicted you and was preparing to destroy. Where is now the fury of the afflicter? He comes quickly, walking to open the way; and he shall not kill unto utter destruction, nor shall his bread fail. For I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea, and its waves swell. The Lord of Hosts is my name. I have put my words in your mouth, and in the shadow of my hand I have protected you, so that you may plant the heavens and found the earth, and say to Zion: You are my people. Awake, awake! Arise, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath. You have drunk even to the bottom of the cup of trembling, and you have drunk even to the dregs. There is no one to sustain her among all the sons she has brought forth, and there is no one to take her hand among all the sons she has nourished. These two things have happened to you: who shall grieve over you? Desolation and destruction, and famine and the sword; who shall comfort you? Your sons have been cast out; they have slept at the head of all the ways like a trapped wild ox, full of the indignation of the Lord, the rebuke of your God. Therefore hear this, you poor little one, drunk, but not with wine. Thus says your Sovereign Lord, and your God who fights for his people: Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of trembling, the bottom of the cup of my indignation; you shall not drink it any longer. And I will put it into the hand of those who have humbled you, and said to your soul: "Bow down, so that we may pass over." And you have laid down your body like the ground, and like a path for those passing by.

<margin>Chapter 52</margin>
**A**rise, arise, put on your strength, O Zion! Put on the garments of your glory, O Jerusalem, city of the Holy One; for the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no longer pass through you. Shake yourself from the dust; arise, sit down, O Jerusalem! Loose the bonds from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion. For thus says the Lord: You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without silver. For thus says the Lord God: My people went down into Egypt at the beginning to be sojourners there; and the Assyrian oppressed them without any cause. And now, what have I here, says the Lord, since my people are taken away for nothing? Their rulers act unjustly, says the Lord, and my name is blasphemed continually all day long. Therefore my people shall know my name in that day; for behold, I myself who spoke am here. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him who announces and preaches peace, announcing good things, preaching salvation, saying to Zion: Your God shall reign! The voice of your watchmen; they have lifted up their voice, together they shall praise; for they shall see eye to eye when the Lord converts Zion. Rejoice and praise together, you deserted places of Jerusalem, because the Lord has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem. The Lord has prepared his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing polluted; go out from the midst of her. Be purified, you who carry the vessels of the Lord, for you shall not go out in a tumult, nor shall you hurry in flight. For the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will gather you together. Behold, my servant shall understand; he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high. Just as many were astonished at you, so shall his look be inglorious among men, and his form among the sons of men. He shall sprinkle many nations; kings shall shut their mouths because of him; for those to whom it was not told about him have seen, and those who did not hear have contemplated.

<margin>Chapter 53</margin>
**L**ord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? And he shall grow up like a tender plant before him, and like a root out of thirsty ground. There is no beauty in him nor comeliness; we saw him, and there was no sightly appearance. And we desired him, despised and the lowliest of men, a man of sorrows and acquainted with infirmity; and his face was as if hidden and despised, wherefore we esteemed him not. Surely he has borne our infirmities, and he has carried our sorrows. And we thought of him as if he were a leper, and struck by God and humbled. But he was wounded for our iniquities; he was bruised for our crimes. The discipline of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; every one has turned aside into his own way. And the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all. He was offered because he himself willed it, and he did not open his mouth. He shall be led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before his shearer he shall be silent, and he shall not open his mouth. He was taken away from distress and from judgment. Who shall declare his generation? For he was cut off from the land of the living. For the crime of my people I struck him. And he shall give the ungodly for his burial, and the rich for his death, because he did no iniquity, nor was deceit in his mouth. And the Lord willed to crush him in infirmity. If he lays down his life for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed, and the will of the Lord shall be directed by his hand. For that which his soul labored, he shall see and be satisfied. By his knowledge, my just servant shall himself justify many, and he himself shall bear their iniquities. Therefore I will distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong, because he delivered his soul unto death and was reputed with the wicked. And he himself bore the sins of many, and prayed for the transgressors.

<margin>Chapter 54</margin>
**P**raise, O barren woman who does not bear! Sing out praise and shout, you who did not give birth; for many are the children of the desolate woman, more than of her who has a husband, says the Lord. Enlarge the place of your tent, and stretch out the skins of your tabernacles—do not spare! Make your cords long and strengthen your pegs. For you shall penetrate to the right and to the left; and your seed shall inherit the nations, and shall inhabit the deserted cities. Do not fear, for you shall not be confounded, nor blush with shame. For you shall not be ashamed, because you shall forget the confusion of your youth, and you shall no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood. For he who made you shall rule over you; the Lord of Hosts is his name. And your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth. For the Lord has called you like a woman forsaken and mourning in spirit, and like a wife cast off from youth, says your God. For a brief moment I forsook you, and with great mercies I will gather you. In a moment of indignation I hid my face a little while from you, and in everlasting mercy I have had compassion on you, says the Lord your redeemer. This is to me as in the days of Noah, to whom I swore that I would no longer bring the waters of Noah over the earth; so have I sworn not to be angry with you, nor to rebuke you. For the mountains shall be moved and the hills shall tremble, but my mercy shall not depart from you, and the covenant of my peace shall not be moved, says the Lord who has mercy on you. Poor little one, tossed by the tempest without any consolation: behold, I will lay your stones in order, and I will found you in sapphires. And I will make your bulwarks of jasper, and your gates of carved stones, and all your borders of desirable stones. All your children shall be taught by the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children. And you shall be founded in justice. Depart far from calumny, for you shall not fear; and from dread, for it shall not come near you. Behold, the settler...

<meta>This page continues the prophetic book of Isaiah, moving from the conclusion of Chapter 54 through the call to the thirsty in Chapter 55, the exhortations on the Sabbath and true fasting in Chapters 56–58, the confession of sin in Chapter 59, and the glorious vision of the new Jerusalem in Chapter 60.</meta>

...to come: he who was not a craftsman <note>original: "fabrum"</note> by his former arrival and assumption. And behold, I have created the smith who blows the coals in the fire and produces a vessel for his work. And I have created the slayer to destroy. Every vessel that is formed against you shall not succeed; and every tongue that resists you in judgment, you shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their justice is with me, says the Lord.

<margin>Isaiah 55</margin>
### **All** you who thirst, come to the waters; and you who have no money, hurry, buy and eat. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without any exchange. Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat what is good, and your soul shall delight in richness. Incline your ear and come to me; hear, and your soul shall live. and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful mercies of David.

### **Behold**, I have given him as a witness to the people, a leader and a teacher to the nations. Behold, you shall call a nation that you did not know, and nations that did not know you shall run to you because of the Lord your God and the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you. Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unjust man his thoughts; and let him return to the Lord, and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he is bountiful in forgiving. For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the Lord. For as the heavens are exalted above the earth, so are my ways exalted above your ways, and my thoughts above your thoughts. And as the rain and the snow come down from heaven and do not return there, but soak the earth and water it, making it to bud and giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes forth from my mouth. It shall not return to me empty, but it shall do whatever I willed, and it shall prosper in the things for which I sent it. For you shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace.

**The mountains** and the hills shall sing praise before you, and all the trees of the countryside shall clap their hands. Instead of the shrub, the fir tree shall come up; and instead of the nettle, the myrtle shall grow; and the Lord shall be named for an everlasting sign that shall not be taken away.

### **Behold**, says the Lord: Keep judgment and do justice, for my salvation is near to come, and my justice to be revealed. Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who takes hold of it, keeping the Sabbath so as not to pollute it, keeping his hands from doing any evil. And let not the son of the stranger who adheres to the Lord say: "The Lord will surely separate me from his people." And let not the eunuch say: "Behold, I am a dry tree." For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: If they keep my Sabbaths and choose the things that I willed and hold fast to my covenant, I will give them a place in my house and within my walls, and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that shall not perish. And the sons of the stranger who adhere to the Lord to worship him and to love his name, to be his servants—all who keep the Sabbath so as not to pollute it and hold fast to my covenant—I will lead them into my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their victims shall please me upon my altar, for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples, says the Lord God, who gathers the dispersed of Israel. I will yet gather others to him besides those who are gathered. All you beasts of the field, come to devour, all you beasts of the forest. His watchmen are all blind; they are all ignorant. They are dumb dogs, unable to bark, seeing vain things, sleeping, and loving dreams. And most impudent dogs, they have never known satiety. The shepherds themselves have lacked understanding. All have turned aside to their own way, every one to his own greed, from the highest to the least. "Come," they say, "let us take wine and be filled with drunkenness; and tomorrow shall be as today, and much more abundant." The just man perishes, and there is no one who considers it in his heart; and men of mercy are taken away, for there is no one who understands. For the just man is taken away from the face of malice. Let peace come; let him rest in his bed who walks in his uprightness. But you, come here, sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the harlot. Against whom have you played? Against whom have you opened your mouth wide and put out your tongue? Are you not wicked children, a lying seed? You who comfort yourselves with idols under every leafy tree, sacrificing little children in the torrents under the high rocks? Your portion is in the parts of the torrent; this is your portion, this is your lot. Even to them you have poured out a drink offering and offered a sacrifice. Shall I not be indignant at these things? Upon a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed, and there you went up to offer victims. And behind the door and behind the post you have set up your memorial, for near me you have uncovered yourself and received an adulteress. You have enlarged your bed and made a covenant with them. You loved their bed with an open hand, and you multiplied your fornications and multiplied your signs. You sent messengers... and you were humbled even to hell <note>original: "inferos," the underworld</note>. You have labored in the multitude of your ways, and you did not say: "I will rest." You found the way of your hand; therefore, you did not ask. For whom have you been solicitous and afraid, that you have lied and not remembered me, nor thought in your heart? For I have been silent and unseeing, and you have forgotten me. I will declare your justice, and your works shall not profit you. When you cry out, let your gathered ones deliver you. But the wind shall carry them all away; the wind shall take them; the breeze shall carry them off. But he who has faith in me shall inherit the land and shall possess my holy mountain. And I will say: Make a way, turn aside from the path, take up the stumbling blocks out of the way of my people. For thus says the High and Lofty One who inhabits eternity, and whose name is Holy: dwelling in the high and holy place, and with a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the contrite. For I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry to the end, because the spirit shall go forth from me, and the breath of life I have made. Because of the iniquity of his greed I was angry and I struck him. I hid from you and was indignant; and he went wandering in the way of his own heart. I saw his ways and I healed him, and I brought him back and restored consolation to him and to his mourners. Creating the fruit of the lips: peace, peace to him who is far off and to him who is near, says the Lord, and I healed him. But the wicked are like a raging sea that cannot rest, and its waves overflow into trampling and mire. There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord God. Cry out, do not stop; lift up your voice like a trumpet and announce their crimes to my people, and their sins to the house of Jacob. For they seek me from day to day and desire to know my ways, as a nation that has done justice and has not forsaken the judgment of its God. They ask me for the judgments of justice and desire to draw near to God. "Why have we fasted and you have not looked? Why have we humbled our souls and you did not know it?" Behold, in the day of your fast your own will is found, and you demand payment from all your debtors. Behold, you fast for strife and contention and strike wickedly with the fist. Do not fast as you do this day,

<column-break/>

to make your voice heard on high. Is this such a fast as I have chosen: for a man to afflict his soul for a day? Is it to bow down his head like a circle <note>original: "circulum," perhaps referring to a bulrush</note> and to spread sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the Lord? Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? Loose the bands of wickedness, undo the heavy bundles. Let those who are broken go free, and break every burden. Deal your bread to the hungry, and bring the needy and the wanderers into your house. When you see the naked, cover him, and do not despise your own flesh. Then shall your light break forth as the morning, and your health shall spring forth speedily; and your justice shall go before your face, and the glory of the Lord shall gather you up. Then you shall call, and the Lord shall hear; you shall cry, and he shall say: "Behold, I am here." If you take away the chain from the midst of you and cease to stretch out your finger and to speak that which is not profitable, when you pour out your soul to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then shall your light rise in darkness, and your darkness shall be as the noonday. And the Lord shall give you rest always and fill your soul with brightness and deliver your bones; and you shall be like a watered garden and like a fountain of water whose waters shall not fail. And the deserts of old shall be built up in you; you shall raise up the foundations of generation upon generation. and you shall be called the builder of hedges, turning the paths into a place of rest. If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your own will on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight and the holy of the Lord glorious, and glorify him while you do not do your own ways and your own will is not found to speak your own word, then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will lift you up above the high places of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

### **Behold**, my hand is not shortened that it cannot save, nor is his ear heavy that it cannot hear. But your sins have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you so that he would not hear. For your hands are polluted with blood and your fingers with iniquity. Your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue speaks iniquity. There is no one who calls upon justice, nor is there any who judges truly; but they trust in nothing and speak vanities. They have conceived labor and brought forth iniquity. They break the eggs of asps and weave the webs of spiders. He who eats of their eggs shall die, and that which is broken shall break out into a basilisk <note>original: "regulum," a mythical venomous serpent</note>. Their webs shall not become clothing, nor shall they cover themselves with their works. Their works are useless works, and the work of iniquity is in their hands. Their feet run to evil and they hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are useless thoughts; wasting and destruction are in their ways. They have not known the way of peace, and there is no judgment in their steps. Their paths are made crooked for them; everyone who treads in them is ignorant of peace. Because of this, judgment is far from you, and justice shall not overtake you. We looked for light, and behold, darkness; for brightness, and we walked in the dark. We have groped for the wall like blind men, and we have felt our way as if we had no eyes. We stumbled at noonday as if in the dark, and in dark places like dead men. We shall all roar like bears and mourn like sighing doves. We looked for judgment, and there is none; for salvation, and it is far from us. For our iniquities are multiplied before you, and our sins have answered us, for our crimes are with us and we have known our iniquities: to sin and to lie against God. And we have turned back from following our God, to speak slander and transgression. We have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood. And judgment is turned backward, and justice has stood far off, for truth has fallen in the street and equity could not enter. And truth has been forgotten, and he who departed from evil lay open to spoil. And the Lord saw, and it appeared evil in his eyes, because there is no judgment. And he saw that there is no man, and he was astonished because there is no one to intercede. And his own arm brought salvation to him, and his justice itself confirmed him. He put on justice as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation was on his head; he put on the garments of vengeance and was covered with a mantle as with zeal: as if for vengeance, for the repayment of indignation to his enemies and a recompense to his adversaries; he will repay the islands their due. And they who are from the west shall fear the name of the Lord, and they from the rising of the sun shall fear his glory, when he shall come like a violent river which the spirit of the Lord drives. And the redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. This is my covenant with them, says the Lord.

### **Arise**, be enlightened, Jerusalem <note>original: "hieru," abbreviated</note>, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon you. For behold, darkness shall cover the earth and a mist the peoples. But the Lord shall arise upon you, and his glory shall be seen in you. And the nations shall walk in your light, and kings in the brightness of your rising. Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these are gathered together, they have come to you. Your sons shall come from afar, and your daughters shall rise up from your side. Then you shall see and abound, and your heart shall wonder and be enlarged, when the multitude of the sea shall be converted to you, and the strength of the nations shall come to you. An inundation of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All they from Sheba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense and announcing the praise of the Lord. All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth shall minister to you. They shall be offered upon my acceptable altar, and I will glorify the house of my majesty. Who are these who fly like clouds and like doves to their windows? For the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea from the beginning, that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the name of the Lord your God and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. And the sons of strangers shall build up your walls, and their kings shall minister to you. For in my indignation I struck you, and in my reconciliation I have had mercy on you. And your gates shall be open continually; they shall not be closed day or night, that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings may be led in. For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you shall perish, and the nations shall be wasted with solitude. And the glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the fir tree, and the box tree, and the pine tree together, to adorn the place of my sanctification; and I will glorify the place of my feet. And the sons of those who humbled you shall come bowing to you, and all who detracted from you shall adore the steps of your feet. And they shall call you the City of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Because you were forsaken and hated, and there was no one who passed through you, I will make you the pride of ages, a joy from generation to generation. For brass I will bring gold, and for iron silver; for wood brass, and for stones iron. And I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers justice. ...no longer shall the sun be for light by day, nor shall the brightness of the moon illuminate you. Instead, the Lord shall be an everlasting light for you, and your God shall be your glory. ### **The Year of the Lord's Favor**

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me. He has sent me to bring good news to the gentle <note>original: "mansuetis," often translated as the "meek" or "humble"</note>, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to those who are bound; to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance for our God; to comfort all who mourn, to provide strength for those who mourn in Zion, and to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a spirit of grief. And they shall be called in that place the strong ones of justice, the planting of the Lord for His glory. And they shall build up the deserts of old, and raise up ancient ruins, and they shall restore the deserted cities that were destroyed from generation to generation. And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of foreigners shall be your farmers and vinedressers. But you shall be called the priests of the Lord; it shall be said to you: "Ministers of our God." You shall eat the strength of the nations, and you shall pride yourselves in their glory. In place of their confusion and shame, they shall praise their portion twice over. Because of this, they shall possess double in their land, and everlasting joy shall be theirs. For I am the Lord, who loves judgment and hates robbery in a burnt offering. And I will make their work truthful, and I will strike an everlasting covenant with them. And their offspring shall be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. All who see them shall acknowledge them, for these are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed.

**I will greatly rejoice** in the Lord, and my soul shall be exalted in my God. For He has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and He has wrapped me in the robe of justice, like a bridegroom adorned with a crown, and like a bride decorated with her jewels. For as the earth brings forth its sprout, and as a garden germinates its seed, so the Lord God will cause justice and praise to sprout before all the nations.

For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her just one goes forth as brightness, and her savior is lit like a lamp. And the nations shall see your just one, and all kings your renowned one. and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord has named. And you shall be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. You shall no longer be called "Forsaken," and your land shall no more be called "Desolate." Instead, you shall be called "My Will is in Her," <note>original: "voluntas mea in ea," referring to the name Hephzibah</note> because the Lord has been well-pleased with you, and your land shall be inhabited. For as a young man lives with a virgin, so your sons shall inhabit you. And as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you. Upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen; all day and all night forever they shall not be silent. You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and give Him no rest until He establishes and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth. The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength: "I will no longer give your grain as food for your enemies, nor shall the sons of foreigners drink the wine for which you have labored." For those who gather it shall eat it and praise the Lord, and those who bring it together shall drink it in my holy courts.

**Pass through, pass through** the gates! Prepare the way for the people! Make the path level and pick up the stones; lift up a standard <note>a military or royal banner</note> for the peoples. For behold, the Lord has made it heard to the ends of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion: "Behold, your Savior comes; behold, His reward is with Him, and His work is before Him." And they shall call them "The Holy People," "The Redeemed of the Lord." And you shall be called "A City Sought Out and Not Forsaken."

### **The Divine Warrior**

Who is this who comes from Edom <note>Edom was a neighboring kingdom often cast as Israel's rival</note>, with dyed garments from Bozrah? This beautiful one in His robe, walking in the multitude of His strength? "It is I, who speaks justice, and am a defender to save." Why then is your clothing red, and your garments like those who tread in the winepress? "I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me. I have trodden them in my fury, and trampled them in my wrath. And their blood is sprinkled upon my garments, and I have stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. I looked around, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was no one to assist. And my own arm saved me, and my indignation itself helped me. And I have trampled the peoples in my fury, and made them drunk in my indignation, and I have cast their strength down to the earth."

I will remember the mercies of the Lord; I will praise the Lord for all things He has rendered to us, and for the multitude of good things to the house of Israel, which He has bestowed upon them according to His indulgence and according to the multitude of His mercies. And He said: "Truly they are my people, sons who do not deny me." And He became a Savior for them. In all their tribulation He was not troubled <note>original: "non est tribulatus," suggesting God's steadfastness or shared suffering depending on the interpretation of the Hebrew source</note>, and the angel of His face saved them. In His love and His indulgence, He Himself redeemed them, and He carried them and lifted them up all the days of the age. But they provoked Him to wrath and afflicted His Holy Spirit. And He was turned into an enemy to them, and He Himself fought against them. And He remembered the days of the age of Moses and his people. Where is He who brought them up from the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is He who placed His Holy Spirit in their midst, who led Moses by the right hand through the arm of His majesty, who divided the waters before them to make for Himself an everlasting name, who led them through the depths like a horse in the desert that does not stumble, like an animal descending into the field? The Spirit of the Lord was its leader; thus you led your people to make for yourself a name of glory.

**Look down from heaven** and see from your holy habitation and the habitation of your glory. Where is your zeal and your strength, the multitude of your heart and your mercies? They have restrained themselves toward me. For you are our Father, though Abraham did not know us, and Israel <note>referring to the patriarch Jacob</note> was ignorant of us. You, O Lord, are our Father; our Redeemer from of old is your name. Why have you made us err, O Lord, from your ways? Why have you hardened our heart so that we did not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance. Your holy people have possessed it as if it were nothing; our enemies have trampled your sanctuary. We have become as we were in the beginning, when you did not rule over us, nor was your name called upon us. O that you would rend the heavens and descend! The mountains would melt away from your face, like the burning of a fire. The waters would boil with glowing fire, so that your name might be made known to your enemies, and the nations might be troubled at your presence. When you do wonderful things, we shall not be able to endure them. You descended, and the mountains flowed away from your face. From of old they have not heard, nor perceived with their ears...

...nor has the eye seen a God besides you, who has prepared such things for those who wait for you. You have met him who rejoices and does justice; in your ways they shall remember you. Behold, you are angry and we have sinned; in these things we have always been, and we shall be saved. And we have all become like one who is unclean; all our justices are like the rag of a menstruating woman. And we have all fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have carried us away. There is no one who calls upon your name, who rises up and holds you. You have hidden your face from us, and you have crushed us by the hand of our iniquity. And now, O Lord, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter, and we are all the work of your hands. Be not very angry, O Lord, and remember our iniquity no longer. Behold, look, we are all your people. The city of your holy one has become a desert; Zion has become a desert; Jerusalem is desolate. The house of our sanctification and our glory, where our fathers praised you, has been burned with fire, and all our desirable things have been turned into ruins. Will you restrain yourself over these things, O Lord? Will you be silent and afflict us vehemently?

### **The New Heavens and the New Earth**

For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be in memory, nor shall they enter the heart. But you shall be glad and exult forever in these things which I create. For behold, I create Jerusalem as an exultation and her people as a joy. And I will exult in Jerusalem and rejoice in my people; and the voice of weeping shall no more be heard in her, nor the voice of crying. There shall no longer be an infant of days there, nor an old man who does not fill his days; for the child shall die at a hundred years, and the sinner at a hundred years shall be accursed. And they shall build houses and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruits. They shall not build and another inhabit; they shall not plant and another eat. For according to the days of a tree shall be the days of my people, and the works of their hands shall endure for my chosen ones. They shall not labor in vain, nor shall they bring forth in trouble; for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their posterity with them. And it shall be that before they cry, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear. The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion and the ox shall eat straw, and dust shall be the serpent’s bread. They shall not hurt nor kill in all my holy mountain, says the Lord.

### HERE ENDS THE BOOK OF ISAIAH THE PROPHET.

## THE PROPHET JEREMIAH, FOR WHOM THIS PROLOGUE IS WRITTEN

Written in a language which, among the Hebrews, seems indeed more rustic than that of Isaiah and Hosea and certain other prophets, but in its meaning it is equal, since he prophesied by the same Spirit. Furthermore, the simplicity of his speech happened because of the place in which he was born; for he was a man of Anathoth, which is even to this day a small village <note>original: "viculus"</note> three miles distant from Jerusalem. He was a priest born of priests, and sanctified in his mother's womb; by his virginity, he dedicated a man of the Gospel to the Church of Christ. This man began to prophesy as a boy, and the captivity of the city and of Judea he witnessed not only in spirit, but also with his fleshly eyes. Already at that time, the Assyrians had transferred the ten tribes to the Medes; already colonies of other nations possessed those lands. Hence, he prophesied only in Judah and Benjamin, and he lamented the ruins of his city in a fourfold alphabet <note>A reference to the acrostic structure of the Book of Lamentations</note>, which we have rendered in its proper measure and meter. Therefore, we have corrected the order of the visions, which was confused among the Hebrews and ourselves, back to its ancient reliability. However, we have omitted the book of Baruch, his scribe, which is neither read nor held among the Hebrews; for all these things, I expect curses from my rivals, to whom it is necessary for me to respond through my individual works. And this besides is to be noted: that the Septuagint <note>original: "septuagesima editio"</note> edition did not choose to include the book of visions again in the way they knew it from the Greeks. Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is from the tribe <note>unclear text in original regarding the tribe name</note>, three miles distant from Jerusalem, was overwhelmed by stones at Tahpanhes in Egypt; he died at the hands of the people. He was buried in a tomb where Pharaoh the king had dwelt, and because by his prayer he had driven away the Egyptian serpents from that land, those who venerate them with great religion made a protection for them.

To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign. And it came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the completion of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the transmigration

of Jerusalem in the fifth month. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

**B**efore I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came forth from the vulva, I sanctified you, and I gave you as a prophet to the nations. And I said: "Ah, ah, ah, <note>An exclamation of distress or inadequacy</note> Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am a child."

**A**nd the Lord said to me: "Do not say, 'I am a child'; for to all to whom I shall send you, you shall go; and everything whatsoever I shall command you, you shall speak. Do not be afraid of their face, for I am with you to deliver you," says the Lord. And the Lord put forth his hand and touched my mouth; and the Lord said to me: "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth. Behold, I have set you today over nations and over kingdoms, to root up, and to pull down, and to waste, and to destroy, and to build, and to plant."

**A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said: "I see a rod of one watching" <note>original: "virgam vigilantem," a wordplay on 'almond' (shaked) and 'watching' (shoked)</note>.

**A**nd the Lord said to me: "You have seen well; for I will watch over my word to perform it."

**A**nd the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying: "What do you see?" And I said: "I see a boiling pot, and its face is from the face of the north."

**A**nd the Lord said to me: "From the north shall evil be opened upon all the inhabitants of the land. For you shall go forth from this one also, and your hands shall be upon your head; because the Lord has crushed your confidence, and you shall have nothing prosperous.'"

It is commonly said: "If a man sends away his wife and, leaving him, she marries another man, will he return to her again? Would that woman not be polluted and defiled?" But you have fornicated with many lovers; yet return to me, says the Lord, and I will receive you. Lift up your eyes to the high places and see where you have not prostituted yourself. Therefore, the showers of rain were withheld, and there was no late-season rain. You have the face of a harlot; you refused to feel shame. So, at least from this moment, call me: "My father, you are the guide of my youth." Will you be angry forever, or will you persist until the end? Behold, you have spoken and done evil things as much as you could.

And the Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah: Have you seen what faithless Israel <note>original: "auersatrix isr'l"</note> has done? She went for herself upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and fornicated there. And I said, after she had done all these things, "Return to me," and she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw this. And I saw that because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I had sent her away and given her a bill of divorce; yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but went and she herself also fornicated. And by the ease of her fornication, she defiled the land; she committed adultery with stone and wood <note>A reference to worshipping idols made of stone and timber</note>. And in all these things, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but only in pretense, says the Lord. And the Lord said to me: Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah. Go and proclaim these words toward the north and say: Return, faithless Israel, says the Lord, and I will not turn my face away from you, for I am holy, says the Lord, and I will not be angry forever. But acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against the Lord your God, and you have scattered your ways to strangers under every leafy tree, and you have not heard my voice, says the Lord. Return, you rebellious children, says the Lord, for I am your husband. And I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you into Zion. And I will give you shepherds according to my heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine. And when you have multiplied and increased in the land in those days, says the Lord, they shall no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the Lord," nor shall it enter their heart, nor shall they remember it, nor shall it be visited, nor shall it be made anymore.

At that time they shall call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all nations shall be gathered to it in the name of the Lord in Jerusalem, and they shall no longer walk after the wickedness of their evil heart. In those days the house of Judah shall go to the house of Israel, and they shall come together from the land of the north to the land which I gave to your fathers. But I said: How shall I place you among the children, and give you a desirable land, the excellent inheritance of the armies of the nations? And I said: You shall call me "Father," and you shall not cease to walk after me. But as a woman despises her lover, so the house of Israel has despised me, says the Lord. A voice was heard in the ways, the weeping and wailing of the children of Israel, because they have made their way wicked; they have forgotten the Lord their God. Return, you rebellious children, and I will heal your rebellions. Behold, we come to you, for you are the Lord our God. Truly the hills were a lie, and the multitude of mountains; truly in the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel. Confusion has devoured the labor of our fathers from our youth—their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters. We shall sleep in our confusion, and our shame shall cover us, because we and our fathers have sinned against the Lord our God from our youth even to this day, and we have not heard the voice of the Lord our God.

If you return, O Israel, says the Lord, return to me. If you take away your stumbling blocks from my sight, you shall not be moved. And you shall swear, "As the Lord lives," in truth, and in judgment, and in justice; and the nations shall bless him, and in him they shall glory. For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Break up your fallow ground <note>original: "nouate uobis nouale," a farming metaphor for spiritual preparation</note>, and do not sow among thorns. Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your hearts, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my indignation go forth like fire and burn, and there be no one to extinguish it, because of the malice of your thoughts. Announce in Judah, and make it heard in Jerusalem. Speak and blow the trumpet in the land; cry out loudly and say: Gather together, and let us enter the fortified cities. Lift up a standard in Zion; be strengthened, do not stand still, for I am bringing evil from the north, and a great destruction. A lion has come up from his lair, and the plunderer of nations has raised himself. He has gone forth from his place to make your land a desolation; your cities shall be laid waste, remaining without an inhabitant. Over this, gird yourselves with haircloth, lament and wail, for the fierce anger of the Lord is not turned away from you. And it shall be in that day, says the Lord, that the heart of the king shall perish, and the heart of the princes; and the priests shall be astonished, and the prophets shall be dismayed.

<margin><note>x</note></margin>
Alas, alas, alas, Lord God! Have you then deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, "Peace shall be to you," and behold, the sword has reached even to the soul? At that time it shall be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A burning wind in the ways which are in the desert—the ways of the daughter of my people—not to fan nor to cleanse. A spirit more full than these shall come to me, and now I will speak my judgments with them. Behold, he shall come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a tempest. His horses are swifter than eagles; woe to us, for we are laid waste! Wash your heart from malice, Jerusalem, that you may be saved; how long shall noxious thoughts abide in you?

For a voice announces from Dan <note>original: "adan," likely a transcription error for "a Dan"</note>, and makes known the idol from mount Ephraim. Remind the nations: behold, it is heard in Jerusalem that guards are coming from a far country, and giving their voice over the cities of Judah. Like keepers of the fields they are placed over her all around, because she has provoked me to wrath, says the Lord. Your ways and your thoughts have done these things to you; this is your wickedness, because it is bitter, because it has touched your heart. My bowels, my bowels! <note>An ancient expression of deep emotional or physical distress</note> I am in pain; the senses of my heart are troubled within me. I will not be silent, for my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet, the cry of battle. Destruction upon destruction is called out, and the whole land is laid waste. Suddenly my tents are destroyed, and my curtains in a moment. How long shall I see the one fleeing, and hear the sound of the trumpet? For my foolish people have not known me; they are senseless and mad children. They are wise to do evil, but to do good they do not know. I looked at the earth, and behold, it was empty and nothing; and at the heavens, and there was no light in them. I saw the mountains, and behold, they were moving, and all the hills were troubled. I looked, and there was no man, and every bird of the air had flown away. I looked, and behold, Carmel was a desert, and all its cities were destroyed before the face of the Lord, and before the face of his fierce anger. For thus says the Lord: All the land shall be desolate, yet I will not make a full end.

<column-break/>

The earth shall mourn, and the heavens above shall be grieved because I have spoken. I have purposed, and I have not repented, nor have I turned away from it. At the noise of the horseman and the archer, the whole city has fled; they have entered the thickets and climbed the rocks. All the cities are forsaken, and no man dwells in them. But you, being laid waste, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself in scarlet, though you are adorned with a golden necklace, and paint your eyes with antimony <note>An ancient mineral used as eyeliner</note>, you mourn in vain. Your lovers have despised you; they will seek your life. For I have heard a voice like that of a woman in labor, distress like that of one bringing forth her first child. The voice of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, spreading out her hands: Woe is me, for my soul faints because of the murderers.

Go about the ways of Jerusalem, and see, and consider, and search in its squares, if you can find a man who performs judgment and seeks faith, and I will be merciful to it. And if they even say, "As the Lord lives," they will also swear this falsely. O Lord, your eyes look upon faith. You have struck them, and they did not grieve; you have bruised them, and they refused to receive discipline. They have hardened their faces more than rock, and they refused to return. But I said: Perhaps they are poor and foolish, ignorant of the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God. I will go therefore to the great men and will speak to them. For they themselves have known the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God. And behold, these together have rather broken the yoke and burst the bonds. Therefore a lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf in the evening has laid them waste, a leopard is watching over their cities. Everyone who goes out from them shall be taken, because their rebellions are multiplied, their desertions are strengthened. How can I be merciful to you? Your children have forsaken me, and they swear by those who are not gods. They were filled, and they committed adultery, and they lived luxuriously in the house of the harlot. They became like lusty horses and stallions; each one neighed after his neighbor's wife. Shall I not visit for these things, says the Lord? And shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation?

Scale her walls and destroy, but do not make a full end. Take away her branches, for they are not the Lord's. For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly treacherous against me, says the Lord. They have denied the Lord and said: "It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us. We shall not see the sword and famine." The prophets spoke into the wind, and there was no answer in them. Therefore these things shall happen to them. Thus says the Lord God of hosts: Because you have spoken this word, behold, I am making my words in your mouth as fire, and this people as wood, and it shall devour them. Behold, I will bring upon you a nation from afar, O house of Israel, says the Lord; a robust nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you will not know, nor understand what it says. Its quiver is like an open sepulcher; they are all valiant men. And it shall eat up your harvest and your bread; it shall devour your sons and your daughters. It shall eat your flock and your herds; it shall eat your vineyard and your fig tree, and it shall crush with the sword your fortified cities in which you trust. Nevertheless, in those days, says the Lord, I will not make a full end of you. And if you say, "Why has the Lord our God done all these things to us?" you shall say to them: Just as you have forsaken me and served foreign gods in your land, so shall you serve strangers in a land that is not yours. Announce this to the house of Jacob, and make it heard in Judah, saying:

Hear this, O foolish people, who have no heart; who having eyes see not, and ears that hear not. Will you not then fear me, says the Lord? and will you not grieve before my face? I who have placed the sand as a bound for the sea, an everlasting command which it shall not pass. And they shall be moved and shall not prevail; and its waves swell and shall not pass over it. But this people has an incredulous and exasperating heart. They have departed and gone away, and they have not said in their heart: "Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and the late rain in its season, and keeps for us the fullness of the yearly harvest." Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withheld good from you, because among my people were found wicked men lying in wait like fowlers, setting snares and traps to catch men. As a trap is full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich, they have grown fat and sleek, and they have passed over my words most wickedly. They have not judged the cause of the widow, they have not directed the cause of the orphan. Shall I not visit for these things, says the Lord? Or shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation?

Astonishment and wonders have been done in the land. The prophets prophesied a lie, and the priests applauded with their hands, and my people loved such things. What then shall be done in its end?

Be strengthened, children of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a standard over Beth-haccerem; for evil is seen from the north, and a great destruction. I have compared the daughter of Zion to a beautiful and delicate woman; shepherds and their flocks shall come to her. They have pitched their tents in her all around; each one shall feed those who are under his hand. Sanctify war against her; arise, and let us go up at midday. Woe to us, for the day has declined, for the evening shadows are grown longer. Arise, and let us go up in the night, and let us destroy her houses, for thus says the Lord of hosts: Cut down her wood, and cast up a mound around Jerusalem. This is the city to be visited; all oppression is in the midst of her. As a cistern keeps its water cold, so she has made her malice cold. Iniquity and destruction shall be heard in her; before me always are infirmity and wounds. Be instructed, Jerusalem, lest my soul depart from you, lest I make you a deserted land, uninhabitable.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: They shall gather the remnants of Israel like a grape-gatherer in a vineyard. Turn back your hand like a vintager to the basket. To whom shall I speak? And whom shall I call to witness, that he may hear? Behold, the word of the Lord has become a reproach to them, and they will not receive it. Therefore I am full of the fury of the Lord; I am weary with holding it in. Pour it out upon the child in the street, and upon the council of young men together. For the man with the woman shall be taken; the old man with him who is full of days. And their houses shall pass to others, their lands and their wives together; for I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord. From the least of them even to the greatest, all are devoted to avarice; and from the prophet even to the priest, all practice deceit. And they healed the wound of the daughter of my people with ignominy, saying, "Peace, peace," when there was no peace. They were confounded because they committed abomination. Rather, they were not confounded by their confusion, and they knew not how to blush. Therefore they shall fall among those who fall; in the time of their visitation they shall collapse, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the ways and see, and ask for the ancient paths <note>original: "uijs antiquis," referring to the traditional laws and ways of the ancestors</note>, which is the good way, and walk in it, and you shall find refreshment for your souls. And they said: "We will not walk in it." And I appointed watchmen over you. Hear the sound of the trumpet. And they said: "We will not hear." Therefore hear, you nations, and know, O congregation, how great things I will do to them. Hear, O earth! Behold, I will bring evil upon this people, the fruit of their own thoughts, because they have not heard my words, and my law...

<summary>This section of the Book of Jeremiah presents God's indictment of Israel and Judah for their spiritual adultery and refusal to repent. It details the coming judgment—a "lion from the north"—while contrasting the superficial peace offered by false prophets with the "ancient paths" of true faith.</summary>
<keywords>Jeremiah, repentance, Israel and Judah, Josiah, destruction from the North, ancient paths, spiritual adultery, Jerusalem</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the prophet Jeremiah's warnings to the kingdom of Judah. In the previous section, the prophet used the metaphor of a failed marriage to describe Israel's unfaithfulness. Here, the tone shifts toward the practical and spiritual consequences of that betrayal: the rejection of empty rituals, the threat of invasion from the "north," and the famous "Temple Sermon" where Jeremiah warns that even the holy Temple cannot protect a people who continue to do evil.</meta>
