Your <term>holocausts</term> <note>These were entirely burnt offerings, where the whole animal was consumed by fire</note> are not accepted, and your sacrifices do not please me. Therefore, the Lord says: Behold, I will bring ruins upon this people; and fathers and sons together, neighbor and friend, shall fall and perish.

**T**hus says the Lord: Behold, a people comes from the land of the north; a great nation shall rise from the ends of the earth. They shall take up the bow and the shield; they are cruel and will show no mercy. Their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall mount upon horses, prepared like a man for battle against you, O daughter of Zion. We have heard the report of them; our hands have grown feeble; trouble has taken hold of us, and sorrows like those of a woman in labor. Do not go out into the fields, and do not walk in the way, for the sword of the enemy and fear are on every side. O daughter of my people, gird yourself with sackcloth and sprinkle yourself with ashes; make for yourself mourning as for an only son, a bitter lamentation, for the destroyer shall suddenly come upon you. I have set you as a strong prover among my people; you shall know and test their way. All these princes are deviating, walking deceitfully; they are copper and iron, all of them are corrupt. The bellows have failed in the fire; the lead is consumed. The smelter has melted in vain, for their wickednesses are not consumed. Call them rejected silver, because the Lord has cast them away.

**S**tand in the gate of the house of the Lord, and preach there this word, and say: Hear the word of the Lord, all you of Judah who enter through these gates to adore the Lord. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Make your ways and your intentions good, and I will dwell with you in this place. Do not trust in lying words, saying: "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is!" For if you truly direct your ways and your intentions, if you execute judgment between a man and his neighbor, if you do not oppress the stranger, the orphan, and the widow, nor shed innocent blood in this place, and do not walk after strange gods to your own harm—then I will dwell with you in this place, in the land which I gave to your fathers, from age to age. Behold, you trust in lying words that will not profit you: to steal, to murder, to commit adultery, to swear falsely, to offer libations to <term>Baal</term> <note>Baal was a Canaanite storm and fertility god whose worship often competed with that of the God of Israel</note>, and to go after strange gods whom you do not know. And yet you come and stand before me in this house, in which my name is invoked, and say: "We are delivered," because we have done all these abominations. Has this house, then, in which my name is invoked, become a den of robbers in your eyes? <note>This phrase, "den of robbers," is famously quoted by Jesus when he clears the Temple in the New Testament</note> I, even I, have seen it, says the Lord. Go to my place in <term>Shiloh</term> <note>Shiloh was an early religious center of Israel that had been destroyed, serving here as a warning of what could happen to Jerusalem</note>, where my name dwelt at the beginning, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel. And now, because you have done all these works, says the Lord—and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, and you did not hear; and I called you, and you did not answer—I will do to this house, in which my name is invoked and in which you have confidence, and to the place which I gave to you and your fathers, just as I did to Shiloh. And I will cast you out from my face, just as I cast out all your brothers, the entire offspring of Ephraim.

Therefore, do not pray for this people, nor take up praise or prayer for them, and do not resist me, for I will not hear you. Do you not see what they do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough to make cakes for the <term>Queen of Heaven</term> <note>Likely referring to the Mesopotamian goddess Ishtar</note>, and to pour out libations to strange gods, to provoke me to anger. Do they provoke me to anger, says the Lord? Is it not themselves, to the confusion of their own faces?

**T**herefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, my fury and my indignation are poured out upon this place, upon men and upon beasts, and upon the trees of the region, and upon the fruits of the land, and it shall be kindled and shall not be extinguished.

**T**hus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Add your holocausts to your sacrifices, and eat the meat. For I did not speak with your fathers, nor did I command them on the day I led them out of the land of Egypt concerning the matter of holocausts and sacrifices. But this word I commanded them, saying: "Hear my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk in every way that I have commanded you, so that it may be well with you." But they did not hear, nor did they incline their ear, but went away in their own pleasures and in the perversity of their wicked heart, and they have gone backward and not forward from the day their fathers went out of the land of Egypt until this day. And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early every day and sending them, yet they did not hear me nor incline their ear, but they hardened their neck and have done worse than their fathers.

**A**nd you shall speak all these words to them, and they will not hear you; and you shall call them, and they will not answer you. And you shall say to them: This is the nation that did not hear the voice of the Lord its God, nor receive discipline. Faith has perished, and it is taken away from their mouth. Cut off your hair and cast it away; and take up a lamentation on high, for the Lord has rejected and forsaken the generation of his fury. For the children of Judah have done evil in my eyes, says the Lord. They have set their offenses in the house in which my name is invoked, to defile it. And they have built the high places of <term>Tophet</term> <note>Tophet was a location in the Valley of Hinnom associated with the sacrifice of children by fire</note>, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire—which I did not command, nor did it enter my heart. Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when it shall no longer be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; and they shall bury in Tophet because there is no other place. And the corpses of this people shall be food for the birds of the heaven and for the beasts of the earth, and there shall be no one to drive them away. And I will cause to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride; for the land shall be a desolation.

**A**t that time, says the Lord, they shall cast out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of its princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of those who dwelt in Jerusalem, from their graves. And they shall spread them out before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they loved, and which they served, and after which they walked, and which they sought and adored. They shall not be gathered nor buried; they shall be like dung upon the face of the earth. And death shall be chosen rather than life by all the survivors who remain of this wicked family in all the places to which I have driven them, says the Lord of hosts.

**A**nd you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Does he who falls not rise again? And he who has turned away, will he not return? Why then has this people in Jerusalem turned away with a contentious turning? They have laid hold of a lie and refused to return. I attended and listened; no one speaks what is good; there is no one who does penance for his sin, saying: "What have I done?" All are turned to their own course, like a horse rushing headlong into battle. Even the kite in the sky knows its time; the turtle-dove, the swallow, and the stork observe the time of their coming, but my people have not known the judgment of the Lord.

<column-break/>

**H**ow do you say, "We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us"? Truly, the lying pen of the scribes has worked a lie. The wise men are confounded, they are terrified and taken. For they have rejected the word of the Lord, and there is no wisdom in them.

**T**herefore, I will give their women to strangers and their fields to heirs, for from the least to the greatest, all follow avarice; from the prophet to the priest, all practice deceit. And they healed the wound of the daughter of my people to her shame, saying: "Peace, peace," when there was no peace. They were confounded because they committed abomination; yet they were not confounded by their confusion, and they did not know how to blush. Therefore, they shall fall among those who fall; in the time of their visitation they shall perish, says the Lord. Gathering, I will gather them, says the Lord; there is no grape on the vines, and there are no figs on the fig tree. The leaf has withered, and I have given them the things that are passed away. Why do we sit still? Assemble yourselves, and let us enter the fortified city, and let us be silent there, for the Lord our God has made us silent and given us the water of gall to drink. For we have sinned against the Lord. We looked for peace, and there was no good; for a time of healing, and behold, terror. From Dan was heard the snorting of his horses. At the sound of the neighing of his warriors, the whole land was moved; and they came and devoured the land and its fullness, the city and its inhabitants. For behold, I will send among you serpents, basilisks, for which there is no charm, and they shall bite you, says the Lord. My sorrow is beyond sorrow; my heart within me is mourning. Behold, the voice of the cry of the daughter of my people from a far country. "Is the Lord not in Zion, or is her King not in her?" Why then have they provoked me to anger with their idols and with foreign vanities? The harvest has passed, the summer is ended, and we are not saved. For the wound of the daughter of my people, I am wounded and covered in darkness; astonishment has taken hold of me. Is there no balm in <term>Gilead</term> <note>Gilead was famous for its medicinal resins used for healing</note>, or is there no physician there? Why then is the scar of the daughter of my people not closed? Who will give water to my head and a fountain of tears to my eyes? And I will weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people! Who will give me a traveler's lodging in the wilderness, so that I may leave my people and go away from them? For they are all adulterers and a company of traitors. They have stretched their tongue like a bow of lies and not of truth. They have grown strong on the earth because they have proceeded from evil to evil, and they have not known me, says the Lord. Let every man guard himself from his neighbor, and have no trust in any brother, for every brother will surely supplant, and every friend will walk deceitfully. A man will deride his brother and they will not speak the truth. For they have taught their tongue to speak lies; they have labored to act wickedly. Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit; in deceit they have refused to know me, says the Lord.

**T**herefore, thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will melt and test them. For what else shall I do before the face of the daughter of my people? Their tongue is a wounding arrow, it has spoken deceit; with his mouth he speaks peace with his friend, but secretly he sets an ambush for him. Shall I not visit them for these things, says the Lord, or shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation? For the mountains I will take up weeping and lamentation, and for the beautiful places of the desert, a wailing, because they are burnt up, because there is no man passing through, and they have not heard the voice of the owner. From the birds of the air to the cattle, they have migrated and gone away. And I will make Jerusalem into heaps of sand and a den of dragons, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation because there is no inhabitant. Who is the wise man who may understand this, and to whom the word of the mouth of the Lord may come, so that he may declare it? Why has the land perished like a wilderness, because there is no one passing through? And the Lord said: Because they have forsaken my law which I gave them, and have not heard my voice, nor walked in it, but have gone after the perversity of their own heart and after the Baals which they learned from their fathers. Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed this people with wormwood and give them the water of gall to drink. And I will scatter them among nations which neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until they are consumed.

**T**hus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Consider and call the mourning women, and let them come; and send for those who are wise and let them hurry. Let them make haste and take up a lamentation over you. And let your eyes shed tears and your eyelids flow with water, for the voice of lamentation is heard from Zion. "How are we wasted and greatly confounded? Because we have left the land, because our dwellings are cast down." Hear, therefore, O women, the word of the Lord, and let your ears receive the word of his mouth. For death has climbed up through your windows and entered your houses, to destroy the little ones from the outside and the young men from the streets. Speak: Thus says the Lord: The corpses of men shall fall like dung upon the face of the country, and like hay behind the back of the reaper, and there is no one to gather them. Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord who performs mercy and judgment and justice on the earth. For these things please me, says the Lord. Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will visit everyone who has the circumcision of the foreskin—upon Egypt and upon Judah and upon Edom and upon the children of Ammon and upon Moab, and upon all who have their hair clipped, dwelling in the desert; for all the nations have the foreskin, but the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

**H**ear the word which the Lord has spoken over you, O house of Israel. And the Lord says: Do not learn according to the ways of the nations, and do not fear the signs of heaven which the nations fear, for the laws of the people are vain. For a work of the hands of the craftsman has cut wood from the forest with an axe. He has decorated it with silver and gold; he has fastened it with nails and hammers so that it does not fall apart. They are fashioned like a palm tree and do not speak; they must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they can do neither good nor evil. There is none like you, O Lord; you are great, and your name is great in strength. Who shall not fear you, O King of the nations? For yours is the glory among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms there is none like you. They shall perish together as foolish and dull. The doctrine of their vanity is wood. Silver wrapped in cloth is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Ophaz, the work of the craftsman and the hands of the goldsmith. Hyacinth <note>A deep blue or violet fabric</note> and purple are their clothing; all these are the work of craftsmen. But the Lord is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his threatening. Thus you shall say to them: The gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from those things that are under heaven.

**B**ehold, I will bring evils upon them from which they shall not be able to escape; and they shall cry out to me, and I will not hear them. And the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall go and cry to the gods to whom they offer libations, and they shall not save them in the time of their affliction. For according to the number of your cities were your gods, O Judah; and according to the number of the streets of Jerusalem you have set up altars of confusion, altars to offer libations to Baal <note>original: *baalim*, the plural form of the Canaanite deity Baal</note>.

**Y**ou, therefore, do not pray for this people, and do not take up praise or prayer for them, for I will not hear in the time of their cry to me, in the time of their affliction.

**W**hat is it that my beloved does in my house, committing many crimes? Can the holy flesh take away your wickedness from you, in which you have gloried? The Lord called your name a plentiful olive tree, fair, fruitful, and beautiful; at the noise of a great speech a fire has been kindled in it, and its shrubs are burnt up. And the Lord of Hosts, who planted you, has spoken evil against you for the evils of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they have done to themselves to provoke me, by offering libations to Baal. But you, O Lord, have shown me and I have known; then you showed me their designs. And I was like a gentle lamb that is carried to the victim; and I did not know that they had devised counsels against me, saying: "Let us put wood in his bread, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, and let his name be remembered no more." But you, O Lord of Sabaoth, who judge justly and test the reins and hearts <note>An ancient idiom meaning the innermost thoughts and emotions</note>, let me see your vengeance upon them. **T**herefore thus says the Lord to the men of Anathoth <note>Jeremiah’s hometown, where his own neighbors plotted against him</note> who seek your life and say: "You shall not prophesy in the name of the Lord, so that you do not die by our hands."

**T**herefore thus says the Lord of Hosts: Behold, I will visit them. Their young men shall die by the sword; their sons and daughters shall die by famine. And there shall be no remnant of them. For I will bring evil upon the men of Anathoth, in the year of their visitation.

**Y**ou are indeed just, O Lord, but if I speak with you, nevertheless I will speak just things to you: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why is it well with all who transgress and act iniquitously? You have planted them, and they have taken root; they grow and bring forth fruit. You are near to their mouths, but far from their hearts. How long shall the land mourn, and the herb of every field wither for the wickedness of those who dwell in it? The animal and the bird are consumed because they said: "He shall not see our last end." If you have labored running with footmen, how can you contend with horses? And if you have been secure in a land of peace, what will you do in the pride of the Jordan? For even your brothers and the house of your father, even they have fought against you, and have cried out after you with a full voice. Do not believe them when they speak good things to you. I have left my house; I have forsaken my inheritance; I have given my beloved soul into the hands of its enemies. My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; it has uttered its voice against me, therefore I have hated it. Is my inheritance a speckled bird to me? Is the bird gathered all around? Come, gather all the beasts of the earth; hasten to devour. Many shepherds have demolished my vineyard; they have trampled my portion. They have made my desirable portion a desert of solitude. They have laid it in desolation, and it has mourned over me.

**W**ith desolation is all the land made desolate, because there is no one who considers it in his heart. Upon all the ways of the desert the wasters have come, for the sword of the Lord shall devour from one end of the earth to the other. There is no peace for all flesh. They have sown wheat and reaped thorns; they have received an inheritance, and it shall not profit them. You shall be confounded by your fruits, because of the anger of the Lord's fury. Thus says the Lord against all my wicked neighbors who touch the inheritance

Your words were found, and I ate them; and your word became a joy and the gladness of my heart, for your name is invoked upon me, O Lord God of hosts <note>original: *domine deus exercituum*</note>. I did not sit in the council of jesters, nor did I boast before your hand; I sat alone because you filled me with threats. Why has my pain become perpetual, and my wound desperate? And if you separate the precious from the worthless, you shall be as my mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them. And I will make you to this people a strong wall of bronze; and they shall fight against you and not prevail, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you, says the Lord. And I will free you from the hand of the wicked, and I will redeem you from the hand of the strong.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: You shall not take a wife, nor shall you have sons and daughters in this place. For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them, and concerning their fathers from whose stock they were born in this land: they shall die by grievous deaths. They shall not be lamented, nor shall they be buried; they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth. They shall be consumed by the sword and by famine, and their carcasses shall be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. For thus says the Lord: Do not enter the house of feasting, nor go to mourn, nor comfort them; for I have taken away my peace from this people, says the Lord, even my mercy and compassions. Both great and small shall die in this land. They shall not be buried, nor shall men lament for them, nor cut themselves for them, nor make themselves bald. They shall not break bread for those in mourning to comfort them over the dead; nor shall they give them the cup of consolation to drink for their father or mother. And you shall not enter the house of feasting to sit with them, and to eat and drink. For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will cause to cease from this place, before your eyes and in your days, the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride. Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when it shall no longer be said, "The Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt," but, "The Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of the north and from all the lands to which he had cast them out." And after this, I will send them many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain and every hill and from the caves of the rocks. For my eyes are upon all their ways; they are not hidden from my face, nor has their iniquity been concealed from my eyes. O Lord, my strength and my might, and my refuge in the day of tribulation, to you the nations shall come from the ends of the earth and say: "Truly our fathers possessed lies, vanity that did not profit them. Shall a man make strange gods for himself, when they are not gods?" Therefore, behold, I will show them this time; I will show them my hand and my power, and they shall know that my name is the Lord.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: Arise and go down to the potter's house, and there you shall hear my words. And I went down to the potter's house, and behold, he was doing a work upon the wheel. And the vessel that he was making of clay with his hands was spoiled; and turning, he made it into another vessel, as it seemed good in his eyes to make it. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Can I not do to you as this potter does, O house of Israel, says the Lord? Behold, as clay in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel. Suddenly I will speak against a nation and against a kingdom, to root out and destroy and scatter it. If that nation does penance for its evil of which I have spoken against it, I also will repent of the evil that I thought to do to it. And suddenly I will speak of a nation and a kingdom, to build and to plant it. If it does evil in my eyes so as not to hear my voice, I will repent of the good that I spoke of doing to it. Now therefore, say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am framing evil against you and thinking a thought against you. Let everyone return from his evil way, and direct your ways and your efforts. But they said: "We have despaired. For we will go after our own thoughts, and we will each do the perversity of his own evil heart." Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask the nations: Who has heard such horrible things as the virgin of Israel has done excessively? Shall the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? Or can the cold flowing waters that break forth be plucked up? Yet my people have forgotten me, sacrificing to vanities in vain, and they stumble in their ways, in the paths of the world, to walk in a path not trodden, so that their land should become a desolation and a perpetual hissing. Everyone who passes by it shall be astonished and shall shake his head. As a burning wind I will scatter them before the enemy; I will show them the back and not the face in the day of their perdition. And they said: "Come and let us devise plans against Jeremiah. For the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come and let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not heed any of his words." Heed me, O Lord, and hear the voice of my adversaries. Is evil rendered for good, that they have dug a pit for my soul? Remember that I stood in your sight to speak good for them, and to turn away your indignation from them. Therefore give their children to famine and deliver them into the hands of the sword. Let their wives be childless and widows, and let their men be slain by death; let their young men be pierced with the sword in battle. Let a cry be heard from their houses. For you will bring a robber upon them suddenly, because they have dug a pit to take me and have hidden snares for my feet. But you, Lord, know all their counsel against me unto death. Do not be merciful to their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from your face. Let them fall in your sight; in the time of your fury, deal with them.

<meta>This page continues the prophetic ministry of Jeremiah. Following the symbolic lesson at the potter’s house, Jeremiah now performs a public sign by breaking a flask to signify the irreversible destruction of Jerusalem. The text records the first physical persecution of the prophet by the temple authorities and transitions into specific judgments against the final kings of Judah (Zedekiah, Jehoiakim, and Coniah) and the corruption of the religious leadership.</meta>

**Y**ou have seduced me, Lord, and I was seduced; you were stronger than I, and you have prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me. ...they have made their fathers forget my name because of Baal. Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, and let him who has my word speak my word faithfully. They do not profit this people at all, says the Lord. 

If this people, or a prophet, or a priest asks you, "What is the burden <term>burden: *onus* — a wordplay in Hebrew and Latin meaning both a prophetic "oracle" and a "heavy load"</term> of the Lord?" you shall say to them, "You are the burden! I will cast you off," says the Lord. As for the prophet, the priest, or the people who say, "The burden of the Lord," I will punish that man and his house. This is what you shall say, every one to his neighbor and every one to his brother: "What has the Lord answered?" and "What has the Lord spoken?" But you shall mention the burden of the Lord no more, for every man's word will be his own burden. You have perverted the words of the living God, the Lord of hosts, our God, says the Lord to the prophet. Why did you not say, "The Lord," and "What has the Lord spoken?" But if you say, "The burden of the Lord," therefore thus says the Lord: Because you said this word, "The burden of the Lord," and I sent to you saying, "Do not say 'the burden of the Lord,'" therefore, behold, I will surely lift you up as a burden and forsake you, and the city that I gave to you and your fathers, and cast you out of my sight. I will bring upon you everlasting reproach and perpetual shame, which shall never be forgotten.

The Lord showed me two baskets full of figs placed before the temple of the Lord. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the princes of Judah, the craftsmen, and the smiths from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon. One basket had very good figs, like the figs that ripen first; but the other basket had very bad figs, which were so bad they could not be eaten. Then the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said, "Figs; the good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten." Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so will I regard the captives of Judah whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good. I will set my eyes upon them for their favor, and I will bring them back to this land; I will build them and not pull them down; I will plant them and not pluck them up. I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, for they shall return to me with their whole heart. But like the bad figs which cannot be eaten because they are so bad, says the Lord, so will I give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this city and those who dwell in the land of Egypt. I will deliver them to be a horror and an affliction to all the kingdoms of the earth, to be a reproach, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I have driven them. I will send the sword, famine, and pestilence among them until they are consumed from the land that I gave to them and their fathers.

The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah (which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon), which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: From the thirteenth year of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, even to this day—this is the twenty-third year—the word of the Lord has come to me, and I have spoken to you persistently, rising early and speaking, but you have not listened. And the Lord has sent to you all his servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, but you have not listened or inclined your ears to hear when they said: "Turn now every one of you from his evil way and from your wicked deeds, and you shall dwell in the land that the Lord has given to you and your fathers forever and ever. Do not go after other gods to serve them and worship them, and do not provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, and I will do you no harm." But you have not listened to me, says the Lord, that you might provoke me to anger with the works of your hands to your own hurt. Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Because you have not heard my words, behold, I will send for all the tribes of the north, says the Lord, and for Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant <note>God refers to the pagan king as his "servant" because he is the instrument of God's judgment.</note>, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants, and against all these surrounding nations. I will take from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp. I will bring upon that land all the words that I have spoken against it, everything written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations. For many nations and great kings shall make slaves of them also, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands. For thus says the Lord God of the hosts of Israel: "Take this cup of the wine of fury from my hand, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it. Therefore you shall prophesy all these words to them and say: "The Lord roars from on high, and from his holy habitation he utters his voice; he will roar mightily over his fold; he shouts, like those who tread grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth. Thus says the Lord of hosts: "Behold, disaster is going forth from nation to nation, and a great tempest is stirring from the farthest parts of the earth. And those slain by the Lord on that day shall extend from one end of the earth to the other. They shall not be lamented, or gathered, or buried; they shall be as dung on the surface of the ground. Wail, you shepherds, and cry out; roll in ashes, you lords of the flock, for the days of your slaughter and dispersion have come, and you shall fall like a choice vessel. Flight shall fail the shepherds, and escape the lords of the flock. Hark, the cry of the shepherds and the wail of the lords of the flock! For the Lord is laying waste their pasture, and the peaceful meadows are silent because of the fierce anger of the Lord. Like a lion he has left his covert, for their land has become a waste because of the sword of the oppressor and because of his fierce anger."

In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the Lord: "Thus says the Lord: Stand in the court of the Lord's house, and speak to all the cities of Judah that come to worship in the house of the Lord all the words that I command you to speak to them; do not hold back a word. It may be they will listen, and every one turn from his evil way, that I may relent of the disaster that I intend to do to them because of their evil deeds. You shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord: If you will not listen to me, to walk in my law which I have set before you, and to listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I send to you urgently, rising early and sending, though you have not listened, then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.'" The priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord. And when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to speak to all the people, then the priests and the prophets and all the people laid hold of him, saying, "You shall surely die! Why have you prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, 'This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate, without inhabitant'?" And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the Lord. When the princes of Judah heard these things, they came up from the king’s house to the house of the Lord and took their seat in the entry of the New Gate of the house of the Lord. Then the priests and the prophets said to the princes and to all the people, "This man deserves the sentence of death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears." Then Jeremiah spoke to all the princes and all the people, saying, "The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the words you have heard. Now therefore mend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will relent of the disaster that he has pronounced against you. But as for me, behold, I am in your hands. Do with me as seems good and right to you. Only know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves and upon this city and its inhabitants, for in truth the Lord sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears." Then the princes and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve the sentence of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God." And certain of the elders of the land arose and spoke to all the assembled people, saying: "Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and said to all the people of Judah: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, Zion shall be plowed as a field; Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.' Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the Lord and entreat the favor of the Lord, and did not the Lord relent of the disaster that he had pronounced against them? But we are about to bring great disaster upon ourselves." There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the Lord, Uriah the son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and against this land in words exactly like those of Jeremiah. And when King Jehoiakim, with all his warriors and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But when Uriah heard of it, he was afraid and fled and escaped to Egypt. Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt, Elnathan the son of Achbor and others with him, and they brought Uriah from Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and dumped his dead body into the burial place of the common people. But the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so that he was not given over to the people to be put to death.

In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord: Thus says the Lord to me: "Make yourself bonds and yoke-bars, and put them on your neck. Send word to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the sons of Ammon, the king of Tyre, and the king of Sidon by the hand of the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah. Give them this charge for their masters: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: This is what you shall say to your masters: It is I who by my great power and my outstretched arm have made the earth, with the men and animals that are on the earth, and I give it to whomever it seems right to me. Now I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, my servant, and I have given him also the beasts of the field to serve him. All the nations shall serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time of his own land comes; then many nations and great kings shall make him their slave. But if any nation or kingdom will not serve this house of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence, says the Lord, until I have consumed it by his hand. So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your fortune-tellers, or your sorcerers, who are saying to you, "You shall not serve the king of Babylon." For it is a lie that they are prophesying to you, with the result that you will be removed far from your land, and I will drive you out, and you will perish. But any nation that will bring its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him, I will leave on its own land, to till it and dwell there, says the Lord.'" To Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in like manner: "Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve..."

...to his prophets and live. Why will you and your people die by the sword, famine, and pestilence, as the Lord has spoken against the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon? Do not listen to the words of the prophets who say to you, "You shall not serve the king of Babylon," for they prophesy a lie to you. "For I have not sent them," says the Lord, "and they prophesy in my name falsely, so that I may drive you out and you may perish, both you and the prophets who prophesy to you."

And to the priests and to this people I spoke, saying: Thus says the Lord: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, saying, "Behold, the vessels <note>The sacred gold and silver items used in Temple worship.</note> of the Lord will now soon be brought back from Babylon." For they prophesy a lie to you. Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city be laid waste? If they are truly prophets and the word of the Lord is in them, let them plead with the Lord of hosts that the vessels which were left in the house of the Lord, and in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem, may not go to Babylon. For thus says the Lord of hosts regarding the pillars, and the sea <note>A massive bronze basin for ceremonial washing in the Temple court.</note>, and the bases, and the rest of the vessels that remained in this city, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried away Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem. For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that were left in the house of the Lord and in the house of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem: They shall be carried to Babylon, and there they shall remain until the day of my visitation, says the Lord; then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.

And it happened in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azzur, a prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the Lord in the presence of the priests and all the people, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon. Within two full years, I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the Lord's house, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon. And Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, I will bring back to this place, says the Lord. For I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon. Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah in the sight of the priests and in the sight of all the people who were standing in the house of the Lord. "Amen! May the Lord do so; may the Lord fulfill your words which you have prophesied, to bring back the vessels into the house of the Lord and all the exiles from Babylon to this place. Nevertheless, hear now this word that I speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people: The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied against many lands and against great kingdoms, of war, and of affliction, and of famine. As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when the word of that prophet comes to pass, then it will be known that the Lord has truly sent him." Then the prophet Hananiah took the chain <note>original: *cathenam* — a yoke or heavy collar Jeremiah wore as a living sign of coming servitude.</note> from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it. And Hananiah spoke in the sight of all the people, saying: Thus says the Lord: "Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations within two full years." And the prophet Jeremiah went his way.

And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah after the prophet Hananiah had broken the chain from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying: Go and tell Hananiah: Thus says the Lord: You have broken wooden chains, but you shall make iron chains in their place. For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they shall serve him. Moreover, I have given him the beasts of the field also. And Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah: "Hear now, Hananiah! The Lord has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie. Therefore, thus says the Lord: Behold, I will cast you from the face of the earth. This year you shall die, for you have spoken against the Lord." And the prophet Hananiah died that same year in the seventh month.

And these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the remnant of the elders in exile, and to the priests, and to the prophets, and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon—after King Jeconiah, and the queen mother, and the eunuchs, and the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and the smiths had departed from Jerusalem—by the hand of Elasah the son of Shaphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, to all the exiles whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon: Build houses and dwell in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit. Take wives and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters; and multiply there, and do not be few in number. And seek the peace of the city to which I have caused you to be carried away, and pray to the Lord for it; for in its peace you will have peace. For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let your prophets who are in your midst and your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to your dreams which you dream. For thus says the Lord: When seventy years are completed in Babylon, I will visit you and perform my good word toward you, to bring you back to this place. For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, says the Lord, thoughts of peace and not of affliction, to give you an end and patience. Then you will call upon me and go and pray to me, and I will listen to you. You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart. And I will be found by you, says the Lord, and I will restore your captivity and gather you from all the nations and from all the places to which I have driven you, says the Lord, and I will cause you to return to the place from which I caused you to be carried away. Because you have said, "The Lord has raised up prophets for us in Babylon," for thus says the Lord to the king who sits on the throne of David and to all the people dwelling in this city—to your brothers who did not go out with you into exile—thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will send upon them the sword, famine, and pestilence, and I will make them like rotten figs that cannot be eaten, they are so bad. And I will pursue them with the sword, famine, and pestilence, and will deliver them to be troubled in all the kingdoms of the earth, to be a curse, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have driven them, because they did not listen to my words, says the Lord, which I sent to them by my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them; but you did not hear, says the Lord.

Hear therefore the word of the Lord, all you of the exile whom I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesy falsely to you in my name: Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he shall slay them before your eyes. And because of them a curse shall be taken up by all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon,

saying: "The Lord make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!"—because they have committed folly in Israel and have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives, and have spoken a word in my name falsely, which I did not command them. I am the judge and the witness, says the Lord. And to Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have sent letters in my name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying: "The Lord has made you priest instead of Jehoiada the priest, to be a leader in the house of the Lord over every man who is frantic <note>original: *arreptitium* — describing someone seized by a religious frenzy or madness.</note> and prophesies, that you should put him in the stocks and in prison." He shall not have a man sitting among this people, nor shall he see the good that I will do for my people, says the Lord, because he has spoken rebellion against the Lord.

These are the words that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: Thus says the Lord God of Israel, saying: Write for yourself all the words that I have spoken to you in a book. For behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the Lord, and I will bring them back to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it. And these are the words that the Lord spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah: For thus says the Lord: We have heard a voice of terror; there is fear and no peace. Ask now and see if a male can give birth. Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor, and all faces turned to paleness? Alas! For that day is great, so that none is like it; and it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he shall be saved out of it. "And it shall come to pass in that day," says the Lord of hosts, "that I will break his yoke from your neck and burst your bonds, and strangers shall no longer make a slave of him; but they shall serve the Lord their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them. Therefore, do not fear, O my servant Jacob," says the Lord, "nor be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from a far country, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. And Jacob shall return and be at rest, and shall be prosperous with all things, and none shall make him afraid. For I am with you," says the Lord, "to save you. For I will make a full end of all the nations where I have dispersed you; but of you I will not make a full end. But I will correct you in judgment, so that you do not seem innocent to yourself." For thus says the Lord: Your fracture is incurable; your wound is very grievous. There is no one to judge your cause, no healing medicines for your binding up. All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I have struck you with the blow of an enemy, with a cruel chastisement. Because of the multitude of your iniquity, your sins have become hardened. Why do you cry out over your affliction? Your pain is incurable. Because of the multitude of your iniquity and because of your hardened sins, I have done these things to you. Therefore, all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your enemies, every one of them, shall go into captivity; and those who plunder you shall be plundered, and all who prey upon you I will give for a prey. For I will bring a scar over you and I will heal you of your wounds, says the Lord. Because they called you an outcast, saying: "This is Zion, whom no one seeks."

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob, and I will have mercy on his dwellings; and the city shall be built upon its own hill, and the temple shall be founded according to its own order. And out of them shall proceed praise and the voice of those who make merry. And I will multiply them, and they shall not diminish; and I will glorify them, and they shall not be thinned out. And his children shall be as from the beginning, and his assembly shall remain before me, and I will visit punishment upon all who trouble him. And his leader shall be from himself, and a prince shall proceed from his midst; and I will bring him near, and he shall approach me. For who is he who would apply his heart to approach me? says the Lord. And you shall be my people, and I will be your God. Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing storm; it shall rest on the head of the wicked. The Lord will not turn away the anger of his indignation until he has executed and performed the thoughts of his heart. In the latter days, you will understand these things.

Hearing, I have heard Ephraim going into exile: "You have chastised me, and I was instructed like an untamed bullock."

...you had turned and repented in my sight, doing what was right in my eyes by proclaiming liberty, each of you to his neighbor. <margin>Jer 32, 1</margin>
**T**he word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar. At that time, the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison which was in the king of Judah’s palace. For Zedekiah, king of Judah, had imprisoned him, saying: "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it; and Zedekiah, king of Judah, shall not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans <note>The dominant ethnic group of the Neo-Babylonian Empire.</note>, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him face to face and see him eye to eye; and he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he shall remain until I visit him, says the Lord; though you fight against the Chaldeans, you shall not prosper'?" And Jeremiah said: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Behold, Hanamel, the son of Shallum your uncle, will come to you, saying, "Buy my field that is in Anathoth, for the right of redemption <note>Under ancient Jewish law, family land was to stay within the lineage; a close relative had the first right/duty to buy it.</note> is yours to buy it." Then Hanamel, my uncle’s son, came to me in the court of the prison according to the word of the Lord, and said to me: "Please buy my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Benjamin; for the right of inheritance is yours, and the redemption is yours; buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord. So I bought the field from Hanamel, my uncle’s son, in Anathoth, and weighed out the money for him: seven staters <note>original: "stateres"; a type of ancient coin or weight.</note> and ten silver pieces. I signed the deed and sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed the money on the scales. Then I took the deed of purchase—both the one that was sealed according to the law and custom, and the one that was open—and I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the presence of Hanamel my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, and before all the Jews who sat in the court of the prison. I charged Baruch before them, saying: "Take these deeds, both this sealed deed of purchase and this open deed, and put them in an earthenware vessel, so that they may last for many days."

**F**or thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be possessed in this land. And after I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord, saying:
"**A**las, alas, alas, Lord God! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm. There is nothing too difficult for you. You show mercy to thousands, and repay the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them. The Great, the Mighty God, the Lord of hosts is your name. You are great in counsel and incomprehensible in thought; your eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of Adam, to give to everyone according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds. You set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, even to this day, and in Israel and among all men; and you have made a name for yourself, as it is this day. You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror. You gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them—a land flowing with milk and honey. And they entered and possessed it, but they did not obey your voice or walk in your law. They have done nothing of all that you commanded them to do; therefore you have caused all this calamity to come upon them. Look, the siege mounds have been built against the city to take it; and the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans who fight against it, because of the sword and famine and pestilence. What you have spoken has happened, as you yourself see. Yet you say to me, O Lord God, 'Buy the field for money and call witnesses'—even though the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans?"

<margin>Jer 32, 29</margin>
...and they poured out drink offerings to foreign gods to provoke my anger. For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have done only evil in my sight from their youth; the children of Israel have done nothing but provoke me with the work of their hands, says the Lord. For this city has been a cause of my fury and indignation from the day they built it until this day, so that it must be removed from my sight because of all the wickedness of the children of Israel and Judah. They, their kings, their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem have provoked me to anger. They turned their backs to me and not their faces; though I taught them early and often, they would not listen or receive discipline. They set their abominations <note>referring to idols.</note> in the house where my name is called, to defile it. They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to initiate <note>A euphemism for human sacrifice.</note> their sons and daughters to Molech, which I did not command them. Nor did it ever enter my mind that they should do this abomination and lead Judah into sin. And now, therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning this city of which you say, "It shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence": Behold, I will gather them out of all the lands where I drove them in my fury and great indignation. I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety. They shall be my people, and I will be their God. I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me forever, for their own good and the good of their children after them. I will make an everlasting covenant with them, and I will not cease from doing good to them; I will put my fear in their hearts so that they will not depart from me. I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will truly plant them in this land with all my heart and all my soul. For thus says the Lord: Just as I have brought all this great calamity upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good that I have promised them. Fields shall be bought in this land, of which you say, "It is desolate, without man or beast; it has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans." Fields will be bought for money, deeds will be signed and sealed, and witnesses called in the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the hill country, in the lowlands, and in the cities of the south; for I will restore their fortunes, says the Lord.

<margin>Jer 33, 1</margin>
**T**he word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the prison, saying: Thus says the Lord who made the earth, who formed it and established it—the Lord is his name: Call to me and I will answer you, and tell you great and mighty things which you do not know. For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah, which have been pulled down to fortify against the siege mounds and the sword of those coming to fight the Chaldeans: they only fill them with the corpses of the men whom I have struck down in my anger and fury, hiding my face from this city because of all their wickedness. Behold, I will bring health and healing to it; I will heal them and reveal to them an abundance of peace and truth. I will restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem and rebuild them as they were at first. I will cleanse them from all the iniquity by which they sinned against me, and I will pardon all their sins by which they rebelled against me and despised me. It shall be to me a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all the nations of the earth who hear of all the good I do for them; they shall fear and tremble because of all the goodness and all the peace that I provide for it. Thus says the Lord: In this place, which you say is a wasteland without man or beast—in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate—there shall again be heard the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the voice of those who say, "Give thanks to the Lord of hosts, for the Lord is good, for his mercy endures forever," as they bring sacrifices of thanksgiving into the house of the Lord. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at first, says the Lord. Thus says the Lord of hosts: In this desolate place, without man or beast, and in all its cities, there shall again be a dwelling for shepherds resting their flocks. In the hill country, the lowlands, the south, the land of Benjamin, around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, flocks shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says the Lord. Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will perform that good thing which I have promised to the house of Israel and the house of Judah. In those days and at that time, I will cause a Righteous Branch <note>original: "germen iustitiae"; a messianic title referring to a future king from the line of David.</note> to sprout for David; he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the earth. In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell safely. And this is the name by which she will be called: "The Lord Our Righteousness." For thus says the Lord: David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel; nor shall the priests and Levites lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings, and to sacrifice continually. And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: Thus says the Lord: If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night do not come at their appointed time, then my covenant with David my servant may be broken, so that he shall not have a son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the Levites and priests, my ministers. As the stars of heaven cannot be numbered, nor the sand of the sea measured, so will I multiply the descendants of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me. The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: Have you not noticed what this people has said: "The Lord has rejected the two families <note>Refers to the northern kingdom of Israel and the southern kingdom of Judah.</note> which he had chosen"? Thus they despise my people, as if they were no longer a nation before them. Thus says the Lord: If I have not established my covenant with day and night and the laws of heaven and earth, then I will reject the descendants of Jacob and David my servant, and will not take any of his descendants to rule over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have mercy on them.

**T**he word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth under his dominion, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities, saying: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire. You shall not escape from his hand, but shall surely be captured and delivered into his hand; your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with you face to face, and you shall go to Babylon. You shall die in peace; and as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, "Alas, lord!" <meta>This page continues the prophetic narrative of Jeremiah during the reigns of Kings Jehoiakim and Zedekiah.
