### Jeremiah the Prophet
Look toward the seat, you as king, when all the armies of the king of Babylon <note>original: "uenu dū om̄s uenerūt," likely a transcription of 'uenerunt'—referring to the Babylonian forces</note> attacked Jerusalem and all the remaining cities of Judah—specifically Lachish and Azekah, for these were the only fortified cities of Judah that remained.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem, proclaiming that everyone should set free their Hebrew slaves, both male and female, so that no one should keep a fellow Judean in bondage. All the princes and the people who had entered the covenant obeyed, releasing their slaves to be free and no longer dominating them. They obeyed and let them go. But afterward, they changed their minds and took back the male and female slaves whom they had set free, and they forced them into subjection as servants again. 

Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, saying: 'At the end of seven years, every one of you shall set free his Hebrew brother who has been sold to you; and when he has served you six years, you shall let him go free from you.' But your fathers did not listen to me, nor did they incline their ear. And you had recently turned and done what was right in my eyes, proclaiming liberty each to his neighbor, and you made a covenant in my presence in the house where my name is called. But then you turned back and profaned my name; each of you took back his male and female slaves whom you had set free to be their own masters, and you forced them to be your slaves once again. 

Therefore, thus says the Lord: You have not listened to me by proclaiming liberty, each to his brother and neighbor. Behold, I now proclaim a 'liberty' for you—says the Lord—to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine! I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth. I will hand over the men who have transgressed my covenant and have not kept the words of the treaty to which they agreed in my presence—the ritual of the calf <note>original: "uitulum"; this refers to an ancient ceremony where a calf was cut in two, and the parties walked between the pieces to show they accepted a similar fate if they broke the oath.</note> which they cut in two and passed between its parts. The princes of Judah and Jerusalem, the eunuchs, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf: I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives. Their corpses shall be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. And Zedekiah, king of Judah, and his princes, I will hand over to their enemies and the armies of the king of Babylon, which have withdrawn from you. Behold, I give the command, says the Lord, and I will bring them back to this city. They shall fight against it, take it, and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a wasteland without an inhabitant."

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying: "Go to the house of the Rechabites <note>The Rechabites were a nomadic group known for their strict adherence to their ancestor's commands, including total abstinence from wine.</note> and speak to them. Bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the side chambers of the treasury, and give them wine to drink." So I took Jaazaniah <note>Latin: "Ieconia," likely a variant for Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah.</note> and his brothers and all his sons and the whole house of the Rechabites. I brought them into the house of the Lord, to the chamber of the sons of Hanan, son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was next to the chamber of the princes, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold. I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pitchers full of wine and cups, and I said to them: "Drink wine." 

But they answered: "We will drink no wine, for Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying: 'You shall never drink wine, neither you nor your sons forever. You shall not build houses, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyards, nor have any. Instead, you shall dwell in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the face of the land where you are travelers.' We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us. We drink no wine all our days—neither we, nor our wives, nor our sons, nor our daughters. We build no houses to dwell in, and we have no vineyard or field or seed. We have lived in tents and have been obedient, doing everything that Jonadab our father commanded us. But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against this land, we said: 'Come, let us enter Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans <term>Chaldeans</term><note>A common biblical term for the Babylonians.</note> and the army of the Syrians.' So we have been staying in Jerusalem."

Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: "Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: 'Will you not receive instruction and obey my words?' says the Lord. 'The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons—not to drink wine—have been kept. They drink no wine to this day, for they have obeyed the command of their father. But I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, yet you have not obeyed me. I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying: "Return now, every man from his evil way, and amend your deeds. Do not go after other gods to serve them, and you shall dwell in the land which I have given to you and your fathers." But you have not inclined your ear or listened to me. Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have carried out the command of their father, but this people has not obeyed me: Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster that I have spoken against them, because I have spoken to them and they have not heard; I have called to them and they have not answered.'" 

But to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said: "Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father and kept all his precepts and done everything he commanded you, therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: There shall not fail to be a man from the line of Jonadab the son of Rechab to stand before me forever."

And it happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: "Take a scroll <note>original: "uolumen libri"</note> and write in it all the words that I have spoken to you against Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you in the days of Josiah until this day. Perhaps when the house of Judah hears all the disaster I intend to do to them, every man will return from his evil way, and I may forgive their iniquity and their sin." 

Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord which he had spoken to him on a scroll. And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying: "I am restricted <note>original: "clausus sum"; meaning he was barred from the Temple precincts.</note> and cannot enter the house of the Lord. Therefore, you go and read from the scroll which you have written from my mouth the words of the Lord in the hearing of the people in the house of the Lord on the day of fasting. Also, you shall read them in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities. Perhaps their prayer will fall before the Lord, and every man will return from his evil way, for great is the anger and indignation that the Lord has spoken against this people." And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to...

<column-break/>

...all the people who had come from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem. Now it happened in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, they proclaimed a fast before the Lord for all the people in Jerusalem and for all the multitude that had gathered from the cities of Judah. 

Then Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah <note>Latin: "gā sophie" (treasury/chamber) of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe</note> the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord, in the hearing of all the people. When Micaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the Lord from the book, he went down to the king's house, to the scribe's chamber. And behold, all the princes were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, Elnathan the son of Achbor, Gemariah <note>Latin: "garias"</note> the son of Shaphan, Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes. Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read the scroll in the hearing of the people. 

Then all the princes sent Jehudi <note>Latin: "iulim"</note> the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying: "Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people and come." So Baruch the son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them. And they said to him: "Sit down and read it in our hearing." So Baruch read it in their hearing. Now it happened, when they had heard all the words, they turned in fear to one another and said to Baruch: "We must tell the king all these words." And they asked him: "Tell us now, how did you write all these words from his mouth?" Baruch answered them: "He spoke all these words to me with his mouth, as if reading to me, and I wrote them in the scroll with ink." Then the princes said to Baruch: "Go, hide yourself, you and Jeremiah; let no one know where you are." 

They went to the king in the court, but they deposited the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe and told all the words in the king's hearing. The king sent Jehudi to bring the scroll. He took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and all the princes who stood around the king. Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, and a brazier <note>Latin: "arula"; a small portable heater for coals.</note> full of burning coals was set before him. When Jehudi had read three or four columns <note>original: "pagellas"</note>, the king cut it with a scribe's knife and threw it into the fire that was in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed by the fire. Yet they were not afraid, nor did they tear their clothes—neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words. Although Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them. And the king commanded Jerahmeel <note>Latin: "hieremiel"</note> the son of Hammelech, Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the Lord hid them.

**Jeremiah the Prophet.** And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll and the words which Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying: "Take another scroll and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll which Jehoiakim the king of Judah burned. And you shall say to Jehoiakim king of Judah: 'Thus says the Lord: You have burned this scroll, saying: "Why have you written in it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and cause man and beast to cease from it?" Therefore thus says the Lord against Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat of the day and the frost of the night. I will punish him, his offspring, and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring upon them and the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the men of Judah all the disaster that I have spoken against them, but they did not listen.'" Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the son of Neriah, the scribe, who wrote in it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.

And King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah. But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord which he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet. King Zedekiah sent Jehucal <note>Latin: "iuchal"</note> the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "Pray now for us to the Lord our God." Now Jeremiah was walking freely among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison. Then Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt; and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.

The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Thus shall you say to the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire: 'Behold, Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, will return to its own land, to Egypt. And the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city, and they will take it and burn it with fire.' Thus says the Lord: 'Do not deceive yourselves, saying: "The Chaldeans will surely depart from us," for they will not depart. For even if you had defeated the whole army of the Chaldeans that fights against you, and there remained only wounded men among them, each man in his tent would rise up and burn this city with fire.'" 

When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go into the land of Benjamin to take possession of his property there among the people. When he was at the Gate of Benjamin, a captain of the guard was there whose name was Irijah <note>Latin: "gerias"</note>, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah. He seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "You are deserting to the Chaldeans!" Jeremiah replied: "That is false! I am not deserting to the Chaldeans." But Irijah would not listen to him; he seized Jeremiah and brought him to the princes. The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and they beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for they had made that the prison. 

So Jeremiah entered the dungeon <note>original: "domum laci" (house of the pit/lake)</note> and the vaulted cells <note>original: "m̄rgastallum," likely a corruption of 'mastubium' or 'magistratum', referring to a dungeon cell</note>, and Jeremiah remained there many days. Then King Zedekiah sent and took him out. The king questioned him secretly in his house and said: "Is there any word from the Lord?" Jeremiah said: "There is." And he said: "You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon." Moreover, Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah: "What sin have I committed against you, or against your servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison? Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying: 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land?' Now therefore, please hear, my lord the king; let my petition be accepted before you. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there." Then King Zedekiah commanded that they should commit Jeremiah to the court of the guard and that they should give him a piece of bread daily from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.

Shephatiah son of Mattan and Gedaliah <note>Latin: "phassur & iuchal" - the text likely refers to the group of officials listed in Jer 38:1</note> son of Pashhur and Jucal son of Shelemiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people, saying: "Thus says the Lord: 'He who remains in this city shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but he who goes over to the Chaldeans...'"

But Johanan the son of Kareah said to Gedaliah privately in Mizpah, speaking: "I will go and strike Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, with no one knowing: lest he kill your soul: and all the Jews who are gathered to you be scattered: and the remnant of Judah perish." And Gedaliah said to Johanan the son of Kareah: "Do not do this thing: for you speak falsely concerning Ishmael."

Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out on the second day after he had killed Gedaliah: while all men were unaware. There came to him from Shechem <note>original: "sichem"</note> and from Shiloh <note>original: "sylo"</note>: and from Samaria eighty men with shaven beards: and torn clothes: and disheveled <note>original: "squalidi"</note>: they had gifts and incense in their hand to offer in the house of the Lord. Therefore Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out to meet them from Mizpah: walking and weeping as he went. But when he had met them: he said to them: "Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam." Who, when they had come to the middle of the city: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah killed them around the middle of the pit <note>original: "lacum," often translated as cistern</note>: he and the men who were with him. But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael: "Do not kill us: for we have treasures in the field of wheat and barley: and of oil and honey:" and he ceased: and did not kill them with their brothers. Now the pit into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men whom he struck because of Gedaliah: it is the same which King Asa made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with those killed. And Ishmael took captive all the remnant of the people who were in Mizpah: the daughters of the king and all the people who remained in Mizpah whom Nebuzaradan the prince of the soldiers had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah took them: and went away to cross over to the children of Ammon.

But Johanan the son of Kareah and all the warrior captains who were with him heard: all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done. And taking all the men: they set out to fight against Ishmael the son of Nethaniah: and they found him at the many waters which are in Gibeon <note>original: "gabaon"</note>. And when all the people who were with Johanan the son of Kareah saw: and all the warrior captains of Ishmael <note>original: "ysmahel," here likely referring to the prisoners Ishmael was leading</note>: they rejoiced. And all the people whom Ishmael had taken in Mizpah turned back: and having turned back, went to Johanan the son of Kareah. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah fled with eight men from the face of Johanan: and went away to the children of Ammon. Therefore Johanan the son of Kareah and all the warrior captains took: all the remnant of the people whom he had brought back from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah from Mizpah: after he struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: strong men for war: and women and children and eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon. And they went and stayed in Geruth Chimham <note>original: "chemaam"</note>: which is near Bethlehem: so that they might proceed and enter Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans. For they feared them: because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had struck Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: whom the king of Babylon had set over the land of Judah.

The word which came to Jeremiah the prophet: when all the warrior captains had approached: and Johanan the son of Kareah: and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah: and the rest of the common people from the least to the greatest: they said to Jeremiah the prophet. "Let our prayer fall in your sight: and pray for us to the Lord your God: for all these remnants: since we are left a few out of many: just as your eyes behold us. And let the Lord your God announce to us the way in which we should walk: and the word that we should do." But Jeremiah the prophet said to them: "I have heard. Behold, I pray to the Lord your God according to your words. Every word whatsoever he shall answer me: I will indicate to you: nor will I hide anything from you." And they said to Jeremiah: "Let the Lord be a witness of truth and faithful between us: unless according to every word in which the Lord your God shall send you to us: so we shall do. Whether it is good or whether it is evil: we will obey the voice of the Lord our God to whom we send you: so that it may be well with us when we have heard the voice of the Lord our God."

And it happened when ten days were completed: the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet. And Johanan the son of Kareah called: and all the warrior captains who were with him: and all the people from the least even to the greatest. And he said to them: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel to whom you sent me that I might offer your prayers in his sight. If staying you remain in this land: I will build you and not destroy you. I will plant you and not pluck you up. For I am now appeased concerning the evil that I have done to you."

### And it came to pass, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to the people all the words of the Lord their God—all these words for which the Lord their God had sent him to them—that Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men spoke, saying to Jeremiah: "You are speaking a lie! The Lord our God did not send you to say, 'Do not enter Egypt to live there.' But Baruch the son of Neriah <note>Baruch was Jeremiah's scribe and close associate</note> incites you against us, so that he may deliver us into the hands of the Chaldeans <note>The Babylonians</note>, to kill us and cause us to be carried away to Babylon." And so Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the leaders of the warriors, and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord to remain in the land of Judah. Instead, Johanan the son of Kareah and all the leaders of the warriors took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations to which they had been scattered to live in the land of Judah—men, women, children, the king's daughters, and every soul that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch the son of Neriah. And they entered the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the Lord; and they came as far as Tahpanhes <note>A city in the Nile Delta</note>. Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying: "Take large stones in your hand and hide them in the vault which is under the brick wall at the gate of Pharaoh’s house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the Jewish men. And say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne upon these stones that I have hidden, and he shall set his throne over them. And coming, he shall strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death to death, those for captivity to captivity, and those for the sword to the sword. And he shall kindle a fire in the shrines of the gods of Egypt; he shall burn them and carry them away captive. And he shall wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak; and he shall go out from there in peace. And he shall break the statues of the House of the Sun <note>original: "domus solis," likely referring to Heliopolis</note> which are in the land of Egypt, and the shrines of the gods of Egypt he shall burn with fire."

### Concerning the word that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews who dwell in the land of Egypt—dwelling in Migdol, in Tahpanhes, in Memphis, and in the land of Pathros <note>Upper Egypt</note>—saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. You have seen all this evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. Behold, they are desolate today, and no one dwells in them because of the wickedness they committed to provoke me to anger, going to sacrifice and worship foreign gods which neither they, nor you, nor your fathers knew. And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising in the night and sending them, saying: "Do not do this kind of abominable thing which I hate." But they did not listen nor incline their ear to turn from their evils and stop sacrificing to foreign gods. And my indignation and my fury were poured out and kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they were turned into a wilderness and a wasteland, as it is this day. And now thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Why do you commit a great evil against your own souls, so that man and woman, child and infant are cut off from you from the midst of Judah, and no remnant is left for you? You provoke me with the works of your hands by sacrificing to foreign gods in the land of Egypt where you have entered to dwell, that you might perish and become a curse and a reproach to all the nations of the earth. Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of their wives, and your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the regions of Jerusalem? They have not been cleansed even to this day; they have not feared nor walked in the law of the Lord and in my precepts which I set before you and before your fathers. Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and I will destroy all Judah. And I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to live there; and they shall all be consumed in the land of Egypt. They shall fall by the sword and by famine, from the least to the greatest; by sword and famine they shall die. And they shall be an object of swearing, a miracle, a curse, and a reproach. And I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem: with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence. And there shall be none who escape or remain of the remnant of the Jews who go to travel in the land of Egypt, intending to return to the land of Judah—to which they lift up their souls to return and dwell there. They shall not return, except those who flee. Then all the men who knew that their wives sacrificed to foreign gods, and all the women standing there in a great multitude, and all the people dwelling in the land of Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying: "The word that you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not hear from you. But we will certainly do every word that goes out of our own mouth: to sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven <note>original: "regine celi," a title for a Near Eastern goddess such as Astarte or Ishtar</note> and to pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our fathers, our kings and our princes have done in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we were filled with bread, and it was well with us, and we saw no evil. But from the time we ceased to sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and by sword and famine

we have been consumed. And if we sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes to worship her and pour out drink offerings without our husbands' consent?" And Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women, and to all the people who had given him this answer: "The sacrifice that you sacrificed in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land—did the Lord not remember these things, and did it not come into His heart? And the Lord could no longer bear it because of the wickedness of your pursuits and because of the abominations you committed. And your land has been made a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse, so that there is no inhabitant, as it is this day. Because you sacrificed to gods and sinned against the Lord, and did not hear the voice of the Lord, and did not walk in His law and in His precepts and in His testimonies: therefore these evils have happened to you, as it is this day." Moreover, Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women: "Hear the word of the Lord, all you of Judah who are in the land of Egypt. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying: 'Let us perform our vows that we have vowed, to sacrifice to the Queen of Heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.' You have indeed fulfilled your vows and performed them in deed! Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all you of Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: Behold, I have sworn by my great name, says the Lord, that my name shall no longer be invoked by the mouth of any man of Judah saying, 'The Lord God lives,' in all the land of Egypt. Behold, I will watch over them for evil and not for good. And all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt shall be consumed by the sword and by famine until they are entirely finished. And those who flee the sword shall return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, only a few men; and all the remnant of Judah who entered the land of Egypt to live there shall know whose word shall be fulfilled: mine or theirs. And this shall be a sign to you, says the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words shall truly be fulfilled against you for evil. Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra <note>original: "ephree"</note>, king of Egypt, into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I delivered Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life."

### The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah, when he had written these words in a volume from the mouth of Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord God of Israel to you, Baruch. For you said: "Woe to me in my misery, for the Lord has added sorrow to my sorrow! I have labored in my groaning and have found no rest." Thus shall you say to him: Behold, what I have built, I destroy, and what I have planted, I pluck up—even this entire land. And do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says the Lord, but I will give you your life as a prize <note>original: "in salutem," for safety/salvation</note> in every place to which you may go.

### The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the nations: against Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, who was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah. Prepare the buckler and the shield, and go forth to war! Yoke the horses and mount up, you horsemen! Stand in your helmets, polish the spears, put on the coats of mail! What then? I saw them terrified and turning their backs; their strong ones were cut down. They fled in haste and did not look back. Terror is on every side, says the Lord. Let not the swift flee, nor the strong think he can save himself. In the north, by the river Euphrates, they were conquered and fell. Who is this that rises like a river, whose waters surge like floods? Egypt rises like a river, and its waves shall be moved like floods. And he shall say: "I will go up and cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants." Mount the horses and exult in the chariots! Let the strong men come forth: Ethiopia and the Libyans holding the shield, and the Lydians taking up and shooting arrows. But that day of the Lord of hosts is a day of vengeance, that He may take vengeance on His enemies. The sword shall devour and be satisfied; it shall be drunk with their blood. For the Lord of hosts has a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates. Go up to Gilead and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt! In vain shall you multiply medicines; there shall be no health for you. The nations have heard of your shame, and your wailing has filled the earth, for the strong man has stumbled against the strong; both have fallen down together.

### The word that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet regarding the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt. Announce it in Egypt, and make it heard in Migdol; let it resonate in Memphis and in Tahpanhes. Say: "Stand and prepare yourself, for the sword shall devour those things that are around you." Why is your strong one cut off? He did not stand because the Lord overthrew him. He multiplied those who fall; man fell upon his neighbor. And they shall say: "Arise, and let us return to our own people and to the land of our birth, from the face of the sword of the dove <note>original: "gladii columbe," a metaphor for an oppressing or devastating sword</note>." As I live, says the King—the Lord of hosts is my name—as surely as Tabor is among the mountains and Carmel is by the sea, he shall come. Prepare for yourself vessels for migration, you inhabitant, daughter of Egypt, for Memphis shall be a wilderness; it shall be deserted and uninhabitable. Egypt is a beautiful and elegant heifer; a goad-fly from the north shall come to her. Her mercenaries also, who were in her midst like fatted calves, have turned and fled together; they could not stand, for the day of their slaughter has come upon them, the time of their visitation. Her voice shall sound like brass <note>or like a serpent hissing</note>, for they shall hasten with an army; they shall come against her with axes like those who cut wood. They have cut down her forest, says the Lord, which could not be counted. They have multiplied more than locusts; they are without number. The daughter of Egypt is confounded and delivered into the hand of the people of the north.

For I will consume all the nations to which I have driven you; but I will not consume you. Instead, I will correct you in judgment, nor will I spare you as if you were innocent.

Concerning Moab, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe upon Nebo, for it is laid waste and confounded; Kiriathaim is captured. The strong city is confounded and has trembled. There is no more rejoicing in Moab; against Heshbon they have devised evil. Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation. Therefore, you shall be silenced, and the sword shall follow you. A voice of a cry from Horonaim, great wasting and crushing. Moab is crushed; announce the cry to her little ones. For by the ascent of Luhith, the mourner shall go up in tears; because in the descent of Horonaim the enemies have heard the wailing of destruction. Flee, save your lives, and you shall be like a tamarisk <note>Original: "mirice," a desert shrub symbolizing desolation</note> in the desert. Because you had trust in your fortifications and in your treasures, you also shall be captured; and Chemosh <note>The national god of the Moabites</note> shall go into exile, his priests and his princes together. And the spoiler shall come to every city, and no city shall be saved. And the valleys shall perish, and the plains shall be scattered, because the Lord has said it. Give wings to Moab, for she shall go out flying, and her cities shall be deserted and uninhabitable. 

**C**ursed is he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully; and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from blood. Moab has been fertile from his youth and has rested on his dregs; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. Therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed. Therefore behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will send to him those who tilt and level the jars; they shall empty his vessels and break his bottles. And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which they had their trust. How do you say, "We are valiant and strong men for war"? Moab is laid waste, and her cities have gone up in smoke, and her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter, says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts. The destruction of Moab is near at hand, and his calamity shall come very swiftly. Comfort him, all you who are around him; and all you who know his name, say: "How is the strong staff broken, the staff of glory!" Come down from your glory and sit in thirst, O inhabitant of the daughter of Dibon, because the spoiler of Moab has come up to you; he has scattered your fortifications. Stand by the way and look out, O inhabitant of Aroer; ask him who flees and her who has escaped, and say: "What has happened?" Moab is confounded because he is conquered. Wail and cry out; announce it in Arnon, that Moab is laid waste. And judgment has come to the plain country: upon Holon, and upon Jahzah, and upon Mephaath, and upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon the house of Diblathaim, and upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon, and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near. The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, says the Lord. Make him drunk, because he has lifted himself up against the Lord; and Moab shall clap his hands in his own vomit, and he also shall be a derision. For was not Israel a derision to you, as if you had found him among thieves? Because of your words which you spoke against him, you shall be led away captive. Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, O inhabitants of Moab; and be like the dove that nests in the highest mouth of the cavern. We have heard of the pride of Moab—he is exceeding proud—of his loftiness, and his arrogance, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. I know his boasting, says the Lord, and that his strength is not according to it, nor has he performed what he attempted. Therefore I will wail for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; I will mourn for the men of the brick wall. I will weep for you with the weeping of Jazer, O vine of Sibmah. Your branches have passed over the sea, they have reached even to the sea of Jazer. The spoiler has rushed upon your harvest and your vintage. Joy and gladness are taken away from Carmel and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses. No treader of the grapes shall sing the customary song, nor shall the cry be heard from Heshbon even to Elealeh and Jahzah; they have uttered their voice from Zoar even to Horonaim, like a heifer of three years old. The waters of Nimrim also shall be very bad and dried up from Moab, says the Lord, for those offering in the high places and sacrificing to their gods. Therefore my heart shall resound for Moab like a pipe, and my heart shall give a sound for the men of the brick wall; because he did more than he was able, therefore they have perished. For every head shall be bald, and every beard shaven; on all hands there shall be bindings, and upon every back sackcloth. And upon all the housetops of Moab and in its streets there is nothing but mourning, because I have broken Moab like a useless vessel, says the Lord. How is he conquered, and they have wailed? How has Moab turned his back and been confounded? And Moab shall be a derision and an example to all those around him. Thus says the Lord: Behold, he shall fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. Kerioth is taken, and the fortifications are seized. And the heart of the mighty men of Moab in that day shall be like the heart of a woman in labor; and Moab shall cease to be a people, because he has boasted against the Lord. Fear, and the pit, and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord. He who flees from the face of fear shall fall into the pit; and he who climbs out of the pit shall be taken in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their visitation, says the Lord. They who fled from the snare stood in the shadow of Heshbon, because a fire has gone forth from Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon; and it shall devour part of Moab and the crown of the head of the children of tumult. Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, because your sons are taken, and your daughters into captivity. And I will bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days, says the Lord.

**H**itherto are the judgments of Moab. To the children of Ammon: Thus says the Lord. Has Israel no sons? Or has he no heir? Why then has Milcom <note>Original: "melchom," the national god of the Ammonites, often associated with child sacrifice</note> possessed Gad by inheritance, and his people dwell in its cities? Therefore behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will cause the noise of war to be heard in Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burnt with fire, and Israel shall possess those who possessed him, says the Lord. Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste. Cry out, O daughters of Rabbah, gird yourselves with sackcloth; mourn and go about by the hedges, for Milcom shall be led into exile, his priests and his princes together. Why do you glory in the valleys? Your valley has flowed away, O lawless daughter, who trusted in your treasures and said: "Who shall come to me?" Behold, I will bring terror upon you,

<meta>This page concludes the historical account of the fall of Jerusalem found in the Book of Jeremiah and begins the Book of Baruch. the army of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the people of Babylon.</note> pursued the king and, overtaking Zedekiah, they brought him to the king of Babylon. All his army was scattered from him. When they had captured the king, they led him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, and he passed judgment upon him. The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he killed all the princes of Judah at Riblah. He put out the eyes of Zedekiah, bound him in fetters, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in prison until the day of his death.

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—this was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzardan, the captain of the guard who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. He burned the house of the Lord <note>The First Temple, built by Solomon.</note>, the king’s palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he consumed with fire. The entire army of the Chaldeans that was with the captain of the guard broke down the whole wall around Jerusalem. Then Nebuzardan, the captain of the guard, carried away into exile some of the poor people, the rest of the common folk who remained in the city, the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen. But some of the poor of the land Nebuzardan the captain left behind to be vinedressers and farmers.

The Chaldeans broke into pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the stands, and the bronze sea <note>term: bronze sea (a massive circular basin used by priests for ritual washing)</note> that was in the house of the Lord, and they carried all their bronze to Babylon. They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the bowls, the censers, and all the bronze vessels used in the temple service. The captain of the guard took the basins, the fire pans, the bowls, the pitchers, the lampstands, the mortars, and the incense burners—whatever was made of gold as gold, and whatever was made of silver as silver. He took the two pillars, the one "sea," and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord. The weight of the bronze of all these vessels was beyond calculation.

As for the pillars: one pillar was eighteen cubits <note>A cubit is roughly the length of a forearm, about 18 inches.</note> high, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it. It was four fingers thick and hollow inside. Upon it was a capital of bronze; the height of the one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar with its pomegranates was similar. There were ninety-six pomegranates hanging down, and all the pomegranates around the network numbered one hundred.

Next, the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold. He also took from the city a certain eunuch who was in charge of the men of war, seven men from the king’s close advisors who were found in the city, the scribe of the captain of the army who mustered the young recruits, and sixty men of the common people who were found in the midst of the city. Nebuzardan the captain took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. And the king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was taken into exile from its land. This is the number of people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews; in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred and thirty-two souls from Jerusalem; in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzardan the captain of the guard carried away seven hundred and forty-five Jews. All the souls numbered four thousand six hundred.

And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, showed favor to Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and brought him out of prison. He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon. He changed his prison clothes, and Jehoiachin ate bread in the king's presence regularly all the days of his life. For his allowance, a regular portion was given to him by the king of Babylon, a fixed amount for each day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

### ->**THESE ARE THE WORDS**<-

These are the words of the book which Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon, in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire. And Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book, and in the hearing of the mighty men and the sons of the kings, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people from the least to the greatest—all who lived in Babylon by the river Sud. 

When they heard it, they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord. They also collected money, according to what each person could afford, and sent it to Jerusalem to Jehoiakim the priest, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the priests and all the people who were found with him in Jerusalem. This was when he received the vessels of the temple of the Lord, which had been taken away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah on the tenth day of the month of Sivan—the silver vessels which Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had captured Jehoiachin and the princes, the captives, the mighty men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem and led them to Babylon.

And they said: "Behold, we have sent you money; buy burnt offerings and incense with it, prepare grain offerings, and offer them for sin at the altar of the Lord our God. And pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar his son <note>original: 'baltasur'</note>, that their days may be as the days of heaven upon the earth. And may the Lord give us strength and enlighten our eyes, that we may live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and under the shadow of Belshazzar his son, and serve them for many days and find favor in their sight. And pray for us also to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his wrath has not been turned away from us even to this day. To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us confusion of face, as it is this day—to every man of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, and our fathers. <meta>This page continues from the fall of Jerusalem, transitioning into the Book of Baruch—a text traditionally attributed to Jeremiah's scribe—and concludes with the opening verses of the Book of Lamentations. This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that exists forever. All who hold fast to her <note>referring to Wisdom or the Law</note> shall find life, but those who have abandoned her shall die. Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of her; walk by the way toward her brightness, in the presence of her light. Do not give your glory to another, nor your dignity to a foreign nation. We are blessed, O Israel, for the things that please God are made manifest to us. Be of better courage, people of God, the memorial of Israel! You were sold to the nations, not for your destruction, but because you provoked God to wrath by your anger; you were handed over to your adversaries. For you provoked Him who made you, the eternal God, by sacrificing to demons and not to God. You forgot the God who nourished you, and you brought sorrow to your nurse, Jerusalem. For she saw the wrath coming upon you from God and said: "Listen, you neighbors of Zion! God has brought great mourning upon me. For I have seen the captivity of my people, of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal One brought upon them. For I nourished them with joy, but I let them go with weeping and mourning. Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and desolate; I have been forsaken by many because of the sins of my children, because they turned away from the law of God. They did not know His justices, nor did they walk in the ways of God’s commandments, nor did they enter the paths of truth with justice. Let the neighbors of Zion come and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal One brought upon them. For He brought against them a nation from afar, a wicked nation of a strange language, who did not respect the elder nor pity the children; they have led away the widow’s beloved ones and left the lonely woman desolate of her sons. But as for me, how can I help you? For He who brought these evils upon you will Himself rescue you from the hands of your enemies. Go your way, children, go your way; for I am left alone. I have put off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of my prayer, and I will cry out to the Most High in my days. Take courage, children! Cry out to the Lord, and He will rescue you from the power of the enemy princes. For I have hoped in the Eternal One for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One because of the mercy that shall come to you from your Eternal Savior. For I saw your mourning and weeping, but He will lead you back to me with joy and gladness forever. For just as the neighbors of Zion have now seen your captivity, so shall they quickly see your salvation from God, which shall come upon you with great honor and eternal splendor. Children, endure patiently the wrath that has come upon you. For your enemy has persecuted you, but you shall soon see his destruction and shall step upon his neck. My delicate ones have walked rough ways, for they were driven like a flock snatched away by enemies. Be of better courage, children, and cry out to God! For you shall be remembered by Him who leads you. For as it was your mind to wander from God, so seek Him ten times more now that you return. For He who brought evils upon you will bring you everlasting gladness again with your salvation. Take courage, Jerusalem, for He who named you encourages you! The wicked who afflicted you shall perish, and those who rejoiced at your ruin shall be punished. The cities where your children served as slaves shall be punished, even she <note>referring to Babylon</note> who received your sons. For just as she rejoiced at your ruin and was glad at your fall, so shall she be grieved at her own desolation. The boasting of her greatness shall be cut off, and her joy shall be turned into mourning. For fire shall come upon her from the Eternal One for long days, and she shall be inhabited by demons for a great length of time. Look around, Jerusalem, toward the east, and see the joy coming to you from God! For behold, your children come, whom you sent away dispersed; they come, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the honor of God. Put off, O Jerusalem, the robe of your mourning and affliction, and clothe yourself in the beauty and honor of that eternal glory which is from God. God will wrap you in a double cloak of justice and place upon your head the crown of eternal honor. For God will show His splendor in you to every nation under heaven. For your name shall be given to you by God forever: the Peace of Justice and the Honor of Piety. Arise, Jerusalem, and stand on high! Look toward the east and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to the west, by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they went out from you on foot, led by enemies, but the Lord brings them back to you, carried in honor like sons of the kingdom. For God has decreed to humble every high mountain and the everlasting rocks, and to fill up the valleys to level the ground, so that Israel may walk diligently in the honor of God. Even the woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel by the command of God. For God will lead Israel with gladness in the light of His majesty, with the mercy and justice that come from Him. Put away the sins you have committed against God; He will lead you through all your tribulation. <insert>Being handed over to the king of Babylon.</insert> You have entered into Babylon; you shall be there for many years and for a long time, even for seven generations. After that, I will bring you out from there in peace. But now you will see in Babylon gods of gold, and silver, and stone, and wood, which are carried on shoulders, showing off fear to the nations. See to it, therefore, that you do not become like these foreigners in their deeds and be afraid, and let fear take hold of you because of them. When you see the crowd before and behind them worshipping, say in your hearts: "It is You, O Lord, who ought to be worshipped." For my angel is with you, and he will look after your souls. For their tongues are polished by a craftsman; they themselves are gilded and silvered, yet they are false and cannot speak. And just as one might for a girl who loves ornaments, they take gold and fashion it. Their gods certainly have golden crowns upon their heads. From these, the priests steal gold and silver and spend it on themselves. They even give some of it to harlots and dress up prostitutes; and when they receive it back from the prostitutes, they dress up their gods again. Yet these gods are not saved from rust and moths. When they have covered them in purple robes, they wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, which is very thick among them. One holds a scepter like a man, like a judge of a region, but he cannot kill the one who sins against him. Another has a sword in his hand and an axe, but he cannot save himself from war or from robbers. By this it is known to you that they are not gods.

Do not, therefore, fear them. For just as a man’s vessel, when broken, becomes useless, such are their gods. When they are placed in their temples, their eyes are full of dust from the feet of those who enter. And just as the courts are closed off for someone who has offended the king, or as a dead man is led to the grave, so the priests secure the doors with bars and locks, lest they be plundered by robbers. They light lamps for them, and many indeed, yet the gods can see none of them. They are like beams in a house. It is said that serpents from the earth lick their hearts while they eat them and their clothing, yet they do not feel it. Their faces are blackened by the smoke of the temple; owls, swallows, and other birds fly over their bodies and heads, and even cats do the same. By this you may know they are not gods.

Do not, therefore, fear them. The gold they have is for appearance; unless someone wipes off the tarnish, they will not shine. Even when they were being cast, they felt nothing. They were bought at a great price, though there is no breath in them. Having no feet, they are carried on shoulders, showing off their worthlessness to men. Let those who worship them also be confounded. For if they fall to the ground, they do not rise by themselves; nor if someone sets one upright will it stand by itself; but gifts are placed before them as if they were dead men. Their priests sell their sacrifices and misuse them. Likewise, their wives take portions of them, giving nothing to the sick or the beggar. Women in labor and those in their monthly period touch their sacrifices. Knowing, therefore, from these things that they are not gods, do not fear them. For why are they called gods? Because women set food before these gods of silver, gold, and wood; and in their temples, the priests sit with torn tunics, their heads and beards shaved, and their heads uncovered. They roar and cry out before their gods as at a funeral feast for the dead. The priests take from their garments and clothe their own wives and children. Whether they suffer any evil from someone or receive any good, they cannot repay it. They can neither set up a king nor take one down. Likewise, they are able neither to give riches nor to repay evil. If someone makes a vow to them and does not fulfill it, they do not require it. They do not save a man from death, nor do they rescue the weak from the powerful. They do not restore sight to a blind man, nor will they deliver a man from necessity. They will not pity the widow, nor do good to the orphans. Their gods are like stones from a mountain: wood, stone, gold, and silver. Those who worship them shall be put to shame. How, then, is it to be thought or said that they are gods? Even the Chaldeans themselves do not honor them; for when they hear of a mute who cannot speak, they offer him to Bel <note>A Babylonian deity.</note>, asking that he may speak, as if those who have no motion could perceive anything. And when they understand this, they will leave them behind. For their gods have no sense themselves. The women, wrapped with cords, sit in the streets, burning olive stones. When one of them is pulled away by a passerby to sleep with him, she reproaches her neighbor because she was not deemed worthy like herself, nor was her cord broken. Everything that happens to them is false. How then can it be thought or said that they are gods? They were made by craftsmen and goldsmiths; they will be nothing other than what the priests want them to be. The craftsmen themselves who make them do not live for a long time. Can the things made by them, then, be gods? They have left behind only lies and a reproach for those who come after. For when war and evils come upon them, the priests consult among themselves where they might hide with them. How then can they be perceived to be gods, who neither save themselves from war nor rescue themselves from evils? For since they are of wood, gilded and silvered, it will be known afterward by all nations and kings that they are false; it is manifest that they are not gods, but the works of human hands, and there is no work of God in them. How then is it known that they are not gods, but the works of human hands? For they do not raise up a king for a region, nor do they give rain to men. They will not judge a cause, nor will they deliver regions from injury, because they are as powerless as crows between heaven and earth. For when fire falls on a temple of wooden, golden, or silver gods, the priests will flee and be saved, but the gods themselves will be burned like beams in the middle. They will not resist a king or a war. How then is it to be thought or accepted that they are gods? Wooden, stone, gilded, and silvered gods will not save themselves from thieves or robbers. Those who are stronger than them will take away the gold and silver and the clothing they are covered with and depart, and they cannot help themselves. Therefore, it is better to be a king showing his power, or a useful vessel in a house in which the owner takes pride, than to be false gods. The sun, moon, and stars, since they are bright and sent out for use, are obedient. Likewise, when lightning appears, it is plain to see. The wind also blows in every region. And the clouds, when they are commanded by God to travel over the whole world, perform what is commanded of them. The fire also, sent from above to consume mountains and forests, does what it is ordered. But these idols are like none of these in appearance or power. Therefore, it is neither to be thought nor said that they are gods, since they can neither judge a case nor do anything for men. Knowing, therefore, that they are not gods, do not love them. For they will neither curse nor bless kings. They will not show signs in the heavens to the nations, nor will they shine like the sun, nor give light like the moon. The beasts are better than they, for they can flee under a roof and help themselves. In no way, therefore, is it manifest to us that they are gods. For this reason, do not fear them. For just as a <term>scarecrow</term> <note>Latin: "formido in cucumerario" - a fear-inducing object in a cucumber garden.</note> in a garden of cucumbers protects nothing, so are their gods of wood, silver, and gold. In the same way, their gods of wood, gold, and silver are like a white thorn bush in a garden, on which every bird sits; or like a dead body cast out into the darkness. By the purple and the marble that are worn away upon them, you shall know that they are not gods. At last, they themselves are eaten, and they shall be a reproach in the land. Better is the just man who has no idols, for he shall be far from reproach.

**L**ook, O Lord, for I am troubled; my belly is disturbed; my heart is overturned within me, for I am full of bitterness. Outside the sword slays, and at home it is like death.
**T**hey heard that I groan, and there is none to comfort me. All my enemies heard of my evil; they rejoiced that You have brought the day of consolation, and they shall become like me.
**L**et all their evil come before You, and harvest them like a vineyard, just as You have harvested me for all my iniquities; for my groans are many and my heart is grieving.

**T**he Lord has become like an enemy; He has cast down Israel; He has cast down all its walls; He has destroyed its strongholds, and has filled the daughter of Judah with mourning and lamentation.

**T**he Lord has rejected His altar, He has cursed His sanctuary; He has delivered into the hand of the enemy the walls of her towers; they have made a noise in the house of the Lord as on a festival day.

**H**er gates are fixed in the ground; He has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no law, and her prophets have found no vision from the Lord.
**T**he elders of the daughter of Zion have sat on the ground and remained silent. They have sprinkled ashes on their heads; they are girded with haircloth; the virgins of Judah have cast their heads down to the ground.
**M**y eyes have failed with tears; my bowels are troubled; my liver is poured out on the ground over the destruction of my people, when the little one and the suckling failed in the streets of the town.
**T**hey said to their mothers: "Where is the wheat and the wine?" when they failed like the wounded in the streets of the city, when they breathed out their souls into their mothers' bosoms.
**T**o whom shall I compare you, or to whom shall I liken you, O daughter of Jerusalem? To whom shall I equate you and comfort you, O daughter of Zion? For your destruction is great like the sea; who shall heal you?
**Y**our prophets have seen false and foolish things; they did not uncover your iniquity to provoke you to repentance; they have seen for you false burdens and banishments.
**A**ll those who pass by the way have clapped their hands over you; they have hissed and shaken their heads over the daughter of Jerusalem, saying: "Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of the whole earth?"
**A**ll your enemies have opened their mouths against you; they have hissed and gnashed their teeth, and said: "We will swallow her up! Behold, this is the day we were waiting for; we have found it, we have seen it."
**T**he Lord has done what He planned; He has fulfilled His word which He had commanded from the days of old. He has destroyed and not spared; and He has caused the enemy to rejoice over you, and has exalted the strength <note>original: "cornu", literally "horn"</note> of your adversaries.
**T**heir heart cried out to the Lord over the walls of the daughter of Zion: "Let tears run down like a torrent day and night; give yourself no rest, nor let the pupil of your eye be still."
**A**rise, praise in the night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the sight of the Lord; lift up your hands to Him for the life of your little ones, who have fainted from hunger at the head of all the crossroads.
**L**ook, O Lord, and consider: whom have You harvested thus? **S**hall women then eat their own fruit—little ones the size of a palm? If the priest and the prophet are killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
**T**he child and the old man have lain on the ground outside; my virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed in the day of Your fury; You have struck and not pitied.

<column-break/>

**Y**ou have called, as if to a festival day, those who would terrify me from all around; and in the day of the Lord's fury there was none who escaped or remained. Those whom I brought up and nourished, my enemy has consumed them.
**I** am the man seeing my poverty under the rod of His indignation. He has driven me and brought me into darkness and not into light.
**O**nly against me has He turned and turned again His hand all the day; He has made my skin and my flesh old; He has broken my bones.
**H**e has built round about me, and surrounded me with gall and labor; He has placed me in dark places like those who have been dead forever.
**H**e has built around me so that I cannot go out; He has made my chain heavy.
**A**nd also when I cry and pray, He has shut out my prayer.
**H**e has closed up my ways with squared stones; He has overturned my paths.
**H**e has become to me like a bear lying in wait, like a lion in hiding. He has overturned my ways and broken me; He has made me desolate.
**H**e has bent His bow and set me as a mark for the arrow. He has sent into my loins the daughters of His quiver <note>meaning his arrows</note>.
**I** have become a derision to all my people, their song all the day long.
**H**e has filled me with bitterness, He has intoxicated me with wormwood. He has broken my teeth one by one; He has fed me with ashes.
**A**nd my soul is repelled from peace; I have forgotten good things.
<margin>And hope</margin>
**A**nd I said: My end has perished, and my hope from the Lord.
<margin>Remember poverty</margin>
**R**emember my poverty and my transgression, and the wormwood and the gall.
<margin>Memory</margin>
**W**ith memory I will remember, and my soul shall languish within me.
<margin>These things</margin>
**T**hese things recalling in my heart, therefore I shall hope.
<margin>Mercies</margin>
**T**he mercies of the Lord are that we are not consumed; for His compassions have not failed.
**T**hey are new at dawn; great is Your faithfulness. "The Lord is my portion," said my soul; therefore I will wait for Him.
<margin>Good</margin>
**T**he Lord is good to those who hope in Him, to the soul that seeks Him.
<margin>Good</margin>
**I**t is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the Lord.
**I**t is good for a man when he has borne the yoke from his youth. He shall sit solitary and remain silent, because he has lifted himself above himself.
<margin>He shall give</margin>
**H**e shall put his mouth in the dust, if perhaps there may be hope.
<margin>Because He will not reject</margin>
**H**e shall give his cheek to the one who strikes him; he shall be filled with reproaches.
**F**or the Lord will not reject forever.
**F**or though He has cast off, yet He will have mercy according to the multitude of His mercies.
**F**or He has not humbled from His heart, nor has He cast off the children of men.
**T**o crush under His feet all the prisoners of the earth.
**T**o turn aside the judgment of a man in the sight of the face of the Most High.
<margin>Man</margin>
**T**o pervert a man in his judgment, the Lord does not ignore.
**W**ho is he who said it should happen, when the Lord does not command it? From the mouth of the Most High neither good nor evil shall proceed.
<margin>Why</margin>
**W**hy has a living man murmured—a man because of his sins?
<margin>Let us search</margin>
**L**et us search our ways and seek, and let us return to the Lord.
<margin>Let us lift up</margin>
**L**et us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in the heavens.
<margin>We</margin>
**W**e have acted wickedly, and we have provoked You to wrath; therefore You are inexorable.
<margin>Not</margin>
**Y**ou have set Yourself against us in fury and struck us; You have killed and not spared.
**Y**ou have set a cloud against Yourself, so that prayer may not pass through.
**Y**ou have made me an uprooting and an abjection in the midst of the peoples.
**A**ll our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
**F**ear and a snare have come upon us: prophecy <note>used here in the sense of a heavy burden or doom</note> and destruction.
<margin>Eye</margin>
**M**y eye has shed torrents of water over the destruction of the daughter of my people.
**M**y eye is afflicted, and has not been silent, because there is no rest.
**U**ntil the Lord should look down and see from the heavens.
**M**y eye has despoiled my soul because of all the daughters of my city. My enemies have caught me for no reason, like a bird, by hunting.
<margin>It has fallen into the pit</margin>
**M**y life has fallen into the pit, and they have placed a stone over me.
<margin>I called</margin>
**W**aters have flowed over my head; I said: "I am lost."
**I** called upon Your name, O Lord, from the deepest pit.
**Y**ou have heard my voice; do not turn away Your ear from my sobbing and cries.
**Y**ou drew near on the day that I called upon You; You said: "Do not fear."
**Y**ou have judged, O Lord, the cause of my soul; You are the redeemer of my life.
**Y**ou have seen, O Lord, their iniquity against me; judge my judgment.
**Y**ou have seen all their fury, all their thoughts against me.
**Y**ou have heard their reproaches, O Lord, all their thoughts against me.
**T**he lips of those rising up against me, and their meditations against me all the day long.
**B**ehold their sitting down and their rising up; look, O Lord, I am their mocking song <note>original: "psalmus"</note>.
<margin>Render</margin>
**R**ender to them a reward, O Lord, according to the works of their hands.
<margin>They shall give</margin>
**Y**ou shall give them a shield for their heart—Your labor <note>meaning the toil and hardship sent by God as punishment</note>. You shall pursue them in fury and crush them under the heavens, O Lord.
<margin>Not</margin>
**H**ow the gold has become dim! The finest color is changed! The stones of the sanctuary are scattered at the head of every street.
**T**he noble sons of Zion, clothed in the first gold: how they are regarded as earthenware vessels, the work of a potter's hands!
**E**ven the sea-monsters <note>original: "lamie", mythological creatures or jackals</note> have bared their breasts and nursed their young; the daughter of my people is cruel like an ostrich in the desert.
**T**he tongue of the suckling has clung to the roof of its mouth in thirst. Little ones have asked for bread, and there was no one to break it for them.
<margin>Those who fed</margin>
**T**hose who fed luxuriously have perished in the streets; those who were brought up in scarlet have embraced dung-heaps.
<margin>And greater</margin>
**A**nd the iniquity of the daughter of my people has become greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overturned in a moment, and no hands reached out to her.
<margin>Whiter</margin>
**H**er Nazirites were whiter than snow, purer than milk, more ruddy than old ivory, more beautiful than sapphire.
<margin>Blackened</margin>
**T**heir face has become blacker than coals, and they are not recognized in the streets; their skin has clung to their bones; it has dried up and become like wood.
**I**t was better for those killed by the sword than for those killed by hunger, for these wasted away, consumed by the barrenness of the earth.
<margin>The hands of women</margin>
**T**he hands of merciful women have boiled their own children; they became their food during the destruction of the daughter of my people.
<margin>The Lord has fulfilled</margin>
**T**he Lord has fulfilled His fury; He has poured out the wrath of His indignation, and has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has devoured her foundations.
**T**he kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world did not believe that the adversary and the enemy would enter through the gates of Jerusalem.
**B**ecause of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed the blood of the just in her midst.
**T**he blind have wandered in the streets, they are polluted with blood; and when they could not help it, they held up their skirts.
"**D**epart, you polluted ones!" they cried to them. "Depart, go away! Do not touch!" For they quarreled and were moved, and they said among the nations: "He shall no longer dwell among them."
**T**he face of the Lord has divided them, and He will no longer look upon them.
**T**hey did not respect the faces of the priests, nor did they have mercy on the elders.
**W**hile we yet remained, our eyes failed for vain help, when we looked toward a nation that could not save us.
**T**hey have made our footsteps slippery in the path of our streets. Our end has drawn near; our days are fulfilled, because our end has come.

Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of heaven; they hunted us upon the mountains and laid traps for us in the wilderness. **T**he breath of our mouth, <note>original: "speculari Christus dominus", usually translated as "the anointed of the Lord." ### The Prayer of Jeremiah the Prophet

**R**emember, O Lord, what has happened to us; look and see our disgrace. Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners. We have become orphans without a father; our mothers are like widows. We drink our own water for money; we buy our own wood at a price. We were driven by the yoke on our necks; though weary, no rest was given to us. We stretched out our hands to Egypt and the Assyrians, just to be filled with bread. Our fathers sinned and are no more, and we have carried the weight of their iniquities. Slaves have ruled over us, and there was no one to rescue us from their hands. We brought in our bread at the peril of our lives <note>original: "In animabus nostris", literally "with our souls"</note> because of the sword in the desert. Our skin was burned as if by an oven, from the face of the storms of hunger. They humbled the women in Zion and the virgins in the cities of Judah. Princes were hanged by their hands; the faces of the elders were not honored. They shamefully abused the young men, and children collapsed under loads of wood. The elders have vanished from the gates, and the young men from the choir of singers. The joy of our heart has failed; our dancing has turned into mourning. The crown has fallen from our head; woe to us, for we have sinned. Because of this, our heart has become sad with grief; therefore, our eyes have grown dim. Because Mount Zion is desolate, foxes walk upon it. But You, O Lord, shall remain forever, and Your throne from generation to generation. Why do You forget us forever and forsake us for such a long time? Turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall be turned; renew our days as they were in the beginning. .7.
