**O**n the [fifth] day of the month—it was the fifth year of the exile of King Joachin—the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was upon him there. And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it; and out of the midst of the fire was something like the appearance of amber <note>original: "electri", a brilliant alloy of gold and silver or a glowing metal.</note>, that is, out of the midst of the fire. And out of the midst of it came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: there was the likeness of a man in them. Every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. Their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot; and they sparkled like the appearance of glowing brass. They had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and the four had their faces and their wings joined. Their wings were joined one to another; they did not turn when they went, but every one went straight forward. As for the likeness of their faces, the four had the face of a man and the face of a lion on the right side; and the four had the face of an ox on the left side; and the four also had the face of an eagle above. Their faces and their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined, and two covered their bodies. And every one went straight forward; where the impulse of the spirit was to go, they went, and they did not turn as they went. As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. This appearance moved back and forth among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went lightning. And the living creatures ran and returned like a flash of lightning. Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold, one wheel appeared upon the earth by the living creatures, having four faces. The appearance of the wheels and their work was like the vision of the sea <note>original: "maris", but often translated as "chrysolite" or "beryl" in this context.</note>. And the four had one likeness; and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. When they went, they went upon their four sides, and they did not turn when they went. As for their rims, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their whole body was full of eyes round about the four of them.

**A**nd when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them; and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, and the wheels were lifted up along with them, for the spirit of life was in the wheels. When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up along with them, for the spirit of life was in the wheels. And the likeness over the heads of the living creatures was as the firmament, like the appearance of crystal, terrible to look at, stretched out over their heads above. And under the firmament were their wings, straight, one toward the other. Every one had two wings which covered his body, and every other one was likewise covered. And I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of many waters, like the voice of the Most High God. When they went, it was like the noise of a multitude, like the noise of an army. And when they stood, they let down their wings. For when a voice came from the firmament that was over their heads, they stood and let down their wings. And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone; and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above it. And I saw as the color of amber, like the appearance of fire within it round about, from his loins upward; and from his loins downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire glowing round about. As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face.

**A**nd I heard the voice of one speaking, and He said to me: "Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you." And the spirit entered into me after He spoke to me, and set me upon my feet. And I heard Him speaking to me and saying: "Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation <note>original: "gentes apostatrices", literally apostate nations</note> that has revolted from Me. They and their fathers have transgressed My covenant even to this day. And the children are of a hard face and an unbreakable heart; it is to them I send you. And you shall say to them: 'Thus says the Lord God.' Whether they hear or whether they refuse—for they are a provoking house—they shall know that a prophet has been among them. And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, nor be afraid of their words; though unbelievers and subverters are with you, and you dwell with scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a provoking house. You shall speak My words to them, whether they hear or whether they refuse, for they are provokers. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you; do not be provoking like that provoking house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."

**A**nd I looked, and behold, a hand was sent to me, in which was a roll of a book. And He spread it before me; and it was written within and without; and there were written in it lamentations, and a song, and woe. And He said to me: "Son of man, eat whatever you find. Eat this roll, and go and speak to the children of Israel." So I opened my mouth, and He fed me that roll. And He said to me: "Son of man, your belly shall eat, and your stomach shall be filled with this roll that I give you." Then I ate it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey. And He said to me: "Son of man, go, get you to the house of Israel, and speak My words to them. For you are not sent to a people of a deep speech and of an unknown tongue, but to the house of Israel; not to many peoples of a deep speech and of an unknown tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you. But the house of Israel will not listen to you, because they will not listen to Me; for all the house of Israel are of a hard forehead and a stiff heart. Behold, I have made your face stronger than their faces, and your forehead harder than their foreheads. As an adamant and as a flint have I made your face. Do not fear them, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a provoking house." Moreover, He said to me: "Son of man, all My words that I shall speak to you, receive in your heart and hear with your ears. And go, get you to the exile, to the children of your people, and speak to them and tell them: 'Thus says the Lord God,' whether they hear or whether they refuse." Then the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great commotion: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place." I heard also the noise of the wings of the living creatures striking one against another, and the noise of the wheels following the living creatures, and a noise of a great commotion.

**S**o the spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the indignation of my spirit; but the hand of the Lord was strong upon me. Then I came to the exiles, to the heap of new fruits <note>original: "acervum novarum frugum", a Latin translation of the place name Tel-Abib</note>, to those who dwelt by the river Chebar, and I sat where they sat, and remained there seven days, mourning in the midst of them. And at the end of seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: "Son of man..."

"I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; and you shall hear the word from my mouth and announce it to them from me. If, when I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' you do not announce it to him nor speak to turn him from his wicked way so that he may live, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at your hand. But if you announce it to the wicked and he is not converted from his wickedness and his wicked way, he indeed shall die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your soul. If the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, I will lay a stumbling block before him; he shall die because you did not announce it to him. He shall die in his sin, and the righteousness he performed shall not be remembered, but I will require his blood at your hand. But if you announce to the righteous man that he should not sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live because you announced it to him, and you have delivered your soul."

**And** you, son of man, take a brick <note>original: "laterem". This refers to a clay tile or tablet common in Babylon for writing or drawing.</note> and place it before you, and describe upon it the city of Jerusalem. And you shall ordain a siege against it, and build forts, and cast up a mound, and place camps around it, and set battering rams around it. And you, take an iron plate <note>original: "ferream sartaginem" or "fertuam ferrā". This symbolizes an unbreakable barrier between God and the city.</note> and place it as an iron wall between you and the city; and you shall set your face toward it, and it shall be under siege, and you shall surround it. This is a sign to the house of Israel. And you shall sleep upon your left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it; and according to the number of days you sleep upon it, you shall bear their iniquity. For I have given you the years of their iniquity by the number of days: three hundred and ninety days; and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel. And when you have completed these, you shall sleep upon your right side, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for forty days—a day for a year, a day for a year I have given to you. And toward the siege of Jerusalem you shall turn your face, and your arm shall be extended, and you shall prophesy against it. Behold, I have surrounded you with chains, and you shall not turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege. And take for yourself wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and vetch; and put them into one vessel, and make bread for yourself according to the number of days you sleep on your side: for three hundred and ninety days you shall eat it. And your food which you shall eat shall be by weight: twenty shekels <note>original: "stateru". A measure of weight; this indicates extreme rationing during a famine.</note> a day; from time to time you shall eat it. And you shall drink water by measure: the sixth part of a hin <note>original: "hin". An ancient Hebrew liquid measure, about 1 liter.</note>; from time to time you shall drink. And you shall eat it as a barley cake baked with dung that comes out of a man, covering it in their sight." And the Lord says, "So shall the children of Israel eat their polluted bread among the nations where I will cast them." And I said, "Ah, Ah, Ah, Lord God! Behold, my soul has not been polluted; I have not eaten anything that died of itself or was torn by beasts from my youth until now, and no unclean flesh has entered my mouth." And He said to me, "Behold, I have given you cow's dung instead of human dung, and you shall make your bread with it." And He said to me, "Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread <note>A biblical metaphor for the food supply that supports life.</note> in Jerusalem; and they shall eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and they shall drink water by measure and in distress, so that bread and water failing, each one may fall against his brother and waste away in their iniquities."

**And** you, son of man, take a sharp sword that cuts hair; and take it and pass it over your head and your beard. And take a balance for weighing and divide the hair. A third part you shall burn with fire in the middle of the city when the days of the siege are completed. And you shall take another third and cut it with the sword all around it. And the other third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will unsheathe a sword after them. And take from there a small number and bind them in the hem of your cloak. And from these again you shall take some and cast them into the midst of the fire and burn them with fire; and from it a fire shall go out into all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: "This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the midst of the nations and the countries round about her. And she has despised my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and my precepts more than the lands around her. For they have rejected my judgments and have not walked in my precepts." Therefore, thus says the Lord God: "Because you have surpassed the nations that are around you, and have not walked in my precepts, and have not kept my judgments, and have not even acted according to the judgments of the nations that are around you; therefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I myself will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations. And I will do in you what I have not done, and the like of which I will never do again, because of all your abominations. Therefore, fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments in you, and I will scatter all your remnants to every wind. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God: surely because you have violated my sanctuary with all your offenses and all your abominations, I also will break you; my eye will not spare, and I will have no pity. A third part of you shall die of pestilence and be consumed by famine in your midst; a third part of you shall fall by the sword around you; and a third part of you I will scatter to every wind, and I will unsheathe a sword after them. And I will accomplish my fury and cause my indignation to rest upon them, and I will be comforted; and they shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my zeal when I have accomplished my indignation upon them. And I will make you a desert and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of everyone passing by. And it shall be a reproach and a blasphemy, an example and an astonishment among the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments in you in fury and in my indignation, and in the rebukes of wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken. When I send the evil arrows of famine among them, which shall be deadly and which I will send to destroy you; and I will gather famine upon you and break the staff of bread. And I will send upon you famine and evil beasts to your destruction, and pestilence and blood shall pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the Lord, have spoken."

**And** the word of the Lord came to me, saying: "Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of the house of Israel and prophesy against them. And you shall say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to the mountains, and to the hills, to the ravines, and to the valleys: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy...

...your high places, and I will demolish your altars, and your idols shall be broken. And I will cast down your slain before your idols, and I will give the carcasses of the children of Israel before the face of your idols, and I will scatter your bones around your dead altars; in all your habitations, the cities shall be deserted, and the high places shall be demolished and dissipated; and your altars shall perish and be broken; and your idols shall cease and your shrines be crushed, and your works shall be blotted out. And the slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I will leave a remnant among you of those who escape the sword among the nations when I scatter you among the lands. And those of you who escape shall remember me among the nations to which they were led captive, because I have crushed their fornicating heart which departed from me, and their eyes which went whoring after their idols; and they shall be displeased with themselves for the evils they have done in all their abominations. And they shall know that I, the Lord, did not speak in vain when I said I would do this evil."

**Thus** says the Lord: "Strike your hand and stamp your foot and say: 'Alas!' for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, who shall fall by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence. He who is far off shall die of the pestilence; he who is near shall fall by the sword; and he who remains and is besieged shall die by famine. And I will accomplish my indignation upon them. And you shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain are in the midst of your idols and around your altars, on every high hill and on the tops of the mountains, and under every leafy tree and under the thick terebinth <note>A species of sumac tree often associated with pagan ritual sites in the Old Testament.</note>, the place where they burned sweet incense to all their idols. And I will stretch out my hand over them and make the land a desert, more desolate than the desert of Diblathah in all their habitations; and they shall know that I am the Lord."

**And** you, son of man, thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel: "The end has come! The end has come upon the four corners of the land. Now the end is upon you, and I will send my fury upon you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will set all your abominations against you. And my eye shall not spare you, nor will I have pity; but I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst; and you shall know that I am the Lord."

**Thus** says the Lord God: "One affliction, behold, one affliction comes. The end comes, the end comes; it has awakened against you; behold, it comes. Destruction comes upon you who dwell in the land; the time comes, the day of slaughter is near, and not of the joy of the mountains. Now I will soon pour out my wrath upon you and accomplish my fury in you; and I will judge you according to your ways and impose upon you all your crimes. And my eye shall not spare, nor will I have pity; but I will impose your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst; and you shall know that I am the Lord who strikes. Behold the day, behold it comes! Destruction has gone forth; the rod has blossomed; pride has budded. Iniquity has risen into a rod of impiety; it is not from them, nor from the people, nor from their noise, and there shall be no rest for them. The time comes, the day approaches; let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all the people. For the seller shall not return to what he has sold, while they are yet among the living; for the vision concerning all its multitude shall not be revoked; and no man shall strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life. Blow the trumpet, prepare all things, yet no one goes to the battle; for my wrath is upon all its people. The sword is outside; pestilence and famine are within. He who is in the field shall die by the sword; and he who is in the city, pestilence and famine shall devour him. And those who escape shall be saved; they shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each in his iniquity. All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall flow with water. And they shall gird themselves with sackcloth, and fear shall cover them; and shame shall be on every face, and baldness on all their heads. They shall cast their silver into the streets, and their gold shall be as dung. Their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord. They shall not satisfy their souls, nor fill their bellies, because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity. And they turned the beauty of their ornaments into pride, and made the images of their abominations and idols from it. For this reason I have made it an uncleanness to them; and I will give it into the hands of strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil, and they shall defile it. And I will turn my face from them, and they shall violate my secret place; and robbers shall enter into it and defile it. Make a chain, for the land is full of bloody judgments and the city is full of iniquity. And I will bring the worst of the nations, and they shall possess their houses; and I will make the pride of the powerful to cease, and they shall possess their sanctuaries. When distress comes, they shall seek peace and there shall be none. Trouble shall come upon trouble, and rumor upon rumor. They shall seek a vision from the prophet; and the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders. The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with sorrow, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled. According to their ways I will do to them, and according to their judgments I will judge them; and they shall know that I am the Lord."

**And** I looked, and behold, in the firmament that was over the head of the cherubim, there appeared over them something like a sapphire stone, like the appearance of a throne. **In** the midst of their moving, they followed the place where the first one turned, and the others did not turn as they moved. This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chebar, and I understood that they were cherubim. Each one had four faces, and each had four wings, and the likeness of a man's hand was under their wings. **And** the word of the Lord came to me in the morning, saying: "Son of man: has the house of Israel, that rebellious house, not said to you: 'What are you doing?' ...fury on that day, and great stones into the wall for its completion. And I will destroy the wall which you have whitewashed with untempered mortar <note>original: "linistis commiscentia," referring to a wall built poorly and then covered with plaster to hide its structural weakness</note>, and I will bring it down to the ground, and its foundation shall be revealed. And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own heart, and prophesy against them, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Woe to those who sew magic cushions <note>original: "pulvillos," small pillows or bands used in folk-magic or divination</note> under every elbow, and make veils for the heads of persons of every age to ensnare souls! When you were ensnaring the souls of my people, you kept their souls alive for yourselves. And you violated my holiness before my people for a handful of barley and a fragment of bread, to kill souls that should not die, and to keep alive souls that should not live, lying to my people who believe your lies. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against your magic cushions with which you ensnare souls as they fly, and I will tear them from your arms; and I will let the souls go—the souls you ensnare to make them fly. And I will tear your veils, and I will deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall no longer be in your hand to be preyed upon; and you shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have grieved the heart of the righteous man with lies, whom I did not sadden, and you have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he would not return from his evil way to live; therefore you shall see vain things no more, and you shall no longer practice divinations; and I will deliver my people from your hand. And you shall know that I am the Lord.

And certain of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, these men have placed their filth <note>original: "immunditias," often referring to idols</note> in their hearts, and have set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces. Should I let myself be questioned by them? Therefore speak to them and say: Thus says the Lord God: Any man of the house of Israel who sets his filth in his heart, and places the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet to inquire of me through him, I, the Lord, will answer him according to the multitude of his filth; so that the house of Israel may be caught in their own heart, whereby they have departed from me for all their idols. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Be converted, and depart from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your contaminations. For any man of the house of Israel, or of the proselytes—whoever is a stranger in Israel—if he separates himself from me and sets his idols in his heart and places the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to a prophet to inquire of me through him, I the Lord will answer him by myself. And I will set my face against that man, and I will make him an example and a proverb, and I will destroy him from the midst of my people; and you shall know that I am the Lord. And when the prophet has gone astray and spoken a word, I the Lord have deceived that prophet <note>A difficult theological passage suggesting God allows false prophets to be misled as part of a judicial punishment on a rebellious people</note>; and I will stretch out my hand upon him and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel. And they shall bear their iniquity; as the iniquity of the inquirer is, so shall the iniquity of the prophet be, so that the house of Israel may no longer go astray from me, nor be polluted by all their transgressions, but may be my people, and I may be their God, says the Lord of hosts.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, when a land sins against me by trespassing grievously, I will stretch out my hand upon it and break its staff of bread <note>original: "virgam panis," meaning the food supply</note>, and I will send famine upon it, and I will kill man and beast from it. And if these three men were in its midst—Noah, Daniel, and Job—they would deliver only their own souls by their justice, says the Lord of hosts. Or if I should bring evil beasts upon the land to waste it, so that it becomes desolate and no one can pass through because of the beasts; even if these three men were in it, as I live, says the Lord God, they would deliver neither sons nor daughters, but they alone would be delivered, and the land would be desolate. Or if I should bring a sword upon that land and say to the sword, "Pass through the land," and I kill man and beast from it, and these three men are in its midst; as I live, says the Lord God, they would not deliver sons or daughters, but they alone would be delivered. Or if I should send a pestilence upon that land and pour out my indignation upon it in blood, to take away from it man and beast, and Noah, Daniel, and Job were in its midst; as I live, says the Lord God, they would deliver neither son nor daughter, but they would deliver only their own souls by their justice. For thus says the Lord God: Even if I send my four most grievous judgments—the sword, famine, evil beasts, and pestilence—upon Jerusalem to kill man and beast from it, yet behold, there shall be left in it a remnant of those who are led out, sons and daughters. Behold, they shall come forth to you, and you shall see their way and their deeds; and you shall be comforted for the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, for all that I have brought upon her. And they shall comfort you when you see their ways and their deeds, and you shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in her, says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, what shall be done with the wood of the vine among all the trees of the forest that are among the trees of the woods? Shall wood be taken from it to make any work? Or will a peg be fashioned from it to hang any vessel upon? Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel; the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is reduced to ash. Will it be useful for any work? Even when it was whole, it was not useful for work; how much less, when the fire has devoured and consumed it, shall any work be made of it? Therefore thus says the Lord God: As the vine wood among the trees of the forest which I have given to the fire to be devoured, so will I give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem and its dwellers. And I will set my face against them; they shall go out from one fire, and another fire shall consume them. And you shall know that I am the Lord when I have set my face against them, and have made the land impassable and desolate, because they have been transgressors, says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations, and you shall say: Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem: Your root and your generation are from the land of Canaan. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite <note>A metaphorical reference to Jerusalem's pagan origins before God chose her</note>. And as for your birth, on the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, and you were not washed in water for health, nor salted with salt <note>An ancient practice thought to harden and cleanse the skin of newborns</note>, nor wrapped in swaddling clothes. No eye spared you to do any of these things for you out of compassion, but you were cast out upon the face of the earth in the bitterness of your soul on the day you were born. But passing by you, I saw you being trampled in your own blood, and I said to you when you were in your blood: Live. Yes, I said to you in your blood: Live. I caused you to multiply like the bud of the field, and you were increased and grew large, and you reached the time of womanly adornment. Your breasts grew firm and your hair

<column-break/>

sprouted, yet you were naked and full of confusion. And I passed by you and saw you, and behold, your time was the time of lovers. And I spread my garment over you and covered your shame. And I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you, says the Lord God, and you became mine. And I washed you with water, and cleansed your blood from you, and I anointed you with oil. And I clothed you with diverse colors, and shod you with violet leather <note>original: "iacincto," likely referring to fine dyed leather</note>, and girded you with fine linen, and clothed you with subtle fabrics, and adorned you with ornaments. And I put bracelets on your hands and a chain around your neck. And I put a ring upon your nose, and earrings in your ears, and a crown of beauty upon your head. And you were adorned with gold and silver, and you were clothed with fine linen and embroidered silk and many colors. You ate fine flour and honey and oil, and you became exceedingly beautiful and advanced even to a kingdom. And your name went forth among the nations because of your beauty, for you were perfect in my glory which I had set upon you, says the Lord God.

But having confidence in your beauty, you played the harlot in my name; and you offered your fornication to every passerby, to become his. And taking of your garments, you made for yourself high places covered with diverse colors, and you played the harlot upon them, as has never been done nor shall be. And you took the vessels of your beauty, of my gold and my silver which I gave to you, and you made for yourself images of men, and played the harlot with them. And you took your garments of diverse colors and clothed them, and you set my oil and my incense before them. And my bread which I gave to you—the fine flour, oil, and honey with which I fed you—you set before them for a sweet odor. And so it was, says the Lord God. And you took your sons and your daughters whom you had borne to me, and you sacrificed them to be devoured. Was your fornication a small thing, that you sacrificed my children and gave them up, consecrating them to idols? And after all your abominations and fornications, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and full of confusion, trampled in your own blood. And it happened after all your wickedness—woe, woe to you, says the Lord God—that you built for yourself a brothel and made for yourself a place of shame in every street. At every head of the way you built a sign of your prostitution, and made your beauty abominable, and divided your feet to every passerby, and multiplied your fornications. And you played the harlot with the Egyptians, your neighbors of great flesh <note>An idiom for physical vigor/lust</note>, and you multiplied your fornication to provoke me. Behold, I will stretch out my hand over you and take away your justification, and I will deliver you to the will of those who hate you—the daughters of the Philistines, who are ashamed of your wicked way. And you played the harlot with the Assyrians, because you were not yet satisfied; and after you had played the harlot, you were still not satisfied. And you multiplied your fornication in the land of Canaan with the Chaldeans, and even then you were not satisfied.

How shall I cleanse your heart, says the Lord God, when you do all these works of a harlot and an unrestrained woman? For you built your brothel at the head of every way, and made your high place in every street; nor were you like a harlot who increases her price out of disdain, but like an adulterous woman who brings in strangers over her husband. To all harlots, gifts are given; but you gave rewards to all your lovers, and you bribed them to come to you from every side to commit fornication with you. And it happened in you contrary to the custom of women in your fornications, and after you there shall be no more fornication. For in that you gave rewards, and no reward was given to you, the contrary happened in you. Therefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because your wealth <note>original: "aes tuum," literally your bronze/money</note> was poured out, and your shame revealed in your fornications with your lovers and with the idols of your abominations, and in the blood of your children whom you gave to them; behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, and all whom you loved with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you from every side, and I will reveal your shame before them, and they shall see all your nakedness. And I will judge you with the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood, and I will give you over to the blood of fury and jealousy. And I will deliver you into their hands, and they shall destroy your brothel and demolish your place of shame. And they shall strip you of your garments, and take away the vessels of your beauty, and leave you naked and full of shame. And they shall bring a multitude against you, and they shall stone you with stones, and strike you through with their swords. And they shall burn your houses with fire and execute judgments upon you in the sight of many women. And you shall cease from being a harlot, and you shall give rewards no more. And my indignation shall rest in you, and my jealousy shall depart from you, and I will be quiet and angry no more; because you did not remember the days of your youth, but provoked me in all these things. Wherefore I also have brought your ways upon your head, says the Lord God, and I have not done according to your crimes in all your abominations.

Behold, everyone who uses a common proverb shall take it up against you, saying: "As the mother is, so also is her daughter." You are the daughter of your mother, who cast off her husband and her children; and the sister of your sisters, who cast off their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite. And your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters who dwell at your left hand; and your younger sister, who dwells at your right hand, is Sodom and her daughters. But you have not walked after their ways, nor done according to their crimes for a little while only; almost you have done more wickedly than they in all your ways. As I live, says the Lord God, Sodom your sister herself and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done. Behold, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, fullness of bread, and abundance, and the idleness of her and her daughters; and they did not stretch out their hand to the needy and the poor. And they were lifted up, and committed abominations before me; and I took them away as I saw fit. And Samaria has not committed half of your sins, but you have surpassed them in your crimes, and have justified your sisters by all the sins which you have committed. Therefore, you also bear your confusion, you who have surpassed your sisters; for your sins which you have committed, perhaps more abominably than they, they are justified in comparison to you. Therefore be confounded, and bear your shame, you who have justified your sisters.

And I will restore them: the restoration of Sodom with her daughters, and the restoration of Samaria and her daughters; and I will restore your restoration in the midst of them, so that you may bear your shame and be confounded in all that you have done, while comforting them. And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their ancient state; and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their ancient state; and you and your daughters shall return to your ancient state. But your sister Sodom was not mentioned by your mouth in the day of your pride, before your malice was revealed, as at this time, for a reproach to the daughters of Syria and all the daughters of the Philistines around you, who encompass you on every side. Your crime and your shame, you have borne them, says the Lord. For thus says the Lord God: I will deal with you as you have done, in that you despised the oath to break the covenant. And I will remember my covenant...

<margin>17</margin>
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, put forth a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel, and say: Thus says the Lord God: A great eagle with large wings and long feathers, full of plumage and various colors, came to Lebanon and took the heart of the cedar <note>original: "medullam," literally the marrow or pith, symbolizing the king or the best of the nation</note>. He broke off the top of its young twigs and carried it into the land of Canaan; he set it in a city of merchants. Then he took some of the seed of the land and planted it in a fertile field by many waters; he set it like a willow tree. And it sprouted and became a low, spreading vine, its branches turning toward the eagle and its roots remaining under him. So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots. But there was another great eagle with large wings and much plumage; and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and stretched out its branches toward him, so that he might water it from the garden beds where it was planted. It had been planted in good soil by many waters to produce branches and bear fruit, and to become a noble vine. Say: Thus says the Lord God: Will it prosper? Will the first eagle not pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers? All its fresh sprouting leaves will wither. It will not require a strong arm or many people to pull it up by the roots. Behold, it is planted; will it prosper? When the scorching burning wind touches it, will it not utterly wither? It will wither in the garden beds where it grew.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Say now to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Say: Behold, the king of Babylon <note>The first eagle</note> came to Jerusalem and took its king and its princes, and led them to himself in Babylon. He took one of the royal seed and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath. He also took away the mighty of the land, so that the kingdom might be humble and not lift itself up, but keep his covenant and stand by it. But the king rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors to Egypt <note>The second eagle</note>, so that they might give him horses and many troops. Will he prosper? Will he who does such things escape? If he breaks the covenant, will he escape? As I live, says the Lord God, in the place where the king lives who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, there in the midst of Babylon he shall die. Neither with a great army nor a large company will Pharaoh help him in the war, when ramps are cast up and siege walls built to destroy many lives. For he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, even though he had given his hand <note>A formal gesture of agreement</note>; because he did all these things, he shall not escape. Therefore thus says the Lord God: As I live, surely my oath which he despised and my covenant which he broke, I will bring down upon his own head. I will spread my net over him, and he shall be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the treason he committed against me. All the fugitives from all his troops shall fall by the sword, and the survivors shall be scattered to every wind; and you shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken. Thus says the Lord God: I myself will take a sprig from the high top of the cedar and set it out; I will break off a tender one from the topmost of its young twigs and plant it on a high and lofty mountain. On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it shall bring forth boughs and bear fruit and become a noble cedar. Under it will dwell every kind of bird; in the shadow of its branches every winged creature will nest. And all the trees of the field shall know that I, the Lord, have brought low the high tree and exalted the low tree, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken and have done it.

<margin>18</margin>
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: What do you mean by repeating this proverb among yourselves in the land of Israel, saying: "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"? <note>This proverb expressed the popular belief that the current generation was being punished solely for the sins of their ancestors</note> As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no longer be used by you in Israel. Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul that sins shall die. If a man is righteous and does what is lawful and right—if he does not eat upon the mountains or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife or approach a woman during her impurity, does not oppress anyone, restores to the debtor his pledge, commits no robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with a garment, does not lend at interest or take any increase, withholds his hand from iniquity, executes true justice between man and man, walks in my statutes, and keeps my judgments to deal faithfully—he is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord God. But if he fathers a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood, who does any of these things (though the father himself did none of them)—if the son eats upon the mountains, defiles his neighbor's wife, oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not restore the pledge, lifts up his eyes to idols, commits abomination, lends at interest and takes increase; shall he then live? He shall not live. Because he has done all these abominations, he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon himself. But if this man fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, he fears and does not do likewise—if he does not eat upon the mountains or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not defile his neighbor's wife, does not oppress anyone, does not withhold the pledge or commit robbery, gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with a garment, withholds his hand from harming the poor, takes no interest or increase, keeps my judgments and walks in my statutes; he shall not die for the iniquity of his father; he shall surely live. As for his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people, behold, he died for his iniquity. Yet you say, "Why should the son not bear the iniquity of the father?" Because the son has done what is lawful and right, has kept all my statutes and observed them, he shall surely live.

The soul that sins shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself. But if a wicked man turns away from all the sins he has committed and keeps all my statutes and does what is lawful and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die. None of the transgressions he has committed shall be remembered against him; for the righteousness he has done, he shall live.

<column-break/>

Do I have any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that he should turn from his ways and live? But when a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done shall be remembered; for the treachery of which he is guilty and the sin he has committed, he shall die. Yet you say, "The way of the Lord is not fair." Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it my way that is not fair? Is it not your ways that are unfair? When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die for it; for the iniquity he has committed, he shall die. And when a wicked man turns away from the wickedness he has committed and does what is lawful and right, he shall save his life. Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he had committed, he shall surely live; he shall not die. Yet the house of Israel says, "The way of the Lord is not fair." O house of Israel, is it my ways that are not fair? Is it not rather your ways that are unfair? Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways, says the Lord God. Repent and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin. Cast away from you all the transgressions you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why will you die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, says the Lord God; so turn and live!

And you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel and say: Why did your mother, a lioness, lie down among lions? In the midst of young lions she reared her cubs. She brought up one of her cubs; he became a young lion, and he learned to catch prey; he devoured men. The nations heard about him; he was caught in their pit, and they led him with hooks to the land of Egypt. When she saw that she was frustrated and her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion. He prowled among the lions; he became a young lion and learned to catch prey; he devoured men. He ravaged their widows <note>original: "viduas," though some translations suggest "strongholds" based on the Hebrew</note> and laid waste their cities; the land and its fullness were appalled at the sound of his roaring. Then the nations set against him from the provinces on every side; they spread their net over him, and he was caught in their pit. They put him in a cage with hooks and brought him to the king of Babylon; they brought him into a stronghold, so that his voice should no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel. Your mother was like a vine in your blood <note>original: "in sanguine tuo," likely a reference to lineage or the vitality of the nation</note>, planted by the waters; it was fruitful and full of branches because of abundant water. It had strong branches for the scepters of rulers; its stature was exalted among the thick foliage, and it was conspicuous for its height and the multitude of its shoots. But the vine was plucked up in fury and cast down to the ground; the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were broken and withered; the fire consumed them. Now it is transplanted into the wilderness, into a dry and thirsty land. And fire has gone out from a branch of its shoots and consumed its fruit, so that there is no strong branch left in it to be a scepter for ruling. This is a lamentation, and it shall be used for a lamentation.

In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, certain of the elders of Israel came to consult the Lord, and sat before me. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Have you come to consult me? As I live, I will not be consulted by you, says the Lord God. Will you judge them, will you judge them, son of man? Show them the abominations of their fathers and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: On the day when I chose Israel, I lifted my hand <note>original: "levavi manum," a gesture of taking a solemn oath</note> to the seed of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I lifted my hand to them, saying, "I am the Lord your God." On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all lands. And I said to them, "Each of you, cast away the foul things your eyes feast on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt; I am the Lord your God." But they rebelled against me and would not listen to me; not one of them cast away the foul things their eyes feasted on, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt. Then I thought I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt. But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I made myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt. So I led them out of the land of Egypt and brought them into the wilderness. I gave them my statutes and showed them my judgments, by which, if a man does them, he shall live. Moreover, I gave them my Sabbaths as a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them. But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness; they did not walk in my statutes but rejected my judgments—by which, if a man does them, he shall live—and my Sabbaths they greatly profaned. Then I thought I would pour out my wrath upon them in the wilderness to consume them. But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out. Moreover, I lifted my hand to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands, because they rejected my judgments and did not walk in my statutes, and profaned my Sabbaths; for their hearts went after their idols. Nevertheless, my eye spared them, and I did not destroy them or consume them in the wilderness. I said to their children in the wilderness, "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols. I am the Lord your God; walk in my statutes, and keep my judgments and do them. Hallow my Sabbaths, that they may be a sign between me and you, that you may know that I am the Lord your God." But the children rebelled against me; they did not walk in my statutes and were not careful to observe my judgments—by which, if a man does them, he shall live; they profaned my Sabbaths. Then I thought I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the wilderness. But I withheld my hand and acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out. Moreover, I lifted my hand to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the lands, because they had not executed my judgments but had rejected my statutes, profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes were set on their fathers' idols. Therefore I also gave them statutes that were not good and judgments by which they could not live <note>This refers to God allowing them to follow their own self-destructive laws as a form of judgment</note>; and I defiled them through their own gifts—when they offered up all their firstborn—so that I might horrifiy them, and that they might know that I am the Lord. Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: In this also your fathers blasphemed me, by dealing treacherously with me. For when I had brought them into the land that I swore to give them, then they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they offered their sacrifices and presented their offensive offerings; there they sent up their soothing aromas and poured out their drink offerings. And I said to them, "What is this high place <note>original: "Bamah"</note> to which you go?" So its name is called "High Place" to this day. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Will you defile yourselves after the manner of your fathers...

When you offer your children to the fire, you are polluted with all your idols even to this day. And should I respond to you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not respond to you. <margin>21</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, set your face toward the way, and drop your word toward the south <note>original: "africum," referring to the south wind or the southern region</note>, and prophesy to the forest of the southern field. And you shall say to the southern forest: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it shall devour every green tree and every dry tree in you. The flame of the burning shall not be quenched, and every face from the south to the north shall be scorched by it. And all flesh shall see that I, the Lord, have kindled it, and it shall not be quenched. And I said:
<margin>D</margin> Ah, ah, ah, Lord God! They say of me: "Does this man not speak in parables?" **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drop your word toward the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel. And you shall say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath, and I will kill the just and the impious within you. Because I have killed both the just and the impious, therefore my sword shall go out of its sheath against all flesh from the south to the north. So all flesh may know that I, the Lord, have drawn my sword from its sheath, and it shall not be returned. And you, son of man, groan with the breaking of your loins and with bitterness; groan before them. And when they say to you, "Why do you groan?" you shall say: Because of the news that is coming; and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall hang limp, and every spirit shall grow faint, and water shall flow down all knees. Behold, it comes, and it shall be done, says the Lord God.

<margin>E</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God. Say: A sword, a sword is sharpened and polished! It is sharpened to slaughter victims; it is polished to glitter. You who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree. And he gave it to be polished so that it might be held in the hand. This sword is sharpened, and it is polished, to be in the hand of the slayer. Cry out and wail, son of man, for this is turned against my people, against all the leaders of Israel who had fled; they are delivered to the sword with my people. Therefore, strike your thigh, for it has been tested; and this shall happen when it has overturned the scepter, and it shall be no more, says the Lord God. You therefore, son of man, prophesy, and strike hand against hand. Let the sword be doubled, and let the sword of the slain be tripled. This is the sword of a great slaughter, which makes them stand aghast, and makes the heart sink, and multiplies the ruins. In all their gates I have set the dread of the sharp sword, made to glitter and polished for devouring. Sharpen yourself; go to the right or to the left, wherever the desire of your face leads. And I will strike hand against hand, and I will satisfy my indignation; I, the Lord, have spoken.

<margin>F</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, mark out two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come; both shall come from one land. And he shall grasp a sign in his hand; he shall choose it at the head of the way to the city. You shall set a way for the sword to come to Rabbath of the children of Ammon, and to Judah, to Jerusalem, the most fortified. For the king of Babylon stood at the fork, at the head of the two ways, seeking a divination <note>The king is depicted using ancient methods like shaking arrows or examining animal livers to decide which city to attack first</note>; mixing arrows, consulting idols, and inspecting entrails. At his right hand, the divination fell upon Jerusalem, to set up battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to lift the voice in wailing, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up a mound, to build fortifications. And it shall be to them as if consulting a vain oracle in their eyes, and imitating the rest of the Sabbaths; but he will remember their iniquity to capture them. Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered, and have revealed your transgressions, and your sins have appeared in all your thoughts—because, I say, you have been remembered, you shall be captured by hand. And you, profane and impious leader of Israel, whose day has come at the time of ultimate iniquity, thus says the Lord God: Remove the diadem, take off the crown. Is this not the one that exalted the humble and humbled the high? Iniquity, iniquity, iniquity I will make it. and this was not so until he came to whom the judgment belongs, and I will deliver it to him. And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God to the children of Ammon and to their reproach; and you shall say: O sword, O sword, drawn from the sheath for slaughter, polished to kill and to glitter, while they see vain things for you and divine lies for you—that you might be laid upon the necks of the impious who are slain, whose day has come at the time of ultimate iniquity. Return to your sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your birth, I will judge you. And I will pour out my indignation upon you; I will blow upon you in the fire of my fury, and I will deliver you into the hands of senseless men who fashion destruction. You shall be fuel for the fire, your blood shall be in the midst of the land. You shall be surrendered to oblivion, for I, the Lord, have spoken.

<margin>22</margin> **S**on of man, will you not judge, will you not judge the city of blood? And you shall show her all her abominations, and say: Thus says the Lord God. And you have caused your days to draw near, and have brought on the time of your years; therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the lands. Those near you and those far from you shall triumph over you, you who are foul, noble, and great in destruction. Behold, the princes of Israel, each according to his power, have been in you to shed blood. They have treated father and mother with contempt in you; they have slandered the foreigner in your midst. They have grieved the orphan and the widow among you. You have despised my sanctuaries and polluted my Sabbaths. Slanderers have been in you to shed blood, and they have eaten upon the mountains in you. They have committed wicked deeds in your midst. They have uncovered the nakedness of the father in you; they have humbled her who was unclean in her menstruation in you. And each one has committed abomination with his neighbor's wife, and a father-in-law has wickedly oppressed his daughter-in-law, and a man has defiled his sister, his father's daughter. They have taken bribes among you to shed blood. You have taken usury and increase, and greedily slandered your neighbors, and you have forgotten me, says the Lord God. Behold, I have struck my hands together over your greed which you have practiced, and over the blood shed in your midst. Shall your heart endure, or shall your hands prevail in the days which I shall bring upon you? I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it. And I will scatter you among the nations, and winnow you into the lands, and I will cause your uncleanness to vanish from you. And I will possess you in the sight of the nations, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

<margin>G</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. As silver, and bronze, and iron, and lead, and tin are gathered into the midst of the furnace, and I will kindle a fire in it to melt them, so I will gather you in my fury and in my wrath, and I will rest and melt you. And I will gather you, and kindle you in the fire of my fury, and you shall be melted in its midst. As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so shall you be in its midst; and you shall know that I, the Lord, have poured out my indignation upon you.

<margin>H</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, say to her: You are an unclean land, not rained upon in the day of fury. There is a conspiracy of prophets in her midst; like a roaring lion seizing prey. They have devoured souls; they have taken riches and treasure. They have multiplied widows in her midst. Her priests have despised my law and polluted my sanctuaries. They have made no distinction between the holy and the profane, and they have not understood the difference between the polluted and the clean. Her princes in her midst are like wolves seizing prey to shed blood, and to destroy souls, and greedily to seek gain. And her prophets smeared them with whitewash <note>original: "linebant eos absq; temperantia," literally "daubing without tempering," meaning they covered up sins with false prophecies</note>, seeing vain things and divining lies for them, saying: "Thus says the Lord God," when the Lord had not spoken. And I sought among them for a man who would build up a wall and stand in the gap against me for the land, so that I might not destroy it, and I found none. <margin>23</margin> **A**nd the word of the Lord came to me, saying: **S**on of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother. And they went whoring in Egypt; in their youth they went whoring. There their breasts were pressed, and the teats of their virginity were bruised. As for their names, Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah. Oholah went whoring against me, and she burned with lust for her lovers, for the Assyrians who were near, clothed in hyacinth-blue, princes and magistrates, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses. And she bestowed her whoredoms upon them, all the chosen men of the Assyrians; and with all for whom she burned, she was polluted by their uncleanness. Moreover, she did not leave her whoredoms which she had in Egypt, for they had slept with her in her youth, and they bruised the breasts of her virginity, and poured out their whoredom upon her. Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of the Assyrians, for whom she was mad with lust. They uncovered her shame; they took her sons and daughters, and they killed her with the sword; and they became famous among women, and they executed judgments upon her. And when her sister Oholibah saw this, she was more mad in her lust than she, and in her whoredom more than the whoredom of her sister. She lusted after the sons of the Assyrians even more—the magistrates and officials, those clothed in varied garments, horsemen who rode on horses, and all desirable young men of various forms. And I saw that she was polluted; both took the same way. And she increased her whoredoms. And when she saw men depicted on the wall, images of the Chaldeans <note>the Babylonians</note> portrayed in colors, with belts around their waists and dyed turbans on their heads, all looking like leaders, in the likeness of the sons of Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans in which they were born; and she was mad for them at the sight of her eyes, and she sent messengers to them in Chaldea. And when the sons of Babylon came to her, to the bed of her breasts, they polluted her with their debauchery, and she was polluted by them, and her soul was satiated by them. She also bared her whoredoms and uncovered her shame. And my soul turned away from her, just as my soul had turned away from her sister. For she multiplied her whoredoms, remembering the days of her youth in which she went whoring in the land of Egypt; and she was mad with lust for their company, whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys and whose flow is as the flow of horses. And you have revisited the wickedness of your youth, when your breasts were pressed in Egypt, and the teats of your youth were bruised. Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will raise up your lovers against you, from whom your soul has been satiated, and I will gather them against you all around: the sons of Babylon, and all the Chaldeans, nobles, tyrants, and princes, all the sons of the Assyrians, young men of excellent form, leaders and magistrates, all of them princes of princes, and renowned riders of horses; and they shall come against you...

Cast it out piece by piece; no lot has fallen upon it. For her blood is in her midst; she poured it out upon the smoothest rock; she did not pour it upon the ground so that it could be covered with dust. That I might bring up my indignation and take vengeance, I have set her blood upon the smoothest rock, so that it should not be covered. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of blood, for which I will make a great pyre. It has been sweated with much labor, yet its great rust has not gone out of it, not even by fire. Your uncleanness is execrable because I wished to cleanse you and you were not cleansed of your filth. But neither shall you be cleansed until I have caused my fury and my indignation to rest upon you. I the Lord have spoken. It shall come to pass, and I will do it. I will not turn back, nor will I spare, nor will I have mercy. According to your ways and according to your inventions, I will judge you, says the Lord.

And you shall do as I have done: you shall not cover your faces with a cloth, nor shall you eat the food of mourners. You shall have crowns on your heads and shoes on your feet.
