Haran, Canneh, and Eden <note>original: "Aman et chenne et eden"</note> were your merchants. Sheba, Assur, and Chilmad sold to you. These were your merchants in many ways: in wrappings of blue and embroidered work, and in chests of precious garments which were wrapped and bound with cords.

### They also had cedars in their trade: the ships of the sea were your leaders in your business. And you were filled and glorified exceedingly in the heart of the sea. Your rowers brought you into many waters: the south wind has broken you in the heart of the sea. Your riches and your treasures, and your many interwoven instruments, your sailors and your pilots who held your furniture: and your people who ruled over you: and your warriors who were in you with all your multitude that is in the midst of you: shall fall into the heart of the sea on the day of your ruin. At the sound of the pilots' cry, the fleets shall be moved: and all who held the oar shall descend from their ships. The sailors and all the pilots of the sea shall stand upon the land: and they shall wail over you with a loud voice, and shall cry bitterly: and they shall cast dust upon their heads and sprinkle themselves with ashes. They shall shave themselves bald for you, and gird themselves with haircloth: and they shall weep for you in bitterness of soul with most bitter mourning. And they shall take up a mournful song over you, lamenting: "Who is like Tyre, which has become silent in the midst of the sea?" You, who by the departure of your wares from the seas satisfied many peoples: in the multitude of your riches and your peoples you enriched the kings of the earth. Now you are broken by the sea: in the depths of the waters: your wealth and all your multitude that was in the midst of you have fallen. All the inhabitants of the islands were stunned over you, and all their kings were struck with a storm and changed their countenance: the merchants of the peoples hissed over you. You have been reduced to nothing, and you shall not be forever.

### And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: Thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said, "I am a god, and I sit in the chair of God in the heart of the sea," though you are a man and not a god: and you have set your heart as the heart of God. Behold, you are wiser than Daniel: no secret is hidden from you. In your wisdom and your prudence you have made yourself strength, and acquired gold and silver in your treasures. In the multitude of your wisdom and in your trade you have multiplied yourself by your strength: and your heart is lifted up in your power. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is lifted up as the heart of God, therefore behold, I will bring upon you the strongest of the nations, and they shall draw their swords over the beauty of your wisdom: and they shall defile your beauty. They shall kill you and drag you down, and you shall die the death of those slain in the heart of the sea. Will you speak and say "I am a god" before those who kill you, when you are a man and not a god in the hand of those who slay you? You shall die the death of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers, for I have spoken, says the Lord God.

### And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: You were the seal of resemblance, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty, you were in the delights of the paradise of God. Every precious stone was your covering: sardius, topaz, and jasper, chrysolite, and onyx, and beryl: sapphire, and carbuncle, and emerald: gold was the work of your beauty, and your holes <note>likely referring to the settings for gems</note> were prepared on the day you were created. You were a cherub, outstretched and protecting: and I set you on the holy mountain of God; you walked in the midst of stones of fire. You were perfect in your ways from the day of your creation, until iniquity was found in you. In the multitude of your trade your inner parts were filled with iniquity, and you sinned: and I cast you out from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, O protecting cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire. And your heart was lifted up in your beauty: you lost your wisdom in your beauty. I cast you to the ground: I gave you before the face of kings that they might behold you. In the multitude of your iniquities and the iniquity of your trade, you defiled your sanctuary. I will therefore bring forth a fire from the middle of you to consume you, and I will turn you to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all who see you. All who see you among the nations shall be stunned over you: you have become nothing, and you shall not be forever.

### And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Sidon, and you shall prophesy of it, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst, and they shall know that I am the Lord when I have executed judgments in her, and I shall be sanctified in her. And I will send pestilence to her, and blood in her streets: and the slain shall fall in her midst by the sword on every side, and they shall know that I am the Lord. And there shall be no more for the house of Israel a brier of bitterness or a thorn bringing pain from all around those who are against them: and they shall know that I am the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are dispersed: I shall be sanctified in them before the nations. And they shall dwell in their land which I gave to my servant Jacob. And they shall dwell in it securely: and they shall build houses and plant vineyards: and they shall dwell confidently when I have executed judgments on all who are against them round about: and they shall know that I am the Lord their God.

<column-break/>

In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the eleventh day of the month: the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and you shall prophesy of him, and of all Egypt. Speak and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon <note>original: "draco magne"; referring to a crocodile as a symbol of the Nile's power</note> who lies in the midst of your rivers: and

### You say: "The river is mine, and I made myself." And I will put a bridle in your jaws: and I will make the fish of your rivers stick to your scales: and I will pull you out of the midst of your rivers, and all your fish shall stick to your scales: and I will cast you out into the desert, and all the fish of your river. You shall fall upon the face of the earth: and you shall not be gathered nor collected. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the heaven. And all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel: when they took hold of you with their hand, you were broken: and you tore their whole shoulder. And when they leaned upon you, they were broken: and you dissolved all their loins. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you: and I will kill man and beast from you. And the land of Egypt shall be a desert and a wilderness: and they shall know that I am the Lord: because he said "the river is mine, and I made it." Therefore behold, I am against you and against your rivers: and I will give the land of Egypt to wildernesses wasted by the sword from the tower of Syene <note>Modern-day Aswan</note> even to the borders of Ethiopia. The foot of man shall not pass through it, nor shall the foot of beast walk in it, and it shall not be inhabited for forty years: and I will make the land of Egypt a desert in the midst of deserted lands, and its cities in the midst of overturned cities. And they shall be desolate for forty years: and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations: and I will winnow them into the lands: for thus says the Lord God. After the end of forty years I will gather Egypt from the peoples among whom they were dispersed. And I will bring back the captivity of Egypt, and I will place them in the land of Pathros, in the land of their birth. And they shall be there as a lowly kingdom: and among the other kingdoms it shall be the lowliest, and it shall no more be lifted up above the nations: and I will diminish them so they do not rule over the nations: nor shall they be anymore a confidence for the house of Israel, teaching iniquity so that they flee and follow them: and they shall know that I am the Lord God. And it came to pass in the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first of the month: the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army serve a great service against Tyre. Every head was made bald, and every shoulder was stripped of hair: and no reward was given to him or his army for the service which he served me against it. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will give Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon the land of Egypt, and he shall take its multitude, and spoil its spoils: and plunder its prey: and it shall be the reward for his army: and for the work for which he served me. I have given him the land of Egypt because he labored for me: says the Lord God. In that day a horn shall sprout for the house of Israel: and I will give you an open mouth in their midst, and they shall know that I am the Lord.

### And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Wail, Woe, woe for the day! For the day is near: and the day of the Lord approaches, a day of clouds. It shall be the time of the nations: and the sword shall come into Egypt, and there shall be dread in Ethiopia: when the wounded shall fall in Egypt, and its multitude shall be taken away: and its foundations destroyed. Ethiopia, and Libya, and the Lydians, and all the rest of the common people, and Chub, and the children of the land of the covenant shall fall with them by the sword. Thus says the Lord God: And those who support Egypt shall fall, and the pride of her empire shall be destroyed. From the tower of Syene they shall fall in it by the sword, says the Lord of hosts. And they shall be scattered in the midst of scattered lands, and its cities shall be in the midst of deserted cities. And they shall know that I am the Lord when I have set a fire in Egypt: and all its helpers have been crushed. In that day messengers shall go forth from my face in galleys: to crush the confidence of Ethiopia, and there shall be dread in them in the day of Egypt, because without doubt it shall come. Thus says the Lord God: And I will make the multitude of Egypt to cease by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He and his people with him, the strongest of nations, shall be brought to destroy the land. And they shall draw their swords over Egypt: and fill the land with the slain: and I will make the channels of the rivers dry, and I will deliver the land into the hand of the wicked: and I will waste it and its fullness by the hand of strangers. I the Lord have spoken. Thus says the Lord God: And I will destroy the idols, and I will make the images to cease from Memphis: and there shall no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt. And I will put terror in the land of Egypt, and I will scatter the land of Pathros. And I will set fire in Zoan <note>original: "taphnis"</note>: and I will execute judgments in Alexandria. And I will pour out my indignation upon Pelusium, the strength of Egypt, and I will kill the multitude of Alexandria: and I will set fire in Egypt. Pelusium shall suffer like one in labor, and Alexandria shall be scattered, and in Memphis there shall be daily distress. The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis shall fall by the sword, and they themselves shall be led captive: and in Tahpanhes the day shall grow dark, when I shall have broken the scepters of Egypt there, and the pride of her power shall fail in her. A cloud shall cover her: and her daughters shall be led into captivity: and I will execute judgments in Egypt: and they shall know that I am the Lord.

<margin>2nd.</margin>
### And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt: and behold, it is not bound up that health might be restored to it, that it might be tied with cloths and wrapped with bandages and might recover strength to hold the sword. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and I will break his arm, the strong one but now broken: and I will cast the sword out of his hand: and I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations: and I will winnow them in the lands. And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon: and I will put my sword in his hand: and I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and they shall groan with the groaning of the wretched before his face. And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon: and the arms of Pharaoh shall fall. And they shall know that I am the Lord: when I have put my sword into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall stretch it out over the land of Egypt. And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and winnow them into the lands: and they shall know that I am the Lord.

### And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man: speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his people: To whom are you like in your greatness? Behold, Assyria was like a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful with branches and leafy with shade, and of a high stature: and its top was elevated among the thick branches. Waters nourished it, the deep exalted it. Its rivers ran around its roots, and it sent out its streams to all the trees of the region. Therefore its height was exalted above all the trees of the country: and its boughs were multiplied, and its branches were lifted up because of many waters: when it had spread out its shadow: all the birds of heaven made their nests in its boughs, and under its leaves the beasts of the forests brought forth their young: and under its shadow dwelt a multitude of many nations: and it was most beautiful in its greatness, and in the spreading of its boughs. For its root was near many waters. The cedars in the paradise of God were not higher than it: the fir trees did not...

According to his wickedness, I have cast him out. And strangers, the most cruel of nations, shall cut him down and cast him upon the mountains. In his ruin, all the birds of the air dwelt, and all the beasts of the field were among his branches. For this reason, all the trees by the waters shall not be lifted up in their height, nor set their top among the leafy and thick boughs, nor shall any that are watered stand up in their loftiness; for they are all delivered unto death, to the lower parts of the earth <note>original: "terram ultimam"; literally "the last land," referring to the underworld or the grave</note> in the midst of the children of men, with those who go down into the pit. Thus says the Lord God: In the day when he went down to the underworld, I brought mourning; I covered the deep for him, and I restrained its floods, and the many waters were stayed. Lebanon mourned for him, and all the trees of the field were shaken. At the sound of his ruin, I moved the nations, when I brought him down to hell <note>original: "infernum"; the realm of the dead</note> with those who descend into the pit. And all the choice and best trees of Lebanon, all that are watered, were comforted in the lowest parts of the earth. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, says the Lord God.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take up a lamentation for Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and you shall say to him: You are like a lion of the nations, and like a dragon that is in the sea. You tossed your horn in your rivers, and troubled the waters with your feet, and trampled their rivers. Therefore, thus says the Lord God: I will spread my net over you with a multitude of many peoples, and I will draw you up in my dragnet. I will cast you upon the land, I will throw you on the face of the field; and I will cause all the birds of the air to dwell upon you, and I will satiate the beasts of the whole earth with you. I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill your hills with your gore. I will water the earth with the stench of your blood upon the mountains, and the valleys shall be filled with you. And when you are extinguished, I will cover the heaven and make its stars dark. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light. All the lights of heaven I will make mourn over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land, says the Lord God, when your wounded shall fall in your land, says the Lord God. And I will provoke the heart of many peoples when I bring your destruction among the nations, upon lands which you know not. I will make many people amazed at you, and their kings shall be horribly afraid for you because of your immense iniquities, when my sword shall begin to fly in their faces; and they shall be astonished, every man for his own life in the day of his ruin. For thus says the Lord God: The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon you. By the swords of the mighty, I will cast down your multitude. All these nations are invincible, and they shall lay waste the pride of Egypt, and its multitude shall be scattered. I will destroy all its cattle that were beside the great waters; neither shall the foot of man trouble them anymore, nor shall the hoof of cattle disturb them. Then I will make their waters pure, and bring their rivers like oil, says the Lord God, when I shall make the land of Egypt desolate. The land shall be forsaken of its fullness when I have struck all those who dwell in it; and they shall know that I am the Lord. This is a lamentation, and they shall lament him; the daughters of the nations shall lament him; over Egypt and over its multitude they shall lament him, says the Lord God.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, sing a song over the multitude of Egypt, and bring it down, itself and the daughters of the mighty nations, to the lower parts of the earth, with those who go down into the pit. Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and sleep with the uncircumcised. They shall fall in the midst of those slain by the sword; the sword is given; they have drawn him and all his peoples. The most powerful of the mighty shall speak to him from the midst of hell, they who with his helpers went down and slept uncircumcised, slain by the sword. There is Assyria and all her multitude; her graves are round about him, all of them slain and those who fell by the sword. Their graves are assigned in the farthest parts of the pit, and his multitude is round about his grave; all of them slain, falling by the sword, who once struck terror in the land of the living. There is Elam and all her multitude round about her grave; all of them conquered and falling by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the lower parts of the earth, who caused their terror in the land of the living, and have borne their shame with those who go down into the pit. In the midst of the slain, they have set a bed for her among all her people; her grave is round about him. All these are uncircumcised and slain by the sword; for they spread their terror in the land of the living and have borne their shame with those who go down into the pit. They are placed in the midst of the slain. There are Meshech and Tubal, and all their multitude. Around him is his grave. All these uncircumcised and slain, falling by the sword, because they gave their terror in the land of the living. And they shall not sleep with the mighty who fall, the uncircumcised who went down to hell with their weapons, and laid their swords under their heads. Their iniquities were in their bones, because they were the terror of the mighty in the land of the living. And you, therefore, shall be broken in the midst of the uncircumcised, and you shall sleep with those slain by the sword. There is Edom and her kings and all her leaders, who were laid with their army with those slain by the sword; they also slept with the uncircumcised and with those who go down into the pit. There are all the princes of the north and all the hunters <note>original: "uenatores"; often interpreted as the Zidonians or leaders of raiding parties</note>, who were brought down with the slain in fear, and were confounded in their strength; and they slept uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and bore their confusion with those who go down into the pit. Having seen them,

Pharaoh was comforted over all his multitude which was slain by the sword; Pharaoh and all his army, says the Lord God. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and say to them: When I bring a sword upon a land, and the people of the land take one man from their borders and appoint him as their watchman, and he sees the sword coming upon the land, and blows the trumpet and warns the people; then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet and does not take warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood shall be upon his own head. He heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take warning; his blood shall be upon himself. But if he takes warning, he shall save his life. But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, and the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes a life from them, that person is taken away in his iniquity; but I will require his blood at the watchman's hand. And you, son of man, I have set you as a watchman for the house of Israel. Therefore, hearing the word from my mouth, you shall warn them from me. If when I say to the wicked, "Wicked man, you shall surely die," you do not speak to warn the wicked man from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at your hand. But if you warn the wicked man to turn from his way, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your soul. And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: You have spoken thus, saying, "Our iniquities and our sins are upon us, and we pine away in them; how then can we live?" Say to them: As I live, says the Lord God, I desire not the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from his evil way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways; for why will you die, O house of Israel? And you, son of man, say to the children of your people: The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day he sins; and as for the wickedness of the wicked, it shall not hurt him in the day he turns from his wickedness. The righteous shall not be able to live by his righteousness in the day he sins. Even if I say to the righteous that he shall surely live, and he, trusting in his righteousness, commits iniquity, all his righteousness shall be forgotten; and in his iniquity that he has committed, in that he shall die. But if I say to the wicked, "You shall surely die," and he does penance for his sin, and does judgment and justice—if that wicked man restores the pledge, and gives back what he had robbed, and walks in the commandments of life, and does nothing unjust—he shall surely live and shall not die. None of the sins he committed shall be imputed to him; he has done judgment and justice; he shall surely live. And the children of your people have said, "The way of the Lord is not of equal weight," <note>original: "equi ponderis"; meaning the Lord's judgment is not fair or balanced</note> when it is their own way that is unjust. For when the righteous turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquities, he shall die in them. And when the wicked turns away from his wickedness and does judgment and justice, he shall live in them. And yet you say, "The way of the Lord is not right." I will judge every one of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, one who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me, saying: "The city is laid waste." Now the hand of the Lord had been upon me in the evening before he who had escaped came, and he opened my mouth until he came to me in the morning; and my mouth being opened, I was silent no more. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, they who inhabit those ruined places in the land of Israel speak, saying: "Abraham was but one, and he possessed the land by inheritance; but we are many, to us the land is given in possession." You stood upon your swords, you committed abominations, and every one defiled his neighbor's wife; and shall you possess the land by inheritance? Thus you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: As I live, they who dwell in the ruined places shall fall by the sword, and he who is in the field shall be given to the beasts to be devoured; and they who are in the strongholds and caves shall die of the pestilence. And it is to them as a musical song which is sung with a sweet and pleasant sound; and they hear your words and do not do them. There they shall rest in green herbs, and in fat pastures they shall be fed upon the mountains of Israel. I will feed my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord God. I will seek that which was lost, and bring back that which was cast away; I will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was weak; and that which was fat and strong I will preserve; and I will feed them in judgment. But as for you, my sheep, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he-goats. Was it not enough for you to have fed upon good pastures? Moreover, you have trodden down with your feet the residue of your pastures: and when you drank the clearest water, you troubled the rest with your feet. And my sheep were fed with that which you had trodden with your feet, and they drank what your feet had troubled.

**Therefore** thus says the Lord God to you: Behold, I myself will judge between the fat cattle and the lean. Because you pushed with sides and shoulders, and tossed all the weak cattle with your horns until they were scattered abroad, I will save my flock, and it shall be no more a spoil; and I will judge between cattle and cattle. And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David <note>The "servant David" refers to a future king in the line of David, often interpreted as the Messiah</note>. He shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd. And I, the Lord, will be their God; and my servant David a prince in the midst of them. I the Lord have spoken it. And I will make a covenant of peace with them, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land; and they that dwell in the wilderness shall sleep secure in the forests. And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the rain to come down in its season; there shall be showers of blessing. And the tree of the field shall yield its fruit, and the earth shall yield her increase, and they shall be in their land without fear; and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have broken the chains of their yoke, and have delivered them out of the hand of those that rule over them. And they shall no more be a spoil to the nations, neither shall the beasts of the earth devour them; but they shall dwell confidently without any terror. And I will raise up for them a plant of renown <note>original: "germen nominatum"; likely referring to the Messiah or a restoration of fertile growth</note>, and they shall be no more consumed with famine in the land, neither shall they bear anymore the reproach of the nations. And they shall know that I the Lord their God am with them, and that they are my people, the house of Israel, says the Lord God. And you, my flocks, the flocks of my pasture, are men; and I am the Lord your God, says the Lord God.

**And** the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against mount Seir <note>Mount Seir is the territory of the Edomites, traditional rivals of Israel</note>, and prophesy concerning it, and say to it:

**Thus** says the Lord God: Behold, I come against you, mount Seir, and I will stretch forth my hand upon you, and I will make you desolate and waste. I will destroy your cities, and you shall be desolate; and you shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have been an everlasting enemy, and have shut up the children of Israel into the hands of the sword in the time of their affliction, in the time of their final iniquity. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, I will deliver you up to blood, and blood shall pursue you; since you have hated blood, even blood shall pursue you. And I will make mount Seir desolate and waste, and I will take away from it him that goes and him that returns. And I will fill his mountains with his slain; in your hills, and in your valleys, and in your torrents, they shall fall, slain by the sword. I will deliver you up to everlasting desolations, and your cities shall not be inhabited; and you shall know that I am the Lord God. Because you have said: "The two nations and the two lands shall be mine, and I will possess them by inheritance," whereas the Lord was there. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God, I will do according to your wrath, and according to your envy which you have exercised in your hatred against them; and I will be made known by them when I shall have judged you. And you shall know that I am the Lord. I have heard all your reproaches which you have spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying: "They are desolate, they are given to us to consume." And you have lifted up yourselves against me with your mouth, and have spoken many words against me; I have heard them. Thus says the Lord God: When the whole earth rejoices, I will make you a wilderness. As you did rejoice over the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was laid waste, so will I do to you. You shall be laid waste, mount Seir, and all Idumea <note>Idumea is the Greek name for the land of Edom</note>; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

But you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel, and say: Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because the enemy has said of you: "Aha, the everlasting heights are given to us for an inheritance," therefore prophesy, and say:

**Thus** says the Lord God: Because you have been desolate and trodden under foot on every side, and made an inheritance to the rest of the nations, and have been brought upon the lips of the tongue and the reproach of the people: therefore, ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and the hills, to the torrents and the valleys, and to the desolate walls and cities, which are forsaken and spoiled by the rest of the nations round about: therefore thus says the Lord God: In the fire of my zeal I have spoken of the rest of the nations, and of all Idumea, who have given my land to themselves for an inheritance with joy, and with all their heart, and with all their mind, and have cast it out to lay it waste. Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and the hills, to the ridges and the valleys: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I have spoken in my zeal and in my fury, because you have borne the shame of the nations. Therefore thus says the Lord God: I have lifted up my hand, that the nations which are round about you shall themselves bear their shame. But you, O mountains of Israel, shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to my people Israel, for they are at hand to come. For behold, I come to you, and I will turn to you, and you shall be plowed and sown. And I will multiply men upon you, and all the house of Israel; and the cities shall be inhabited, and the ruinous places shall be repaired. And I will fill you with men and cattle, and they shall be multiplied and increase; and I will cause you to dwell as from the beginning, and I will give you greater gifts than you had from the first; and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I will bring men upon you, even my people Israel, and they shall possess you by inheritance; and you shall be their inheritance, and you shall no more be without them. Thus says the Lord God: Because they say of you: "You are a devourer of men, and one that suffocates your nation," therefore you shall eat men no more, and you shall no more kill your nation, says the Lord God. Neither will I cause men to hear in you anymore the shame of the nations, and you shall no more bear the reproach of the peoples, and you shall not lose your nation from henceforth, says the Lord God.

**And** the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, and they polluted it with their own ways and with their doings; their way was before me as the uncleanness of a menstruous woman <note>A metaphor for ritual impurity under Mosaic law</note>. And I poured out my indignation upon them for the blood which they had shed upon the land, and with their idols they polluted it. And I scattered them among the nations, and they are dispersed through the countries. According to their ways and their devices I have judged them. And they entered among the nations whither they

<column-break/>

went, and they polluted my holy name, when it was said of them: "This is the people of the Lord, and they are come forth out of his land." And I spared my holy name, which the house of Israel had polluted among the nations whither they went. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: It is not for your sake that I will do this, O house of Israel, but for my holy name's sake, which you have polluted among the nations whither you went. And I will sanctify my great name, which was polluted among the nations, which you have polluted in the midst of them: that the nations may know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. For I will take you from among the nations, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. And I will pour upon you clean water, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness, and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit in the midst of you: and I will cause you to walk in my commandments, and to keep my judgments, and do them. And you shall dwell in the land which I gave to your fathers; and you shall be my people, and I will be your God. And I will save you from all your filthiness: and I will call for the grain, and will multiply it, and will lay no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that you may bear no more the reproach of famine among the nations. And you shall remember your wicked ways, and your doings that were not good: and your iniquities and your wicked deeds shall displease you. It is not for your sakes that I will do this, says the Lord God, be it known to you: be confounded and ashamed at your own ways, O house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities, and shall have caused you to dwell in the cities, and shall have repaired the ruinous places, and the desolate land shall be tilled, which before was waste in the sight of all that passed by, they shall say: "This land that was untilled is become as a garden of pleasure <note>original: "hortus uoluptatis"; often used as a synonym for the Garden of Eden</note>, and the cities that were desolate and abandoned and destroyed are become fenced and inhabited." And the nations that shall be left round about you shall know that I the Lord have built up the destroyed places, and planted the untilled places; I the Lord have spoken it, and done it.

**Thus** says the Lord God: Moreover in this shall the house of Israel find me, that I may do it for them: I will multiply them as a flock of men, as a holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts: so shall the waste cities be full of flocks of men: and they shall know that I am the Lord.

**The** hand of the Lord was upon me, and brought me forth in the spirit of the Lord: and set me down in the midst of a plain that was full of bones. **He led** me about through them on every side. And there were very many upon the face of the plain, and they were exceeding dry. And he said to me: Son of man, do you think these bones shall live? And I said: Lord God, you know. And he said to me: Prophesy concerning these bones; and say to them: Ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will send spirit <note>original: "spiritum"; can mean breath, spirit, or wind</note> into you, and you shall live. And I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to grow over you, and will cover you with skin: and I will give you spirit and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as he had commanded me: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a commotion: and the bones came together, each one to its joint. And I saw, and behold the sinews and the flesh came up upon them: and the skin was stretched out over them, but there was no spirit in them. And he said to me: Prophesy to the spirit, prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord God: Come, spirit, from the four winds, and blow upon these slain, and let them live again. And I prophesied as he had commanded me: and the spirit entered into them, and they lived: and they stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. And he said to me: Son of man, all these bones are the house of Israel: they say: "Our bones are dried up, and our hope is lost, and we are cut off." Therefore prophesy, and say to them:

**Thus** says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your graves, and will bring you out of your sepulchres, O my people: and will bring you into the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall have opened your sepulchres, and shall have brought you out of your graves, O my people: and shall have put my spirit in you, and you shall live, and I shall make you rest upon your own ground: and you shall know that I the Lord have spoken, and done it, says the Lord God.

**And** the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, take a single stick, and write upon it: "Of Judah, and of the children of Israel his associates": and take another stick and write upon it: "For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his associates": and join them one to the other into one stick, and they shall become one in your hand. And when the children of your people shall speak to you, saying: "Will you not tell us what you mean by these things?" You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel that are joined to him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah, and will make them one stick: and they shall be one in his hand. And the sticks whereon you shall write shall be in your hand before their eyes. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the children of Israel from the midst of the nations whither they are gone: and I will gather them on every side, and will bring them to their own ground. And I will make them one nation in the land on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king over them all: and they shall no more be two nations, neither shall they be divided anymore into two kingdoms. Nor shall they be defiled anymore with their idols, nor with their abominations, nor with all their iniquities: and I will save them out of all the places in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God. And my servant David shall be king over them, and they shall have one shepherd: they shall walk in my judgments, and shall keep my commandments, and shall do them. And they shall dwell in the land which I gave to my servant Jacob, wherein your fathers dwelt: and they shall dwell in it, they and their children, and their children's children, even forever: and David my servant shall be their prince forever. And I will make a covenant of peace with them, it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will establish them, and will multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them forever. And my tabernacle shall be with them: and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And the nations shall know that I am the Lord the sanctifier of Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them forever.

**And** the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal <note>Gog and Magog are figures representing ultimate enemies of God's people in apocalyptic literature</note>: and prophesy concerning him, and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I come against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And I will turn you about, and I will put a bit into your jaws: and I will bring you forth, and all your army, horses and horsemen all clothed with coats of mail, a great multitude, armed with spears and shields and swords. It also introduces the apocalyptic figures of Gog and Magog, representing the final enemies of God's people.</summary>

Behold, it comes, and it is done, says the Lord God.

<margin>Ezekiel 39</margin>
**T**his is the day of which I have spoken. And the inhabitants shall go forth from the cities of Israel, and they shall set on fire and burn the weapons: the shields and the spears, the bows and the arrows, the hand-staves and the lances. And they shall burn them with fire for seven years. And they shall not carry wood from the fields, nor cut it from the forests, because they shall burn the weapons with fire. And they shall spoil those to whom they had been a prey, and they shall waste their wasters, says the Lord God. And it shall come to pass in that day that I will give Gog a place named for a grave in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea, which causes those passing by to be astonished. And there they shall bury Gog and all his multitude, and it shall be called the Valley of the Multitude of Gog <note>Hamon-gog</note>. And the house of Israel shall bury them, so that they may cleanse the land for seven months. Indeed, all the people of the land shall bury them, and it shall be for them a famous day, the day in which I am glorified, says the Lord God. And they shall appoint men to continually survey the land, to bury and search for those who remained upon the face of the earth, so that they may cleanse it. After seven months they shall begin to search, and they shall go through the land. And when they see a human bone, they shall set up a sign by it, until the undertakers <note>original: "pollinctores," those who prepare the dead for burial</note> bury it in the Valley of the Multitude of Gog. And the name of the city shall be Hamonah; and they shall cleanse the land.

## DANIEL THE PROPHET

<margin>Jerome's Preface</margin>
The Church of the Lord our Savior does not read the version of Daniel according to the seventy interpreters <note>the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible</note>; instead, they use the edition of Theodotion <note>a 2nd-century scholar who produced a Greek version of the Old Testament closer to the Hebrew text</note>. Why this happened, I do not know. Whether it was because the language is Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note>, and it differs from our speech by certain unique properties, and so the seventy interpreters did not wish to preserve those same features in the Latin language; or whether the book was published under their name by some unknown person who did not sufficiently know the Chaldean language; or whatever other cause might have existed, I am ignorant. One thing I can affirm: that it differs greatly from the truth and was rightly rejected by sound judgment. It should be known that Daniel and Ezra are indeed written in Hebrew letters, but much of them is in the Aramaic <note>original: "ambitalice," likely "chaldaice"</note> language. Finally, I have written on Daniel after a brief reading of the "flowers" <note>choice excerpts</note> of Theodotion, whose translations into Latin are now rarely seen shining through; but you will be able to read these things from the Lord later. Nothing in them is merely empty, clattering words. And soon regarding our Daniel: I have been affected by such a great desire—lest I should seem to despise your labor or the effort of your whole number. Indeed, with Judah the Hebrew <note>a Jewish teacher who assisted Jerome</note> encouraging me, and frequently urging it in his own language, labor has conquered all things. I know that many among you suspect that I want to favor my Hebrew friends so that I might know how to read and understand the Chaldean language in the Chaldean script. We have mentioned these things now in the preface: for the history of Daniel also contains a vision, and also the hymn of the three youths, and the stories of Bel and the Dragon <note>referring to the deuterocanonical additions to Daniel</note>. Because these are dispersed throughout the whole world, we have placed them at the end, marked with a spit <note>the "obelus" symbol used to indicate text not found in the Hebrew</note>, so that we would not seem to the unlearned to have cut off a great part of the volume. I heard from a certain one of the teachers of the Jews, when this vision concerning Daniel... <unclear>who confesses it is missing from the Hebrew...</unclear>

# IN THE THIRTIETH YEAR OF THE REIGN OF JEHOIAKIM, KING OF JUDAH, NEBUCHADNEZZAR KING OF BABYLON CAME TO JERUSALEM <note>The large header incorrectly states "thirtieth" (tricesimo); the main text below correctly identifies it as the "third" (tertio) year</note>

In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it. And the Lord delivered Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his hand, along with part of the vessels of the house of the Lord; and he carried them away into the land of Shinar <note>Babylonia</note>, into the house of his god, and he put the vessels into the treasury of his god. And the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some of the children of Israel, of the royal seed and of the nobles: youths in whom there was no blemish, handsome in form, and skillful in all wisdom, careful in knowledge, and learned in teaching, who might be able to stand in the king's palace, so that he might teach them the letters and language of the Chaldeans. And the king appointed them a daily portion of his own food, and of the wine which he himself drank, so that after three years of training, they might stand in the king's presence. Now among these were the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. And the chief of the eunuchs gave them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego. But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not be defiled by the king’s table, nor by the wine of his drink; and he asked the chief of the eunuchs that he might not be defiled. And God gave Daniel grace and mercy in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs. And the prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel: "I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and drink; for if he should see your faces thinner than those of the other youths of your age, you will endanger my head to the king." And Daniel said to Malasar <note>the steward</note>, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael: "Test us, I beseech you, your servants, for ten days, and let pulse <note>vegetables</note> be given us to eat and water to drink. And then let our countenances be compared with the countenances of the youths who eat the king’s food, and as you shall see, deal with your servants." Having heard this proposal, he tested them for ten days. And after ten days, their countenances appeared better and fatter than all the youths who ate the king’s food. Therefore, Malasar took away their portion and the wine of their drink and gave them pulse. And to these youths, God gave knowledge and instruction in every book and wisdom; but to Daniel, he gave understanding of all visions and dreams. So when the days were completed after which the king had said they should be brought in, the chief of the eunuchs brought them into the presence of Nebuchadnezzar. And when the king had spoken with them, there were none found among them all like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. And they stood in the presence of the king. And in every word of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the diviners and magicians who were in all his kingdom. And Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus. In the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar saw a dream, and his spirit was terrified, and his dream fled from him. Therefore, the king commanded that the diviners, magicians, sorcerers, and Chaldeans should be called together to tell the king his dreams. When they had come, they stood before the king. And the king said to them: "I have seen a dream, and being confused in mind, I do not know what I saw." And the Chaldeans answered the king in Syriac <note>Aramaic</note>: "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will show its interpretation." The king answered and said to the Chaldeans: "The word has gone out from me <note>meaning: my decree is firm</note>: unless you tell me the dream and its meaning, you shall perish, and your houses shall be made public property. But if you tell the dream and its meaning, you shall receive from me rewards and gifts and great honor. Therefore, show me the dream and its interpretation." They answered a second time and said: "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will show its interpretation." The king answered and said: "I know for certain that you are trying to buy time, knowing that the word has gone out from me. If therefore you do not show me the dream, there is but one sentence for you: that you have prepared a false and deceptive interpretation, full of deceit, to speak before me."

### Then Daniel inquired concerning the law and the decree from Arioch, the captain of the king’s military, who had gone out to slay the wise men of Babylon. When Arioch had explained the matter to Daniel, Daniel went in and asked the king that he would give him time to show the solution to the king. And he entered his house, and showed the matter to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions, so that they might seek mercy from the face of the God of heaven concerning this mystery <note>original: "sacramento," here meaning a hidden or sacred mystery</note>, and that Daniel and his companions might not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon. Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel by a vision in the night. And Daniel blessed the God of heaven and spoke: Let the name of the Lord be blessed from age to age <note>original: "a selo & usq[ue] in selm," a Latinization of the Hebrew "olam," meaning eternity or world</note>, for wisdom and strength are His. ### Then Arioch in haste brought Daniel to the king and said to him: I have found a man among the children of the captivity of Judah who will announce the solution to the king. The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar <note>original: "balchasar," a variant spelling of Belteshazzar</note>: Do you think you can truly show me the dream which I saw and its interpretation? And Daniel, answering before the king, said: The mystery which the king asks, the wise men, the magicians, the soothsayers, and the diviners cannot show to the king. But there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, who has shown to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, what things are to come in the latter times. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are of this sort: You, O king, began to think upon your couch what should be hereafter: and He who reveals mysteries showed you what is to come—and this not by any wisdom that is in me more than in all the living, but this mystery was revealed so that the interpretation might be made manifest to the king, and that you might know the thoughts of your mind.

### You, O king, were watching, and behold, as it were, a single great statue. That statue, large and of lofty stature, stood before you, and its appearance was terrible. The head of this statue was of the finest gold; but the chest and arms were of silver; the belly and thighs were of bronze; the legs, however, were of iron. Of the feet, one part was iron, but another part was clay. You saw it thus until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them. Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of a summer threshing floor, which are carried away by the wind; and no place was found for them. But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth. This is the dream. We will also tell its interpretation before you. You are a king of kings, and the God of heaven has given you a kingdom, and strength, and power, and glory. And all places where the children of men dwell, and the beasts of the field, and the birds of the air, He has given into your hand, and has established all things under your dominion. You, therefore, are the golden head. And after you another kingdom shall rise, less than yours, of silver. And another third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over the whole world. And the fourth kingdom shall be as iron. Just as iron crushes and subdues all things, so shall it crush and break all these. Furthermore, because you saw the part of the feet and toes to be of potter’s clay and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; yet it shall be of the iron plant <note>original: "plantario ferrei," suggesting the root or stock of the iron</note>, according to what you saw of the iron mixed with miry clay. And as the toes of the feet were part of iron and part of clay, the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly broken. And whereas you saw iron mixed with miry clay, they shall indeed mingle themselves with the seed of man, but they shall not stick to one another, just as iron cannot be mixed with clay. But in the days of those kingdoms, the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that shall not be destroyed forever, and His kingdom shall not be delivered to another people. It shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and itself shall stand forever, according to what you saw, that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and it crushed the clay, and the iron, and the bronze, and the silver, and the gold. The great God has shown the king what things shall come to pass hereafter; and the dream is true, and its interpretation is faithful. Then Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer sacrifices and incense to him. Therefore the king, speaking, said to Daniel: Truly your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of mysteries, since you could open this secret. Then the king raised Daniel to a high station and gave him many great gifts, and appointed him prince over all the provinces of Babylon, and prefect of the magistrates over all the wise men of Babylon. But Daniel requested of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego <note>original: "sydrac. mysac. & abdenago"</note> over the works of the province of Babylon; but Daniel himself was at the king's gates.

**T**hen King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose up quickly: and he said to his nobles, "Did we not cast three men bound into the midst of the fire?" They answered the king and said, "True, O king." The king answered and said, "Behold, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and there is no harm in them; and the appearance of the fourth is like the Son of God." Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the burning fiery furnace and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here." And immediately Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire. And the satraps, magistrates, judges, and the king's powerful men gathered to look at those men, seeing that the fire had no power over their bodies, and the hair of their head was not singed, and their cloaks were not changed, and the smell of fire had not passed onto them. And breaking forth, Nebuchadnezzar said, "Blessed be their God—the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who sent his angel and delivered his servants who believed in him. They changed the king's word and yielded their bodies so that they might not serve or worship any god except their own God. Therefore, this decree is established by me: that every people, tribe, and language, whichever shall speak blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall perish and his house shall be laid waste. For there is no other God who can save in this way." Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.

---

**N**ebuchadnezzar the king, to all peoples, nations, and languages that dwell in all the earth: peace be multiplied to you. The Most High God has performed signs and wonders toward me. It has pleased me to preach his signs, for they are great; and his wonders, for they are mighty; and his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his power is from generation to generation. I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house and flourishing in my palace. I saw a dream that terrified me: and my thoughts upon my bed and the visions of my head troubled me. And a decree was made by me to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, that they might show me the interpretation of the dream. Then the <term>magi</term> <note>magicians or wise men</note>, soothsayers, Chaldeans, and <term>diviners</term> <note>original: "aruspices," those who interpret signs</note> entered: and I told the dream in their presence, but they did not show me its interpretation, until at last my colleague Daniel entered before me, whose name is Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, who has the spirit of the holy gods in himself. And I spoke the dream before him: "Belteshazzar, prince of soothsayers, whom I know to have the spirit of the holy gods in you, and that no mystery is impossible for you: tell the vision of my dream which I saw, and its interpretation. The vision of my head in my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was exceeding great. The tree was great and strong: and its top reached unto heaven. Its sight was unto the ends of all the earth. Its leaves were most beautiful, and its fruit exceeding much, and in it was food for all. Under it dwelt the animals and beasts, and in its branches lived the birds of the air, and from it all flesh was fed. I saw in the vision of my head upon my bed, and behold, a <term>watcher</term> <note>original: "vigil," a class of angel</note> and a holy one came down from heaven. And he cried aloud and said thus: 'Cut down the tree and chop off its branches; shake off its leaves and scatter its fruit; let the beasts flee from under it, and the birds from its branches. Nevertheless, leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and let it be bound with a band of iron and brass among the grass that is outside; and let it be wet with the dew of heaven, and let its portion be with the wild beasts in the grass of the earth. Let his heart be changed from a human one, and let the heart of a beast be given to him, and let seven times pass over him. This is the decree by the sentence of the watchers, and the word and petition of the holy ones, until the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and he will give it to whomever he wills, and will appoint over it the lowest of men.'"

---

**H**ere there shall be no end to this discourse. "You, Belteshazzar, interpret it, for all the wise men of my kingdom were not able to show me the interpretation. But you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you." Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, began to think silently within himself for about one hour, and his thoughts troubled him. But the king answered and said, "Belteshazzar, let not the dream and its interpretation trouble you." Belteshazzar answered and said, "My lord, may the dream be to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your enemies. The tree that you saw, lofty and strong, whose height reached to heaven and was visible to all the earth, whose branches were most beautiful and its fruit abundant, providing food for all, under which the beasts of the field dwelt and in whose branches the birds of the air remained: you are that king, who has become great. Your greatness has grown and reached unto heaven, and your power to the ends of the earth. And as for what the king saw—a watcher and a holy one coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and des-

<column-break/>

-troy it, yet leave the stump of its roots in the earth, and let it be bound with iron and brass in the grass outside, and let it be sprinkled with the dew of heaven, and let his feeding be with the wild beasts until seven times pass over him'—this is the interpretation of the sentence of the Most High, which has come upon my lord the king. They shall cast you out from men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts and wild animals; and you shall eat grass like an ox, and you shall be drenched with the dew of heaven; seven times also shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wills. And as for the command to leave the stump of the roots (that is, of the tree), your kingdom shall remain for you after you have known that the power is from heaven. Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you: and redeem your sins with alms, and your iniquities with works of mercy to the poor; perhaps he will forgive your offenses." All these things came upon King Nebuchadnezzar. After the end of twelve months, the king was walking in the palace of Babylon; the king spoke and said, "Is not this great Babylon, which I have built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the glory of my beauty?"

---

**W**hile the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice fell from heaven: "To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: The kingdom has passed from you. And they shall cast you out from men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts and wild animals; you shall eat grass like an ox, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wills." In the same hour, the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar, and he was alienated from men, and ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of eagles and his nails like the claws of birds. Therefore, after the end of those days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my senses were restored to me; and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and glorified him who lives forever, for his power is an everlasting power, and his kingdom is from generation to generation. And all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing before him. For he does according to his will, both among the powers of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth; and there is none who can resist his hand and say to him, "Why have you done this?" At that same time my senses returned to me, and I came to the honor and glory of my kingdom; and my appearance returned to me, and my nobles and magistrates sought me out; and I was re-established in my kingdom, and even greater magnificence was added to me. Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and magnify and glorify the King of heaven, because all his works are true and his ways are judgments, and those who walk in pride he is able to humble.

---

**B**elshazzar <note>original: "Baltasar," the son or successor of Nebuchadnezzar</note> the king made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and each one drank according to his age. Being already drunk, he commanded that the gold and silver vessels should be brought which his father Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from the temple that was in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them. Then the gold and silver vessels were brought which had been in the temple in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them. They drank wine and praised their gods of gold and silver, of brass, iron, wood, and stone. In that same hour, there appeared fingers as if of a man writing against the lampstand upon the surface of the wall of the king's palace; and the king watched the joints of the hand as it wrote. Then the king's face was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees knocked against one another. Therefore he cried out loudly to bring in the magi, Chaldeans, and diviners. And the king spoke and said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever shall read this writing and show me its interpretation shall be clothed in purple, and shall have a gold chain around his neck, and shall be the third in my kingdom." Then all the king's wise men entered, but they could neither read the writing nor show the interpretation to the king. Wherefore King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, and his countenance was changed, and his nobles were troubled. But the Queen, because of the thing that had happened to the king and his nobles, entered the banquet house and speaking, said, "O king, live forever. Let not your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed. There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him; and in the days of your father, knowledge and wisdom were found in him. For King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners—your father, O king. For a greater spirit and prudence and understanding, and the interpretation of dreams, and the showing of secrets, and the solving of difficult problems were found in him—that is, in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now therefore, let Daniel be called, and he will tell the interpretation." Then Daniel was brought before the king. To whom the king said, "Are you Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom my father the king brought from Judea? I have heard of you, that you have the spirit of the gods, and that knowledge, understanding, and greater wisdom are found in you. And now the wise men and magi have entered into my sight to read this writing and show me its interpretation, and they could not declare the sense of this word to me."

"Furthermore, I have heard of you that you can interpret obscure things and dissolve difficult knots. If, therefore, you can read the writing and show me its interpretation, you shall be clothed in purple, and shall have a gold chain around your neck, and shall be the third prince in my kingdom." To which Daniel, answering before the king, said, "Keep your rewards for yourself, and give the gifts of your house to another. But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit hardened in pride, he was deposed from the throne of his kingdom, and his glory was taken away. **T**hat same night, Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was slain, and Darius the Mede succeeded to the kingdom at the age of sixty-two. It pleased Darius to appoint over the kingdom one hundred and twenty <term>satraps<note>Provincial governors in the Persian Empire.</note></term> to be throughout the whole kingdom, and over them three princes, of whom Daniel was one, so that the satraps might give account to them and the king should suffer no loss. Thus Daniel excelled all the princes and satraps because the spirit of God was more abundant in him. Furthermore, the king thought to set him over the entire realm. Whereupon the princes and satraps sought an occasion to find a charge against Daniel concerning the king's business, but they could find no cause or suspicion, because he was faithful, and no fault or suspicion was found in him. Therefore those men said: "We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, unless perhaps in the law of his God." Then the princes and satraps crept in to the king and spoke thus to him: "King Darius, live forever! All the princes of the kingdom, the magistrates and satraps, the senators and judges, have consulted together to establish a royal decree and an edict: that whoever shall ask any petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions. Now therefore, O king, confirm the sentence and sign the decree, so that what is established by the Medes and Persians may not be changed, nor may any transgression be allowed." Therefore King Darius set forth the edict and established it.

<margin>7</margin>
**W**hen Daniel learned of this—that is, the established law—he entered his house, and with the windows open in his upper chamber toward Jerusalem, three times a day he knelt down and adored and gave thanks before his God, just as he had been accustomed to do before. Then those men, searching curiously, found Daniel praying and beseeching his God. Approaching the king, they spoke to him about the edict: "O king, did you not decree that every man who should ask anything of any of the gods or men for thirty days, except of you, O king, should be cast into the den of lions?" The king answered and said: "The word is true, according to the decree of the Medes and Persians." It was a true and direct word. To which they answered and said before the king: "Daniel, of the children of the captivity of Judah, has not cared for your law, nor for the edict you established, but three times a day he prays his prayer." When the king heard this word, he was greatly grieved, and he set his heart on Daniel to deliver him, and until the setting of the sun he labored to rescue him. But the men, understanding this, said to the king: "Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is that every decree which the king establishes may not be changed." <note>The repetition "immutari mutari" in the Latin likely reflects a scribal error or emphasis on the unchangeable nature of the law.</note> Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and cast him into the den of lions. And the king said to Daniel: "Your God, whom you always worship, he will deliver you." And a stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, which the king sealed with his own ring and with the ring of his nobles, so that nothing might be done against Daniel. And the king went to his house and slept fasting, and food was not brought before him; moreover, sleep fled from him. Then the king, rising early at dawn, went in haste to the den of lions. And approaching the den, he cried out with a tearful voice and spoke to him: "Daniel, servant of the living God, do you think your God, whom you serve always, was able to rescue you from the lions?" And Daniel, answering the king, said: "O king, live forever! My God sent his angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not hurt me, because before him justice was found in me; and also before you, O king, I have done no wrong." Then the king was exceedingly glad for him, and commanded Daniel to be taken out of the den. And Daniel was taken out of the den, and no injury was found in him, because he believed in his God. Moreover, by the king’s command, those men who had accused Daniel were brought and cast into the den of lions, they and their children and their wives; and they did not reach the bottom of the den before the lions seized them and crushed all their bones. Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, tribes, and languages dwelling in all the earth: "May peace be multiplied to you. A decree is established by me that in all my empire and kingdom men should tremble and fear the God of Daniel. He is the living and eternal God forever, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed, and his power is forever. He is the deliverer and savior, performing signs and wonders and marvels in heaven and on earth, who has delivered Daniel from the den of lions." Furthermore, Daniel continued until the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

<margin>A</margin>
**I**n the first year of Belshazzar, king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream. Moreover, the vision of his head was in his bed, and writing the dream in a brief discourse, he reached the sum of the matter and said: "I saw in my vision by night, and behold, the four winds of heaven fought upon the great sea. And four great beasts came up from the sea, different from one another. The first was like a lioness, and had wings of an eagle. I beheld until its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the earth and stood upon its feet like a man, and the heart of a man was given to it. And behold, another beast, like a bear, stood on one side, and there were three rows in its mouth and in its teeth, and they said to it: 'Arise, devour much flesh.' After this I beheld, and behold, another like a leopard, and it had wings upon it like a bird—four of them—and there were four heads on the beast, and power was given to it. After this I beheld in the night vision, and behold, a fourth beast, terrible and wonderful and exceeding strong. It had great iron teeth, eating and breaking in pieces, and trampling the rest with its feet. Moreover, it was unlike the other beasts which I had seen before, and it had ten horns. I considered the horns, and behold, another little horn came up from the midst of them, and three of the first horns were plucked out from before it. And behold, eyes like the eyes of a man were in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things. I beheld until thrones were placed, and the Ancient of Days <note>A title for God emphasizing His eternal nature.</note> sat. His garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like clean wool. His throne was flames of fire, its wheels

<column-break/>

burning fire. A fiery and rapid stream issued from before him. Thousands of thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand times a hundred thousand stood before him. The judgment sat, and the books were opened. I beheld because of the voice of the great words which that horn spoke; and I saw that the beast was slain, and its body perished, and was given to be burned with fire. And the power of the other beasts was taken away, and times of life were appointed to them for a time and a time. I beheld therefore in the vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven, one like the Son of Man came even to the Ancient of Days, and they presented him before his sight. And he gave him power and honor and a kingdom, and all peoples, tribes, and languages shall serve him. My spirit shuddered; I, Daniel, was terrified by these things, and the visions of my head troubled me. I approached one of those standing by and asked the truth from him concerning all these things. He told me the interpretation of the words and taught me: 'These four great beasts are four kingdoms that shall rise out of the earth. But the holy ones of the most high God shall receive the kingdom from the earth and shall obtain the kingdom forever and ever.' After this I wished to learn diligently concerning the fourth beast, which was very different from all the others and exceeding terrible; its teeth and claws were of iron; it devoured and broke in pieces and trampled the rest with its feet; and concerning the ten horns which it had on its head, and concerning the other which had come up, before which three horns had fallen; and concerning that horn which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and was greater than the rest. I beheld, and behold, that horn made war against the holy ones and prevailed over them, until the Ancient of Days came and gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came and the holy ones obtained the kingdom. And thus he said: 'The fourth beast shall be the fourth kingdom upon earth, which shall be greater than all kingdoms, and shall devour the whole earth, and shall trample it and break it in pieces. Moreover, the ten horns of that kingdom are ten kings, and another shall rise after them, and he shall be mightier than the former, and he shall humble three kings. And the judgment shall sit, that his power may be taken away and be crushed and perish even to the end; but the kingdom and power and the greatness of the kingdom which is under the whole heaven shall be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all kings shall serve and obey him.' As for me, Daniel, I was much troubled by my thoughts, and my countenance was changed in me, but I kept the word in my heart."
