**I**n the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me. I, Daniel, after that which I had seen at the beginning, saw in a vision when I was in the fortress of Susa, which is in the city of Elam. Moreover, I saw in my vision that I was over the gate of Ulay. And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a ram stood before the marsh, having high horns, and one higher than the other, and growing larger. Afterward, I saw the ram pushing with his horns against the west, and against the north, and against the south, and all the beasts could not resist him, nor be delivered from his hand. And he did according to his will and became great. And as I was considering, behold, a he-goat came from the west over the face of the whole earth, and he did not touch the ground. Moreover, the goat had a notable horn between his eyes. And he came even to that horned ram which I had seen standing before the gate, and ran at him in the force of his strength. And when he had come near the ram, he was enraged against him, and struck the ram, and broke his two horns, and the ram could not resist him. And when he had cast him to the ground, he trampled him, and no one was able to deliver the ram from his hand. But the he-goat became exceeding great. And when he had grown, the great horn was broken, and four horns arose under it, toward the four winds of heaven. And out of one of them came forth a little horn, and it became great toward the south, and toward the east, and toward the strength <note>Usually translated as "the pleasant land" or the land of Israel.</note>. And it was magnified even to the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the stars to the earth, and of the stars, and trampled them. And it was magnified even to the prince of the host, and from him it took away the continual sacrifice and cast down the place of his sanctuary. Moreover, the he-goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn that was between his eyes is the first king. And he shall rise up against the Prince of princes and shall be crushed without hand. And the vision of the morning and evening which was told is true. You therefore seal up the vision, because it shall be after many days." And I, Daniel, fainted and was sick for some days. And when I rose up, I did the king’s business; and I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one who could interpret it.

**A**nd I set my face toward the Lord my God to pray and to make supplication with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

**A**las, Lord God, great and terrible, keeping your covenant and mercy for those who love you and keep your commandments. We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have acted impiously and have rebelled; we have turned away from your commandments and your judgments. We have not obeyed your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, our fathers, and to all the people of the land. To you, O Lord, belongs justice, but to us confusion of face, as it is today: to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, to those who are near and those who are far off in all the lands to which you have driven them because of the iniquities they committed against you. O Lord, to us belongs confusion of face—to our kings, our princes, and our fathers who have sinned against you. But to you, O Lord our God, belongs mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against you and have not heard the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his law which he set before us through his servants the prophets. And all Israel has transgressed your law and turned away so as not to hear your voice; and the curse and the detestation written in the book of Moses, the servant of God, has rained down upon us because we have sinned against him. And he has confirmed his words which he spoke against us and against our rulers who judged us, to bring upon us a great evil, such as has never happened under all the heavens as what has been done in Jerusalem. Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil has come upon us, and we did not entreat your face, O Lord our God, that we might turn back from our iniquities and consider your truth.

**A**nd the Lord kept watch over the malice and brought it upon us. The Lord our God is just in all his works which he has done, for we did not hear his voice. And now, O Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for yourself according to this day, we have sinned, we have committed iniquity, O Lord, against all your justice. Let your wrath and your fury be turned away, I beseech you, from your city Jerusalem and your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people are a reproach to everyone around us. Now therefore, O our God, hear the prayer of your servant and his petitions, and show your face upon your sanctuary which is deserted, for your own sake. Incline your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolation and the city upon which your name is invoked. For it is not on the basis of our own justifications that we present our prayers before your face, but on the basis of your many mercies. Hear, O Lord; be appeased, O Lord; attend and act; do not delay for your own sake, my God, because your name is invoked upon the city and upon your people.

**A**nd while I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel, so that I might lay my prayers in the sight of my God for the holy mountain of my God—

**W**hile I was still speaking in prayer, behold the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flying swiftly, touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice. And he instructed me and spoke to me and said: "Daniel, I have now come forth to teach you so that you might understand. From the beginning of your prayers, the word went forth; and I have come to tell you, because you are a man of desires <note>original: "vir desideriorum"; often translated as "greatly beloved."</note>. Therefore, consider the word and understand the vision."

**S**eventy weeks <note>The Hebrew "shabuim" refers to units of seven, usually interpreted by scholars as seventy weeks of years (490 years).</note> are shortened for your people and for your holy city, so that transgression may be finished and sin may reach an end, and iniquity may be blotted out and everlasting justice may be brought in, and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled, and the Holy of Holies may be anointed. Know therefore and take notice: From the going forth of the word that Jerusalem should be built again until the Anointed Leader <note>original: "xpm ducem"; refers to the Messiah (Christos) the Prince.</note>, there shall be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. And the street and the walls shall be built again in a time of distress. And after sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One shall be slain, and the people who shall deny him shall not be his. And the people, with a leader to come, shall destroy the city and the sanctuary. And its end shall be devastation. And after the end of the war, the decreed desolation. And one week shall confirm the covenant for many. And in the middle of the week, the victim and the sacrifice shall fail, and in the temple there shall be the abomination of desolation, and the desolation shall persevere until the consummation and the end.

**I**n the third year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was Belshazzar, and a true word and great strength. And he understood the word; for understanding is necessary in a vision. In those days, I, Daniel, mourned for three weeks of days. I ate no desirable bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth. Neither was I anointed with ointment until the days of the three weeks were completed. On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was by the great river, which is the Tigris. And I lifted up my eyes and saw: and behold, a man clothed in linen, and his loins were girded with fine gold. And his body was like <term>chrysolite<note>A yellowish-green gemstone.</note></term>, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like a burning lamp, and his arms and the parts downward to his feet like the appearance of glowing bronze, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude. I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. Moreover, the men who were with me did not see it, but a great terror fell upon them, and they fled into hiding. And I was left alone and saw this great vision. And no strength remained in me. But even my appearance was changed in me, and I withered away and had no strength at all. And I heard the voice of his words, and hearing them, I lay stunned on my face. And my face was pressed to the ground.

**A**nd behold, a hand touched me and lifted me up on my knees and on the joints of my hands and said to me: "Daniel, man of desires, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright in your place. For now I have been sent to you." And when he had spoken this word to me, I stood trembling. And he said to me: "Fear not, Daniel, because from the first day you set your heart to understand, so that you might afflict yourself in the sight of your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words. But the prince of the kingdom of the Persians resisted me for twenty-one days. And behold, Michael, one of the primary princes, came to help me, and I remained there by the king of the Persians. But I have come to teach you what shall come to your people in the latter days, because the vision is still for many days."

**A**nd when he spoke to me with words of this kind, I cast my face to the ground and was silent. And behold, something like the likeness of a son of man touched my lips. And opening my mouth, I spoke and said to him who stood before me: "My lord, in your vision my joints are loosened and no strength remains in me. And how can the servant of my lord speak with my lord? No strength remains in me; even my breath is cut off." Therefore, he touched me again, like the appearance of a man, and strengthened me and said: "Fear not, man of desires. Peace be to you. Be strengthened and be robust." And when he spoke with me, I recovered my strength and said: "Speak, my lord, because you have strengthened me." And he said: "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight against the prince of the Persians. For when I was going forth, the prince 

<column-break/>

of the Greeks appeared, coming. Nevertheless, I will announce to you what is expressed in the scripture of truth. And no one is my helper in all these things except Michael, your prince. <margin>xi</margin> <note>Daniel 11: This chapter details the historical conflicts between the Hellenistic kingdoms (the Ptolemies and Seleucids).</note> Moreover, from the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood by him so that he might be comforted and strengthened. And now I will announce the truth to you.

**B**ehold, three more kings shall stand in Persia, and the fourth shall be enriched with exceeding riches above all, and when he has grown strong in his riches, he shall stir up all against the kingdom of Greece. And a strong king shall stand and shall rule with great power and shall do whatever pleases him. And when he has stood, his kingdom shall be broken and shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not to his posterity, nor according to his power with which he ruled. For his kingdom shall be torn apart, even for outsiders, besides these.

**A**nd the king of the south <note>Referring to the Ptolemaic dynasty of Egypt.</note> shall be strengthened, and one of his princes shall be strengthened over him and shall rule with authority. For his dominion shall be great. And after the end of years, they shall be allied. And the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north <note>Referring to the Seleucid dynasty of Syria.</note> to make a friendship, and she shall not obtain the strength of her arm, nor shall her seed stand. And she herself shall be delivered up, along with those who brought her, her youths, and those who comforted her in her times. And there shall stand a plant from the sprout of her roots, and he shall come with an army and shall enter the province of the king of the north, and he shall abuse them and prevail. Moreover, their gods and their sculptures, and also their precious vessels of silver and gold, he shall carry away captive into Egypt. He himself shall prevail against the king of the north. And the king of the south shall enter the kingdom and shall return to his own land. But his sons shall be provoked and shall gather a multitude of many armies. And he coming shall hasten and overflow, and he shall return and be stirred up and shall join battle with his strength. And the king of the south, being provoked, shall go forth and fight against the king of the north and shall prepare an exceeding multitude, and the multitude shall be given into his hand. And he shall take the multitude, and his heart shall be exalted, and he shall cast down many thousands, but he shall not prevail.

**F**or the king of the north shall return and shall prepare a multitude much greater than before. And at the end of times and years, he shall come in haste with a great army and exceeding riches. And in those times many shall rise up against the king of the south; the sons of the transgressors of your people shall also be lifted up to fulfill the vision, and they shall fall. And the king of the north shall come and shall heap up a mound and shall take the most fortified cities, and the arms of the south shall not withstand. And his chosen ones shall rise up to resist, and there shall be no strength. And he, coming upon him, shall do according to his own pleasure; and there shall be no one to stand against his face. And he shall stand in the glorious land, and it shall be consumed in his hand. And he shall set his face to come and hold his whole kingdom, and he shall do right things with him. And he shall give him the daughter of women to overthrow it. And she shall not stand, nor shall she be his. And he shall turn his face toward the islands and shall take many. And he shall cause the prince of his reproach to cease, and his reproach shall be turned upon him. And he shall turn his face to the empire of his own land; and he shall stumble and fall and shall not be found. And there shall stand in his place one most vile and most unworthy of the kingly dignity; and in a few days he shall be broken, not in fury nor in battle. And there shall stand in his place a despised person, and kingly honor shall not be given to him, and he shall come secretly and shall obtain the kingdom through fraud. And the arms of the fighter shall be overcome by his face and shall be broken. Moreover, also the leader of the covenant. And after friendships with him, he shall act deceitfully; and he shall go up and shall overcome with a small people. And he shall enter into abundant and rich cities and shall do what his fathers and his fathers' fathers did not do. He shall dissipate their spoils and plunder and riches. And he shall initiate counsels against the most fortified thoughts, and this for a time.

**A**nd his strength and his heart shall be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army. And the king of the south shall be provoked to war with many and very strong aids. And they shall not stand, because they shall initiate counsels against him. And those who eat bread with him shall crush him, and his army shall be oppressed and many shall fall slain. And the heart of the two kings shall be to do evil, and they shall speak lies at one table. And they shall not prosper, because the end is still for another time. And he shall return to his land with many riches. And his heart shall be against the holy covenant, and he shall act and return to his land. At the appointed time he shall return and come to the south, and the latter shall not be like the former. And the triremes <note>original: "trieres"; ancient Mediterranean warships with three banks of oars.</note> and the Romans shall come upon him, and he shall be struck. And he shall return and be indignant against the holy covenant and shall act; and he shall return and take thought against those who have forsaken the holy covenant. And arms from him shall stand and shall pollute the sanctuary of strength and shall take away the continual sacrifice and shall give the abomination unto desolation. And the impious shall act deceitfully regarding the covenant.

**B**ut the people who know their God shall prevail and act. And the learned among the people shall teach many and shall fall by the sword and by flame and by captivity and by the plunder of days. And when they fall, they shall be relieved with a little help. And many shall be joined to them deceitfully. And some of the learned shall fall, so that they might be refined and chosen and made white until the predefined time, because there shall yet be another time. And the king shall do according to his will, and he shall be lifted up and magnified against every god; and against the God of gods he shall speak magnificent things, and he shall be directed until the wrath is completed. For the definition is performed. And he shall not regard the God of his fathers, and he shall be in the desires of women, nor shall he care for any of the gods, because he shall rise up against all things. But he shall worship the god Maozim <note>original: "Maozim"; likely referring to the "God of Fortresses."</note> in his place. And a god whom his fathers did not know, he shall worship with gold and silver and precious stone and precious things. And he shall act so as to fortify Maozim with a foreign god whom he has acknowledged. And he shall multiply glory and give them power over many and shall divide the land freely. And at the predefined time the king of the south shall fight against him. And the king of the north shall come against him like a tempest with chariots and horsemen and a great fleet. And he shall enter the lands and shall crush and pass through. And he shall enter into the glorious land and many shall fall. But these alone shall be saved from his hand: Edom and Moab and the beginning of the sons of Ammon. And he shall stretch out his hand upon the lands, and the land of Egypt shall not escape. And he shall rule over the treasures of gold and silver and in all the precious things of Egypt; he shall also pass through Libya and Ethiopia. And news from the east and from the north shall trouble him, and he shall come with a great multitude to crush and to kill many. And he shall fix his tabernacle, Apadno <note>original: "apadno"; likely a royal tent or palace location.</note>, between the seas upon the glorious and holy mountain, and he shall come even to the summit of it, and no one shall help him.

**A**t that time Michael shall rise up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people, and a time shall come such as never was...

But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book until the appointed time. Many shall pass through and knowledge shall be manifold. **And** I, Daniel, looked, and behold, as it were two others stood: one here upon the bank of the river, and the other there upon the other bank of the river. And I said to the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river: "How long until the end of these wonders?" **And** I heard the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river: when he had lifted up his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and had sworn by him who lives forever, that it would be for a time, and times, and half a time <note>A symbolic period of three and a half years, often interpreted as a time of intense trial or the duration of a specific historical persecution.</note>. And when the dispersal of the hand of the holy people shall be completed, all these things shall be fulfilled. And I heard and did not understand. Many shall be chosen and made white and tested as if by fire; and the impious shall act impiously, nor shall any of the impious understand. The learned, however, shall understand. And from the time when the continual sacrifice shall be taken away and the abomination unto desolation shall be set up, there shall be one thousand two hundred ninety days. Blessed is he who waits and reaches one thousand three hundred thirty-five days. But you, Daniel, go toward your pre-determined place, and rest; and you shall stand in your lot at the end of days."

**And** there was a man in Babylon, and his name was Joachim. And he took a wife named Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah, who was exceedingly beautiful and one who feared the Lord. **Her** parents, since they were just, instructed their daughter according to the law of Moses. And Joachim was very wealthy, and he had an orchard <note>The Latin 'pomerium' refers to an orchard or garden plot adjacent to a house.</note> near his house, and the Jews flocked to him because he was more honorable than all others. And two elders were appointed as judges in that year, of whom the Lord spoke: "Iniquity came out of Babylon from the elder judges, who seemed to rule the people." **These** men frequented the house of Joachim, and all who had judgments to be made came to them. But when the people returned at midday, Susanna would enter and walk in her husband's orchard. And the elders saw her daily entering and walking, and they burned with lust for her. And they perverted their own sense and turned away their eyes so that they would not look toward heaven, nor remember just judgments. They were both wounded with love for her, yet they did not show their pain to each other. For they were ashamed to indicate their lust, wanting to lie with her; and they watched daily with anxiety to see her. And one said to the other, "Let us go home, for it is the hour for lunch." And having gone out, they departed from each other. And when they had departed, they came back into one place; and questioning each other for the cause, they confessed their lust. And then they together appointed a time when they might be able to find her alone.

**It** happened, however, while they were watching for a favorable opportunity, that she went in as she had yesterday and the day before with only two young girls, and she wished to wash in the orchard, for it was heat <note>The Latin 'estus' indicates a period of oppressive heat.</note>. And no one was there except the two elders hidden and contemplating her. Therefore she said to the girls, "Bring me oil and ointments <term>smigmata: cleansing salves or soaps used for bathing</term> and shut the doors of the orchard so that I may wash." And they did as commanded, and they shut the doors of the orchard and went out through a back door to bring what she had ordered; and they did not know the elders were hidden inside. But when the girls had gone out, the two elders rose up and ran to her and said, "Behold, the doors of the orchard are shut, and no one sees us, and we are in lust for you. Therefore comply with us and lie with us. But if you will not, we will give testimony against you that a young man was with you, and for this reason you sent the girls away from you." Susanna groaned and said, "I am in straits on every side. For if I do this, it is death to me; but if I do not do it, I shall not escape your hands. But it is better for me to fall into your hands without the deed than to sin in the sight of the Lord." And Susanna cried out with a loud voice. But the elders also cried out against her, and one ran and opened the doors of the orchard. But when the servants of the house heard the cry in the orchard, they rushed in through the back door to see what it was. After the elders had spoken, however, the servants were greatly ashamed, because never had a word of this kind been said about Susanna. And the next day came.

**And** when the people had come to Joachim her husband, the two elders also came, full of wicked intent against Susanna to put her to death. And they said before the people, "Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, wife of Joachim." And immediately they sent for her. **And** she came with her parents and children and all her relatives. Now Susanna was exceedingly delicate and beautiful of face. But those wicked men commanded that she be uncovered (for she was covered up), so that they might be sated with her beauty. Therefore her own people and all who knew her wept. But the two priests <note>The text uses 'presbyteri' (elders/priests) interchangeably with 'senes' (old men).</note> rising up in the midst of the people, placed their hands upon her head. She, weeping, looked up toward heaven, for her heart had trust in the Lord. And the priests said, "While we were walking in the orchard alone, this woman entered with two girls, and shut the doors of the orchard and sent the girls away. And a young man who was hidden came to her and lay with her. Moreover, we, being in a corner of the orchard and seeing the iniquity, ran to them, and we saw them lying together. And him indeed we could not catch because he was stronger than us, and having opened the doors he leaped out. But having caught this woman, we asked who the young man was, and she would not tell us. We are witnesses of this matter." The multitude believed them as elders of the people and judges, and they condemned her to death. But Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said, "**Eternal** God, who are the knower of hidden things, who know all things before they happen: you know that they have borne false witness against me. And behold I die, though I have done none of these things which these men have maliciously invented against me."

**And** the Lord heard her voice. And while she was being led to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young boy whose name was Daniel. And he cried out with a loud voice, "I am clean of the blood of this woman!" And all the people, turning toward him, said, "What is this word which you have spoken?" And as he stood in the midst

<column-break/>

of them, he said, "**Are** you such fools, sons of Israel, not judging nor knowing what is true, that you have condemned a daughter of Israel? Return to judgment, because they have spoken false witness against her." Therefore the people returned with haste. And the elders said to him, "Come and sit in our midst and judge us, because God has given you the honor of old age." **Then** Daniel began: "Separate them from each other by a distance, and I will judge them." And when they were divided one from the other, he called one of them and said to him, "**You** who have grown old in evil days, now your sins have come upon you which you worked before, judging unjust judgments, oppressing the innocent and letting the guilty go free, though the Lord says: 'You shall not kill the innocent and the just.' Now therefore, if you saw her, tell under which tree you saw them talking to each other?" And he said, "Under a mastic tree <note>Latin: 'schino'. Daniel uses the name of the tree for a wordplay on the punishment.</note>." **And** Daniel said, "Rightly have you lied against your own head. For behold, the angel of the Lord, having received the sentence from God, shall cut <note>original: 'scindet'—punning on 'schino'</note> you in the middle." And having moved him away, he ordered the other to come, and said to him, "Seed of Canaan and not of Judah, beauty has deceived you, and lust has subverted your heart. Thus you did to the daughters of Israel, and they, fearing you, spoke with you. But the daughter of Judah did not endure your iniquity. Now therefore, tell under which tree you caught them talking to each other?" And he said, "Under an evergreen oak <note>Latin: 'prino'.</note>." **Daniel** said to him, "Rightly have you also lied against your own head. For the angel of the Lord remains, having a sword, to cut <note>original: 'secet'—punning on 'prino'</note> you in the middle and kill you." And so the whole assembly cried out with a loud voice and blessed God, who saves those who hope in Him. And they rose up against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them by their own mouth of having spoken false witness. And they did to them as they had evilly intended to do against their neighbor, to act according to the law of Moses, and they killed them. And innocent blood was saved on that day. But Hilkiah and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joachim her husband and all her relatives, because no shameful thing was found in her. And Daniel became great in the sight of the people from that day and thereafter.

**And** King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom. And Daniel was a guest of the king and honored above all his friends. Now there was an idol named Bel among the Babylonians, and they spent on it every day twelve great measures <term>artabae: a Persian/Egyptian unit of dry volume, roughly 50 liters</term> of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels <term>amphorae: large ceramic jars for wine</term> of wine. The king also worshiped it and went every day to adore it. But Daniel adored his own God. And the king said to him, "Why do you not adore Bel?" And he, answering, said to him, "Because I do not worship idols made by hand, but the living Lord who created heaven and earth and has power over all flesh." And the king said to him, "Does Bel not seem to you to be a living god? Do you not see how much he eats and drinks every day?" And Daniel, smiling, said, "Do not be deceived, O king. For this one is clay within and bronze without, nor does it ever eat." And the king, being angry, called his priests and said to them, "Unless you tell me who it is that eats these expenses, you shall die. But if you show that Bel eats these things, Daniel shall die, who has blasphemed against Bel." And Daniel said to the king, "Let it be according to your word." Now there were seventy priests of Bel, besides their wives and little ones and sons. And the king came with Daniel into the temple of Bel. And the priests of Bel said, "Behold, we are going outside; and you, O king, set the food and mix the wine and shut the door and seal it with your ring. And when you enter in the morning, unless you find everything eaten by Bel, we shall die—or else Daniel, who has lied against us." But they were confident because they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and through it they always entered and devoured those things. And it happened after they had gone out, the king set the food before Bel. But Daniel commanded his servants and they brought ashes, and they sifted them through the whole temple before the king. And they went out and shut the door and sealed it with the king's ring and departed. But the priests entered by night according to their custom, with their wives and children, and they ate and drank everything. And the king rose at first light, and Daniel with him. And the king said, "Are the seals safe, Daniel?" And he answered, "Safe, O king." And immediately when he had opened the door, the king looked at the table and cried out with a loud voice, "Great are you, Bel, and there is no deception with you!" And Daniel laughed and held the king so he would not enter inside, and said, "Look at the floor and recognize whose footprints these are." And the king said, "I see the footprints of men and women and infants." And the king was angry. And then he apprehended the priests and their wives and children, and they showed him the hidden little doors through which they entered and consumed what was on the table. Therefore the king killed them and delivered Bel into the power of Daniel, who destroyed it and its temple.

**And** there was a great dragon in that place, and the Babylonians worshiped it. And the king said to Daniel, "Behold, now you cannot say that this is not a living god. Therefore adore him." And Daniel said, "I adore the Lord my God, for He is the living God; but this one is not a living god. But you, O king, give me power, and I will kill the dragon without sword or club." And the king said, "I give it to you." Therefore Daniel took pitch and fat and hair and cooked them together and made lumps, and he put them into the mouth of the dragon, and the dragon burst asunder. And he said, "Behold what you worshiped." When the Babylonians heard this, they were exceedingly indignant and gathered against the king and said, "The king has become a Jew! He has destroyed Bel, killed the dragon, and slain the priests." **And** they said when they came to the king, "Deliver Daniel to us. Otherwise we will kill you and your house." Therefore the king saw they rushed upon him violently, and compelled by necessity he delivered Daniel to them. They cast him into the lions' den, and he was there for six days. Now in the den were seven lions, and they were given daily two bodies and two sheep; and then they were not given to them so that they might devour Daniel. But there was Habakkuk the prophet in Judea, and he had cooked a pottage and had broken bread into a bowl and was going into the field to carry it to the reapers. And the angel of the Lord said to Habakkuk, "Carry the lunch you have to Babylon, to Daniel, who is in the lions' den." And Habakkuk said, "Lord, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know the den." And the angel of the Lord took him by the crown of his head and carried him by the hair of his head and placed him in Babylon over the den by the force of his spirit. And Habakkuk cried out, saying, "Daniel, servant of God, take the lunch which God has sent to you." And Daniel said, "You have remembered me, O Lord, and you have not forsaken those who love you." And Daniel, rising, ate. Moreover, the angel of the Lord restored Habakkuk immediately to his place. Therefore the king came on the seventh day to mourn Daniel, and he came to the den and looked in; and behold, Daniel was sitting there. And he cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Great are you, Lord God of Daniel!" And he drew him out of the lions' den. Moreover, those who had been the cause of his destruction he cast into the den, and they were devoured in a moment before him.

THE ORDER OF THE TWELVE PROPHETS IS NOT THE SAME
among the Hebrews as it is among us: and so according to what is read there, the arrangement is also taken up here. For they are one single book: and speaking as if through short sentences, it contains as many plain meanings. It is somewhat obscure until it reaches Malachi; each prophet has his own specialty, yet they write the same thing. Let us listen to the Hebrew tradition, from which it would be too long to speak now. I only wish for us to have done this work as a reminder: that there is one book of the twelve prophets, and they are contemporary with Isaiah, Jeremiah, Micah, Haggai, Zechariah, and Joseph <note>likely a reference to the tradition of the prophets during the era of the Restoration</note>; among whom there is a double count among the Hebrews, and here in three verses which are also in the first chapter, his meaning is found. For they say many things because they were warned by the same prophets, just as they report the Vulgate <note>original: "uulcatum," likely referring to the common Greek or Latin version</note>, so that by his own name he knows his prophet; the following is known: Ezra himself, however great a writer of the prophets, writes under the name of Malachi. One thing remains: that from the prophets themselves they are gathered by a certain sure voice.

son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
The **B**eginning of the Lord’s speaking to Hosea. And the Lord said to Hosea: "Go, take for yourself a wife of harlotries and have children of harlotries, because the land, committing harlotry, shall depart from the Lord." And he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim. And she conceived and bore him a son. And the Lord said to him: "Call his name Jezreel, for in a little while I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease. And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel." And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him: "Call her name 'Without Mercy' <note>original: "absq; miseria," reflecting the Hebrew Lo-Ruhamah</note>, for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them. But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them in the Lord their God; and I will not save them by bow, or sword, or war, or horses, or horsemen." And she weaned her who was 'Without Mercy.' And she conceived and bore a son. And He said: "Call his name 'Not My People' <note>original: "non populus mS," reflecting the Hebrew Lo-Ammi</note>, for you are not my people, and I will not be your God."

**A**nd the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea, which is without measure and cannot be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it shall be said to them, "Children of the living God." And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and they shall come up from the land, for great is the day of Jezreel. Say to your brothers, "My people," and to your sister, "She who has obtained mercy."

**J**udge your mother, judge her! For she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her take away her harlotries from her face and her adulteries from between her breasts, lest I strip her naked and set her as on the day of her birth, and make her like a wilderness, and set her like a parched land, and kill her with thirst. And I will not have mercy on her children, for they are children of harlotries. For their mother has committed harlotry; she who conceived them is put to shame. For she said: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."

**T**herefore, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will wall her in with a stone wall, and she shall not find her paths. And she shall follow her lovers and shall not overtake them; and she shall seek them and shall not find them. And she shall say: "I will go and return to my first husband, because it was better for me then than now." And she did not know that I gave her grain, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they used for Baal <term>Baal: a Canaanite fertility god often worshipped by Israelites in place of the Lord</term>. Therefore, I will turn and take my grain in its time, and my wine in its season, and I will set free my wool and my flax which covered her shame. And now I will reveal her folly in the eyes of her lovers, and no man shall rescue her from my hand. And I will cause all her joy to cease, her solemnities, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her festal times. And I will ruin her vineyard and her fig tree, of which she said: "These are my wages which my lovers have given me." And I will make them a forest, and the beast of the field shall eat them. And I will visit upon her the days of the Baals, to whom she burned incense, and she adorned herself with her earrings and her necklace, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, says the Lord. Therefore, behold, I will allure her and lead her into the wilderness, and I will speak to her heart. And I will give her vinedressers from that same place, and the Valley of Achor <note>meaning "Valley of Trouble"</note> for a door of hope; and she shall sing there as in the days of her youth, and as in the days of her coming up from the land of Egypt.

**A**nd it shall be on that day, says the Lord, she shall call me "My Husband," and she shall no longer call me "My Baal." And I will take away the names of the Baals from her mouth, and she shall no longer remember their name. And I will strike a covenant with them on that day: with the beast of the field, and with the bird of the heaven, and with the creeping thing of the earth. And I will break the bow, and the sword, and war from the land, and I will make them sleep securely.

And the earth shall hear the grain, and the wine, and the oil, and these shall hear Jezreel. And I will sow her for myself in the land, and I will have mercy on her who was without mercy. Because for many days the children of Israel shall sit without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an ephod <term>ephod: a priestly garment used in divination</term>, and without teraphim <term>teraphim: household idols or tools for oracles</term>. **F**or this reason the land shall mourn, and everyone who dwells in it shall languish, with the beast of the field and the bird of the heaven; even the fish of the sea shall be gathered up. In the night I have made your mother silent. My people have been silent because they had no knowledge. According to their multitude, so they have sinned against me; I will change their glory into shame. They shall eat the sins of my people and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity. And it shall be: like people, like priest. And I will visit his ways upon him and render his thoughts to him. And they shall eat and not be satisfied; they have committed harlotry and have not ceased, because they have forsaken the Lord by not keeping His ways. Harlotry and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. My people have inquired of their wood <note>referring to wooden idols</note>, and their staff has announced to them. For the spirit of harlotries has deceived them, and they have committed harlotry away from their God. Upon the tops of the mountains they were sacrificing, and upon the hills they were burning incense, under the oak, and the poplar, and the terebinth tree, because its shade was good. Therefore your daughters shall commit harlotry, and your spouses shall be adulteresses. I will not visit punishment upon your daughters when they commit harlotry, or upon your spouses when they commit adultery, since they themselves were consorting with harlots and sacrificing with the effeminate; and a people that does not understand shall be beaten. If you, Israel, commit harlotry, at least let Judah not offend. And do not enter into Gilgal, and do not go up to Beth-aven <note>literally "House of Iniquity," a derogatory name for Bethel</note>, nor swear "The Lord lives," since Israel has turned aside like a wanton heifer. Now the Lord will feed them like a lamb in a wide place. Ephraim <note>often used to represent the northern kingdom of Israel</note> is a partner of idols; let him be; their banquet is separated. They have committed harlotry with harlotry; their protectors have loved to bring shame. The spirit has bound him in his wings, and they shall be confounded by their sacrifices.

**H**ear this, O priests, and attend, O house of Israel, and listen, O house of the king, for the judgment is for you; for you have been made a snare for the watchtower and a net spread over Tabor. **T**hey will not give their thoughts to return to their God, because the spirit of harlotries is in their midst, and they have not known the Lord. The princes of Judah have become like those who move a boundary marker <note>original: "assumentes terminum," a grave sin in ancient law</note>. Upon them I will pour out my wrath like water. Ephraim suffers calumny, broken by judgment, because he began to go after filth. And I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like rottenness to the house of Judah. For I am like a lioness to Ephraim and like a lion’s cub to the house of Judah. I will seize, and I will go, I will take away, and there is no one to rescue. Going, I will return to my place until you fail and seek my face.

**I**n their tribulation they shall rise early to me. "Come and let us return to the Lord, because He has seized us and He will heal us; He has struck us and He will heal us. For I desired mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than holocausts." But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they have acted treacherously. In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there are the harlotries of Ephraim; Israel is contaminated. # THE WORD OF THE LORD WHICH WAS MADE TO JOEL

son of Pethuel. Hear this, you old men, and receive it with your ears, all you inhabitants of the land. Has such a thing happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers? Tell your children about this, and let your children tell their children, and their children to another generation. That which the caterpillar left, the locust has eaten; and that which the locust left, the beetle has eaten; and that which the beetle left, the blight has eaten. Awake, you drunkards, and weep; and howl, all you who drink wine in sweetness, for it has perished from your mouth. For a nation has ascended over my land, strong and innumerable: its teeth are like the teeth of lions, and its molars like those of a lion’s whelp. It has laid my vineyard waste and stripped the bark from my fig tree. It has stripped it bare and cast it away; its branches are made white. Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth. The sacrifice and libation have perished from the house of the Lord; the priests, the ministers of the Lord, have mourned. The region is occupied: the ground has mourned, for the wheat is devastated. The wine is confounded: the oil has languished. The husbandmen are confounded; the vine-dressers have howled over the wheat and the barley, because the harvest of the field has perished. The vineyard is confounded, and the fig tree has languished; the pomegranate and the palm, and the apple, and all the trees of the field have withered, because joy is confounded away from the sons of men. Gird yourselves and lament, you priests; howl, you ministers of the altar; enter, lie in sackcloth, you ministers of my God: for sacrifice and libation have perished from the house of your God.

Sanctify a fast, call an assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of the Lord your God, and cry out to the Lord: Alas, alas, alas! <note>original: "Aaaa aa a," a phonetic rendering of an outcry of grief</note> for the day of the Lord is near, and it shall come as a waste from the Almighty. Have not the provisions perished before your eyes? Joy and exultation from the house of our God? The beasts have rotted in their dung; the barns are demolished. The storehouses are destroyed because the wheat is confounded. Why do the animals groan? Why have the herds of cattle lowed? Because there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep have perished. To you, O Lord, I will cry out: for fire has eaten the beautiful things of the desert, and a flame has burned all the trees of the region. But even the beasts of the field, like a parched land, look up to you: because the fountains of waters are dried up, and fire has devoured the beautiful things of the desert. Blow the trumpet in Zion, howl on my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land be troubled, for the day of the Lord is coming, for it is near. A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and whirlwind. Like the dawn spread upon the mountains: a people many and strong: the like of it has not been from the beginning, and after it there shall not be even to the years of generation and generation. Before its face is a devouring fire, and after it a burning flame. The land is like a garden of pleasure before it, and after it a desert solitude: and there is no one who may escape it. Like the appearance of

horses, and like horsemen, so shall they run. Like the sound of four-horse chariots they shall leap upon the tops of the mountains, like the noise of a flame of fire devouring the stubble, like a strong people prepared for battle. From its face the peoples shall be tormented; all faces shall be drawn into a pot <note>original: "in ollam," a Vulgate idiom meaning to grow pale or turn dark with fear</note>. Like strong men they shall run, and like warriors they shall ascend the wall. Men shall walk in their ways, and they shall not turn aside from their paths. And the Lord has given his voice before the face of his army, for his camps are very many: for they are strong and do his word. For the day of the Lord is great and very terrible: and who can endure it?

Now therefore, says the Lord, turn to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning. And rend your hearts and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and of much mercy, and ready to relent over the evil. Who knows if he will turn and forgive, and leave a blessing behind him? A sacrifice and a libation to the Lord our God. Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call an assembly, gather the people, sanctify the church, unite the elders, gather the little ones and those sucking at the breasts. Let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride from her bridal bed. Between the porch and the altar let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep and say: "Spare, O Lord, spare your people, and do not give your inheritance to reproach, that the nations should rule over them." Why do they say among the peoples: "Where is their God?" The Lord has been zealous for his land and has spared his people. And the Lord answered and said to his people: "Behold, I will send you wheat, and wine, and oil, and you shall be filled with them: and I will no longer give you as a reproach to the nations. And I will remove far from you the one who is from the north, and I will expel him into a land impassable and desert: his face toward the eastern sea, and his furthest part toward the last sea. And his stench shall ascend, and his rot shall ascend, because he has acted proudly." Fear not, O land; exult and be glad, for the Lord has magnified his works. Fear not, animals of the region, for the beautiful things of the desert have germinated, for the tree has brought forth its fruit; the fig tree and the vine have given their strength.

And I will restore to you the years which the locust, the beetle, the blight, and the caterpillar have eaten—my great strength which I sent among you. And it shall be after these things: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy. Your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. Moreover, upon my servants and upon my handmaids in those days I will pour out my spirit. And I will give portents in heaven and on earth: blood and fire, and the vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and horrible day of the Lord comes. And it shall be: everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be salvation, as the Lord has said, and in the residues whom the Lord shall call. For behold, in those days and in that time when I shall turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem: I will gather all nations and lead them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and I will plead with them there over my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they have dispersed among the nations: and they have divided my land. And they have cast lots over my people. And they have placed a boy in a brothel and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink. But what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the borders of the Palestinians? Will you render vengeance to me? For you have taken my silver and my gold, and you have brought my desirable and most beautiful things into your temples. And Judea shall be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. And I will cleanse their blood, which I had not cleansed: and the Lord shall dwell in Zion.

The book of Joel ends.

<meta>This page transitions from the general introduction to the Minor Prophets into the specific introduction and opening chapters of the Book of Amos. It maintains the sequence of the "Twelve Prophets" found in the Latin Vulgate tradition.</meta>

Amos, a shepherd and a rustic man who cleared away briars, cannot be explained in just a few words. For what is said expresses these things: namely, the three crimes of Damascus, the fourth of Tyre, of Edom, of the children of Ammon, and of Moab; and included in this are Judah and Israel. <note>original: "tria scelera... quarte," referring to the prophetic formula "For three transgressions... and for four," signifying a full measure of sin that has finally exhausted God's patience.</note> Here he speaks to the "fat cows" who were on the mountain of Samaria, and he testifies to the ruin of both the great and the small houses. He himself beholds the maker of the locusts, and the Lord standing upon a plastered wall, and the vision of the summer fruit, and finally the punishments of sinners, and a famine—not of bread nor a thirst for water, but for hearing the word of God. O Israel, at that time when the religion of God was zealously observed with care, he read the law of Moses with a pious heart and received it with divine grace. Here, historically, he sat after the fruit-gathering <note>original: "post pomonem," likely referring to his seasonal work as a dresser of sycamore figs</note> to show that the priestly office was being conducted most wickedly. O blessed thing, that the word is established to be prayed for in the temple of God, which also the prophet Zechariah mentions. Before the kings trembled, the prophet Amos sang in those times: specifically, in the times of King Uzziah and Jeroboam, the son of Joash, king of Israel; he shows that these matters are understood through reading, and he denounces future events for these reasons and for memory. For it seems most wicked when he says: "For three... and for four, I will not convert him," <note>original: "non conuertam eum," meaning "I will not turn back [the punishment]."</note> which signified that God could give indulgence to the sinner then; but because they admitted those same sins a fourth time, he announces that he will give neither repentance nor indulgence. For instead of three, which signifies a likeness where one might be sent kneeling for sin, the fourth signifies that their life is unrecallable to salvation; they wish to be shown as warned out of their sins.

For behold, I will command and I will shake the house of Israel among all nations, just as wheat is shaken in a sieve, and not a small stone shall fall upon the ground. In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David which has fallen, and I will rebuild the openings of its walls, and I will restore what had fallen; and I will rebuild it as in the days of old, so that they may possess the remnants of Edom and all the nations, because my name has been invoked upon them," says the Lord who does these things. "Behold, the days are coming," says the Lord, "and the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that sows the seed; and the mountains shall drop sweetness, and all the hills shall be cultivated. And I will turn the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall build the deserted cities and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they shall make gardens and eat their fruits. And I will plant them upon their own soil, and I will not uproot them anymore from their land which I have given them," says the Lord your God.

**OBADIAH, WHICH IS INTERPRETED AS THE SERVANT OF THE LORD**
<note>This introduction provides traditional interpretations of the prophet's name and his relationship to the historical conflict between Israel and Edom.</note>
...prophecy against Edom. His name is interpreted as "Servant of the Lord," and he writes against the bloodthirsty. He frequently describes the constant rivalry with Jacob. Jacob is shown to have the inheritance. This man [Edom], when he had not received his brother's portion, was called Edom in the Hebrew language: nevertheless, he is "bloody." This man, when he had not received his brother's portion, burned with grave hatred against them as strangers. For this reason, all who hate the people of Israel—that is, the sons of the patriarch Jacob—with a true hatred in their hearts are called Edom. And because the people of Israel were recalled to Jerusalem from the captivity of the Chaldeans by the decree of God, and were gravely afflicted and oppressed by other kings, therefore this kingdom, which followed the aforementioned people in the manner of Esau, is named by the announcement of the prophet Obadiah; because he received his right in the aforementioned land from the indignation of God. Concerning this kingdom, it was once dictated by David in Psalm 136: "Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem." Since the rest of the reading is understood, the prophet Obadiah here prophesies the future judgment of the Jews because of their crimes, and the return of the kingdom. The Hebrews say that this man is he who, under Ahab the king of Samaria, hid a hundred prophets in caves so they would not bow the knee to Baal, and who was the steward over the seven thousand whom Elijah did not know. His sepulcher is held in veneration even today in Sebastia—which was once called Samaria—along with the prophets Elisha and John the Baptist. Herod, the son of Antipater, called this place Augusta in the Greek name in honor of Augustus Caesar. He, because he received the prophets, received a prophet's reward, and led the army... [commentary continues identifying the prophet's merit]. Just as Stephen is named for the "crown" of his passion, so this man is called the "Servant of the Lord," for Obadiah translates as "Servant of the Lord."

**JONAH THE MOST BEAUTIFUL DOVE**
By his shipwreck, he prefigures the Passion of the Lord; he calls the world to repentance and, under the name of Nineveh, announces salvation to the nations. The Hebrew sound of "Jonah" confirms he is the son of the widow of Zarephath, whom Elijah the prophet raised from the dead; his mother afterwards said to him: "Now I know that you are a man of God, and the word of God in your mouth is true." And for this reason, the boy himself is like the oracle of Amittai <note>transcribed as "Amachi"</note>. For "Amittai" in our language sounds like "truth," because Elijah spoke the truth; he who was raised is called the "son of truth." Therefore, from truth, the dove is born, for "Jonah" sounds like "dove." According to our interpretation, however, Jonah warns of rest, for while he was bringing repentance to them, they persisted in malice. And specifically, you recognize Jonah as our Lord, who, having left the Lord with his people in Samaria, fascinated by idols, was the whole of prophecy; the history of the four books indicates this. When prophecy, illuminating the path of sinners toward Nineveh, saw they had obtained mercy, he did not want to go to announce the city's destruction, lest he be seen as preaching falsely. For just as it is said to Abraham regarding the impiety of the Sodomites, "the cry of the Sodomites and Gomorrahs has come up to me," so it is said of Nineveh, because the cry of its malice ascended to him. And because the sentence of God regarding Sodom was carried out, but regarding Nineveh it was revoked, so Jonah did not want to be the one to bring the sentence against Nineveh, being ignorant of the divine dispensation which prefers the salvation of men who turn back to Him over their destruction. This happened to him because Israel alone ignored that the child of the woman was about to die. And therefore Jonah thought he could flee from the sight of the Lord. He suffered a human error, as David says: "Where shall I go from your spirit, and where shall I flee from your face?"

And Jonah went out of the city and sat toward the east of the city; and he made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shadow, until he might see what would happen to the city. And the Lord God prepared an ivy <note>original: "ederam," often translated as a gourd or vine</note>, and it grew up over the head of Jonah to be a shadow over his head and to protect him; for he had labored. And Jonah was glad of the ivy with great joy. And God prepared a worm at the rising of the dawn the next day, and it struck the ivy and it withered. And when the sun had risen, the Lord commanded a hot and burning wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, and he was parched with heat. And he requested for his soul that he might die, and said: "It is better for me to die than to live." And the Lord said to Jonah: "Do you think you are right to be angry over the ivy?" And he said: "I am right to be angry, even unto death." And the Lord said: "You grieve over the ivy, for which you did not labor, nor did you make it grow; it was born in one night and perished in one night. And should I not spare Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who know not what is between their right hand and their left, and many mute beasts?" The Book of Jonah ends.

**MICAH OF MORESHETH**
A co-heir of Christ, he announces devastation to the daughter of Zion and sets a siege against her, because they have struck the cheek of the judge of Israel. The reading itself demonstrates that in the times of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings in Judah, Micah was filled with the Holy Spirit for this prophecy. But it is also said that of the stated number of kings, Jotham and Hezekiah pleased God by their religion, as the history of the Book of Kings says in a partial account. Ahaz, however, having abandoned the Lord, worshipped the idols of Samaria and Syria, and offered his sons to be consumed in the fire. He had confounded Israel. On the day of his death, both the king of Israel and of Judah, who with their idols and superstition had abandoned the Lord, found their dissipation to be a common ruin. He follows with words against the people of Israel for their prevarication and against its princes, who had pushed the same people with fallacious persuasion to worship idols. He announces the coming captivity and misery.

O my people, what have I done to you, or in what have I been troublesome to you? Answer me. For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and delivered you out of the house of slaves; and I sent before your face Moses, and Aaron, and Miriam. O my people, remember, I pray you, what Balak king of Moab purposed, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him, from Shittim <note>original: "setthin"</note> even to Gilgal, that you might know the justices of the Lord. What shall I offer to the Lord that is worthy? Shall I bow my knees before the high God? Shall I offer him holocausts, and calves of a year old? Can the Lord be appeased with thousands of rams, or with many thousands of fat he-goats? Shall I give my firstborn for my crime, the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul? I will show you, O man, what is good, and what the Lord requires of you: Verily, to do judgment, and to love mercy, and to walk solicitous <note>original: "sollicitum"; meaning humble or carefully attentive</note> with your God. The voice of the Lord cries to the city, and salvation shall be to those who fear your name. Hear, O tribe, and who shall approve it?

<margin>chapter 7</margin>
As yet there is a fire in the house of the wicked, and the treasures of iniquity, and a deceitful measure full of wrath. Shall I justify the wicked balance, and the deceitful weights of the bag? By which her rich men were filled with iniquity, and the inhabitants thereof spoke lies, and their tongue was deceitful in their mouth. And I therefore began to strike you with destruction for your sins. You shall eat and not be filled, and your humiliation shall be in the midst of you; and you shall take hold, and shall not save; and those whom you shall save, I will give to the sword. You shall sow, and not reap; you shall tread the olives, and not be anointed with the oil; and the new wine, and not drink wine. And you have kept the precepts of Omri <note>original: "amri"; a king of Israel noted for wickedness</note>, and all the works of the house of Ahab; and you have walked in their wills, that I should make you a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof a hissing, and you shall bear the reproach of my people. Woe is me, for I have become as one who gathers the grapes of the vintage in autumn. There is no cluster to eat; my soul desired the first-ripe figs. The holy man has perished from the earth, and there is none upright among men; they all lie in wait for blood, every man hunts his brother to death. The evil of their hands they call good. The prince requires, and the judge is for giving a reward; the great man has spoken the desire of his soul, and they have troubled it. He that is best among them is as a brier; and he that is upright, as a thorn of the hedge. The day of your inspection, your visitation comes; now shall be their ruin. Believe not a friend, and trust not in a leader; from her that sleeps in your bosom, keep the doors of your mouth. For the son dishonors the father, and the daughter rises up against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; and a man's enemies are they of his own household. But I will look to the Lord, I will wait for God my savior; my God will hear me. Rejoice not, my enemy, over me, because I am fallen; I shall arise, when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light. I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he judge my cause and execute judgment for me. He will bring me forth into the light, I shall see his justice. And my enemy shall behold, and she shall be covered with confusion, who says to me: "Where is the Lord your God?" My eyes shall behold her; now shall she be trodden under foot as the mud of the streets. The day is coming that your walls may be built; in that day the law shall be far removed. In that day they shall come even to you from Assyria even to the fortified cities; and from the fortified cities even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain. And the land shall be made desolate because of the inhabitants thereof, and for the fruit of their thoughts. Feed your people with your rod, the flock of your inheritance, dwelling alone in the forest in the midst of Carmel; they shall feed in Bashan and Gilead, according to the days of old. According to the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders. The nations shall see, and shall be confounded at all their strength; they shall put their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf. They shall lick the dust like serpents, like the creeping things of the earth they shall be troubled in their houses. They shall dread the Lord our God, and shall fear you. Who is a God like you, who takes away iniquity, and passes over the sin of the remnant of your inheritance? He will send forth his fury no more, because he delights in mercy. He will turn again and have mercy on us; he will put away our iniquities, and he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea. You will perform the truth to Jacob, the mercy to Abraham, which you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.

# NAHUM, THE COMFORTER OF THE WORLD, REBUKES
the city of blood. And after its destruction, he speaks: "Behold upon the feet of him that brings good tidings, of him that announces peace." The prophet Nahum is interpreted as "helper" or "comforter" <note>original: "ad adiuuandum interpreatur"; the name Nahum in Hebrew relates to consolation</note>, for he had already seen Israel led captive into his own region. Hebrew tradition confirms this. Indeed, below the beginning of this reading, he shows the device of the King of the Assyrians. But while he dwelt in Nineveh, near the aroused city, preaching the divine will—not as it was announced according to the mercy shown to penitents—but because when repentance ceased, the mercy of God turned away because they had again made themselves to be oppressed by iniquity. For which cause, he spoke concerning its destruction, or rather, the command of the divine announcer. O secular and [unclear] Lord! Thus, ten tribes had been led into captivity by the Assyrians under Hezekiah, king of Judah. Under him also, in the consolation of the people who had been moved to the island, he saw a vision. For it was no small consolation both to those who served the Assyrians and to the rest who were under Hezekiah of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, who were besieged by the enemy; they heard the miserable Assyrians [saying] that they were to be captured by the Chaldeans. Thus it will be shown in the following parts of this book. It should be known, however, that Nineveh, according to the Hebrew language, sounds like "beautiful." This world is called "beautiful" <note>original: "speciosum"</note>. Whence also among the Greeks, the name *cosmos* <note>original: "κόσμος"</note> took its name from "ornament." And all things now said to this world are figuratively preached to the world. For which cause also the name of the Assyrians, which is interpreted as "directing the spirit," designates the adversary of Christ, the Antichrist <note>original: "anti xp̄m"</note>. For all things, both concerning him and his members, the prophetic song predicted, and this end shall not be lifted from the rest. At the same time, it should be noted here that this very assumption, proposed in all things, was the vision of the prophecy. For he does not speak in vain like a worldly person or a singer in false tranquility, but they understand that the book of prophets is of vision. All the things he speaks, and the weight of them all, he makes a vision for his people, and the consummation of truth; but he is stirred up in the consolation of the prophets according to the acts of the city, so that whoever in the world sees that the figure and image pass away may despise them, and prepare themselves for the judgment of God, where the Lord shall be the avenger against the guilty Assyrians.

The lion took enough for his cubs and killed for his lionesses. He filled his caves with prey, and his den with rapine.

The gates of your land shall be set wide open to your enemies; fire shall devour your bars. Draw water for the siege; build up your bulwarks. The sun is risen and they have flown away, and their place is not known where they have been. Have your shepherds slumbered, O king of Assyria? Your princes shall be buried. Your people have hidden in the mountains, and there is no one to gather them. Your destruction is not hidden; your wound is very grievous. All who have heard the report of you have clapped their hands over you; for upon whom has not your malice passed continually? The Book of Nahum ends.

### HABAKKUK, THE STRONGEST WRESTLER

His brightness shall be as the light; horns are in his hands; there his strength was hidden." The prophet Habakkuk is called "Embrace" <note>original: "amplexatio"</note>, either because he is loved by the Lord, or because he enters into a struggle with God; the name is said to mean "embracing wrestler." For no one has dared to provoke the Lord to a discussion of justice with such a bold voice, asking why in human affairs and in this world iniquity should turn as in hell? In the beginning of his book, he pronounces the advent of the passion of the Lord Savior regarding the extirpation of the devil against his limb [Antichrist]. What is this, if not either the two Testaments, or in the midst of two thieves, or the mercy of Moses and Elijah talking with him on the mountain? When the years draw near, he is known; in the coming of the times, he will be shown. But in the excess of my soul, I will be mindful of mercy. However, this prophet properly places the name of the Savior here, saying: "But I will exult in the Lord my God; I will rejoice in God my Jesus" <note>original: "gaudebā in deo ih̄u meo"; the Latin text uses "Jesus" where modern translations often say "Savior" or "Salvation"</note>, which is to us a friend and sweet; to announce and to preach.

How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and you will not hear? <note>original: "Usquequo domine clamabo"</note> Shall I cry out to you suffering violence, and you will not save? Why have you shown me iniquity and toil, to see plunder and injustice against me? And judgment has been made, and opposition is more powerful. Because of this, the law is torn apart, and judgment does not reach its end. For the wicked prevails against the just; therefore, perverse judgment goes forth. Behold among the nations, and see: admire, and be astonished! For a work is done in your days which no one will believe when it is told. For behold, I will raise up the Chaldeans <note>The Babylonians, known for their fierce military expansion.</note>, a bitter and swift nation, walking across the breadth of the earth to possess tabernacles not their own. It is horrible and terrible; from itself its judgment and its burden shall go forth. Its horses are lighter than leopards and swifter than evening wolves; its horsemen shall spread out. For its horsemen shall come from afar; they shall fly like an eagle hastening to eat. All shall come for the prey; their faces are like a burning wind. And he shall gather captives like sand, and he shall triumph over kings, and tyrants shall be his laughingstock. He shall laugh at every fortress, and shall cast up a mound and take it. Then his spirit shall be changed, and he shall pass through and fall: this is his strength, belonging to his god. Have you not been from the beginning, O Lord my God, my Holy One, and we shall not die? O Lord, you have set him for judgment, and established him as strong to chastise. Your eyes are pure, that you may not see evil, and you cannot look upon iniquity. Why do you not look upon those who act iniquitously? And why are you silent while the wicked devours one more just than himself? And you will make men like the fish of the sea, and like creeping things having no ruler. He lifted up everything with a hook; he drew them out in his dragnet and gathered them into his net. Over this, he will rejoice and exult; therefore he will offer victims to his dragnet and sacrifice to his net, because through them his portion is made fat, and his food is choice. Because of this, therefore, he spreads his dragnet and will not spare to slay the nations always.

**I** will stand upon my watch and fix my step upon the fortress, and I will contemplate to see what may be said to me, and what I may answer to him who reproves me. And the Lord answered me and said: Write the vision and explain it upon tablets, so that he who reads it may run. For the vision is yet far off, and it shall appear at the end and shall not lie. If it makes a delay, wait for it; because it shall surely come, and it shall not tarry. Behold, he who is unbelieving, his soul shall not be right in himself; but the just shall live in his faith. And as wine deceives the one who drinks, so shall the proud man be, and he shall not be enriched; he who has enlarged his soul like hell, and is like death, and is not satisfied. And he shall gather to himself all nations, and shall heap together to himself all peoples. Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a dark speech concerning him? And they shall say: Woe to him who multiplies things that are not his own! How long? And he heaps up against himself thick clay. Shall they not suddenly rise up that shall bite you, and they shall be stirred up that shall tear you, and you shall be a spoil to them? Because you have despoiled many nations, all who are left of the people shall despoil you, because of the blood of man and the iniquity of the land, of the city, and of all who dwell therein. Woe to him who gathers evil greed for his house, that his nest may be on high, and thinks he may be delivered from the hand of evil. You have devised confusion for your house; you have cut off many peoples, and your soul has sinned. For the stone shall cry out from the wall, and the timber that is between the joints of the buildings shall answer. Woe to him who builds a city in blood, and prepares a town in iniquity. Are these things not from the Lord of hosts? For the peoples shall labor in much fire, and the nations in vain, and they shall fail. For the earth shall be filled, that they may know the glory of the Lord, like waters covering the sea. Woe to him who gives drink to his friend, mixing in his gall, and making him drunk so that he may look upon his nakedness. You are filled with ignominy instead of glory; drink you also and fall asleep; the cup of the right hand of the Lord shall encompass you, and shameful vomiting shall be upon your glory. For the iniquity of Lebanon shall cover you, and the waste of animals shall terrify them, because of the blood of men and the iniquity of the land and the city, and of all who dwell therein. What profit is the graven image, that its maker has carved it? A molten thing and a false image, because its maker has trusted in the fiction, to make dumb idols? Woe to him who says to the wood: Awake; and to the silent stone: Arise! Shall it be able to teach? Behold, it is covered with gold and silver, and there is no spirit in its bowels. But the Lord is in his holy temple; let all the earth be silent before his face.

**O** Lord, I have heard your report and was afraid. O Lord, revive your work in the midst of the years. In a roar you will trample the earth; in fury you will astonish the nations. You went forth for the salvation of your people, for salvation with your Christ <note>original: "cum christo tuo"; meaning 'with your anointed one'</note>.
