### Right Column

**ZEPHANIAH, THE WATCHMAN OF THE INHABITANTS.**
He is the knower of the Word, and by hearing, a cry from the Fish Gate, and a wailing from the second part, and a crashing from the hills; he also brings wailing to the inhabitants of the Mortar, because all the people of Canaan are silent. All who were wrapped in silver have perished. The Hebrews hand down traditions of this kind: that the prophet was a secret counselor <note>original: "aricanum" likely for "arcanum"</note>; for this reason he was seen to have been among the prophets. Whence also Amos, one of the twelve prophets who is called a prophet in the bone, not the son of a prophet, but a herdsman of goats plucking sycamores, is said to have no name for his father. This may also be the prophet Zephaniah <note>Sophonias</note> who described his generation—not only his prophetic one—but the glory of his ancestors, word by word in order. But these things, as we said above for the meantime, are how he comes from the fathers: Amasias, Azarias, Hezekiah. And they say such a one was joined from the Arameans, embraced by gold. For Zephaniah <note>Sophonias</note> means "high watchtower" or "the secret of the Lord," while Josiah means "salvation." Whether he is interpreted as "watchtower" or "the hidden thing of the Lord," both suit prophecy. For Ezekiel says to the son of man that he has placed him as a watchman for the Lord of Israel. And he is the prophet who was established on the watchtower and in high places, and knew the mysteries of the daughters of men; and in all of them there was humility. He had a grandfather, Gedaliah, which is interpreted as "the greatness of the Lord," and a father, Amasias, which is "truth itself in the word of the Lord," and a great-grandfather Hezekiah, which sounds like "strength in the Lord." Of him, therefore, it is said more truly: the word of the Lord was born. And from the word of God was born the greatness of the Lord, and from the greatness of the Lord was born humility; nor did truth come to the prophet to say what he was not worthy to be called. And that in the Psalms: "Every man is a liar," but the word of God is true, and the truth of God remains forever. Also, it is found that Zephaniah prophesied in the times of Josiah, king of Judah; regarding the king's fathers, see how he approved. Regarding these things which are wept over, the Books of Kings and Chronicles <note>original: "paliprambipomeron" for "paralipomenon"</note> demonstrate them. In summary, the idols which Amon and his grandfather Manasseh had placed in the temple of God were cast down together, as is demonstrated. For in the time when Amon and Moses acted, they caused the grandfather to make the people err regarding the destruction and the deceits of the gods; even until the righteous day, that is, the Passover, the most invincible in the memory of the king’s times, those things which were to come were shown to the nation. For by the reading of Josiah we are figured for an inheritance: the salvation of the people of Israel and the restoration of the city of Jerusalem in the time of tribulations are announced by the text of the lesson.

You looked for much, and behold, it became little; and you brought it into the house, and I blew it away. For what cause, says the Lord of hosts? Because my house is a desert, and you hasten every man to his own house. Therefore, the heavens above you are stayed from giving dew, and the earth is stayed from giving her fruit. And I have called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the wine, and upon the oil, and upon whatever the ground brings forth, and upon men, and upon cattle, and upon all the labor of the hands."

And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn to me, says the Lord of hosts, and I will turn to you, says the Lord of hosts. Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn from your evil ways and from your wicked thoughts. But they did not hear nor attend to me, says the Lord. Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, shall they live forever? But my words and my laws, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? And they returned and said: As the Lord of hosts thought to do to us, according to our ways and according to our inventions, so he has done to us. On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is called Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying: I saw by night, and behold a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in the bottom; and behind him were red, white, and black horses. And I said: What are these, my lord? And the angel who spoke in me said to me: I will show you what these are. And the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said: These are those whom the Lord has sent to walk through the earth. And they answered the angel of the Lord who stood among the myrtle trees, and said: We have walked through the earth, and behold, all the earth is inhabited and is at rest. ### And it happened in the fourth year of King Darius, that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev. <note>original: "casleu"; the ninth month of the Hebrew calendar, roughly November-December.</note> And they sent to the house of God Sharezer and Regem-melech, and the men who were with them, to entreat the face of the Lord, so that they might speak to the priests of the house of the Lord of hosts, and to the prophets, saying: "Should I weep in the fifth month, or must I sanctify myself, as I have done now for many years?"

### The word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying: Speak to all the people of the land, and to the priests, saying: "When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months through these seventy years, did you truly fast for me? And when you ate and drank, did you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves? ### And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Judge true judgment, and show mercy and compassion, each one to his brother. ## MALACHI INTERPRETED IN LATIN

The angel of the Lord also called this man. For whatever he spoke, he believed it to be a command as if from a counselor. Whence one translator changed the name, saying: "The burden of the word of the Lord over Israel by the hand of his angel." <note>The name Malachi literally means "My Messenger" or "My Angel."</note> He prophesied as the last in Jerusalem, when Haggai and Zechariah also prophesied at the end of all things, regarding the rejection of Israel and the calling of the nations. For it is also in the sections of this book: "Because the Lord loved Israel." From the rising of the sun even to its setting, my name is great among the nations, and in every place there is sacrifice. He will make this offering for the people of Israel. Indeed, he called the victims of all the people to offer to him, because he gave his law to rule the people for this reason: so that they might remember God through the offering of sacrifice. Whence in this place he rebukes the priests of God if they wish to accept easy gifts which they might despise. He further points out that the people and priests make their way defiled over Israel, and being stained with crimes and iniquities, they dare to offer to God. But through Malachi the prophet, he rebukes you, the people of Israel. I have loved you, says the Lord. And you said: "In what way have you loved us?" Was not Esau Jacob's brother, says the Lord? Yet I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated. And further: "If I am a father, where is my honor? If I am a master, where is my fear?" says the Lord. Then the merit of Jacob is made manifest, since he was hated by his brother Jacob <note>The text likely meant Esau here, reflecting the biblical rivalry.</note> who sought to kill him. To whom the King says: "Esau I have hated." In just works, he remembers whichever of the nations he wishes, just as Esau made his purpose manifest by selling his birthright; and the just Jacob is affirmed by this voice. Jacob fled and stayed in the tent. For they embrace the calling of Jacob... they were commanded not to worship alien gods.

Who is there among you who would shut the doors and kindle my altar for nothing? I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord of hosts, and I will not receive a gift from your hand. For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, my name is great among the nations; and in every place a clean offering is sacrificed and offered to my name, for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts. But you have polluted it, in that you say: "The table of the Lord is contaminated, and that which is placed upon it is contemptible," along with the fire that devours it. And you said: "Behold, what a labor!" and you have puffed at it, says the Lord of hosts. And you brought in that which was taken by violence, and the lame, and the sick, and you brought in an offering. Shall I receive it from your hand? says the Lord. Cursed is the deceitful man who has in his flock a male, and making a vow, sacrifices a weak thing to the Lord. For I am a great King, says the Lord of hosts, and my name is terrible among the nations. **And** now, O priests, this commandment is for you. If you will not hear, and if you will not lay it to heart to give glory to my name, says the Lord of hosts, I will send poverty upon you and I will curse your blessings; and I will curse them, because you have not laid it to heart. Behold, I will cast the arm against you, and I will scatter upon your face the dung of your solemnities, and it shall take you away with it. And you shall know that I sent this commandment to you, that my covenant might be with Levi, says the Lord of hosts. My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave him fear, and he feared me; he was humbled before my name. The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips; he walked with me in peace and equity, and turned many away from iniquity. For the lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts. But you have departed from the way and have caused many to stumble in the law. You have made void the covenant of Levi, says the Lord of hosts. Therefore I also have made you contemptible and base before all people, just as you have not kept my ways and have shown partiality in the law. Is there not one father for us all? Has not one God created us? Why then does each one of us despise his brother, violating the covenant of our fathers? Judah has transgressed, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has contaminated the holiness of the Lord, which he loved, and has married the daughter of a foreign god. The Lord will destroy the man who does this, both the master and the scholar from the tabernacles of Jacob, and him who offers a gift to the Lord of hosts.

<margin><note>Abbr: 100</note></margin>

And this again you have done: you covered the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping and moaning, so that I no longer look toward the sacrifice, nor receive anything pleasing from your hand. And you said: "For what reason?" Because the Lord has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have despised; yet she was your companion and the wife of your covenant. Did not one make her, and the residue of the spirit is his? And what does the one seek, except the seed of God? Guard then your spirit, and do not despise the wife of your youth. When you hate her, dismiss her, says the Lord God of Israel. But iniquity shall cover his garment, says the Lord of hosts. Guard your spirit, and do not despise. You have made the Lord weary with your words. And you said: "In what way have we made him weary?" In that you say: "Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the Lord, and such please him." Or certainly: "Where is the God of judgment?"
**Behold**, I send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And presently the Lord whom you seek, and the messenger of the testament <note>original: "angelus testamenti"; the 'messenger of the covenant'.</note> whom you desire, shall come to his temple. Behold, he comes, says the Lord of hosts. And who can think of the day of his coming, and who shall stand to see him? For he is like a refining fire, and like fullers' herb <note>original: "herba fullonum"; a plant used for cleaning and whitening cloth.</note>. And he shall sit refining and cleansing silver; and he shall purify the sons of Levi and strain them like gold and like silver; and they shall be offering sacrifices to the Lord in justice. And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem shall please the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in ancient years. And I will come to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, and adulterers, and perjurers, and those who cheat the hired man of his wages, and the widows, and the strangers, and the orphans, and those who oppress the poor and have not feared me, says the Lord of hosts. For I am the Lord, and I do not change; and you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed. For from the days of your fathers, you have departed from my ordinances and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts. And you said: "In what way shall we return?" Shall a man afflict God? for you afflict me. And you said: "In what way do we afflict you?" In tithes and in first-fruits. And in poverty you are cursed, and you afflict me as a whole nation. Bring all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house; and test me in this, says the Lord, if I do not open for you the floodgates of heaven and pour out a blessing for you even unto abundance. And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not corrupt the fruit of your land; nor shall the vine in the field be barren, says the Lord of hosts. And all nations shall call you blessed, for you shall be a desirable land, says the Lord of hosts. Your words have grown strong against me, says the Lord. And you said: "What have we spoken against you?" You said: "It is vain to serve God. And what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances, and that we walked mournfully before the Lord of hosts?" Therefore now we call the arrogant blessed; for they who work impiety are built up, and they have tempted God and are set free. Then those who feared the Lord spoke, each one with his neighbor; and the Lord attended and heard. And a book of remembrance was written before him for those who fear the Lord and think upon his name. And they shall be mine, says the Lord of hosts, in the day that I make my special possession; and I will spare them as a man spares his own son who serves him. And you shall return, and you shall see what is the difference between the just and the impious, and between him who serves God and him who serves him not. **For behold**, the day comes, burning like a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work impiety, shall be stubble. And the day that is coming shall set them on fire, says the Lord of hosts, and it shall leave them neither root nor sprout. But to you who fear my name, the sun of justice shall arise, and health in its wings. And you shall go forth and leap like calves from the herd. And you shall tread down the impious when they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I act, says the Lord of hosts. Remember the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded him in Horeb for all Israel, the precepts and judgments. Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and terrible day of the Lord. And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with anathema. Thus ends Malachi.

<meta>This page transitions from the prophetic books of the Old Testament to the Book of Job. It begins with St. Jerome’s famous prologue defending his translation of Job from the original Hebrew, followed by the opening chapters of the narrative detailing Job’s trials and the arrival of his three friends.</meta>

# TO GATHER FOR EACH OF THE BOOKS OF HOLY SCRIPTURE
a response to you, I confess, I would hardly wish: those who [criticize] my work with their own reproof. I, who am before all a native <note>Jerome refers to himself as a "native" of the Latin language, defending his translation skills</note>: as if among the Greeks, Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion brought forth a type of translation—either word for word <note>original: "uerbo e uerbo"</note>, or sense for sense <note>original: "sensum de sensu"</note>, or a mixture of both, a tempered middle style. All the volumes of the Old Instrument <note>The Old Testament</note> were distinguished by Origen with obeli <note>A mark (÷) used to indicate text present in the Greek Septuagint but missing in the Hebrew</note> and asterisks <note>A mark (*) used to indicate text present in the Hebrew but missing in the Greek</note>, which were added from Theodotion. These additions, after so many years, were brought in to defend the text. All of these, by means of asterisks—that is, marks placed to show what was missing—were sprinkled throughout; and in my interpretation, nothing of the others has been erased. For it cannot be that from many, one version should remain... <note>The OCR for the middle of this prologue is highly fragmented, but Jerome is arguing for the necessity of returning to the "Hebrew Truth" (Hebraica Veritas) because the Greek versions differed so wildly</note>. Especially in Job, if anyone should look under the asterisks, they would find additions... and from the varied authors... and the apocryphal. Furthermore, I recently published [the version] marked with asterisks and obeli. It is decorated with nearly five hundred or eight hundred verses... and it was gnawed away by time; the foulness of it should be read publicly. These things I speak... it follows... from the Hebrew, Arabic, and Syrian speech. Often words, not the sense, are translated... for it will not sound right. Because of these things, among the Hebrews the book is... which the Greeks call... IN THIS ESTIMATION. Ladies and gentlemen: it is one thing to speak, another to do. Just as a slippery eel or a small lamprey escapes the hands when held tightly, so the more one tries to press [the translator], the more he slips away. I remember that in the common understanding of this volume, many believed it was held first among the Hebrews; not previously redeemed with coins, since I do not know how to prefer doctrine over anyone. This one thing I know: I was able to translate what was before me. For the appropriation of the volume as far as the word "Job" is considered difficult among the Hebrews. Furthermore, regarding the words of Job: "Perish the day on which I was born" and "the night in which it was said a man is conceived," up to the place where it says at the end of the volume: "Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in embers and ashes." <note>Jerome is noting that the middle of the book of Job is written in verse/poetry, while the beginning and end are prose</note> These are written in hexameter lines, using dactyls and spondees... not by the counting of syllables, but by the weight of time... like the poems of Pindar or Alcaeus, or the Psalter, or the Lamentations of Jeremiah. If any should be incredulous... let them look to the Hebrews... and they will find it so. Let them hear how I have labored in this volume, not so that I might reprehend the ancient translation, but so that those things which in it are obscure, or omitted, or corrupted by the fault of copyists, might be corrected. For there were those who learned the Hebrew speech in part... and in Latin... from the tablets of grammarians, rhetoricians, and philosophers. If any Greek wishes to challenge this, let him see that Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion... who concealed many mysteries of the Savior under figures in their interpretation, and yet they are held in example... since I, as a Christian born of Christian parents, carry the banner of the cross on my forehead, whose study it was to restore the omitted, correct the corrupted, and open the pure and faithful language. Let those who want them have their old books written on purple skins with gold and silver letters, or in uncials <note>large, rounded capital letters</note>—burdens of writing rather than accurate copies—while they permit me and my poor friends to have our small sheets, and not so much beautiful codes as corrected ones. To the honor of the work... among the Hebrews... I have labored: let each choose what he wishes, and show himself a studious friend rather than a malevolent judge.

Who said to her: "You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, why should we not receive evil?" In all these things Job did not sin with his lips. <margin>they came to him as friends to console him</margin> Now when Job's three friends heard of all the evil that had befallen him, they came each from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. For they had made an appointment to come together to visit him and comfort him. And when they had lifted up their eyes from afar, they did not know him, and crying out, they wept; and having rent their garments, they sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven. And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.

# AFTER THIS
Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day. And he spoke:

Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night in which it was said: "A man is conceived." Let that day be turned into darkness, and let not God regard it from above, and let it not be enlightened with light. Let darkness and the shadow of death obscure it, let a mist occupy it, and let it be wrapped in bitterness. Let a darksome whirlwind possess that night; let it not be counted in the days of the year, nor numbered in the months. Let that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise. Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to raise up Leviathan <note>A primordial sea monster, representing chaos</note>. Let the stars be darkened with the mist thereof: let it expect light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawning day. Because it did not shut up the doors of the womb that bore me, nor take away evils from my eyes. Why did I not die in the womb? Why did I not perish immediately as I came out of the belly? Why was I received upon the knees? Why was I suckled at the breasts? For now, sleeping, I should be silent, and in my sleep I should rest with kings and counselors of the earth, who build solitudes for themselves. Or with princes who possess gold and fill their houses with silver. Or as a hidden miscarriage I should not have existed, or like those who being conceived have not seen the light. There the impious cease from tumult, and there the weary in strength have rested. And those once bound are together without molestation; they have not heard the voice of the oppressor. The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master. Why is light given to the miserable, and life to those who are in bitterness of soul? Who look for death, and it comes not, as those who dig for a treasure; and they rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave. To a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has surrounded with darkness? Before I eat, I sigh, and like overflowing water, so is my roaring. For the fear which I feared has happened to me, and that which I dreaded has occurred. Have I not dissembled? Have I not been silent? Have I not been quiet? And your indignation has come upon me.

But now the plague has come upon you, and you have fainted; it has touched you, and you are troubled. Where is your fear, and your fortitude, your patience, and the perfection of your ways? Remember, I beseech you: who ever perished being innocent? Or when were the upright destroyed? On the contrary...

<meta>This page continues the Book of Job, skipping from the end of chapter 5 to the latter half of chapter 13. This selection highlights Job’s desperate plea to God and the increasingly harsh rebukes from his friends, Eliphaz and Bildad.</meta>

<margin>Job 13.</margin>
Why do you hide your face, and consider me your enemy? You show your power against a leaf that is carried away by the wind, and you pursue dry stubble. For you write bitter things against me, and you wish to consume me for the sins of my youth. You have put my feet in the <term>stocks<note>original: "nervo," a wooden frame used to restrain the feet of prisoners.</note></term>, and you have watched all my paths, and you have considered the steps of my feet. I am to be consumed like something rotten, and like a garment that is eaten by a moth.

<margin>14.</margin>
Man, born of woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries. Like a flower he comes forth and is crushed; he flees like a shadow and never remains in the same state. And do you think it worthy to open your eyes upon such a one, and to bring him into judgment with you? Who can make a clean thing out of an unclean conception? Are you not the only one who can? The days of man are short; the number of his months is with you. You have set his limits, which cannot be passed. Depart a little from him, so that he may rest, until his desired day comes, like that of a hired hand. A tree has hope: if it is cut down, it grows green again, and its branches sprout. If its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the dust, at the scent of water it will bud and bring forth foliage, as when it was first planted. But when a man dies and is laid bare and consumed, where, I ask, is he? Just as if the waters should recede from the sea, and a river should dry up and become empty, so when a man has fallen asleep, he shall not rise again; until the heavens are worn away, he shall not wake nor rise from his sleep. Who will grant me this: that you might protect me in the <term>underworld<note>original: "inferno," referring to the realm of the dead or the grave.</note></term> and hide me until your wrath passes, and that you would set a time for me when you would remember me? Do you think a dead man might live again? All the days in which I now serve as a soldier, I wait until my change comes. You will call me, and I will answer you; you will reach out your right hand to the work of your hands. Indeed, you have numbered my steps, but spare my sins. You have sealed my offenses as if in a pouch, but you have healed my iniquity. A falling mountain slides away, and a rock is moved from its place. Waters hollow out stones, and the earth is consumed little by little by a flood. And in the same way, you destroy man. You strengthened him for a little while, so that he might pass away forever. You changed his face, and you sent him away. Whether his sons are noble or ignoble, he will not understand. Yet while he lives, his flesh shall grieve, and his soul shall mourn over itself.

<margin>15.</margin>
**Then Eliphaz** the Temanite responded and said: Will a wise man answer as if speaking into the wind, and fill his stomach with burning heat? You argue with words that are not equal to you, and you speak what does not benefit you. As much as is in you, you have done away with fear, and you have taken away prayers before God. For your iniquity has taught your mouth, and you imitate the tongue of blasphemers. Your own mouth will condemn you, and not I; and your own lips will answer you. Were you the first man born, and were you formed before the hills? Have you heard the counsel of God, and will wisdom be inferior to you? What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that we are ignorant of? Both the aged and the ancient are among us, much older than your fathers. Is it a small thing that God should comfort you? But your wicked words prevent this. Why does your heart lift you up, and as if thinking of great things, why do you have astonished eyes? Why does your spirit swell against God, so that you utter such words from your mouth? What is man, that he should be without spot, and that he should appear just, though born of a woman? Behold, among his saints no one is unchangeable, and the heavens are not pure in his sight. How much more abominable and useless is man, who drinks iniquity like water? I will show you, hear me: what I have seen, I will tell you. Wise men confess, and they do not hide what they heard from their fathers, to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed through them. All his days the wicked man is proud, and the number of the years of his tyranny is uncertain. The sound of terror is always in his ears, and even when there is peace, he suspects an ambush. He does not believe that he can return from darkness to light, looking around on every side for the sword. When he moves to seek bread, he knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand. Tribulation shall terrify him, and anguish shall hem him in, like a king prepared for battle. For he stretched out his hand against God, and he strengthened himself against the Almighty. He ran against him with a stiff neck, and was armed with a fat neck. Fatness covered his face, and grease hangs from his sides. He lived in desolate cities, and in deserted houses which have been turned into mounds. He shall not be enriched, nor shall his substance remain, nor shall he send his root into the earth. He shall not depart from darkness. A flame shall dry up his branches, and he shall be taken away by the breath of his mouth. Let him not believe, deceived by a vain error, that he is to be redeemed by any price. Before his days are full, he shall perish, and his hands shall wither. His cluster of grapes shall be damaged like a vine in its first flower, and like an olive tree casting off its bloom. For the congregation of the hypocrite is sterile, and fire shall devour the tents of those who freely accept bribes. He has conceived sorrow and brought forth iniquity, and his womb prepares deceits.

<column-break/>

<margin>16. Job</margin>
**But Job** responding said: I have frequently heard such things. You are all burdensome comforters. Will windy words ever have an end, or is it a trouble to you if you speak? I also could speak things similar to you; if only your soul were in place of my soul. I too would comfort you with speeches, and I would wag my head over you. I would strengthen you with my mouth, and I would move my lips as if sparing you. If I speak, my pain will not rest; and if I keep silent, it will not depart from me. But now my pain has crushed me, and all my limbs are reduced to nothing. my wrinkles bear witness against me, and a false speaker is raised up against my face, contradicting me. He gathered his fury against me, and threatening me, he gnashed with his teeth. My enemy has looked upon me with terrible eyes. They opened their mouths over me, and reproaching me, they struck my jaw; they satisfied themselves with my punishments. God has shut me up with the wicked, and delivered me into the hands of the impious. I, who was once wealthy, was suddenly crushed. He took me by my neck, he broke me, and he set me up as his target. He surrounded me with his spears; he wounded my loins and did not spare, and he poured my vitals out onto the earth. He cut me with wound upon wound; he rushed at me like a giant. I sewed <term>sackcloth<note>original: "Sacciū," a coarse cloth worn as a sign of mourning or penitence.</note></term> over my skin, and I covered my horn with ash. My face is swollen from weeping, and my eyelids have grown dim. I have suffered these things without iniquity in my hand, since I had pure prayers to God. O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry find no place of hiding in you. For behold, my witness is in heaven, and he who knows my conscience is on high. My friends are full of words; my eye drops tears to God. And if only a man might be judged with God, just as a son of man is judged with his companion. For behold, the short years pass away, and I walk the path by which I shall not return.

<margin>17.</margin>
My spirit shall be thinned, my days shall be shortened, and only the grave remains for me. I have not sinned, and yet my eye lingers in bitterness. Deliver me, Lord, and set me beside you, and let any man's hand fight against me. You have kept their hearts far from discipline, and therefore they shall not be exalted. He promises a prize to his companions, and the eyes of his children shall fail. He has set me as a proverb for the common people; I am an example before them. My eyes have grown dim with indignation, and my limbs are reduced as if to nothing. The just shall be stunned by this, and the innocent shall be raised up against the hypocrite. And the just man shall hold to his way, and he with clean hands shall add to his strength. Therefore, all of you, turn back and come; and I shall not find any wise man among you. My days have passed away, my thoughts are scattered, twisting my heart. They turned night into day, and again after the darkness I hope for light. If I wait, the underworld is my house; and I have spread my bed in the darkness. I said to corruption: "You are my father," and to the worms: "My mother and my sister." Where, then, is my expectation now, and who considers my patience? All my things shall descend into the deepest underworld; do you think that at least there I shall have rest?

<margin>18. Bildad</margin>
**Then Bildad** the Shuhite responded and said: How long will you throw about words? Understand first, and then let us speak. Why are we considered as cattle, and why have we become vile in your sight? You who destroy your soul in your fury, shall the earth be abandoned because of you, and shall rocks be moved from their place? Shall not the light of the wicked be extinguished, and the flame of his fire not shine? Light shall grow dark in his tent, and the lamp that is over him shall be put out. The steps of his strength shall be narrowed, and his own counsel shall cast him down. For he has thrust his feet into a net, and he walks in its meshes. His heel shall be held in a snare, and thirst shall burn against him. A trap is hidden for him in the ground, and his pitfall is upon the path. Terrors shall frighten him on every side, and shall entangle his feet. Let his strength be thinned by hunger, and let famine invade his ribs. Let death, the firstborn, devour the beauty of his skin, and consume his arms. Let his confidence be torn away from his tent, and let destruction trample over him like a king. Let the companions of him who is no more dwell in his tent; let sulfur be scattered in his dwelling. Let his roots be dried up below, and his harvest be thinned above. Let his memory perish from the earth, and let his name not be celebrated in the streets. He shall expel him from light into darkness, and transfer him out of the world. He shall have no seed, nor offspring among his people, nor any remnants in his regions. Those who come after him shall be stunned by his day, and horror shall seize those who went before. These, then, are the tabernacles of the wicked, and this is the place of him who does not know God.

<margin>19. Job</margin>
**But Job** responding said: How long will you afflict my soul, and crush me with speeches? Behold, ten times you have confounded me, and you are not ashamed, oppressing me. For even if I have been ignorant, my ignorance will be with me. But you rise up against me, and you rebuke me with my reproaches. At least now understand that God has afflicted me with an unequal judgment, and has surrounded me with his whips. Behold, I cry out, suffering violence, and no one will hear; I shall shout aloud, and there is no one to judge. He has hedged in my way so that I cannot pass, and he has placed darkness in my paths. He has stripped me of my glory,

...mine. And you have destroyed my hope like a tree. His fury is kindled against me, and he treats me like his enemy. His troops came together and made their way through me; they besieged my tent on every side. He has put my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances have pulled away from me like strangers. My kinsmen have forsaken me, and those who knew me have forgotten me. The guests in my house and my maidservants treated me as a stranger; I was like an alien in their eyes. I called my servant and he did not answer; I pleaded with him with my own mouth. My wife loathes my breath, and I entreated the children of my own womb. Even the foolish despised me; when I left them, they spoke against me. My former counselors detested me, and the one I loved most has turned against me. My bone clings to my skin and my flesh, and only the skin of my teeth remains. Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, for the hand of the Lord has touched me. Why do you persecute me as God does, and glut yourselves on my flesh? Who will grant me that my words be written? Who will give me that they be inscribed in a book with an iron pen and a plate of lead, or carved with a <term>chisel<note>original: "celte," a stone or metal tool used for carving or hacking.</note></term> in flint? For I know that my redeemer lives, and on the last day I shall rise from the earth. And again I shall be clothed with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see my God. Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another. This hope is laid up in my bosom. Why then do you now say, "Let us persecute him and find a root of complaint against him?" Flee therefore from the face of the sword, for the sword is the avenger of iniquities; and know that there is a judgment.

<margin>R</margin>
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said: Therefore my varied thoughts succeed one another, and my mind is hurried in different directions. I will hear the doctrine with which you rebuke me, and the spirit of my understanding shall answer me. This I have known from the beginning, since man was placed upon the earth: that the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite is but for a moment. Though his pride should rise up to heaven and his head touch the clouds, he shall be destroyed in the end like a dung-heap; and those who had seen him shall say, "Where is he?" Like a fleeing dream he shall not be found; he shall pass away like a vision of the night. The eye that had seen him shall see him no more, nor shall his place behold him any longer. His children shall be worn down with poverty, and his hands shall return his sorrow to him. His bones shall be filled with the vices of his youth, and they shall sleep with him in the dust. For when evil is sweet in his mouth, he hides it under his tongue. He will spare it and not leave it, and hide it in his throat. His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of <term>asps<note>The asp was a term used for several species of venomous snakes, particularly the Egyptian cobra, often used as a symbol of hidden poison.</note></term> within him. The riches he swallowed, he shall vomit up, and God shall draw them out of his belly. He shall suck the head of asps, and the tongue of the viper shall kill him. He shall not see the streams of the river, nor the torrents of honey and butter. He shall pay for all he did, yet he shall not be consumed; according to the multitude of his inventions, so shall he suffer. For by crushing the poor he left them naked; he seized a house and did not build it. His belly was never satisfied, and when he has what he desired, he shall not be able to possess it. Nothing remained of his food, and therefore nothing shall remain of his goods. When he is filled, he shall be straightened; he shall burn, and every sorrow shall fall upon him. Would that his belly were filled, so that He might send the wrath of His fury upon him and rain His war upon him. He shall flee from iron weapons and fall upon a bronze bow. Drawn and coming out of its scabbard, and flashing in its bitterness, it goes; and terrible things tremble over him. All darkness is hidden in his secret places. A fire not kindled by man shall devour him; he that is left in his tent shall be afflicted. The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him. The offspring of his house shall be exposed; it shall be dragged away in the day of the Lord's fury. This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance from the Lord.

<margin>R</margin>
Then Job answered and said: Hear, I beseech you, my words, and do penance. Bear with me that I also may speak; and after my words, if it seems right, you may laugh. Is my dispute against man, that I should not be justly saddened? Look at me and be astonished, and lay your finger on your mouth. As for me, when I remember, I am afraid, and trembling shakes my flesh. Why then do the wicked live? They are lifted up and strengthened with riches. Their seed remains before them, a crowd of kinsmen and grandsons in their sight. Their houses are secure and peaceful, and the rod of God is not upon them. Their bull conceives and does not fail; their cow gives birth and is not deprived of her offspring. Their little ones go forth like flocks, and their infants jump for joy in play. They hold the timbrel and the harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ. They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to the <term>underworld<note>original: "inferna," referring to the place of the dead.</note></term>. They said to God: "Depart from us; we do not want the knowledge of your ways. Who is the Almighty that we should serve him? And what does it profit us if we pray to him?" Yet, because their good things are not in their own hand, let the counsel of the wicked be far from me. How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished, and a flood comes upon them, and He distributes sorrows in His fury? They shall be like straw before the face of the wind, and like ashes which the whirlwind scatters. God shall save the sorrow of the father for his children; and when He repays him, then he shall know. His eyes shall see his own destruction, and he shall drink of the fury of the Almighty. For what does it matter to him concerning his house after him, even if the number of his months be halved? Shall anyone teach God knowledge, when He judges those who are high? One dies strong and healthy, rich and happy; his bowels are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow. But another dies in the bitterness of his soul without any riches; and yet both shall sleep in the dust, and worms shall cover them. Truly I know your thoughts and your unjust judgments against me. For you say, "Where is the house of the prince? And where are the tents of the wicked?" Ask any of the travelers, and you will realize they understand these same things: that the wicked man is preserved for the day of perdition, and he shall be led to the day of fury. Who shall rebuke his way before his face? And who shall repay him for what he has done? He shall be led to the graves and shall keep watch in the heap of the dead. He was sweet to the pebbles of <term>Cocytus<note>original: "cocyti," a classical reference to a river in the Greek underworld. The Latin translator uses it to represent the depths of the grave.</note></term>; and he draws every man after him, and innumerable ones before him. How then do you comfort me in vain, when your answer is shown to resist the truth?

<margin>R</margin>
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: Can a man be compared to God, even when he is of perfect knowledge? Does it profit God if you are just? Or what do you give Him if your life is unspotted? Will He rebuke you because He fears you, and enter into judgment with you? Is it not because of your great malice and your infinite iniquities? For you have taken a pledge from your brothers without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing. You did not give water to the weary, and you withdrew bread from the hungry. By the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and being most powerful you held it. You sent widows away empty, and you crushed the arms of orphans.

<column-break/>

Therefore you are surrounded with snares, and sudden fear troubles you. And you thought you would not see the darkness, and would not be overwhelmed by the rush of cleansing waters. Do you think that God is higher than heaven, and exalted above the tops of the stars? And you say: "What does God know? He judges as if through a mist. Clouds are His hiding place, and He does not consider our affairs; He walks about the hinges of heaven." Do you desire to keep the path of the ages, which wicked men have trodden? They were taken away before their time, and a flood overturned their foundation. They said to God, "Depart from us," and they thought the Almighty could do nothing to them, even though He had filled their houses with good things. Let their judgment be far from me! The just shall see and rejoice, and the innocent shall mock them. Has not their status been cut down, and fire shall devour the remnants of them? Submit yourself to Him, therefore, and have peace; and by this you shall have the best fruits. Receive the law from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, and you shall put iniquity far from your tent. He shall give flint for earth, and for flint, torrents of gold. And the Almighty shall be against your enemies, and silver shall be heaped up for you. Then you shall abound in delights over the Almighty, and you shall lift up your face to God. You shall pray to Him and He will hear you, and you shall pay your vows. You shall decide a matter and it shall come to you, and light shall shine on your ways. For he who has been humbled shall be in glory; and he who has bowed his eyes shall be saved. The innocent shall be saved; and he shall be saved by the cleanness of his hands.

<margin>R</margin>
Then Job answered and said: Now also my speech is in bitterness, and the hand of my wound is heavy beyond my groaning. Who will grant me that I might know and find Him, and come even to His throne? I would set my judgment before Him, and fill my mouth with rebukes, so that I might know the words He would answer me, and understand what He would say to me. I do not want Him to contend with me with great force, nor overwhelm me with the weight of His greatness. Let Him propose equity against me, so that my judgment might reach victory. If I go to the east, He does not appear; if to the west, I do not perceive Him. If I go to the left, what shall I do? I shall not catch Him. If I turn to the right, I shall not see Him. But He knows my way, and He shall try me like gold that passes through the fire. My foot has followed His steps; I have kept His way and not turned aside from it. I have not departed from the commandments of His lips, and I have hidden the words of His mouth in my bosom. For He is alone, and no one can turn away His thought; and whatever His soul has willed, that He has done. When He has fulfilled His will in me, many other similar things are also ready with Him. And therefore I am troubled at His presence, and considering Him, I am anxious with fear. God has softened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me. For I did not perish because of the looming darkness, nor did the mist cover my face. Times are not hidden from the Almighty, but those who know Him are ignorant of His days. Others have moved boundaries; they have plundered flocks and fed them. They have driven away the donkey of orphans, and taken the widow’s ox for a pledge. They have subverted the way of the poor, and oppressed the meek of the earth together. Others, like <term>wild asses<note>original: "onagri," referring to the Asiatic wild ass, known for being untameable and living in desert regions.</note></term> in the desert, go out to their work; watching for prey, they prepare bread for their children. They reap a field that is not their own, and they gather the vintage of the one they have oppressed by force. They leave men naked, taking away their clothing, so they have no covering in the cold. The rains of the mountains soak them, and having no shelter, they embrace the rocks. They have used violence in plundering orphans, and have stripped the common people of the poor. From the naked and those walking without clothing, and from the hungry, they have taken away the ears of grain. They have rested at noon within the walls of those who, having trodden the winepresses, are thirsty. They have made men groan from the cities, and the soul of the wounded has cried out; and God does not let it go unavenged. These were rebels against the light; they did not know His ways, nor did they return by His paths. At early dawn the murderer rises; he kills the needy and the poor, and by night he will be like a thief. The eye of the adulterer watches for the darkness, saying, "No eye shall see me," and he covers his face. He digs through houses in the dark, as they agreed among themselves by night, and they did not know the light. If the dawn appears suddenly, they think it the shadow of death; and so they walk in darkness as if in light. He is light upon the face of the water. Let his portion on earth be cursed, and let him not walk by the way of the vineyards. Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat, and let his sin reach even to the underworld. Let mercy forget him; let his sweetness be the worm. Let him not be in remembrance, but let him be broken like an unfruitful tree. For he fed the sterile woman who does not bear, and did not do well for the widow. He pulled down the strong in his strength; and when he stands, he will not trust his own life. God gave him a place for penance, and he abuses it in pride. But His eyes are on his ways. They are lifted up for a little while and shall not stand; they shall be humbled like all things, and taken away; and they shall be crushed like the tops of the ears of grain. But if it is not so, who can convict me of lying, and set my words before God?

<margin>R</margin>
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: Power and terror are with Him, who makes peace in His high places. Is there any number to His soldiers? And upon whom does His light not shine? Can a man be justified when compared to God, or can he appear clean who is born of a woman? Behold, even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not clean in His sight. How much less man, who is rottenness, and the son of man, a worm?

<margin>R</margin>
Then Job answered and said: Whose helper are you? Is it the weak man's? And do you support the arm of him who is not strong? To whom have you given counsel? Perhaps to him who has no wisdom? And have you shown your great prudence? Whom did you want to teach? Was it not Him who made the breath of life? Behold, the <term>giants<note>original: "gigantes," often referring in the Vulgate to the Rephaim or the mighty ones of old who were thought to dwell in the depths.</note></term> groan under the waters, and those who dwell with them. The underworld is naked before Him, and there is no covering for perdition. He stretches out the north over the void, and hangs the earth upon nothing. He binds the waters in His clouds, so they do not break out all at once downward. He holds the face of His throne and spreads His mist over it. He has surrounded the waters with a limit, until light and darkness come to an end. The pillars of heaven tremble and are afraid at His nod. By His strength the seas were suddenly gathered together, and His wisdom struck the proud one. His spirit adorned the heavens, and by His hand as a midwife, the <term>twisted serpent<note>original: "coluber tortuosus," likely a reference to the Leviathan or a celestial constellation symbolizing chaos subdued by God.</note></term> was brought forth. Behold, these things are said in part of His ways; and since we have scarcely heard a small drop of His word, who can behold the thunder of His greatness?

<meta>This page continues from Job 27:5. The previous page ended with Job's friends pressuring him to confess, and this page opens with Job's steadfast refusal to renounce his integrity. The catchword "cru-" at the end of the first column connects to "crudelem" at the start of the second.</meta>

...from my innocence, and my justification which I have begun I will not desert. Nor shall my heart reproach me in all my life. Let my enemy be as the ungodly, and my adversary as the wicked. For what is the hope of the hypocrite, if he greedily robs, and God does not deliver his soul? Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? Or can he delight in the Almighty, and call upon God at all times? I will teach you by the hand of God what the Almighty possesses, and I will not hide it. Behold, you all know it, so why do you speak such vain things without cause? This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they shall receive from the Almighty Lord. If his children are multiplied, they shall be for the sword, and his grandsons shall not be satisfied with bread. Those who remain of him shall be buried in destruction, and his widows shall not weep. If he heaps up silver like the earth, and prepares garments as the clay, he may prepare them, but the just shall be clothed in them, and the innocent shall divide the silver. He built his house like a moth, and like a watchman he made a booth. The rich man, when he sleeps, shall take nothing with him; he shall open his eyes and find nothing. Poverty shall overtake him like water; a tempest shall overwhelm him in the night. A burning wind shall take him up and carry him away, and like a whirlwind it shall snatch him from his place. He shall send it upon him and not spare; fleeing, he shall flee from his hand. He shall clap his hands over him, and shall hiss at him, looking upon his place. 

Silver has the beginnings of its veins, and gold has a place where it is melted. Iron is taken from the earth, and stone melted by heat is turned into brass. He has set a limit to the darkness, and he himself beholds the end of all things. The stone of gloom and the shadow of death is divided by a torrent from the people on pilgrimage; those whom the foot of the needy man has forgotten, and the pathless. The earth, from which bread arose, is overturned in its place by fire. The place of sapphire is its stones, and its clods are gold. The bird has not known the path, nor has the eye of the vulture beheld it. The sons of the <term>merchants<note>original: "institorum," referring to traders or those who set up stalls.</note></term> have not trodden it, nor has the lioness passed through it. He stretches out his hand to the flint; he overturns mountains from the roots. In the rocks he has cut rivers, and his eye has seen every precious thing. He has also searched the depths of the rivers, and brought hidden things to light. 

But where is **wisdom** found? And where is the place of understanding? Man does not know its price, nor is it found in the land of those who live pleasantly. The abyss says, "It is not in me," and the sea speaks, "It is not with me." <term>Pure gold<note>original: "aurum obrizum," the highest quality of refined gold.</note></term> shall not be given for it, nor shall silver be weighed in exchange for it. It shall not be compared to the dyed colors of India, nor to the most precious sardonyx stone, nor the sapphire. Gold or glass shall not equal it, nor shall vessels of gold be exchanged for it. High things and silk nets and memorable things shall not be mentioned in comparison. For wisdom is drawn from hidden places, and the topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, nor shall it be compared to the purest cleansing. 

Whence then does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding? It is hidden from the eyes of all living, and it lies hid from the birds of the air. Destruction and death have said, "With our ears we have heard the fame of it." God understands its way, and he knows its place. For he beholds the ends of the world, and looks upon all things that are under heaven; he who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters in a measure. When he gave a law for the rain, and a way for the sounding storms, then he saw it and declared it, and prepared it and searched it out. And he said to man: "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding."

And Job added, taking up his parable, and said: Who will grant me that I might be as in the months past, according to the days in which God kept me? When his lamp shined over my head, and by his light I walked in darkness; as I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly in my tabernacle, when the Almighty was with me, and my boys were round about me; when I washed my feet with butter, and the rock poured out for me rivers of oil; when I went out to the gate of the city, and they prepared a seat for me in the street. The young men saw me and hid themselves, and the old men rose up and stood. The princes ceased to speak, and laid their finger on their mouth. The leaders held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to their throat. The ear that heard me blessed me, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me, because I had delivered the poor man that cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper. The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow. I was clothed with justice, and I robed myself with my judgment as with a garment and a diadem. I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame. I was a father to the poor, and the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently. I broke the jaws of the wicked man, and from his teeth I took away the prey. And I said, "I shall die in my little nest, and like a palm tree I shall multiply my days." My root is opened by the waters, and the dew shall dwell upon my harvest. My glory shall always be renewed, and my bow shall be restored in my hand. They that heard me waited for my sentence, and being attentive held their peace at my counsel. To my words they dared add nothing, and my eloquence dropped upon them. They waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouth as for the late shower. If I laughed at them, they believed it not, and the light of my countenance did not fall to the ground. If I wished to go to them, I sat first. When I sat as a king with an army standing round, I was yet a comforter of those that mourned.

**But** now those younger in time deride me, whose fathers I did not think worthy to place with the dogs of my flock; the strength of whose hands was as nothing to me, and they were thought unworthy of life itself. Barren with want and hunger, who gnawed in the solitude, needy with want and calamity and misery; and they ate grass and the bark of trees, and the root of junipers was their food. They who, snatching these things from the valleys, when they had found each thing, they rushed with a cry. They dwelt in the desert places of torrents, in caves of the earth, or upon the flint. They who rejoiced among such things, and counted it a delight to be under the thorns. The sons of fools and ignoble men, and not appearing at all upon the earth. Now I am become their song, and I am become a proverb to them. They abhor me, and flee far from me, and they do not fear to spit in my face. For he has opened his quiver and afflicted me, and has put a bridle into my mouth. At the right hand of the east my calamities rose up immediately. They have overturned my feet and overwhelmed me with their paths as with waves. They have destroyed my ways, they have lain in wait for me, and they have prevailed; and there was no one to bring help. They rushed in upon me as when a wall is broken and a gate opened, and I was rolled down to my miseries. I am reduced to nothing; he has taken away my desire as a wind, and my salvation has passed away like a cloud. But now my soul withers within myself, and the days of affliction possess me. In the night my bone is pierced with sorrows, and they that consume me do not sleep. In the multitude of them my garment is consumed, and they have girded me about like the collar of my coat. I am compared to clay, and I am likened to ashes and cinders. I cry to you and you do not hear me; I stand and you do not look at me. You are changed to be cru-

**These** three men ceased to answer Job, because he seemed just to himself. And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was angry and indignant. For His eyes are upon the ways of men, and He considers all their steps. There is no darkness, and there is no shadow of death, where those who work iniquity may be hidden. For it is no longer in the power of man to come to God in judgment. He shall break in pieces many and innumerable, and shall make others stand in their place. For He knows their works, and therefore He will bring night, and they shall be crushed. He has struck them like impious men in the place of onlookers, who as if by design retreated from Him, and would not understand all His ways; so that they caused the cry of the needy to come to Him, and He heard the voice of the poor. For when He grants peace, who is there that can condemn? And when He hides His face, who is there that can behold Him, both over a nation and over all men? If I have erred, teach me; if I have spoken iniquity, I will add no more. Does God require it of you because you were displeased with Him? For you have chosen, and not I. If you know anything better, speak. Let men of understanding speak to me, and let a wise man hear me. But Job has spoken foolishly, and his words do not sound like discipline. Therefore, most pious one, let him not cease even to the end from men of iniquity, who added blasphemy over his sins; let him be constrained among us in the meantime, and then let him provoke God to judgment with his words.

Does your thought seem equal to you, so that you would say: "I am more just than God"? For you said: "What is just does not please You," or "What will it profit You if I have sinned?" Therefore, I will answer your words, and your friends who are with you. Look up at the heaven and behold, and contemplate the ether, which is higher than you. If you sin, how will you hurt Him? And if your iniquities are multiplied, what will you do against Him? Furthermore, if you act justly, what will you give Him, or what will He receive from your hand? Your impiety will hurt a man who is like you, and your justice will help the son of man. Because of the multitude of calumniators they shall cry out, and they shall wail because of the violence of the arm of tyrants. And he did not say: "Where is God who made me, who gave songs in the night? Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and instructs us more than the birds of the heaven?" In his eyes, as with a hook, He shall catch him, and with stakes He shall pierce his jaws. Can you draw out Leviathan <note>A great sea monster, often identified as a crocodile or a dragon</note> with a hook, and tie his tongue with a rope? Can you put a ring in his nose, or pierce his jaw with a bracelet? ... Will he multiply prayers to you, or speak soft words to you? Will he make a covenant with you, and will you take him as an eternal servant? Will you play with him as with a bird, or tie him up for your young girls? Will his friends cut him up; will the merchants divide him? Can you fill his skin with nets, or his head with a cabin of fish? Lay your hand upon him; remember the battle, and speak no more. Behold, his hope shall fail him, and in the sight of all he shall be cast down. Not as one who is cruel will I stir him up. For who can resist my face? Who has given to me first, that I should repay him? All things that are under heaven are mine. I will not spare him, nor his powerful words, composed for comparison. Who will reveal the face of his garment, and who will enter into the midst of his mouth? Who shall open the gates of his face? Terror is round about his teeth. His body is like molten shields, compacted with scales pressing upon one another. One is joined to another, and not even a breathing hole exists between them. One shall stick to the other, and holding each other, they shall never be separated. His sneezing is a splendor of fire, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. From his mouth go forth lamps, like sparks of fire. From his nostrils comes smoke, like a pot that is heated and boiling. His breath makes coals burn, and a flame comes out of his mouth. In his neck dwells strength, and poverty goes before his face. The members of his flesh cling together; He shall send lightning against him, and he shall not be carried to another place. His heart shall be hardened like a stone, and tightened like a blacksmith's anvil. When he is raised up, the angels shall fear, and being terrified, they shall be purified. When the sword reaches him, it will not be able to stand, nor the spear, nor the dart, nor the breastplate. For he shall account iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood. The archer shall not put him to flight; the stones of the sling are turned into stubble for him. He shall esteem the hammer as stubble, and he shall laugh at the quivering spear. Under him are the rays of the sun; he shall spread gold under him like mud. He shall make the deep sea boil like a pot, and shall set it like boiling ointments. A path shall shine after him; he shall esteem the abyss as growing old. There is no power upon earth that can be compared to him, who was made to fear no one. He beholds every high thing; he is king over all the children of pride.

<margin>40.</margin>
**Then** the Lord answered Job from the whirlwind and said: Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you, and you indicate the answer to me. Will you make my judgment void, and condemn me so that you may be justified? ... And if you have an arm like God, and if you thunder with a voice like His, deck yourself with beauty, and be lifted up on high, and be glorious, and clothe yourself with beautiful garments. Scatter the proud in your fury; and looking upon every arrogant man, humble him. Look upon all the proud and confound them, and crush the wicked in their place. Hide them in the dust together, and drown their faces in the pit. And then I will confess that your own right hand can save you.

<margin>39.</margin>
**Then** Job, answering the Lord, said: I know that you can do all things, and no thought is hidden from you. Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and of things that far exceeded my knowledge. Hear, and I will speak; I will question you, and you answer me. With the hearing of the ear I have heard you, but now my eye sees you. Therefore I reprehend myself, and I do penance in embers and ashes. Now after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite: My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken what is right before me, as my servant Job has. Therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. But Job, my servant, shall pray for you; I will accept his face, so that your folly may not be imputed to you. For you have not spoken what is right before me, as my servant Job has. So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job. The Lord also turned to the repentance of Job when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord added double to all that Job had possessed. Then all his brothers came to him, and all his sisters, and all who had known him before, and they ate bread with him in his house; they shook their heads over him and comforted him for all the evil that God had brought upon him. And each one gave him one sheep and one golden earring. And the Lord blessed the later end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys. And he had seven sons and three daughters. And he called the name of the first Day <note>original: "diem", for Jemimah</note>, and the name of the second Cassia <note>Keziah</note>, and the name of the third Horn of Antimony <note>original: "cornu stibii", for Keren-happuch, referring to eye-makeup</note>. And there were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job in all the earth. And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers. Now Job lived after these things one hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and his sons' sons even to the fourth generation; and he died an old man and full of days. Here ends the book of Job.

<column-break/>

**There are** twenty-two letters among the Hebrews, which is the language that the Chaldeans and Syrians largely share. These same elements have the same sound, but different characters. For the Samaritans also carve the Pentateuch <note>The first five books of the Bible</note> of Moses with these same letters; they differ only in a few shapes and flourishes. It is certain that Ezra the scribe and teacher of the law, after the capture of Jerusalem and the restoration of the temple under Zerubbabel, found other letters which we now use, since up to that time it is clear that the characters of the Samaritans and the Hebrews were the same. In the Book of Numbers, this same count is reckoned under the number seventy-two for the whole multitude of Israel. In the Lamentations of Jeremiah, there are four alphabets; each one is woven in various ways with volumes and words. The first two of these are written as if in Sapphic meter. The third... is written in the alphabet. The fourth is similar to the first and second. In the fifth also, each is a fifty-syllable alphabet... of four verses. ... Jerome... some say there are five double letters: Caph, Mem, Nun, Phe, Sade. Whence also five books are estimated by many to be double: Samuel, Kings <note>original: "malachim"</note>, Chronicles <note>original: "dabreiamin"</note>, Ezra, and Jeremiah with his *Cynoth*, that is, his Lamentations. Since there are twenty-two elements by which we speak in Hebrew, and from which the human voice is woven, twenty-two volumes are reckoned, by which, as if by letters and beginnings in the doctrine of God, the tender and nursing infancy of the just man is instructed. The first book among them is called *Bresith* <note>Hebrew: "In the beginning"</note> which we call Genesis. The second is *Ellesmoth* which is called Exodus. The third is *Vaiycra*, that is, Leviticus. The fourth is *Vagedaber*, which we call Numbers. The fifth is *Helleaddabarim*, which is noted as Deuteronomy. These are the five books of Moses, which they properly call the *Thora*, that is, the Law. Following the order of the Prophets: they begin from Joshua the son of Nun... then *Sophtin*, that is, Judges... Samuel, which we call the First and Second of Kings... *Malachim*, that is, Kings: which is contained in the third and fourth volumes of Kings. And it is much better to say *Malachim*, that is, Kings, than *Malachoth*, that is, of Kingdoms. For it does not describe the kingdoms of many nations, but of one Israelite people, which is contained in twelve tribes. The ninth is Isaiah. The tenth is Jeremiah. The eleventh is Ezekiel. The twelfth is the Twelve Prophets... who among them are at the end of a single volume. The third order holds the Hagiographa <note>The "Holy Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible</note>. And the first book begins from Job. The second from David... the third, Solomon has three books: that is, Proverbs, that is, Ecclesiastes, that is, the Song of Songs. The sixth is Daniel. The seventh is *Dabreiamin*, that is, the Words of Days <note>Chronicles</note>... the eighth is Ezra... the ninth is Esther. And so there are likewise twenty-two books of the Old Law: that is, five of Moses, eight of the Prophets, and nine of the Hagiographa, although some count Ruth and Lamentations <note>Cynoth</note> among the Hagiographa and extend the number in their reckoning of books to twenty-four. Whatever is outside of these is to be counted among the apocrypha. Wisdom, which is commonly inscribed as Solomon's, and the book of Jesus the son of Sirach, Judith and Tobit and the Shepherd are not in the canon. ... I found the first book of Maccabees in Hebrew. The second is Greek, which can be proven from the phrasing itself. ... Certainly, I will confess my error in them... for if you wish to read for justice and not for envy, turn yourselves to the sources... Farewell in the Lord... Be silent and humble yourself under every hand...

# BOOK OF KINGS, WHICH IS
# CALLED MALACHIM.
