## Setting Out
Departing from there, he found Elisha <note>original: "hely," a variant spelling for Eliseus or Elisha</note> the son of Shaphat plowing with twelve yokes of oxen, and he himself was with the twelfth. When Elijah came to him, he cast his mantle over him. He immediately left the oxen and ran after Elijah, saying: "I pray you, let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you." And he said to him: "Go and return, for what was mine to do, I have done for you." Having returned from him, he took a pair of oxen and slaughtered them; he cooked the meat using the wooden yokes <note>original: "stramie(n) boum," literally the straw or harness equipment</note> of the oxen as fuel, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then rising up, he went and followed Elijah and ministered to him.

<image-desc>Large decorative initial P in red and blue ink with fine penwork flourishes.</image-desc>

## Furthermore
Ben-hadad, king of Syria, gathered his entire army together, and thirty-two kings with him, along with horses and chariots. Ascending, he fought against Samaria and besieged it. Sending messengers to Ahab, king of Israel, in the city, he said: "Thus says Ben-hadad: Your silver and your gold are mine; your wives and your best children are mine." The king of Israel answered: "According to your word, my lord king, I am yours and all that I have." The messengers returned and said: "Thus says Ben-hadad who sent us to you: You shall give me your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children. Tomorrow, therefore, at this same hour, I will send my servants to you, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants; and whatever pleases them, they shall take in their hands and carry away." Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land and said: "Take note and see that this man is setting a trap for us. For he sent to me for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not refuse him." All the elders and the whole people said to him: "Do not listen, nor consent to him." So he answered the messengers of Ben-hadad: "Tell my lord the king: All that you sent for to me, your servant, at the beginning, I will do; but this thing I cannot do." The messengers returned and brought him the word. He sent back and said: "May the gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people who follow me." And the king of Israel answering said: "Tell him: Let not the one who puts on his armor boast like the one who takes it off." <note>A proverbial warning against overconfidence before a battle has been won.</note> It happened that when he heard this word, he was drinking with the kings in the pavilions, and he said to his servants: "Surround the city." And they surrounded it. And behold, a certain prophet approached Ahab, king of Israel, and said: "Thus says the Lord: Have you indeed seen all this vast multitude? Behold, I will deliver it into your hand today, so that you may know that I am the Lord." And Ahab said: "By whom?" And he said to him: "Thus says the Lord: By the servants of the princes of the provinces." And he said: "Who shall begin the battle?" And he said: "You." He then mustered the servants of the princes of the provinces and found the number to be two hundred thirty-two; and after them, he mustered all the people, all the children of Israel, seven thousand. They went out at noon. But Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in his pavilion, and the thirty-two kings with him who had come to help him. The servants of the princes went out in the first rank. Ben-hadad sent out scouts who reported to him, saying: "Men have come out from Samaria." And he said: "Whether they come for peace, take them alive; or whether they come for battle, take them alive." So the servants of the princes went out, and the rest of the army followed. Each one struck down the man who came against him, and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them. Ben-hadad the king of Syria also fled on a horse with his horsemen. The king of Israel went out and struck the horses and chariots, and defeated Syria with a great slaughter.

<image-desc>Decorative initial A in red ink.</image-desc>

## Approaching
The prophet then approached the king of Israel and said: "Go and strengthen yourself, and know and see what you must do; for in the following year, the king of Syria will come up against you." But the servants of the king of Syria said to him: "Their gods are gods of the mountains, and therefore they have overcome us. It is better that we fight against them in the plains, and we shall prevail over them. Therefore, do this: Remove each of the kings from his army and put captains in their place. Restore the number of soldiers who fell from yours, and horses like the former horses, and chariots like the chariots you had before; and we will fight against them in the plains, and you will see that we shall prevail over them." He believed their counsel and did so. Therefore, after a year had passed, Ben-hadad mustered the Syrians and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel. Furthermore, the children of Israel were mustered and, having received provisions, they set out and camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats; but the Syrians filled the land. And a man of God approached and said to the king of Israel: "Thus says the Lord: Because the Syrians have said, 'The Lord is a god of the mountains and he is not a god of the valleys,' I will deliver all this great multitude into your hand, and you shall know that I am the Lord." They remained in formation for seven days, one side against the other. On the seventh day, the battle was joined. The children of Israel struck down one hundred thousand Syrian footmen in one day. Those who remained fled into the city of Aphek, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand of the men who were left. Ben-hadad, fleeing, entered the city into an inner chamber. His servants said to him: "Behold, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful. Let us, therefore, put sackcloth on our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will save your life." They girded sackcloth on their waists and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said: "Your servant Ben-hadad says: 'I pray you, let me live.'" And he said: "If he is still alive, he is my brother." The men took this as an omen, and quickly catching the word from his mouth, they said: "Your brother Ben-hadad lives." And he said to them: "Go and bring him." So Ben-hadad came out to him, and he took him up into his chariot. Ben-hadad said to him: "The cities which my father took from your father, I will restore; and you may make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab replied: "And I will let you go with this covenant." So he made a covenant and let him go. Then a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the Lord: "Strike me." But the man refused to strike him. He said to him: "Because you would not listen to the word of the Lord, behold, as you depart from me, a lion shall strike you." And when he had departed a little way from him, a lion found him and killed him. Finding another man, he said: "Strike me." And he struck him and wounded him. So the prophet departed and met the king on the road, and changed his appearance by a bandage over his eyes. As the king passed by, he cried out to the king and said: "Your servant went out into the midst of the battle, and when a certain man had fled, someone brought him to me and said: 'Guard this man; if he goes missing, your life shall be for his life, or you shall pay a talent of silver.' While I, being troubled, turned here and there, suddenly he was gone." The king of Israel said to him: "This is your judgment, which you yourself have decided." Then he immediately took the bandage from his face, and the king of Israel recognized that he was one of the prophets. He said to him: "Thus says the Lord: Because you have let a man worthy of death escape from your hand, your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people." The king of Israel returned to his house, scorning to listen, and came into Samaria in a rage.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Decorative initial P in red and blue ink.</image-desc>

## After
these words, at that time, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, near the palace of the king of Samaria. Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying: "Give me your vineyard so that I may make a vegetable garden of it, because it is near and close to my house; and I will give you a better vineyard for it, or if you think it more convenient, I will give you the price in silver that it is worth." Naboth answered him: "The Lord be merciful to me, that I should not give the inheritance of my fathers to you." Ahab went into his house indignant and gnashing his teeth <note>original: "frendens," expressing intense frustration or anger</note> because of the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, saying: "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And casting himself upon his bed, he turned his face to the wall and would not eat bread. But Jezebel his wife came in to him and said to him: "What is this, that your soul is so dismayed, and why do you eat no bread?" He answered her: "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him: 'Give me your vineyard for money, or if it pleases you, I will give you a vineyard for it.' And he said: 'I will not give you my vineyard.'" Jezebel his wife then said to him: "You are of great authority, and you rule the kingdom of Israel well. Rise and eat bread, and be of good cheer; I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite." So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name and sealed them with his ring, and sent them to the elders and the leading men who were in his city and lived with Naboth. This was the substance of the letters: "Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth among the chief of the people, and bring in two men, sons of Belial <note>A Hebrew term meaning "worthless" or "wicked" men, used here to describe false witnesses.</note>, against him, and let them bear false witness, saying: 'He has cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him, and so let him die." The citizens, the elders, and the leading men who lived with him in the city did as Jezebel had commanded them and as it was written in the letters she had sent to them. They proclaimed a fast and set Naboth among the chief of the people. And bringing in two men, sons of Belial, they made them sit opposite him. And they—the men of Belial—spoke the testimony against him before the multitude: "Naboth has cursed God and the king." For this reason, they led him outside the city and killed him with stones. They sent word to Jezebel, saying: "Naboth has been stoned and is dead." It happened that when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned and dead, she spoke to Ahab: "Rise and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he would not yield to you for money; for Naboth is not alive, but dead." When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he rose up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.

<image-desc>Decorative initial F in red and blue ink with fine penwork.</image-desc>

## And it happened
that the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: "Rise and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is going down to the vineyard of Naboth to take possession of it. And you shall speak to him, saying: 'Thus says the Lord: You have killed, and moreover, you have taken possession.' And again you shall say: 'Thus says the Lord: In this place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth, they shall also lick your blood.'" Ahab said to Elijah: "Have you found me, my enemy?" And he said: "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the Lord. Behold, I will bring evil upon you and will cut off your posterity; and I will kill from Ahab every male <note>original: "mingente(m) ad parietem," a biblical idiom for all males.</note>, whether shut up or left in Israel. And I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have chosen to provoke me to anger and have made Israel to sin." But the Lord also spoke concerning Jezebel, saying: "The dogs shall eat Jezebel in the field of Jezreel. If Ahab dies in the city, the dogs shall eat him; if he dies in the field, the birds of the air shall eat him." Truly, there was never another like Ahab, who sold himself to do evil in the sight of the Lord; for Jezebel his wife incited him. And he became abominable, so much so that he followed the idols which the Amorites made, whom the Lord consumed before the face of the children of Israel. Therefore, when Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted, and slept in sackcloth, and walked with his head bowed down. Then the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself for my sake, I will not bring the evil in his days, but in the days of his son I will bring the evil upon his house." Three years passed without war between Syria and Israel. In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel. The king of Israel said to his servants: "Do you not know that Ramoth-Gilead is ours, and we neglect to take it out of the hand of the king of Syria?" And he said to Jehoshaphat: "Will you come with me to battle at Ramoth-Gilead?" Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: "As I am, so are you. My people are your people, and my horsemen are your horsemen." Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel: "I pray you, consult the word of the Lord first today." So the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said to them: "Should I go to Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or should I remain at peace?" They answered: "Go up, and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king." But Jehoshaphat said: "Is there not here some prophet of the Lord, that we might inquire through him?" The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "There remains one man through whom we might consult the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but evil: Micaiah the son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said: "Let not the king say so." Therefore, the king of Israel called a certain eunuch and said to him: "Hurry and bring Micaiah the son of Imlah." The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, dressed in royal attire, in an open area near the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah also made iron horns for himself and said: "Thus says the Lord: With these you shall gore the Syrians until you have destroyed them." All the prophets prophesied similarly, saying: "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and prosper, for the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king." The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying: "Behold, the words of the prophets with one voice predict good things for the king; let your word, therefore, be like theirs, and speak good things." Micaiah said to him: "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak." So he came to the king, and the king said to him: "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or should we stop?" He answered him: "Go up and prosper, and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king." And the king said to him: "Again and again I adjure you, that you tell me nothing but what is true in the name of the Lord." And he said: "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. And the Lord said: 'These have no master; let each one return to his house in peace.'" Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good for me, but always evil?" But Micaiah added: "Therefore hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and the whole host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left. And the Lord said: 'Who shall deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?' And one said one thing, and another said another."

<summary>This page recounts Elisha's calling, the military victories of Israel over Syria, and the tragic judicial murder of Naboth orchestrated by Jezebel. It concludes with Micaiah's dire prophecy of Ahab's death in the upcoming battle for Ramoth-Gilead.</summary>

<meta>This page continues from the previous narrative where King Ahab of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah form an alliance. The text moves from the prophetic warnings of Micaiah regarding the battle at Ramoth-gilead to the death of Ahab, the reign of his successor Ahaziah, and the dramatic transition of prophetic authority from Elijah to Elisha.</meta>

The king of Israel went out before the Lord and said: "Gather to me all the prophets so they may tell me: should I go to Ramoth-gilead to battle or should I remain at peace?" They said: "Go up, and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king." But Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, said: "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here through whom we might inquire?" The king of Israel said: "There remains one man through whom we can inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but evil: Micaiah, the son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said: "Let the king not say such things." So the king of Israel sent a eunuch and said: "Hasten, bring Micaiah the son of Imlah." Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, were each sitting on his throne, dressed in royal robes in an open space near the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying in their presence. Also, Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said: "Thus says the Lord: With these you shall gore Syria until you destroy them." All the prophets likewise prophesied, saying: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and be victorious, for the Lord will deliver it into the king’s hand."

The messenger who had gone to Micaiah spoke to him, saying: "Behold, the words of the prophets with one voice predict good things for the king; let your word, therefore, be like theirs, and speak good things." But Micaiah said: "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak." So he came to the king, and the king said to him: "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or should we remain at peace?" He answered him: "Go up and be victorious, and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king." The king said: "Again and again I adjure you, that you tell me nothing but what is true in the name of the Lord." Then he said: "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. And the Lord said: 'These have no master; let each one return to his house in peace.'" Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good for me, but evil?"

But Micaiah said: "Therefore hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting upon His throne, and the entire host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left. And the Lord said: 'Who will deceive Ahab, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said this, and another said that. Then a spirit came forward and stood before the Lord and said: 'I will deceive him.' The Lord said to him: 'In what way?' And he said: 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And the Lord said: 'You shall deceive him and you shall prevail; go out and do so.' Now, therefore, behold, the Lord has put a spirit of lying in the mouth of all these your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."

Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek, saying: "Has the spirit of the Lord left me to speak to you?" And Micaiah said: "You shall see on that day when you enter a chamber within a chamber to hide yourself." The king of Israel said: "Take Micaiah and let him stay with Amon, the governor of the city, and with Joash, the son of Amalech, and tell them: 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him with the bread of affliction and the water of anguish, until I return in peace.'" Micaiah said: "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken through me." And he said: "Hear, all you people!"

So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went up to Ramoth-gilead. The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Take up arms and enter the battle, and put on your own robes." But the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle. Now the king of Syria had commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying: "You shall not fight with small or great, but only against the king of Israel." Therefore, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they suspected that he was the king of Israel, and they turned to fight against him. And Jehoshaphat cried out. Then the captains of the chariots realized he was not the king of Israel, and they ceased pursuing him.

But a certain man drew his bow at a venture, aiming his arrow, and by chance he struck the king of Israel between the lungs and the stomach. And the king said to his charioteer: "Turn your hand and carry me out of the army, for I am gravely wounded." The battle raged that day, and the king of Israel stood in his chariot against the Syrians, and he died in the evening. The blood of his wound flowed into the bottom of the chariot, and a herald proclaimed throughout the whole army before the sun set, saying: "Let every man return to his city and his own land." So the king died and was carried to Samaria, and they buried him in Samaria. And they washed his chariot in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, and they washed the reins <note>original: "habenas," refers to the leather straps or harness</note> according to the word which the Lord had spoken. As for the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house <note>Archaeological evidence has confirmed the existence of ivory-inlaid furniture and paneling in Samaria from this period.</note> that he built, and all the cities he constructed, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel? So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

<margin>3 Kings 22</margin>Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, king of Israel. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi. He walked in all the ways of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from them. He did what was right in the sight of the Lord. Nevertheless, the high places <note>term for local sacrificial shrines used before the centralization of worship in Jerusalem.</note> were not taken away, for the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. Jehoshaphat also had peace with the king of Israel. As for the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his mighty deeds and the battles he fought, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? He also removed from the land the remnant of the cult prostitutes <note>original: "effeminatorum," referring to those involved in pagan ritual practices.</note> who remained from the days of his father Asa. At that time there was no king appointed in Edom. King Jehoshaphat had built a fleet of ships at sea to sail to Ophir for gold, but they could not go, for they were wrecked at Ezion-geber. Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat: "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat would not. Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David his father. And Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned over Israel for two years. He did evil in the sight of the Lord and walked in the way of his father and his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin. He also served Baal and worshiped him, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done.

**Now Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died. And Ahaziah fell...**

<margin>77.</margin>Now Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died. And Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper chamber which he had in Samaria, and he was injured. He sent messengers, saying to them: "Go and consult Baal-zebub <note>Literally "Lord of the Flies," the god of the Philistine city of Ekron.</note>, the god of Ekron, whether I shall recover from this infirmity." But the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?' Therefore thus says the Lord: From the bed upon which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die." And Elijah went away.

The messengers returned to the king, and he said to them: "Why have you returned?" They answered him: "A man came to meet us and said to us: 'Go and return to the king who sent you, and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you send to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore, from the bed upon which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die.'" He said to them: "What was the appearance and dress of the man who met you and spoke these words?" They said: "A hairy man, with a leather belt girded around his loins." And he said: "It is Elijah the Tishbite."

Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. He went up to him while he was sitting on the top of a hill and said: "Man of God, the king commands you to come down." Elijah answered and said to the captain: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." So fire came down from heaven and devoured him and the fifty who were with him.

<column-break/>

And the king sent again another captain of fifty and the fifty over whom he presided. When he came to him, he fell on his knees before Elijah and said: "Man of God, do not despise my life and the lives of your servants who are with me. Behold, fire came down from heaven and devoured the two previous captains of fifty and the hundred who were with them. But I beseech you to have mercy on my life." Then the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah, saying: "Go down with him; do not be afraid." So he arose and went down with him to the king and spoke to him: "Thus says the Lord: Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel from whom you could inquire of his word, therefore from the bed upon which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die."

So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram his brother reigned in his place in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, for he had no son. As for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?

Now it happened, when the Lord was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, that Elijah and Elisha were going from Gilgal. Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." And when they had gone down to Bethel, the sons of the prophets <note>A guild or community of prophets living together in various cities.</note> who were in Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him: "Do you know that today the Lord will take away your master from you?" He answered: "I also know it. Be silent." Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he said: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." And when they had come to Jericho, the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him: "Do you know that today the Lord will take away your master from you?" And he said: "I also know it. Be silent." Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to the Jordan." He said: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you."

So they both went on together, and fifty men of the sons of the prophets followed them and stood at a distance opposite them. But the two of them stood by the Jordan. Elijah took his mantle, rolled it up, and struck the waters, which were divided to one side and the other, and they both crossed over on dry ground. When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha: "Ask what you want me to do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said: "I beseech you, let a double portion of your spirit be upon me." He answered: "You have asked a difficult thing. Nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be as you asked; but if you do not see me, it shall not be."

As they continued walking and talking, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. Elisha saw it and cried out: "My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and its driver!" And he saw him no more. He took hold of his own clothes and tore them into two pieces. Then he picked up the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him and, returning, stood upon the bank of the Jordan. He struck the waters with the mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him, but they were not divided. And he said: "Where is the God of Elijah even now?" He struck the waters again, and they were divided this way and that, and Elisha crossed over.

When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from a distance, they said: "The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha." And coming to meet him, they bowed down to the ground before him. They said to him: "Behold, there are fifty strong men with your servants who can go and seek your master, lest perhaps the spirit of the Lord has taken him up and cast him on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." He said: "Do not send them." But they urged him until he yielded and said: "Send them." So they sent fifty men, who sought for three days but did not find him. They returned to him while he was staying in Jericho, and he said to them: "Did I not tell you, 'Do not go'?"

The men of the city said to Elisha: "Behold, the situation of this city is excellent, as you yourself, my lord, can see; but the waters are very bad and the land is barren." He said: "Bring me a new jar and put salt in it." When they had brought it, he went out to the spring of waters, threw the salt into it, and said: "Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters, and there shall no longer be death or barrenness in them." So the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.

Then he went up from there to Bethel. And as he was going up by the way, small boys came out of the city and mocked him, saying: "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!" When he looked back and saw them, he cursed them in the name of the Lord. And two bears came out of the forest and mangled forty-two of the boys. From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

Now Jehoram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned twelve years and did evil before the Lord, but not like his father and mother. For he removed the statues of Baal which his father had made; nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, and did not depart from them. Now Mesha, king of Moab, was a breeder of many animals, and he paid to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams with their wool. But when Ahab died, he broke the covenant he had with the king of Israel. Therefore King Jehoram went out of Samaria on that day and mustered all Israel. He sent to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, saying: "The king of Moab has revolted from me. Come with me to battle against him." He answered: "I will go up. What is mine is yours; my people are your people, and my horses are your horses." And he asked: "By which way shall we go up?" He answered: "Through the desert of Edom."

So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out. They traveled in a circuitous way for seven days, and there was no water for the army or the animals that followed them. The king of Israel said: "Alas, alas, alas! The Lord has gathered these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab." But Jehoshaphat said: "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, so that we may entreat the Lord through him?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered: "Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah." Jehoshaphat said: "The word of the Lord is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him. Elisha said to the king of Israel: "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and your mother." But the king of Israel said to him: "Why has the Lord gathered these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab?" Elisha said to him: "As the Lord of hosts lives, in whose presence I stand, if I did not respect the presence of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would not even look at you or notice you. But now, bring me a musician." While the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon him, and he said: "Thus says the Lord: Make..."

**A certain woman** of the wives of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the Lord; and behold, the creditor has come to take my two sons to be his slaves." Elisha said to her, "What do you want me to do for you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?" And she replied, "Your handmaid has nothing in my house except a little oil with which to anoint myself." And he said, "Go, borrow empty vessels from all your neighbors—not a few. Then go in and shut the door when you and your sons are inside, and pour from the oil into all these vessels; and when they are full, set them aside." So the woman went and shut the door upon herself and her sons. They brought the vessels, and she poured. And when the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he replied, "I have no more." Then the oil stopped flowing. And she came and told the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your creditor; then you and your sons may live on the rest."

**It happened** one day that Elisha passed through Shunem. And there was a great woman there <note>meaning a woman of high social status or wealth</note>, who persuaded him to eat bread. And as often as he passed by, he turned in to her to eat bread. And she said to her husband, "I perceive that this is a holy man of God who passes by us frequently. Let us make a small upper room for him and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand in it for him, so that when he comes to us, he may stay there." So it happened one day that he came and turned into the upper room and rested there. And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite." When he had called her and she stood before him, he said to his servant, "Say to her: 'Behold, you have been careful to serve us in all these ways; what do you want me to do for you? Do you have any business or wish for me to speak to the king or the commander of the army?'" She replied, "I dwell among my own people." And he said, "What then does she want me to do for her?" And Gehazi said, "Do not ask; she has no son, and her husband is old." Therefore, he commanded him to call her. When she had been called and stood at the door, he said to her, "At this time next year, if life continues, you shall have a son in your womb." But she replied, "Do not, I pray you, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your handmaid." And the woman conceived and bore a son at that very time and hour that Elisha had said. But the child grew. And it happened one day, when he had gone out to his father among the reapers, he said to his father, "My head aches, my head aches!" And he said to a servant, "Take him and lead him to his mother." When he had taken him and led him to his mother, she set him on her knees until midday, and he died. Then she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door, and went out and called her husband, saying, "Send me, I pray you, one of the servants and a donkey, that I may run to the man of God and return." He said to her, "Why are you going to him? Today is neither the new moon nor the Sabbath." She replied, "I will go." And she saddled the donkey and commanded the servant, "Drive and press on; do not slow down for me in going unless I tell you." So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Behold, that Shunammite. Go to meet her and say to her: 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with your son?'" She said, "It is well." And when she came to the man of God on the mountain, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Let her alone, for her soul is in bitterness, and the Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me." Then she said, "Did I ask a son of my lord? Did I not say to you, 'Do not deceive me'?" And he said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins and take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet any man, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him; and lay my staff upon the face of the child." But the mother of the child said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So he arose and followed her. Gehazi had gone on before them and had laid the staff upon the face of the child, but there was neither voice nor sense. He returned to meet him and reported to him, saying, "The child has not awakened." Then Elisha entered the house, and behold, the child lay dead upon his bed. He went in, shut the door upon the two of them, and prayed to the Lord. And he went up and lay upon the child; he put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands, and he bowed himself over him, and the flesh of the child grew warm. Then he returned and walked once to and fro in the house. And he went up and bowed himself over him; and the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes. And he called Gehazi and said to him, "Call this Shunammite." When she was called, she went in to him. And he said, "Take up your son." She came and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground; then she took up her son and went out.

**And** Elisha returned to Gilgal. Now there was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets dwelt before him. And he said to one of his servants, "Put on the large pot and cook stew for the sons of the prophets." One went out into the field to gather wild herbs and found something like a wild vine, and gathered from it wild gourds <term>colocynthidas: the bitter apple, which is purgative and toxic in large amounts</term> and filled his cloak. He returned and sliced them into the pot of stew, for he did not know what they were. Then they poured it out for the men to eat. But when they had tasted the cooked food, they cried out, saying, "There is death in the pot, O man of God!" and they could not eat it. But he said, "Bring flour." When they had brought it, he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people that they may eat." And there was no more bitterness in the pot.

**A certain man** came from Baal-shalisha bringing the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty barley loaves, and new grain in his sack. But Elisha said, "Give it to the people that they may eat." And his minister <note>servant or attendant</note> replied, "How much is this, that I should set it before a hundred men?" Again he said, "Give it to the people that they may eat; for thus says the Lord: 'They shall eat, and there shall be some left over.'" So he set it before them; and they ate, and some was left over, according to the word of the Lord.

**Naaman**, commander of the army of the King of Syria, was a great man with his lord and highly honored, because through him the Lord had given deliverance to Syria. He was a brave and wealthy man, but he was a leper. Now, raiding parties had gone out from Syria and had led away a young girl captive from the land of Israel, who served Naaman's wife. She said to her mistress, "If only my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! He would surely cure him of the leprosy he has." So Naaman went in to his lord and told him, saying, "Thus and so spoke the girl from the land of Israel." And the King of Syria said, "Go, and I will send a letter to the King of Israel." When he had departed, he took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing. He brought the letter to the King of Israel, which said: "When you receive this letter, know that I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may cure him of his leprosy." When the King of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, that I can kill and give life, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Note and see how he seeks a quarrel against me!" When Elisha the man of God heard that the King of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to him, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel." So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha's house. And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall be restored to health, and you shall be clean." But Naaman was angry and went away, saying, "I thought that he would surely come out to me and stand and call upon the name of the Lord his God, and touch the place of leprosy with his hand and cure me. Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel, that I might wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage. But his servants came near and spoke to him: "Father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, surely you would have done it. How much more, then, when he says to you: 'Wash, and be clean'?" So he went down and washed in the Jordan seven times according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was cleansed. Then he returned to the man of God with all his company; he came and stood before him and said, "Truly I know that there is no other God in all the earth except in Israel. Therefore, I pray you, accept a gift from your servant." But he replied, "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it." And though he urged him, he would not agree. Then Naaman said, "As you wish. But I pray you, let there be given to me, your servant, as much earth as two mules can carry; for your servant will no longer offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to foreign gods, but only to the Lord. But in this one thing may the Lord pardon your servant: when my master enters the temple of Rimmon to worship, leaning on my hand, if I bow in the temple of Rimmon when my master worships in that same place, may the Lord forgive your servant for this thing." And Elisha said to him, "Go in peace." So he departed from him for a distance. But Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, said, "My lord has spared Naaman this Syrian, by not receiving from him what he brought. As the Lord lives, I will run after him and take something from him." So Gehazi followed after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he climbed down from his chariot to meet him and said, "Is all well?" And he said, "All is well. My lord has sent me to you, saying: 'Just now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'" Naaman said, "It is better that you take two talents." And he urged him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags with two changes of clothes, and laid them on two of his servants, who carried them before him. When it was evening, he took them from their hands and put them away in the house; then he dismissed the men and they departed. But he went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He replied, "Your servant went nowhere." But he said, "Was not my heart present when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Now you have accepted silver and clothes, to buy olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and oxen, and male and female servants. Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring forever." And he went out from his presence a leper, white as snow.

**The sons** of the prophets said to Elisha, "Behold, the place where we dwell before you is too cramped for us. Let us go to the Jordan, and let each of us take a beam from the woods, so that we may build a place for ourselves to live there." He said, "Go." And one of them said, "Come with your servants." He replied, "I will come." So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down wood. But it happened that as one was felling a beam, the iron head of the axe fell into the water. And he cried out and said, "Alas, alas, my lord! And it was borrowed!" But the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. Then he cut a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron floated. And he said, "Take it up." So he reached out his hand and took it.

**Now the King** of Syria was warring against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "In such and such a place let us lay an ambush." Then the man of God sent to the King of Israel, saying, "Beware that you do not pass that place, for the Syrians are in ambush there." So the King of Israel sent to the place that the man of God had told him, and he occupied it and watched himself there more than once or twice. And the heart of the King of Syria was troubled by this thing; and calling his servants together, he said, "Why do you not tell me who is the traitor among us to the King of Israel?" And one of his servants said, "No, my lord king; but Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, tells the King of Israel everything."

The armies of Syria had gone out and had taken captive from the land of Israel a little girl, who was in the service of Naaman’s wife. And he brought the letter to the King of Israel, with these words: "When you receive this letter, know that I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy." And when the King of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said: "Am I God, that I can kill and give life, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? When Elisha, the man of God, had heard this—namely, that the King of Israel had torn his clothes—he sent to him, saying: "Why have you torn your clothes? Naaman, being angry, went away, saying: "I thought that he would surely come out to me, and standing, would call upon the name of the Lord his God, and touch the place of the leprosy with his hand, and cure me. Are not the Abana and the Pharphar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel, that I might wash in them and be made clean?" When he had turned and was going away in indignation, his servants came to him and said to him: "Father, even if the prophet had told you to do something great, you certainly ought to have done it; how much more now that he has said to you: 'Wash and be clean'?" He went down and washed in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was made clean. And returning to the man of God with his whole company, he came and stood before him, and said: "Truly I know that there is no other God in all the earth, except only in Israel. But he replied: "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it." And though he urged him, he utterly refused. And Naaman said: "As you wish. This thing alone is there for which you shall pray to the Lord for your servant: when my master enters the temple of Rimmon <note>a Syrian deity</note> to worship, and he leans on my hand, if I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, while he worships in that same place, may the Lord forgive me, your servant, for this thing." And he said to him: "Go in peace." So he departed from him in the chosen time of the land.

To this, Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, replied: "My lord has spared Naaman this Syrian, by not receiving from him what he brought. As the Lord lives, I will run after him and take something from him." And Gehazi followed after Naaman's back. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he leaped down from his chariot to meet him, and said: "Is all well?" And he said: "It is well. My lord has sent me to you, saying: 'Just now two young men from the hill country of Ephraim, of the sons of the prophets, have come to me. Give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.'" And Naaman said: "It is better that you take two talents." And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and laid them upon two of his servants, who carried them before him. When they had already come in the evening, he took them from their hands and stored them in the house. And he dismissed the men, and they departed. But he himself went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him: "From where do you come, Gehazi?" He replied: "Your servant went nowhere." But he said: "Was my heart not present when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Now, therefore, you have received silver and received clothing, to buy olive groves and vineyards and sheep and oxen and menservants and maidservants. But the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your offspring forever." And he went out from him a leper, white as snow.

And when the sons of the prophets came to Elisha, they said: "Behold, the place in which we live before you is too narrow for us. Let us go as far as the Jordan, and let each of us take a beam from the woods, so that we may build for ourselves a place to live there." He said: "Go." And one of them said: "Come then, you also, with your servants." He replied: "I will come." And he went with them. When they had come to the Jordan, they were cutting wood. It happened, however, that while one was felling a beam, the iron of his axe fell into the water. And he cried out and said: "Alas, alas, alas, my lord! And this very thing I had borrowed." But the man of God said: "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. So he cut a piece of wood and threw it there; and the iron floated. And he said: "Take it up." And he stretched out his hand and took it.

When the King of Syria heard these things, he was at war against Israel, and took counsel with his servants, saying: "In such and such a place let us lay an ambush." Therefore, the man of God sent to the King of Israel, saying: "Beware that you do not pass through that place, for the Syrians are there in ambush." So the King of Israel sent to the place that the man of God had told him, and occupied it. And he saved himself there not once or twice. And the heart of the King of Syria was troubled by this matter. And having called together his servants, he said: "Why do you not tell me who is the traitor among us to the King of Israel?" And one of his servants said: "By no means, my lord king; but Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, tells the King of Israel all the words that you speak in your bedchamber." And he said to them: "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and capture him." And it was reported to him, saying: "Behold, he is in Dothan." He sent there horses and chariots and a strong part of the army. When they had come by night, they surrounded the city. Rising at dawn, the minister of the man of God went out and saw the army surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. And he reported it to him, saying: "Alas, alas, alas, my lord, what shall we do?" But he replied: "Do not fear; for there are more with us than with them." And when Elisha had prayed, he said: "Lord, open the eyes of this man so that he may see." And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha. And the enemies descended toward him. For which Elisha prayed to the Lord, saying: "Strike, I beseech you, this people with blindness." And the Lord struck them so they could not see, according to the words of Elisha. But Elisha said to them: "This is not the way, nor is this the city. Follow me, and I will show you the man you seek." And he led them into Samaria. When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said: "Lord, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see." And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw themselves to be in the middle of Samaria. And the King of Israel said to the man of God when he saw them: "Shall I strike them down, my father?" But he said: "You shall not strike them. For you did not capture them with your sword or your bow, that you should strike them. But set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink, and go to their master." And a great feast was set before them; and after they had eaten and drunk, he dismissed them. And they went to their master, and the raiders of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.

But this is what happened afterward: Ben-hadad, the King of Syria, gathered his whole army and went up and besieged Samaria. And there was a great famine in Samaria; and it was besieged for so long that the head of a donkey was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a *cab* <note>a dry measure of about 2 liters</note> of dove's dung for five pieces of silver. And as the King of Israel was passing by on the wall, a certain woman cried out to him, saying: "Save me, my lord king!" He said: "If the Lord does not save you, from where can I save you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?" And the king said to her: "What do you want?" She replied: "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.' So we boiled my son and ate him. And I said to her the next day, 'Give up your son so that we may eat him,' but she has hidden her son." When the king had heard this, he tore his clothes and passed along the wall. And all the people saw the haircloth <note>sackcloth worn as a sign of mourning or penance</note> which he wore next to his flesh inside. And the king said: "May God do this to me and add more to it, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on him today." But Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. So he sent a man ahead. And before that messenger arrived, he said to the elders: "Do you know that this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door, and do not let him enter. For behold, the sound of his master's feet is behind him." While he was still speaking with them, the messenger appeared and came to him and said: "Behold, such great evil is from the Lord; what more shall I hope from the Lord?"

But Elisha said: "Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: 'At this time tomorrow, a measure of fine flour shall be sold for a stater <note>a Greek silver coin</note>, and two measures of barley for a stater, in the gate of Samaria.'" One of the commanders, on whose hand the king leaned, replied to the man of God and said: "Even if the Lord made floodgates in heaven, could this thing be that you speak?" He said: "You shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat of it." Now there were four leprous men near the entrance of the gate of Samaria, who said to one another: "Why do we want to stay here until we die? If we want to enter the city, we shall die of famine; if we remain here, we must die. Come, therefore, and let us desert to the camp of Syria. If they spare us, we shall live. If they choose to kill us, we shall die regardless." So they rose in the evening to come to the Syrian camp. When they had come to the edge of the Syrian camp, they found no one there. For indeed the Lord had made a sound in the camp of Syria of chariots and horses and a very great army. And they said to one another: "Behold, the King of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the Egyptians, and they have come upon us." Therefore they rose and fled in the darkness, and left behind their tents and horses and mules and donkeys in the camp; they fled, desiring only to save their lives. When those men came to the edge of the camp, they entered one tent and ate and drank; and they took from there gold and silver and clothes, and went and hid them. They returned again to another tent, and taking things from there likewise, they hid them. And they said to one another: "We are not doing right; for this is a day of good news. If we keep silent and do not want to report it until dawn, we will be accused of a crime; let us go and report it in the king's court." When they had come to the gate of the city, they told them, saying: "We went to the camp of Syria, and found no man there, only horses and donkeys tied, and the tents fixed." Then the messengers went and reported it inside the king's court. He rose in the night and said to his servants: "I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are suffering from famine, and therefore they have gone out of the camp and hidden in the fields, saying: 'When they have gone out of the city, we shall capture them alive, and then we shall enter the way of the city.'" But one of his servants replied and said: "Let us take five horses that remain in the city—for they are all that are left of the multitude of Israel, the others having been consumed—and by sending them we shall be able to explore." So they brought two horses, and the king sent to the camp of the Syrians, saying: "Go and see." They went after them as far as the Jordan. And behold, the whole way was full of clothes and vessels, which the Syrians had thrown away when they were panicked. And the messengers returned and told the king. The people went out and plundered the camp of Syria; and a measure of fine flour was sold for a stater, and two measures of barley for a stater, according to the word of the Lord. Furthermore, the king had appointed that commander on whose hand he leaned to be at the gate; he was trampled by the multitude and died, just as the man of God had spoken when the king came down to him. And it happened according to the word of the man of God which he had spoken to the king, when he said: "Two measures of barley shall be for one stater, and a measure of fine flour for one stater, at this same time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria." But that commander had replied to the man of God and said: "If the Lord made floodgates in heaven, could this be that you speak?" And he said: "You shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat of it." So it happened to him as had been predicted, and the people trampled him in the gate and he died.

<column-break/>

...they were fine and he had borrowed them from a woman of his helpers. And he revealed everything to her in his house. And he said: "Let it be done." But the king went according to the word of the man of God and said: "Now may your way live, and may all things you do follow happily." And when Gehazi wished to tell how he had raised the dead to life, the woman appeared whose son he had restored to life, crying out to the king for her house and for her fields. And Gehazi said: "My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha raised up." And the woman confessed to the king, and she told everything. And the king said to one of the eunuch officers, saying: "Restore to her all things that are hers, and all the income of the fields from the day she left the land until the present."

To this, the King of Israel and Jehoshaphat, the King of Judah, sat each on his throne, dressed in royal attire, in the open space near the entrance of the gate of Samaria. And all the prophets were prophesying in their sight. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made for himself iron horns and said: "Thus says the Lord: With these you shall gore Syria until you destroy it." And all the prophets prophesied similarly, saying: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and you shall prosper; and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hand." But the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying: "Behold, the words of the prophets with one voice predict good things for the king. Let your word, therefore, be like theirs, and speak good things." Micaiah said to him: "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak." So he came to the king. And the king said to him: "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or should we refrain?" To which he replied: "Go up and go prosperously, and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hand." And the king said to him: "Again and again I adjure you that you speak nothing to me but what is true in the name of the Lord." But he said: "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep not having a shepherd." And the Lord said: "These have no master; let each one return to his house in peace." And the King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good things to me but always evil?" But he added: "Therefore hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right and on his left. And the Lord said: 'Who will deceive Ahab, the King of Israel, so that he may go up and fall in Ramoth-gilead?' And one said words of this sort, and another otherwise. But a spirit came forth and stood before the Lord and said: 'I will deceive him.' To whom the Lord spoke: 'In what way?' And he said: 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And the Lord said: 'You shall deceive and you shall prevail. Go out and do so.' Now, therefore, behold, the Lord has put a spirit of lying in the mouth of all your prophets; and the Lord has spoken evil against you." Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said: "By which way did the spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?" And Micaiah said: "You shall see on that day when you enter into a chamber within a chamber <note>meaning an inner room</note> to hide yourself." And the King of Israel said: "Take Micaiah, and let him stay with Amon the prince of the city and with Joash the son of Amelech; and you shall say to them: 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and sustain him with the bread of affliction and the water of distress until I return in peace.'" And Micaiah said: "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken through me." And he said: "Hear, all you people!" So the King of Israel and Jehoshaphat the King of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead. And the King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Take your armor and enter the battle, and put on your clothes. But the King of Israel changed his attire and entered the war." Now the King of Syria had commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying: "You shall not fight against the small or the great, but against the King of Israel alone." When the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they thought he was the King of Israel, and making an attack, they fought against him. And Jehoshaphat cried out. And the captains of the chariots saw that he was not the King of Israel, and they turned away from him. A certain man drew his bow, directing an arrow at random <note>original: "in incertum," meaning aimlessly or without a specific target</note>, and struck the King of Israel between the lungs and the stomach. But he said to his chariot driver: "Turn your hand and carry me out of the army, because I am gravely wounded." So the battle was joined on that day, and the King of Israel stood in his chariot against the Syrians and died in the evening. And the blood of the wound flowed into the floor of the chariot. and a herald's voice rang through the whole army before the sun set, saying: "Let every man return to his city and to his land." So the king died and was brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria. And they washed his chariot in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked his blood, and they washed the reins, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken. As for the rest of the words of Ahab and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he constructed, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel? So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him: "Gird your loins, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead. When you arrive there, you shall see Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi; and entering, you shall raise him up from the midst of his brothers and lead him into an inner chamber. And taking the flask of oil, you shall pour it over his head and say: 'Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then you shall open the door and flee, and you shall not stay there." So the young man, the servant of the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead and entered there. And behold, the captains of the army were sitting; and he said: "I have a word for you, O captain." And Jehu said: "To which of all of us?" And he said: "To you, O captain." And he rose and entered the chamber. But he poured the oil over his head and said: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the Lord, Israel. And you shall strike the house of Ahab your lord, so that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezebel. And I will destroy the whole house of Ahab, and I will kill of Ahab every male <note>original: "mingentem ad parietem," literally "one who urinates against a wall"</note>, both the bond and the free in Israel. And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah. Also, the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the field of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her." And he opened the door and fled. Jehu then came out to the servants of his lord. They said to him: "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" He said to them: "You know the man and what he said." But they replied: "It is false. Tell us instead." He said to them: "Thus and so he spoke to me, and said: 'Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.'" So they hurried, and each one taking his cloak, they laid them under his feet in the likeness of a tribunal <note>a raised platform</note>; and they sounded the trumpet and said: "Jehu is king!" So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram was besieging Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael the King of Syria. And he had returned to be cured in Jezreel of his wounds, because the Syrians had struck him while he fought against Hazael the King of Syria. And Jehu said: "If it pleases you, let no one go out as a fugitive from the city, lest he go and tell it in Jezreel." And he mounted and set out for Jezreel. For Joram was lying ill there, and Ahaziah the King of Judah had come down to visit Joram. Therefore the watchman who stood upon the tower of Jezreel saw the troop of Jehu coming, and said: "I see a troop." And Joram said: "Take a chariot and send to meet them, and let the rider say: 'Is all well?'" So one who had mounted a chariot went to meet him and said: "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said: "What have you to do with peace? Turn and follow me." The watchman also reported, saying: "The messenger came to them and does not return." He sent also a second chariot with horses, and it came to them and said: "Thus says the king: 'Is there peace?'" And Jehu said: "What have you to do with peace? Turn and follow me." Then the watchman reported, saying: "He has reached them and does not return. But the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives headlong." And Joram said: "Yoke the chariot." And they yoked his chariot. And Joram the King of Israel and Ahaziah the King of Judah went out, each in his own chariot. And they went out to meet Jehu, and they found him in the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. When Joram saw Jehu, he said: "Is it peace, Jehu?" But he replied: "What peace? While the fornications of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries are still flourishing." And Joram turned his hand and fled, and said to Ahaziah: "Treachery, Ahaziah!" But Jehu drew his bow with his hand and struck Joram between the shoulders, and the arrow went out through his heart, and he collapsed in his chariot. And Jehu said to Bidkar his captain: "Take him and throw him in the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. For remember when you and I sat in a chariot following Ahab his father, that the Lord laid this burden upon him, saying: 'If I do not, for the blood of Naboth and for the blood of his sons which I saw yesterday, says the Lord, repay you in this field, says the Lord.' Now therefore take and throw him into the field according to the word of the Lord." Ahaziah the King of Judah, seeing this, fled by the way of the garden house. And Jehu pursued him and said: "Strike this man also in his chariot." And they struck him on the ascent of Gur, which is near Ibleam. He fled into Megiddo and died there. And his servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the City of David. In the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah reigned over Judah. And Jehu came into Jezreel. Now Jezebel, having heard of his entrance, painted her eyes with antimony <note>makeup</note> and adorned her head, and looked out through the window at Jehu entering through the gate, and said: "Can there be peace for Zimri, who killed his master?" <note>Zimri was a previous usurper who lasted only seven days</note> Jehu lifted his face to the window and said: "Who is this?" And two or three eunuchs leaned out. To whom he said: "Throw her down." And they threw her down, and the wall was splashed with blood, and the hooves of the horses trampled her. When he had entered to eat and drink, he said: "Go and see that cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter." But when they went to bury her, they found nothing but the skull and the feet and the tips of the hands. And returning, they told him. And Jehu said: "It is the word of the Lord, which he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying: 'In the field of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel; and the flesh of Jezebel shall be like dung upon the face of the earth in the field of Jezreel, so that those passing by shall say: Is this that Jezebel?'"

Is all well? And he said: "It is well."

<summary>This page recounts the influential career of the prophet Elisha, from the healing of Naaman the Syrian to the miraculous end of the siege of Samaria. It concludes with the violent downfall of the house of Ahab as Jehu is anointed king and executes Joram, Ahaziah, and the infamous Queen Jezebel.</summary>
