->Unto the end, for Jeduthun, a psalm of Asaph.<-
<margin>V</margin>
I cried to the Lord with my voice: with my voice to God, and he gave heed to me. In the day of my trouble I sought God: with my hands in the night before him: and I was not deceived. My soul refused to be comforted: I was mindful of God and was delighted, and I was exercised: and my spirit fainted. My eyes anticipated the watches: I was troubled and I spoke not. I thought upon the days of old: and I had in my mind the eternal years. 
And I meditated in the night with my own heart: and I was exercised and I swept my spirit. <note>original: "scobēbam" for "scopebam," meaning to sweep or search diligently.</note> Will God then cast off for ever? Or will he never be more favorable again? Or will he cut off his mercy until the end: from generation to generation? Will God forget to show mercy? Or will he, in his anger, shut up his mercies? And I said: "Now I have begun: this is the change of the right hand of the Most High." I remembered the works of the Lord: for I will be mindful of your wonders from the beginning. And I will meditate on all your works: and I will be exercised in your inventions. O God, your way is in the holy place. What god is as great as our God? You are the God who alone does wonders. You have made your power known among the peoples: with your arm you have redeemed your people: the sons of Jacob and Joseph. The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you and they were afraid: and the depths were troubled. A multitude of the sound of waters: the clouds sent out a voice. For your arrows pass through: the voice of your thunder is in a wheel. Your lightnings enlightened the world: the earth shook and trembled. Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters: and your footsteps shall not be known. You led your people like sheep: by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
---
->An instruction of Asaph.<-
<margin>A</margin>
Attend, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth. I will open my mouth in parables: I will speak propositions from the beginning. How many things have we heard and known: and our fathers have told us. They have not been hidden from their children: in another generation. Telling the praises of the Lord, and his powers: and his wonders which he has done. And he set up a testimony in Jacob: and made a law in Israel. How many things he commanded our fathers to make known to their children: that another generation might know them. 
The children who shall be born and shall rise up: and shall tell them to their children. That they may set their hope in God and not forget the works of God: and seek his commandments. Lest they become like their fathers: a perverse and exasperating generation. A generation that set not their heart aright: and whose spirit was not faithful to God. The sons of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow: turned back in the day of battle. They kept not the covenant of God: and in his law they would not walk. And they forgot his benefits: and his wonders that he showed them. 
In the sight of their fathers he did wonders: in the land of Egypt, in the field of Tanis. <note>original: "field of thaneos" — the ancient Egyptian city of Zoan.</note> He divided the sea and brought them through: and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel. And he conducted them with a cloud by day: and all the night with a light of fire. He struck the rock in the wilderness: and gave them to drink as out of a great deep. And he brought forth water out of the rock: and made water to run down like rivers. And they added yet more sin against him: they provoked the Most High to wrath in the place without water. And they tempted God in their hearts: by asking meat for their souls. 
And they spoke against God; they said: "Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?" Because he struck the rock and the waters gushed out: and the streams overflowed. "Can he also give bread: or provide a table for his people?" Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel. Because they believed not in God: and hoped not in his salvation. And he commanded the clouds from above: and opened the doors of heaven. And he rained down manna upon them to eat: and had given them the bread of heaven. 
Man ate the bread of angels: he sent them provisions in abundance. He moved the south wind from heaven: and by his power he brought in the south-west wind. And he rained flesh upon them as dust: and feathered fowls like the sand of the sea. And they fell in the midst of their camp: round about their pavilions. And they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: they were not defrauded of that which they craved. 
As yet their meat was in their mouth: and the wrath of God came upon them. And he slew the fat ones among them: and brought down the chosen men of Israel. In all these things they sinned still: and they believed not for his wondrous works. And their days were consumed in vanity: and their years in haste. When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned, and came to God early in the morning. And they remembered that God was their helper: and the Most High God their redeemer. And they loved him with their mouth: and with their tongue they lied to him. 
But their heart was not right with him: nor were they counted faithful in his covenant. But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: and will not destroy them. And many a time did he turn away his anger: and did not kindle all his wrath. And he remembered that they are flesh: a wind that goes and returns not. How often did they provoke him in the desert: and move him to wrath in the place without water? 
And they turned back and tempted God: and exasperated the Holy One of Israel. They remembered not his hand: the day that he redeemed them from the hand of the afflicter. How he wrought his signs in Egypt: and his wonders in the field of Tanis. And he turned their rivers into blood: and their showers, so that they might not drink. He sent among them the dog-fly, which devoured them: and the frog, which destroyed them. And he gave up their fruits to the blast: and their labors to the locust. 
And he destroyed their vineyards with hail: and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost. And he gave up their cattle to the hail: and their stock to the fire. He sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels. He made a way for the path of his anger: and he spared not their souls from death: and their cattle he shut up in death. And he killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt: the firstfruits of all their labor in the tabernacles of Ham. 
And he took away his own people like sheep: and guided them in the wilderness like a flock. And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: and the sea overwhelmed their enemies. And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: the mountain which his right hand had purchased. And he expelled the Gentiles from before them: and divided the land to them by line. And he made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tabernacles. 
Yet they tempted and provoked the Most High God: and they kept not his testimonies. And they turned away and kept not the covenant: even like their fathers they were turned into a crooked bow. They provoked him to anger on their hills: and moved him to jealousy with their graven images. God heard, and despised them: and he reduced Israel exceedingly to nothing. And he rejected the tabernacle of Shiloh: his own tabernacle where he dwelt among men. 
And he delivered their strength into captivity: and their beauty into the hands of the enemy. And he shut up his people under the sword: and he despised his inheritance. Fire consumed their young men: and their virgins were not lamented. Their priests fell by the sword: and their widows did not weep. 
And the Lord was awoken as one out of sleep: and like a mighty man surfeited with wine. And he struck his enemies on the hinder parts: he put them to an everlasting reproach. And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: and chose not the tribe of Ephraim. But he chose the tribe of Judah: Mount Zion which he loved. And he built his sanctuary like that of unicorns: <note>original: "unicornium" — a term used in the Vulgate to denote strength or height, often translated as "wild oxen" in modern Bibles.</note> in the earth which he founded for ever. 
And he chose David his servant and took him from the flocks of sheep: from following the ewes great with young he took him. To feed Jacob his servant: and Israel his inheritance. And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands.

<column-break/>

->A psalm of Asaph.<-
<margin>D</margin>
O God, the nations have come into your inheritance: they have defiled your holy temple: they have made Jerusalem as a storehouse for fruit. They have given the dead bodies of your servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: the flesh of your saints for the beasts of the earth. They have poured out their blood like water round about Jerusalem: and there was none to bury them. We are become a reproach to our neighbors: a scorn and derision to them that are round about us. 
How long, O Lord, will you be angry until the end? Shall your zeal be kindled like fire? Pour out your wrath upon the nations that have not known you: and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your name. Because they have devoured Jacob: and have laid waste his place. Remember not our former iniquities: let your mercies speedily prevent us: for we are become exceeding poor. Help us, O God, our savior: and for the glory of your name, O Lord, deliver us: and be merciful to our sins for your name’s sake. 
Lest they should say among the nations: "Where is their God?" And let the vengeance of your servants’ blood, which has been shed, be made known among the nations before our eyes. Let the sighing of the prisoners come before you: according to the greatness of your arm, take possession of the children of them that have been put to death. And render to our neighbors sevenfold in their bosom: the reproach wherewith they have reproached you, O Lord. But we, your people, and the sheep of your pasture: will give thanks to you for ever. We will show forth your praise: from generation to generation.

->Unto the end, for those who shall be changed, a testimony for Asaph, a psalm.<-
<margin>Q</margin>
Give ear, O shepherd of Israel: you who lead Joseph like a sheep. You who sit upon the cherubim: shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Stir up your might, and come: to save us. Convert us, O God: and show us your face, and we shall be saved. O Lord God of hosts: how long will you be angry against the prayer of your servant? You will feed us with the bread of tears: and give us tears to drink in measure. You have made us a contradiction to our neighbors: and our enemies have scoffed at us. 
O God of hosts, convert us: and show us your face, and we shall be saved. You brought a vine out of Egypt: you cast out the nations and planted it. You were the guide of its journey in its sight: and you planted the roots thereof, and it filled the land. The shadow of it covered the hills: and the branches thereof the cedars of God. It stretched forth its boughs unto the sea: and its branches unto the river. 
Why then have you broken down its wall: so that all who pass by the way do pluck it? The boar out of the wood has laid it waste: and a singular wild beast has devoured it. Turn again, O God of hosts: look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard. And perfect the same which your right hand has planted: and upon the son of man whom you have confirmed for yourself. Things set on fire and dug down: shall perish at the rebuke of your countenance. Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand: and upon the son of man whom you have confirmed for yourself. And we depart not from you, you shall quicken us: and we will call upon your name. O Lord God of hosts, convert us: and show us your face, and we shall be saved.

->Unto the end, for the winepresses, a psalm of Asaph.<-
<margin>E</margin>
Rejoice in God our helper: sing aloud to the God of Jacob. Take up a psalm, and bring the timbrel: the pleasant psaltery with the harp. Blow the trumpet in the new moon: on the noted day of your solemnity. For it is a commandment in Israel: and a judgment to the God of Jacob. He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph: when he came out of the land of Egypt: he heard a tongue which he knew not. 
He removed his back from the burdens: his hands had served in baskets. In tribulation you called upon me, and I delivered you: I heard you in the secret place of tempest: I proved you at the waters of contradiction. <note>original: "aquam contradictionis" — referring to Meribah, where the Israelites tested God's patience.</note> Hear, O my people, and I will testify to you: O Israel, if you will listen to me, there shall be no new god in you: neither shall you adore a strange god. For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt: open your mouth wide, and I will fill it. 
But my people heard not my voice: and Israel hearkened not to me. So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions. If my people had heard me: if Israel had walked in my ways: I should perhaps have humbled their enemies to nothing: and laid my hand upon them that troubled them. The enemies of the Lord have lied to him: and their time shall be for ever. And he fed them with the fat of wheat: and filled them with honey out of the rock.
---
->A psalm of Asaph.<-
<margin>D</margin>
God has stood in the assembly of gods: and being in the midst of them he judges the gods. How long will you judge iniquity: and accept the faces of the wicked? Judge for the needy and fatherless: do justice to the humble and the poor. Rescue the poor: and deliver the needy out of the hand of the sinner. They have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth shall be moved. 
I have said: "You are gods: and all of you the sons of the Most High." But you like men shall die: and shall fall like one of the princes. Arise, O God, judge the earth: for you shall inherit among all nations.
---
->A song of a psalm of Asaph.<-
<margin>D</margin>
O God, who shall be like to you? Hold not your peace, neither be restrained, O God. For lo, your enemies have made a noise: and they that hate you have lifted up the head. They have taken a malicious counsel against your people: and have consulted against your saints. They have said: "Come and let us destroy them, so that they be not a nation: and let the name of Israel be remembered no more." 
For they have consulted with one accord: they have made a covenant together against you: the tabernacles of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites. Moab and the Hagarenes: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek: the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre. For Assyria also is come with them: they have helped the children of Lot. Do to them as you did to Midian and Sisera: and as to Jabin at the brook of Kishon. Who perished at Endor: and became as dung for the earth. 
Make their princes like Oreb and Zeeb: and Zebah and Zalmunna. All their princes who have said: "Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance." O my God, make them like a wheel: and as stubble before the face of the wind. As fire which burns the wood: and as a flame burning the mountains. So shall you pursue them with your tempest: and shall trouble them in your wrath. Fill their faces with shame: and they shall seek your name, O Lord. 
Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever: and let them be confounded and perish. And let them know that the Lord is your name: you alone are the Most High over all the earth.
---
->Unto the end, for the winepresses, a psalm for the sons of Korah.<-
<margin>Q</margin>
How lovely are your tabernacles, O Lord of hosts: my soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh: have rejoiced in the living God. For the sparrow has found herself a house: and the turtle-dove a nest for herself where she may lay her young. Your altars, O Lord of hosts: my king and my God. Blessed are they that dwell in your house, O Lord: they shall praise you for ever and ever. 
Blessed is the man whose help is from you: in his heart he has disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears, in the place which he has set. For the lawgiver shall give a blessing: they shall go from virtue to virtue: the God of gods shall be seen in Zion. O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: give ear, O God of Jacob. Behold, O God our protector: and look on the face of your Christ. <note>original: "christi tui" — meaning 'your anointed one,' usually referring to the King or the Messiah.</note> 
For better is one day in your courts above thousands. I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God: rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners. For God loves mercy and truth: the Lord will give grace and glory. He will not deprive them of good things that walk in innocence: O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusts in you.

From the rising of the sun and its setting: from the north and the sea. They wandered in the wilderness in a waterless place: they did not find the way to a city of habitation. And he led them into the right way: that they might go to a city of habitation. Let them confess to the Lord for his mercies: and his wonders to the sons of men. Because he has satisfied the empty soul: and filled the hungry soul with good things.

If you, Lord, should mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? For with you there is propitiation, and because of your law I have waited for you, O Lord. My soul has relied on his word; my soul has hoped in the Lord. From the morning watch even until night, let Israel hope in the Lord. Because with the Lord there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption. And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.
->A song of ascents.<-
<margin>D</margin><margin>V</margin>**L**ord, my heart is not exalted, nor are my eyes lifted up. Neither have I walked in great matters, nor in wonderful things above me. If I was not humbly minded, but exalted my soul: as a child weaned from his mother, so is the retribution in my soul. Let Israel hope in the Lord, from this time forth and forever.
->A song of ascents.<-
<margin>O</margin><margin>O</margin>**R**emember, O Lord, David, and all his meekness. How he swore to the Lord, and vowed a vow to the God of Jacob. "If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house, if I shall go up into the bed where I lie. If I shall give sleep to my eyes, and slumber to my eyelids, and rest to my temples: until I find a place for the Lord, a tabernacle for the God of Jacob." Behold, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of the wood. We will enter into his tabernacle; we will adore in the place where his feet stood. Arise, O Lord, into your rest; you and the ark of your sanctification. Let your priests be clothed with justice, and let your saints exult. For the sake of David your servant...

<margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>
**Behold** now, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. In the nights, lift up your hands toward the holy places and bless the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion, he who made heaven and earth.

<margin>Psalm 134</margin>
**Because** you should praise the Lord, praise the name of the Lord; praise him, you servants of the Lord. You who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; sing psalms to his name, for it is sweet. For the Lord has chosen Jacob for himself, and Israel for his own possession. For I have known that the Lord is great, and our God is above all gods. All things whatsoever the Lord willed, he has done in heaven and in earth, in the sea and in all the abysses. Bringing forth clouds from the end of the earth, he has made lightnings into rain. He who brings forth winds from his treasuries; he who struck the firstborn of Egypt, from man even to beast. He sent signs and wonders into the midst of you, O Egypt, upon Pharaoh and upon all his servants. He who struck many nations and killed mighty kings: Seon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan <note>Seon and Og were two powerful kings defeated by the Israelites during their journey to the Promised Land, as recounted in the Book of Numbers.</note>, and all the kingdoms of Canaan. And he gave their land for an inheritance, an inheritance for Israel his people. O Lord, your name is forever; O Lord, your memorial is from generation to generation. For the Lord will judge his people and will be entreated for his servants. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of the hands of men. They have mouths and will not speak; they have eyes and will not see. They have ears and will not hear; for there is no breath in their mouths. Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them. House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord. House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord. Blessed be the Lord from Zion, who dwells in Jerusalem. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 135</margin>
**Give praise** to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endures forever. Give praise to the God of gods: for his mercy endures forever. Give praise to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endures forever. Who alone does great wonders: for his mercy endures forever. Who made the heavens by understanding: for his mercy endures forever. Who established the earth above the waters: for his mercy endures forever. Who made the great lights: for his mercy endures forever. The sun to rule the day: for his mercy endures forever. The moon and the stars to rule the night: for his mercy endures forever. Who struck Egypt with their firstborn: for his mercy endures forever. Who led Israel out from the midst of them: for his mercy endures forever. With a mighty hand and an outstretched arm: for his mercy endures forever. Who divided the Red Sea into parts: for his mercy endures forever. And led Israel through the midst of it: for his mercy endures forever. And overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea: for his mercy endures forever. Who led his people through the desert: for his mercy endures forever. Who struck great kings: for his mercy endures forever. And killed mighty kings: for his mercy endures forever. Seon, king of the Amorites: for his mercy endures forever. And Og, king of Bashan: for his mercy endures forever. And gave their land for an inheritance: for his mercy endures forever. An inheritance to Israel his servant: for his mercy endures forever. For in our lowliness he was mindful of us: for his mercy endures forever. And he redeemed us from our enemies: for his mercy endures forever. Who gives food to all flesh: for his mercy endures forever. Give praise to the God of heaven: for his mercy endures forever. Give praise to the Lord of lords: for his mercy endures forever.

<margin>Psalm 136</margin>
**Upon** the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept, when we remembered Zion. On the willow trees in the midst of it, we hung up our instruments. For there they who led us into captivity asked us for the words of songs. And they who carried us away said: Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land? If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten. Let my tongue cleave to my jaws if I do not remember you; if I do not set Jerusalem at the beginning of my joy. Remember, O Lord, the sons of Edom, in the day of Jerusalem: who say, "Lay it bare, lay it bare, even to the foundation thereof!" O wretched daughter of Babylon, blessed is he who shall repay you with the payment you have paid to us. Blessed is he who shall take and dash your little ones against the rock.

<margin>Psalm 137</margin>
**I will praise** you, Lord, with my whole heart, for you have heard the words of my mouth. In the sight of the angels I will sing psalms to you; I will worship toward your holy temple and praise your name. For your mercy and your truth, for you have magnified your holy name above all. On whatever day I shall call upon you, hear me; you shall multiply strength in my soul. Let all the kings of the earth praise you, O Lord, for they have heard the words of your mouth. And let them sing in the ways of the Lord, for great is the glory of the Lord. For the Lord is high and looks upon the lowly, and the lofty he knows from afar. If I shall walk in the midst of tribulation, you will quicken me; and you have stretched forth your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand has saved me. The Lord will repay for me; O Lord, your mercy is forever; do not despise the works of your hands.

<margin>Psalm 46</margin>
**All** you nations, clap your hands; shout to God with the voice of exultation. For the Lord is high, terrible: a great king over all the earth. He has subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet. He has chosen for us his inheritance, the beauty of Jacob which he loved. God has ascended with a shout, and the Lord with the sound of the trumpet. Sing psalms to our God, sing; sing psalms to our king, sing. For God is the king of all the earth; sing psalms wisely. God shall reign over the nations; God sits upon his holy throne. The princes of the people are gathered together with the God of Abraham, for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.

<margin>Psalm 139</margin>
**Deliver** me, O Lord, from the evil man; rescue me from the unjust man. Who have devised iniquities in their heart; all the day long they designed battles. They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; the venom of asps is under their lips. Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner, and deliver me from unjust men. Who have intended to supplant my steps; the proud have hidden a snare for me. And they have stretched out cords for a trap; they have set a stumbling block for me near the path. I said to the Lord: You are my God; hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication. O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have overshadowed my head in the day of battle. Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire to the sinner; they have plotted against me, do not abandon me, lest they should triumph. The head of them that compass me about: the labor of their own lips shall overwhelm them. Burning coals shall fall upon them; you shall cast them down into the fire; they shall not stand in miseries. A man full of tongue shall not be established in the earth; evils shall catch the unjust man unto destruction. I have known, O Lord, that the Lord will do judgment for the needy and revenge for the poor. But the just shall praise your name, and the upright shall dwell with your countenance.

<margin>Psalm 143</margin>
**Blessed** is the Lord my God, who teaches my hands for battle and my fingers for war. My mercy and my refuge, my supporter and my deliverer. My protector, and in him have I hoped, who subdues my people under me. Lord, what is man, that you have made yourself known to him? Or the son of man, that you make account of him? Man is made like vanity; his days pass away like a shadow. Lord, bow down your heavens and descend; touch the mountains and they shall smoke. Send forth lightning and you shall scatter them; shoot out your arrows and you shall trouble them. Send forth your hand from on high; deliver me and rescue me from many waters, from the hand of foreign children. Whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity. To you, O God, I will sing a new song; on the psaltery <note>The psaltery was a stringed instrument similar to a zither or harp, often used in medieval worship.</note> of ten strings I will sing to you. Who give salvation to kings, who have redeemed David your servant from the cruel sword, deliver me. And rescue me from the hand of foreign children, whose mouth has spoken vanity, and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity. Whose sons are like new plants in their youth. Their daughters are trimmed, adorned like the likeness of a temple. Their storehouses are full, overflowing from this into that. Their sheep are fruitful, abounding in their goings forth; their oxen are fat. There is no breach of wall, nor passage, nor crying out in their streets. They have called the people happy that has these things; happy is that people whose God is the Lord.

<margin>Psalm 58</margin>
**Deliver** me from my enemies, O my God, and rescue me from them that rise up against me. Deliver me from them that work iniquity, and save me from men of blood. For behold, they have caught my soul; the mighty have rushed in upon me. Neither is it my iniquity nor my sin, O Lord; without iniquity have I run and directed my steps. Rise up to meet me and see; and you, O Lord, God of hosts, the God of Israel. Attend to visit all the nations; have no mercy on all them that work iniquity. They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs, and shall go round about the city. Behold, they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips; for who has heard? But you, O Lord, shall laugh at them; you shall bring all the nations to nothing. I will keep my strength to you, for you are my supporter, O God. My God, his mercy shall prevent me. God has shown me for my enemies: do not kill them, lest my people forget. Scatter them by your power, and bring them down, O Lord my protector. For the sin of their mouth and the word of their lips, let them be taken in their pride. And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of in their destruction. In the wrath of destruction, and they shall be no more; and they shall know that God shall rule over Jacob and the ends of the earth. They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs, and shall go round about the city. They shall be scattered abroad to eat; and if they be not filled, they will murmur. But I will sing of your strength and will extol your mercy in the morning. For you have become my supporter and my refuge in the day of my tribulation. My helper, to you will I sing, for you, O God, are my supporter; my God is my mercy.

<margin>Psalm 140</margin>
...my [soul] has raised the Lord. Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth, and a door of restraint around my lips. Incline not my heart to evil words, to make excuses for sins. With men that work iniquity; and I will not communicate with the choicest of them. The just man shall correct me in mercy and shall reprove me; but let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head. For yet my prayer also shall be against their pleasures; their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed up. They shall hear my words, for they have prevailed; as when the thickness of the earth is broken up upon the ground. Our bones are scattered near hell; but to you, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes; in you have I hoped, take not away my soul. Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me, and from the stumbling blocks of them that work iniquity. The wicked shall fall in his net; I am alone until I pass by. I cried to the Lord with my voice; with my voice I made supplication to the Lord. I pour out my prayer in his sight, and before him I declare my trouble. When my spirit failed me, then you knew my paths. In this way wherein I walked, they have hidden a snare for me. I looked on my right hand and beheld, and there was no one that would know me. Flight has failed me, and there is no one that has regard for my soul. I cried to you, O Lord; I said: You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living. Attend to my supplication, for I am brought very low. Deliver me from my persecutors, for they are stronger than I. Bring my soul out of prison, that I may praise your name; the just wait for me, until you reward me.

<margin>Psalm 142</margin>
**Hear**, O Lord, my prayer; give ear to my supplication in your truth; hear me in your justice. And enter not into judgment with your servant; for in your sight no man living shall be justified. For the enemy has persecuted my soul; he has brought down my life to the earth. He has made me to dwell in darkness as those that have been dead of old; and my spirit is in anguish within me; my heart within me is troubled. I remembered the days of old; I meditated on all your works; I meditated upon the deeds of your hands. I stretched forth my hands to you; my soul is as earth without water unto you. Hear me speedily, O Lord; my spirit has fainted away. Turn not away your face from me, or I shall be like them that go down into the pit. Cause me to hear your mercy in the morning, for in you have I hoped. Make the way known to me wherein I should walk, for I have lifted up my soul to you. Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord, to you have I fled. Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit shall lead me into the right land. For your name's sake, O Lord, you will quicken me in your equity. You will bring my soul out of trouble, and in your mercy you will destroy my enemies. And you will destroy all them that afflict my soul, for I am your servant. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 143</margin>

<margin>Psalm 144</margin>
**I will extol** you, O Lord my God, the king; and I will bless your name forever, and for ages of ages. Every day will I bless you; and I will praise your name forever, and for ages of ages. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; and of his greatness there is no end. Generation and generation shall praise your works, and they shall declare your power. They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of your holiness, and shall tell your wondrous works. And they shall speak of the might of your terrible acts, and shall declare your greatness. They shall publish the memory of the abundance of your sweetness, and shall rejoice in your justice. The Lord is gracious and merciful; patient and of great mercy. The Lord is sweet to all, and his tender mercies are over all his works. Let all your works, O Lord, praise you, and let your saints bless you. They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom and shall tell of your power. To make your power known to the sons of men, and the glory of the magnificence of your kingdom. Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and your dominion is in every generation and generation. The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works. The Lord lifts up all that fall, and sets up all that are cast down. The eyes of all hope in you, O Lord, and you give them food in due season. You open your hand and fill every living creature with blessing. The Lord is just in all his ways and holy in all his works. The Lord is near to all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth. He will do the will of them that fear him, and he will hear their prayer and save them. The Lord keeps all them that love him, but all the wicked he will destroy. My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name, forever and for ages of ages. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 33</margin> <insert>book of wisdom <note>original: "libri sapie" - This insertion suggests the scribe or a later reader associated this Psalm with the wisdom literature tradition.</note></insert>
**I will bless** the Lord at all times; his praise shall be always in my mouth. In the Lord shall my soul be praised; let the meek hear and rejoice. O magnify the Lord with me, and let us extol his name together. I sought the Lord and he heard me, and he delivered me from all my troubles. Come to him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be confounded. This poor man cried and the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles. The angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him and shall deliver them. O taste and see that the Lord is sweet; blessed is the man that hopes in him. Fear the Lord, all you his saints, for there is no want to them that fear him. The rich have wanted and have suffered hunger, but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good. Come, children, hearken to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the man that desires life, who loves to see good days? Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking guile. Turn away from evil and do good; seek after peace and pursue it. The eyes of the Lord are upon the just, and his ears unto their prayers. But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth. The just cried and the Lord heard them, and delivered them out of all their troubles. The Lord is near to them that are of a contrite heart, and he will save the lowly in spirit. Many are the afflictions of the just, but out of them all will the Lord deliver them. The Lord keeps all their bones; not one of them shall be broken. The death of the wicked is very evil, and they that hate the just shall be guilty. The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and none of them that hope in him shall be desolate. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 145</margin>
**Praise** the Lord, O my soul; in my life I will praise the Lord; I will sing to my God as long as I shall be. Put not your trust in princes, in the children of men, in whom there is no salvation. His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth; in that day all their thoughts shall perish. Blessed is he who has the God of Jacob for his helper, whose hope is in the Lord his God: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them. Who keeps truth forever; who executes judgment for them that suffer wrong; who gives food to the hungry. The Lord looses them that are fettered; the Lord enlightens the blind. The Lord lifts up them that are cast down; the Lord loves the just. The Lord keeps the strangers; he will support the fatherless and the widow; and the ways of sinners he will destroy. The Lord shall reign forever: your God, O Zion, unto generation and generation. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 146</margin>
**Praise** the Lord, for a psalm is good; to our God be joyful and comely praise. The Lord builds up Jerusalem; he will gather together the dispersed of Israel. Who heals the broken of heart and binds up their bruises. Who numbers the multitude of stars and calls them all by their names. Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and of his wisdom there is no number. The Lord lifts up the meek and brings the wicked down even to the ground. Sing to the Lord with confession; sing to our God upon the harp. Who covers the heaven with clouds and prepares rain for the earth. Who makes grass to grow on the mountains, and herbs for the service of men. Who gives to beasts their food, and to the young ravens that call upon him. He shall not delight in the strength of the horse, nor shall he take pleasure in the legs of a man. The Lord takes pleasure in them that fear him, and in them that hope in his mercy. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 147</margin>
**Praise** the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion. For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you. Who has placed peace in your borders and fills you with the fat of corn. Who sends forth his speech to the earth; his word runs swiftly. Who gives snow like wool; he scatters mists like ashes. He sends his crystal like morsels; who shall stand before the face of his cold? He shall send out his word and shall melt them; his spirit shall blow and the waters shall run. Who declares his word to Jacob: his justices and his judgments to Israel. He has not done in like manner to every nation, and his judgments he has not made manifest to them. <margin>Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluia"</note></margin>

<margin>Psalm 148</margin>
**Praise** the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the high places. Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts. Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you stars and light. Praise him, heaven of heavens; and let all the waters that are above the heavens praise the name of the Lord. For he spoke and they were made; he commanded and they were created. He has established them forever, and for ages of ages; he has made a decree, and it shall not pass away. Praise the Lord from the earth, you dragons and all abysses. Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds, which fulfill his word. Mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars. Beasts and all cattle, serpents and feathered fowls. Kings of the earth and all people, princes and all judges of the earth. Young men and virgins; let the old with the younger praise the name of the Lord: for his name alone is exalted. His praise is above heaven and earth: and he has exalted the horn of his people. A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching to him.

# PROLOGUE
# IN THE BO-
# OK OF PROVERBS
# OF SOLOMON WHICH
# IS CALLED MASLOTH <note>original: "Masloth" — a Latin transliteration of the Hebrew 'Mishlei', meaning Proverbs.</note>

LET THIS LETTER JOIN those whom the priesthood joins: or rather, let the parchment not divide those whom the love of Christ binds together. You ask that I should have written commentaries on Moses, Amos, Zechariah, and Malachi: but I was prevented by illness. You send solace for expenses, supporting our scribes and librarians, so that our talent might exert itself chiefly for you. And behold, from the side comes a frequent crowd of diverse people asking for things: as if it were either fair that I should labor for others while you are hungry, or that I should be indebted to anyone besides you in the account of giving and receiving. Therefore, although broken by a long sickness, so as not to be entirely silent this year and mute toward you, I have consecrated three days’ work to your name. This is the interpretation of the three volumes of Solomon: *Masloth*, which the Hebrews call Parables and the common edition calls Proverbs; *Coheleth*, which in Greek I may call *Ecclesiastes* and in Latin *The Preacher*; and *Syrasyrim*, which in our language translates as *Song of Songs*.

There is also carried about the book *Panarethos* <note>original: "Panarethos" — a Greek term meaning "All-Virtuous," often applied to the Book of Sirach.</note> of Jesus son of Sirach, and another false-writing <note>original: "pseudographus" — a work falsely attributed to an author.</note> which is inscribed as the *Wisdom of Solomon*. I found the first of these in Hebrew—not called "Ecclesiasticus" as among the Latins, but titled "Parables." To it were joined Ecclesiastes and the Song of Songs, so that it might match Solomon not only in the number of books but also in the type of subject matter. The second is nowhere found among the Hebrews, for its very style reeks of Greek eloquence, and several of the ancient writers affirm this to be the work of Philo the Jew. Therefore, just as the Church reads the books of Judith, Tobit, and the Maccabees, but does not receive them among the canonical scriptures, so also let it read these two volumes for the edification of the people, but not to confirm the authority of ecclesiastical dogmas.

If anyone is more pleased by the edition of the Seventy Interpreters <note>original: "Septuaginta" — the Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note>, they have it as corrected by us long ago; for we do not forge new things in a way that destroys the old. And yet, when one reads most diligently, let them know that our work is better understood—not being "poured into a third vessel" <note>St. Jerome famously argued that translating a translation (Hebrew to Greek to Latin) caused the meaning to "sour" or fade, like wine transferred between too many jars. He preferred going "straight from the press" (the original Hebrew).</note> where it might sour, but preserved in its own flavor, having been committed most purely from the press. **The prologue ends.**

Possess wisdom, because it is better than gold: and acquire prudence, because it is more precious than silver. The path of the righteous turns away from evils: the guardian of his own soul keeps his way. Pride precedes destruction: and before a fall the spirit is exalted. It is better to be humbled with the meek: than to divide spoils with the proud. One learned in the word shall find good things: and he who hopes in the Lord is blessed.

**Q**ui <note>original: "Qui" — He who</note> he who is wise in heart shall be called prudent: and he who is sweet in speech shall find greater things. The fountain of life is the learning of him who possesses it: the doctrine of fools is fatuity. The heart of the wise shall instruct his mouth: and shall add grace to his lips. Well-ordered words are a honeycomb: sweetness to the soul and health to the bones. There is a way which seems right to a man: and its ends lead to death.

**O**mnia <note>original: "Omnia" — All</note> all the words of my mouth are just: there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. They are right to those who understand: and equitable to those who find knowledge. Receive my discipline and not money: choose doctrine more than gold. For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and everything desirable cannot be compared to it. I, Wisdom, dwell in counsel: and I am present among learned thoughts. The fear of the Lord hates evil: I detest arrogance and pride and the wicked way and a double-tongued mouth. Counsel and equity are mine: prudence is mine, strength is mine. By me kings reign: and the makers of laws decree just things. By me princes command: and the powerful decree justice. I love those who love me: and those who watch for me in the morning shall find me. With me are riches and glory: proud wealth and justice. My fruit is better than gold and precious stone: and my offspring better than choice silver. I walk in the ways of justice: in the midst of the paths of judgment. That I may enrich those who love me: and fill their treasures. The Lord possessed me in the beginning of His ways: before He made anything from the start. I was ordained from eternity: and from of old, before the earth was made. The depths <note>original: "abyssi"</note> were not yet: and I was already conceived. Not yet had the fountains of waters burst forth: not yet had the mountains settled with their heavy mass. Before the hills I was brought forth: He had not yet made the earth and the rivers and the hinges of the world. When He prepared the heavens, I was there: when with a fixed law and a circle He enclosed the depths. When He established the sky above: and balanced the fountains of waters. When He surrounded the sea with its limit: and set a law for the waters that they should not pass their borders. When He weighed the foundations of the earth: I was with Him composing all things. And I was delighted day by day: playing before Him at all times. Playing in the world: and my delights were to be with the children of men. Now therefore, sons, hear me: blessed are they who keep my ways. Hear discipline and be wise: and do not reject it. Blessed is the man who hears me: and who watches at my gates daily and waits at the posts of my door. He who finds me shall find life: and shall draw salvation from the Lord. But he who shall sin against me shall hurt his own soul: all who hate me love death.

**Q**ui <note>original: "Qui" — He who</note> he who instructs a mocker does an injury to himself: and he who rebukes a wicked man generates a stain for himself. Do not rebuke a mocker lest he hate you: rebuke a wise man and he will love you. Give an opportunity to a wise man and wisdom shall be added to him: teach a righteous man and he will hasten to receive it. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord: and the knowledge of the holy ones is prudence. For by me your days shall be multiplied: and years of life shall be added to you. If you are wise, you shall be so for yourself: but if you are a mocker, you alone shall bear the evil. A foolish and clamorous woman, full of allurements and knowing nothing at all: sat at the doors of her house upon a chair in a high place of the city. That she might call those passing by the way and going on their journey. He who is a little one, let him turn aside to me: and to the heartless she spoke. Stolen waters are sweeter: and hidden bread is more pleasant. And he knew not that giants are there: and her guests are in the depths of hell. A wise son makes a father glad: but a foolish son is the sorrow of his mother. Treasures of wickedness shall profit nothing: but justice indeed shall deliver from death. The Lord will not afflict the soul of the just with hunger: and he will subvert the deceits of the wicked. The slack hand has worked poverty: but the hand of the strong prepares riches. He who gathers in the harvest is a wise son: but he who snores in summer is a son of confusion. The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity. The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot. The wise in heart shall receive precepts: a fool shall be beaten by his lips. He who walks simply walks confidently: but he who perverts his ways shall be manifest. He who winks with the eye shall give sorrow: and the fool shall be beaten by his lips. The mouth of the just is a vein of life: and the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity. Hatred stirs up brawls: and charity covers all offenses. In the lips of the wise shall wisdom be found: and a rod on the back of him who is lacking in heart. The wise hide knowledge: but the mouth of the fool is near to confusion.

# S

Golden apples in silver carvings is he who speaks a word in its proper time. Like a golden earring and a shining pearl is he who reproves a wise man and an obedient ear. As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to him who sent him; he brings rest to his soul. Like clouds and wind not followed by rain is a man who boasts of a promise he does not fulfill. Through patience, a leader will be gently overcome, and a soft tongue will break hardness. You have found honey: eat what is enough for you, lest perhaps being filled you vomit it up. Withdraw your foot from the house of your neighbor, lest at some point being sated, he hates you. A dart, a sword, and a sharp arrow: such is the man who speaks false testimony against his neighbor. Like rot in the teeth is he who hopes in a [failing] foot in a day of distress, and loses mercy.

# R

Vinegar on soda <note>original: "acetum in nitro" — soda (natron) reacts violently with vinegar; this describes the jarring effect of singing happy songs to a heavy heart.</note> is he who sings songs to a wicked heart. As a garment in winter, and a worm in wood, so the sadness of a man harms the heart. If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for you will gather coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will repay you. As the north wind scatters the rain, so a sad face [scatters] a backbiting tongue. It is better to sit in a corner of the house than with a quarrelsome woman in a shared house. Cold water to a thirsty soul is like good news from a far country. A fountain troubled by a foot and a corrupted spring is a just man falling before the wicked. He who eats much honey, it is not good for him. Nor will he who searches into majesty be overwhelmed by glory. Like an open city without the circle of walls, so is a man who cannot restrain his spirit in speaking. As snow in summer and rain in harvest, so glory does not befit a fool. As a bird flying to other places and a sparrow wherever it may go, so a curse uttered in vain will come upon someone. A whip for the horse, a muzzle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of the imprudent. Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he seem wise to himself. [Like one who cuts off his own] feet and drinks iniquity is he who sends words by a foolish messenger.

# I

Just as a lame man has beautiful legs in vain, so the fool loses the speech in his mouth. Like one who throws a stone into a heap of Mercury, <note>original: "acervum mercurii" — a reference to the 'herm,' a roadside cairn to the god Mercury; here it suggests a useless or idolatrous honor.</note> so is he who gives honor to the wicked. As if a thorn grows in the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. Judgment determines causes, and he who imposes silence on a fool will mitigate anger. As [dogs] return to their vomit, so the imprudent return to their sin. Have you seen a man who seems wise to himself? There will be more hope for a fool than for him.

# L

The sluggard says, "A lion is in the way, a lioness is in the paths." As a door turns on its hinge, so does the sluggard in his bed. The sluggard hides his hand under his armpit and it wearies him if he must turn it to his mouth. The sluggard seems wiser to himself than seven men speaking sentences. Like one who takes a dog by the ears, so is he who passes by and impatiently involves himself in another's quarrel. As one is harmful who sends spears and arrows unto death, so is the man who deceitfully harms his friend and, when caught, says "I did it in play." When wood fails, the fire will be extinguished; and when the whisperer is removed, brawls fall quiet. As coals are to burning coals and wood to fire, so an angry man stirs up quarrels. The words of a whisperer are as if simple, yet they reach the inner parts of the belly. As if you wished to decorate an earthenware vessel with impure silver, so are swelling lips joined with a wicked heart.

# O

An enemy is understood by his lips when he treats of deceit in his heart. When he lowers his voice, do not believe him, for he has seven wickednesses in his heart. He who covers hatred deceitfully, his malice shall be revealed in the assembly. He who digs a pit shall fall into it, and he who rolls a stone, it will return upon him. A deceitful tongue does not love the truth, and a slippery mouth works ruin.

# A

Do not boast of tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day may bring forth. Let another praise you and not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips. A stone is heavy and sand is burdensome, but the anger of a fool is heavier than both. It has no mercy, nor bursting fury, and friendship cannot bear the onset. Better is an open correction than a hidden love. More faithful are the wounds of a lover than the deceitful kisses of one who hates. A sated soul will trample a honeycomb; a hungry soul will take even the bitter for sweet. Like a bird wandering from its nest, so is a man who leaves his place. The heart is delighted by ointment and various scents, and the soul is sweetened by the good counsels of a friend. Do not forsake your friend and the friend of your father, and do not enter the house of your brother in the day of your affliction. A neighbor nearby is better than a brother far off. Study wisdom, my son, and make my heart joyful, so that you may be able to answer a word to one who reproaches you. The shrewd man sees evil and hides himself; the little ones passing through suffer the loss. Take the garment of him who has stood surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for outsiders. He who blesses his neighbor with a loud voice, rising in the night, shall be like one who curses. A leaking roof on a cold day and a quarrelsome woman are compared. He who restrains her is like one who would hold the wind, and he shall call upon the oil of his right hand. As an edge is sharpened by iron, so a man sharpens the face of his friend. He who tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit, and he who is the guardian of his master shall be glorified.

# M

As faces shine back in the water to those looking in, so the hearts of the prudent are manifest to men. Hell and destruction are never filled, and the eyes of men are insatiable. As silver is tested in the forge and gold in the furnace, so a man is tested by the mouth of one praising him. The heart of the wicked seeks out evils, but the upright heart seeks knowledge. Even if you crush a fool in a mortar as if with a pestle striking grain from above, his folly will not be taken from him. Diligently know the face of your cattle, and consider your flocks. For you will not have power forever, but a crown is granted from generation to generation.

# O

The meadows are open, and the green herbs have appeared, and hay is gathered from the mountains. Four things are the smallest of the earth, and they are wiser than the wise. The ants, a weak people, who prepare their food in the harvest. The rabbits, a powerless folk, who place their bed in the rock. The locust has no king, yet the whole [army] goes out by their ranks. The lizard supports itself with its hands and dwells in the palaces of kings. There are three things that walk well, and a fourth that proceeds happily. The lion, the strongest of beasts, will fear no one he meets. The rooster with girded loins, and the ram, and there is no king who can resist him. If you have appeared foolish after you have been lifted up on high, put your hand over your mouth. He who strongly presses the teats to draw out milk squeezes out butter; and he who violently blows his nose brings out blood; and he who provokes anger produces discord.
<meta>catchword: thunders.</meta>

# Q

The earth is never satisfied with water, and fire never says "it is enough." The eye that mocks a father and despises the labor of his mother, let the ravens of the torrents pick it out, and let the sons of the eagle eat it. Three things are difficult for me, and a fourth I am entirely ignorant of: The way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a serpent upon a rock, the way of a ship in the middle of the sea, and the way of a man in his youth. Such also is the way of an adulterous woman, who eats and, wiping her mouth, says: "I have done no evil." By three things the earth is moved, and a fourth it cannot endure: By a servant when he reigns, by a fool when he is filled with food. By a hateful woman when she is taken in marriage, and by a handmaid when she is the heir to her mistress.

# A

Agur, son of the vomiting Vace. <note>The scribe has interpreted the Hebrew name "Jakeh" as "Vomentis" (vomiting).</note> The vision which the man spoke, with whom God is, and who, being strengthened by God's assistance, said: I am the most foolish of men, and the wisdom of men is not with me. I have not learned wisdom, and I have known the knowledge of the saints. Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his hands? Who has bound the waters as if in a garment? Who has raised up all the ends of the earth? What is his name? And what is the name of his son, if you know? Every word of God is fire-tested; he is a shield to those hoping in him. Add nothing to his words, lest you be reproved and found a liar. Two things I have asked of you, do not deny me before I die: Remove vanity and lying words far from me; give me neither beggary nor riches; grant only what is necessary for my sustenance; lest perhaps being filled I be enticed to deny you and say: "Who is the Lord?" or being compelled by poverty I should steal, and swear falsely by the name of my God.

# C

To some, the son delivers a burden in his voice. For being drunk and wicked, words are gathered for four reasons: a son of the mind, a vision of the man, as the man with whom God is, and who, being strengthened by God's assistance, said: I am the most foolish of men, and the wisdom of men is not with me. I have not learned wisdom, and I have known the knowledge of the saints. Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the spirit in his hands? Who has bound the waters as if in a garment? Who has raised up all the ends of the earth? What is his name? And what is the name of his son, if you know? Every word of God is fire-tested; he is a shield to those hoping in him. Add nothing to his words, lest you be reproved and found a liar. Two things I have asked of you, do not deny me before I die. Remove vanity and lying words far from me; give me neither beggary nor riches. Grant only what is necessary for my sustenance: lest perhaps being filled I be enticed to deny you and say: "Who is the Lord?" or being compelled by poverty I should steal, and swear falsely by the name of my God. Do not [accuse] a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you fall. There is a generation that curses its father, and does not bless its mother. A generation that seems pure to itself, and yet is not washed from its filth. A generation whose eyes are lofty, and its eyelids raised on high. A generation that has swords for teeth, and devours with its molars: that it may eat the needy from the earth and the poor from among men. The leech has two daughters saying: "Bring, bring." There are three things insatiable, and a fourth never says: "it is enough." Hell, and the opening of the womb, and the earth which is not satisfied with water, but fire never says "it is enough." The eye that mocks a father and despises the labor of his mother, let the ravens pick it out, and the young of the eagle shall eat it.

# L

<insert>The words of King Lemuel.</insert>
<insert>The words of King Lemuel. The vision by which his mother taught him.</insert>

What, my beloved? What, the beloved of my womb? What, the beloved of my vows? Do not give your substance to women, nor your life to the destroying of kings. Do not give wine to kings, because there is no secret where drunkenness reigns. Lest perhaps they drink and forget judgment, and change the cause of the children of the poor. Give strong drink to those who are grieving, and wine to those who are of a bitter soul. Let them drink and forget their poverty, and remember their pain no more. Open your mouth for the mute, and for the causes of all the children who pass away. Open your mouth, judge what is just, and judge the needy and the poor.

# V

Who shall find a valiant woman? Far off and from the uttermost ends is her price. The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he shall not lack for spoils. She will render him good and not evil all the days of her life. She sought wool and flax, and worked by the counsel of her hands. She is made like a merchant's ship, bringing her bread from afar.

# HERE BEGINS THE BOOK OF ECCLESIASTES

## WHO IS CALLED CELETH <note>original: "Celeth" — a Latinized form of the Hebrew 'Qoheleth,' meaning 'The Preacher' or 'The Assembler.'</note>

### THIS BOOK HAS 31 CHAPTERS AND 800 VERSES.

<image-desc>A large, highly decorative historiated initial 'V' dominates the left center of the page. It is rendered in deep blue and red with intricate white vine-like tracery and geometric patterns. The letter is set against a textured gold-leaf background. It marks the start of the word 'Verba'.</image-desc> **THE WORDS OF ECCLESIASTES, THE SON OF DAVID, KING OF ISRAEL.**

<margin>
Vanity of vanities, says Ecclesiastes: vanity of vanities, & all is vanity. What more does a man have from all his labor, by which he toils under the sun? A generation passes & a generation arrives: but the earth stands forever.
</margin>

**A**ll is vanity, said Ecclesiastes: vanity of vanities, and all is vanity.
**W**hat more does a man have from all his labor: by which he toils under the sun?
**A** generation passes and a generation arrives: but the earth stands forever.
**T**he sun rises and sets: and returns to its place: and there, being reborn, it circles through the south: and turns to the north. The spirit goes through all things in its circuit: and returns into its cycles.
**A**ll rivers enter the sea: and the sea does not overflow. To the place from which the rivers come, they return: so that they may flow again.
**A**ll things are difficult: man cannot explain them in speech.
**T**he eye is not satisfied with seeing: nor is the ear filled with hearing.
**W**hat is it that was? The same as what shall be.
**W**hat is it that was done? The same as what is to be done.
**T**here is nothing new under the sun: nor can anyone say: behold, this is fresh. For it had already preceded in the ages that were before us.
**T**here is no memory of earlier things: but neither of those things which are to be in the future: there will be no record among those who shall be in the end.
**I**, Ecclesiastes, was king of Israel in Jerusalem, and I proposed in my mind to seek and investigate wisely concerning all things that are done under the sun.
**T**his worst occupation God has given to the sons of men: so that they might be occupied in it.
**I** have seen all things that are done under the sun: and behold, all is vanity and affliction of spirit.
**T**he perverse are corrected with difficulty: and the number of fools is infinite.
**I** spoke in my heart, saying: Behold, I have become great: and have excelled all in wisdom who were before me in Jerusalem. And my mind contemplated many things wisely: and I learned.
**A**nd I gave my heart that I might know prudence: and doctrine: and errors: and folly. And I recognized that in these things also there was labor and affliction of spirit; because
**I**n much wisdom there is much indignation: and he who adds knowledge: adds also labor.

**I** said in my heart: I will go and overflow with delights and enjoy good things. And I saw that this also was vanity.
**L**aughter I considered an error: and to joy I said: why are you fruitlessly deceived?
**I** thought in my heart to withdraw my flesh from wine: so that I might transfer my mind to wisdom, and avoid folly: until I might see what was useful for the sons of men: what work is needed under the sun, for the number of the days of their life.
**I** magnified my works: I built houses for myself: I planted vineyards.
**I** made gardens and orchards: and I planted them with every kind of tree.
**A**nd I constructed pools of water: that I might irrigate the forest of budding wood.
**I** possessed male and female servants: and I had a large household; also herds: and great flocks of sheep: beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem.
**I** amassed for myself silver and gold: and the wealth of kings: and of provinces. I made for myself male and female singers: and the delights of the sons of men: cups: and pitchers for service in pouring wines. And I surpassed in riches all who were before me in Jerusalem; wisdom also persevered with me.
**A**nd all that my eyes desired: I did not deny them. Nor did I forbid my heart from enjoying every pleasure: and delighting itself in those things which I had prepared. And I thought this to be my portion: if I used my labor.
**A**nd when I had turned myself to all the works which my hands had made: and to the labors in which [I had toiled] in vain

<column-break/>

the desired fruit: which he does not find: from sadness & affliction of mind: for sadness and affliction of mind. But even in this my mind [wondered]: lest perhaps it could not find rest, even for those who are weak. For what is man, that he should follow after the king, his maker?
**I** saw that wisdom so far preceded folly: as much as light differs from darkness.
**T**he eyes of the wise man are in his head: the fool walks in darkness: and I learned that there was one end for both.
**A**nd I said in my heart: If one end shall be for the fool and for me: what does it profit me, that I have given myself to greater wisdom?
**A**nd speaking with my mind: I noticed that this also was vanity.
**F**or there shall be no memory of the wise similarly as of the fools forever: and future times shall cover all things equally with oblivion. The learned man dies similarly as the unlearned: and therefore I was weary of my life: seeing all things under the sun to be evil: and all things vanity: and affliction of spirit.
**A**gain, I detested all my industry: by which I labored most studiously under the sun: being about to have an heir after me: whom I know not whether he shall be wise: or a fool; and he shall rule over my labors: in which I have sweated and been anxious. And is anything so vain?
**W**hence I ceased: and my heart renounced laboring any further under the sun.
**F**or when one labors in wisdom and doctrine: and anxiety: he leaves his acquisitions to an idle man: and this therefore is vanity: and a great evil.
**F**or what will it profit a man from all his labor and affliction of spirit: by which he was tormented under the sun?
**A**ll his days are full of sorrows and hardships: nor does his mind rest by night. And is this not vanity?
**I**s it not better to eat and drink: and to show his soul good things from his labors? And this is from the hand of God.
**W**ho shall devour so much: and overflow with delights as I have?
**T**o a man good in his sight: God has given wisdom: and knowledge: and joy. But to the sinner he has given affliction: and superfluous care: that he might add and gather: and deliver it to him who has pleased God. But this also is vanity: and a hollow anxiety of the mind.

**T**o everything there is a season: and all things under heaven pass away in their spans.
**A** time for being born: and a time for dying. A time for planting: and a time for uprooting what was planted.
**A** time for killing: and a time for healing. A time for destroying: and a time for building.
**A** time for weeping: and a time for laughing. A time for mourning: and a time for dancing.
**A** time for scattering stones: and a time for gathering them. A time for embracing: and a time to be far from embraces.
**A** time for acquiring: and a time for losing. A time for keeping: and a time for casting away.
**A** time for tearing: and a time for sewing. A time for being silent: and a time for speaking. A time for love: and a time for hate. A time for war: and a time for peace.
**W**hat more does a man have from his labor?
**I** have seen the affliction which God has given to the sons of men: that they might be stretched out in it.
**H**e made all things good in their time: and delivered the world to their dispute: so that man cannot find the work: from the beginning even unto the end.
**I** recognized that there was nothing better than to be glad: and to do well in one’s life.
**F**or every man who eats: and drinks: and sees good from his labor: this is the gift of God.
**I** learned that all the works which God has made persevere forever. We cannot add anything to them: nor take away: which things God has made so that he might be feared.
**T**hat which was done: remains the same; the things that are to be: have been: and God restores that which has passed away.
**I** saw under the sun in the place of judgment, impiety: and in the place of justice, iniquity: and I said in my heart: God shall judge the just and the impious: and the time of every thing shall be then.
**I** said in my heart concerning the sons of men: that God might prove them: and show them to be similar to beasts.
**T**herefore, one is the end of man: and of beasts: and the condition of both is equal. As man dies: so also they die.
**A**ll things breathe similarly: and man has nothing more than the beast. All things are subject to vanity: and all things go to one place.
**F**rom the earth they were made: and into the earth they shall return together.
**W**ho knows if the spirit of the sons of Adam ascends upward: and if the spirit of the beasts descends downward?
**A**nd I discovered nothing to be better: than for a man to be glad in his work: and this to be his portion. For who shall lead him: that he may know the things that are to come after?

**H**e turned me to other things: and I saw the calumnies which are carried out under the sun. And the tears of the innocent: and no comforter: nor were they able to resist their violence: all being destitute of help.
**A**nd I praised the dead more than the living: and I judged him more fortunate than both: who is not yet born: nor has seen the evils which are done under the sun.
**A**gain, I contemplated all the labors of men: and their industries: I noticed they lie open to the envy of a neighbor. And in this therefore is vanity: and hollow anxiety.
**T**he fool folds his hands: and eats his own flesh, saying:
**B**etter is a handful with rest: than both hands full: with labor and affliction of mind.
**C**onsidering, I found another vanity under the sun.
**T**here is one: and he has no second: no son: no brother: and yet he does not cease to labor. Nor are his eyes satisfied with riches: nor does he reconsider, saying: For whom do I labor and defraud my soul of good things? In this also is vanity: and a most wretched affliction.
**I**t is better for two to be together than one. For they have the reward of their society.
**I**f one falls: he shall be supported by the other. Woe to him who is alone: because when he falls: he has no one to lift him up.
**A**nd if two sleep together: they shall warm each other. How shall one be warmed?
**A**nd if someone prevails against one: two shall resist him.
**A** threefold cord: is difficult to break.
**B**etter is a poor and wise boy than an old and foolish king: who knows not how to provide for the future.
**B**ecause sometimes someone goes out from prison and chains: to a kingdom. And another born in a kingdom: is consumed by poverty.
**I** have seen all the living who walk under the sun: with the second youth: who shall rise up in his place.
**I**nfinite is the number of the people: of all who were before him. And those who are to be afterward: shall not rejoice in him. But this also is vanity: and affliction of spirit.
**G**uard your foot entering the house of God: and draw near so that you may hear. For obedience is much better than the victims of fools: who know not what evil they do.

**B**e not rash in what you say: nor let your heart be swift: to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven: and you are upon the earth. Therefore let your words be few.
**D**reams follow many cares: and in many words: folly is found.
**I**f you have vowed anything to the Lord, do not delay to pay it. For an unhappy and foolish promise displeases him. But whatever you have vowed: pay it.
**I**t is much better not to vow: than after a vow not to pay what was promised.
**D**o not give your mouth that it may make your flesh to sin. Nor say before the angel: there is no providence. Lest perhaps God, being angry at your words: should dissipate all the works of your hands.
**W**here there are many dreams: there are many vanities: and innumerable words. But you, fear God.
**I**f you see the calumnies of the needy: and violent judgments: and justice subverted in a province: do not wonder at this matter. Because another is higher than the high: and over these: others are more eminent and high. And furthermore, the king of the land commands the servant.

**T**he avaricious man will not be satisfied with money. And he who loves riches: shall not take fruit [from them]. And this therefore is vanity.
**W**here there are many riches: there are many also who eat them. And what does it profit the owner: except that he sees it with his eyes?
**S**leep is sweet to the laborer: whether he has eaten little or much. But the satiety of the rich man does not allow him to sleep.
**T**here is also another most wretched infirmity: which I saw under the sun. Riches kept to the hurt of their owner. For they perish in the worst affliction.
**H**e has begotten a son who shall be in extreme want.
**A**s he came out naked from his mother’s womb: so he shall return: and he shall carry nothing with him from his labor.
**A** wretched infirmity indeed. Just as he came: so shall he return. What therefore does it profit him: that he has labored for the wind?
**A**ll the days of his life he eats in darkness: and in many cares: in gloom: and in sadness.
**T**his therefore seemed good to me: that one should eat: and drink: and enjoy gladness.
