Submit your shoulder and carry her, and do not be weary of her bonds. Approach her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your strength. Search for her, and she will be revealed to you; and once you have gained possession, do not let her go. For in the end you will find her rest, and she shall be turned into your delight. Then her shackles will be a strong protection for you and her foundations a support of virtue; her yoke shall be a robe of glory. For the color of life <note>original: "color vitae"; this refers to the vibrant, life-giving beauty found in following Wisdom.</note> is in her, and her bonds are a saving bandage. You shall put her on as a robe of glory, and set her upon you as a crown of joy. My son, if you pay attention, you will learn these things; and if you apply your mind, you will be wise. If you incline your ear, you will receive instruction; and if you love to listen, you will be wise. Stand in the company of the prudent elders, and join yourself to their wisdom from your heart, so that you may hear every discourse about God, and let the praise-filled proverbs not escape you. And if you see a man of understanding, wake up early to go to him, and let your feet wear out the steps of his doors. Let your thoughts be on the precepts of God, and be especially constant in His commandments; and He Himself will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom shall be granted to you.

My soul approached life even before death, and my life was drawing near to the world below <note>original: "inferno deorsum"; in this context, it refers to the grave or the depths of Sheol rather than a place of punishment.</note>. I looked for the help of men, and there was none. I was mindful of Your mercy, O Lord, and of Your works which have been from the beginning of time. For You rescue those who wait for You, Lord, and You deliver them from the hands of the nations. You have exalted my dwelling upon the earth, and I prayed against the flowing away of death. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord <note>original: "patrem domini mei"; medieval commentators often interpreted this as an early reference to the Trinity (God the Father and the Son), though in the original Hebrew it likely meant "the Father of my life."</note>, that He might not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help. I will praise Your name constantly, and I will praise it with thanksgiving, and my prayer was heard. And You delivered me from destruction, and rescued me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks and sing praise to You, and I will bless the name of the Lord.

Do not say, "It is because of God that she [Wisdom] is absent," for you should not do what He hates. Do not say, "He Himself led me astray," for He has no need of a wicked man. The Lord hates every abomination of error, and it will not be loved by those who fear Him. He Himself established man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his own counsel <note>This refers to the concept of free will; God gave humanity the power to choose their own path.</note>. He added His commandments and precepts: if you wish to keep the commandments, they shall preserve you, and to perform faithful service forever. He has set before you water and fire; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish. Before man is life and death, good and evil; whatever he chooses shall be given to him. For the wisdom of God is great, and He is mighty in power, seeing all things without ceasing. The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear Him, and He Himself recognizes every work of man. He has commanded no one to act wickedly, and He has given no one permission to sin.

I will explain discipline to you, and I will search out my discourse in truth. By the judgment of God His works have been from the beginning, and from their institution He distinguished their parts. He adorned their works forever; they have not hungered, nor labored, and they have not ceased from their works. No one shall ever crowd his neighbor. Do not be unbelieving of His word. After these things, God looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things. The soul of every animal declared itself before His face, and into the earth is their return again.

<margin>n</margin>
Do not become an enemy to your neighbor instead of a friend, for the wicked man shall inherit reproach and insult, as will every envious and double-tongued sinner. Do not exalt yourself in the thoughts of your soul like a bull, lest perhaps your strength be shattered through folly, and it eat your leaves, and destroy your fruits, and you be left like a dry tree in the desert. For a wicked soul will destroy the one who possesses it, and gives him over to the joy of his enemies, and leads him into the lot of the ungodly.

The substance of a man perishes in luxury, and his riches will be cast away. My son, let there be no sins in you, and do not add sin upon sin. And do not say, "The mercy of the Lord is great, He will have mercy on the multitude of my sins." For both mercy and wrath come quickly from Him, and His anger looks upon sinners. Do not delay to be converted to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day. For His wrath shall come suddenly, and in the time of vengeance He will destroy you. Do not be anxious for unjust riches, for they will profit you nothing in the day of death and vengeance.

<column-break/>

...let it not please you in the way of the unjust, knowing that even unto the depths below they will not be pleasing. Keep far from the man who has the power to kill, and you will not have the suspicion of the fear of death. And if you approach him, do not commit any fault, lest perhaps he take away your life. Know that you are walking in the midst of snares, and you are walking upon the battlements. According to your strength, guard yourself from your neighbor, and treat with the wise and the prudent.

Wisdom preaches outdoors; she gives her voice in the streets. She cries out at the head of the crowds; at the entrance of the city gates she utters her words, saying: "How long, O little ones, will you love childhood? And how long will fools desire those things which are harmful to them, and the imprudent hate knowledge? Turn back at my correction. Behold, I will bring forth my spirit to you, and I will show you my words. Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and there was no one who looked. You have despised all my counsel, and neglected my rebukes. I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will mock when that which you feared comes upon you—when sudden calamity rushes in, and destruction seizes you like a storm; when tribulation and distress come upon you. Then they will call upon me, and I will not hear; they will rise early and they will not find me. This is because they hated discipline, and did not choose the fear of the Lord, nor did they consent to my counsel, and they detracted from all my correction. Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own counsels. The turning away of the little ones shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them. But he who hears me shall rest without fear, and shall enjoy abundance, with the fear of evils taken away."

He who fears the Lord will tremble at nothing, and he will not be afraid, because He Himself is his hope. Blessed is the soul of one who fears the Lord. To whom does he look, and who is his strength? The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear Him. He is a protector of power, a pillar of virtue, a shelter from the heat, and a shade for the midday. He is a guard against stumbling and a help against falling. He exalts the soul and illuminates the eyes, giving health, and life, and blessing. The offering of those who sacrifice from ill-gotten gains is stained, and the mockeries of the unjust are not accepted. The Lord is for those alone who wait for Him in the way of truth and justice. The Most High does not approve the gifts of the wicked, nor does He look upon the offerings of the unjust, nor will He be appeased for sins by a multitude of their sacrifices. He who offers a sacrifice from the substance of the poor is like one who kills a son in the sight of his father. The bread of the needy is the life of the poor; he who defrauds them is a man of blood. He who takes away bread earned in sweat is like one who kills his neighbor. He who sheds blood and he who defrauds a laborer are brothers. One building and another tearing down—what does it profit them but labor? One praying and another cursing—whose voice will God hear? He who is washed after touching a corpse <note>original: "baptizatur a mortuo"; this refers to ritual purification laws in the Old Testament where touching a dead body rendered a person "unclean."</note> and touches it again, what does his washing profit him? So is the man who fasts for his sins, and doing the same things again—what does he profit by humbling himself? Who will hear his prayer?

Let it not hold you back from paying a debt in its time, and do not delay to be justified even until death, for the reward of God remains forever. Before prayer, prepare your soul, and do not be like a man who tempts God. Remember the wrath on the day of your end, and the time of retribution when He shall turn away His face. Remember poverty in the time of abundance, and the needs of poverty in the day of riches. From morning until evening the time shall be changed, and all these things are swift in the eyes of God. A wise man will be fearful in all things, and in the days of sins he will beware of sluggishness. Every shrewd person recognizes wisdom, and to the one who finds her, he will give praise. Those who are sensible in words have themselves acted wisely, and understood truth and justice, and poured forth proverbs and judgments. Do not follow after your lusts, and turn away from your own will. If you grant your soul its desire, it will make you a joy to your enemies. Do not delight in crowds, nor in small groups, for their gathering is constant. Do not be diminished in a contest over a loan when you have nothing in your purse. For you will be an enemy to your own life.

The beauty of a woman gladdens the face of her husband, and she is a desire beyond all a man's longing. If there is a tongue of healing, and of mitigation, and of mercy, her husband is not like the other sons of men. He who possesses a good wife begins a possession; she is a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest. Where there is no hedge, the possession will be plundered; and where there is no woman, the needy man groans. Who trusts a man who has no nest, and who turns aside wherever evening finds him, like a robber prepared to go from city to city?

<meta>This page continues the moral and ethical instructions found in the Book of Sirach (also known as Ecclesiasticus). Following the previous discussion on the discipline of Wisdom, the text now moves into practical warnings regarding social associations, the nature of wealth, the inevitability of death, and the vastness of God’s judgment. It emphasizes the importance of the "fear of the Lord" as the foundation of a virtuous life.</meta>

<margin>A</margin>
**W**ho will pity a snake charmer bitten by a serpent, or anyone who approaches wild beasts? So it is for one who keeps company with a sinner and is entangled in his sins. **H**e will stay with you for an hour, but if you turn away, he will not endure it. **A**n enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he schemes to throw you into a pit. **A**n enemy has tears in his eyes, but if the opportunity arises, he will not be satisfied with blood. **I**f evils befall you, you will find him there ahead of you. **W**ith his eyes he will appear humble, but as if helping you, he will undermine your footsteps. **H**e will wag his head and clap his hands, and whispering many things, he will change his expression.

<margin>Q</margin>
**H**e who touches pitch shall be defiled by it, and he who associates with the proud will put on pride. **H**e takes a burden upon himself who associates with one more honorable than himself; do not be a companion to one richer than you. **W**hat agreement can there be between a cooking pot and an earthenware jar? For when they collide, the jar will be broken. <note>original: "caccabus ad ollam"; this proverb warns that the poor (the fragile clay jar) cannot survive a social "collision" with the wealthy (the heavy iron pot).</note> **T**he rich man acts unjustly and fumes; but the poor man, though harmed, remains silent. **I**f you are generous, he will use you; if you have nothing, he will abandon you. **I**f you have means, he will live with you and exhaust you, and he will feel no sorrow for you. **I**f he has a need, he will deceive you; smiling, he will give you hope, telling you good things and saying: "What do you need?" **A**nd he will shame you with his feasts until he drains you two or three times over, and in the end, he will mock you. Later, seeing you, he will abandon you and wag his head at you. **H**umble yourself before God, and wait for His hand. **T**ake care that you are not seduced into folly and humbled. **D**o not be humble in your wisdom, lest being humbled you are seduced into foolishness. **W**hen invited by a powerful man, withdraw; and because of this, he will invite you all the more. **D**o not be pushy, lest you be repelled; but do not stay too far away, lest you be forgotten. **D**o not try to speak with him as an equal, nor believe his many words. For with much talk he will test you, and smiling, he will question you about your secrets. **H**is cruel mind will preserve your words; he will not spare you from malice or chains. **B**e cautious and pay diligent attention to what you hear, for you walk on the edge of your own ruin. **H**earing these things, see them as if in a dream, and stay awake. **T**hroughout all your life, love God and call upon Him for your salvation. **E**very animal loves its own kind, and so every man his neighbor. **A**ll flesh joins with its like, and every man associates with his own kind. **I**f a wolf associates with a lamb, so does a sinner with the righteous. **W**hat fellowship is there between a holy man and a dog? Or what portion has the rich with the poor? **T**he wild donkey in the desert is the prey of lions; so the poor are the pastures of the rich. **A**nd as humility is an abomination to the proud, so the poor man is an execration to the rich. **A** rich man, when shaken, is supported by his friends; but when the humble falls, he is pushed away even by those he knows. **W**hen a rich man is deceived, he has many to help him; he speaks proudly, and they justify him. **T**he humble man is deceived and is even rebuked; he speaks sensibly, and no place is given to him. **T**he rich man speaks, and everyone is silent, and they carry his word up to the clouds. **T**he poor man speaks, and they say: "Who is this?" And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him.

<margin>B</margin>
**W**ealth is good for him who has no sin in his conscience, and poverty is most wicked in the mouth of the ungodly. **T**he heart of a man changes his face, whether for good or for evil. **T**he trace of a good heart and a good face you will find with difficulty and labor. **B**lessed is the man who has not slipped by a word from his mouth, and is not stung by the sorrow of sin. **H**appy is he who has no sorrow of mind, and has not fallen away from his hope. **F**or a greedy and grasping man, wealth is without reason; and for an envious man, to what end is gold? **H**e who gathers by depriving his own soul gathers for others, and another shall live luxuriously on his goods. **H**e who is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? He shall not find joy in his own goods. **N**one is more wicked than he who envies himself, for this is the reward of his malice. **E**ven if he does good, he does it ignorantly and unwillingly, and in the end, he manifests his malice. **W**icked is the eye of the envious, turning away his face and despising his own soul. **T**he eye of the greedy is insatiable in his portion of iniquity; he will not be satisfied until he consumes and withers his own soul. **A**n evil eye tends toward evil, and he shall not be satisfied with bread; he shall be in need and sorrow at his own table.

<margin>F</margin>
**M**y son, if you have anything, do good for yourself and offer worthy oblations to God. **R**emember that death does not delay, and the decree of the underworld has been shown to you. <note>original: "testamentum inferni"; refers to the biblical concept that Sheol or the grave is the final destination for all living things.</note> **F**or the covenant of this world shall die by death. **B**efore death, do good to your friend, and according to your strength, stretch out your hand and give to the poor. **D**o not be cheated of a good day, and let not a small portion of a good gift pass you by. **W**ill you not leave your sorrows and labors to others? **I**n the division of the lot, give and receive, and justify your soul. **B**efore your death, work righteousness, for there is no food to be found in the underworld. **A**ll flesh shall grow old like grass, and like a leaf budding on a green tree. **S**ome are born and others are cast down; so is the generation of flesh and blood: one ends and another is born. **E**very corruptible work shall fail in the end, and he who works it shall go with it. **B**ut every chosen work shall be justified, and he who works it shall be honored for it. **B**lessed is the man who dwells in wisdom, and who meditates on his justice, and thinks in his mind of the oversight of God. **H**e who considers her ways in his heart, and understands her secrets, goes after her like a tracker and stays in her paths. **H**e looks through her windows and listens at her doors. **H**e rests near her house and, driving a stake into her wall, he will set up his little hut by her hand, and good things shall rest in his hut forever. **H**e shall set his children under her shelter and shall dwell under her branches. **H**e shall be protected under her shelter from the heat and shall rest in her glory.

<margin>Q</margin>
**H**e who fears God will do good, and he who possesses justice will lay hold of her. **S**he will meet him like an honored mother, and like a bride taken from virginity, she will receive him. **S**he will feed him with the bread of life and understanding, and give him the water of saving wisdom to drink. **S**he will be established in him and he shall not be moved; she will hold him and he shall not be put to shame. **S**he will exalt him among his neighbors. **A**nd in the midst of the assembly, she will open his mouth and fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothe him with a robe of glory. **S**he will heap joy and exultation upon him and give him an everlasting name for an inheritance. **F**oolish men will not lay hold of her, but sensible men will meet her. **F**oolish men will not see her, for she is far from pride and deceit. **L**ying men will not be mindful of her, but truthful men shall be found in her and shall have success even until the inspection of God. **P**raise is not beautiful in the mouth of a sinner, for wisdom was not sent by God. **F**or the wisdom of God shall stand by praise, and shall abound in a faithful mouth, and the Ruler will give it to him. **D**o not say: "Through God she is absent," for you should not do what He hates. **D**o not say: "He has led me astray," for He has no need of ungodly men. **T**he Lord hates every abomination of error, and it will not be loved by those who fear Him. **G**od made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel. **H**e added His commandments and precepts. If you choose to keep the commandments, they shall preserve you, and to keep faith forever is well-pleasing. **H**e has set before you water and fire; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish. **B**efore man are life and death, good and evil; whatever pleases him shall be given to him. **F**or the wisdom of God is great, and He is strong in power, seeing all things without ceasing. **T**he eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear Him, and He knows every work of man. **H**e has commanded no one to act ungodly, and He has given no one license to sin. **F**or He does not desire a multitude of unfaithful and useless children.

<column-break/>

<margin>N</margin>
**D**o not rejoice in ungodly children if they are multiplied. Do not take delight in them if the fear of God is not in them. **D**o not trust in their life, and do not look upon their labors. **F**or one who fears God is better than a thousand ungodly children. **A**nd it is more useful to die without children than to leave behind ungodly ones. **B**y one wise man a country shall be inhabited, but by three ungodly men it shall be made desolate. **M**y eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard even stronger things than these. **I**n a congregation of sinners a fire will be kindled, and in an unbelieving nation wrath will burn. **T**he giants of old did not pray for their sins, who were destroyed for trusting in their own strength. <note>original: "antiqui gigantes"; a reference to the Nephilim or the rebels before the Flood in Genesis.</note> **H**e did not spare the place where Lot resided, but detested them for the pride of their word. **H**e had no mercy on them, destroying the whole nation that extolled itself in its sins. **A**nd so it was with the six hundred thousand footmen who were gathered in the hardness of their hearts; and if there had been one stiff-necked man, it would be a wonder if he had gone unpunished. **F**or mercy and wrath are with Him; He is powerful to forgive and to pour out wrath. **A**s His mercy is great, so also is His correction; He judges a man according to his works. **T**he sinner shall not escape with his plunder, and the suffering of the one who shows mercy shall not be delayed. **E**very mercy shall make a place for each one according to the merit of his works and according to the understanding of his pilgrimage. **D**o not say: "I shall be hidden from God; who will remember me from on high?" **I** shall not be recognized among a great people; for what is my soul in such an immense creation? **B**ehold, the heaven, and the heavens of heavens, the abyss, and the whole earth, and all that are in them, shall be moved in His sight. **T**he mountains and the hills and the foundations of the earth, when God looks upon them, shall be shaken with trembling. **I**n all these things the heart is senseless; but every heart is understood by Him. **W**ho understands His ways and the tempest which the eye of man shall not see? **F**or many of His works are hidden; but who shall declare the works of His justice? Or who shall endure them? **F**or the covenant is far from some, and the examination of men is at the end. **H**e who is small in heart thinks vain things, and the imprudent and erring man thinks foolish things. **H**ear me, my son, and learn the discipline of understanding, and pay attention to my words in your heart. **I** will speak discipline in equity and seek to declare wisdom. **P**ay attention to my words in your heart, and in equity of spirit I declare the virtues which God placed in His works from the beginning, and His knowledge in truth. **B**y the judgment of God His works are from the beginning, and from their institution He distinguished their parts and their beginnings in their generations. **H**e adorned their works forever; they have neither hungered nor labored, and they have not ceased from their works. **N**o one shall crowd his neighbor forever. **D**o not be unbelieving of His word. **A**fter this, God looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things. **T**he soul of every living thing He declared before His face, and into it they shall return again.

<margin>D</margin>
**G**od created man from the earth and made him according to His own image. **H**e turned him back into it again and clothed him with strength like Himself. **H**e gave him a number of days and time and gave him power over those things that are upon the earth. **H**e put the fear of man over all flesh, and he ruled over beasts and birds. **H**e created from him a helper like himself; He gave them counsel, a tongue, eyes, ears, and a heart to think with, and He filled them with the discipline of understanding. **H**e created in them the science of the spirit, filled their hearts with sense, and showed them both evil and good. **H**e set His eye upon their hearts to show them the greatness of His works, that they might praise the name of holiness and glory in His wonders, and declare the greatness of His works. **H**e gave them discipline and gave them the law of life for an inheritance. **H**e established an eternal covenant with them and showed them the justice of His judgments. **T**heir eyes saw the greatness of His honor, and their ears heard the honor of His voice. **A**nd He said to them: "Keep yourselves from all iniquity." **A**nd He gave each of them commandments concerning his neighbor. **T**heir ways are always before Him; they are not hidden from His eyes. **O**ver every nation He appointed a ruler, but Israel became the manifest portion of God. **A**ll their works are like the sun in the sight of God, and His eyes look without ceasing upon their ways. **T**heir iniquities are not hidden from God, and all their sins are in the sight of God. **T**he alms of a man are like a signet ring with Him, and He will preserve the grace of a man as the apple of his eye. **A**nd afterward He will rise up and render retribution to each of them upon their heads and turn them down into the lower parts of the earth. **B**ut to those who repent He has given the way of justice, and He has strengthened those who were failing in endurance and appointed for them the lot of truth. **T**urn to the Lord and leave your sins. **P**ray before the face of the Lord and diminish your offenses. **R**eturn to the Lord and turn away from your injustice, and hate abomination exceedingly. **K**now the justices and judgments of God, and stand in the lot of the proposal and prayer of the Most High God. **G**o into the portions of the holy world with the living and those who give praise to God. **D**o not delay in the error of the ungodly; confess before death. Confession perishes from the dead as if it were nothing. **A**s one living and sound, you shall confess and praise God and glory in His mercies. **H**ow great is the mercy of the Lord and His forgiveness for those who turn to Him! **F**or all things cannot be in men, because the son of man is not immortal, and they have taken pleasure in the vanity of evil. **W**hat is brighter than the sun? Yet it fails. Or what is more wicked than that which flesh and blood has conceived? And this shall be rebuked. **H**e beholds the power of the height of heaven, while all men are but earth and ashes.

<margin>Q</margin>
**H**e who lives forever created all things together. **G**od alone shall be justified, and He remains an unconquered King forever. **W**ho is able to declare His works? **W**ho shall investigate His great deeds? **W**ho shall declare the power of His greatness? Or who shall further declare His mercy? **I**t is not possible to diminish or increase, nor to find the great works of God. **W**hen a man has finished, then he shall begin; and when he rests, he shall work. <note>original: "Cum consummauerit homo, tunc incipiet"; suggests that human understanding is so limited that when we think we have finished learning about God, we are only just beginning.</note> **W**hat is man, and what is his glory? Or what is his good, or what is his evil? **T**he number of the days of men is at most a hundred years; they are accounted as a drop of water from the sea, and as a pebble of sand; so are a few years in the day of eternity. **B**ecause of this, God is patient with them and pours out His mercy upon them. **H**e saw that the presumption of their heart was evil and knew their destruction was wicked. **T**herefore He fulfilled His forgiveness toward them and showed them the way of equity. **T**he compassion of man is toward his neighbor, but the mercy of God is upon all flesh. **H**e who has mercy teaches and instructs like a shepherd ruling his flock. **H**e has mercy on those who receive the instruction of His judgments and those who hasten in His decrees.

<margin>F</margin>
**M**y son, in your good deeds give no complaint, and in every gift do not give the sorrow of an evil word. **D**oes not the dew cool the heat? So a word is better than a gift. **B**ehold, is not a word better than a good gift? But both are found with a justified man. **A** fool will upbraid bitterly, and the gift of the undisciplined makes the eyes waste away. **B**efore judgment, prepare justice for yourself, and learn before you speak. **A**pply medicine before you are sick, and before judgment examine yourself, and in the sight of God you will find forgiveness. **H**umble yourself before you are sick, and in the time of infirmity show your conversation. <note>original: "conuersationem"; in this context, it refers to one's conduct or way of life.</note> **D**o not be hindered from praying always, and do not fear to be justified even unto death, for the reward of God remains forever. **B**efore prayer, prepare your soul, and do not be like a man who tempts God. **R**emember the wrath in the day of consummation and the time of retribution in the turning of His face. **R**emember poverty in the time of abundance and the needs of poverty in the day of riches. **F**rom morning until evening the time shall be changed, and all these things are swift in the eyes of God. **A** wise man will fear in all things, and in the days of sins he will guard against sloth. **E**very clever man recognizes wisdom and will give praise to him who finds her. **T**hose sensible in words have themselves acted wisely and understood truth and justice and poured forth perfect proverbs. **D**o not follow after your lusts, and turn away from your own will. **I**f you grant your soul its desires, it will make you a joy to your enemies. **D**o not delight in crowds, nor in small ones, for their gathering is constant. **D**o not be impoverished by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse, **f**or you will be envious of your own life.

<margin>O</margin>
**A** drunken workman shall not be enriched, and he who despises small things shall fall away little by little.

<summary>This page contains a series of moral instructions from the Book of Sirach, warning against bad company, the dangers of wealth without virtue, and the certainty of death. It emphasizes God's role as the Creator who gave humans free will, wisdom, and the law, while highlighting the vastness of divine mercy compared to human frailty.</summary>

--- Page 181 ---
<meta>This page continues the moral and ethical instructions found in the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), moving from social interactions with the wealthy into specific warnings against personal vices—such as lust, drunkenness, and gossip—and culminating in a poetic personification of Wisdom herself.</meta>

<margin>V</margin>**W**ine and women will make even the wise fall away <note>original: "apostatare"; to abandon one's faith or moral standing</note>, and will bring rebuke upon the sensible. He who joins himself to prostitutes will become wicked. Decay and worms will inherit him, and he shall be held up as a great example of ruin; his soul shall be taken out of the number of the living.
<margin>Q</margin>**H**e who believes quickly is fickle of heart and will be diminished; and he who sins against his own soul shall have nothing. He who rejoices in iniquity shall be marked with disgrace, and he who hates correction shall have a shortened life; but he who hates gossip extinguishes malice. He who sins against his own soul shall repent, and he who delights in malice shall be branded. Do not repeat a wicked or harsh word, and you will not be diminished.
<margin>N</margin>**D**o not reveal your thoughts to either friend or foe; and if you have committed a fault, do not lay it bare. For he will hear you, and watch you, and while pretending to defend your sin, he will threaten you—and so it will be for you forever. Have you heard a word against your neighbor? Let it die within you, trusting that it will not burst you. A fool is in labor because of a word, like the groaning of a woman giving birth to a child. As an arrow stuck in a dog’s thigh, so is a word in the heart of a fool.
<margin>C</margin>**A**dmonish a friend, for perhaps he did not know and might say: "I did not do it." Or if he did do it, that he may not do it again. Admonish your neighbor, for perhaps he did not say it; and if he did say it, that he may not repeat it. Admonish a friend, for often a mistake is made; and do not believe every word. There is one who slips with the tongue, but not from the heart. For who is there who has not offended with his tongue? Admonish your neighbor before you threaten him, and give place to the fear of the Most High. For all wisdom is the fear of God, and in it is the fear of God; and in all wisdom is the fulfillment of the law. The learning of wickedness is not wisdom, and the thoughts of sinners are not prudence. There is a wickedness that is an abomination, and there is a fool who is lacking in wisdom.
<margin>M</margin>**B**etter is a man who lacks wisdom but is deficient in understanding yet lives in fear, than one who abounds in understanding but transgresses the law of the Most High. There is a certain cleverness that is unjust, and there is one who speaks a certain word while telling the truth. There is one who wickedly humbles himself, while his inner parts are full of deceit. And there is a just man who submits himself excessively out of great humility. And there is one who bows his face and pretends not to see what is unknown; and if he is prevented from sinning by weakness of strength, if he finds a time for doing evil, he will do it. A man is known by his appearance, and a sensible man is recognized by the look on his face. The clothing of the body, the laughter of the teeth, and the gait of a man announce the truth about him. There is a false rebuke in the anger of an insulting person, and there is a judgment that is not proven to be good; and there is one who is silent, and he is the prudent one.
<margin>Q</margin>**H**ow good it is to reprove rather than to be angry, and not to hinder one who confesses in prayer. The lust of a eunuch deflowering a young girl is like one who renders an unjust judgment by force. How good it is, when reproved, to show repentance, for so you shall escape voluntary sin. There is one who is silent and is found to be wise, and there is one who is hateful because he is headlong in speaking. There is one who is silent because he has no skill in speech, and there is one who is silent knowing the proper time for moderation. A wise man will be silent until the right time, but the wanton and the imprudent will not observe the time. He who uses many words will wound his own soul, and he who takes authority upon himself unjustly shall be hated. There is success in evil things for an undisciplined man, and there is a find that leads to loss. There is a gift that is not useful, and there is a gift whose reward is double. There is a loss for the sake of glory, and there is one who shall lift his head from a state of humility. There is one who redeems many things for a small price, and restores them sevenfold.
<margin>S</margin>**A** wise man makes himself lovable in his words, but the graces of fools shall be poured away. The gift of a fool will not be useful to you, for his eyes are sevenfold <note>original: "septupli sunt"; meaning he expects seven times more in return</note>. He will give little and reproach much, and the opening of his mouth is an inflammation. Today a man lends, and tomorrow he asks for it back; such a man is hateful. A fool will have no friend, and there will be no thanks for his good deeds. For those who eat his bread have false tongues. How often and how many will laugh at him? For he does not distribute what he had to hold with a right judgment, nor likewise what he did not have. A slip of a false tongue is like one falling on a pavement; thus the fall of the wicked will come quickly. A graceless man is like a vain fable; it will be constantly in the mouth of the undisciplined. A parable from a fool's mouth will be rejected, for he does not tell it in its proper time. There is one who is forbidden to sin by poverty, and in his rest he will be stung. There is one who loses his soul through shame, and because of an imprudent person he will lose it; by respecting persons <note>original: "personæ acceptione"; showing favoritism or fearing what others think</note>, he will destroy himself.
<margin>E</margin>**T**here is one who out of shame makes a promise to a friend, and has gained him as an enemy for nothing. A lie is a wicked disgrace in a man, and it will be constantly in the mouth of the undisciplined. A thief is better than a constant liar, but both shall inherit perdition. The habits of lying men are without honor, and their confusion is with them without ceasing.
<margin>S</margin>**A** wise man brings himself forward in his words, and a prudent man will please the great. He who works the land shall exalt his heap of grain, and he who works justice shall himself be exalted; but he who pleases the great escapes iniquity. Presents and gifts blind the eyes of judges, and like a muzzle in the mouth, they turn away their rebukes. Hidden wisdom and invisible treasure: what use is there in either? Better is he who hides his folly than a man who hides his wisdom.

<column-break/>

<margin>I</margin>**T**he lazy man is pelted with a filthy stone, and everyone will speak of his disgrace. The lazy man is pelted with the dung of oxen, and everyone who touches him will shake his hands. A father's shame comes from an undisciplined son, and a daughter shall be born to his diminishment. A prudent daughter is an inheritance to her husband, but she who brings shame becomes a disgrace to her parent. The bold woman shames both father and husband, and she shall not be less than the impious; she shall be dishonored by both. Music during mourning is an untimely story, but stripes and doctrine <note>instruction through discipline</note> are at all times part of wisdom.
<margin>Q</margin>**H**e who teaches a fool is like one who glues a potsherd together.
<margin>Q</margin>**H**e who tells a story to one who does not listen is like one who wakes a sleeper from a deep sleep. In a monument for a fool, it is known what is there; weep over the dead, for his light has failed; and weep over the fool, for his understanding has failed. Weep but a little over the dead, because he has found rest. But the wicked life of the most wicked is worse than the death of a fool. Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for a fool and the impious, it lasts all the days of their life. Do not talk much with a fool, and do not go to the senseless man. Guard yourself from him so that you do not have trouble, and you will not be defiled by his sin. Turn away from him and you will find rest, and you will not be wearied by his folly. What is heavier than lead? And what other name does it have than "fool"? Sand, salt, and a mass of iron are easier to carry than an imprudent, foolish, and impious man. A wooden frame bound into the foundation of a building will not be shaken; so also is a heart established in the thought of counsel. The thought of the wise will not be corrupted by fear at any time. Like a fence on a high place, or a plastering on a wall exposed to the wind, so a fearful heart in the thought of a fool will not stand against any rush of bitterness. A trembling heart in the thought of a fool will not fear at any time; so also is he who remains always in the commandments of God. He who pricks the eye brings forth tears; and he who pricks the heart brings forth feeling.
<margin>I</margin>**H**e who throws a stone at birds drives them away; so also he who insults a friend dissolves the friendship. Even if you have drawn a sword against a friend, do not despair; for there is a way back to a friend. If you have opened a sad mouth against a friend, do not fear; for there can be reconciliation, except in the case of insult, and reproach, and pride, and the revealing of secrets, and a treacherous wound; in all these things a friend will flee. Maintain faithfulness with a friend in his poverty, so that you may also rejoice in his prosperity. In the time of his trouble remain faithful to him, so that you may be a co-heir in his inheritance. Before a fire in a furnace, vapor and smoke rise up; so before blood come curses and insults and threats. I will not be ashamed to greet a friend, nor will I hide myself from his face; and if evils happen to me through him, I will endure it. Everyone who hears will beware of him. Who will set a guard over my mouth, and a reliable seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall because of them, and that my tongue may not destroy me?
<margin>D</margin>**O** Lord, Father and Ruler of my life, do not leave me to their counsel, nor let me fall into that reproach. Who will apply whips to my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom to my heart, so that they may not spare me in my ignorances, and that their faults may not appear, lest my ignorances increase, and my ignorances be multiplied, and my sins abound in your sight, and I fall in the sight of my adversaries, and my enemy rejoices? O Lord, Father and God of my life, do not leave me to their thoughts. Do not give me haughty eyes, and turn away all evil desire from me. Take from me the lusts of the belly, and let not the lusts of the flesh take hold of me, and do not give me over to an irreverent and unrestrained mind.
**H**ear, children, the discipline of the mouth; and he who keeps it shall not perish by his lips, nor be scandalized by wicked works. A sinner is caught in his own vanity; and the proud and the curser shall be scandalized by them. Let not your mouth be accustomed to swearing oaths, for there are many falls in it. Let not the naming of God be continuous in your mouth, and do not mix in the names of the saints, for you will not be free from blame regarding them.
<margin>S</margin>**F**or just as a servant who is constantly questioned does not lack bruises, so everyone who swears and uses the Name shall not be entirely purged from sin. A man who swears much shall be filled with iniquity, and the scourge shall not depart from his house. And if he makes it void, his sin shall be upon him; and if he dissembles, he sins doubly; and if he swears in vain, he shall not be justified, for his house shall be filled with retribution. There is also another kind of speech that is opposite to death; let it not be found in the heritage of Jacob. For all these things shall be taken away from the merciful, and they shall not wallow in sins. Let not your mouth be accustomed to undisciplined speech, for in it is the word of sin. Remember your father and mother, for you sit in the midst of the great; lest perhaps God forget you in their sight, and through your constant habit you become foolish and suffer reproach, and wish you had not been born, and curse the day of your birth. A man accustomed to words of reproach will not be instructed in all his days. Two kinds of men abound in sins, and the third brings on wrath and destruction. A hot soul, like a burning fire, will not be extinguished until it swallows something. And a wicked man in the mouth of his flesh will not cease until he kindles a fire. To every fornicator, every bread is sweet; he will not grow weary until the end. Every man who transgresses his own bed, despising his own soul and saying: "Who sees me? Darkness surrounds me, and the walls cover me, and no one beholds me; whom do I fear? The Most High will not remember my sins." And he does not understand that His eye sees everything; for the fear of such a man expels the fear of God from him. He fears only the eyes of men, and does not know that the eyes of the Lord are much brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and the depth of the abyss, and looking into the hidden parts of the hearts of men. For to the Lord God all things were known before they were created; so also after they are perfected, He looks upon all things. This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and shall be chased like a young colt; and where he did not expect, he shall be caught. And he shall be a disgrace to all, because he did not understand the fear of the Lord. So also is every woman who leaves her husband and establishes an inheritance from an adulterous marriage. For first, she was unfaithful to the law of the Most High; second, she sinned against her husband; third, she played the harlot in adultery and established children for herself by another man. This woman shall be brought into the assembly, and her children shall be looked upon. Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall yield no fruit. She shall leave her curse for a memory, and her disgrace shall not be blotted out. And those who are left behind shall recognize that nothing is better than the fear of God, and nothing is sweeter than to look upon the commandments of the Lord. It is great glory to follow the Lord; for length of days shall be received from Him.
<margin>S</margin>**W**isdom shall praise her own soul, and she shall be honored in God, and she shall glory in the midst of her people. In the assemblies of the Most High she shall open her mouth, and in the presence of His power she shall glory. In the midst of her people she shall be exalted, and in the holy fullness she shall be admired. In the multitude of the elect she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed, saying: "I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature. I made it so that an unfailing light arose in the heavens, and I covered the whole earth like a mist. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of cloud. I alone have compassed the circuit of heaven, and have penetrated into the bottom of the deep, and have walked in the waves of the sea, and have stood in all the earth. And in every people, and in every nation, I have had the primacy. And by my power I have trodden under foot the hearts of all the high and the low; and in all these things I have sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord. Then the Creator of all things commanded and spoke to me, and He who created me rested in my tabernacle, and He said to me: 'Dwell in Jacob, and have your inheritance in Israel, and take root in my elect.' From the beginning, and before the ages, I was created, and unto the world to come I shall not cease to be, and in the holy dwelling place I have ministered before Him."

<meta>This page continues the moral and ethical instructions from the Book of Sirach (also known as Ecclesiasticus). ## And so in Zion I was established; and in the holy city likewise I rested, and in Jerusalem was my power. And I took root in an honored people, and in the portion of my God is his inheritance, and in the full assembly of the saints is my stay. I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and as a cypress tree on Mount Zion. I was exalted like a palm tree in Kadesh, and as a rose plant in Jericho. As a fair olive tree in the plains, and as a plane tree was I exalted by the water in the streets. Like cinnamon and aromatic balsam, I gave forth a scent. Like choice myrrh, I yielded a sweet smell; and like galbanum, and onyx, and stacte <note>original: "ungula & gutta"; these refer to precious ingredients used in holy incense</note>, and like unburnt frankincense <note>original: "lybanus in non resuscitatus"</note> in my dwelling, and my odor is like undiluted balsam. I, like the turpentine tree, have stretched out my branches; and my branches are of honor and grace. I, like the vine, have brought forth a pleasant odor: and my flowers are the fruit of honor and honesty. I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope. In me is all grace of the way and of truth; in me is all hope of life and of virtue. Come over to me, all you that desire me, and be filled with my fruits. For my spirit is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance is above honey and the honeycomb. My memory is unto everlasting generations. They that eat me shall yet hunger, and they that drink me shall yet thirst. He that listens to me shall not be confounded, and they that work in me shall not sin. They that explain me shall have life everlasting. All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth. Moses commanded a law in the precepts of justice, and an inheritance to the house of Jacob, and the promises to Israel through the brother of David. He established for his son, born of a virgin, a most just king on the throne of honor. For he fills wisdom like the Pishon <note>A river mentioned in Genesis associated with the Garden of Eden</note>, and like the Tigris in the days of the new fruits. He makes understanding abound like the Euphrates, and multiplies it like the Jordan in the time of harvest. He sends instruction like the light, and stands like the Gihon in the day of the vintage. He is the first that has perfect knowledge of her, and the weak man shall not find her out. For her thoughts are more vast than the sea, and her counsels more deep than the great abyss. I, Wisdom, have poured out rivers. I am like a channel of immense water from a river. I am like the river Dorix <note>likely a variant of "Doris" or a geographical error in the transcription for a river name</note>, and like an aqueduct I came out of paradise. I said: I will water my garden of plants, and I will water abundantly the fruit of my meadow. And behold, my channel became a great river, and my river drew near to the sea. For I make doctrine to shine forth to all as the morning light, and I will declare it afar off. I will penetrate to all the lower parts of the earth, and will behold all that sleep, and will enlighten all that hope in the Lord. I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to them that seek wisdom, and will not cease to instruct their offspring even to the holy age. See that I have not labored for myself only, but for all that seek out the truth.

In three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and men: the concord of brothers, and the love of neighbors, and a man and wife that agree well together. Three sorts of people my soul hates, and I am greatly grieved at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old man that is a fool and doting. The things that you have not gathered in your youth, how shall you find them in your old age? How beautiful is judgment for the grey-haired, and for the elders to know counsel! How glorious is the wisdom of the aged, and the understanding and counsel of the honored! Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory. Nine things that are beyond suspicion have I magnified in my heart, and the tenth I will declare to men with my tongue: A man that has joy in his children, being alive and seeing the ruin of his enemies. Blessed is he that dwells with a sensible woman, and he that has not slipped with his tongue, and he that has not served those unworthy of him. Blessed is he that finds a true friend, and he that declares justice to an ear that hears. How great is he that finds wisdom and knowledge! But there is none above him that fears the Lord. The fear of God has set itself above all things. Blessed is the man to whom it is given to have the fear of God: he that holds it, to whom shall he be likened? The fear of God is the beginning of his love, and the beginning of faith is to be fast joined to it.

## Every wound is a sadness of heart, and every malice is the wickedness of a woman. A man will see every wound, but not the wound of the heart; and every wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman; and every oppression, but not the oppression of those who hate him; and every vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies. There is no head worse than the head of a serpent, and there is no anger above the anger of a woman. It will be more agreeable to abide with a lion and a dragon than to dwell with a wicked woman. The wickedness of a woman changes her face, and darkens her countenance like a bear, and shows itself like sackcloth in the midst of her neighbors. Her husband, hearing this, sighed a little. All malice is short compared to the malice of a woman; let the lot of sinners fall upon her. As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a talkative woman to a quiet man. Do not look upon a woman's beauty, and do not desire a woman for her appearance. A woman's anger is an insult and a great confusion. If a woman has the upper hand, she is contrary to her husband. A humble heart, a sad face, and a wounded heart is a wicked woman. Feeble hands and trembling knees is a woman who does not make her husband happy. From a woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die. Give no water an outlet, not even a little, nor to a wicked woman the liberty to gad abroad. If she does not walk according to your hand, she will confound you in the sight of your enemies. Cut her off from your flesh, lest she always abuse you.

## Happy is the husband of a good wife, for the number of his years is doubled. A strong woman delights her husband, and shall fill the years of his life in peace. A good wife is a good portion; she shall be given in the portion of them that fear God, to a man for his good deeds. Whether rich or poor, a good heart makes a joyful face at all times. The grace of a diligent woman shall delight her husband, and shall fatten his bones. Her discipline is a gift of God. A sensible and silent woman is an unchangeable gift. A holy and modest woman is grace upon grace. And no price is worthy of a continent soul. As the sun rising in the world in the high places of God, so is the beauty of a good wife for the ornament of her house. As the lamp shining upon the holy candlestick, so is the beauty of the face upon a steady stature. As golden pillars upon bases of silver, so are the firm feet upon the soles of a steady woman. Eternal foundations upon a solid rock, so the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman. At two things my heart is grieved, and at the third anger comes upon me: a man of war fainting through poverty, and a man of sense despised, and he that passes over from justice to sin; God has prepared him for the sword. Two sorts of things have appeared difficult and dangerous to me: it is hard for a merchant to be free from <unclear>negligence</unclear>, and a shopkeeper shall not be justified from the sins of the lips.

## Because of poverty many have sinned; and he that seeks to be enriched turns away his eye. As a stake is driven into the middle of a joint of stones, so also shall sin be crushed between buying and selling.

<column-break/>

## Unless you hold yourself diligently in the fear of the Lord, your house shall quickly be overthrown. As when a sieve is shaken, the dust and dung remain; so the perplexity of a man is in his thoughts. The furnace tries the potter’s vessels, and the trial of affliction tries just men. As the dressing of a tree shows the fruit thereof, so a word shows the thought of the heart of a man. Praise no man before he speaks, for this is the trial of men. If you follow justice, you shall obtain her, and shall put her on as a long robe of honor <note>original: "poderem"; a priestly or royal robe reaching to the feet</note>; and you shall dwell with her, and she shall protect you forever, and in the day of recognition you shall find a strong foundation. Birds resort to their like, and truth shall return to them that practice it. The lion always lies in wait for prey; so do sins for them that work iniquity. A holy man continues in wisdom as the sun, but a fool changes like the moon. In the midst of the senseless, keep track of the time; but in the midst of the thoughtful, be constant. The stories of fools are hateful, and their laughter is in the pleasures of sin. Speech that swears much shall make the hair of the head stand on end, and its irreverence shall make one stop their ears. The shedding of blood is in the quarrels of the proud, and their cursing is a grievous hearing. He that discloses the secrets of a friend loses his credit, and shall never find a friend to his mind. Love your neighbor and be joined in faith with him. But if you discover his secrets, follow no more after him. For as a man that loses his friend, so is he that loses the friendship of his neighbor. And as one that lets a bird go out of his hand, so have you let your neighbor go, and you shall not catch him again. Follow him not, for he is far off; he has escaped like a roe out of a snare, because his soul is wounded. You can no longer bind him. For a curse, there is reconciliation; but to disclose the mysteries of a friend is the despair of an unfaithful soul. He that winks with the eye works iniquity, and no man will cast him off. In the sight of your eyes he will sweeten his mouth, and will admire your words; but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and on your words he will lay a scandal. I have hated many things, but I have not equated anything to him, and the Lord will hate him. He that throws a stone high up, it shall fall upon his own head; and a deceitful blow of the deceitful shall divide wounds. He that digs a pit shall fall into it, and he that sets a stone for his neighbor shall stumble upon it, and he that lays a snare for another shall perish in it. A wicked counsel shall fall back upon him that devised it, and he shall not know from where it comes to him. Mockery and reproach are of the proud, and vengeance as a lion shall lie in wait for him. They that rejoice in the fall of the just shall perish in a snare, and sorrow shall consume them before they die. Anger and fury are both abominable, and the sinful man shall be subject to them.

## He that seeks vengeance from the Lord shall find vengeance, and He will surely keep his sins in remembrance. Forgive your neighbor if he has hurt you, and then shall your sins be forgiven to you when you pray. One man keeps anger against another, and does he seek a remedy from God? He has no mercy on a man like himself, and does he entreat for his own sins? He that is but flesh nourishes anger, and does he ask forgiveness from God? Who shall obtain pardon for his sins? Remember your last things, and let enmity cease. For decay and death are imminent in the commandments. Remember the fear of God, and be not angry with your neighbor. Remember the covenant of the Most High, and overlook the ignorance of your neighbor. Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins. For a passionate man kindles strife, and a sinful man will trouble his friends, and bring in enmity in the midst of them that are at peace. For as the wood of the forest is, so the fire burns; and as a man’s strength is, so shall his anger be; and according to his riches, he shall increase his anger. A hasty contention kindles a fire, and a hasty quarrel sheds blood, and a testifying tongue brings death. If you blow the spark, it shall burn as a fire; and if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched; both come out of the mouth.

## The whisperer and the double-tongued are accursed, for they have troubled many that were at peace. A third tongue <note>A Hebrew idiom for a gossiping or slandering tongue that affects three people: the speaker, the listener, and the subject</note> has disquieted many, and scattered them from nation to nation. It has destroyed the strong cities of the rich, and overthrown the houses of great men. It has subdued the power of peoples, and dissolved strong nations. A third tongue has cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labors. He that listens to it shall find no rest, nor shall he have a friend in whom he may repose. The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh, but the stroke of the tongue will break the bones. Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have perished by their own tongue. Blessed is he that is sheltered from a wicked tongue, that has not passed into its anger, and that has not drawn the yoke thereof, and has not been bound in its bands. For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its bands are bands of brass. Its death is a most evil death, and hell is more useful than it. Its endurance shall not last, but it shall possess the ways of the unjust, and in its flame it shall not burn the just. They that forsake God shall fall into it, and it shall burn in them, and shall not be quenched; and it shall be sent upon them as a lion, and as a leopard it shall tear them. Hedge in your ears with thorns, and listen not to a wicked tongue, and make doors and bars for your mouth. Melt down your gold and silver, and make a balance for your words, and a right bridle for your mouth. And take heed lest you slip with your tongue, and fall in the sight of your enemies who lie in wait for you, and your fall be incurable unto death.

## He that shows mercy lends to his neighbor; and he that is stronger in hand <note>meaning someone who has the means or ability</note> keeps the commandments. Lend to your neighbor in the time of his need, and pay your neighbor again in due time. Keep your word and deal faithfully with him, and you shall at all times find that which is necessary for you. Many have looked upon a loan as a find, and have given trouble to them that helped them. Until they receive, they kiss the hands of the giver, and in their promises they humble their voices. But in the time of repayment, they will ask for more time, and will speak words of weariness and murmuring, and will complain of the time. And if they are able to pay, they will resist; they will hardly pay half a penny <note>original: "asse"; a small Roman coin</note>, and will count it as a lucky find. But if not, they will defraud the lender of his money, and he has him for an enemy without cause. And he will pay him with reproaches and curses, and instead of honor and benefit will pay him with contumely. Many have refused to lend, not out of wickedness, but they were afraid to be defrauded without cause. But yet, be more steadfast toward a man of humble mind, and do not delay him for your alms. Help the poor because of the commandment, and send him not away empty because of his poverty. Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and hide it not under a stone to be lost. Place your treasure in the commandments of the Most High, and it shall profit you more than gold.

## Shut up alms in the heart of the poor, and it shall obtain help for you against all evil. The gratitude of a man is as a signet ring with him, and he shall keep the favor of a man as the apple of his eye. And afterward he shall rise up and shall render them a reward, to every one upon their own head. Above the shield of the mighty and above the spear against your enemy, it shall fight for you. A good man is surety for his neighbor; and he that has lost shame will leave him to himself. Forget not the kindness of your backer <note>original: "fide iussoris"; a guarantor or bondsman</note>, for he has given his life for you. The sinner and the unclean flee from the one who promised for them. A sinner attributes to himself the goods of his backer, and he that is of an ungrateful mind will leave him that delivered him. A man is surety for his neighbor; and when he has lost all shame, he will forsake him. Evil suretyship has undone many that were prosperous, and has tossed them as a wave of the sea. It has caused powerful men to move from place to place, and they have wandered in strange nations. A sinner that transgresses the commandments of the Lord shall fall into an unjust promise; and he that tries to do many things shall fall into judgment. Recover your neighbor according to your power, and take heed to yourself that you fall not.
