The Lord is judge, and with him there is no respect of persons. He will not show partiality against the poor, and he will hear the prayer of the oppressed. He will not despise the prayers of the orphan, nor the widow when she pours out her grieving speech. Do not the widow’s tears run down her cheek, and is not her cry against the one who caused them? For from the cheek they go up even to heaven, and the Lord who hears them will not be delighted by them. The prayer of the one who humbles himself shall pierce the clouds, and it will not depart until the Most High beholds it and judges justly and executes judgment. And the Lord will not delay, nor will he endure those people until he crushes the backs of the unmerciful and repays vengeance to the nations; until he takes away the multitude of the proud and breaks the scepters of the unrighteous; until he repays men according to their actions and according to the works of Adam <note>original: "opera ade"; referring here to the "works of man" or "human deeds"</note> and according to his presumption; until he judges the judgment of his people and delights the just with his mercy—mercy that is as beautiful in the time of tribulation as a rain cloud in a time of drought. Have mercy on us, O God of all, and behold us, and show us the light of your mercies; and send your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, that they may know there is no God but you, and that they may declare your great works. Lift up your hand over the foreign nations, that they may see your power. For as you were sanctified in us in their sight, so be magnified in them in our sight, that they may know you as we have known you: that there is no God beside you, O Lord. Renew your signs and change your wonders. Glorify your hand and your right arm. Raise up indignation and pour out wrath. Take away the adversary and afflict the enemy. Hasten the time and remember the end, that they may declare your wonders. Let the flame of wrath devour the one who is saved, and let those who oppress your people find perdition. Crush the heads of the princes of the enemies who say: "There is no other beside us." Gather all the tribes of Jacob, and let them know that there is no God but you, and let them declare your great works, and he shall inherit them as from the beginning. Have mercy on your people, upon whom your name is invoked, and Israel, whom you have made equal to your firstborn. Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of your rest. Fill Zion with your unspeakable words, and your people with your glory.

**A**ll wisdom is from the Lord God, and has been with him always, and is before all time. Who has numbered the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of the world? Who has measured the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss? Who has searched out the wisdom of God which precedes all things? Wisdom was created before all things, and the understanding of prudence is from eternity. The source of wisdom is the word of God on high, and its entrance is the eternal commandments. To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? And who has known her cunning ways? To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed and manifested? And who has understood the multiplicity of her entrance? There is one most high Creator, almighty, and greatly to be feared, a powerful king and exceedingly amiable, sitting upon his throne and ruling as God. He created her in the Holy Spirit, and saw her, and numbered her, and measured her. And he poured her out upon all his works, and upon all flesh according to his gift, and has given her to those who love him.

**W**isdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins. For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw itself from thoughts that are without understanding, and will be corrected by iniquity when it comes. For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not deliver the curser from his own lips, for God is the witness of his reins <note>original: "renum"; ancient term for the seat of emotions or the "inner self"</note>, and the true searcher of his heart, and the hearer of his tongue. For the spirit of the Lord has filled the whole world, and that which contains all things has knowledge of the voice. Therefore, he who speaks unjust things cannot be hidden, nor shall the chastising judgment pass him by. For there shall be an inquiry into the thoughts of the impious, and the sound of his words shall reach the Lord for the correction of his iniquities. For the ear of jealousy hears all things, and the noise of murmuring shall not be hidden. Keep yourselves, therefore, from murmuring, which profits nothing, and refrain your tongue from detraction, for an obscure speech shall not go for nothing, and the mouth that lies kills the soul.

**B**etter is a little with justice than the great treasures of the wicked. Better is a little with the fear of the Lord than great and insatiable treasures. Better is it to be invited by a friend to a meal of herbs with love than to a fatted calf with hatred. Better is a dry morsel with joy than a house full of sacrifices with strife. Better is it to dwell in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and angry woman. Better is it to dwell in a corner of the housetop than with a litigious woman in a shared house. A good name is better than many riches; good favor is above silver and gold. Better is the just man who walks in his simplicity, and he shall leave blessed children after him. Wisdom is better than strength, and a prudent man is more than a strong one. Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who knows not how to look forward to the future. Wisdom is better than the most precious things, and everything desirable cannot be compared to it.

**A** bright eye rejoices the soul, and a good report makes the bones fat. The seeing eye and the hearing ear: the Lord made them both. The watchful eye that guards the city and does not sleep in the days of harvest. The eye that mocks his father and despises the labor of his mother: let the ravens of the brooks pick it out, and the young eagles eat it. The eyes of the Lord in every place behold the good and the evil. The eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and the depth of the abyss, and looking into the hearts of men in their hidden parts.

**H**idden wisdom and invisible treasure: what use is there in either? Better is the man who hides his folly than the man who hides his wisdom. The wisdom of the humble man shall exalt his head and make him sit in the midst of great men. The wisdom of a man shines in his countenance, and the Most Powerful has changed his face. Wisdom cries out in the streets, she gives her voice in the squares; she cries out at the head of the crowds, in the entry of the gates of the city she utters her words, saying: "How long, you little ones, will you love childhood, and fools covet those things which are harmful to them, and the imprudent hate knowledge? Turn at my correction."

**F**riendship, if it has a friend, will be like him. A faithful friend is a strong protection, and he who finds him finds a treasure. There is no comparison to a faithful friend, and no weight of gold or silver is worthy of the goodness of his faith. A faithful friend is the medicine of life and immortality, and those who fear the Lord shall find him. He who fears God shall have good friendship likewise, for according to him, so shall his friend be. If a friend remains steadfast, he shall be as an equal to you, and shall act confidently among your household. If he humbles himself before you and hides himself from your face, you shall have a good and one-minded friendship. A friend is not known in prosperity, and an enemy is not hidden in adversity. In a man’s prosperity, his enemies are in sorrow; but in his adversity, even a friend will depart. Every friend will say, "I also have joined in friendship," but there is a friend who is a friend in name only. Friends are multiplied to a sweet-speaking friend, and they mitigate enemies, and a thankful tongue abounds in a good man. Let many be at peace with you, but let your counselor be one among a thousand. If you gain a friend, gain him in a time of trial, and do not be quick to trust him. For there is a friend according to his own occasion, and he will not remain in the day of tribulation. And there is a friend who turns to enmity, and there is a friend who will lay bare hatred and strife and insults. There is also a friend who is a companion at the table, and he will not remain in the day of necessity. A faithful friend, if he remains steadfast, shall be equal to you, and shall act confidently among your household.

**F**or I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature. I made that in the heavens there should rise a light that never fails, and as a cloud I covered all the earth. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of a cloud. I alone have compassed the circuit of heaven, and have penetrated into the depth of the abyss; I have walked in the waves of the sea and stood in every land; and in every people and in every nation I have had the primacy. And by my power I have trodden under foot the hearts of all the high and the low, and in all these I sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord. Then the Creator of all things commanded and said to me—and he who created me rested in my tabernacle—and he said to me: "Dwell in Jacob, and inherit in Israel, and take root in my elect." From the beginning and before the world was I created, and unto the world to come I shall not cease to be, and in the holy dwelling place I have ministered before him. And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem. And I took root in an honored people, and in the portion of my God is his inheritance, and in the fullness of the saints

<column-break/>

is my abiding place. I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and as a cypress tree on Mount Zion. I was exalted like a palm tree in En-Gedi <note>original: "cades"; likely referencing the oasis of En-Gedi</note>, and as a rose plant in Jericho. As a fair olive tree in the plains, and as a plane tree I was exalted by the water in the streets. I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aromatic balm; I yielded a sweet odor like choice myrrh. And as storax, and galbanum, and onyx, and stacte, and as the frankincense not cut, I perfumed my dwelling; and my odor is as the unmixed balm. I, as the turpentine tree, have stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honor and grace. As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odor, and my flowers are the fruit of honor and honesty. I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope. In me is all grace of the way and of the truth; in me is all hope of life and of virtue. Come over to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits. For my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb. My memory is unto the generations of ages. They that eat me shall yet hunger, and they that drink me shall yet thirst. He that hears me shall not be confounded, and they that work in me shall not sin. They that explain me shall have life everlasting. All these things are the book of life, and the testament of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth.

**E**very plague is the sadness of the heart, and every malice is the wickedness of a woman. There is no head more wicked than the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath above the wrath of a woman. It will be more agreeable to abide with a lion and a dragon than to dwell with a wicked woman. The wickedness of a woman changes her face, and she darkens her countenance like a bear. Her husband groaned in the midst of his neighbors, and hearing it, he sighed a little. All malice is short compared to the malice of a woman; let the lot of sinners fall upon her. As the climbing up of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a talkative woman to a quiet man. Gaze not upon a woman’s beauty, and do not desire a woman for her beauty. A woman's good grace will delight her husband and make his bones fat. A diligent woman is a crown to her husband, but she who brings confusion is like rottenness in his bones. Happy is the husband of a good woman, for the number of his years is double. A brave woman delights her husband and shall fill the years of his life in peace. A holy and modest woman is grace upon grace. The grace of a good and disciplined woman is beyond price, and no weight is worthy of a continent soul. As the sun rising to the world in the high places of God, so is the beauty of a good woman for the ornament of her house. As a lamp shining upon the holy candlestick, so is the beauty of the face upon a steady stature. As golden pillars upon bases of silver, so are the firm feet upon the soles of a steady woman. As eternal foundations upon a solid rock, so are the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman.

**T**he wisdom of a scribe <note>term: "Scribe" (Latin: *scriba*); in this context, a professional scholar of the law and scriptures.</note> comes in a time of leisure, and he that is less occupied shall receive wisdom. What wisdom shall he hold who holds the plow, and glories in the goad, who drives the oxen and is occupied in their labors, and whose talk is about the offspring of bulls? He will give his heart to turning up furrows, and his waking care is for the fattening of cows. So is every craftsman and architect who passes the night as the day, who carves engraved signets, and his diligence varies the figure. He will give his heart to the likeness of the picture, and his waking care perfects the work. So is the smith sitting by the anvil and considering the iron work. The vapor of the fire scorches his flesh, and he contends with the heat of the furnace. The noise of the hammer is ever in his ears, and his eye is upon the pattern of the vessel. He will give his heart to the finishing of his works, and his waking care will adorn them to perfection. So is the potter sitting at his work, turning the wheel with his feet, who is always set in care for his work, and all his operation is by number. He will fashion the clay with his arm and bow down his strength before his feet. He will give his heart to finish the glazing, and his waking care is to clean the furnace. All these have trusted in their hands, and every one is wise in his own art. Without these a city shall not be built, and they shall not dwell therein nor walk about. But they shall not leap into the assembly; they shall not sit upon the judge’s seat, and they shall not understand the testament of judgment, nor make discipline and judgment manifest; and they shall not be found in parables. But they shall strengthen the state of the world, and their prayer is in the operation of their art, applying their soul and searching into the law of the Most High.

**T**he wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets. He will keep the sayings of renowned men and will enter withal into the subtleties of parables. He will search out the hidden meanings of proverbs and will be conversant in the secrets of parables. He shall serve among great men and appear before the governor. He shall pass into strange countries, for he shall try good and evil among men. He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the Most High. He will open his mouth in prayer and will make supplication for his sins. For if the great Lord is willing, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding. And he shall pour forth the words of his wisdom as showers, and in his prayer he shall confess to the Lord. And he shall direct his counsel and his knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate. He shall show forth the discipline of his doctrine and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord. Many shall praise his wisdom, and it shall never be blotted out. The memory of him shall not depart, and his name shall be in demand from generation to generation. Nations shall declare his wisdom, and the church shall show forth his praise.

**T**here is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace. There is one who destroys his soul through shamefacedness, and by an imprudent regard for a person he will destroy it. There is one who through shame promises to his friend and has made him an enemy for nothing. A man who lies is a most wicked thing, and he will be continually in the mouth of men without discipline. A thief is better than the persistence of a lying man, but both shall inherit perdition. The manners of lying men are without honor, and their confusion is with them without ceasing.

**D**o not rebuke a man who turns away from sin, nor reproach him. Remember that we are all under correction. Do not despise a man in his old age, for we also grow old. Do not rejoice over your dead enemy, knowing that we all die. Do not despise the discourse of wise elders, but be conversant in their proverbs. For from them you shall learn wisdom and the doctrine of understanding, and how to serve great men without blame. Let not the discourse of the ancients escape you, for they have learned from their fathers; from them you shall learn understanding, and how to give an answer in time of need. Do not kindle the coals of sinners by rebuking them, lest you be burnt with the flame of the fire of their sins. Do not stand against the face of an insulting man, lest he sit as a spy at your mouth. Do not lend to a man who is mightier than yourself; but if you do lend, count it as lost. Do not promise beyond your power; but if you do promise, take care to perform it. Do not judge against a judge, for he judges according to his justice. Do not go on the way with a bold man, lest he burden you with his evils. For he goes according to his own will, and you shall perish together with his folly. Do not quarrel with a passionate man, and do not go into the desert with him, for blood is as nothing before God, and where there is no help, he will strike you down. Have no counsel with a fool, for he can love nothing but what pleases him. Do no act of counsel before a stranger, for you know not what he may bring forth. Do not open your heart to every man, lest he perhaps repay you with false favor and speak insults to you.

**A**ll flesh shall fade as grass, and as a leaf that grows on a green tree. Some are born, and others are cast off; so is the generation of flesh and blood. One comes to an end, and another is born. Every corruptible work shall fail in the end, and he that works it shall go with it. And every chosen work shall be justified, and he that works it shall be honored therein.

**D**o not say: "I am driven away by God," for you should not do the things that God hates. Do not say: "He has led me astray," for he has no need of impious men. The Lord hates every error of abomination, and it shall not be amiable to those who fear him. He himself made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel. He added his commandments and precepts: if you will keep the commandments, they shall preserve you, and to perform acceptable fidelity forever. He has set water and fire before you: stretch forth your hand to whichever you will. Before man is life and death, good and evil; that which he likes shall be given to him. For the wisdom of God is great, and he is strong in power, seeing all men without ceasing. The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him, and he knows every work of man. He has commanded no man to act impiously, and he has given no man space to sin. For one who fears God is better than a thousand impious sons. And it is more useful to die without children than to leave impious children. For by one man of understanding shall a country be inhabited, but it shall be made desolate by three who are impious.

It emphasizes personal responsibility and the "fear of the Lord" as the foundation of a righteous life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the moral and instructional tone of the previous section. While the preceding text focused on the cries of the oppressed and God’s impartial judgment, this page shifts toward an anthology of "Sapiential" (wisdom) literature. It draws heavily from the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus), Proverbs, and the Wisdom of Solomon to define the origin of wisdom and provide practical social ethics.</meta>

Let everyone here bless the shepherd; and do not speak ill of him: and may the peace of the Lord God be with you: and may you have much peace in eternity. Everyone who sins, sins against their own soul; and whoever acts with justice shall be justified: and shall live forever.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 1</margin>
All wisdom is from the Lord God, and has been with him always, and exists before time began. Who can count the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, or the days of the ages? Who has measured the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, or the depth of the abyss? Who has searched out the wisdom of God, which precedes all things? Wisdom was created before all other things, and the understanding of prudence is from eternity. The fountain of wisdom is the word of God on high, and her ways are eternal commandments. To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed, and who has known her clever insights? To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed and made manifest? And who has understood the many ways of her entrance? There is one most high Creator, the Almighty, and a powerful King, greatly to be feared, sitting upon his throne, and a ruling God. He himself created her in the Holy Spirit, and saw her, and numbered her, and measured her. And he poured her out upon all his works, and upon all flesh according to his gift, and he has provided her to those who love him. The fear of the Lord is glory and boasting, and gladness and a crown of exultation. The fear of the Lord will delight the heart, and give gladness and joy and length of days. It shall go well in the end for the one who fears the Lord, and he shall be blessed on the day of his death. The love of God is honorable wisdom: and to those to whom she appears in a vision, they love her by seeing her and by acknowledging her great works. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and it was created together with the faithful in the womb; it walks with chosen women, and is recognized among the just and the faithful. The fear of the Lord is the religious devotion of knowledge. This devotion shall guard and justify the heart, and shall give happiness and joy. It shall go well for the one who fears the Lord, and he shall be blessed in the days of his consolation. To fear God is the fullness of wisdom, and fullness comes from her fruits. She shall fill his whole house with her generations, and the storehouses with her treasures. The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, filling one with peace and the fruit of salvation: and he saw her and numbered her: for both are the gifts of God. Wisdom shall share out knowledge and the understanding of prudence: and she exalts the glory of those who hold onto her. The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are long-lived. In the treasures of wisdom are understanding and the religious devotion of knowledge: but wisdom is an abomination to sinners. The fear of the Lord drives out sin: for he who is without fear cannot be justified: for the heat of his anger is his own downfall. A patient man will hold out until the proper time, and afterward comes the return of joy. Good sense will hide his words until the right time, and the lips of many shall tell of his understanding. In the treasures of wisdom is the meaning of discipline: but the worship of God is an abomination to a sinner. Son, if you desire wisdom, keep justice, and God will provide it to you. For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline: and what is pleasing to him is faith and gentleness. Do not be unbelieving toward the fear of the Lord: and do not approach him with a double heart. Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men, and do not let your own lips cause you to stumble. Pay attention to them, lest perhaps you fall and bring dishonor to your soul: and God may reveal your secrets and cast you down in the middle of the congregation: because you approached the Lord wickedly, and your heart is full of deceit and fallacy.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 40</margin>
All things that are from the earth shall return to the earth: and those things which are from the waters shall return to the sea. Every bribe and iniquity shall be blotted out: but faith shall stand forever. The riches of the unjust shall be dried up like a river: and they shall perish like a great thunderclap in the rain. A man will rejoice in opening his hands: so shall transgressors waste away in their final end. The descendants of the ungodly shall not multiply their branches: and impure roots make a sound upon a sharp rock. Every green herb by any water, or at the edge of a river, shall be pulled up before any grass. Grace is like a paradise in blessings, and mercy remains forever.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 21</margin>
Indeed, he who sins, sins against his own soul: and he who acts with justice shall be justified. Indeed, he who shows mercy, sows it: and he who sows it, shall reap it. Indeed, he who sows in the flesh, shall reap corruption from the flesh: but he who sows in the spirit, shall reap eternal life from the spirit.

<margin>Proverbs 22</margin>
A good name is better than many riches: good favor is better than gold and silver. The rich and the poor have met one another: the Lord is the maker of both. The clever man sees evil and hides himself: the innocent man passes through and is afflicted with loss. The reward of discipline and humility is the fear of the Lord, and riches, and glory, and life. Arms and swords are in the wicked way: but the guardian of his own soul departs far from them.

<margin>Wisdom 4</margin>
O how beautiful is the chaste generation with radiance! For the memory of it is immortal: because it is known both before God and before men. When it is present, they imitate it, and they long for it when it has withdrawn itself: and it triumphs forever, crowned, winning the reward of undefiled conflicts.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 25</margin>
There is no wickedness greater than the wickedness of a woman: and no anger above the anger of an enemy. It will be more pleasing to dwell with a lion and a dragon than to live with a wicked woman. The wickedness of a woman changes her face: and she has darkened her countenance like a bear, and she groans in the midst of her neighbors. All malice is short compared to the malice of a woman: let the lot of sinners fall upon her. <note>These passages reflect the historical misogyny common in ancient "Wisdom" literature, often using the "wicked woman" as a personification of folly or social disorder.</note>

<margin>Proverbs 8</margin>
Wisdom is better than gold: and discipline is more precious than silver. Receive my discipline and not money: choose doctrine rather than choice gold. For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and everything desirable cannot be compared to her. I, Wisdom, dwell in counsel, and I am present among learned thoughts. The fear of the Lord hates evil: I detest arrogance and pride, and the wicked way, and the double-tongued mouth.

<column-break/>

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 20</margin>
A wise man makes himself beloved through his words: but the favors of fools shall be poured out <note>meaning: wasted or lost</note>. The gift of a fool will not be useful to you: for his eyes are sevenfold <note>original: "septemplices"; meaning he expects seven times more in return</note>. He will give little, and reproach much: and the opening of his mouth is an inflammation. Today a man lends, and tomorrow he asks for it back: such a man is hateful. A fool shall have no friend, and there shall be no thanks for his good deeds. For those who eat his bread have vain tongues. How often and how many shall laugh him to scorn? For he does not distribute with a right judgment what ought to be held; likewise, he distributes what ought not to be held. A slip on the pavement is like one who falls from the floor: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily. An ungracious man is like a vain story: it will be constantly in the mouth of the undisciplined. A parable shall be rejected from a fool's mouth: for he does not speak it in its proper time. There is one who is hindered from sinning by poverty: and in his rest he shall be pricked. There is one who loses his soul through shame: and he loses it because of an unwise person. There is one who makes a promise to a friend out of shame: and he has gained an enemy for nothing. A lie is a wicked reproach in a man: and it will be constantly in the mouth of the undisciplined. A thief is better than the persistence of a lying man: but both shall inherit perdition. The habits of lying men are without honor: and their confusion is with them without ceasing. A wise man makes himself beloved through his words: and the favors of great men are pleasing. He who works the land shall exalt his heap of grain: and he who works justice, he himself shall be exalted: and he who pleases great men shall escape iniquity. Gifts and presents blind the eyes of judges: and like one who is mute in the mouth, he turns away their corrections. Wisdom that is hidden and a treasure that is unseen: what is the use in either? Better is the man who hides his folly than the man who hides his wisdom.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 21</margin>
Son, have you sinned? Do not do so again: but also pray for your former sins, that they may be forgiven you. Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent: for if you go near them, they will take hold of you. Their teeth are the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. All iniquity is like a two-edged sword: there is no healing for its wound. Scolding and insults will bring wealth to nothing: and the house that is very rich shall be brought to nothing by pride: thus the substance of the proud shall be rooted out. The prayer of the poor man goes from his mouth straight to the ears <note>of God</note>: and judgment shall come to him speedily. He who hates correction follows in the track of a sinner: and he who fears God will turn to his own heart. A powerful man is bold in speech: and he is known from afar by the prudent. He who builds his house at another's expense is like one who gathers his stones in winter. A congregation of sinners is like gathered tow <note>coarse flax used as tinder</note>: and their end is a flame of fire. The way of sinners is paved with stones: and at their end are hell, darkness, and punishments. He who keeps the law shall master its meaning. The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding. He who is not wise in what is good will not be taught. But there is a wisdom which abounds in evil: and there is no understanding where there is bitterness. The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel remains like a fountain of life. The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel: and it will hold no wisdom. If a learned man hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it: the luxurious man heard it, and it displeased him, and he cast it behind his back. The talk of a fool is like a burden on a journey: but grace shall be found on the lips of the prudent. The mouth of the prudent is sought in the church: and they shall ponder his words in their hearts.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 41</margin>
All things that are of the earth shall return to the earth: so the ungodly go from a curse to destruction. The mourning of men is in their bodies: but the name of the ungodly shall be blotted out. Have a care for a good name: for this shall remain with you more than a thousand precious and great treasures. A good life has a number of days: but a good name shall remain forever.

<margin>Matthew 6</margin>
The lamp of the body is the eye: if your eye is simple <note>or "single," meaning clear/focused</note>, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is wicked, your whole body will be full of darkness. See to it, therefore, that the light which is in you is not darkness. If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part in darkness, the whole shall be bright, and as a lamp of brilliance it shall illuminate you.

<margin>Proverbs 27</margin>
Behold, as a face is reflected in water to the one looking: so the hearts of men are manifest to the prudent. Hell and destruction are never full: likewise the eyes of men are insatiable. As silver is tried in the refinery, and gold in the furnace: so a man is tried by the mouth of one who praises him.

<margin>Luke 11</margin>
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place, nor under a basket: but upon a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light. The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is simple, your whole body will be full of light: but if it is wicked, your body also will be full of darkness.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 41</margin>
O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who has peace in his possessions: to a quiet man, and one whose ways are directed in all things, and who is still strong enough to take food! O death, your sentence is good to a man who is in need, and whose strength fails, being old in age, and who is anxious about everything, and to the distrustful man who loses patience! Do not fear the sentence of death. Remember those who were before you, and those who are to come after you: this is the judgment from the Lord upon all flesh. And what shall come upon you by the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it be ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.

<margin>Ecclesiasticus 25</margin>
The crown of old men is much experience, and their glory is the fear of God. In three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and men: the concord of brothers, the love of neighbors, and a husband and wife who agree well together. Three types of people my soul hates, and I am greatly burdened by their souls: a proud poor man, a lying rich man, and a foolish and senseless old man.

<margin>
The memory of Joshua
</margin>
He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, in the assault against his enemies on every side; and the Lord removed from them the great power <note>original: "cornu," literally "horn," a common biblical metaphor for strength or military might</note> of the nation, and the children of Israel were strengthened. In all his work, he gave thanks to the Holy One, the Most High, with words of glory. With all his heart, he praised the Lord and loved God who made him, and God gave him power against his enemies. He also appointed singers to stand before the altar, and by their voices, he made sweet melodies. He gave beauty to the celebrations and adorned the seasons until the end of his life, so that they might praise the holy name of the Lord and magnify the sanctuary of God from early morning. The Lord cleansed his sins and exalted his power forever; he gave him the covenant of the kingdom and a throne of glory in Israel.

---

After these things, the prophet Nathan arose in the days of David; and as the fat is separated from the meat, so was David separated from the children of Israel. He played with lions as if they were lambs, and did the same with bears as if they were young sheep. In his youth, did he not kill the giant <note>A reference to Goliath</note> and take away the reproach from his people? In raising his hand with the stone in his sling, he cast down the boasting of Goliath; for he called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, and He gave strength to his right hand to strike down the warrior and to exalt the power of his nation. Thus, they glorified him among ten thousand and praised him with the blessings of the Lord, offering him a crown of glory. For he crushed his enemies on every side and wiped out the Philistines, his adversaries, even to this day. He crushed their power forever.

---

Solomon ruled in days of peace, to whom the Lord subjected all enemies, so that he might build a house in His name and prepare a sanctuary for eternity. O Solomon, how learned you were in your youth! You were filled with wisdom like a river. Your mind covered the earth <note>A poetic way of saying his knowledge was vast and all-encompassing</note>, and you filled it with parables and riddles. Your name was spread abroad to distant islands, and you were loved for your peace. The lands marveled at your songs, proverbs, comparisons, and interpretations, and at the name of the Lord God, who is surnamed the God of Israel. You gathered gold as if it were brass <note>original: "aurichalcum," an alloy of copper and zinc highly valued in antiquity</note> and piled up lead as if it were silver. But you bent your loins toward women, and you were given power over your own body. You brought a stain upon your glory and profaned your lineage, bringing wrath upon your children and causing them to be struck by your foolishness. Thus the kingdom was divided in two, and a rebellious ruler rose out of Ephraim. But the Lord will never leave behind his mercy, nor will He corrupt or destroy His own works; He will not wipe out the descendants of His chosen ones, nor will the seed of those who love the Lord be destroyed. And He gave a remnant to Jacob, and a root to the lineage of David. And Solomon rested with his fathers. And he left behind him a foolish heir for his people.

And he was not abandoned in his sin, nor corrupted, nor was his posterity destroyed; nor were the descendants of his chosen ones wiped out. And in the nest of prudence was Rehoboam, who turned away the people by his counsel, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin and gave Ephraim the way of sinning. And their sins multiplied greatly, for they drove them far away from their land. They sought out every kind of wickedness until defense came to them, and He delivered them from all sins.

---

Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst; he dug through the rock with iron and built a well for the water. In his days, Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh; he raised his hand against them and stretched out his hand against Zion, becoming proud in his power. Then their hearts and hands were moved, and they suffered like women in labor; and they called upon the Lord of mercy. Spreading their hands to the Lord, the Lord Most High heard their voice. He did not remember their sins, nor did He give them over to their enemies, but He purified them by the hand of Isaiah, the holy prophet. He overthrew the camp of the Assyrians, and the angel of the Lord crushed them. For did not Hezekiah do what pleased God and walk in the way of David his father, as Isaiah the great and faithful prophet commanded in the sight of God? In his days the sun went backward, and he added life to the king. By a great spirit, Isaiah saw the final things and comforted the mourners in Zion; he showed what was to come for eternity, and hidden things before they happened. In every work, he gave thanks to the Holy One on high with words of glory.

<column-break/>

After him, the memory of Josiah is worthy, like a blend of incense prepared by the work of a perfumer. In every mouth, his memory is sweet as honey, and like music at a banquet of wine. He was divinely guided in the repentance of the nation and removed the abominations of ungodliness. He directed his heart toward the Lord, and in the days of sinners, he strengthened piety. Except for David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, everyone committed sin. For the kings of Judah abandoned the law of the Mighty One and despised the fear of God. They gave their kingdom to others and their glory to a foreign nation. They set fire to the chosen city of the sanctuary and made its streets a desert through the hand of Jeremiah. For they treated him badly, he who was consecrated as a prophet from his mother's womb, to overthrow, uproot, and destroy—and again to build and renew. Ezekiel was the one who saw the vision of glory, which God showed him on the chariot of the cherubim. For he also remembered the enemies in the rain, to do good to those who showed right ways. And may the bones of the twelve prophets sprout from their place! For they strengthened Jacob and redeemed themselves through the faith of virtue. How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? For he was like a signet ring on the right hand of Israel. And Jeshua, the son of Jozadak? Who in their days built the house and raised the holy temple to the Lord, prepared for eternal glory. And Nehemiah is remembered for a long time, he who raised up for us the fallen walls, set up the gates and bars, and rebuilt our houses. No one was born on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth. Nor was any man born like Joseph, the prince of his brothers, the support of the nation, the ruler of his brethren, and the stability of the people; even his bones were visited, and they prophesied after his death. Seth and Shem attained glory among men, and above every living soul in the beginning was Adam.

---

Simon, son of Onias, the high priest, who in his life propped up the house and in his days strengthened the temple. The height of the temple was also founded by him—the double building and the high wall of the temple. In his days, a reservoir of water flowed out, and it was filled beyond measure like a sea. He took care of his people and delivered them from destruction. He prevailed in enlarging the city. He attained glory in his dealings with the people, and he enlarged the entrance of the house and the court. He shone like the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and like the full moon in its days. And like the sun shining back, so he shone in the temple of God. And like a rainbow shining in the clouds of glory, and like the flower of roses in the days of spring. Like lilies that are by the water's edge, and like fragrant frankincense in the days of summer. Like a fire shining, and incense burning in the fire. Like a vessel of solid gold adorned with every precious stone. Like a budding olive tree and a cypress tree raising itself to the heights; when he put on the robe of glory and was clothed in the perfection of power. In his ascent to the holy altar, he gave glory to the garment of holiness. When he received the portions from the hand of the priests, he himself stood by the altar. Around him was a crown of brothers like a plantation of cedars on Mount Lebanon. So they stood around him like palm branches—all the sons of Aaron in their glory. The offering of the Lord was in their hands before the entire congregation of Israel. And performing the service at the altar, to enlarge the offering to the Most High, the Almighty. He stretched out his hand for the libation and poured out the blood of the grape. He poured out at the base of the altar a divine fragrance to the High Prince. Then the sons of Aaron shouted; they sounded the trumpets of hammered metal and made a great voice heard in memory before God. Then all the people together made haste and fell on their faces upon the earth to adore the Lord their God and to offer prayers to the Almighty God Most High. And the singers sang with their voices, and in that great house the sweet sound increased. And the people begged the Lord Most High in prayer until the honor of the Lord was completed and they finished their service. Then descending, he stretched out his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips and to glory in His name. And he repeated his prayer, wishing to show the power of God. And he praised the Lord of all, who has done great things in all the earth; who has increased our days from our mother's womb and dealt with us according to His mercy. May He give us joy of heart, and may peace be in our days in Israel forever. May Israel believe that the mercy of God is with us, so that He may deliver us in his days.

---

There are two nations that my soul hates, and the third is not even a nation that I should hate: those who sit on Mount Seir, the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem. Joshua <note>original: "ihesus," referring to Jesus/Joshua ben Sirach</note> the son of Sirach of Jerusalem, wrote the doctrine of wisdom and discipline in this book; he who renewed wisdom from his heart. Blessed is he who occupies himself with these good things; he who places them in his heart shall always be wise. For if he does these things, he shall be strong in all things, because the light of God is his footprint.

Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore. I will give thanks to you, O Lord King, and I will praise you, God my Savior. I will give thanks to your name, for you have become my helper and protector; and you have delivered my body from destruction, from the snare of a wicked tongue and from the lips of those who work lies. In the presence of those who stood by, you became my helper; and you delivered me according to the abundance of the mercy of your name, from the roaring ones ready for food, from the hands of those who seek my soul, and from the gates of tribulations that surrounded me. From the depth of the flame that surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burned. From the depth of the belly of hell, and from a defiled tongue, and from the word of a lie; from an unjust king and from an unrighteous tongue. My soul shall praise the Lord even unto death. And my life was drawing near to hell below. They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help. I looked for the help of men, and there was none. I was mindful of your mercy, O Lord, and of your works which are from the beginning of the world; because you rescue those who wait for you, O Lord, and you deliver them from the hands of the nations. You exalted my dwelling place upon the earth, and I prayed against the torrent of death. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that He would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help. I will praise your name continually and will praise it with thanksgiving; and my prayer was heard. And you delivered me from destruction and rescued me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks and sing praise to you, and bless the name of the Lord. When I was still young, before I went astray, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer. Before the temple I asked for her, and even to the very last I will seek her. And she flourished like a ripening grape. My heart rejoiced in her; my foot walked a straight path. From my youth I searched for her. I inclined my ear a little and received her. I found much wisdom in myself and I profited much in it. To Him who gives me wisdom, I will give glory. For I have resolved to practice it. I have been zealous for what is good, and I shall not be confounded. My soul has struggled in it, and in doing it I was confirmed. I stretched out my hands on high, and my soul lamented its ignorance of her. I directed my soul toward her, and in knowledge I found her. I possessed a heart with her from the beginning; therefore I shall not be abandoned. My belly was troubled in seeking her; therefore I shall possess a good possession. The Lord has given me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise Him. Draw near to me, you unlearned, and gather yourselves together in the house of discipline. Why do you still delay, and what do you say of these things? Your souls are very thirsty. I opened my mouth and spoke: "Buy her for yourselves without money. Submit my neck to the yoke, and let your soul receive discipline." For she is near at hand to be found. See with your eyes how I have labored but a little and have found much rest for myself. Receive discipline with a great sum of silver, and possess much gold through her. Let your soul rejoice in His mercy, and be not confounded in His praise. Do your work before the time, and He will give you your reward in His time.

IF THE VERSION OF THE SEVENTY INTERPRETERS HAD REMAINED PURE and as it was published by them in the Greek, it would be superfluous, my most holy and learned Bishop Chromatius, for you to urge me to translate the Hebrew volumes into the Latin language. For that which had once occupied the ears of men and strengthened the roots of the growing Church was rightly to be approved even by our silence. But now, since different versions are carried about according to the variety of regions—and that ancient version is corrupted, which is said to be <unclear>confused</unclear> and corrupted—men at their own will have either <unclear>prayed</unclear> or <unclear>changed</unclear> what they wanted; and yet this happened not so much among the translators as among the scribes through <unclear>rash</unclear> additions, or by those who seemed not to understand what they saw. Alexandria and Egypt praise Hesychius as the author of their Seventy. Constantinople as far as Antioch approves the copies of Lucian the Martyr. The provinces between these read Palestinian codices which, having been worked upon by Origen, Eusebius and Pamphilus made public. And so the whole world fights among itself with this threefold variety. And certainly Origen not only composed copies of one version, but also described the edition of all, writing out individual words and noting where they disagreed. He placed here the sign of the *obelus* <note>term: obelus; a mark (†) used in ancient manuscripts to indicate that a word or passage is suspected of being spurious or should be deleted.</note>, that is, a little rod, so that it might be seen where he wished to condemn anything in the divine text. He inserted the *asterisk* <note>term: asterisk; a star-shaped mark (*) used by Jerome to indicate text that was present in the Hebrew original but missing from the Greek translation.</note> designating how much he found in the Hebrew vocabulary that had been set aside. Each sought to bring to light what he once took up <unclear>...proposed</unclear>. After the obelus, however, look upon the truth which is common without authority, each one strong. And this <unclear>he sought</unclear> to follow because they do not know this, or they think me foolish, having sacrificed to many of the Latins <unclear>...to the same...</unclear> after the transition of the truth, I settled in working upon the Hebrew. And I offer much to these and to the apostolic authors. The seventy books from the work which they interpreted show that precept from the Gospel called "that three-fold one," which was born: "He shall be called a Nazarene," and "They shall look upon him whom they have pierced," and other apostolic words. But if they see it has not come into the <unclear>...home...</unclear> nor ascended into the heart of man, those things which God has prepared for those who love him, and other similar things in the books of the Hebrews. Certainly the apostles, when they brought forth testimonies in words, knew them; and as they have them from the true Hebrew. Lest it seem that I do not lose any contest as I run in the <unclear>throat</unclear> but in the light, which is certain to me here while serving the Lord. I draw and flow from the living water. Everywhere it is separate to be that the Savior ceased the Seventy. Wherever in this and to dwell Revelation reveals. But they offer what they feared while it is in many places and <unclear>...also...</unclear> thus they presume copies. And a few of the old things he reads, and there are many obscurities in the canons of all which with truth <unclear>come forth</unclear> from many, provident about the Hebrew. Reading is manifest. Therefore he both <unclear>exasperates</unclear> and defends when they offer in others that they feared this, because either many feared in our books they knew the author alone. This is the common edition. When however another was amended from the Greek, it would have moved; and it ought not to be estimated as too much of theirs, because they found it always for the sake of edification. And because God does not say words in you in brief, I inserted this; but he made it in vocabulary, knots and a forest of names, which is separate; the <unclear>method</unclear> of the series has been confused, taking up the barbarism of the water and the child, of the right hand having been found by himself, and many sing the true history, if the ears of others shall be deaf.

Now those who first inhabited their possessions and cities were: the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants <term>Nethinim: Temple assistants given for service.</term>. Uthai the son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, of the sons of Perez the son of Judah. And of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons. Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their brothers: six hundred and ninety. Furthermore, of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah. And Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah; and their brothers according to their families: nine hundred and fifty-six. All these were heads of their ancestral houses, according to the houses of their fathers.

And of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin. Also Azariah the son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the leader of the house of God. Furthermore, Adaiah the son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; and Maasai the son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer; also their brothers, heads of their families: one thousand seven hundred and sixty most valiant men for the work of the ministry in the house of God. Of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari. Bakbakkar also, the carpenter, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph; and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah the son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites. The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman; and their brothers: Shallum was the chief; until that time they kept watch by their turns in the King’s Gate on the east, among the sons of Levi. Shallum the son of Kore, son of Abiasaph, son of Korah; his brothers from the house of his father, the Korahites, were over the work of the ministry, guardians of the thresholds of the tabernacle; and their families by turns serving at the entrance of the camp of the Lord. Phinehas the son of Eleazar was their leader before the Lord. Furthermore, Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper of the door of the tabernacle of testimony. All these chosen as gatekeepers at the gates were two hundred and twelve; and they were registered in their own villages, whom David and Samuel the Seer <note>original: "Samuel videns"</note> established in their trust: both them and their sons at the doors of the Lord and in the tabernacle.

Behold, by their turns. The gatekeepers were toward the four winds: that is, to the east, to the west, to the north, and to the south. Their brothers lived in the villages and came during their Sabbaths from time to time. The whole number of gatekeepers was committed to these four Levites, and they were over the chambers and treasuries of the Lord. They also stayed around the temple of the Lord in their watches, so that when it was time, they might open the doors in the morning. Of their kind were also those over the vessels of ministry; for by number the vessels were brought in and brought out. Also of those who had the sanctuary utensils entrusted to them: they were in charge of the fine flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices. The sons of the priests prepared the ointments from the spices. And Mattithiah the Levite, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was faithful in those things which were fried in the pan. Furthermore, of the sons of Kohath, their brothers, were over the loaves of proposition <term>Showbread: twelve loaves of bread placed on a table in the sanctuary every Sabbath.</term>, to always prepare new ones for each Sabbath. These are the chief singers among the families of the Levites, who stayed in the chambers, so that they were free from other ministries to serve. The heads of the Levites, leaders by their families, remained in Jerusalem. In Gibeon dwelt Jeiel, the father of Gibeon; and the name of his wife was Maachah. His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, Gedor also, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth. Furthermore, Mikloth fathered Shimeam; they dwelt opposite their brothers in Jerusalem with their brothers. Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul. Furthermore, Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal. And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; and Merib-baal fathered Micah. Furthermore, the sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea. Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmavoth, and Zimri. Zimri fathered Moza. Moza fathered Rephaiah; his son was Eleasah, from whom was born Azel. Now Azel had six sons whose names were these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These are the sons of Azel.

<margin>1 Chronicles 10</margin>
Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from the Palestinians <note>original: "palestinos"</note>; and they fell wounded on Mount Gilboa. When the Philistines had approached, pursuing Saul and his sons, they struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul. And the battle grew heavy against Saul; the archers found him and wounded him with javelins. Saul said to his armor-bearer: "Draw your sword and kill me, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me." But his armor-bearer would not do it, being terrified with fear. Therefore Saul took the sword and fell upon it. When his armor-bearer saw this—namely, that Saul was dead—he also fell upon his own sword and died. Thus Saul perished with his three sons, and all his house fell together. When the men of Israel who lived in the plains saw this, they fled. And Saul and his sons being dead, they abandoned their cities and were scattered here and there; and the Philistines came and lived in them. On the next day, while the Philistines were stripping the spoils of the slain, they found Saul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa. When they had stripped him and cut off his head and bared him of his armor, they sent into their land so that it might be carried around and shown in the temples of the idols and to the people. They consecrated his armor in the shrine of their god and fixed his head in the temple of Dagon. When the men of Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul, all the brave men arose and took the bodies of Saul and his sons; they brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones under the oak which was in Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days. Thus Saul died because of his iniquities, because he transgressed the command of the Lord which he had commanded and did not keep it, but moreover even consulted a medium <note>original: "pythonissam"</note> and did not hope in the Lord. For this reason He killed him and transferred his kingdom to David the son of Jesse.

<margin>1 Chronicles 11</margin>
Therefore all Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying: "We are your bone and your flesh. Also yesterday and the day before, while Saul was still reigning, you were the one who led Israel out and in. For the Lord your God said to you: You shall feed my people Israel, and you shall be the leader over them." So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them before the Lord. And they anointed him king over Israel, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke by the hand of Samuel. David and all Israel went to Jerusalem; this is Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were. And those who lived in Jebus said to David: "You shall not enter here." Furthermore, David took the fortress of Zion, which is the city of David, and he proposed a reward, saying: "Whoever strikes a Jebusite first shall be chief and leader." So Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first and was made chief. David lived in the fortress, and for that reason it was called the City of David. He built the city round about from Millo to the surrounding wall; and Joab rebuilt the rest of the city. And David went on and grew, and the Lord of hosts was with him. These are the heads of the brave men of David who helped him to become king over all Israel according to the word of the Lord which He spoke to Israel. And this is the number of David’s strong men. Jashobeam the son of Hachmoni, the chief among thirty; he lifted his spear against three hundred wounded at one time. And after him Eleazar the son of his uncle the Ahohite, who was among the three mighty ones. He was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines were gathered to that place for battle; and there was a field in that region full of barley, and the people had fled from before the Philistines. He stood in the middle of the field and defended it. When he had struck the Philistines, the Lord gave a great salvation to His people. Also three of the thirty leaders went down to the rock where David was, to the cave of Adullam, when the Philistines had encamped in the valley of Rephaim. Furthermore, David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem. David longed and said: "Oh, that someone would give me water from the cistern of Bethlehem which is at the gate!" So these three broke through the middle of the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the cistern of Bethlehem which was at the gate, and brought it to David to drink. He would not, but instead poured it out as an offering to the Lord, saying: "Far be it from me that I should do this in the sight of my God, and drink the blood of these men, because at the peril of their lives they brought me water." And for this reason he would not drink. These things the three most valiant men did.

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a most valiant man who had performed many deeds, from Kabzeel. He struck down the two Ariels of Moab; and he went down and killed a lion in the middle of a cistern in the time of snow. And he struck an Egyptian man whose stature was five cubits, and who had a spear like a weaver's beam. He went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear which he held in his hand, and killed him with his own spear. These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, who was most famous among the three strong men, and first among the thirty. However, he did not reach the three. And David set him over his bodyguard <note>original: "super aurem suam"</note>. Furthermore, the most valiant in the army were: Asahel the brother of Joab, and Elhanan the son of his uncle from Bethlehem, Shammoth the Harodite, Helez the Pelonite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite, Sibbechai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ithai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hurai of the brook Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite, Azmavoth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite. The sons of Hashem the Gizonite: Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sachar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur, Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite, Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai, Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri, Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah. Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite, Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai. Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, leader of the Reubenites, and with him thirty; Hanan the son of Maachah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite.
