Twenty-eighth: He fathered <unclear>Asahel</unclear> his son. <unclear>Abner</unclear> was the son of <unclear>Ner</unclear>. And <unclear>Kish</unclear> and <unclear>Asahel</unclear> the son of David. And Abijah his daughter. And the rest of the book of Chronicles <note>original: "paralipomenon," a title for the Books of Chronicles meaning "things omitted"</note> chapter 11.

These are the men who gathered to David at Ziklag, while he was still a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. They were among the most powerful and distinguished warriors, skilled with the bow, using both the right hand and the left to hurl stones with slings and shoot arrows; they were from the tribe of Benjamin. Their leaders were Ahiezer son of Amasai and Joash the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite, and Azmaveth and Berakah and Jehu the Anathothite; also Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and a leader over the thirty. Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite; Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite; Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, and from the Korahites <unclear>Jeroham</unclear> and Jozabad the sons of Jeroham of Gedor. And from the Gadites, some brave warriors deserted to David while he was hiding in the wilderness—mighty men of valor, trained for war, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and who were as swift as gazelles on the mountains: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third, Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth, Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh, Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth, Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh. These Gadites were leaders in the army; the least was over a hundred soldiers, and the greatest over a thousand. These are the ones who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks, and they put to flight all those in the valleys, toward the east and toward the west. Some from the tribe of Benjamin and Judah also came to the stronghold where David was staying. David went out to meet them and said: "If you have come peacefully to me to help me, my heart shall be joined to yours. But if you come to betray me to my enemies, though I have no guilt on my hands, may the God of our ancestors see and judge." Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, the chief of the thirty, and he said: "We are yours, O David, and with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, for your God helps you." So David received them and made them captains of his band. Moreover, some from Manasseh deserted to David when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul (though they did not actually fight for them, because the leaders of the Philistines took counsel and sent him away, saying, "At the peril of our heads he will desert to his master Saul"). When David was returning to Ziklag, these men from Manasseh deserted to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, and <unclear>Machbannai</unclear>, captains of thousands in Manasseh. They provided help to David against the raiding bands, for they were all mighty men of valor and became captains in the army. Indeed, day by day men came to David to help him, until there was a great army, like the army of God. These are the numbers of the leaders of the armed troops who came to David at Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, according to the word of the Lord. The sons of Judah, carrying shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred, prepared for war. Of the sons of Simeon, mighty men of valor for war: seven thousand one hundred. Of the sons of Levi: four thousand six hundred. Jehoiada also, the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred. Also Zadok, a young man of great courage, and from his father’s house twenty-two leaders. Of the sons of Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul: three thousand, for until then the greatest part of them had remained loyal to the house of Saul. Moreover, of the sons of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their ancestral houses. From the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make David king. And of the sons of Issachar, men who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do: two hundred chiefs, and all their kinsmen were at their command. Of Zebulun, such as went out to battle and could draw up in formation with all weapons of war: fifty thousand, they came to help him with an undivided heart. Of Naphtali: one thousand captains, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear. Of Dan, prepared for battle: twenty-eight thousand six hundred. Of Asher, such as went out to battle and could draw up in formation: forty thousand. From across the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all the weapons of war for battle: one hundred and twenty thousand. All these warriors, marshaled for battle, came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest of Israel were of one heart to make David king. They were there with David for three days, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had prepared for them. Moreover, those who were near them, as far as Issachar and Naphtali, were bringing bread on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen—provisions of flour, cakes of figs <note>original: "palathas," a term for pressed cakes of dried fruit</note>, clusters of raisins, oil, wine, oxen, and sheep in great abundance. For there was joy in Israel.

David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and with every leader. And David said to all the assembly of Israel: "If it seems good to you, and if it is from the Lord our God, let us send word abroad to our brothers who remain in all the regions of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities and pasturelands, that they may gather to us. And let us bring again the Ark of our God to us, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul." And all the assembly agreed to do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people. So David gathered all Israel together, from the Shihor of Egypt to the entrance of Hamath, to bring the Ark of God from Kiriath-jearim. David and all Israel went up to the hill of Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the Ark of God the Lord, who sits enthroned above the cherubim, where His name is invoked. They carried the Ark of God on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and his brothers drove the cart. David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their might, with songs and lyres and harps and tambourines and cymbals and trumpets. When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza reached out his hand to steady the Ark, for the oxen stumbled. The anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzza, and He struck him down because he put his hand to the Ark; and he died there before God. David was grieved because the Lord had broken out against Uzza; and that place is called "The Breach of Uzza" <note>original: "divisio oza"</note> to this day. David was afraid of God that day, saying, "How can I bring the Ark of God home to me?" So David did not take the Ark with him into the City of David, but took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. The Ark of God remained with the family of Obed-edom in his house for three months, and the Lord blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that he had. Now Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, masons, and carpenters to build a palace for him. And David perceived that the Lord had established him as king over Israel, and that his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of His people Israel.

David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David fathered more sons and daughters. These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all went up to search for him. When David heard of it, he went out against them. Now the Philistines had come and made a raid in the Valley of Rephaim. David inquired of God, saying, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?" And the Lord said to him, "Go up, and I will deliver them into your hand." So they went up to Baal-perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand, like a breakthrough of water." Therefore the name

<column-break/>

of that place was called Baal-perazim <note>Literally "The Lord of Breakthroughs"</note>. The Philistines abandoned their gods there, and David gave orders to burn them. Once again the Philistines made a raid in the valley. David inquired of God again, and God said to him, "Do not go up after them; turn away from them and come upon them opposite the pear trees <note>Often translated as balsam or mulberry trees</note>. When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the pear trees, then go out to battle, for God has gone out before you to strike down the army of the Philistines." David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon to Gezer. The fame of David went out into all lands, and the Lord brought the fear of him upon all nations. David built houses for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the Ark of God and pitched a tent for it. Then David said, "No one but the Levites may carry the Ark of God, for the Lord chose them to carry the Ark of the Lord and to minister to Him forever." David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the Ark of the Lord to the place he had prepared for it. He also gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites: of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, with one hundred and twenty of his kinsmen; of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, with two hundred and ten of his kinsmen; of the sons of Gershon, Joel the chief, with one hundred and thirty of his kinsmen; of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, with two hundred of his kinsmen; of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, with eighty of his kinsmen; of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, with one hundred and twelve of his kinsmen. Then David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab, and said to them, "You are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites. Consecrate yourselves, you and your kinsmen, so that you may bring up the Ark of the Lord, the God of Israel, to the place that I have prepared for it. Because you did not carry it the first time, the Lord our God broke out against us, because we did not seek Him according to the rule." So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the Ark of the Lord, the God of Israel. And the Levites carried the Ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the Lord.

So David and the elders of Israel and the captains of thousands went to bring up the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord from the house of Obed-edom with rejoicing. And because God helped the Levites who were carrying the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams. David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the Ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the leader of the music among the singers. David also wore a linen ephod. So all Israel brought up the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord with shouting, to the sound of the horn, trumpets, and cymbals, playing loudly on harps and lyres. As the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord came to the City of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window and saw King David dancing and celebrating, and she despised him in her heart. They brought the Ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God. When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord and distributed to every person in Israel, both man and woman, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins. He appointed some of the Levites as ministers before the Ark of the Lord, to invoke, to thank, and to praise the Lord, the God of Israel: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, who were to play harps and lyres; Asaph was to make a sound with cymbals, and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets continually before the Ark of the Covenant of God. Then on that day David first appointed Asaph and his kinsmen to give thanks to the Lord:

> Give thanks to the Lord,
and call upon His name; make known His deeds among the peoples!
Sing to Him, sing praises to Him; tell of all His wondrous works! Glory in His holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice! Seek the Lord and His strength; seek His presence continually! Remember the wondrous works that He has done, His miracles and the judgments He uttered, O offspring of Israel His servant, children of Jacob, His chosen ones! He is the Lord our God; His judgments are in all the earth. Remember His covenant forever, the word that He commanded, for a thousand generations, the covenant that He made with Abraham, His sworn promise to Isaac, which He confirmed to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant, saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as your portion for an inheritance." When you were few in number, of little account, and sojourners in it, wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people, He allowed no one to oppress them; He rebuked kings on their account, saying, "Touch not my anointed ones, do my prophets no harm!"
Sing to the Lord, all the earth! Tell of His salvation from day to day. Declare His glory among the nations, His marvelous works among all the peoples! For great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised, and He is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the Lord made the heavens. Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and joy are in His place. Ascribe to the Lord, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the Lord glory and strength! Ascribe to the Lord the glory due His name; bring an offering and come before Him! Worship the Lord in the splendor of holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth; yes, the world is established; it shall never be moved. Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice, and let them say among the nations, "The Lord reigns!" Let the sea roar, and all that fills it; let the field exult, and everything in it! Then shall the trees of the forest sing for joy before the Lord, for He comes to judge the earth. Oh give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; for His steadfast love endures forever! Say also: "Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather and deliver us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name and glory in Your praise." Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Then all the people said, "Amen!" and praised the Lord.

As for the rest, David left Asaph and his kinsmen there before the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord to minister regularly before the Ark as each day required, and also Obed-edom and his sixty-eight kinsmen, while Obed-edom the son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers. And he left Zadok the priest and his brothers the priests before the tabernacle of the Lord in the high place that was at Gibeon, to offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of burnt offering regularly morning and evening, according to all that is written in the Law of the Lord that He commanded Israel. With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and expressly named to give thanks to the Lord, for His steadfast love endures forever. Heman and Jeduthun had trumpets and cymbals for the music and instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were appointed to the gate. Then all the people departed each to his house, and David returned to bless his own household.

Now when David lived in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, "Behold, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord is under a tent." And Nathan said to David, "Do all that is in your heart, for God is with you." But that same night the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying, "Go and tell my servant David, 'Thus says the Lord: It is not you who will build me a house to dwell in...'"

...a house to dwell in, nor did the men remain, and I conceived the plan to build a house in which the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord and the footstool of the feet of our God might rest. And I prepared everything for the building. But God said to me: "You shall not build a house to my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood." However, the Lord God of Israel chose me from my father’s entire house to be king over Israel forever. For from Judah he chose the leaders, and from the house of Judah, my father’s house; and among the sons of my father, it pleased him to appoint me as king over all Israel. And of my sons—for the Lord has given me many sons—he chose my son Solomon to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel. And he said to me: "Solomon your son shall build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be a father to him. And I will establish his kingdom forever, if he perseveres in performing my commandments and my judgments, as he does this day." Now therefore, in the sight of the entire assembly of Israel and in the hearing of our God, keep and seek out all the commandments of the Lord your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it to your children after you forever. 

And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a perfect heart and a willing mind. For the Lord searches all hearts and understands all the thoughts of the mind. If you seek him, you will find him; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever. Now therefore, because the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary, be strengthened and complete it. Then David gave his son Solomon the description <note>original: "descriptionem," referring to the architectural plans or pattern</note> of the porch, the temple, the storehouses, the upper rooms, the inner chambers, and the house of the mercy seat <note>The "propitiatorium" or lid of the Ark</note>. He also gave him the plans for all the courts he had imagined, and the chambers all around for the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the holy things; and for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the work of the service of the house of the Lord, and for all the vessels used in the ministry of the temple of the Lord. 

He designated gold by weight for each vessel of the ministry, and silver by weight according to the diversity of the vessels and works. He also assigned gold for the golden lampstands and their lamps, according to the measure of each lampstand and its lamps. Similarly, he distinguished the weight of silver for the silver lampstands and their lamps according to the diversity of their size. He also gave gold for the tables of showbread <note>original: "mensas propositionis"</note> according to the different tables, and silver for other silver tables. He designated gold of the purest kind for the flesh-hooks, bowls, and censers, and for the golden basins, weight by weight for each basin; and likewise, he separated the weight of silver for the silver basins. He made the altar on which incense is burned from the purest gold, so that from it the likeness of the chariot of the cherubim extending their wings and covering the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord might be formed. "All these things," he said, "came to me written by the hand of the Lord, so that I might understand all the works of the pattern." 

David also said to his son Solomon: "Be strengthened, be robust, and act. Do not fear and do not be dismayed. For the Lord my God will be with you; he will not fail you nor forsake you until you finish every work of the service of the house of the Lord. Behold, the divisions of the priests and the Levites are ready for every service of the house of God; they are with you and are prepared for every work, and both the leaders and the people are ready for all your commands."

<margin>1 Chronicles 29</margin>
**A**nd I, King David, spoke to the whole assembly: "Solomon my son is the only one whom God has chosen, still a youth and tender. But the work is great, for this habitation is prepared not for man, but for God. With all my strength, I have prepared the costs for the house of my God: gold for the gold vessels, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, wood for the wood, onyx stones and stones like antimony <note>original: "stibinos," a dark mineral used for decoration or eye makeup</note> and of various colors, and every kind of precious stone, and Parian marble in great abundance. And beyond these things which I have offered for the house of my God, from my own wealth I give gold and silver to the temple of my God, besides what I have prepared for the holy house: three thousand talents of gold from the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of most refined silver for plating the walls of the temple. And wherever gold is needed for gold, and wherever silver is needed for silver, let the works be done by the hands of craftsmen. And if anyone is willing, let him fill his hand today and offer whatever he wishes to the Lord."

**S**o the leaders of the families, the princes of the tribes of Israel, the captains of thousands and hundreds, and the overseers of the king's works made their promises. And they gave for the works of the house of God five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand darics <note>original: "solidos," likely referring to the Persian daric or a similar gold coin</note>; ten thousand talents of silver; eighteen thousand talents of bronze; and one hundred thousand talents of iron. And whoever was found to have precious stones gave them to the treasures of the house of the Lord by the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite. And the people rejoiced when they promised these vows voluntarily, because they offered them to the Lord with their whole heart; but King David also rejoiced with great joy. And he blessed the Lord before the whole multitude and said: "Blessed are you, O Lord God of Israel our father, from eternity to eternity."

**A**nd David said: "Yours, O Lord, is the magnificence, and the power, and the glory, and the victory; and to you is the praise. For all things that are in heaven and on earth are yours. Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom, and you are above all princes. Yours are the riches, and yours is the glory. You rule over all; in your hand is strength and power; in your hand is greatness and the empire over all. Now therefore, our God, we confess to you and we praise your glorious name."

<column-break/>

"**F**or who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to promise all these things to you? All things are yours, and we have given to you what we received from your hand. For we are pilgrims before you and strangers, just like all our fathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no staying. **O** Lord our God, all this abundance which we have prepared so that a house might be built to your holy name is from your hand, and all things are yours. **I** know, my God, that you prove hearts and love simplicity; therefore, in the simplicity of my heart, I have joyfully offered all these things. And I have seen your people who were present offer their gifts to you with immense joy. **O** Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel our fathers, keep this will of their heart forever, and let this mind always remain in veneration of you. **A**nd give to my son Solomon a perfect heart, that he may keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your ceremonies, and do all things, and build the temple which I have prepared." 

**T**hen David commanded the whole assembly: "Bless the Lord your God." And the whole assembly blessed the Lord God of their fathers, and they bowed themselves and adored God, and then the king. And they sacrificed victims to the Lord and offered burnt offerings the following day: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs with their drink offerings, and every rite in great abundance. And they ate and drank before the Lord on that day with great gladness. And they anointed Solomon the son of David a second time. They anointed him to the Lord as prince, and Zadok as high priest. And Solomon sat upon the throne of the Lord as king in place of David his father, and he pleased everyone, and all Israel obeyed him. Moreover, all the princes and powerful men, and all the sons of King David, gave their hand and were subject to King Solomon. Therefore, the Lord magnified Solomon above all Israel and gave him the glory of a kingdom such as no king of Israel had before him. 

Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel. And the days that he reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. He died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and glory. And Solomon his son reigned in his place. Now the deeds of King David, from first to last, are written in the book of Samuel the seer, in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the volume of Gad the seer, concerning his entire reign, his strength, and the times that passed under him, whether in Israel or in all the kingdoms of the earth.

<margin>2 Chronicles 1</margin>
**S**o Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him, and magnified him to a high degree. **A**nd Solomon gave orders to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and hundreds, to the judges and leaders of all Israel, and the princes of the families. And he went with the entire multitude to the high place of Gibeon, where the Tabernacle of the Covenant of God was, which Moses the servant of God had made in the wilderness. However, David had brought the Ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, and where he had pitched a tent for it; that is, in Jerusalem. The bronze altar also, which Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had fabricated, was there before the Tabernacle of the Lord; and Solomon and all the assembly sought it out. And Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the Tabernacle of the Covenant of the Lord and offered a thousand victims upon it. 

Behold, in that very night, God appeared to him, saying: "Ask what you wish that I should give to you." And Solomon said to God: "You have shown great mercy to David my father, and have appointed me king in his place. Now therefore, O Lord God, let your word which you promised to David my father be fulfilled; for you have made me king over your people, who are as numerous as the dust of the earth. Give me wisdom and understanding, that I may go in and out before your people. For who can worthily judge this people of yours, which is so great?" And the Lord said to Solomon: "Because this pleased your heart more, and you did not ask for riches, wealth, or glory, nor for the lives of those who hate you, nor for many days of life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge so that you might judge my people over whom I have appointed you king: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. And I will give you riches, wealth, and glory, so that no king before you or after you shall be like you." 

Then Solomon came from the high place of Gibeon to Jerusalem, before the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and reigned over Israel. And he gathered to himself chariots and horsemen; and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem. And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamore trees that grow in the plains. And horses were brought to him from Egypt and from Kue <note>original: "Coa," identifying a region in Cilicia famous for horse breeding</note> by the king's merchants, who bought and sold them at a price. A chariot of four horses from Egypt cost six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse one hundred and fifty; likewise, purchases were made from all the kingdoms of the Hittites and from the kings of Syria.

<margin>2 Chronicles 2</margin> **A**nd Solomon decreed to build a house to the name of the Lord and a palace for himself. And he counted out seventy thousand men to carry burdens on their shoulders, and eighty thousand who would cut stones in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers over them. He also sent word to Hiram, the king of Tyre, saying: "As you did for David my father, sending him cedar logs to build himself a house in which he dwelt, so do for me, that I may build a house to the name of the Lord my God, to dedicate it for burning incense before him, for smoking aromatics, for the continual showbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, new moons, and the festivals of the Lord our God forever, which are commanded to Israel. For the house I desire to build is great; for our God is greater than all gods. Who then can prevail to build him a worthy house, if the heaven and the heavens of heavens cannot contain him? Who am I that I should be able to build him a house, except for this purpose: that incense may be burned before him? 

Therefore, send me a learned man who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, purple, scarlet, and hyacinth <note>A blue or violet-colored fabric</note>, and who knows how to carve engravings, together with the craftsmen I have with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared. Send also cedar, fir, and pine logs from Lebanon. For I know that your servants know how to cut timber from Lebanon, and my servants shall be with your servants, so that many logs may be prepared for me. For the house I desire to build will be exceedingly magnificent. Furthermore, to the workmen who will cut the timber, your servants, I will give as food twenty thousand cors <note>A biblical unit of dry measure, roughly 220 liters</note> of wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, fifteen thousand baths <note>original: "metros," a liquid measure</note> of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."

Then Hiram the king of Tyre replied in a letter which he sent to Solomon: "Because the Lord loved his people, he has made you king over them." And he added, saying: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave to King David a son who is wise, learned, skilled, and intelligent, to build a house for the Lord and a palace for himself. I have now sent to you a prudent and most skillful man, Hiram my father <note>original: "hiram patrem meum" - a title of honor for the master craftsman Hiram-Abi</note>, the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, whose father was a Tyrian. He knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, marble and wood, also in purple, hyacinth, fine linen, and scarlet, and who knows how to carve every kind of engraving and to devise prudently whatever is necessary in the work, along with your craftsmen and the craftsmen of my lord David your father. Therefore, my lord, send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine which you promised to your servants. We will cut as many logs from Lebanon as you need and will bring them on rafts by sea to Joppa; it will be your task to transport them to Jerusalem." 

Solomon then numbered all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel after the census his father David had made, and there were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred. And he made seventy thousand of them to carry burdens on their shoulders, and eighty thousand to cut stones in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers of the work for the people.

# Solomon was strengthened

<column-break/>

<margin>
3 Kings 3 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 1 Kings 3.</note>
</margin>

Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom, and the Lord was with him, and magnified him to the highest degree. And Solomon gave orders to all Israel: to the tribunes and centurions, and the leaders and judges of all Israel, and the princes of families. And he went with the entire multitude to the high place of Gibeon, where the tabernacle of the covenant of the Lord was, which Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the wilderness. However, David had brought the Ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, and where he had pitched a tabernacle for it, which is in Jerusalem. Also the bronze altar which <term>Bezalel</term><note>The chief artisan of the Tabernacle in the time of Moses.</note> the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had fashioned was there in the sight of the tabernacle of the Lord; and Solomon and all the assembly sought it out. And Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the tabernacle of the covenant of the Lord and offered a thousand victims upon it. And behold, in that very night, the Lord appeared to him, saying: "Ask what you wish, that I may give it to you." And Solomon said to God: "You have shown great mercy to my father David, and have appointed me king in his place. Now therefore, O Lord God, let your word which you promised to my father David be fulfilled. For you have made me king over your people, who are as numerous as the dust of the earth. Give me wisdom and intelligence, so that I may go in and out before your people. For who can worthily rule this your people, who are so great and innumerable?" And the Lord said to Solomon: "Because this has pleased your heart more, and you have not asked for riches, or wealth, or glory, nor for the lives of those who hate you, nor even for many days of life; but have asked for wisdom and knowledge, so that you might be able to judge my people over whom I have appointed you king: wisdom and knowledge are given to you. Moreover, I will give you riches and glory and wealth, such as no king before you has had, nor shall any after you have the like." Solomon then came from the high place of Gibeon to Jerusalem, before the tabernacle of the covenant, and reigned over Israel. And he gathered to himself chariots and horsemen; and there were a thousand four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem. And the king made silver and gold in Jerusalem as common as stones, and cedars like the sycamore trees that grow in the plains in great multitude. Horses were brought to him from Egypt and from Kue by the king’s merchants, who went and bought them at a price: a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Likewise, for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria, the purchase was carried out. And Solomon intended to build a house for the name of the Lord and a palace for himself. And he numbered eighty thousand men to carry burdens on their shoulders, and eighty thousand to cut stones in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers over them.

<margin>
3 Kings 5
</margin>

And he sent to Hiram the king of Tyre, saying: "As you dealt with my father, sending him cedar logs to build a house for himself to dwell in, so deal with me, that I may build a house for the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it for the burning of incense before him, and for the fuming of aromatics, and for the continual setting out of the bread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths also, and at the new moons, and on the festivals of the Lord our God forever, as has been commanded to Israel. For the house which I desire to build is great. For our God is great above all gods. Who then could prevail to build him a house? If heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain him, how great am I, that I should be able to build him a house? But it is for this purpose only: that incense may be burned before him. Therefore, send me a learned man who knows how to work in gold and silver, and brass and iron, and purple and crimson and blue, and who knows how to engrave carvings with these craftsmen whom I have with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom my father prepared. Also send me cedar logs, and fir and pine from Lebanon. For I know that your servants know how to cut trees in Lebanon. And my servants will be with your servants, so that they may prepare many logs for me. For the house which I desire to build is exceedingly great and high. I will provide for the workmen who cut the wood as food: twenty thousand <term>cors</term><note>A biblical unit of dry volume, roughly equal to 220 liters.</note> of wheat, and as many of barley, and twenty thousand <term>metretas</term><note>A liquid measure, roughly 39 liters.</note> of wine, and twenty thousand of oil." Then Hiram king of Tyre replied by letter, which he sent to Solomon: "Because the Lord loved his people, he made you king over them." And he added, saying: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, and who gave to King David a wise son, learned and sensible and prudent, to build a house for the Lord and a palace for himself. I have therefore sent to you a wise and extraordinary man, <term>Huram-abi</term><note>Often translated as "Hiram my father," a title of respect for the master craftsman.</note>, the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, whose father was a Tyrian. He knows how to work in gold and silver, and brass and iron, and marble and wood, also in purple and blue and fine linen and crimson; and he knows how to engrave all carvings and to invent prudently whatever is necessary for the work with your craftsmen, and with the craftsmen of my lord David your father. Now therefore, the wheat and the barley and the wine and the oil which you promised, my lord, send to your servants. We will cut the wood from Lebanon, as much as you need, and we will bring them in rafts by sea to Joppa; it will be your task to carry them up to Jerusalem." Then Solomon numbered all the men who were foreigners in the land of Israel, after the numbering which his father David had performed; and there were found a hundred and fifty-three thousand and six hundred. And he made eighty thousand of them carriers of burdens on their shoulders, and eighty thousand who should cut stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred who were overseers of the work of the people.

And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, which had been shown to David his father, in the place David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. And he began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign. And these are the foundations which Solomon laid to build the house of the Lord: the length in cubits by the first measure was sixty, and the width twenty. The porch indeed, which was in front, in length according to the measure of the width of the house, was twenty cubits. Furthermore, the height was a hundred and twenty cubits; and he gilded it on the inside with purest gold. The greater house he paneled with fir-wood, and fixed plates of finest gold over the whole. He carved palms in them and what seemed like little chains entwining one another. He paved the floor of the temple with most precious marble of great beauty. Moreover, the gold was of the most refined sort; he overlaid its plates and walls and posts and doors—as much as was of the rooms—and he carved cherubim on the walls. He also made the house of the Holy of Holies; its length according to the width of the house was twenty cubits, and the width was similarly twenty cubits. He covered it with gold plates which were worth six hundred talents. Moreover, for the golden nails, he so ordered it that each nail should weigh fifty shekels; he also covered the upper chambers with gold. He also made in the house of the Holy of Holies two cherubim of statuary work, and covered them with gold. The wings of the cherubim were extended twenty cubits, so that one wing of a cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and the other wing reached the wing of the other cherub. Similarly, the wing of the other cherub touched the wall, and its other wing touched the wing of the first cherub; and so the wings of these two cherubim being spread out, they extended for twenty cubits. They themselves stood upright on their feet, and their faces were toward the outer house. He also made the veil of blue, purple, fine linen, and crimson, and wove cherubim into it.

**S**he then gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, and very many spices, and most precious stones. There were no such spices as those which the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon. But the servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon also brought gold from Ophir, and <term>thyine wood</term><note>Likely aromatic citron-wood or sandalwood.</note>, and most precious stones. From the thyine wood, the king made steps in the house of the Lord and in the royal house, as well as harps and lyres for the singers; never were such woods seen in the land of Judah. And King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba all that she desired and asked for, far more than she had brought to him. She then returned to her own land with her servants. Now the weight of gold offered to Solomon each year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold, besides the sum which the envoys of various nations and merchants were accustomed to bring. All the kings of Arabia and the <term>satraps</term><note>Provincial governors or local rulers.</note> of the lands also brought gold and silver to Solomon. King Solomon therefore made two hundred golden shields, using six hundred pieces of gold for each shield. Also three hundred bucklers of the purest gold, using five hundred pieces of gold for each buckler; and the king placed them in the armory of the Forest of Lebanon, made of the purest gold. Indeed, silver in those days was considered of no value. For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram once every three years, and they brought from there gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. Thus Solomon was magnified above all the kings of the earth in riches and glory. And all the kings of the earth desired to see Solomon's face, to hear the wisdom which God had put in his heart. And they offered him gifts: vessels of silver and gold, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules every year.

**S**olomon also had forty thousand horses in stalls, and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; some of whom he stationed in the chariot cities, and others with the king in Jerusalem. **R**ehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem and built walled cities in Judah. Now the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel came to him from all their dwellings, leaving their possessions and their fields, and gathered to Judah and Jerusalem; because Jeroboam and his successors had cast them out, so that they might not perform the priestly office for the Lord. For [Jeroboam] appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for the demons, and for the calves he had made. But also from all the tribes of Israel, whoever had set their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem to sacrifice victims before the Lord God of their fathers. And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and confirmed Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years. For they walked in the ways of David and Solomon for three years.

**W**hen the kingdom of Rehoboam had been strengthened and made firm, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him. In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, <term>Shishak</term><note>The biblical name for Pharaoh Sheshonq I.</note> king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord, with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; and there was no numbering the common people who came with him from Egypt—namely Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians. And he took the most fortified cities in Judah and came as far as Jerusalem. Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem, fleeing from Shishak, and said to them: "Thus says the Lord: You have left me, and I have left you in the hand of Shishak." And the princes of Israel and the king, being struck with fear, said: "The Lord is just." When the Lord saw that they were humbled, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying: "Because they are humbled, I will not destroy them; I will give them a little help, and my fury shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless, they shall serve him, that they may know the difference between my service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands." So Shishak king of Egypt departed from Jerusalem, having taken away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house; he took everything, even the golden shields that Solomon had made. In place of which, the king made bronze ones and delivered them to the captains of the shield-bearers who guarded the entrance of the palace. And when the king entered the house of the Lord, the shield-bearers came and took them, and later returned them to their armory.

---

**R**ehoboam had eighteen wives and sixty concubines; he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters. But he loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines. And he appointed Abijah her son as the head, the leader over all his brothers, for he intended to make him king. He was wiser and more powerful in all his borders. Rehoboam truly [ruled] in Judah and Benjamin and in all the fortified cities; and he gave them plenty of food and sought many wives.

---

**I**n the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah reigned over Judah. He reigned for three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Maacah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam. When Abijah had entered the battle, he had most warlike men, and four hundred thousand chosen men. Jeroboam set the battle line against him with eight hundred thousand men, who were also chosen and most valiant for war. Then Abijah stood upon Mount Zemaraim and said: "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel! Are you ignorant that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and his sons by a <term>covenant of salt</term><note>A symbolic expression meaning a perpetual, incorruptible agreement.</note>? And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord. And there were gathered to him most vain men and <term>sons of Belial</term><note>A Hebrew idiom for wicked, worthless, or lawless people.</note>, and they prevailed against Rehoboam the son of Solomon. Furthermore, Rehoboam was unrefined and of a fearful heart, and could not resist them. Now therefore, you say that you can resist the kingdom of the Lord which the sons of David hold; and you have a very great multitude, and the golden calves which Jeroboam made for you as gods. And you have cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made for yourselves priests like all the peoples of the lands. Whoever comes and sacrifices a bull among the oxen and seven rams becomes a priest of those who are not gods. But our Lord is God, whom we do not forsake; and the priests, the sons of Aaron, minister to the Lord, and the Levites are in their order. Indeed, they offer holocausts to the Lord every day, morning and evening, and incense composed according to the commands of the law; and they place the <term>showbread</term><note>Original: "panes propositionis" - twelve loaves of bread set out in the Temple as a ritual offering.</note> upon a most clean table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps, that they may burn always at evening. For we keep the commands of the Lord our God, whom you have forsaken. Therefore, in our army God is the leader, and his priests, who sound the trumpets and cry out against you, sons of Israel! Do not fight against the Lord God of your fathers, for it is not expedient for you."

<meta>This page continues the history of the kings of Judah, following the death of Abijah and the accession of his son Asa. It covers the religious reforms and military victories of Asa, his eventual lapse in faith, and the beginning of the righteous reign of his son Jehoshaphat.</meta>

Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David.

### And Asa his son reigned in his stead; in his days the land was quiet for ten years.

<margin>2 Chronicles 14</margin>
Asa did what was good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord his God. He overturned the altars of foreign worship and the high places; he broke the statues and cut down the sacred groves <note>Latin: *lucos*. These were wooded areas dedicated to pagan deities, often associated with Asherah.</note>. He commanded Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and all the commandments. He removed the altars and shrines from all the cities of Judah, and he reigned in peace. He also built fortified cities in Judah because there was rest, and no wars arose in those times, for the Lord granted him peace. And he said to Judah: "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls, and strengthen them with towers, gates, and bars while the land is free from war; for we have sought the Lord our God, and He has given us peace on every side." So they built, and there was no hindrance in their construction. Asa had in his army three hundred thousand men from Judah who carried shields and spears, and from Benjamin two hundred and eighty thousand shield-bearers and archers. All these were very valiant men. But Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah. Asa went out to meet him and set his battle line in the valley of Zephathah, which is near Mareshah. He called upon the Lord his God and said: "Lord, it is no different for You to help whether with few or with many. Help us, O Lord our God. For in You and in Your name we have come against this multitude, having our confidence. O Lord, You are our God; let not man prevail against You." The Lord terrified the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians fled. Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and the Ethiopians fell until they were utterly destroyed, for they were crushed by the Lord's stroke and by the fighting of His army. They took much spoil and struck all the cities around Gerar, for a great terror had seized everyone; they plundered the cities and carried away much booty. They also destroyed the sheepfolds and took away innumerable flocks of sheep and camels, and then they returned to Jerusalem.

### Now Azariah the son of Oded, moved by the Holy Spirit, went out to meet Asa and said to him: "Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin."

<margin>2 Chronicles 15</margin>
Now Azariah the son of Oded, moved by the Spirit of God, went out to meet Asa and said to him: "Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you because you have been with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you. For many days Israel shall be without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without the law. But when they return in their distress and cry out to the Lord, the God of Israel, and seek Him, they shall find Him. In that time there shall be no peace for going out or coming in, but terrors on every side among all the inhabitants of the earth. For nation shall fight against nation and city against city, because the Lord will trouble them with every distress. But as for you, take courage and let not your hands be weak, for there shall be a reward for your work." When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Azariah the son of Oded the prophet, he took courage and removed the idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim; and he dedicated the altar of the Lord that was before the porch of the Lord. He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon. For many had fled to him from Israel when they saw that the Lord his God was with him. When they had come to Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign, they sacrificed to the Lord on that day from the spoils and booty they had brought: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand rams. They entered into a covenant, according to custom, to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul. He said: "If anyone does not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, let them die, from the least to the greatest, from man to woman." And they swore to the Lord with a loud voice, with shouting, with the blast of trumpets, and the sound of horns—all who were in Judah with an oath. For they had sworn with all their heart and sought Him with all their will, and they found Him. And the Lord provided them rest on every side. He even removed Maachah, King Asa’s mother, from her royal authority <note original="exaugustio">from her high dignity or queenly status</note> because she had made an abominable idol of Priapus <note>Latin: *simulacrum priapi*. In a Christian context, this refers to a phallic or lewd fertility idol.</note> in a grove; this he crushed entirely, breaking it into pieces and burning it at the brook Kidron. Although the high places remained in Israel, nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. He brought the things his father had vowed and those he himself had vowed into the house of the Lord: silver, gold, and various vessels of furniture. There was war between Asa and Baasha, the king of Israel, until the thirty-sixth year of his reign.

<margin>2 Chronicles 16</margin>
In the thirty-sixth year of his reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built a wall around Ramah, so that no one could go out or come into the kingdom of Asa. Asa then brought out silver and gold from the treasures of the house of the Lord and the king's treasures, and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying: "There is a league between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Therefore I have sent you silver and gold so that you may come and break the league you have with Baasha king of Israel, and make him withdraw from me." Having agreed to this, Ben-hadad sent the captains of his armies to the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the walled cities of Naphtali. When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and abandoned his work. Then King Asa took all Judah and they carried away the stones and timber from Ramah which Baasha had prepared for building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah. At that time, Hanani the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said to him: "Because you have placed your trust in the king of Syria and not in the Lord your God, therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped from your hand. Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans much more numerous, with chariots and horsemen and an exceeding multitude? Yet when you believed in the Lord, He delivered them into your hand. For the eyes of the Lord behold the whole earth and provide strength to those who believe in Him with a perfect heart. You have acted foolishly, and therefore from this time wars shall rise against you." Asa was angry with the seer and ordered him to be put in the stocks <note>Latin: *neruum*. A physical restraint or prison cell for punishment.</note>, for he was greatly indignant with the Lord over this. And at that time, he killed many of the people. Now the acts of Asa, first and last, are written in the books of the kings of Judah and Israel. Asa became sick in the thirty-ninth year of his reign with a most violent pain in his feet, yet even in his infirmity he did not seek the Lord, but rather trusted in the skill of physicians. He slept with his fathers and died in the forty-first year of his reign. They buried him in his own tomb which he had dug for himself in the city of David; they laid him upon his bed filled with spices and ointments prepared by the perfumer’s art, and they burned an exceedingly great quantity over him.

<margin>2 Chronicles 17</margin>
Now Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead and grew strong against Israel. He stationed a number of soldiers in all the fortified cities of Judah and placed garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim which his father Asa had captured. And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David and did not hope in the Baals, but in the God of his father, and walked in His commandments and not according to the sins of Israel. The Lord confirmed the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat; he attained infinite riches and great glory. When his heart took courage in the ways of the Lord, he also took away the high houses and the groves from Judah. In the third year of his reign, he sent his princes—Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah. And with them he sent the Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah; and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram. They taught the people in Judah, having the book of the law of the Lord, and they went about 

<column-break/>

all the cities of Judah and instructed the people. Therefore the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, and they did not dare to make war against Jehoshaphat. Even the Philistines brought gifts to Jehoshaphat and a tribute of silver. The Arabs also brought cattle: seven thousand seven hundred rams and as many he-goats.

### You see that the judgment of the Lord is just regarding the sons of Ahab...

Jehoshaphat grew and was magnified to a high degree; he built houses in the likeness of towers in Judah and fortified cities, and he prepared many works in the cities of Judah. There were also warriors and strong men in Jerusalem, whose number according to their houses and families is this: in Judah, the prince of the army was Adnah, and with him three hundred thousand warriors. After him was Jehohanan the prince, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand. After him also was Amasiah the son of Zichri, consecrated to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand strong men. Following him was Eliada, a strong man from Benjamin, and with him two hundred thousand who held the bow and shield. After him also was Jehozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand ready soldiers. All these were at the hand of the king, besides others whom he had placed in fortified cities throughout all Judah. Jehoshaphat was very rich and glorious, and he became related by marriage to Ahab. After some years, he went down to him in Samaria; at his arrival, Ahab slaughtered many rams and oxen for him and for the people who had come with him. He persuaded him to go up against Ramoth-gilead. And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah:

### Come with me to Ramoth-gilead.

<margin>2 Chronicles 18</margin>
"Come with me to Ramoth-gilead." He replied: "As I am, so are you; as my people are, so are yours. We will be with you in the war." And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: "I pray you, consult the word of the Lord for the present." So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them: "Should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should we refrain?" They said: "Go up, and God will deliver it into the king's hand." But Jehoshaphat said: "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, so that we might also inquire of him?" The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "There is one man from whom we might seek the Lord’s will, but I hate him, because he never prophesies good for me, but always evil. This is Micaiah the son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said: "Let not the king speak in this manner." So the king of Israel called one of the eunuchs and said to him: "Bring Micaiah the son of Imla quickly." Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were both sitting on their thrones, clothed in royal attire. They sat in an open space near the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said: "Thus says the Lord: With these you shall toss Syria until you consume it." All the prophets likewise prophesied, saying: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and you shall prosper, and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hand." The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah said to him: "The words of all the prophets with one voice announce good things to the king; I pray you, let your word be like one of theirs, and speak what is prosperous." Micaiah answered him: "As the Lord lives, whatever my God says, that I will speak."

### Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should we refrain?

So Micaiah came to the king. The king said to him: "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead to fight, or should we refrain?" He replied: "Go up, for all things shall be prosperous, and the enemies shall be delivered into your hands." The king said: "Again and again I adjure you that you speak to me nothing but what is true in the name of the Lord." Then he said: "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. And the Lord said: These have no master. Let each one return to his house in peace." And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy any good to me, but only what is evil?" But Micaiah said: "Therefore hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing by Him on the right and on the left. And the Lord said: Who will deceive Ahab king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And as one said this way and another that way, a spirit came forward and stood before the Lord and said: I will deceive him. The Lord said to him: By what means will you deceive him? He replied: I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said: You shall deceive him and you shall prevail. Go out and do so. Now, therefore, behold, the Lord has put a spirit of lying in the mouth of all your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil concerning you." Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said: "By which way did the Spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?" Micaiah said: "You yourself shall see on that day when you enter into a chamber within a chamber to hide yourself." Then the king of Israel commanded, saying: "Take Micaiah and lead him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the son of Amelech, and say: Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and give him a little bread and a little water until I return in peace." Micaiah said: "If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me." And he said: "Hear, all you people!" So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead. The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "I will change my clothes and so I will go to battle, but you put on your own garments." The king of Israel having changed his attire, he went into the battle. But the king of Syria had commanded the captains of his horsemen, saying: "Fight not against the least or the greatest, but against the king of Israel alone." Therefore, when the captains of the horsemen saw Jehoshaphat, they said: "It is the king of Israel," and they surrounded him as they fought. But he cried out to the Lord, and He helped him and turned them away from him. For when the captains of the horsemen saw that it was not the king of Israel, they left him. Now it happened that a certain man of the people shot an arrow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the armor. He said to his charioteer: "Turn your hand and carry me out of the battle line, for I am wounded." The battle ended on that day. The king of Israel stood in his chariot against the Syrians until evening and died at sunset. Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in peace in Jerusalem. Jehu the son of Hanani the seer met him and said to him: "You give help to the ungodly and join in friendship with those who hate the Lord; therefore you deserved the wrath of the Lord. But good works are found in you, because you have taken away the groves from the land of Judah and have prepared your heart to seek the Lord, the God of your fathers." Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again to the people from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim and recalled them to the Lord, the God of their fathers. He also appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city. And charging the judges, he said: "See what you do. For you do not exercise the judgment of man, but of the Lord. And whatever you judge shall redound upon you. Let the fear of the Lord be with you, and do everything with diligence. For there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor desire for gifts." In Jerusalem also, Jehoshaphat appointed Levites and priests and heads of families from Israel to judge the judgment and cause of the Lord for its inhabitants. He commanded them, saying: "Thus shall you act in the fear of the Lord, faithfully and with a perfect heart. Every cause that comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities—between kinsman and kinsman, wherever there is a question concerning the law, the commandment, ceremonies, or justifications—show them, so that they do not sin against the Lord and so that wrath does not come upon you and upon your brothers. By doing this, you shall not sin. Amariah the priest and high priest shall preside over those things which pertain to the Lord. And Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, who is the ruler in the house of Judah, shall preside over those works which pertain to the king; and you have the Levites as masters before you. Take courage and act diligently, and the Lord will be with you in good things."

<margin>2 Chronicles 20</margin>
After this, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Edomites, gathered against Jehoshaphat to fight against him. Messengers came and told Jehoshaphat, saying: "A great multitude is coming against you from those places which are across the sea, from Syria; and behold, they stand in Hazazon-tamar..."

And He sent to the prophet so that he might return: then he who would lead them to the truth. And truly, although the Syrians had come with a small number, the Lord delivered an infinite multitude into their hands because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers. They also executed ignominious judgments upon Joash, and they went away, leaving him in great illness.

Amaziah son of Joash reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. And he did what was good before the Lord, yet not like David his father. According to all things that Joash his father had done, he did: except that he did not take away the high places. For the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. And when his kingdom was strengthened, he struck down his servants who had killed the king his father. But the sons of those who had killed him, he did not kill, according to what is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded, saying: "Fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor children for the fathers: but everyone shall die in his own sin." Amaziah also gathered Judah ...

<margin>2 Kings 14</margin>
In the eighth year Amaziah reigned. And in all these things that the Lord did, the Lord did not forsake him. However, he would not listen to the voice of the prophet, but gathered a large army against him. And he came into Judah and Jerusalem and killed ten thousand of them, and the other ten thousand he led bound to Jerusalem and cast them down from a precipice. Amaziah, king of Judah, also began again to worship the gods of the Edomites. When he had returned from the slaughter of the Edomites and offered sacrifices to them, the Lord was angry against him, and sent to him a prophet who would rebuke him. To whom, when the king spoke, the king said: "Are you a counselor of the king? Be quiet, lest you be killed." And the prophet, departing, said: "I know that the Lord has intended to kill you, because you have not listened to my counsel." Then Amaziah king of Judah, having taken very bad counsel, sent to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying: "Come, let us look each other in the face." To whom the king of Israel sent, saying: "The thistle that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying: 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And behold, the beasts that were in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle. Because you have conquered, your heart is lifted up in pride. Stay in your house. Why do you invite trouble for yourself, so that you fall, and Judah with you?" Amaziah would not listen, because it was the will of the Lord that they be delivered into the hands of the enemy because of the gods of the Edomites whom he had worshipped. And he and Jehoash ascended together: and they fought at Beth-shemesh of Judah. And Judah fled before Israel: and everyone to his own tents. Moreover, the king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh: and he brought him to Jerusalem and destroyed the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. And all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord and in the treasures of the king, as well as the children of the hostages, he took away to Samaria. And Amaziah king of Judah lived fifteen years after Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, died. But the rest of the words of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?

<margin>2 Kings 15</margin>
And Azariah son of Amaziah reigned over Judah twenty-eight years <note>Biblical texts usually record 52 years; 28 may be a manuscript variation or refer to a co-regency.</note>. And he did what was right before the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father had done. However, he did not take away the high places: for the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. And the Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death: and he lived in a free house <term>domo libera</term> <note>This refers to a house of isolation or separate living, mandatory for lepers under Jewish law.</note> apart. And Jotham the son of the king governed the house and judged the people of the land. But the rest of the words of Azariah and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? And Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his elders in the city of David. And Jotham his son reigned in his place.

<margin>2 Chronicles 25</margin>
But after Amaziah turned away from the Lord, they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem. And he fled to Lachish. And they sent after him to Lachish and killed him there. And they brought him back on horses: and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old: and they made him king in place of his father Amaziah. He built Elath: and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.

<margin>2 Kings 13</margin>
In all these days in which Amaziah reigned in Judah: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, reigned in Israel twenty-four years. And he did what was evil before the Lord: he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin. But he walked in them. But the rest of the words of Jehoash and all that he did: and his strength, how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah: are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel? And Jehoash slept with his fathers: and Jeroboam reigned upon his throne.

<margin>2 Kings 14</margin>
In all these parts: the children of Israel who were in Samaria made Jeroboam, the son of Jehoash king of Israel, king over them: and he reigned forty-one years. And he did what was evil before the Lord: he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin. He restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the wilderness: according to the word of the Lord God of Israel which He spoke through His servant Jonah, son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath which is in Hepher.

<margin>2 Chronicles 26</margin>
And Azariah son of Amaziah did what was good before the Lord. He was twenty-five years old when he had begun to reign: and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem. And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord: according to all that Amaziah his father had done. However, he did not take away the high places: the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. The Lord also struck the king: and he was a leper until the day of his death. And he lived in a free house apart. And Jotham the son of the king governed the house and judged the people of the land.

<margin>2 Chronicles 26</margin>
And when the kingdom of Azariah was strengthened, his heart was lifted up to his own destruction: and he neglected the Lord his God. And having entered the Temple of the Lord, he wanted to burn incense upon the altar of incense. And when the priests of the Lord, Azariah and with him eighty priests, most valiant men, resisted him: he would not listen to them. But the anger of the Lord was against him, and leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord upon the altar of incense. And when the priests looked at him, they saw the leprosy on his forehead. And they quickly expelled him: but he himself, being struck, hurried to go out. Therefore, King Azariah was a leper until the day of his death: and he lived in a free house apart. And Jotham the son of the king governed the house and judged the people of the land.

<margin>2 Kings 15</margin>
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam king of Israel: Zechariah his son reigned over Israel in Samaria six months. And he did what was evil before the Lord, just as his fathers had done. He did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin. And Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him openly: and he killed him and reigned in his place. But the rest of the words of Zechariah, behold they are written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel.

<margin>2 Kings 15</margin>

And Menahem son of Gadi ascended from Tirzah and came to Samaria. And he struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him and reigned in his place. But the rest of the words of Shallum and his conspiracy by which he laid snares: behold they are written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel.

And likewise: for sustenance and mercy: it is written here in the tablets: or indeed: they brought glory into the treasury. For the stolen goods and the sons: and all the Capuans <note>original: "capuanū"; this may be a scribal error or a specific regional reference not found in the standard biblical text</note> to stand near Bochac.
