And when: for sustenance and mercy: it is written here in the tablets: or indeed: they brought glory into the treasury. For the stolen goods and the sons: and all the Capuans to stand near Bochac. Now it pleases: truly you seek the adulterers: but the Lord to the just Lord: so that he might lead from here by faith and counsel and command: to the second procurement: which is commanded. Then arose the sons of the Mahath of the family of Amasai: and Joel the son of Azariah of the family of the Kohathites: and of the family of Merari: Kish the son of Abdi, and Azarias the son of Jehalelel: and of the family of Gershon, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah. And of the sons of Elisaphat: Shimri and Jeiel: and of the sons of Asaph: Zechariah and Mattaniah: and of the sons of Heman: Jehiel and Shimei. And of the sons of Jeduthun: Shemaiah and Uzziel.

They gathered their brothers: and they were sanctified: and they entered according to the king’s command and the Lord’s authority: to cleanse the house of the Lord: which they found to be filled with uncleanness: otherwise, they cast out every impurity: which they found in the vestibule of the Lord. The Levites took these things: and carried them out to the Kidron Valley <note>The Kidron Valley was a common place for disposing of idols and ritual impurities during religious reforms.</note>. They began to cleanse on the first day of the first month. And on the eighth day of the same month: they entered the porch of the temple of the Lord. And they purified the temple in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the same month: they finished what they had begun. Therefore, they went in to King Hezekiah and said to him: We have sanctified the entire house of the Lord: and the altar of burnt offerings: and its vessels: and also the table of showbread with all its vessels. And all the furniture of the temple: which King Ahaz had polluted during his reign after he had transgressed: behold, all things are set out before the altar of the Lord. And King Hezekiah, rising at dawn: gathered all the leaders of the city: and went up into the house of the Lord. And they offered together seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven he-goats for a sin offering: for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah: and he told the sons of Aaron: to offer them upon the altar of the Lord. So they killed the bulls: and the priests took the blood and poured it upon the altar: they also killed the rams: and poured their blood; they killed the lambs and poured the blood upon the altar. And they brought the he-goats for the sin offering before the king: and the whole multitude: and they laid their hands upon them: and the priests sacrificed them: and sprinkled their blood before the altar: for the atonement of all Israel. For the king had commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.

And when: the praise of the Lord was in the house of the Lord with cymbals and psalteries and harps according to the arrangement of David the king and Gad the king’s seer: and Nathan the prophet. For it was the Lord’s command: by the hand of his prophets: and the Levites stood: playing the instruments of David, and the priests with trumpets: and with voices in harmony: and they made the burnt offering upon the altar. And when the burnt offering was being offered, they began to sing praises to the Lord: and to sound the trumpets: and to play various instruments: which David the king of Israel had prepared. While the whole crowd worshipped: the singers: and those who held the trumpets: performed their office, until the burnt offering was completed. And when they had finished the offering: the king and all who were with him bowed down and worshipped. Hezekiah and the princes also commanded the Levites: to praise the Lord with the words of David: and of Asaph the seer. They praised Him with great joy: and with bowed knees they worshipped. And Hezekiah added this: You have filled your hands for the Lord <term>filled your hands: a Hebrew idiom meaning to be consecrated or ordained for service</term>. Come near and offer victims and praises in the house of the Lord. Therefore, the whole multitude offered sacrifices and praises: and burnt offerings: with a devoted mind. Furthermore, the number of burnt offerings: which the multitude offered: was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs. They sanctified these to the Lord in that month. But the Lord, the Lord God. They also sanctified the vessels near... then those who wished to offer the Lord's burnt offerings suffered. Then the Levites and the priests were gathered... for they had purified and sanctified themselves in great number: for the sanctified ones had indeed become many: according to the Lord. There were many burnt offerings, with the fat of the peace offerings: and the drink offerings of the burnt offerings. And the service of the house of the Lord was completed.

So Hezekiah spoke: and all the people, because the ministry of the Lord was fulfilled. For it had pleased them that this should be done suddenly. And Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah: and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh: that they should come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem: to keep the Passover <term>Passover: referred to in the Latin text as 'Phase', from the Hebrew 'Pesach'</term> to the Lord God of Israel. For the king, the princes, and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had taken counsel: to decree that they should keep the Passover in the second month. For they could not keep it at its proper time: because enough priests had not been sanctified: and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem. And the word pleased the king and the whole multitude. And they decreed that messengers should be sent throughout all Israel: from Beersheba to Dan: that they should come and keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem. For they had not kept it for a long time as it was prescribed in the law. Then the couriers went with the letters from the king: and the princes by the king's will throughout all Israel and Judah: according to what the leading preacher had commanded. Sons of Israel, return to the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel: and He will return to the remnant: who escaped the hand of the king of the Assyrians. Do not be like your fathers and brothers who departed from the Lord God of their fathers, and He delivered them to destruction: as you see. Do not harden your necks: like your fathers. Yield your hands to the Lord: and come to His sanctuary: which He has sanctified forever: and serve the Lord your God: that He may turn the wrath of His fury from you. For if you return to the Lord: your brothers and children will find mercy before those who took them captive, and they will return to this land. For the Lord your God is pious and merciful: so that He will not turn His face from you: if you return to Him. So the couriers went from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun: they mocked them and laughed them to scorn. Nevertheless, some men of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Zebulun: agreed to the counsel and came to Jerusalem.

In Judah also the hand of the Lord was present: to give them one heart: and to do the one word of the Lord: and according to the command of the king and the princes. And a great many people gathered in Jerusalem: to keep the solemnity of Unleavened Bread <note>original: "azimorū", refers to the seven-day feast following the Passover</note> in the second month. And rising up, they destroyed the altars that were in Jerusalem: and they overturned the tables where they burned incense to idols: and threw them into the Kidron Valley. And they sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. But the priests and the Levites, having finally been sanctified: offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord. And they stood in their order: according to the institution and the law of Moses, the man of God: but the priests received the blood from the hands of the Levites: because many were not sanctified in mind. And therefore, the Levites sacrificed the Passover for those who had not come to be sanctified to the Lord. For a great part of the people from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun: who were not sanctified: ate the Passover, but not according to what was written. And Hezekiah prayed for them, saying: The good Lord will be merciful to everyone who prepares his heart to seek the Lord God of his fathers: even if he is not purified according to the sanctuary. And the Lord heard him: and was appeased toward the people. And the children of Israel who were found in Jerusalem: kept the solemnity of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy: the Levites and priests praising the Lord every day with instruments that suited their office. And Hezekiah spoke to the hearts of all the Levites: who had good understanding concerning the Lord. And they ate for the seven days of the solemnity: sacrificing victims of peace offerings and praising the Lord God of their fathers.

He also commanded the whole multitude: that they should celebrate another seven days: which they did with great joy. For Hezekiah, king of Judah, had given the multitude a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep. And the princes gave the people a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. And a very great number of priests were sanctified. And the whole crowd of Judah was filled with joy: both priests and Levites: as well as all the assembly that had come from Israel. The proselytes also: who had come from the land of Israel: and those dwelling in Judah: were joyful. And there was great joy in Jerusalem such as had not been since the time of Solomon. Then the priests and Levites arose and blessed the people: and their voice was heard: and their prayer reached the holy habitation of heaven. And when these things were properly celebrated: all Israel went out: who were found in the cities of Judah: and they broke

<column-break/>

the idols: and cut down the sacred groves: they demolished the high places and the altars: and destroyed them not only in Judah and Benjamin, but also in Ephraim and Manasseh: until they were utterly overturned. And all the children of Israel returned to their own possessions and cities. Then Hezekiah: appointed the divisions of the priests and Levites by their turns: each one in his own office: for burnt offerings and peace offerings: that they might minister and give thanks and sing in the gates of the Lord's camp. The king's portion was: to offer burnt offerings from his own substance in the morning and evening: also on the Sabbaths: on the new moons: and on the solemnities: as it is written in the law of the Lord.

Afterward, he commanded the inhabitants of Jerusalem: to give portions to the priests and Levites: so that they might devote themselves to the law of the Lord. When this was made public: the multitude offered a great abundance of firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, and honey: and they brought tithes of all things that the earth produces. But also the children of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah: offered tithes of oxen and sheep, and tithes of holy things which they had vowed to the Lord their God: and bringing them all together: they made many heaps. In the third month they began to lay the foundations of the heaps: and in the seventh month they finished them. And when Hezekiah and the princes entered: and saw the heaps: they blessed the Lord and the people of Israel. And Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites: why the heaps lay there. And Azariah the priest of the line of Zadok answered him, saying: Since they began to offer the firstfruits to the house of the Lord: we have eaten and are satisfied: and many things remain: because the Lord has blessed His people. What you see is the remainder. Hezekiah commanded that they should prepare storehouses in the house of the Lord. When they had done so: they brought in both the firstfruits and the tithes and whatever they had vowed faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was the overseer: and Shimei his brother was second. After him were Jehiel, Azaziah, Mahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah: under the command of Conaniah and Shimei his brother: by the order of King Hezekiah and Azariah the high priest of the house of the Lord: to whom all things belonged. Kore, the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter of the east gate, was over those things that were offered voluntarily to the Lord: the firstfruits and the most holy things. Under his care were Eden, Benjamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah: in the cities of the priests: to distribute faithfully to their brothers by their divisions: to the great as well as the small: besides their genealogy: to all males from three years old and upward: who entered the temple of the Lord. And whatever was needed for each day's service: in the ministry and worship according to their divisions. To the priests by their families: and to the Levites from the twentieth year and upward by their divisions and their ranks: and to the whole multitude of their little ones, wives, and children: for they were faithfully sanctified. Also for the sons of Aaron in the fields and suburbs of the cities, individual men were appointed: to distribute portions to every male among the priests and Levites. Thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah: and he worked what was good, right, and true before the Lord his God in the entire ministry of the worship of the house of the Lord: according to the law and ceremonies: wishing to seek the Lord his God with all his heart: and he prospered.

In the fourteenth year: in faithfulness and truth: Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came: and entering Judah: he besieged the fortified cities: wishing to take them. When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and intended to attack Jerusalem: he took counsel with the princes and his men of valor: to stop up the heads of the springs that were outside the city: and everyone agreed to this plan. They gathered a very great multitude: and stopped up all the springs and the brook: which flowed through the middle of the land, saying: Lest the kings of the Assyrians come and find an abundance of water. Hezekiah also built up the wall where it had been broken down: and raised towers upon it: and built another wall outside. And he repaired Millo in the city of David: and made weapons of every kind and shields. He appointed military captains over the army: and called them all together in the street of the city gate: and spoke to their hearts, saying: Act manfully and be strengthened. Do not fear or be afraid of the king of the Assyrians and the entire multitude that is with him. For there are many more with us than with him. With him is an arm of flesh: but with us is the Lord our God: who fights for us as our helper. And the people were comforted by these words of Hezekiah, king of Judah. After these things were done: Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, sent his servants to Jerusalem (for he himself was besieging Lachish with all his army) to Hezekiah, king of Judah, and to all the people in Jerusalem: and Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, said: In what do you trust, that you stay besieged in Jerusalem? Does Hezekiah not deceive you, to deliver you to death by famine and thirst, claiming: the Lord our God will free us from the hand of the king of the Assyrians? Is this not the same Hezekiah who destroyed His high places and altars: and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying: you shall worship before one altar and burn incense upon it? Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Have the gods of the nations and of all the lands been able to deliver their regions from my hand? Who among all the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed: was able to rescue his people from my hand: that your God should be able to deliver you from my hand? Therefore, let not Hezekiah deceive you: nor persuade you in this way: nor believe him. For if no god of any nation or kingdom could deliver his people from my hand and the hand of my fathers: then your God will not be able to rescue you from my hand.

And when: he feared... But his servants spoke many other things against the Lord God and against Hezekiah. He also wrote letters full of blasphemy against the Lord God of Israel: and they spoke against Him: just as the gods of the other nations could not deliver their people from my hand: so the God of Hezekiah cannot rescue His people from my hand. Furthermore, they cried out with a loud voice in the Jewish language against the people who sat on the walls of Jerusalem to terrify them: so they might take the city. They spoke against the God of Jerusalem: as against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of men's hands. Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed against this blasphemy: and cried out to heaven. And the Lord sent an angel who struck down every robust man, and the warriors, and the leaders of the army of the king of the Assyrians. And he returned with shame to his own land. And when he entered the temple of his god: his sons who had come forth from his own body: slew him there with the sword. Thus the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, and from the hand of all others: and granted them peace on every side. For many brought victims and sacrifices to the Lord in Jerusalem and gifts to Hezekiah, king of Judah: who was exalted after this before all nations. In those days Hezekiah was sick even unto death: and he prayed to the Lord: who heard him and gave him a sign. But he did not return thanks according to the benefit he received: for his heart was exalted. And wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem. But afterward, he humbled himself because his heart had been exalted: both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and therefore the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah. Hezekiah had very great riches and glory: and he gathered for himself treasures of silver, gold, precious stones, spices, and armor of every kind: and vessels of great price. Also storehouses for grain, wine, and oil: and stalls for all kinds of beasts, and folds for the flocks. He built cities for himself and had innumerable flocks of sheep and herds of oxen: for the Lord had given him very much substance. This is the same Hezekiah who stopped the upper spring of the waters of Gihon: and diverted them down to the west side of the city of David. In all his works, he acted prosperously.

<summary>This page recounts King Hezekiah's purification of the Temple, the restoration of the Passover, and the miraculous defeat of Sennacherib's Assyrian army through prayer and divine intervention. It highlights the king's religious reforms, his strengthening of Jerusalem's defenses, and his eventual prosperity despite a period of prideful illness.</summary>

**M**anasseh was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah. And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the idols of the nations which the Lord destroyed before the face of the children of Israel. And he turned back and rebuilt the high places <note>altars on hills or platforms for pagan worship</note> which Hezekiah his father had destroyed. And he raised up altars to Baal and made sacred groves as Ahab the king of Israel had done. And he adored all the host of heaven and worshipped them. And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said: "In Jerusalem I will put my name." And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the temple of the Lord. And he made his son pass through fire <note>a reference to human sacrifice</note>; and he practiced soothsaying and observed omens. And he established mediums and diviners: and he multiplied his efforts to do evil before the Lord and to provoke him. And he set an idol of the grove which he had made in the temple of the Lord, concerning which the Lord had spoken to David and to Solomon his son: "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever. And I will no longer make the foot of Israel move from the land which I gave to their fathers: if only they will keep and do all that I have commanded them, and the whole law which my servant Moses commanded them." But they did not listen: but were seduced by Manasseh to do evil beyond the nations which the Lord destroyed before the face of the children of Israel. And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying: "Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these most wicked abominations, beyond all that the Amorites did before him, and has made Judah to sin with his filthiness: Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I will bring evils upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that whoever hears it, both his ears shall tingle. And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the weight of the house of Ahab. And I will wipe away Jerusalem as tablets are usually wiped away: and wiping it, I will turn it and pass the stylus over its face frequently <note>a metaphor for complete destruction and "erasing" the city's inhabitants</note>. Indeed, I will cast off the remnant of my inheritance, and I will deliver them into the hands of their enemies. And they shall be for a desolation and for a prey to all their adversaries: because they have done evil before me and have continued provoking me, from the day their fathers came out of Egypt even to this day." Moreover, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he had filled Jerusalem up to the mouth: besides his sins by which he made Judah to sin, to do evil before the Lord.

**J**osiah was eight years old when he began to reign: and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath. And he did what was pleasing before the Lord, and walked in all the ways of David his father: he turned not aside to the right hand or to the left. Now in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, the scribe of the temple of the Lord, saying to him: "Go to Hilkiah the high priest, that the money may be melted down which has been brought into the temple of the Lord, which the doorkeepers of the people have gathered from the common folk. And let it be given to the craftsmen by the overseers of the house of the Lord: and let them distribute it to those who work in the temple of the Lord, to restore the repairs <term>sarta tecta</term> <note>a legal term for keeping buildings in good repair</note> of the temple. Namely, to the carpenters and the masons, and to those who fix what is broken. And so that timber and stones from the quarries may be bought to restore the temple of the Lord. Nevertheless, let the silver they receive not be accounted to them, but let them have it in their power and in faith." And Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe: "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the volume to Shaphan, who also read it. Shaphan the scribe also came to the king and reported to him what he had commanded. And he said: "Your servants have melted down the money found in the house of the Lord, and have given it to be put before the craftsmen by the overseers of the works of the temple of the Lord." Shaphan the scribe also told the king, saying: "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." And when Shaphan had read it before the king, and the king had heard the words of the book of the law of the Lord, he rent his garments. And he commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying: "Go and consult the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this volume which has been found. For the wrath of the Lord is kindled against us, because our fathers did not hear the words of this book, to do all that is written for us."

**Z**edekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign: and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done. For the Lord was angry against Jerusalem and against Judah, until he cast them away from his face. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. Now it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, to Jerusalem, and they besieged it. And they built fortifications around it. And the city was closed and besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah. But on the ninth day of the month, famine prevailed in the city, nor was there bread for the people of the land. And the city was broken into, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate which is between the double wall to the king's garden. Now the Chaldeans <note>the Babylonians</note> were besieging the city round about. And so Zedekiah fled by the way that leads to the plains of the wilderness. And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and caught him in the plains of Jericho. And all the warriors who were with him were dispersed and left him. Therefore, having apprehended the king, they led him to the king of Babylon in Riblah, who spoke judgment with him. He also killed the sons of Zedekiah before him, and gouged out his eyes, and bound him with shackles, and led him to Babylon. But in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—that is the nineteenth year of the king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the army and servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. And he set fire to the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and the houses of Jerusalem, and every large house he burned with fire. And the whole army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the soldiers destroyed the walls of Jerusalem round about. But the rest of the part of the people who had remained in the city, and the fugitives who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the captain of the army carried away. But of the poor of the land, he left vinedressers and farmers.

## HERE BEGINS THE PREFACE OF JEROME THE PRIEST TO THE BOOK OF EZRA

Whether it is more difficult to do what you ask or to refuse it, is not easy for me to judge. For neither are you demanding—where there is true charity—nor shall I be found proud toward you if I refused the command, lest perhaps you find that your demand must be vindicated. To assist me in this, Ezra has led me, who strikes with the rebuke of friends and brothers, and had poured out a pure voice, so that those resisting might be confounded; let him speak publicly what all read, to cry out in truth, and to amplify, and to teach. Every soul of the books has been received by us with labor: by some because they wish it and write, as they say, on the spur of the moment; others bring back what seemed good to them. 

If anything in this place seemed to him to be in the habit and will of the righteous, that one thing is done in some, and another in others, just as these or those have found it; to use it in vain with the perverse, he says: "what I see is that nothing else is to be done except to seek hatred, and to depart mercifully." Therefore I beseech you, my lord, and by the request of those most dear: that if any read the book, and see the book, they should not confidently deny that this was not in them, even though they see it. And so over him who wishes to sing, let his voice be heard. And if perhaps he should see where they wished. But if anyone says who wrote this: if anyone even wished this one to be seen: it will not be in those in which it is said that it was done. 

What is contained in this volume is open and distinct through your turns. And nothing in one will be able to have corrected the book. In those two books, indeed, you have inserted your diligence. For let not one book published by us move you, as if he had not seen this; and then let the fourth part of the book delight with words: because even among the Hebrews, the discourses of Ezra and Nehemiah are squeezed into one volume, and what they do not have, they may find among these; they are held in the words of the Scriptures. If anything in them seems to you to be seen, and you wish it to be done: read from these your own copies which I have translated from the authority of the Latin canon. 

And I warn you that this should be done: so that it may not be found placed for you in your copy from the Old Testament, which are held interchangeably among these; or as that which they wished for you, and if from the sons of neighbors they came. And you will see more by your own will: nourished: some of you persuaded by others: and what from these copies, which were recently published by us, leave the slanderers with a sharper confession. But let us not, when we have seen another, be vacant or let it be done for others who have gone out from the duty. And therefore let it hold something for you, nor let it have otherwise what has been turned by me. By whose inspiration do they rejoice? Let them question the Hebrews: and if the authority is granted to the authors, then let them know my faith either of arrogance or of folly. 

Through the mouths, it is one thing to have spoken thus, another to have wished to say thus, or to speak evil: so that unless they find favor, they persuade: and benevolence to those who can, well with labors; and I have written and do you shine, do they see and grow dull? It is your praise, in which it perishes by inheritance: as most of all: and then where concerning the equating of rarity: they read: and the skill of the lips as they said they had given to you. Although however of the Latins it may seem to be, that it is not granted to them from the canon, as some have found. For in vain rather did those men do it: and in the difficulties to be made, the copies could have all things, clear also what they had: they bring from the Hebrews what is restored: they will err more than they deny. For who would come to drink against his will? 

But also let the most skillful hear what was recently inscribed among the Greeks, or while he wrote perhaps they would leave; each one to himself: let them follow the error made. We, however, who confess this with the Hebrews, likewise have Jeremiah. And praise to you and of your vow: as is fitting. You, as it were, might be able to warn more. And if any think we have read: and they are interpreted in the languages. Therefore: although from a certain faith, and the life of your speech being directed: never had they gone into one for me, if I trust the service. They stammer those things through deceit. Wherefore also you who had not the volume, and someone comes among these to calumniate: I shall be provoked more by your charity, and by hatred: than by the detestation of them: and I shall detest with a sharper hatred.
<margin>JOSHUA</margin>

...from the mouth of Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of the Persians: and he proclaimed by voice in his entire kingdom, and also through writing, saying:
> Thus says Cyrus, king of the Persians. All the kingdoms of the earth the Lord God of heaven has given to me, and he himself has commanded me that I should build him a house in Jerusalem which is in Judea. He is the God who is in Jerusalem. And let all the rest in all places, wherever they dwell, help him—the men of his place—with silver, and gold, and goods, and cattle, besides that which they offer voluntarily for the temple of God, which is in Jerusalem.

And the leaders of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the priests, and the <term>Levites</term><note>Members of the tribe of Levi who assisted the priests in the Temple.</note>, everyone whose spirit God had stirred up, to go up to build the temple of the Lord which was in Jerusalem. King Cyrus also brought forth the vessels of the temple of the Lord which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and had placed in the temple of his god. Cyrus, king of the Persians, brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the son of <term>Gazabar</term><note>A title meaning "treasurer."</note>, and he counted them out to <term>Sheshbazzar</term><note>original: "saszabasar"; the prince or leader of the returning Jews.</note> the prince of Judah.

Now the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in their cities. Then the people gathered together as one man to Jerusalem. And Jesua the son of Jozadak arose, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, and they built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God. They set the altar of God upon its bases, even though the peoples of the lands around them terrified them. And they offered burnt offerings on it to the Lord, morning and evening. And they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, and the daily burnt offerings in order, according to the command for each day's work. And after this, the continual burnt offering, both on the new moons and on all the set feasts of the Lord that were consecrated, and for everyone who willingly offered a gift to God. From the first day of the seventh month, they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord. 

However, the foundation of the temple of the Lord was not yet laid. They gave money to the masons and stonecutters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and Tyrians, to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the grant that Cyrus, king of the Persians, had given them.

In the second year of their coming to the temple of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jesua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work. And they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the Lord. And Jesua stood with his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Judah, as one man, to oversee those who did the work in the temple of God; the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brothers the Levites.

When the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the Lord, the priests stood in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise God according to the direction of David, king of Israel. And they sang together in hymns and confession to the Lord: "Because he is good, for his mercy endures forever over Israel." And all the people shouted with a great shout in praising the Lord, because the foundation of the temple of the Lord was laid. But many of the priests and Levites and leaders of the fathers, the old men who had seen the first temple, and this temple before their eyes, wept with a loud voice. And many shouted for joy and lifted up their voices. Nor could anyone distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people. For the people shouted with a loud cry, and the sound was heard far off.

Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord God of Israel. And they approached Zerubbabel and the leaders of the fathers and said to them: "Let us build with you, for we seek your God just as you do. Behold, we have sacrificed victims since the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, who brought us here." But Zerubbabel and Jesua answered them...

Moreover, in the reign of Artaxerxes <note>original: "Artaxersis"; likely referring to Ahasuerus/Xerxes</note>, king of the Persians, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. The letter of accusation was written in Aramaic <note>original: "syriace"</note> and was read in the Aramaic tongue. Rehum <note>original: "Reumbeltheem"</note> the chancellor and Shimshai <note>original: "famfai"</note> the scribe wrote a single letter regarding those who were in Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes. Rehum and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their fellow-officials: the Dinaites <note>original: "aidani"</note>, the Apharsathchites <note>original: "pharsacei"</note>, the Tarpelites <note>original: "cherphalei"</note>, the Apharsites, the Archevites <note>original: "harurei"</note>, the Babylonians, the Susanchites <note>original: "sussani"</note>, the Dehavites <note>original: "chaiet"</note>, the Elamites, and the rest of the nations whom the great and glorious Osnappar <note>original: "asennaphar"</note> deported and settled in the cities of Samaria: and the rest who were in the regions across the river in peace. This is the copy of the letter which they sent to him: "To Artaxerxes the king, your servants who are across the river send greetings. Let it be known to the king that the Jews who went up from you have come to us in the city of Jerusalem, a rebellious and most wicked city which they are rebuilding; they are constructing its walls and have prepared the foundations.

# Now therefore, let it be known to the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls constructed, they will not pay tribute, nor tax, nor yearly rent, and this loss will reach even to the kings. And since we are mindful of the salt <note>original: "fati gō"; likely "salis" - a metaphor for being in the king's service</note> we have eaten in the palace, and because we deem it a crime to see the injury of the king, we have therefore sent and notified the king, so that a search may be made in the books of the histories of your fathers. You will find it written in the commentaries and will know that this city is rebellious and harmful to kings and provinces, and has incited wars within it from ancient days; for which reason the city itself was destroyed. We notify the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls restored, you will have no possession across the river." The king sent word back to Rehum and Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest who were in their counsel, the inhabitants of Samaria and others across the river, saying: "Greetings and peace. The accusation which you sent to us has been clearly read before me. I gave the command, and they have searched and found that this city from ancient days has rebelled against kings, and seditions and battles are stirred up within it. There were very strong kings in Jerusalem who ruled over all the regions across the river, and tribute, tax, and yearly rent were paid to them. Now therefore, give the order to prohibit those men, so that the city is not rebuilt unless perhaps a command is issued by me. See that you do not perform this negligently, lest the evil gradually increase against the kings." Then the copy of the letter of Artaxerxes was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their companions, and they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and stopped them with arm and strength. Then the work on the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was interrupted, and it remained so until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.

# After this, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel <note>original: "salathel"</note> and Jeshua the son of Jozadak <note>original: "iosedech"</note> arose toward the mountains that were in Judea and in Jerusalem in the name of the Lord of Israel. Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose and began to build the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, and all the prophets of the Lord were helping them. At that same time, Tatnai, who was the governor across the river, and Shethar-boznai <note>original: "starbusanai"</note>, and their companions came to them and said: "Who gave you the counsel to build this house and to restore these walls?" To which we answered <note>original: "respondimus"</note> who were the names of the men who were the authors of that building. But the eye of their Lord was upon the elders of the Jews, and they could not hinder them. It was decided that the matter should be referred to Darius, and then they would provide satisfaction against that accusation. Tatnai, the governor of the region across the river, and Shethar-boznai and his counselors, the Apharsachites who were across the river, sent a copy of the letter to King Darius. The message they sent him was written thus: "To King Darius, all peace. Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great Lord, which is being built with unpolished stone, and timber is being placed in the walls; that work is being carried out diligently and prospers in their hands. We questioned those elders and said thus to them: 'Who gave you the power to build this house and to restore the walls?' But we also asked their names so that we might report to you, and we have written the names of the men who are the leaders among them. They answered us with a speech of this sort, saying: 'We are the servants of the Lord of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was constructed many years ago, which a great king of Israel had built and erected.'

<margin>Here begins Ezra</margin>

# "But after our fathers provoked the Lord of heaven to anger, he delivered them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "nabugodonosor"</note>, the Chaldean king of Babylon, who destroyed this house and transported its people to Babylon. However, in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued an edict that the house of the Lord should be rebuilt. For even the gold and silver vessels of the temple of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple that was in Jerusalem and had carried into the temple of Babylon, King Cyrus brought out from the temple of Babylon and delivered them to one named Sheshbazzar <note>original: "sasabassaro"</note>, whom he had appointed as governor. And he told him: 'Take these, go, and place them in the temple which is in Jerusalem, and let the house of the Lord be in its former place.' Then that Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it is being built, and it is not yet completed. Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let it be searched in the king's library which is in Babylon, whether it was commanded by King Cyrus that the house of the Lord in Jerusalem be rebuilt, and let the king's will regarding this be sent back to us." Then King Darius commanded, and they searched in the library of books that were stored in Babylon. And in Ecbatana <note>original: "egbathanis"</note>, which is a fortress in the province of Media, a single scroll was found, and in it was written a memorandum: "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus decreed that the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem should be rebuilt in the place where they offer sacrifices, and that supporting foundations be laid. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits, with three rows of unpolished stones and one row of new timber. The expense shall be given from the king's house. Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the temple of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, shall be restored and returned to the temple of Jerusalem to their place, which were placed in the temple of the Lord."

# "Now therefore, Tatnai, governor of the region across the river, and Shethar-boznai, and your counselors the Apharsachites who are across the river: keep your distance from them and allow the temple of the Lord to be made by the governor of the Jews and by the elders of the Jews, so that they may build that temple in its place. Moreover, I have commanded what ought to be done by those elders of the Jews so that the house of the Lord may be built: namely, that from the king's revenues—that is, from the tribute across the river—the expenses shall be given to those men most diligently, so that the work is not hindered. If it is necessary, let calves, rams, and lambs for a burnt offering to the Lord of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the rite of the priests who are in Jerusalem, be given to them day by day, so that there is no complaint. And let them offer oblations to the Lord of heaven, and let them pray for the life of the king and his sons. For I have commanded that whoever—whatever man—shall change this order, let a beam be taken

<column-break/>

from his own house, and let it be set up, and let him be fastened upon it. Moreover, let his house be confiscated. And may the God who caused his name to dwell there destroy all kingdoms and people who shall stretch out their hand to resist and destroy that house which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have established the decree, which I wish to be fulfilled diligently."

# Afterward, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, there came up Ezra the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth, son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki, son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest from the beginning. This Ezra went up from Babylon; he was a scribe swift in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had given. And the king gave him everything he sought, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him. And there came with him some of the children of Israel, and of the children of the priests, and of the children of the Levites, and of the singers, and of the gatekeepers, and of the Nethinim, to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes. They arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month; that is the seventh year of the king. For on the first day of the first month he began to go up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month he arrived in Jerusalem, according to the good hand of his God upon him. For Ezra had prepared his heart to investigate the law of the Lord, and to do and to teach the precept and judgment in Israel.

# He also wrote here the letter which King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe learned in the words of the precepts of the Lord and his ceremonies in Israel: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, learned in the law of the Lord of heaven, greetings. It is decreed by me that whoever in my kingdom of the people of Israel and of its priests and of the Levites wishes to go to Jerusalem, may go with you. For you are sent by the face of the king and his seven counselors to visit Judea and Jerusalem according to the law of your God which is in your hand. And that you may carry the silver and gold which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose tabernacle is in Jerusalem. And all the silver and gold, whatever you shall find in the entire province of Babylon, and which the people wish to offer to the Lord their God in Jerusalem, accept freely. And with this money buy diligently calves, rams, lambs, and their sacrifices and drink offerings, and offer them upon the altar of the temple of our Lord God which is in Jerusalem. Moreover, if it seems good to you and your brothers to do anything with the rest of the silver and gold, do so according to the will of our Lord God. But the vessels which were given to you for the ministry of the house of your God, return in the sight of God in Jerusalem. And other things which you may need for the house of your God, whatever is necessary to be given, you shall give from the king's treasures. And I, Artaxerxes the king, have established and decreed to all the keepers of the treasury who are across the river: that whatever Ezra the priest, the teacher of the law of the Lord of heaven, shall ask of you, you shall give without delay, up to a hundred talents of silver, and up to a hundred cors of wheat, and up to a hundred baths of wine, and up to a hundred baths of oil, and salt indeed without measure. All that pertains to the worship of the God of heaven shall be contributed diligently in the house of the Lord of heaven, lest perhaps he be angry against the kingdom of the king and his sons. And we make known to you, regarding all the priests and Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and ministers of this house: that no one has the power to impose tax, or tribute, or yearly rent upon them. And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint judges and governors, that they may judge all the people who are across the river, namely those who know the law of your God; and teach those who are ignorant freely. And everyone who does not follow the law of your God and the law of the king, judgment shall be diligently executed upon him, whether unto death, or unto exile, or unto the confiscation of his property, or unto prison."

# But also those who were with Ezra, whom the Lord snatched from this trouble: they in turn blessed the Lord God of our fathers, who enlightened the Lord in Jerusalem with his mercy for the veneration of the sight of the king and his counselors and all the powerful princes of the king. I was strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God which was upon me, and I gathered the leaders of Israel to go up with me. These are the leaders of the families and their genealogy who went up with me from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes: Of the sons of Phinehas: Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar: Daniel. Of the sons of David: Hattush. Of the sons of Shecaniah <note>original: "fethanie"</note>, of the sons of Parosh: Zechariah, and with him were numbered 150 men. Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Eliehoenai <note>original: "elionai"</note> the son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men. Of the sons of Shecaniah: the son of Jahaziel, and with him 200 men. Of the sons of Adin: Ebed <note>original: "abiech"</note> the son of Jonathan, and with him 50 men. Of the sons of Elam: Jeshaiah <note>original: "itai"</note> the son of Athaliah, and with him 70 men. Of the sons of Shephatiah: Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him 80 men. Of the sons of Joab: Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men. Of the sons of Shelomith: the son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men. Of the sons of Bebai: Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him 28 men. Of the sons of Azgad: Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men. Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them 60 men. Of the sons of Bigvai: Uthai <note>original: "hai"</note> and Zaccur, and with him 70 men. I gathered them at the river that runs toward Ahava <note>original: "auua"</note>, and we stayed there for three days. And I searched among the people and the priests for the sons of Levi, and found none there. Therefore I sent Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah <note>original: "chanabam"</note>, Meshullam <note>original: "masoram"</note>, and Joiarib <note>original: "netollam"</note>, leaders; and Joiarib and Elnathan, wise men. And I sent them to Iddo <note>original: "dŕm"</note>, who is the chief at the place Casiphia <note>original: "masepha"</note>; I put words in their mouths that they should speak to Iddo and to his brothers the Nethinim in the place Casiphia, that they should bring to us ministers for the house of our Lord.

# And they brought to us, by the good hand of our Lord upon us, a most learned man of the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel: Sherebiah <note>original: "sarabia"</note>, and his sons and his brothers, 18; and Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah <note>original: "uiaiam"</note> of the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, 20. And of the Nethinim, whom the Lord and the princes had given for the ministry of the Levites: 220 Nethinim. All these were called by their names. And I proclaimed a fast there by the river Ahava, so that we might be afflicted before the Lord and seek from him a right way for us and for our children and for all our substance. For I was ashamed to ask from the king an escort of soldiers and horsemen.

...because they made us most just, for they said: "A great King from heaven." And they did everything according to the things that had been commanded them. And the favor of the Lord our God was upon them in these matters. Indeed, let this be prescribed to you concerning the princes, the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, the attendants, and the ministers in the house of God: that no one has the power to impose any exaction, tribute, or other tax upon them. You, Ezra, according to the wisdom God has given you, appoint judges and justices so that they may judge in all Syria and Phoenicia; you shall teach both those who know the law of your God and those who do not. And whoever transgresses the law of your God or the law of the king shall be diligently punished, whether by death, by torture, by a fine of money, or by exile. Blessed be the Lord alone, who put these things into the heart of the king to glorify his house which is in Jerusalem; and he has shown his mercy to me before the king and his friends and all his powerful officials. I was strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God assisting me, and I gathered men from Israel to go up with me. These are their lineages: the leaders according to their paternal houses who went down with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes. Of the sons of Phinehas: Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar: Amahel. Of the sons of David: Hattush. Of the sons of Parosh <note>original: "Phares"</note>: Zechariah, and with him were listed one hundred and fifty men. Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Eliehoenai <note>original: "eliaonias"</note> son of Zerahiah <note>original: "zecchrei"</note>, and with him two hundred men. Of the sons of Zattu: Jecheniah son of Jahaziel <note>original: "ezel"</note>, and with him three hundred men. Of the sons of Adin: Ebed <note>original: "obeth"</note> son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men. Of the sons of Elam: Jeshaiah <note>original: "iesias"</note> son of Athaliah <note>original: "gotholias"</note>, and with him seventy men. Of the sons of Shephatiah: Zebadiah <note>original: "zecharias"</note> son of Michael, and with him eighty men. Of the sons of Joab: Obadiah <note>original: "abdias"</note> son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and twelve men. Of the sons of Bani: Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty men. Of the sons of Bebai: Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men. Of the sons of Azgad: Johanan son of Hakkatan <note>original: "acatan"</note>, and with him one hundred and ten men. Of the last sons of Adonikam, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men. Of the sons of Bigvai <note>original: "bago"</note>: Uthai, and with him seventy men. And I gathered them at the river called Ahava <note>original: "thia"</note>. And we stayed there for three days; and I reviewed the people and the priests, and I found no sons of Levi there. I sent for Eliezer, Ariel <note>original: "iduhel"</note>, Shemaiah <note>original: "masmam"</note>, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam <note>original: "mosollamum"</note>, who were leaders, and for Jarib and Elnathan, who were wise men. And I told them to go to Iddo, who was in the place of the treasury <note>original: "gazophylacii"; referring to the temple storage</note>. I commanded them to tell Iddo and his brothers and those in the treasury to send us priests to minister in the house of the Lord our God. And they brought to us, according to the hand of our God upon us, men of understanding from the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel: Sherebiah <note>original: "seberebiam"</note> with his sons and eighteen brothers. And Hashabiah <note>original: "asebiam"</note>, and Annus, and his brother Jeshaiah <note>original: "osiam"</note> of the sons of Merari, and their sons, twenty men. And of the temple servants whom David and the princes had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty men; and the names of all were recorded in writing. And there I vowed a fast before the Lord our God, that we might seek from him a right way for ourselves, our children, and our livestock. For I was ashamed to ask the king for footmen and horsemen as an escort for safety against our adversaries. For we had told the king: "The power of the Lord our God will be with those who seek him with all their heart." And again we prayed to the Lord our God concerning these things, and he was favorable to us. And I set apart twelve of the chief priests: Sherebiah and Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers. And I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the sacred vessels which the king, his counselors, his princes, and all Israel had donated. I weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, one hundred silver vessels, one hundred talents of gold, twenty gold vessels, and twelve vessels of fine shining bronze <note>original: "aeneorum uasorum ex bono metallo"</note> as precious as gold. And I said to them: "You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold are a vow to the Lord, the God of your fathers. Watch and guard them until you deliver them before the chief priests, the Levites, and the leaders of the families of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers <note>term: "pastophoris" — side-rooms or cells in the temple complex</note> of the house of our God." So the priests and Levites received the silver, the gold, and the vessels that were for Jerusalem and brought them into the temple of the Lord. And we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, until we came to Jerusalem according to the mighty hand of the Lord our God over us; and he delivered us from the raid of all our enemies. And we came to Jerusalem, and when we had been there for three days, on the fourth day, the silver and gold were weighed in the house of the Lord our God by the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad <note>original: "iosabdus"</note> son of Jeshua and Noadiah <note>original: "moeth"</note> son of Binnui, the Levites. Everything was recorded by number and weight, and the total weight was noted at that hour. And those who had come from captivity offered burnt offerings <note>term: "holocausta" — sacrifices entirely consumed by fire</note> to the Lord God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve he-goats for sin—all as a sacrifice to the Lord. And they delivered the king's commands to the royal officials and the governors of Coelesyria and Phoenicia; and they honored the people and the temple of God.

**A**fter these things were completed, the leaders came to me, saying: "The people of Israel, the princes, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the foreign peoples and the nations of the land, nor from their impurities—the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites. For they have mingled with their nations and have taken their daughters for themselves and their sons. And the holy seed has been mixed with the foreign peoples of the land; and the leaders and magistrates have been participants in this iniquity from the very beginning." As soon as I heard these things, I tore my garments and my sacred tunic, and I pulled out the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat mourning and sad. And all those who were called by the word of the Lord God of Israel gathered to me as I wailed over this iniquity. And I sat sad until the evening sacrifice. Rising from my fast with my garments and sacred tunic torn, I knelt down and stretched out my hands to the Lord and said: "Lord, I am confounded and ashamed before your face. For our sins have multiplied over our heads, and our iniquities have reached up to heaven since the times of our fathers. We are in great sin even to this day. Because of our sins and those of our fathers, we have been delivered with our brothers, our kings, and our priests to the sword, to captivity, and to plundering with confusion, even to this day. And now, how much mercy has been shown to us by the Lord our God, that he might leave us a root and a name in the place of his sanctification, and that he might light a lamp for us in the house of the Lord our God and give us food in the time of our servitude. And though we were slaves, the Lord our God did not abandon us, but placed us in favor before the kings of the Persians, that they might give us food, glorify the temple of our Lord, raise up the desolation of Zion, and give us stability in Judea and Jerusalem. And now, Lord, what shall we say, having these things? For I have bypassed your commandments which you gave through the hands of your servants the prophets, saying: 'The land into which you enter to possess it is a polluted land, through the mingling of foreigners and their impurity they have filled it.' And now, do not join your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, and never seek peace with them, so that being strengthened, you may eat the good things of the land and leave an inheritance to your children forever. All that has happened to us is because of our evil works and our great sins. For you, Lord, have lightened our sins and given us such a root. And yet we have turned back to bypass your law and mingle with the impurity of the nations of the earth. Are you not angry with us even to the point of extermination, so that no root, name, or place would be left for us? Lord God of Israel, you are truthful; for we are left as a root even to this day. Behold, now we are in your sight in our iniquities. For we cannot stand before you in these things."

**A**nd as Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping while lying before the temple of God, a very great crowd gathered to him from Jerusalem—men, women, and youths. For there was great weeping in the multitude. And Shecaniah <note>original: "iechonias"</note> son of Jehiel, of the sons of Israel, cried out and said to Ezra: "We have sinned against the Lord, for we have settled with and taken wives from the nations of the land. But now there is hope for all Israel in this. Let us swear to the Lord that we will cast out all our wives who are from the nations, along with their children, as it seems good to you and to all who obey the law of the Lord."

**"R**ise up and help us, and we will be with you; act manfully." And Ezra, rising up, made the chief priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do according to these things. And they swore.

**A**nd Ezra, rising from before the court of the temple, went into the chamber of Jehohanan <note>original: "ioanan"</note> son of Eliashib. While staying there, he ate no bread and drank no water, mourning for the iniquities of the multitude. And they sent word through all Judea and in Jerusalem that all who were from the captivity should gather in Jerusalem. Whoever did not appear within three days, according to the counsel of the elders and the magistrates, his substance would be taken away and he himself would be considered a stranger to the multitude of the captivity. Then all who were in Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem within three days. This was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. And the entire multitude sat in the open area of the temple, trembling because of the approaching winter. And Ezra, rising up, said to them: "You have acted unjustly in taking foreign wives in marriage, adding sin upon Israel. Now give confession and glory to the Lord God of your fathers; do his will and separate yourselves from the nations of the land and from foreign wives." And the whole multitude cried out with a loud voice: "As you have said, so we will do. But because the multitude is great and it is winter time, we cannot stand out in the open; and this work is not for one day or two, for we have sinned greatly in these matters. Let the leaders of the multitude be appointed, and let all who dwell with us and who have foreign wives be present at a set time, with the elders and judges from place to place, until the wrath of the Lord is turned away from us regarding this matter."

the sons of the sons of the priests who came from Anach: who are the sons of Jedaiah <note>original: "sedech"</note>, and the sons of Joiarib, and the sons of Jedaiah, and the sons of Gedaliah; Sedeh; his sons twenty-four; they were Suat and the others of the same, ten; offering a ram for their offenses: Zebadiah; and the sons of Joiarib, and the sons of Jesiah, and the sons of Sersa, and Sabel, and Hodiah. Of the sons of Bani: Addi, Amram, Zhubel, Benaiah, and Bedaias, Chely, Annama, Meremoth, and Eliashib, Mattenai, Madanay, and Castasii, and Bary, and Binnui, Senei, and Salmas, and Nadan, and Adadai, Nechue, Cabia, Siris, Sarai, and Azarel, and Shelemiah, Shimera, Shallum, Amariah, Joseph. Of the sons of Nebo: Mattenai, Zabad, Zabra-fedu, and Joel, Benaiah. All these had taken foreign wives, and there were women among them who had borne children.

**T**he words of Nehemiah
son of Hacaliah. And it happened in the month of Kislev <note>original: "casleu"</note>, in the twentieth year, while I was in the fortress of Susa <note>original: "susis"</note>. And Hanani, one of my brothers, came—he and some men from Judah. And I asked them about the Jews who had remained and survived the captivity, and about Jerusalem. And they said to me: "Those who remained and survived the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach; and the wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates are burned with fire." When I heard such words, I sat down and wept, and I mourned for many days; and I fasted and prayed before the face of the God of heaven. And I said: "I beseech you, Lord God of heaven, strong, great, and terrible, who keeps the covenant and mercy with those who love you and keep your commandments: let your ear be listening and your eyes open, that they may hear the prayer of your servant, which I pray before you today, night and day, for the children of Israel your servants. And I confess the sins of the children of Israel, which they have sinned against you; both I and my father’s house have sinned. We have been seduced by vanity, and we have not known your commandments, nor the judgments and testimonies which you commanded your servant Moses. Remember the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying: 'When you transgress, I will scatter you among the peoples; but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, even if you were led away to the furthest parts of heaven, from there I will gather you and bring you to the place I have chosen, so that my name may dwell there.' And these are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand. I beseech you, Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who wish to fear your name; and direct your servant today, and grant him mercy before this man." For I was the king's cupbearer <note>term: "pincerna" — a high-ranking official responsible for serving the king's wine and often acting as a trusted advisor</note>.

**A**nd it happened in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, that wine was before him; and I took up the wine and gave it to the king, and I had never been as one languishing before his face. And the king said to me: "Why is your face sad, since I do not see that you are sick? This is not for nothing; rather, some evil is in your heart." And I feared very, very much, and I said to the king: "O King, live forever. Why should my face not mourn, since the city, the house of the tombs of my fathers, is deserted, and its gates are burned with fire?" And the king said to me: "For what thing do you make a request?" And I prayed to the God of heaven, and I said to the king: "If it seems good to the king, and if your servant finds favor before your face, that you would send me to Judea, to the city of the tomb of my father, and I will rebuild it." And the king said to me, with the queen sitting next to him: "How long will your journey be, and when will you return?" And it pleased the king, and he sent me; and I set a time for him. And I said to the king: "If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the region across the river, that they may escort me until I come to Judea; and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to cover the gates of the temple house, and the city wall, and the house into which I shall enter." And the king granted it to me according to the good hand of my God upon me. And I came to the governors of the region across the river and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent with me captains of the soldiers and horsemen. And Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, and they were saddened with great affliction that a man had come who sought the prosperity of the children of Israel.

**S**o I came to Jerusalem and was there for three days. And I rose in the night, I and a few men with me, and I did not tell anyone what God had put in my heart to do in Jerusalem. And there was no beast with me except the animal upon which I sat. And I went out by the Valley Gate at night, and past the Dragon's Spring, and to the Dung Gate; and I considered the wall of Jerusalem, which was broken down, and its gates burned with fire. And I passed to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Aqueduct, but there was no place for the beast I sat upon to pass. And I went up by the torrent at night and considered the wall; and turning back, I came to the Valley Gate and returned. But the magistrates did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. Neither to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the magistrates, nor to the rest who were doing the work had I indicated anything up to that point. Then I said to them: "You know the affliction in which we are, because Jerusalem is deserted and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us build the walls of Jerusalem, and let us no longer be a reproach." And I told them of the hand of my God, how it had been good with me, and the king's words which he had spoken to me; and I said: "Let us rise up and build." And their hands were strengthened for good. But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard it, they mocked us and despised us. And they said: "What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?" And I returned word to them and said: "The God of heaven himself helps us, and we are his servants; let us rise and build. But you have no part, nor justice, nor memory in Jerusalem."

**A**nd Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They sanctified it and set its doors; and they sanctified it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, and even to the Tower of Hananel. And next to him the men of Jericho built; and next to them, Zaccur son of Imri built. But the Fish Gate was built by the sons of Hassenaah. They roofed it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars. And next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, built. And next to him, Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, built. And next to him, Zadok son of Baana built. And next to them, the Tekoites built; but their nobles did not put their necks to the work of their Lord. And the Old Gate was built by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They roofed it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars. And next to them, Melatiah the Gibeonite built, and Jadon the Meronothite, men of Gibeon and Mizpah, for the governor who was in the region across the river. And next to him, Uzziel son of Harhaiah, the goldsmith, built.
