Now it happened that when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was very angry and greatly moved; he mocked the Jews and spoke before his brothers and the army of the Samaritans: "What are these weak Jews doing? Will the nations let them be? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they recover stones from the heaps of dust that are burned?" But Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, "Let them build. If even a fox climbs up, he will jump over their stone wall." Hear, our God, for we have become an object of contempt. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them up to contempt in a land of captivity.

And it happened when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and the Arabs, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the healing of the walls of Jerusalem was going forward and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they were very angry. And they all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to plot ambushes. And we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night. But Judah said: "The strength of the burden-bearers is failing, and there is too much rubble; we are not able to build the wall." And our enemies said: "Let them not know or see until we come into their midst and kill them and cause the work to cease." Now it happened that when the Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times, from all the places where they had come to us, I stationed people in the place behind the wall in a circuit, in order with their swords, spears, and bows. And I looked and arose and said to the nobles, the magistrates, and the rest of the common people: "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and terrible, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives, and your houses."

<column-break/>

...do not cover their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from before your face, for they have mocked the builders. So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together to half its height, and the heart of the people was encouraged to work. Now it happened when I heard it was reported to us that their counsel was frustrated, we all returned to the walls, each to his own work. And it happened from that day that half of the young men did the work, and the other half were prepared for war with spears, shields, bows, and armor; and the leaders stood behind the whole house of Judah. Of those building the wall and those carrying burdens and those loading them, each with one hand performed the work and with the other held a sword. For each of the builders was girded with a sword at his side and built. And the trumpeter was beside me. And I said to the nobles, the magistrates, and the rest of the common people: "The work is great and large, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another. In whatever place you hear the sound of the trumpet, run there to us. Our God will fight for us." And so we did the work, and half of us held spears from the rising of the dawn until the stars came out. At that time I also said to the people: "Let every man and his servant stay in the middle of Jerusalem, and let them be guards for you by night and work by day." But I, my brothers, my servants, and the guards who were behind me did not take off our clothes; each one only undressed for washing.

And there arose a great cry of the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers. For there were those who said: "Our sons and our daughters are very many; let us receive grain for them, that we may eat and live." And there were those who said: "Let us mortgage our fields, our vineyards, and our houses to get grain during the famine." And others said: "We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute, and we have given our fields and vineyards. And now, as the flesh of our brothers is, so is our flesh; and as their sons are, so are our sons. Behold, we are subjecting our sons and daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We have no way to redeem them, and others possess our fields and vineyards." And I was very angry when I heard their cry according to these words. And my heart pondered within me, and I rebuked the magistrates and nobles, and I said to them: "Are you each demanding usury from your brothers?" And I gathered a great assembly against them and said to them: "As you know, we have redeemed our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations according to our ability. And will you then sell your brothers, and shall we buy them back?" And they were silent, finding nothing to answer. And I said to them: "The thing you are doing is not good. Why do you not walk in the fear of our God, lest we be reproached by the nations, our enemies? I and my brothers and my servants have lent many people money and grain. Let us not demand this back in common, and let us forgive what is owed to us. Restore to them this day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses; moreover, the hundredth part of the money, grain, wine, and oil that you used to demand from them, return it for them." And they said: "We will restore them and require nothing from them; we will do as you say." And I called the priests and made them swear to do according to what I had said. Moreover, I shook out the fold of my garment and said: "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labors who does not fulfill this word; so may he be shaken out and become empty." And the whole multitude said "Amen" and praised God. And the people did according to what had been said.

Moreover, from the day the king commanded me to be governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—I and my brothers did not eat the food allotted to the governor. But the previous governors who were before me burdened the people and took from them bread, wine, and forty shekels of money daily; even their servants oppressed the people. But I did not do so because of the fear of God. Rather, I labored on the work of the wall, and I bought no field; and all my servants were gathered there for the work. There were also at my table one hundred and fifty Jews and magistrates, besides those who came to us from the nations around us. Every day one ox and six choice rams were prepared for me, besides poultry; and every ten days, various wines and many other things were provided. Yet I did not demand the governor's food allowance, for the people were very much impoverished. Remember me, my God, for good, according to all I have done for this people.

And when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall and that no breach was left in it (though at that time I had not yet set the doors in the gates), Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying: "Come, and let us strike a covenant together in the villages in the plain of Ono." But they were thinking to do me harm. I sent messengers to them, saying: "I am doing a great work and I cannot come down, lest the work should stop while I leave it and come down to you." And they sent to me according to this word four times, and I answered them in the same way. Then Sanballat sent his servant to me in the same way a fifth time with an unsealed letter in his hand, written in this manner: "It is heard among the nations, and Geshem says, that you and the Jews are thinking of rebelling, and therefore you are building the wall and wish to raise yourself as king over them. For which cause you have sent prophets to preach of you in Jerusalem, saying, 'There is a king in Judea.' The king is going to hear these words. Therefore come now, let us take counsel together." And I sent to them, saying: "Nothing has been done according to these words you speak; for you are inventing them from your own heart." For they were all trying to terrify us, thinking our hands would cease from the work and we would rest. Therefore I strengthened my hand even more.

And I went into the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, in secret. He said: "Let us gather together in the house of God, in the middle of the temple, and let us shut the doors of the sanctuary, because they are coming to kill you; they are coming to kill you by night." And I said: "Should a man like me flee? And who like me would enter the temple to save his life? I will not enter." And I understood that God had not sent him, but that he spoke as if prophesying against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him. For he had received a price to make me afraid and so I would sin, and they would have an evil report to reproach me. Remember me, my God, for Tobiah and Sanballat according to such works of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the other prophets who tried to terrify me. So the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul, in fifty-two days. And it happened when all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us feared and were cast down within themselves, and they knew that this work was done by God. But also in those many days, the nobles of Judah sent letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah came to them. For there were many in Judah who had sworn an oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah as his wife. Moreover, they praised him before me and reported my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to terrify me.

After the wall was built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed, I gave charge over Jerusalem to my brother Hanani and to Hananiah, the leader of the palace, for he was a faithful man and feared God more than many others. And I said to them: "Let not the gates of Jerusalem be opened until the sun is hot; and while they are still standing guard, let the doors be shut and barred." And I appointed guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each in his watch and each opposite his own house. Now the city was very wide and large, and the people were few in the middle of it, and the houses were not built. But God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, the magistrates, and the common people to take a census. <margin>Nethinim. 1 Chronicles 9; Ezra 2.</margin> **The Nethinim** <note>original: "Nethinim"; these were temple servants or assistants, likely of non-Israelite origin, dedicated to service in the sanctuary</note> were the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabaoth, the sons of Keros, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padon, the sons of Lebana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephushsim, the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur, the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha, the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah, the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatupha. The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Perida, the sons of Jaala, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel, the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Amon. All the Nethinim and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred ninety-two.

<margin>Ezra 2</margin> And these were those who went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; but they could not prove their ancestral houses or their lineage, whether they were of Israel: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred forty-two. And of the priests: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name. These sought their registration in the genealogy but it was not found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean. And the Tirshatha <note>original: "atharsetas"; a Persian title for a governor, here referring to Nehemiah</note> told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should stand up with Urim and Thummim <note>original: "doctus et eruditus"; literally "learned and scholarly," referring to the priest's ability to consult God's will through sacred lots</note>. The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred sixty, besides their male and female servants, who were seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and they had two hundred forty-five singers, male and female. Their horses were seven hundred thirty-six; their mules, two hundred forty-five; their camels, four hundred thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred twenty.

<margin>1 Chronicles 9; Ezra 2</margin> **Now some** of the heads of the families gave to the work. The Tirshatha gave to the treasury a thousand drachmas <note>An ancient unit of currency or weight</note> of gold, fifty bowls, and five hundred thirty priestly tunics. And some of the heads of families gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand drachmas of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver. And what the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand drachmas of gold, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priestly tunics. So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the Nethinim, and all Israel lived in their towns. And when the seventh month came, the children of Israel were in their towns.

<margin>Ezra 3; 3 Ezra 5</margin> **All the people** gathered as one man in the square that was before the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel. So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men and women and all who could understand, on the first day of the seventh month. And he read from it openly in the square that was before the Water Gate from morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand. And the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law. And Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform <note>original: "gradum ligneum"; a wooden step or pulpit</note> which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand; and on his left hand Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam. And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was standing above all the people. And as he opened it, all the people stood up. And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God; and all the people answered, "Amen, Amen," lifting up their hands. And they bowed their heads and worshiped God with their faces to the ground. Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites helped the people to understand the Law; and the people stood in their places. And they read from the book of the Law of God distinctly and clearly to provide understanding; and they understood as it was read. And Nehemiah (who is the Tirshatha) and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were interpreting to all the people, said: "This day is holy to the Lord our God; do not mourn or weep." For all the people wept as they heard the words of the Law. Then he said to them: "Go, eat the fat, and drink the sweet wine, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is holy to our Lord, and do not be grieved. For the joy of the Lord is your strength." So the Levites stilled all the people, saying, "Be quiet, for the day is holy; do not be grieved." And all the people went their way to eat and drink, to send portions and to make great rejoicing, because they had understood the words that were taught to them.

<margin>Leviticus 23; Deuteronomy 16</margin> **And** on the second day, the heads of the ancestral houses of all the people, the priests, and the Levites were gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law. And they found it written in the Law, which the Lord had commanded through Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths <note>original: "tabernaculis"; shelters made of branches for the Festival of Tabernacles</note> during the feast of the seventh month. And that they should proclaim and publish this voice in all their towns and in Jerusalem, saying: "Go out to the mountain and bring olive branches, and branches of beautiful wood, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written." So the people went out and brought them. And they made booths for themselves, each on his roof, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the square of the Water Gate, and in the square of the Ephraim Gate. And the whole assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in them. For from the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the children of Israel had not done so. And there was very great rejoicing. And he read from the book of the Law of God every day, from the first day to the last. They celebrated the feast for seven days; and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly according to the custom.

<margin>1 Ezra 9</margin> **Now on** the twenty-fourth day of this month, the children of Israel were assembled with fasting and in sackcloth, and with dust on their heads. And the lineage of the children of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers. And they rose up to stand, and they read from the scroll of the Law of the Lord their God four times in the day; and four times they confessed and worshiped the Lord their God. Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the platform of the Levites and cried with a loud voice to the Lord their God. And the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: "Stand up, bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting! And let them bless your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise. You alone are the Lord; you made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host; the earth and all things that are on it; the seas and all that is in them; and you preserve them all, and the host of heaven worships you. You are the Lord God, who chose Abram and brought him out of the fire of the Chaldeans <note>original: "igne chaldaeorum"; usually interpreted as "Ur of the Chaldeans"</note> and gave him the name Abraham. And you found his heart faithful before you, and made a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites, to give it to his offspring; and you have fulfilled your words, for you are righteous. And you saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and heard their cry at the Red Sea. And you showed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, and against all his servants, and against all the people of his land; for you knew that they acted insolently against them; and you made a name for yourself, as it is to this day. And you divided the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground; but you threw their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters. And in a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they should go.

<margin>Exodus 19; 20</margin> **You** also came down upon Mount Sinai, and spoke with them from heaven, and gave them right judgments and laws of truth, ceremonies, and good commandments; and you made known to them your holy Sabbath, and commanded them mandates and ceremonies and the law by the hand of Moses your servant. You also gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and brought forth water for them from the rock for their thirst; and you told them to go in and possess the land over which you had lifted your hand to give them. But they and our fathers acted insolently and hardened their necks, and did not listen to your commandments. And they refused to listen, and were not mindful of your wonders that you had performed for them. They hardened their necks and appointed a leader to return to their slavery, as if by rebellion. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and merciful, long-suffering and of great compassion, and you did not forsake them. Even when they had made for themselves a cast calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' and had committed great blasphemies. Yet you in your great mercies did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from them by day to lead them in the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to show them the path by which they should go. And you gave your good spirit to instruct them; and you did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst. For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness, and they lacked nothing; their clothes did not wear out,

<column-break/>

and their feet did not swell. And you gave them kingdoms and peoples, and distributed them in portions; so they possessed the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan. You also multiplied their children as the stars of heaven, and brought them into the land of which you had told their fathers that they should enter and possess it. So the children went in and possessed the land, and you subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hands, with their kings and the peoples of the land, that they might do with them as they pleased. And they took fortified cities and a rich land; and possessed houses full of all good things, cisterns hewn by others, vineyards, olive groves, and many fruit trees; so they ate and were filled and grew fat, and abounded in delights in your great goodness. But they provoked you to anger and rebelled against you, and cast your law behind their backs; and they killed your prophets who warned them to return to you, and they committed great blasphemies. Therefore you gave them into the hand of their enemies, who afflicted them. And in the time of their trouble they cried to you, and you heard them from heaven; and according to your great mercies you gave them saviors who saved them from the hand of their enemies. But after they had rest, they returned to doing evil in your sight, and you left them in the hand of their enemies, so that they had dominion over them.

<margin>2 Kings 17</margin> **Yet when they** returned and cried to you, you heard them from heaven, and many times you delivered them according to your mercies. And you warned them to return to your law. But the children acted insolently and did not listen to your commandments, and they sinned against your judgments (which, if a man does, he shall live in them); and they turned a stubborn shoulder and hardened their neck, and would not hear. And you sustained them for many years, and warned them by your spirit through the hand of your prophets; yet they would not listen; and you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands. Nevertheless, in your great mercies you did not make a full end of them, nor forsake them; for you are a gracious and merciful God. Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and mercy, let not all the hardship seem little before you, which has come upon us, on our kings, on our princes, on our priests, on our prophets, on our fathers, and on all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day. Yet you are just in all that has come upon us, for you have acted faithfully, but we have acted wickedly. Our kings, our princes, our priests, and our fathers have not kept your law, and have not attended to your commandments and your testimonies which you testified against them. And they, in their kingdoms and in your great goodness which you gave them, and in the broad and rich land which you set before them, did not serve you, nor did they turn from their wicked deeds. Behold, we are servants this day; and the land that you gave to our fathers to eat its fruit and its good things—behold, we are servants in it. And its produce yields largely to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins; also they have dominion over our bodies and over our livestock at their pleasure; and we are in great distress.

<margin>2 Ezra 10</margin> **Because of all this**, we make a firm covenant and write it down; and our princes, our Levites, and our priests seal it. Those who set their seal were: Nehemiah the Tirshatha, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah, Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah. These were the priests. And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel; and their brothers Shebaniah, Hodaviah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, Hodiah, Bani, Beninu. The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, Hodiah, Hashum, Besai, Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, Malluch, Harim, Baanah. And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding, promising for their brothers: their nobles, who came to pledge and swear an oath to walk in God's law, which was given by the hand of Moses the servant of God; and to observe and do all the commandments of the Lord our God, and his judgments and his ceremonies; and that we would not give our daughters to the people of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons.

<margin>Deuteronomy 7; Exodus 23</margin> **And if the peoples** of the land bring wares and all things for use on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. And we will forgo the seventh year and the exaction of every debt. Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to give yearly the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God, for the showbread, and for the continual grain offering, and for the continual burnt offering, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, on the set feasts, and for the holy things; and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God. We also cast lots among the priests, the Levites, and the people for the wood offering, to bring it into the house of our God by our fathers' houses at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law of Moses; and to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of the Lord; and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the law; and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God; and that we should bring the firstfruits of our dough and our offerings, the fruit of every tree, the new wine and the oil, to the priests, to the chambers <note>original: "gazophylacium"; a treasury or storehouse</note> of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground to the Levites; for the Levites themselves take the tithes in all the towns where we work. And the priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites take tithes; and the Levites shall bring up the tenth of the tithes to the house of our God, to the chambers of the storehouse. For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the offerings of grain, new wine, and oil to the chambers. And there are the vessels of the sanctuary, and the priests who minister, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the ministers. And we will not neglect the house of our God.

<margin>1 Chronicles 9</margin> **Now the leaders** of the people lived in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine parts remained in the other towns. And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to live in Jerusalem. These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah. But everyone lived on his own property in his own town—Israel, the priests, the Levites, the Nethinim, and the sons of Solomon's servants. And some of the children of Judah and of the children of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the children of Perez; and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite. And after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred twenty-eight. Joel son of Zichri was their overseer; and Judah son of Hassenuah was second over the city. And of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin, Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the leader...

And certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were joined to Benjamin.

These are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Jeshua. Joiakim was the father of Eliashib, Eliashib of Joiada, Joiada of Jonathan, and Jonathan of Jaddua. And in the days of Joiakim were priests, heads of ancestral houses: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah; of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan; of Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph; of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai; of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam; of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin and Moadiah, Piltai; of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan; of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi; of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber; of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah, Nethanel. As for the Levites, in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, there were recorded the heads of ancestral houses; also the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian. The sons of Levi, heads of ancestral houses, were written in the Book of the Chronicles <note>Latin: libro verborum dierum; literally "the book of the words of the days"</note> until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib. And the heads of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their brothers opposite them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, watch by watch. Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers standing guard at the storehouses of the gates.

These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe. At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with gladness, with thanksgivings and with singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. And the sons of the singers gathered together from the district surrounding Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites; also from Beth-gilgal and from the region of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built for themselves villages around Jerusalem. And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall. Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs that gave thanks. One went to the right on the wall to the Dung Gate. And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah, and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, and certain of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph; and his brothers, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them. At the Fountain Gate they went up straight before them by the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, to the Water Gate on the east. The other choir of those who gave thanks went to the north, and I followed them with half of the people, on the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens, to the Broad Wall, and above the Gate of Ephraim, and by the Old Gate, and by the Fish Gate and the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard. So both choirs of those who gave thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me; and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets; and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers sang loudly with Jezrahiah as their leader. And they offered great sacrifices that day and rejoiced, for God had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and children also rejoiced. And the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away. On that day men were appointed over the chambers for the stores, the contributions, the first fruits, and the tithes, to gather into them the portions required by the law for the priests and for the Levites from the fields belonging to the towns; for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered. And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon. For in the days of David and Asaph of old there were chiefs of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they set apart that which was for the Levites; and the Levites set apart that which was for the sons of Aaron.

On that day the book of Moses was read in the hearing of the people. And in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, because they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them. Yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.

As soon as the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent. Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah, had prepared for Tobiah a large chamber where they had previously put the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given by commandment to the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests. While this was taking place, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king. And after some time I asked leave of the king and came to Jerusalem, and I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing for him a chamber in the courts of the house of God. And this

<column-break/>

seemed very evil to me. And I threw all the household furniture of Tobiah out of the chamber. Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers, and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense. I also found out that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers, who did the work, had fled each to his field. So I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" And I gathered them together and set them in their stations. Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses. And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, and as their assistant Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were considered reliable, and their duty was to distribute to their brothers. Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds <note>Latin: misericordias meas; literally "my mercies" or "acts of devotion"</note> that I have done for the house of my God and for his service.

In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold food. Tyrians also, who lived in the city, brought in fish and all kinds of goods and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself! Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath." As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and gave orders that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my servants at the gates, that no load might be brought in on the Sabbath day. Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem once or twice. But I warned them and said to them, "Why do you spend the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. Then I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.

In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people. And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair. And I made them take an oath in the name of God, saying, "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves. Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin. Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?" And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite; therefore I chased him from me. Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites. Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work; and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the first fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

# HERE BEGINS THE PREFACE OF JEROME THE PRIEST TO THE BOOK OF TOBIT.

To the bishops CHROMATIUS AND HELIODORUS, Jerome the priest sends greetings in the Lord. I do not cease to wonder at the urgency of your demand. For you require that I translate a book written in the Chaldean language <note>Jerome refers to Aramaic as "Chaldean"</note> into the Latin style, namely the book of Tobit, which the Hebrews, cutting it out from the catalog of Divine Scriptures, have relegated to those writings they call Hagiographa <note>Jerome notes that Tobit was not in the Hebrew canon but was part of the "holy writings" or apocrypha</note>. I have done as you wished, but not out of my own desire. For the studies of the Hebrews reproach us and accuse us of bringing such things to Latin ears against their canon. But judging it better to displease the judgment of the Pharisees and to obey the command of bishops, I have persisted as best I could. And because the Chaldean language is close to the Hebrew speech, finding a speaker very skilled in both languages, I took up the labor of a single day; and whatever he expressed to me in Hebrew words, I, having summoned a secretary, set forth in Latin speech. I shall be compensated for the reward of this work by your prayers, when I learn that you are pleased that I have completed what you commanded me.

**W**hen, therefore, it was necessary at this present time for his son to go for the money which he had given as a loan to Gabael, a man living in Rages, a city of the Medes, he remembered this precept. For never did the precepts of God the Father permit sons to become masters of money, except as often as his own justice acts, which is more about justice than about the life of merchants: since justice will foresee where the precept of truth might lose mercy.

Then that merchant gave him his lord: so that on the morrow he might make the journey for him; and he gave him the presence of those whom he wished, who would have freedom wherever indeed he wanted.

**E**at your bread with the hungry, and make clothing for the naked: as it is commonly said: it shall be an honor to live as a person of merciful character. Because mercy cannot be created outside of me. Because unless the heart catches fire, virtue does not go forth, so that it might be able to obtain memory. After many words of mercy, therefore, coming to Rages, the son had a reputation by the precept of the merchant; indeed, he had mercy.

Now, he is called a merchant who is a "trader" <note>term: merchant (Latin: mercator); here used as an allegory for a wise soul or Christ, who "trades" earthly life for spiritual virtues</note>, so that he may make a trade from his talents. Truly the Lord dwells in the merchant where the merchant is wise, as it is said: "The merchant is a wise man who is able to trade where he renders justice."

Then the angel Raphael said to him: "Hear me, and I will show you who they are over whom the demon can prevail. # ## HERE BEGINS THE PROLOGUE TO THE BOOK OF JUDITH

**AMONG THE HEBREWS, THE BOOK OF JUDITH IS READ AMONG THE HAGIOGRAPHA** <note>The Hagiographa, or "Holy Writings," are the third section of the Hebrew Bible, distinct from the Law and the Prophets.</note>. Its authority is judged less suitable for strengthening those things which come into dispute. It was written in the Chaldean <note>Aramaic</note> language, yet it is counted among the histories. But because the Council of Nicaea is said to have counted this book in the number of the Holy Scriptures, I have yielded to your request—or rather, your demand. Having set aside the occupations by which I was vehemently held back, I have given one late-night's labor <note>original: "lucubratiuncula"</note> to this, translating sense for sense <note>original: "sensum ex sensu"</note> rather than word for word. I have cut away the most faulty variety of many manuscripts; I have expressed in Latin only those things which I could find in total integrity of understanding within the Chaldean words. Receive Judith the widow as an example of chastity, and declare her with perpetual praises in triumphal honor. For He has given her to be imitated not only by women but also by men—He who is the rewarder of their chastity, and who granted such virtue that she might conquer him who was a conqueror of all men, and surpass the unsurpassable.

Then, taking up their weapons of war, they sat in the places where the narrow paths lead, and they came to the mountain from which they could see. However, Holofernes found the springs which flowed through an aqueduct from the southern part outside the city, and he commanded the aqueduct to be cut. There were also springs not far from the walls from which they were seen drawing water in secret, rather for refreshment than for drinking. But the children of Ammon and Moab came to Holofernes, saying: "The children of Israel do not trust in spear or arrow, but the mountains defend them, and the hills protect them. Therefore, so that you may overcome them without a battle, place guards at the springs so that they cannot draw water. Then they will perish by the sword without a fight, or certainly, being exhausted, they will deliver up their city, which they think cannot be overcome because it is positioned in the mountains."

<column-break/>

**A**nd these words pleased Holofernes and all his attendants, and he appointed guards for every spring. When this guard had been maintained for twenty days, the cisterns and the collection of waters failed for all the inhabitants of Bethulia, so that there was not enough within the city to satisfy them for even one day, for water was given to the people daily by measure. Then the men and women, young and old, and children gathered to Uzziah, all saying with one voice: "Let the Lord judge between us and you, for you have done evil against us by not wanting to speak peaceably with the Assyrians. And because of this, the Lord has sold us into their hands. And there is no one to help us, while we are cast down before their eyes in thirst and great distress. And now gather everyone who remains in the city, so that we may voluntarily deliver ourselves to all the people of Holofernes. For it is better that as captives we bless the Lord while living, than that we die and become a disgrace to all flesh, seeing our wives and our infants die before our eyes. We call to witness today heaven and earth, and the God of our fathers, and our Lord, who punishes us according to our sins, that you should now deliver the city into the hand of Holofernes' soldiers, so that our end may be short by the edge of the sword, which is made longer by the heat of thirst." When they had said these things, there was great weeping and wailing throughout the city among all, and for many hours they cried out to the Lord with one voice, saying: "We have sinned with our fathers, we have acted unjustly, we have committed iniquity. Because you are merciful, have mercy on us, or avenge our iniquities with your own scourge. Do not deliver those who confess you to a people that does not know you, so that they may not say among the nations: 'Where is their God?'" But when they were weary and exhausted by these cries and weepings, Uzziah rose up, bathed in tears, and said: "Be of good courage, brothers, and let us wait these five days for mercy from the Lord. For perhaps he will cut off his anger and give glory to his name. But if, after five days have passed, help does not come, we will do according to the words you have spoken."

<margin>Judith 8</margin>
**N**ow there was Judith, a widow for three years and six months. In the upper parts of her house, she had made for herself a secret chamber in which she remained shut up with her maids. Having sackcloth <note>original: "cilicium" — a garment made of coarse animal hair used for mourning or penance</note> upon her loins, she fasted every day of her life, except for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the festivals of the house of Israel. She was exceedingly beautiful in appearance, and her husband had left her much wealth, a large household, and possessions full of herds of oxen and flocks of sheep. She was most famous among everyone because she feared the Lord greatly, and there was no one who spoke an evil word about her. Therefore, when she heard that Uzziah had promised to deliver the city after five days, she sent for the elders Chabri and Charmi, and they came to her. And she said to them: "What is this word in which you have consented to deliver the city to the Assyrians if help does not come to you within five days? And who are you who have tempted the Lord? This is not a speech that provokes mercy, but rather one that excites anger and kindles fury. You have set a time for the Lord’s mercy, and according to your own judgment, you have appointed a day. But because the Lord is patient, let us repent of this very thing and seek his indulgence with tears. For God is not like a man, that he should be threatened, nor like a son of man, that he should be inflamed to anger. And therefore, let us humble our souls to him, and being settled in a humble spirit, let us serve him. Let us say to the Lord with tears that he should show his mercy toward us according to his will; so that as our heart is troubled by their pride, we may also glory in our humility, for we have not followed the sins of our fathers, who forsook their God and adored foreign gods. Because of this, they were given over to the sword, to plunder, and to confusion among their enemies. But we know no other God besides him. We humbly expect his consolation, and he will require our blood for the affliction of our enemies." And all those humbling themselves before him sought that his memory might conquer us <note>The Latin here is somewhat garbled in the OCR; Judith is likely urging the elders to remember how God tested their fathers like Abraham and Isaac.</note>.

**T**hen Uzziah and the elders, answering, said to her: "All the things you have spoken are true, and there is no fault in your words. Now therefore, pray for us, for you are a holy woman and one who fears the Lord." And Judith said to them: "Just as you know that what I have been able to speak is from God, so prove if what I have disposed to do is from God, and pray that the Lord may confirm my plan. You shall stand at the gate tonight, and I will go out with my maid; and within the five days you have promised, the Lord will look upon his people Israel. But I do not want you to search into my act; and until I report back to you, let nothing else be done but prayer for me to the Lord our God." And Uzziah, the prince of Judah, said to her: "Go in peace, and the Lord be with you in taking vengeance upon our enemies." And they returned and went away.

<margin>Judith 9</margin>
**T**hen Judith entered her oratory, and putting on sackcloth, she put ashes upon her head; and prostrating herself before the Lord, she cried to the Lord her God, saying:

> Lord God of my fathers, who gave them the sword for defense against the foreigners who wanted to violate the modest and strip them bare for their confusion; you gave their women for a prey and their daughters into captivity, and all their spoil to be divided among your servants who were zealous for you. Look, O Lord my God, upon me, a widow. For you have done the things of old, and those things were prepared, and you have placed your judgments in your providence. **O** you have thought of things after those, and this has been done which you yourself willed. For all your ways are prepared, and you have placed your judgments in your providence. Look upon the camps of the Assyrians now, just as you once deigned to look upon the camps of the Egyptians, when they ran armed after your servants, trusting in their chariots, in their cavalry, and in the multitude of their warriors. But you looked upon their camp, and darkness exhausted them. The abyss held their feet, and the waters covered them. So let it be with these also, O Lord, who trust in their multitude, in their chariots, in their pikes, in their arrows, and in their spears, and do not know that you are our Lord, who breaks wars from the beginning; the Lord is your name. Lift up your arm as from the beginning, and crush their power by your power. Let their power fall by your curse, they who promise themselves to violate your sanctuary, to pollute the tabernacle of your name, and to strike down with the sword the sanctuary of your altar. Grant, O Lord, that his pride may be cut off by his own sword. Let him be caught by the snare of his eyes in me, and strike him from the lips of my love <note>Judith asks God to use her beauty and her speech to entrap Holofernes.</note>. Give me a constant mind in my heart, that I may despise him and his power, so that I may overthrow him. For it will be a memorial to your name when the hand of a woman has struck him down. For your power, O Lord, is not in a multitude, nor is your will in the strength of horses; nor have the proud pleased you from the beginning, but the prayer of the humble and the meek has always pleased you. O God of heaven and creator of the waters, and Lord of every creature, hear me, a miserable woman, praying and trusting in your mercy. Remember, O Lord, your covenant, and put a word in my mouth, and strengthen my heart in the defense of my mind, so that your house may remain in your sanctification, and all nations may know that you are God, and there is no other besides you.

<margin>Judith 10</margin>
**I**n the meantime, when she had ceased crying to the Lord, she rose from the place where she lay prostrate before the Lord, and called her maid. They went down into her house, and she took off the sackcloth and stripped herself of the garments of her widowhood. She washed her body and anointed herself with the best myrrh. She combed the hair of her head and placed a headdress <note>original: "mitram"</note> upon her head, and clothed herself with the garments of her joy. She put sandals on her feet and took her bracelets, lilies, earrings, and rings, and adorned herself with all her ornaments. To this, the Lord also added splendor, because all this dressing up did not depend on lust but on virtue. And therefore, the Lord increased this beauty in her, so that she appeared with inestimable loveliness to the eyes of all. She then placed upon her maid a skin of wine, a vessel of oil, parched corn, dates, bread, and cheese, and she set out. And when she had come to the gate of the city, she found waiting...

<margin>10</margin>
Now on the fourth day, Holofernes made a feast for his personal servants, and he said to Bagoas his eunuch: "Go and persuade that Hebrew woman to consent of her own accord to dwell with me. For it is a disgrace among the Assyrians if a woman mocks a man, so that she remains without his company." Then Bagoas went in to Judith and said: "Let it not be a burden for a good woman to go in to my lord, that she may be honored before his face, and drink wine with him, and be made joyful as one of the daughters of the Assyrians who reside in the house of the king." To whom Judith responded: "Who am I that I should contradict my lord? For everything that is good and best in his eyes, I will do; and whatever shall please him, that shall be the best for me all the days of my life." And she rose and adorned herself with her garments, and entering, she stood before his face. And the heart of Holofernes was troubled, for he was burning with desire for her. And Holofernes said to her: "Drink now and sit down in joy, for you have found favor before me." And Judith said: "I will drink, my lord, because my soul is magnified today above all the days of my life." And she took and ate and drank before him those things which her handmaid had prepared for her. And Holofernes was made joyful toward her, and he drank exceedingly much wine, more than he had ever drunk in his life.

<margin>Judith 13</margin>
<margin>110</margin>
Then, when evening had come, his servants hastened to their lodgings, and Bagoas closed the doors of the bedchamber and went away. And they were all weary from the wine; and Judith was alone in the bedchamber. Furthermore, Holofernes lay upon the bed, overcome by excessive drunkenness. And Judith commanded her girl to stand outside before the bedchamber and keep watch. And Judith stood before the bed, praying with tears and saying with a silent movement of her lips: "Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel; look in this hour upon the works of my hands, that as you have promised, you may raise up your city Jerusalem; and that I may finish this thing which I believed could be done through you." And when she had said this, she went to the pillar that was at the head of his bed, and his dagger, which was tied to it...

<column-break/>

...she unfastened. And when she had drawn it, she took hold of the hair of his head and said: "Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, in this hour." And she struck twice upon his neck, and cut off his head, and took down his canopy <note>original: "canopeum"; a mosquito net or decorative curtain over the bed, which she used to wrap the body.</note> from the pillars, and rolled away his headless body. And after a little while, she went out and delivered the head of Holofernes to her handmaid, and ordered her to put it into her pouch. And the two went out according to their custom, as if for prayer, and they passed through the camp, and circling through the valley, they came to the gate of the city. And Judith said from afar to the guards of the walls: "Open the gates, for God is with us, who has shown his power in Israel." And it happened, when they had heard her voice, they called the elders of the city, and everyone ran to her, from the least to the greatest, because they had hoped she would no longer return. And lighting lamps, they gathered around her everyone. But she, ascending to a higher place, commanded silence to be made. And when all were silent, Judith said:
"Praise the Lord our God, who does not desert those who hope in him; and in me, his handmaid, he has fulfilled his mercy which he promised to the house of Israel, and he has slain the enemy of his people by my hand this night."
And bringing the head of Holofernes out of the pouch, she showed it to them, saying: "Behold the head of Holofernes, the prince of the Assyrian army; and behold his canopy in which he lay in his drunkenness, where the Lord our God struck him by the hand of a woman. As the Lord lives, his angel has kept me both going hence, and staying there, and returning here from there; and the Lord did not permit me, his handmaid, to be defiled, but without the pollution of sin he has brought me back to you, rejoicing in his victory, in my escape, and in your liberation. Confess to him all of you, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever." And all of them adored the Lord and said to her: "The Lord has blessed you in his power, because through you he has brought our enemies to nothing." Then Achior <note>Achior was an Ammonite leader who had previously warned the Assyrians about the power of the God of Israel.</note> was called and came, and Judith said: "Blessed are you by the Lord God Most High above all women upon the earth; and blessed be the Lord who created heaven and earth, who directed you to the wounding of the head of the prince of our enemies; because today he has so magnified your name that your praise shall not depart from the mouths of men, who shall be mindful of the power of the Lord forever; for whom you have not spared your life on account of the distress and tribulation of your kin, but have come to the aid of our ruin before the sight of our God." And all the people said: "Amen, amen." Then Achior, having been called, came and seeing the head of Holofernes, fell upon his face for fear, and his soul fainted. But after he had recovered his spirit and was revived, he fell at her feet and adored her, and said: "Blessed are you by your God in every tent of Jacob; for in every nation that shall hear your name, the God of Israel shall be magnified because of you."

<margin>Judith 14</margin>
And Judith said to all the people: "Hear me, my brothers; hang this head upon our walls. and it shall be when the sun has risen, let every man take his arms, and go out with a rush, not as if to descend below, but as if making an attack. Then it will be necessary for the scouts to flee to wake their prince for battle. And when their leaders have run to the tent of Holofernes and find him headless, wallowing in his own blood, fear shall fall upon them. And when you know they are fleeing, go after them securely, for the Lord shall crush them under your feet." 
Then Achior, seeing the power that the God of Israel had shown, left behind his pagan rites and believed in God; and he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was added to the people of Israel, and all the succession of his kindred even to this day. But as soon as the day had dawned, they hung the head of Holofernes upon the walls; and every man took up his arms, and they went out with a great noise and shouting. Seeing this, the scouts ran to the tent. Furthermore, those who were in the tent came and made a noise before the entrance of the bedchamber; for the sake of waking him, they devised a disturbance, so that Holofernes might wake from the noise, yet none of the Assyrian power dared to knock or enter. But when his leaders and tribunes had come, and all the elders of the Assyrian army, they said to the chamberlains: "Enter and wake him, for the mice have come out of their holes and have dared to challenge us to battle." Then Bagoas, having entered his chamber, stood before the curtain and clapped with his hands; for he suspected that he was sleeping with Judith. But when he perceived no movement of those lying there by his sense of hearing, he went closer to the curtain, and lifting it, he saw the headless corpse of Holofernes lying upon the ground, stained in his own blood. And he cried out with a loud voice with weeping, and tore his garments. And entering the tent of Judith, he did not find her; and he leaped out to the people and said: "One Hebrew woman has brought confusion to the house of King Nebuchadnezzar! For behold, Holofernes lies on the ground, and his head is not on him." When the princes of the Assyrian power heard this, they tore their garments, and intolerable fear and trembling fell upon them, and their minds were greatly troubled. And an incomparable cry was made in the midst of the camp.

<margin>Judith 15</margin>
And when the whole army heard that Holofernes was decapitated, mind and counsel fled from them; and agitated by trembling and fear alone, they sought safety in flight. No one whispered or spoke with his neighbor, but with heads bowed and leaving all behind, they desired to escape the Hebrews, whom they heard coming armed upon them, fleeing through the ways of the fields and the paths of the hills. Therefore, the children of Israel, seeing them fleeing, descended after them with trumpeting and shouting. And because the Assyrians, gathered in a group, went headlong in flight, the children of Israel, following in one line, struck down all whom they could find. Therefore Ozias sent messengers through all the cities and regions of Israel. Every region and every city sent chosen armed youth after them, and they pursued them at the edge of the sword until they came to the extremity of their borders. But the rest who were in Bethulia entered the camp of the Assyrians and took the spoil which the fleeing Assyrians had left; and they were greatly burdened with it. Those indeed who returned victorious to Bethulia brought with them all that had been theirs, so that there was no number to the cattle, the beasts of burden, and all movable goods, because from the least to the greatest, everyone was made rich from their spoil. Joachim, however, the high priest from Jerusalem, came to Bethulia with all his elders to see Judith. When she went out to him, they all blessed her with one voice, saying: "You are the glory of Jerusalem, you are the joy of Israel, you are the honor of our people. For you have acted manfully, and your heart has been strengthened because you loved chastity, and after your husband you have known no other; therefore also the hand of the Lord has strengthened you, and you shall be blessed forever." And all the people said: "Amen, amen." For thirty days, the spoils of the Assyrians were scarcely gathered by the people of Israel. Furthermore, all things that were proved to have been Holofernes' own, they gave to Judith in gold and silver, and clothes, and gems, and all household goods; and all things were delivered to her by the people. And all the people rejoiced with the women, and the virgins, and the young men, with instruments and harps. Then Judith sang this song to the Lord God, saying:

<margin>Judith 16</margin>
"Begin unto the Lord with timbrels; sing unto the Lord with cymbals; tune unto him..."

And all the people mourned her for seven days. In all the space of her life, there was no one who troubled Israel, nor for many years after her death. The day of the victory of this festival is received by the Hebrews into the number of holy days, and is cherished by the Jews from that time until the present day.

### HERE BEGINS THE PREFACE
### OF JEROME THE
### PRIEST TO THE BOOK OF 
### ESTHER

<image-desc>Large decorative 'L' containing a seated figure (Saint Jerome), surrounded by intricate multi-colored vine scrolls and foliage in red, green, blue, and gold leaf.</image-desc>

**It is certain** that the Book of Esther has been corrupted by various translators. I, revealing it from the archives of the Hebrews, have translated it more closely, word for word. The common edition <note>Referring to the "Vetus Latina" or Old Latin version used before Jerome's Vulgate.</note> drags this book here and there with ragged ropes of words, adding things that could have been said and heard on the spot, as is customary in school exercises—taking a theme and imagining what words a man might use who suffers an injury, or the one who did the injury. But you, O Paula and Eustochium <note>Two of Jerome's most devoted students and patrons in Bethlehem.</note>, since you have been eager to enter the libraries of the Hebrews and have approved of the struggles with Hebrew texts, take this Hebrew book of Esther and look at our translation word for word, so that you may recognize that I have added nothing for show, but have simply delivered the Hebrew history into the Latin language with faithful testimony, just as it is held in the Hebrew rite. We do not seek the praises of men, nor do we fear their reproaches. For striving to please God, we do not fear the threats of men at all, who destroy with their displays those who desire to please men. And according to the Apostle, those who are of this sort cannot be servants of Christ. At the end of the book of Esther, I have placed the alphabetical sections <note>Jerome is referring to the additions to Esther found in the Greek version but not the Hebrew, which he moved to the end of the book.</note> up to the final letters; I have done this so the reader may know the order. 

<image-desc>Magnificent full-height illuminated initial 'I' spanning the height of the column. The letter is composed of architectural tiers, column segments, and circular frames containing small figures or decorative motifs, intertwined with foliage in gold, blue, green, and red.</image-desc>

# IN THE DAYS OF AHASU-
# ERUS THE KING WHO REIG-

ned from India to Ethiopia over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces: when he sat on the throne of his kingdom. In the city of Susa was the beginning of his reign. In the third year of his empire, he made a great feast for all his princes and his servants, for the strongest of the Persians and Medes, the nobles and the governors of the provinces before him, so that he might show the riches of his glory and the magnitude and boasting of his power for a long time, namely, one hundred and eighty days. And when the days of the feast were completed, he invited all the people who were found in Susa, from the greatest to the least; and for seven days he ordered a feast to be prepared in the vestibule of the garden and the grove, which had been planted by royal care and hand. And there hung on every side tents of sky-blue, and white, and violet, supported by cords of fine linen and purple, which were inserted into ivory rings and supported by marble columns. There were also beds of gold and silver placed upon a pavement of emerald and Parian stone, which was decorated with pictures of wonderful variety. And those who were invited drank from golden cups, and food was brought in various vessels. The wine also was abundant, as was fitting 

<column-break/>

for royal mercy, so that those who wished were not forced to drink; but as the king had appointed, placing one of his princes at each table, so that everyone might take what he wanted. Vashti the queen also made a feast for the women in the palace where King Ahasuerus was accustomed to stay. Therefore, on the seventh day, when the king was more cheerful and had become warm with wine after much drinking, he commanded Haman, and Biztha, and Harbona, and Bigtha, and Abagtha, and Zethar, and Carcas—the seven eunuchs who ministered in his sight—to bring in Queen Vashti before the king, with the royal crown set upon her head, to show her beauty to all the people and the princes; for she was exceedingly beautiful. But she refused, and according to the king's command which he had sent by the eunuchs, she scorned to come. Wherefore the king, being angry and inflamed with excessive fury, consulted the wise men who, according to royal custom, were always with him, and he did all things by their counsel, as they knew the laws and rights of the ancestors. And the first and chief among them were Carshena, Sethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan: the seven princes of the Persians and Medes who saw the face of the king and were accustomed to sit first after him. He asked what sentence Queen Vashti should undergo, who had been unwilling to do the command of King Ahasuerus which he had sent by the eunuchs. Memucan answered, in the hearing of the king and the princes: "Queen Vashti has not only offended the king, but also all the princes and peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. For the word of the queen will go out to all women, so that they will despise their husbands and say: 'King Ahasuerus commanded that Queen Vashti should come in to him, and she would not.' And by this example, all the wives of the princes of the Persians and Medes will little value the commands of their husbands. Wherefore the indignation of the king is just. If it please you, let an edict go out from your presence, and let it be written according to the law of the Persians and Medes, which it is unlawful to transgress: that Vashti shall no more come in to the king, but another who is better than she shall receive her kingdom. And let this be published throughout all the empire of your provinces, which is very wide: and let all wives honor their husbands, both the greater and the lesser." His counsel pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the counsel of Memucan, and sent letters to all the provinces of his kingdom, so that every nation could hear and read, in various languages and letters, that husbands should be princes and masters in their own houses, and that this should be published among all peoples.

There was a Jewish man in the city of Susa named Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, who had been carried away from Jerusalem at the time when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah king of Judah. He was the foster-father of his brother’s daughter, Hadassah, who was called by another name, Esther; and she had lost both her parents. She was very beautiful and of a graceful countenance. After her father died, Mordecai adopted her as his own daughter. And when the king's command was spread abroad, and many beautiful girls were brought to Susa and delivered to Hegai the eunuch, Esther also was delivered to him among the other girls, to be kept among the women. And she pleased him and found favor in his sight, so that he hastened her ornaments and gave her her portions, and seven of the most beautiful girls from the king's house, to adorn and provide for her and her maids. She would not reveal her people or her country to him, for Mordecai had commanded her to be silent about this matter. He walked every day before the vestibule of the house in which the chosen virgins were kept, having a care for Esther’s welfare and wanting to know what would happen to her. Now when the time came for each girl in order to go in to the king, after twelve months of preparation for the women's beauty—six months anointed with oil of myrrh, and another six months using certain pigments and spices—they went in to the king. Whatever they asked for pertaining to their adornment they received, and as it pleased them, they went from the women's chamber to the king's chamber. And she who entered in the evening came out in the morning, and was led to the second house, which was under the hand of Shaashgaz the eunuch, who presided over the king's concubines. Nor had she the power to return to the king anymore, unless the king desired it and had commanded her to be called by name.

It was investigated and found true, and they were both hanged on a gallows; and it was recorded in the histories and the commentaries of the king's annals.

To whom the king's servants, who presided at the doors of the palace, said: "Why do you not observe the command?" And when they said this frequently and he would not listen, they told Haman, desiring to know whether he would persist in his decision. For he had told them that he was a Jew. When Haman heard this and proved it by experience, that Mordecai did not bow his knees to him nor adore him, he was very angry. And he thought it a small thing to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for he had heard that he was of the Jewish race, and he wanted to destroy the whole nation of the Jews that were in the kingdom of Ahasuerus.
