### LVI
And it happened when Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea across the Jordan. And great crowds followed him, and he healed them there. And the Pharisees approached him, testing him and saying: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?" He answering said to them: "Have you not read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female?" And he said: "For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and shall cleave to his wife, and the two shall be in one flesh. Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate." They said to him: "Why then did Moses command to give a bill of divorce and to dismiss her?" He said to them: "Because Moses, on account of the hardness of your hearts, permitted you to divorce your wives. But from the beginning it was not so. And I say to you, that whoever dismisses his wife, except for fornication, and marries another, commits adultery. And he who marries her who is dismissed commits adultery." His disciples said to him: "If such is the case of a man with a wife, it is not expedient to marry." He said to them: "Not all can accept this word, but those to whom it is given. For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made so by men; and there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. He who can accept it, let him accept it." Then little children were offered to him, that he might lay his hands on them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them. But Jesus said to them: "Allow the little children to come to me, and do not forbid them; for of such is the kingdom of heaven." And when he had laid his hands on them, he departed from there.

### LVII
And behold, one approaching said to him: "Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?" He said to him: "Why do you ask me about what is good? One is good, God. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments." He said to him: "Which ones?" And Jesus said: "You shall not commit murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor your father and mother; and, you shall love your neighbor as yourself." The young man said to him: "All these I have kept. What do I still lack?" Jesus said to him: "If you wish to be perfect: go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me." But when the young man heard the word, he went away sad, for he was one having many possessions. And Jesus said to his disciples: "Amen I say to you, that a rich man shall with difficulty enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say to you: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven." Having heard these things, the disciples wondered greatly, saying: "Who then can be saved?" But Jesus, looking at them, said: "With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible." Then Peter, responding, said to him: "Behold, we have left all things and followed you; what then shall there be for us?" And Jesus said to them: "Amen I say to you, that you who have followed me, in the regeneration <note>original: "regeneratione"; referring to the renewal of the world</note> when the Son of Man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit upon twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. And everyone who has left house or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my name's sake shall receive a hundredfold and shall possess eternal life. But many who are first shall be last, and the last first."

<margin>xx</margin>
### LVIII
The kingdom of heaven is like a man, a master of a house, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard. And having made an agreement with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard. And going out about the third hour <note>about 9:00 AM</note>, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace. And he said to them: "You go also into my vineyard, and what is just I will give to you." And they went. Again he went out about the sixth <note>noon</note> and ninth hour <note>3:00 PM</note> and did likewise. But about the eleventh hour <note>5:00 PM</note> he went out and found others standing, and he said to them: "Why do you stand here idle all day?" They said to him: "Because no one has hired us." He said to them: "You go also into my vineyard." And when evening was come, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward: "Call the laborers and pay them their wage, beginning from the last even to the first." When they therefore came who had come about the eleventh hour, they received each a denarius. But when the first came, they thought they would receive more. But they also received each a denarius. And receiving it, they murmured against the master of the house, saying: "These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the heat." But he, responding to one of them, said: "Friend, I do you no wrong. Did you not agree with me for a denarius? Take what is yours and go. I wish to give to this last one even as to you. Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good?" So the last shall be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.

### LIX
"Behold we go up to Jerusalem. And the Son of Man shall be betrayed to the chief priests and the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, and they shall deliver him to the Gentiles to be mocked, and scourged, and crucified; and on the third day he shall rise again." Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, adoring and asking something of him. He said to her: "What do you wish?" She said to him: "Say that these my two sons may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom." But Jesus answering said: "You do not know what you ask. Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink?" They said to him: "We can." He said to them: "You shall indeed drink my cup; but to sit at my right hand or my left is not mine to give to you, but to those for whom it is prepared by my Father." And the ten hearing this were indignant at the two brothers. But Jesus called them to himself and said: "You know that the princes of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those who are greater exercise power over them. It shall not be so among you. But whoever wishes to become greater among you, let him be your minister. And whoever wishes to be first among you shall be your servant. Even as the Son of Man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life as a redemption for many."

### LX
And as they were departing from Jericho, a great crowd followed him. And behold, two blind men sitting by the way heard that Jesus was passing by, and they cried out, saying: "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!" But the crowd rebuked them that they should be silent. But they cried out the more, saying: "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!" And Jesus stood still and called them and said: "What do you wish

that I should do for you?" They said to him: "Lord, that our eyes may be opened." And Jesus, having mercy on them, touched their eyes; and immediately they saw, and they followed him.

### LXI
And when he had drawn near to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples, saying to them: "Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me. And if anyone says anything to you, say that the Lord has need of them, and immediately he will let them go." Now all this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying: "Say to the daughter of Zion, behold your king comes to you, meek, sitting upon a donkey, and a colt, the foal of a beast of burden." And the disciples, going, did just as Jesus had commanded them. And they brought the donkey and the colt, and they placed their garments upon them, and they made him sit thereon. And a very great crowd spread their garments in the way. Others cut branches from the trees and spread them in the way. And the crowds that went before and those that followed cried out, saying: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!" And when he had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was moved, saying: "Who is this?" But the people said: "This is Jesus the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee." And Jesus entered into the temple of God and cast out all who were selling and buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money-changers and the chairs of those who sold doves. And he said to them: "It is written: My house shall be called a house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves." And the blind and the lame approached him in the temple, and he healed them. But the chief priests and scribes, seeing the wonderful things he did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying: "Hosanna to the Son of David," were indignant and said to him: "Do you hear what these are saying?" But Jesus said to them: "Certainly. Have you never read: Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babes you have perfected praise?" And leaving them, he went out of the city into Bethany, and there he remained. Now in the morning, returning to the city, he was hungry. And seeing a certain fig tree by the way, he came to it and found nothing on it but leaves only. And he said to it: "May no fruit ever grow from you again forever." And immediately the fig tree withered away. And the disciples, seeing it, wondered, saying: "How did it wither so quickly?" But Jesus answering said to them: "Amen I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, not only shall you do this of the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain: 'Be lifted up and cast into the sea,' it shall be done. And all things whatsoever you shall ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive."

### LXII
And when he had come into the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people approached him as he was teaching, saying: "By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?" Jesus answering said to them: "I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?" But they thought within themselves, saying: "If we say 'from heaven,' he will say to us: 'Why then did you not believe him?' But if we say 'from men,' we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet." And answering Jesus, they said: "We do not know." He also said to them: "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things. But what do you think? A certain man had two sons, and approaching the first, he said: 'Son, go work today in my vineyard.' He answering said: 'I will not.' But afterward, moved by repentance, he went. And approaching the other, he said likewise. But he answering said: 'I go, lord,' and he did not go. Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said to him: "The first." Jesus said to them: "Amen I say to you, that the tax collectors and harlots shall go before you into the kingdom of God. For John came to you in the way of justice, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and harlots believed him. But you, seeing it, did not even have repentance afterward, so as to believe him."

### LXIII
"Hear another parable. There was a man, a master of a house, who planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to farmers, and went into a far country. And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the farmers that they might receive its fruits. And the farmers, having seized his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another. Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they did to them likewise. But last of all he sent his son to them, saying: 'They will reverence my son.' But the farmers, seeing the son, said within themselves: 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and we shall have his inheritance.' And having seized him, they cast him out of the vineyard and killed him. When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do to those farmers?" They said to him: "He will bring those evil men to an evil end, and will let out his vineyard to other farmers who shall render him the fruit in its seasons." Jesus said to them: "Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner. This was done by the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes? Therefore I say to you, that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits. And he who falls upon this stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will crush him." And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they knew that he spoke of them. And seeking to lay hold of him, they feared the crowds, because they held him as a prophet.

### LXIV
And Jesus, responding, spoke to them again in parables, saying: "The kingdom of heaven is made like to a man, a king, who made a marriage for his son. And he sent his servants to call those who were invited to the marriage, and they would not come. Again he sent other servants, saying: 'Tell those who are invited: behold, I have prepared my dinner; my bulls and fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage.' But they neglected it and went away, one to his farm and another to his business. But the rest seized his servants and, having treated them shamefully, killed them. But when the king heard of it, he was angry, and having sent his armies, he destroyed those murderers and burnt their city. Then he said to his servants: 'The marriage indeed is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy. Go therefore to the exits of the highways, and whomever you find, call to the marriage.' And his servants, going out into the ways, gathered together all whom they found, both good and bad, and the marriage was filled with guests. But the king entered to see the guests, and he saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment. And he said to him: 'Friend, how did you enter here not having a wedding garment?' But he was silent. Then the king said to the ministers: 'Having bound his hands and feet, cast him into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.' For many are called, but few chosen."

<margin>xxii</margin>
### LXV
Then the Pharisees, going away, took counsel how they might trap him in his speech. And they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying: "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not care for anyone, for you do not look upon the person of men. Tell us therefore what you think: is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?" But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said: "Why do you test me, hypocrites? Show me the coin of the tribute." And they offered him a denarius. And Jesus said to them: "Whose image and inscription is this?" They said to him: "Caesar's." Then he said to them: "Render therefore the things that are Caesar's to Caesar, and the things that are God's to God." And hearing this, they wondered, and leaving him, they went away.

And when the crowds heard this, they wondered at his teaching. But the Pharisees, hearing that he had silenced the Sadducees <note>The Sadducees were a Jewish sect that denied the resurrection of the dead; Jesus uses the Torah to refute them</note>, gathered together. <margin>VI</margin>
## Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples, saying: The scribes and the Pharisees have sat upon the chair of Moses. Therefore, observe and do everything whatever they tell you. But do not act according to their works. For they speak, but they do not act. For they bind heavy and unbearable burdens and lay them on men's shoulders. But they are unwilling to move them with even a finger. Indeed, they do all their works so that they may be seen by men. For they widen their phylacteries <term>phylactery: small leather boxes containing scripture texts, worn on the forehead and arm during prayer</term> and enlarge their tassels. They love the places of honor at feasts and the first seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the marketplace, and to be called 'Rabbi' by men. But you, do not be called Rabbi. For one is your teacher, and you are all brothers. And do not call anyone on earth your 'father'; for one is your Father, who is in heaven. Neither be called masters; for one is your master, the Christ. He who is greater among you shall be your servant. But whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted. But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut the kingdom of heaven before men. For you do not enter yourselves, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you consume the houses of widows while praying long prayers; because of this, you will receive a greater judgment. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Who travel over sea and dry land to make one convert <note>original: "proselitum," a Greek term for a convert to Judaism</note>, and when he has been made, you make him a son of hell twice as much as yourselves. Woe to you, blind guides! Who say, "whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound by his oath." Fools and blind! For which is greater: the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold? And "whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is upon it is bound." Blind! For which is greater: the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift? Therefore, whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by all things that are upon it. And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by him who dwells in it. And he who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by him who sits upon it. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have left behind the weightier matters of the law: judgment and mercy and faith. These things you ought to have done, and not omit the others. Blind guides, straining out a gnat <note>original: "culicem," a small insect</note> but swallowing a camel! Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are full of greed and uncleanness. Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside may also become clean. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful to men, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and all filthiness. So you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous and say: "If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets." Thus you witness against yourselves that you are the sons of those who killed the prophets. Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers. Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you escape from the judgment of hell? Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets and wise men and scribes. And some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city. So that upon you may come all the righteous blood that has been shed upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen I say to you: all these things shall come upon this generation.

<margin>VII</margin>
## Jerusalem, Jerusalem: you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you. How often I wanted to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing. Behold, your house shall be left to you deserted. For I say to you: you shall not see me from now on until you say, "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."

<margin>LXX</margin>
**And Jesus, departing from the temple, went away.** And his disciples approached him to show him the buildings of the temple. But he answering said to them: "Do you see all these things? Amen I say to you: there shall not be left here one stone upon another that shall not be destroyed."

<margin>IX</margin>
## But as he sat upon the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached him privately, saying: "Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign of your coming, and of the end of the age?" And Jesus answering said to them: "See that no one leads you astray. For many will come in my name, saying 'I am the Christ,' and they will lead many astray. For you will hear of battles and rumors of wars. See that you are not troubled. For these things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be pestilences and famines and earthquakes in various places. But all these are the beginnings of sorrows. Then they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you; and you will be hated by all nations because of my name. And then many will fall away, and will betray one another, and hate one another. And many false prophets will arise and lead many astray. And because iniquity will abound, the charity of many will grow cold. But he who perseveres to the end shall be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come. Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let him who reads understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let him who is on the roof not go down to take anything from his house. And he who is in the field, let him not return to take his tunic. But woe to those who are pregnant and those who nurse in those days. Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on the Sabbath. For then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever shall be. And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be shortened. Then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Christ,' or 'there,' do not believe it. For false Christs and false prophets will arise, and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead into error, if possible, even the elect. Behold, I have foretold it to you. If therefore they say to you, 'Behold, he is in the desert,' do not go out; 'behold, he is in the inner rooms,' do not believe it. For as lightning comes out from the east and appears even unto the west, so also shall be the coming of the Son of Man. Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together. But immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be moved. And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven. And then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man

<column-break/>

coming on the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty. And he will send his angels with a trumpet and a great voice, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the highest parts of the heavens to their furthest bounds. So when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors. Amen I say to you that this generation shall not pass away until all these things happen. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. But concerning that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, but the Father alone. For as it was in the days of Noah, so also will be the coming of the Son of Man. For just as in those days before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until that day when Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the flood came and took them all away, so also will be the coming of the Son of Man. Then two will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left. Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left. Watch, therefore, because you do not know at what hour your Lord is coming. But know this: if the master of the house knew at what hour the thief was coming, he would surely watch and would not allow his house to be broken into. Therefore you also must be ready, because you do not know at what hour the Son of Man is coming. Who do you think is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household to give them food in due season? Blessed is that servant whom his lord, when he comes, shall find so doing. Amen I say to you, that he will set him over all his goods. But if that evil servant says in his heart, "My lord is delayed in coming," and begins to strike his fellow servants, and eats and drinks with drunkards, the lord of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him off <note>original: "dividet eum," literally "divide him," implying a severe punishment or execution</note> and place his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

<margin>LXXI</margin>
## Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins, who taking their lamps went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride. But five of them were foolish, and five were prudent. But the five foolish ones, having taken their lamps, took no oil with them. But the prudent ones took oil in their vessels with the lamps. Now while the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and slept. But at midnight a cry was made: "Behold, the bridegroom comes; go out to meet him." Then all those virgins rose up and trimmed their lamps. But the foolish said to the wise: "Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out." The prudent answered, saying: "Lest perhaps there be not enough for us and for you, go rather to those who sell and buy for yourselves." But while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came; and those who were ready entered with him to the wedding, and the door was shut. At last the other virgins also came, saying: "Lord, Lord, open to us." But he answering said: "Amen I say to you, I do not know you." Watch, therefore, because you know neither the day nor the hour.

<margin>X</margin>
**For it is as a man going abroad** who called his servants and handed over his goods to them. And to one he gave five talents <term>talent: a very large unit of currency, equivalent to about 6,000 denarii or 20 years of labor for a common worker</term>, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and immediately he set out. He who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and gained another five. Similarly, he who had received two gained another two. But he who had received one went and dug in the earth and hid his lord's money. Now after a long time, the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with them. And he who had received the five talents approached and offered another five talents, saying: "Lord, you delivered five talents to me; behold, I have gained five more on top of them." His lord said to him: "Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your lord." And he who had received two talents also approached and said: "Lord, you delivered two talents to me; behold, I have gained another two." His lord said to him: "Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your lord." But he who had received the one talent approached and said: "Lord, I know that you are a hard man; you reap where you did not sow and gather where you did not scatter. And being afraid, I went and hid your talent in the earth; behold, you have what is yours." But his lord answering said to him: "Wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I have not scattered. Therefore, you ought to have put my money with the bankers, and at my coming I would surely have received what is mine with interest. Take, therefore, the talent from him and give it to him who has ten talents. For to everyone who has, more will be given and he will abound; but from him who has not, even what he seems to have will be taken away. And cast the useless servant into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth." But when the Son of Man comes in his majesty, and all the angels with him, then he will sit upon the throne of his majesty. And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them one from another, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will place the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on his left. Then the King will say to those who will be on his right: "Come, you blessed of my Father, possess the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger and you took me in; naked and you clothed me; sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me." Then the righteous will answer him, saying: "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? When did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you? Or when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?" And the King answering will say to them: "Amen I say to you, as long as you did it for one of these, my least brothers, you did it for me." Then he will also say to those who will be on his left: "Depart from me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you did not give me to eat; I was thirsty and you did not give me to drink; I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me." Then they will also answer, saying: "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not minister to you?" Then he will answer them, saying: "Amen I say to you, as long as you did not do it for one of these least ones, you did it not to me." And these will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

**O**n the first day of Unleavened Bread <note>The Jewish festival of Passover, where no leavened bread is eaten</note>, the disciples came to Jesus, saying: "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?" And Jesus said: "Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: 'The Master says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples.'" And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover. Now when evening had come, he sat down with his twelve disciples. And as they were eating, he said: "Truly I say to you, that one of you is going to betray me." And being deeply saddened, they each began to say: "Is it I, Lord?" But he answering said: "He who dips his hand with me in the dish <note>term: parapside; a communal bowl used for dipping bread</note>, he will betray me. And he came to his disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter: "So, could you not watch with me for one hour? Watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." Again he went away a second time and prayed, saying: "My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, Your will be done." And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words. Then he came to his disciples and said to them: "Sleep now and take your rest. Behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us go; behold, he who betrays me is at hand." And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs, <margin>Betrayal</margin> sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people. In that hour, Jesus said to the crowds: "Have you come out as if against a thief with swords and clubs to capture me? Daily I sat among you teaching in the temple, and you did not hold me. But all this has happened so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples, leaving him, fled. But they, holding Jesus, led him to Caiaphas the high priest, <margin>Caiaphas</margin> where the scribes and elders had gathered. But Peter followed him from a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest; and going inside, he sat with the attendants to see the end. Now the chief priests and the whole council sought false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death; and they found none, though many false witnesses had come forward. And the high priest, rising, said to him: "Do you answer nothing to the things these men testify against you?" But Jesus remained silent. Then they spat in his face and struck him with fists; others gave him blows to the face with their palms, saying: "Prophesy to us, O Christ, who is it that struck you?" But Peter <margin>Peter</margin> was sitting outside in the courtyard. And a servant girl came to him, saying: "You also were with Jesus the Galilean." But he denied it before everyone, saying: "I do not know what you are talking about." Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death. And they led him away bound and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor. Then Judas, who betrayed him, seeing that he was condemned, moved by repentance, brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying: "I have sinned by betraying innocent blood." But they said: "What is that to us? You see to it." And throwing down the pieces of silver in the temple, he withdrew, and going away, he hanged himself with a noose. But the chief priests, taking the silver pieces, said: "It is not lawful to put them into the treasury <note>term: corbanan; the sacred treasury of the Temple</note>, because it is the price of blood." And having taken counsel, they bought with them the potter's field for the burial of foreigners. For this reason, that field has been called *Akeldama*, that is, the Field of Blood, to this very day. Then was fulfilled what was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying: *And they took thirty silver pieces, the price of the one who was appraised, whom they appraised from the children of Israel, and gave...*

<column-break/>

...them more for the marks of his conscience unto death. <gloss>Alas, wild souls! And they are hardened.</gloss> <note>original: "Heu feras animas. Et indurant." This gloss likely comments on the hard-heartedness of the priests compared to Judas's regret.</note> And they summoned her <note>likely referring to the soul or the crowd</note> from the chief priests, and being bereaved, they answer nothing. Then Pilate said to them: "Do you not hear how many testimonies they speak against you?" And he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor wondered greatly. Now on the feast day, the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner whom they wanted. He had at that time a notorious prisoner who was called Barabbas. Therefore, when they were gathered, Pilate said: "Whom do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?" For he knew that they had delivered him out of envy. While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying: "Have nothing to do with that just man; for I have suffered many things in a vision today because of him." But the chief priests and elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas, and to destroy Jesus. But the governor answering said to them: "Which of the two do you want to be released to you?" And they said: "Barabbas." Pilate said to them: "What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?" They all said: "Let him be crucified." Pilate said to them: "Why, what evil has he done?" But they cried out all the more, saying: "Let him be crucified." Then Pilate, seeing that he was accomplishing nothing but rather that a riot was starting, took water and washed his hands before the people, saying: "I am innocent of the blood of this just man; you see to it." And the whole people answering said: "His blood be upon us and upon our children." Then he released Barabbas to them; but having scourged Jesus, he delivered him to them to be crucified. Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus into the praetorium <note>The governor's official residence or headquarters</note>, gathered the whole cohort around him. And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak around him; and weaving a crown of thorns, they placed it on his head, and a reed in his right hand. And kneeling before him, they mocked him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews." And spitting on him, they took the reed and struck his head. And after they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to be crucified. As they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene named Simon; they forced him to carry his cross. And they came to a place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull. And they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall; and when he had tasted it, he would not drink. But after they had crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: *They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots.* And sitting down, they watched him. And they placed over his head his cause written: THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS. Then two thieves were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left. And those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads and saying: "Aha! You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross." Similarly, the chief priests mocking him with the scribes and elders said: "He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusts in the Lord; let him deliver him now if he wants him; for he said: 'I am the Son of God.'" And the thieves who were crucified with him also reproached him with the same thing. Now from the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour. And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying: "Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?" <note>original: "hely hely lama sabachtani"</note> which is, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" And some of those standing there, hearing it, said: "This man is calling Elijah." And immediately one of them, running, took a sponge and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink. But the others said: "Wait, let us see if Elijah comes to save him." But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up his spirit. And behold, the veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom; and the earth shook, and the rocks were split, and the tombs were opened; and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep arose. And coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they came into the holy city and appeared to many. Now the centurion and those who were with him guarding Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that were happening, were very afraid, saying: "Truly this was the Son of God." And many women were there from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering to him; among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
**N**ow when evening was come, there came a certain rich man from Arimathea named Joseph, who himself was also a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered the body to be given. And Joseph, taking the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth and placed it in his own new tomb which he had cut in the rock; and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb and went away. Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb. The next day, which is the day after the Day of Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate, saying: "Sir, we remember that that deceiver said while he was still alive: 'After three days I will rise again.' Therefore, order the tomb to be guarded until the third day, lest his disciples come and steal him away and say to the people, 'He has risen from the dead,' and the last error will be worse than the first." Pilate said to them: "You have a guard; go, guard it as you know how." So they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone with the guards.
Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb. And behold, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and approaching, rolled back the stone and sat upon it. His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing like snow. And for fear of him, the guards were terrified and became like dead men. But the angel answering said to the women: "Do not be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord was laid. And going quickly, tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead. And behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him. Behold, I have foretold it to you." And they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to tell his disciples. And behold, Jesus met them, saying: "Greetings!" <note>original: "Auete" - Hail / Rejoice</note> But they approached and held his feet and adored him. Then Jesus said to them: "Do not be afraid. Go, tell my brothers to go into Galilee; there they will see me." When they had departed, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all that had happened. And gathering with the elders, having taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers, saying: "Say that his disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping. And if this is heard by the governor, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble." So they, taking the money, did as they were instructed; and this story has been spread among the Jews to this very day. But the eleven disciples went away into Galilee to the mountain where Jesus had directed them. And seeing him, they adored him; but some doubted. And Jesus, approaching, spoke to them, saying: "All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things whatever I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you all days, even to the end of the age." The Gospel according to Matthew ends.

# HERE BEGINS THE PREFACE ACCORDING TO MARK.

MARK, THE EVANGELIST of God, and the son of Peter in baptism, and a disciple in the divine word, acted as a priest in Israel, a Levite <note>The Levites were the tribe of Israel responsible for priestly duties</note> according to the flesh. Having been converted to the faith of Christ, he wrote his Gospel in Italy, showing in it what he owed to his own lineage and to Christ. For, establishing the start of his beginning with the voice of a prophetic outcry <note>Refers to the "voice crying in the wilderness" from Mark 1:3</note>, he showed the order of the Levitical election. This was so that by preaching the predestined John, the son of Zechariah, sent out by the voice of an announcing angel, he might show at the start of the Gospel preaching not only the Word made flesh, but also the body of the Lord animated by the word of the divine voice. Thus, whoever reads this might know to whom the beginning of the flesh in the Lord Jesus arriving, and the dwelling place of the flesh, should be acknowledged; and that through the voice of prophecy he might show in himself what had come into him. Finally, he is said to have cut off his own thumb <note>original: "ampuccasse sibi... pollicem"; this refers to a tradition that Mark was called "Colobodactylus" or "stump-fingered," either due to a natural defect or self-mutilation to avoid the priesthood</note> after accepting the faith, so that he might be considered unfit for the priesthood. Yet his predestined election, consenting to the faith, was so powerful that even so he did not lose in the work of the Word what he had previously earned by his lineage. For he was the Bishop of Alexandria. It is necessary to seek out his work in detail, to arrange the sayings of the Gospel in order, to recognize the discipline of the Law in himself, and to understand the divine nature in the flesh. We wish to acknowledge these things after they have been inspected, having the reward of encouragement; for it is God who plants and God who waters into one, but it is a pious faith that gives the increase, etc.

**And** it happened when Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered to Him, and He was near the sea. And one of the rulers of the synagogue came, named Jairus; and seeing Him, he fell at His feet. And he begged Him much, saying, "My daughter is at the point of death; come and lay Your hand upon her so that she may be made well and live." And He went with him, and a large crowd followed Him and pressed against Him. And there was a woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, and she had suffered much under many physicians and had spent all she had, and was no better but rather grew worse. When she heard about Jesus, she came up in the crowd behind Him and touched His garment. For she said, "If I touch even His garments, I shall be made well." And immediately the fountain of her blood dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of the plague. And immediately Jesus, knowing in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched My garments?" And His disciples said to Him, "You see the crowd pressing against You, and You say, 'Who touched Me?'" And He looked around to see her who had done this. But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened in her, came and fell down before Him and told Him the whole truth. And He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace and be healed of your plague."

# A XXX
<image-desc>A decorative red and blue circular initial 'A' next to the Roman numeral XXX.</image-desc>
**While** He was still speaking, people came to the ruler of the synagogue, saying, "Your daughter is dead; why trouble the Teacher any further?" But Jesus, having heard the word that was spoken, said to the ruler of the synagogue, "Do not fear, only believe." And He allowed no one to follow Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James. And they come to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and He sees a commotion, people weeping and wailing loudly. And having entered, He said to them, "Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The girl is not dead, but sleeping." And they laughed at Him. But He, having put them all out, took the father and mother of the girl and those who were with Him, and entered where the girl was lying. And taking her hand, He said to her, "<term>Talitha cumi</term>," <note>An Aramaic phrase preserved in the original Greek and Latin texts.</note> which is interpreted, "Little girl, I say to you, arise." And immediately the girl rose and began to walk, for she was twelve years old; and they were overcome with great amazement. And He strictly charged them that no one should know this, and told them to give her something to eat.

# XXXI
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'E' contains the Roman numeral XXXI.</image-desc>
**And** He went into His own country, and His disciples followed Him. And it happened on the Sabbath, He began to teach in the synagogue. And many hearing Him were astonished at His teaching, saying, "Where did this man get all these things? And what is the wisdom given to Him, and such miracles that are performed by His hands? Is this not the craftsman, the son of Mary, the brother of James and Joseph and Judas and Simon? And are not His sisters here with us?" And they took offense at Him. And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house." And He could do no miracle there, except that He healed a few sick people by laying His hands on them. And He wondered because of their unbelief. And He went about the villages in a circuit, teaching.

# XXXII
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'V' contains the Roman numeral XXXII.</image-desc>
**And** He called the twelve, and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over unclean spirits. And He commanded them to take nothing for the journey except a staff only—no bag, no bread, nor money in their belts—but to wear sandals and not put on two tunics. And He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you depart from that place. And whoever will not receive you nor hear you, when you depart from there, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them." And going out, they preached that people should repent. And they cast out many demons and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.

# XXXIII
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'A' contains the Roman numeral XXXIII.</image-desc>
**And** King Herod heard of it, for His name had become well known. And they were saying that John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and therefore miracles are at work in Him. Others said, "It is Elijah." And others said, "It is a prophet, like one of the prophets." When Herod heard this, he said, "The John whom I beheaded has risen from the dead." For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her. For John was saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife." Now Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but she could not. For Herod feared John, knowing him to be a just and holy man, and he protected him. And when he heard him, he did many things and heard him gladly. When an opportune day came—the birthday of Herod—he gave a banquet for his nobles and high officers and the leading men of Galilee. And when the daughter of Herodias herself had entered and danced, and pleased Herod and those who reclined at the table with him, the king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you." And he swore to her, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom." When she went out, she said to her mother, "What shall I ask?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptist." And having immediately entered with haste to the king, she asked, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist." And the king was deeply grieved; because of his oaths and because of those reclining with him, he did not want to refuse her. And immediately having sent an executioner, he commanded that his head be brought on a platter. And he beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother. When his disciples heard of it, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.

# XXXIIII
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'E' contains the Roman numeral XXXIIII.</image-desc>
**And** the apostles gathered to Jesus and told Him all they had done and taught. And He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little." For there were many coming and going, and they had no time even to eat. And climbing into the boat, they went away to a deserted place by themselves. And they saw them departing, and many recognized them, and they ran there on foot from all the cities and arrived before them. And Jesus, going out, saw a large crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things. And when the hour was already late, His disciples came to Him, saying, "This is a deserted place, and the hour is already late;

<column-break/>

send them away so that going into the nearby villas and villages they may buy themselves food to eat." But He answered and said to them, "You give them something to eat." And they said to Him, "Shall we go and buy two hundred <term>denarii</term> <note>A denarius was a standard silver coin, roughly a day's wage for a laborer.</note> worth of bread and give it to them to eat?" And He says to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they found out, they say to Him, "Five loaves and two fish." And He commanded them to make everyone sit down by groups on the green grass. And they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties. And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven, He blessed and broke the loaves and gave them to His disciples to set before them; and He divided the two fish among them all. And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up the remains of the fragments, twelve baskets full, and also of the fish. Now those who had eaten were five thousand men.

# XXXV
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'E' contains the Roman numeral XXXV.</image-desc>
**And** immediately He compelled His disciples to get into the boat to go before Him across the water to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the people. And when He had dismissed them, He went onto the mountain to pray. When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land. And seeing them straining at the oars—for the wind was against them—about the fourth watch of the night He came to them walking on the sea, and He intended to pass by them. But when they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost <note>original: "fantasma"</note> and cried out. For they all saw Him and were troubled. And immediately He spoke with them and said to them, "Take heart; it is I, do not be afraid." And He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. And they were greatly amazed within themselves, for they did not understand about the loaves; for their hearts were hardened.

<image-desc>A decorative red and blue circular initial 'V' next to the Roman numeral V.</image-desc>
**And** when they had crossed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and moored there. And when they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized Him. And running through that whole region, they began to carry about on mats those who were sick to wherever they heard He was. And wherever He entered—into villages or villas or cities—they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched Him were made well.

# XXXVI
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'T' contains the Roman numeral XXXVI.</image-desc>
**Then** the Pharisees and some of the scribes coming from Jerusalem gathered to Him. And when they saw some of His disciples eating bread with common hands—that is, unwashed—they found fault. For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands frequently, holding to the traditions of the elders; and returning from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash; and there are many other things which have been handed down to them to keep: the washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and couches. And the Pharisees and scribes asked Him, "Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with common hands?" But He answering said to them, "Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.' For leaving the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men: the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other such things you do." And He said to them, "You have a fine way of rejecting the commandment of God so that you may keep your own tradition. For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and 'He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him die the death.' But you say, 'If a man says to his father or mother, "Whatever profit you might have had from me is <term>Corban</term>,"' <note>original: "corban q̄d est donum" — Corban is a Hebrew word meaning a gift dedicated to God.</note>—and you no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother, making void the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down; and many such things you do." And calling the crowd again, He said to them, "Hear me, all of you, and understand: There is nothing outside a man that, entering into him, can defile him; but the things which come out of a man are those that defile a man. If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear." And when He had entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. And He says to them, "Are you also so without understanding? Do you not understand that everything from outside entering into a man cannot defile him, because it does not enter into his heart but goes into his stomach and passes out into the latrine, thus purifying all foods?" But He was saying that the things which come out of a man are what defile a man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lewdness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. All these evil things proceed from within and defile a man.

# XXXVII
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'E' contains the Roman numeral XXXVII.</image-desc>
**And** rising from there He went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. And entering a house, He wanted no one to know, but He could not be hidden. For immediately a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him and entered and fell at His feet. Now the woman was a Gentile, a Syrophoenician by race. And she begged Him to cast the demon out of her daughter. But He said to her, "Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs." But she answered and said to Him, "Yes, Lord; for even the little dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs." And He said to her, "For this saying, go your way; the demon has gone out of your daughter." And when she had gone to her house, she found the girl lying on the bed and the demon gone out.

# XXXVIII
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'I' contains the Roman numeral XXXVIII.</image-desc>
**And** again departing from the borders of Tyre, He came by way of Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis. And they bring to Him one who was deaf and mute, and they begged Him to lay His hand on him. And taking him aside from the crowd, He put His fingers into his ears, and spitting, He touched his tongue; and looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, "<term>Effeta</term>," <note>original: "Effeta" — an Aramaic word meaning "Be opened."</note> which is, "Be opened." And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plainly. And He commanded them that they should tell no one; but the more He commanded them, so much the more they proclaimed it, and they were astonished beyond measure, saying, "He has done all things well; He makes both the deaf to hear and the mute to speak."

<image-desc>A decorative red and blue circular initial next to the Roman numeral XXX VIIII.</image-desc>
**In** those days, when there was again a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, having called His disciples together, He says to them, "I have compassion on the crowd, because behold, they have now remained with me three days and have nothing to eat; and if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away." And His disciples answered Him, "How can anyone satisfy these people with bread here in the wilderness?" And He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven." And He commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves and giving thanks, He broke them and gave them to His disciples to set before them, and they set them before the crowd. They also had a few small fish; and He blessed them and commanded them to be set before them also. So they ate and were satisfied. And they took up seven large baskets of the fragments that were left. Now those who had eaten were about four thousand; and He sent them away.

# XL I
<image-desc>A large decorative red and blue circular initial 'E' contains the Roman numeral XL I.</image-desc>
**And** immediately getting into the boat with His disciples, He came into the region of Dalmanutha. And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, testing Him. And sighing deeply in His spirit, He says, "Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign shall be given to this generation." And leaving them, He got into the boat again and departed to the other side.

<summary>This page covers a large section of Mark's Gospel, including the raising of Jairus' daughter, the death of John the Baptist, the feeding of both the five thousand and the four thousand, and Jesus walking on water. It highlights Jesus' miracles and his disputes with the Pharisees over tradition and ritual purity.</summary>

<margin>XL VIII</margin>
At the crossing: and they had forgotten to take bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the boat. And He commanded them, saying: "Watch and beware of the **leaven** <note>original: 'fermento'; leaven or yeast is used here as a metaphor for the pervasive and corrupting influence of teaching or hypocrisy.</note> of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod." And they reasoned among themselves, saying: "It is because we have no bread." Knowing this, Jesus said to them: "Why do you reason because you have no bread? Do you not yet know or understand? Is your heart still blinded? Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? Do you not remember when I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, and how many <term>cophinoi</term> <note>original: 'coffinos'; a type of small sturdy wicker basket used by Jews.</note> of fragments you took up?" They said to Him: "Twelve." "And when the seven loaves were among the four thousand, how many <term>spyridas</term> <note>original: 'sportas'; a larger type of flexible hamper or grain basket.</note> of fragments did you carry away?" And they said to Him: "Seven." And He said to them: "How is it that you do not yet understand?"

And they came to Bethsaida. And they brought a blind man to Him and begged Him to touch him. And taking the hand of the blind man, He led him out of the village. And spitting into his eyes, laying His hands on him, He asked him if he saw anything. And looking up, he said: "I see men as if they were trees walking." Then again He laid His hands upon his eyes, and he began to see. And he was restored, so that he saw everything clearly. And He sent him to his house, saying: "Go to your house, and if you enter the village, tell no one."

<margin>XL VIIII</margin>
And Jesus and His disciples went out into the towns of Caesarea Philippi. And on the way, He asked His disciples, saying to them: "Who do men say that I am?" And they answered Him, saying: "**John the Baptist**; others say **Elijah**; but others, as if one of the prophets." Then Jesus said to them: "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answering said to Him: "You are the **Christ**." <note>original: 'xps' (Christus); the Anointed One or Messiah.</note> And He strictly warned them not to tell anyone about Him. And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again. And He spoke the word openly. And Peter, taking Him aside, began to rebuke Him. But He, turning around and seeing His disciples, rebuked Peter, saying: "Get behind me, Satan! For you do not savor the things that are of God, but the things that are of men."

<margin>L</margin>
And calling the crowd with His disciples, He said to them: "If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and the gospel’s will save it. For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world and suffers the loss of his soul? Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul? For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels." And He said to them: "Amen I say to you, that there are some of those standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God coming in power."

<margin>L I</margin>
And after six days, Jesus took Peter and James and John, and led them up onto a high mountain apart by themselves. And He was **transfigured** before them. And His garments became shining, exceedingly white like snow, such as no **fuller** <note>original: 'fullo'; a person whose trade was to wash and whiten cloth.</note> on earth can whiten. And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus. And Peter answering said to Jesus: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." For he did not know what he was saying, for they were terrified with fear. And a cloud came overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud, saying: "This is my most beloved Son; listen to Him." And suddenly, looking around, they saw no one anymore, except Jesus alone with them. And as they were coming down from the mountain, He commanded them not to tell anyone what they had seen, until the Son of Man had risen from the dead. And they kept the word to themselves, questioning

<margin>L II</margin>
what it might mean, "when He had risen from the dead." And they asked Him, saying: "Why then do the scribes and Pharisees say that Elijah must come first?" Answering, He said to them: "Elijah, when he comes, will restore all things; and how it is written of the Son of Man that He must suffer many things and be treated with contempt. But I say to you, that Elijah has also come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him."

<margin>L III</margin>
And coming to His disciples, He saw a great crowd around them, and the scribes questioning them. And immediately all the people, seeing Jesus, were amazed; and running to Him, they greeted Him. And He asked them: "What are you questioning among yourselves?" And one from the crowd answering, said: "Master, I brought to You my son who has a mute spirit. And wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. And I spoke to Your disciples that they might cast it out, and they could not." Answering them, He said: "O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him to me." And they brought him. And when he saw Him, immediately the spirit troubled him, and being thrown to the ground, he rolled about foaming. And He asked his father: "How much time is it since this happened to him?" And he said: "From infancy. And it has frequently cast him into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if You can do anything, help us, having mercy on us." Jesus said to him: "If you can believe, all things are possible to the one who believes." And immediately the father of the boy, crying out with tears, said: "I believe, Lord; help my unbelief." And when Jesus saw the crowd running together, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: "Deaf and mute spirit, I command you, come out of him and enter him no more." And crying out and greatly tearing him, it went out of him. And he became as one dead, so that many said, "He is dead." But Jesus, taking his hand, lifted him up, and he arose. And when He had entered the house, His disciples asked Him privately: "Why could we not cast it out?" And He said to them: "This kind can come out by nothing but prayer and fasting."

<margin>L IIII</margin>
And departing from there, they went through Galilee, and He did not want anyone to know. For He was teaching His disciples and saying to them: "The Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of sinful men, and they will kill Him, and having been killed, on the third day He will rise." But they did not understand the word and were afraid to ask Him. And they came to Capernaum. When they were in the house, He asked them: "What were you discussing on the way?" But they were silent. For indeed, on the way they had disputed among themselves who was the greatest of them. And sitting down, He called the twelve and said to them: "If anyone wants to be first, he shall be the last of all and the servant of all." And taking a child, He set him in their midst; and when He had embraced him, He said to them: "Whoever receives one of such children in my name, receives me. And whoever receives me, receives not me, but Him who sent me." **John** answering Him, said: "Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we forbade him because he does not follow us." But Jesus said: "Do not forbid him. For there is no one who does a miracle in my name and can quickly speak evil of me. For he who is not against us is for us. For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name because you are Christ’s, amen I say to you, he will not lose

<column-break/>

his reward. And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a millstone <note>original: 'mola asinaria'; literally a millstone turned by a donkey, signifying a very large, heavy stone.</note> were hung around his neck and he were cast into the sea."

<margin>L V</margin>
"And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life crippled than having two hands to go into **Gehenna** <note>original: 'gehennam'; a valley near Jerusalem used as a metaphor for a place of eternal punishment/hell.</note>, into the unquenchable fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished. And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into eternal life lame than having two feet to be cast into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished. And if your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire, where their worm does not die and the fire is not extinguished. For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt."

<margin>L VI</margin>
"Salt is good. But if the salt becomes flavorless, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace among yourselves."

<margin>L VII</margin>
And rising up from there, He came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan. And crowds gathered to Him again, and as He was accustomed, He taught them again. And the Pharisees approaching asked Him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"—testing Him. But He answering, said to them: "What did Moses command you?" And they said: "Moses permitted a written notice of dismissal to be written and to divorce her." Answering them, Jesus said: "Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote this precept for you. But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female. For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and shall cleave to his wife, and the two shall be one flesh. Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined, let no man separate." And in the house His disciples asked Him again about this matter. And He said to them: "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her. And if a wife divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."

<margin>L VIII</margin>
And they offered little children to Him so that He might touch them. But the disciples rebuked those who offered them. When Jesus saw this, He took it indignantly and said to them: "Let the little children come to me, and do not forbid them; for of such is the kingdom of God. Amen I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it." And embracing them and laying His hands upon them, He blessed them.

<margin>L VIIII</margin>
And when He had gone out onto the way, a certain man running up and kneeling before Him, asked Him, saying: "Good Master, what shall I do that I may receive eternal life?" But Jesus said: "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God. You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not kill. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother." But he answering, said to Him: "Master, all these I have observed from my youth." But Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him: "One thing is lacking to you. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me." But he, saddened by this word, went away grieving, for he had many possessions. And looking around, Jesus said to His disciples: "How difficult it will be for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!" And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus answering again, said to them: "Children, how difficult it is for those trusting in riches to enter the kingdom of God. It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God." They were even more astonished among themselves, saying: "And who can be saved?" And looking at them, Jesus said: "With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."

<margin>L X</margin>
And Peter began to say to Him: "Behold, we have left all things and followed You." Answering, Jesus said: "Amen I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or lands for my sake and the gospel’s, who shall not receive a hundred times as much now in this time—houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and lands, with persecutions—and in the world to come, eternal life. But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

<margin>L XI</margin>
And they were on the way going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was preceding them. And they were amazed, and those who followed Him were afraid. And taking the twelve again, He began to tell them the things that were to come: "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be betrayed to the chief priests and the scribes and the elders, and they will condemn Him to death and deliver Him to the Gentiles; and they will mock Him and spit on Him and scourge Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise."

<margin>L XII</margin>
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approached Him, saying: "Master, we want You to do for us whatever we ask." And He said to them: "What do you want me to do for you?" And they said: "Grant to us that we may sit, one at Your right hand and one at Your left hand, in Your glory." But Jesus said to them: "You do not know what you ask. Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink, or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?" And they said to Him: "We can." But Jesus said to them: "You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized, you shall be baptized. But to sit at my right hand or left is not mine to give to you, but for whom it is prepared." And when the ten heard this, they began to be indignant toward James and John.

<margin>L XIII</margin>
But Jesus calling them, said to them: "You know that those who are seen as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their princes have power over them. It is not so among you; but whoever wishes to be greater shall be your servant. And whoever wishes to be first among you shall be the servant of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many."

<margin>L XIIII</margin>
And they came to Jericho. And as He was departing from Jericho with His disciples and a very great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus the blind man, sat by the way begging. When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out and say: "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" And many rebuked him so that he would be silent. But he cried out all the more: "Son of David, have mercy on me!" And Jesus, standing still, ordered him to be called. And they called the blind man, saying to him: "Be of better heart! Rise, He calls you." And throwing off his garment, leaping up, he came to Him. Answering him, Jesus said: "What do you want me to do for you?"

<margin>L XV</margin>
And the blind man said to Him: "**Rabboni** <note>original: 'Rabboni'; a title of great respect for a teacher, meaning 'my master' or 'my great teacher'.</note>, that I may see."
