Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men from every nation under heaven. When this sound was heard, the multitude came together and was confused in mind, because each one heard them speaking in his own language. They were all amazed and wondered, saying: "Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans? And how is it that we hear, each of us, our own native language in which we were born? Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those who inhabit Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and visitors from Rome, both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in our own tongues the mighty works of God." And they were all amazed and wondered, saying to one another: "What does this mean?" But others, mocking, said: "They are full of new wine" <note>original: "musto pleni"; must is the freshly pressed juice of grapes that has not yet fully fermented into wine</note>.

But Peter, standing with the eleven, lifted up his voice and spoke to them: "Men of Judea and all you who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen to my words. For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is only the third hour of the day <note>about 9:00 AM</note>. But this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel: 'And it shall come to pass in the last days, says the Lord, I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams. And indeed, upon my servants and upon my handmaids in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy. And I will show wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes. And it shall be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.' Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God among you by miracles and wonders and signs which God did through him in your midst, as you yourselves know—this man, delivered up by the set plan and foreknowledge of God, you have crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men. But God raised him up, having loosed the sorrows of hell <note>original: "inferni"; referring here to the realm of the dead</note>, because it was impossible for him to be held by it. For David says concerning him: 'I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is at my right hand, that I may not be moved. Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; moreover, my flesh also will rest in hope. For you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you allow your Holy One to see corruption. You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with joy with your countenance.' Brothers, let me speak freely to you about the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his tomb is with us to this day. Therefore, since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that of the fruit of his loins one would sit upon his throne, he, foreseeing this, spoke of the resurrection of Christ: that he was neither left in hell, nor did his flesh see corruption. This Jesus God raised up, of which we are all witnesses."

Being exalted, therefore, by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this which you see and hear. For David did not ascend into heaven, but he himself said: 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.' Therefore let all the house of Israel know most certainly that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ." Now when they heard these things, they were pierced to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles: "What shall we do, brothers?" But Peter said to them: "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of your sins; and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. For the promise is for you and for your children, and for all who are far off, whomever the Lord our God shall call." And with many other words he testified and exhorted them, saying: "Save yourselves from this crooked generation." Those, therefore, who received his word were baptized: and about three thousand souls were added that day. And they were persevering in the doctrine of the apostles, and in the communication of the breaking of bread, and in prayers. And fear came upon every soul: many wonders also and signs were done through the apostles in Jerusalem, and there was great fear in all. And all who believed were together and had all things in common. They sold their possessions and goods and divided them among all, as anyone had need. And daily, attending the temple with one accord and breaking bread in their houses, they took their food with gladness and simplicity of heart, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added daily to their number those who were being saved.

Now Peter and John were going up to the temple at the ninth hour of prayer <note>about 3:00 PM</note>. And a certain man who was lame from his mother's womb was being carried, whom they placed daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, so that he might ask for alms from those entering the temple. When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms. But Peter, looking intently at him with John, said: "Look at us." And he fixed his attention on them, hoping to receive something from them. But Peter said: "Silver and gold I have none; but what I have, I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk." And taking him by the right hand, he lifted him up. And immediately his feet and ankles were strengthened. And leaping up, he stood and walked, and entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God. And all the people saw him walking and praising God. And they recognized him as the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple: and they were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him.

While he held Peter and John, all the people ran together to them at the portico called Solomon’s, in astonishment. Seeing this, Peter answered the people: "Men of Israel, why do you wonder at this, or why do you look at us as if by our own power or holiness we had made this man walk? The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his servant Jesus, whom you indeed delivered up and denied before the face of Pilate, when he had judged that he should be released. But you denied the Holy and Just One, and asked for a murderer to be granted to you; but the Author of life you killed, whom God raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses. And by faith in his name, his name has strengthened this man whom you see and know: and the faith which is through him has given this complete healing in the sight of you all. And now, brothers, I know that you did it through ignorance, as did your rulers. But God has thus fulfilled what he announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer. Repent, therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, so that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and he may send Jesus Christ, who was preached to you, whom heaven indeed must receive until the times of the restoration of all things, which God has spoken through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old. Moses indeed said: 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; you shall listen to him in all things, whatever he shall speak to you. And it shall be that every soul who will not listen to that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people.' And all the prophets from Samuel and those who followed, as many as have spoken, have announced these days. You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham: 'And in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.' To you first, God, raising up his Son, sent him to bless you, that everyone should turn away from his wickedness."

While they were speaking to the people, the priests and the officer of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them, being grieved that they were teaching the people and announcing in Jesus the resurrection from the dead. And they laid hands on them and put them in custody until the next day; for it was already evening. But many of those who had heard the word believed; and the number of the men became five thousand. And it came to pass the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem; and Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the priestly lineage. And setting them in the midst, they questioned them: "By what power or in what name have you done this?" Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: "Rulers of the people and elders, listen. If we are judged today for a good deed done to an infirm man, by what means he has been made well: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by him this man stands before you whole."

<column-break/>

"This is the stone which was rejected by you builders, which has become the head of the corner. And there is salvation in no other. For there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."

Now when they saw the constancy of Peter and John, and understood that they were illiterate and ignorant men <note>original: "idiote"; in this context, it means laypeople without formal rabbinic training</note>, they wondered; and they recognized them, that they had been with Jesus. And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say in contradiction. But they ordered them to go outside the council, and they conferred among themselves, saying: "What shall we do to these men? For indeed a notable sign has been done through them; it is manifest to all who dwell in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it. But that it may be spread no further among the people, let us threaten them that they speak henceforth to no man in this name." And calling them, they charged them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. But Peter and John, answering, said to them: "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard." But they, threatening them, let them go, finding no way to punish them because of the people; for all were glorifying God for that which had been done. For the man on whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old.

When they were released, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them. When they heard this, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord and said: "Lord, you are he who made heaven and earth and the sea and all that is in them. Who, by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of our father David, your servant, said: 'Why did the Gentiles rage, and the people meditate on vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers gathered together as one against the Lord and against his Christ.' For truly in this city there gathered together against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, to do what your hand and your counsel had decreed to be done. And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to your servants that with all boldness they may speak your word, while you stretch out your hand for healings and signs and wonders to be done through the name of your holy Son Jesus." And when they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.

And the multitude of believers had one heart and one soul; nor did anyone say that any of the things he possessed was his own, but they had all things in common. And with great power the apostles gave testimony of the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord: and great grace was upon them all. For there was no one needy among them. For as many as were owners of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things they sold, and laid them at the apostles' feet. And distribution was made to each one as he had need. And Joseph, who was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles (which is translated 'Son of Consolation'), a Levite, a Cypriot by birth, having land, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.

But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a field and kept back part of the price of the field, his wife also being aware of it. And bringing a certain part, he laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said: "Ananias, why has Satan tempted your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back part of the price of the field? While it remained, did it not remain your own? and after it was sold, was it not in your power? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God." And Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard it. And the young men rising up removed him and, carrying him out, buried him. And it happened about three hours later that his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in. Peter said to her: "Tell me, did you sell the field for so much?" And she said: "Yes, for so much." But Peter said to her: "Why have you agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they shall carry you out." Immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last. And the young men coming in found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her by her husband. And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.

And by the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all with one accord in Solomon’s portico. But of the rest, no one dared to join them, yet the people magnified them. And the multitude of men and women believing in the Lord increased more and more, so that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, so that at least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them, and they might be delivered from their infirmities. There also gathered a multitude from the neighboring cities to Jerusalem, bringing sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.

But the high priest rose up, and all who were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with jealousy, and laid hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison. But an angel of the Lord by night opened the doors of the prison and, leading them out, said: "Go, and standing in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life." When they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and taught. But the high priest came, and those who were with him, and called the council together and all the elders of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought. But when the officers came and did not find them in the prison, they returned and reported, saying: "We found the prison indeed shut with all diligence, and the guards standing at the doors; but when we opened it, we found no one inside." Now when the officer of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were uncertain about them, what this would come to. But someone came and told them: "Behold, the men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people." Then the officer went with the ministers and brought them, but not with violence; for they feared the people, lest they should be stoned. And when they had brought them, they set them before the council. And the high priest questioned them, saying: "We strictly commanded you that you should not teach in this name; and behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and you wish to bring the blood of this man upon us." But Peter and the apostles answering said: "We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree. Him God has exalted with his right hand as Prince and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and remission of sins. And we are witnesses of these words, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to all who obey him." When they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and they intended to kill them.

But a certain Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, rising up, commanded the men to be put outside for a little while. And he said to them: "Men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what you intend to do regarding these men. For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined him; he was killed, and all who believed in him were scattered and brought to nothing. After him, Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away the people after him; he also perished, and all as many as obeyed him were dispersed. And now therefore I say to you: refrain from these men and let them alone; for if this counsel or this work is of men, it will be dissolved; but if it is of God, you will not be able to dissolve it; lest perhaps you be found even to fight against God." And they agreed with him. And calling the apostles, after they had beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak at all in the name of Jesus, and they let them go. They went, therefore, rejoicing...

<meta>This page continues from the previous account of the early Church in Jerusalem following Pentecost. It transitions from general exhortations on the Christian life into the historical narrative of the first martyr, Stephen, the mission to Samaria, and the dramatic conversion of Saul of Tarsus.</meta>

Know, then, that you were made in the image of God, just as the apostle says: "The image of God is within you." <note>original: "Ymago dei in uobis est."</note> Know that it is no honor to you if you lose your angelic dignity through your sins. 2.

It profits you nothing to be the image of God if you are not like Him who created you in that likeness. For just as a painted wall, if it is defiled with mud, is no longer called the image of a king but is called mud; so also your soul, if it is stained with sins, is not called the image of God but is called sin. Therefore, be watchful, my brothers, so that you may be pure in heart, for they shall see God. Be watchful, so that you may be full of the Holy Spirit, for He will teach you all truth. Be watchful, so that you may be full of charity, for charity covers a multitude of sins. Be watchful, so that you may be full of humility, for God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. Be watchful, so that you may be full of patience, for in your patience you will possess your souls. Be watchful, so that you may be full of mercy, for mercy triumphs over judgment. Be watchful, so that you may be full of faith, for without faith it is impossible to please God. Be watchful, so that you may be full of hope, for hope does not disappoint. Be watchful, so that you may be full of the fear of God, for the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. 3.

But there arose certain men from the synagogue which is called that of the Freedmen, <note>original: "libertinorum"; these were likely former slaves or their descendants who had been granted Roman citizenship.</note> and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of those who were from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen. And they could not resist the wisdom and the Spirit that spoke through him. Then they suborned men to say they had heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moses and against God. And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes; and running together, they seized him and brought him into the council. And they set up false witnesses, saying: "This man does not cease to speak words against the holy place and the law; for we have heard him saying that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and will change the traditions which Moses delivered to us." And all those who sat in the council, looking intently at him, saw his face as if it were the face of an angel. Then the high priest said to Stephen: "Are these things so?" 4.

And he said: "Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran, and said to him: 'Go out from your land and from your kindred, and come into the land which I shall show you.' Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and dwelt in Haran. And from there, after his father was dead, He moved him into this land in which you now dwell. And He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's breadth; but He promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after him, even though he had no son. And God spoke to him in this way: that his offspring would be sojourners in a foreign land, and that they would be brought into bondage and treated badly for four hundred years. 'And the nation to which they are in bondage I will judge,' says the Lord, 'and after these things they shall come out and serve me in this place.' And He gave him the covenant of circumcision. And so he begot Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day; and Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs. And the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt; but God was with him and rescued him from all his tribulations. And He gave him grace and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and appointed him governor over Egypt and over all his house. Now a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great tribulation, and our fathers found no food. But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers there the first time. And at the second time, Joseph was recognized by his brothers, and his family became known to Pharaoh. And Joseph sent and called for his father Jacob and all his kindred, seventy-five souls in all. And Jacob went down into Egypt, and he died, as did our fathers. And they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor, the son of Shechem. But as the time of the promise drew near, which God had confessed to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who did not know Joseph. This man, dealing craftily with our race, afflicted our fathers so that they would expose their infants, lest they should live. At which time Moses was born, and he was pleasing to God; and he was nourished for three months in his father's house. And when he was exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him as her own son. And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was mighty in his words and deeds. But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel. And when he saw one of them suffering wrong, he defended him and avenged him who was suffering the wrong by striking down the Egyptian. For he thought that his brothers would understand that God was giving them salvation by his hand, but they did not understand. And the following day he appeared to them as they were quarreling and tried to reconcile them in peace, saying: 'Men, you are brothers; why do you wrong one another?' But he who was doing the wrong to his neighbor pushed him away, saying: 'Who appointed you a prince or a judge over us? Do you want to kill me, just as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?' And Moses fled at this word and became a stranger in the land of Midian, where he begot two sons. And when forty years were completed, there appeared to him in the desert of Mount Sinai an angel in the flame of a burning bush. And Moses, seeing it, wondered at the vision. And as he drew near to consider it, the voice of the Lord came to him, saying: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob.' And Moses, trembling, did not dare to look. And the Lord said to him: 'Loose the sandals from your feet, for the place where you stand is holy ground. Seeing, I have seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt.' This Moses, whom they refused, saying: 'Who appointed you a prince or a judge?'—this man God sent to be a prince and a redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush. He led them out, performing signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the desert for forty years. This is the Moses who said to the children of Israel: 'God will raise up for you a prophet from your brothers, like myself; you shall listen to him.' This is he who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; he received living words to give to us. Our fathers would not obey him, but pushed him away, and in their hearts they turned back to Egypt, saying to Aaron: 'Make for us gods to go before us. For this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.' And they made a calf in those days and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands. But God turned away and gave them up to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you offer victims or sacrifices to me for forty years in the desert, O house of Israel? And you took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Rephan, figures which you made to worship them. And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.' Our fathers had the tabernacle of testimony in the desert, just as God directed when speaking to Moses, that he should make it according to the form he had seen. Which also our fathers, receiving it, brought in with Joshua <note>original: "ihesu"; in Latin and Greek, the name for Joshua and Jesus is the same.</note> into the possession of the nations, whom God drove out from the face of our fathers until the days of David, who found grace before God and asked that he might find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob. But Solomon built Him a house. Yet the Most High does not dwell in houses made by hands, as the prophet says: 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What house will you build for me, says the Lord? Or what is the place of my rest? Has not my hand made all these things?' You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you. Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who foretold the coming of the Just One, of whom you have now been the betrayers and murderers. You who received the law by the disposition of angels and have not kept it." 5.

Hearing these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed their teeth at him. But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looking up to heaven, saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God, and he said: "Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man 

<column-break/>

standing at the right hand of God." Then crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed upon him with one accord. And casting him out of the city, they stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man who was called Saul. And they stoned Stephen as he was calling upon God and saying: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit." And falling on his knees, he cried with a loud voice, saying: "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord. And Saul was consenting to his death. 6.

And on that day a great persecution arose against the church which was in Jerusalem, and they were all dispersed through the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles. Devout men buried Stephen and made great lamentation over him. But Saul was ravaging the church, entering houses and dragging out men and women, committing them to prison. Therefore those who were dispersed went about preaching the word of God. And Philip, going down to a city of Samaria, preached Christ to them. And the crowds with one accord gave heed to the things spoken by Philip, hearing him and seeing the signs which he did. For many of those who had unclean spirits, crying out with a loud voice, came out of them. And many who were paralyzed and lame were healed. And there was great joy in that city. 7.

But there was a certain man named Simon, who previously practiced magic in the city and amazed the people of Samaria, saying that he was someone great. To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying: "This man is the power of God, which is called Great." And they gave heed to him because for a long time he had dazed them with his sorceries. But when they believed Philip preaching the kingdom of God in the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself also believed, and being baptized, he stayed close to Philip. Seeing also the signs and great miracles that were done, he was amazed and wondered. Now when the apostles who were in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them. Who, when they had come, prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Spirit. For He had not yet come upon any of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit. 8.

And when Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money, saying: "Give me also this power, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit." <note>This attempt to buy spiritual power is the origin of the term "simony."</note> But Peter said to him: "May your money perish with you, because you thought the gift of God could be purchased with money. You have no part or lot in this matter, for your heart is not right before God. Repent, therefore, of this wickedness of yours, and pray to God if perhaps this thought of your heart may be forgiven you. For I see that you are in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity." Then Simon answered and said: "Pray for me to the Lord, that nothing of what you have said may come upon me." And they indeed, having testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel to many regions of the Samaritans. 9.

But an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying: "Arise and go toward the south, to the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza; this is a desert road." And he arose and went. And behold, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a powerful official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasures, had come to Jerusalem to worship. And he was returning, sitting in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah. Then the Spirit said to Philip: "Go near and join yourself to this chariot." And Philip, running up to him, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah and said: "Do you think you understand what you are reading?" And he said: "How can I, unless someone shows me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him. Now the place of the scripture which he was reading was this: "As a sheep he was led to the slaughter; and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who shall declare his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth." And the eunuch, answering Philip, said: "I beseech you, of whom does the prophet say this? Of himself, or of someone else?" Then Philip, opening his mouth and beginning from this scripture, preached Jesus to him. And as they went along the way, they came to some water. And the eunuch said: "Behold, here is water; what prevents me from being baptized?" And Philip said: "If you believe with all your heart, you may." And he answered and said: "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God." And he commanded the chariot to stand still; and they both went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him. And when they had come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more. And he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus; and passing through, he preached the gospel to all the cities until he came to Caesarea. 10.

But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any of this Way, men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem. And as he was journeying, it happened that he drew near to Damascus. And suddenly a light from heaven shone around him. And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" And he said: "Who are you, Lord?" And He said: "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. It is hard for you to kick against the goad." And trembling and astonished, he said: "Lord, what do you want me to do?" And the Lord said to him: "Arise and enter the city, and there it will be told to you what you must do." And the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one. Then Saul arose from the ground; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. But leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus. And he was there for three days without sight, and he neither ate nor drank. Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision: "Ananias." And he said: "Behold, here I am, Lord." And the Lord said to him: "Arise and go to the street which is called Straight, and look in the house of Judas for a man of Tarsus named Saul. For behold, he is praying." And he saw a man named Ananias coming in and laying his hands on him, so that he might receive his sight. But Ananias answered: "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints in Jerusalem. And here he has authority from the high priests to bind all who call upon your name." But the Lord said to him: "Go, for he is a chosen vessel to me, to carry my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel. For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name's sake." And Ananias went and entered the house; and laying his hands on him, he said: "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the way as you were coming, has sent me so that you may see and be filled with the Holy Spirit." And immediately there fell from his eyes something like scales, and he received his sight. And arising, he was baptized. And when he had taken food, he was strengthened. And he was with the disciples who were in Damascus for some days. And immediately he preached Jesus in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. And all who heard him were amazed and said: "Is not this he who ravaged those in Jerusalem who called upon this name? And did he not come here for this purpose, to lead them bound to the high priests?" But Saul grew much stronger and confounded the Jews who dwelt in Damascus, affirming that this is the Christ. And when many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him. But their plot became known to Saul. And they watched the gates day and night so that they might kill him. But the disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket. And when he had come to Jerusalem, he tried to join himself to the disciples. But they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple. But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and related to them how he had seen the Lord on the way, and that He had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had acted boldly in the name of Jesus. And he was with them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem, and acting boldly in the name of the Lord. He also spoke and disputed with the Greeks. But they sought to kill him. When the brothers knew this, they brought him down to Caesarea.

<meta>This page contains the text of the Acts of the Apostles, specifically chapters 13 through 15. It chronicles the beginning of the first missionary journey of Paul and Barnabas and the subsequent Council of Jerusalem.</meta>

Now there were in the church at Antioch certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon (who was called Niger), Lucius of Cyrene, Manahen <note>Manahen is described as the foster-brother of Herod the Tetrarch, the ruler who executed John the Baptist.</note>, and Saul. While they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." Then, after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus. When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the <term>synagogues</term> <note>A Jewish house of prayer and study.</note> of the Jews; and they had John as their assistant. When they had gone through the whole island as far as Paphos, they met a certain magician, a Jewish false prophet named Bar-Jesus, who was with the <term>proconsul</term> <note>A high-ranking Roman official governing a province.</note> Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. He summoned Barnabas and Saul and desired to hear the word of God. But Elymas the magician (for that is how his name is translated) opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him and said, "O man full of all deceit and all fraud, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop perverting the right ways of the Lord? And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you; you will be blind and unable to see the sun for a time." Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking someone to lead him by the hand. Then the proconsul, when he saw what had happened, believed, for he was astonished at the teaching of the Lord.

When Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia; but John <note>This is John Mark, the traditional author of the Gospel of Mark.</note> left them and returned to Jerusalem. But they went on from Perga and came to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day, they entered the synagogue and sat down. After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the officials of the synagogue sent word to them, saying, "Brothers, if you have any word of exhortation for the people, speak."

So Paul stood up, and motioning with his hand for silence, he said: "Men of Israel and you who fear God, listen. The God of this people Israel chose our ancestors and made the people great during their stay in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm he led them out of it. For about forty years he put up with their behavior in the wilderness. After destroying seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land as an inheritance for about four hundred and fifty years. After that, he gave them judges until the time of the prophet Samuel. Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, who reigned for forty years. When he had removed him, he raised up David as their king, of whom he testified: 'I have found David son of Jesse to be a man after my heart, who will carry out all my wishes.' From this man’s descendants God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised. Before his coming, John had already proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel. And as John was finishing his work, he said, 'Who do you suppose that I am? I am not he. No, but one is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thongs of the sandals on his feet.'

"Brothers, children of the family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us the message of this salvation has been sent. Because the residents of Jerusalem and their leaders did not recognize him or understand the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, they fulfilled those words by condemning him. Even though they found no cause for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him killed. When they had carried out everything that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb. But God raised him from the dead on the third day, and for many days he appeared to those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people. And we bring you the good news that what God promised to our ancestors he has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising Jesus; as also it is written in the second psalm: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you.' As for the fact that he raised him from the dead, no more to return to corruption, he has spoken in this way: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.' Therefore he also says in another psalm: 'You will not let your Holy One experience corruption.' For David, after he had served the purpose of God in his own generation, died, was laid beside his ancestors, and experienced corruption; but he whom God raised up did not experience corruption. Let it be known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you; by this Jesus everyone who believes is set free from all those sins from which you could not be freed by the law of Moses. Beware, therefore, that what the prophets said does not happen to you: 'Look, you scoffers! Be amazed and perish, for in your days I am doing a work, a work that you will never believe, even if someone tells you.'"

<column-break/>

As they were leaving, the people kept begging that these things might be told them the next Sabbath. When the meeting of the synagogue broke up, many Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.

The next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord. But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and blaspheming, they contradicted what was spoken by Paul. Then both Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly, saying, "It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken first to you. Since you reject it and judge yourselves to be unworthy of eternal life, we are now turning to the Gentiles <note>A term for non-Jewish people.</note>. For so the Lord has commanded us, saying, 'I have set you to be a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"

When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the word of the Lord; and as many as had been destined for eternal life became believers. Thus the word of the Lord spread throughout the region. But the Jews incited the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their region. So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium. And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

The same thing occurred in Iconium, where they entered the Jewish synagogue together and spoke in such a way that a great number of both Jews and Greeks became believers. But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers. So they remained for a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace by granting signs and wonders to be done through them. But the residents of the city were divided; some sided with the Jews, and some with the apostles. And when an attempt was made by both Gentiles and Jews, with their rulers, to mistreat them and to stone them, the apostles learned of it and fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and to the surrounding country; and there they continued proclaiming the good news.

In Lystra there was a man sitting who could not use his feet and had never walked, for he had been lame from birth. He listened to Paul as he was speaking. And Paul, looking at him intently and seeing that he had faith to be healed, said in a loud voice, "Stand upright on your feet." And the man sprang up and began to walk. When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us in human form!" Barnabas they called Jupiter <note>Original Latin: Iovem. The Roman king of the gods, identified with the Greek Zeus.</note>, and Paul they called Mercury <note>Original Latin: Hermen. The messenger god, identified with the Greek Hermes, because Paul was the chief speaker.</note>, because he was the chief speaker. The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was just outside the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates; he and the crowds wanted to offer sacrifice.

When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting, "Friends, why are you doing this? We are mortals just like you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them. In past generations he allowed all nations to follow their own ways; yet he has not left himself without a witness in doing good—giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, and filling you with food and your hearts with joy." Even with these words, they scarcely restrained the crowds from offering sacrifice to them.

But Jews came there from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. Then they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead. But when the disciples surrounded him, he got up and went into the city. The next day he went on with Barnabas to Derbe. After they had proclaimed the good news to that city and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, then on to Iconium and Antioch. There they strengthened the souls of the disciples and encouraged them to continue in the faith, saying, "It is through many persecutions that we must enter the kingdom of God." And after they had appointed elders for them in each church, with prayer and fasting they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had come to believe.

Then they passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia. When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia. From there they sailed back to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work that they had completed. When they arrived, they called the church together and related all that God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith for the Gentiles. And they stayed there with the disciples for some time.

Then certain individuals came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved." And after Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them, Paul and Barnabas and some of the others were appointed to go up to Jerusalem to discuss this question with the apostles and the elders. So they were sent on their way by the church, and as they passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, they reported the conversion of the Gentiles, and brought great joy to all the believers. When they came to Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all that God had done with them. But some believers who belonged to the sect of the Pharisees stood up and said, "It is necessary for them to be circumcised and ordered to keep the law of Moses."

The apostles and the elders met together to consider this matter. After there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them, "Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you, that I should be the one through whom the Gentiles would hear the message of the gospel and become believers. And God, who knows the human heart, testified to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us; and in cleansing their hearts by faith he has made no distinction between them and us. Now therefore why are you putting God to the test by placing on the neck of the disciples a yoke that neither our ancestors nor we have been able to bear? On the contrary, we believe that we will be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."

The whole assembly kept silence, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul as they told of all the signs and wonders that God had done through them among the Gentiles. After they finished speaking, James replied, "Brothers, listen to me. Simeon <note>Referring to the Apostle Peter.</note> has related how God first looked favorably on the Gentiles, to take from among them a people for his name. This agrees with the words of the prophets, as it is written: 'After this I will return, and I will rebuild the dwelling of David, which has fallen; from its ruins I will rebuild it, and I will set it up, so that all other peoples may seek the Lord— even all the Gentiles over whom my name has been called. Thus says the Lord, who has been making these things known from of old.' Therefore I have reached the decision that we should not trouble those Gentiles who are turning to God, but we should write to them to abstain only from things polluted by idols and from fornication and from whatever has been strangled and from blood. For in every city, for generations past, Moses has had those who proclaim him, for he has been read aloud every Sabbath in the synagogues."

<summary>This text recounts the first missionary journey of Paul and Barnabas through Cyprus and Asia Minor, ending with the Council of Jerusalem where the apostles decide that Gentile converts do not need to follow the full Mosaic Law.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the narrative of the Acts of the Apostles, specifically the events leading to Saint Paul's arrest in Jerusalem and his subsequent legal defense before Roman governors.</meta>

And they warned him: he wished to kill a certain power <note>original: "pōtē aliquē"; likely referring to the prophetic warning about Paul's arrest</note>: a certain Judean arrived: where it does not help to act: with the adversaries: and the Lord conquers. And they took Paul outside the temple: it was seen: and he went out. But these: the appearance. Where however it is of the man: there it is acted where it is said: and he was handed over into the hands of the Gentiles. But those who were there asked him not to go. In that place they did not want Paul to ascend: here they wish: and it is true: that they were going out. What are you doing weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound: but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. And when they could not persuade him: we were silent, saying: let the will of the Lord be done.

But after these days: we were prepared: and we ascended to Jerusalem. And the disciples from Caesarea came with us: bringing with them one with whom we might lodge, a certain Mnason <note>The OCR reads "iasone" (Jason), but the Biblical context identifies him as Mnason of Cyprus</note>, an old disciple. And when we had come to Jerusalem: the brothers received us joyfully. On the following day Paul went in with us to James: and all the elders assembled. When he had greeted them: Paul recounted one by one: the things which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry. When they had heard it: they magnified God: and said to him: you see, brother: how many thousands there are among the Jews who have believed: and they are all zealots for the law. But they have been informed about you: that you teach a falling away from Moses for the Gentiles: and he says you see: that they should not circumcise their sons: nor walk according to the custom. What then is it? Certainly: the multitude must assemble: for they will hear that you have come here. Do this therefore: which we tell you. We have four men: having a vow upon them. Taking these: and purify yourself with them: and pay for them: so that they may shave their heads. And all may know: that the things they heard about you: are false: but you yourself also walk keeping the law. For those of the Gentiles who have believed: they have nothing to say about it. For we have written judging: that they should keep themselves from idols: and blood: and things strangled: and fornication.

Then Paul, having taken the men the next day: being purified with them: entered into the temple: announcing the completion of the days of purification: until an offering should be offered for each one of them. And when the seven days were being completed: the Jews who were from Asia: saw him in the temple: they stirred up the whole crowd: and laid hands on him, crying out: men of Israel: help! This is the man: who is against the law: and this place: and teaches everyone everywhere: moreover he even brought Greeks into the temple: and violated: and defiled this holy place. For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him: whom they thought: that Paul had introduced into the temple. And the whole city was moved: and a running together of the people occurred. And having seized Paul: they dragged him outside the temple: and immediately the gates were shut. And while they were confused seeking to kill him: it was reported to the tribune <term>Tribunus</term> <note>A Roman military officer, usually in command of a cohort of about 1,000 men</note> of the cohort: that all Jerusalem was in confusion. Who immediately, having taken soldiers: and centurions: ran down to them. When they saw the tribune and the soldiers: they stopped beating Paul. And the tribune approaching: seized him: and ordered him to be bound with two chains: and asked who he was: and what he had done. In different voices: others were crying out in the crowd. And when he could not know the truth because of the tumult: he ordered him to be led into the barracks. And when he had come to the steps: it happened: that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the people: for the multitude followed, crying out: take him away! And as he was being led into the barracks: Paul said to the tribune. Is it permitted for me to speak to you? Who said: do you know Greek? Are you not that Egyptian: who before these days stirred up: and led out into the desert four thousand men of the assassins <note>original: "sicariorū", refering to the Sicarii, a Jewish rebel group</note>? Paul said: I am a Jewish man: from Tarsus in Cilicia: a citizen of no obscure city. I ask you therefore: permit me to speak to the people. And when he had permitted it: Paul standing on the steps: signaled with his hand to the people. And a great: silence being made: he addressed them in the Hebrew language.

Men, brothers, and fathers: hear my words: which I now say to you. And when they heard: that he spoke in the Hebrew language: they kept more silence. And he said: I am a Jewish man: born in Tarsus of Cilicia: but nourished in this city at the feet of Gamaliel <note>A famous and highly respected teacher of the law in Jerusalem</note>: instructed according to the diligence of the law of the fathers: a zealot for the Lord: just as you all are today. Who persecuted this Way even unto death: binding and delivering into custody men and women: just as the high priest: and all the elders bear witness to me: from whom I also received letters: and to the brothers: when I was going to Damascus. So that I might lead those who were there bound to Jerusalem: so that they might be punished: just as they were of this Way.

But it happened to me as I was going: and approaching Damascus: suddenly at midday a great light from heaven shone around me. And I fell to the ground: and I heard a voice saying: Saul, Saul: why do you persecute me? I however answered: who are you, Lord? and he said to me: I am Jesus of Nazareth: whom you persecute. And those who were with me: saw the light indeed: but they did not hear the voice: of him who was speaking with me. And I said: what shall I do, Lord? But the Lord said to me: arise: and go to Damascus: and there it shall be told of all things: which it behoves you to do. But when I could not see: because of the brightness of that light: by the right hand: and led by the hand by those who were with me: I came to Damascus. But a certain Ananias: a man according to the law: having testimony from all the Jews: living there came to me: and standing said to me: brother Saul: look up. And I in that same hour: looked at him. And he said: the God of our fathers: has ordained you: that you should know his will: and see the Just One: and hear the voice from his mouth. Because you shall be a witness for him to all men: of those things which you have seen: and which you have heard. And now why do you delay? arise: and be baptized: and wash away your sins: calling upon his name. But it happened when I returned to Jerusalem: and was praying in the temple: that I was in an ecstasy of mind: and saw him saying to me. Hurry and go quickly out of Jerusalem: because they will not receive your testimony concerning me. And I said: Lord: they themselves know: that I was shutting up in prison: and beating through every synagogue: those who believed in you. And when the blood of Stephen your witness was being shed: I also was standing by: and consenting: and keeping the clothes of those who killed him. And he said to me: Go: for I will send you far off to the Gentiles.

But they heard him up to this word: and they lifted up their voice, saying: Take away such a one from the earth! for it is not right for him to live. But as they were crying out: and throwing off their clothes: and throwing dust into the air: the tribune ordered him to be led into the barracks: and ordered him to be examined with scourges: so that he might know for what cause they thus cried out against him. And when they had bound him with thongs: he said to the centurion standing by: Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is Roman and uncondemned? Having heard this: the centurion went to the tribune: and reported to him, saying: what are you about to do? for this man is a Roman citizen. But the tribune approaching: said to him: tell me: are you Roman? And he said: yes. And the tribune answered: I obtained this citizenship with a great sum of money. And Paul said: But I was even born so. Immediately therefore: they departed from him: those who were about to examine him. And the tribune was afraid: having known: that he is Roman: and because he had bound him. But on the next day, wishing to know: why he was accused by the Jews: he released him: and ordered the chief priests to assemble: and the whole council: and bringing Paul forward: he set him among them. But Paul, looking intently at the Lord <note>original: "i dñm paulū", likely "in concilium" (into the council)</note>, said: Men, brothers: I have lived with all good conscience: before God: until this day.

But the high priest Ananias: ordered those standing by him: to strike the mouth of Paul.

<column-break/>

Then Paul said to him: God shall strike you: you whitewashed wall <note>A "whitewashed wall" refers to a surface that looks clean on the outside but is made of common clay or filth underneath—a metaphor for hypocrisy</note>. And do you sit judging me according to the law: and against the law order me to be struck? And those who stood by: said: do you revile the high priest of God? Paul said: I did not know, brothers: that he is the high priest. For it is written: you shall not speak evil of the prince of your people. But Paul knowing: that one part was of the Sadducees: and the other of the Pharisees: cried out in the council. Men, brothers: I am a Pharisee: the son of Pharisees: concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead: I am judged today. And when he had said this: a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided. For the Sadducees say: there is no resurrection: nor angel: nor spirit. but the Pharisees confess both. And a great cry arose. And some of the scribes of the part of the Pharisees rising up: fought, saying: we find no evil in this man. What if a spirit has spoken to him: or an angel? And when a great dissension had arisen: the tribune fearing: lest Paul should be torn apart by them: ordered the army to descend: and to snatch him from the middle of them: and to lead him back to the barracks. But the following night: the Lord standing by him said: Be constant. For just as you have testified of me in Jerusalem: so it behoves you: to testify also at Rome.

But when day was come: some of the Jews gathered together: and bound themselves by a vow, saying: that they would neither eat: nor drink: until they had killed Paul. There were more than forty: who had made this conspiracy. Who came to the chief priests and the elders: and said: we have bound ourselves with a curse: to taste nothing: or drink: until we kill Paul. Now therefore you arrange a plan with the council: tell the tribune: that he should bring him forward to you: as if you were going to know something more certain: but we, before he approaches: are ready to kill him. When the son of Paul's sister had heard of the ambush: he came: and entered into the barracks: and told Paul. But Paul called to himself one of the centurions: and said: lead this young man to the tribune: for he has something to tell him. And he taking him: led him to the tribune: and said Paul the prisoner: asked me: to lead this young man to you: who has something to tell you. But the tribune took his hand: and went aside with him: and asked: what is it that you have to tell me? He said the Jews: have agreed to ask you: that tomorrow you should bring Paul into the council: as if they were going to know something more certain about him. You therefore do not believe them. For more than forty men of them are lying in wait for him: who have bound themselves: neither to eat: nor drink: until they kill him. and now they are ready: waiting for your promise.

The tribune therefore dismissed the young man: commanding him: that he should tell no one: that you have made these things known to me. And having called two centurions: he said: prepare two hundred soldiers: that they may go as far as Caesarea: and seventy horsemen: and two hundred spearmen: from the third hour of the night. and prepare beasts: so that Paul being set upon them: they may lead him safe to Felix the governor <term>Felix</term> <note>Marcus Antonius Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea from c. 52–60 AD</note>. For he feared lest perhaps the Jews should snatch him away: and kill him: and he himself should afterwards suffer slander: as if he were willing to take money. He wrote moreover a letter: having this form. Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix, greeting. This man having been seized by the Jews: and judged: to be killed by them: I came upon them with the army: I rescued him: when I heard: that he is a Roman. And wishing to know the cause: which they objected against him: I led him into their council. Whom I found: to be accused of nothing else: but of their law: and of God: but nothing: as when he had known those doing: whom I rescued according to the Lord. And when it was reported to me of the ambush: which they had prepared for him: I sent him to you: notifying the adversaries: that they should speak against him: before you. Farewell.

The soldiers therefore according to the command: taking Paul: led him by night into Antipatris. And on the next day: the horsemen being sent: to lead him: they returned to the barracks. Who when they had come to Caesarea: and had delivered the letter to the governor: they set Paul also before him. When he had read it: and asked: from which province he was: and known: that he was from Cilicia: I will hear you, he said: when your adversaries have come. And he ordered him to be kept in Herod's praetorium.

But after five days: the high priest Ananias descended: with certain elders: and a certain orator Tertullus. who approached the governor: against Paul. And Paul being cited: Tertullus began to accuse him saying: Since we act in much peace through you: and many things are corrected: by your providence: always and everywhere having performed: most excellent Felix: we receive it with all giving of thanks. But lest I detain you longer: hear us briefly: in your clemency. For we have found this man pestilent: and stirring up sedition: among all the Jews: in the whole world: and the author of the sedition: and of the sect: and among all the Jews: and of the sect of the Nazarenes. who also attempted to violate the temple. whom being seized we wished to judge according to our law. But the tribune Lysias coming upon us: with great force: rescued him from our hands: and ordered his adversaries to come to the governor: from whom you may: yourself also judging: concerning all these things: of which we accuse him: know. But the Jews also added: saying: that these things were so.

Paul however answered: the governor nodding to him to speak. For a long time I have seen you to be a judge to this nation: and with a good mind: I will render an account of myself. As you can know: that there are not more than twelve days: since I ascended to Jerusalem: to worship: and they found me neither in the temple: disputing with anyone: nor making a concourse of the crowd: nor in the synagogues: nor in the city: nor can they prove: the things of which they now accuse me. But I confess this to you: that according to the sect: which they call so: I serve the God of my fathers: believing all things: which are written in the law: and the prophets: having hope in the Lord: which even these themselves expect: a future resurrection: of the just: and the unjust. In this I also study: to have a conscience: having always toward the Lord and men. But after many years: I came: to do alms to my nation: and offerings: and vows: in which they found me purified in the temple: not with a crowd: nor with tumult. But certain Jews from Asia: who ought: to be present before you: and accuse: if they had anything against me. Or let these themselves say: if they found any injustice in me: while I stood in the council: except for this one voice only: which I cried out: concerning the resurrection of the dead: I am judged today by you.

But Felix deferred them: knowing most certainly: of this Way saying: When Lysias the tribune descends: I will hear you. And he ordered the centurion: to keep him: and to have rest. nor to prohibit anyone: of his own to minister to him. But after some days: Felix came: with Drusilla his wife: who was a Jewess: and called Paul: and heard from him: of the faith: which is in Christ Jesus. And as he disputed: of justice: and chastity: and of the judgment to come: Felix being terrified: answered: For what pertains now: go. but at an opportune time: I will call you. At the same time also hoping: that money would be given to him by Paul: for which cause also frequently calling him: he spoke with him. But when two years were completed: Felix received a successor: Porcius Festus <note>Festus replaced Felix as procurator of Judea around 60 AD</note>. But wishing to show grace to the Jews: Felix: left Paul in bonds.

Festus therefore when he had come into the province: after three days: ascended to Jerusalem from Caesarea. And the chief priests: and the leading men of the Jews approached him: against Paul: and they asked him: making a request: against Paul: that he would judge: at Jerusalem: laying an ambush: that they might kill him on the way. But Festus answered: that Paul was kept in Caesarea. and that he himself in a short time: would set out. Those therefore among you, he said: who are powerful: descending together: if there is any crime in the man: let them accuse him. And when he had stayed among them: not more than eight: or ten days: he descended to Caesarea. And the next day: he sat on the judgment seat: and ordered Paul to be brought. Who when he was brought: those who were Jews who had descended from Jerusalem stood around him: objecting many and heavy crimes: which they could not prove. But Paul rendering an account: that neither against the law of the Jews: nor against the temple: nor against Caesar: have I sinned in anything. But Festus wishing to show grace to the Jews: answered Paul: Do you wish to ascend to Jerusalem: and there be judged concerning these things: before me? But Paul said: I stand at Caesar's judgment seat: where it behoves me to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews: as you very well know. For if I have done wrong: or committed anything worthy of death: I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing: of these things: which they accuse: no one can give me to them. I appeal to Caesar. Then Festus: when he had spoken with the council: answered: To Caesar you have appealed: to Caesar you shall go.

And when no one could restrain us, the ship gave way to the sea, and so we were driven along by the blowing wind, having been pushed toward that island...
<note>The left column continues the narrative of Paul’s journey to Rome under guard, specifically the shipwreck described in Chapters 27 and 28.</note>
...And when day dawned, they did not recognize the land: but they spotted a certain bay with a beach, into which they planned, if possible, to run the ship aground. And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves to the sea, at the same time loosening the lashings of the rudders: and having hoisted the mainsail <note>original: "artemone"</note> to the blowing wind, they made for the beach. And when we had fallen into a place where two seas met <note>original: "bithalassum," referring to a sandbar or strait</note>, they ran the ship aground: and the prow indeed remained fixed and immovable, but the stern was broken by the force of the sea. Now the soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any should swim away and escape. But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, forbade this from being done: and he ordered those who could swim to cast themselves first into the sea and get to land: and the rest were carried on planks, and some on things that belonged to the ship. And so it happened that every soul escaped to the land.

<margin>
Acts 28
</margin>
And once we had escaped, we then learned that the island was called Malta <note>original: "Melitene"</note>. But the natives <note>original: "Barbari," referring here to non-Greek speakers, or locals</note> showed us no small kindness. For they kindled a fire and refreshed us all because of the rain that was falling and the cold. Now when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand. When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another: "Surely this man is a murderer, for though he has escaped from the sea, Justice does not permit him to live." But he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm. However, they expected him to swell up or suddenly fall down and die. But after they had waited a long time and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god. In those places were the estates of the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and entertained us kindly for three days. It happened that the father of Publius lay sick with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and when he had prayed and laid his hands on him, he healed him. After this was done, everyone on the island who had infirmities came and was healed: they also honored us with many honors, and when we sailed, they provided us with the things that were necessary.

And after three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship which had wintered at the island, whose sign was the Twin Brothers <note>original: "castorum," referring to the Greek gods Castor and Pollux</note>. And when we had come to Syracuse, we stayed there for three days. From there, following the coast, we reached Rhegium: and after one day, the south wind blowing, we came on the second day to Puteoli. Where, having found brothers, we were invited to stay with them for seven days: and so we came to Rome. And from there, when the brothers had heard about us, they came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he gave thanks to God and took courage. And when we had come to Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with a soldier to guard him. After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. And when they had assembled, he said to them: "Brothers, though I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans. Who, when they had examined me, wished to release me because there was no cause of death in me. But because the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar—not as if I had any charge to bring against my nation. For this reason, therefore, I have asked to see you and speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel, I am bound with this chain." But they said to him: "We have received no letters from Judea concerning you, nor has any of the brothers who arrived reported or spoken any evil of you. But we desire to hear from you what you think: for concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere." And when they had appointed a day for him, many came to him at his lodging, to whom he explained and testified about the kingdom of God, persuading them about Jesus from the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening. And some believed the things that were said, but some did not believe. And when they did not agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one word: "Well did the Holy Spirit speak through the prophet Isaiah to our fathers, saying: Go to this people and say to them: You shall hear with your ears and not understand, and seeing you shall see and not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown dull, and their ears are hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes; lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and be converted, and I should heal them. Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen." And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having much dispute among themselves. And he remained two whole years in his own rented lodging: and he received all who came to him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

# HERE BEGINS THE PROLOGUE TO THE SEVEN CANONICAL EPISTLES

**T**HE ORDER IS NOT THE SAME AMONG THE GREEKS who are fully wise and follow the right faith—regarding the seven epistles which are called "canonical"—as is found in the Latin manuscripts. Because while Peter is first in the number of the apostles, his epistles are also first in the order of the others. But just as we recently corrected the Evangelists to the line of truth, so we have restored these to their proper order with God’s help. For the first of them is one by James, two by Peter, three by John, and one by Jude. If these were faithfully translated into the Latin tongue by interpreters just as they were arranged by the authors, they would not cause ambiguity for readers, nor would the variety of words conflict with itself—especially in that place where we read about the unity of the Trinity in the first epistle of John. In that passage, we have found that much error has been made from the truth of the faith by unfaithful translators <note>Jerome is referring to the "Johannine Comma," a disputed verse in 1 John 5:7-8 regarding the Trinity</note>, while they put only three words in their edition—that is, "water, blood, and spirit"—and omit the testimony of the Father, the Word, and the Spirit: by which the Catholic faith is most greatly strengthened, and the single substance of the divinity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit is proven. As for how much others differ in the rest of the epistles, I leave it to the prudence of the reader. But you, Eustochium, virgin of Christ <note>Jerome’s close friend and a scholarly nun in Bethlehem</note>, while you seek the truth of Scripture more earnestly from me, you expose my old age to be gnawed by the teeth of the envious, who proclaim me a forger and a corrupter of the sacred Scriptures. But in such a work, I neither fear the envy of my rivals, nor will I deny the truth of Holy Scripture to those who ask for it.

# THE PROLOGUE TO THE SEVEN CANONICAL EPISTLES BEGINS

**T**HE ORDER IS NOT THUS AMONG THE GREEKS who are fully wise and follow the right faith: that of the seven epistles which are called "canonical," as it is found in the Latin codices. Because Peter is first in the number of the Apostles, his epistles are also first in the order of the others. But just as we corrected the Evangelists <note>the four Gospel writers</note> to the line of truth a while ago, so we have restored these to their proper order, God helping us. 

For the first of them is one by James; two by Peter; three by John; and one by Jude. If these were translated faithfully into the Latin language by interpreters just as they were arranged by the authors, they would neither cause ambiguity for readers, nor would they contradict themselves by a variety of words. Especially in that place where we read the passage about the unity of the Trinity in the first epistle of John <note>This refers to the "Comma Johanneum," a controversial addition to 1 John 5:7-8 regarding the Father, Word, and Holy Spirit</note>. In this we have found that much error has been made by unfaithful translators from the truth of the faith, placing in their edition only the names of three things—that is, the water, the blood, and the spirit—and omitting the testimony of the Father, the Word, and the Spirit, by which the Catholic faith is especially strengthened, and the one substance of the divinity of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is proven. 

But how much our edition differs from others in the rest of the epistles, I leave to the prudence of the reader. But you, virgin of Christ, Eustochium <note>Saint Jerome’s close associate and student</note>, while you seek the truth of Scripture from me so urgently, you expose my old age, in a way, to be gnawed by the teeth of the envious, who pronounce me a falsifier and a corrupter of the sacred Scriptures. But in such a work, I neither fear the envy of my rivals, nor will I deny the truth of the sacred Scripture to those who ask for it.
