# JAMES, SERVANT OF GOD AND OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, TO THE TWELVE TRIBES

who are in the dispersion, greetings. Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations. Knowing that the proof of your faith works patience. But let patience have a perfect work: that you may be perfect and entire, failing in nothing. But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all abundantly and does not reproach: and it shall be given to him. But let him ask in faith, hesitating in nothing.

<margin>274.</margin>
**F**or he who hesitates is like a wave of the sea which is moved and carried about by the wind. Therefore, let not that man think that he shall receive anything from the Lord. A man double in mind is inconstant in all his ways. But let the humble brother glory in his humility, and the rich in his exaltation, because like the flower of the grass he shall pass away. For the sun has risen with heat, and dried the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished: so also shall the rich man wither in his journeys.

**B**lessed is the man who suffers temptation, because when he has been proven, he shall receive the crown of life which God has promised to those who love him. Let no one, when he is tempted, say that he is tempted by God. For God is not a tempter of evils: he himself tempts no one. But each one is tempted by his own concupiscence <note>intense desire or lust</note>, being drawn away and enticed. Then, when concupiscence has conceived, it gives birth to sin; but sin, when it is completed, generates death.

**D**o not err, therefore, my most beloved brothers. Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of turning. Voluntarily he begot us by the word of truth, that we might be some beginning of his creature. You know, my most beloved brothers. But let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak, and slow to anger. For the anger of man does not work the justice of God. Because of which, casting away all uncleanness and abundance of malice, receive with meekness the implanted word which can save your souls.

**B**e doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. Because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer: he shall be compared to a man considering his natural face in a mirror. For he considered himself and went away, and immediately forgot what kind of man he was. But he who looks into the law of perfect liberty and remains in it, not having become a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

**B**ut if anyone thinks himself to be religious, not restraining his tongue, but seducing his own heart, this man's religion is vain. Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father is this: To visit orphans and widows in their tribulation, and to keep oneself unspotted from this world.

**M**y brothers, do not have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ with respect of persons. For if there comes into your assembly a man having a gold ring, in white clothing, and there comes in also a poor man in filthy clothing, and you look upon him who is clothed in excellent clothing, and say to him, "You sit here well," but say to the poor man, "You stand there," or "Sit under my footstool," do you not judge within yourselves, and have become judges of unjust thoughts?

**H**ear, my most beloved brothers. Has not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom, which God promised to those who love him? But you have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you by power, and they themselves drag you to judgments? Do they not blaspheme the good name which is invoked upon you?

**I**f, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scriptures, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well. But if you accept persons, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors. For whoever keeps the whole law, but offends in one point, has become guilty of all. For he who said, "You shall not commit adultery," said also, "You shall not kill." But if you do not commit adultery, but you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so do, as those beginning to be judged by the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to him who has not done mercy. But mercy exalts itself above judgment. What will it profit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith, but does not have works?

Calling ten of his servants, he gave them ten minas <note>original: "mnas"; a Greek unit of currency worth about 100 drachmas or three months' wages</note> and said to them: 'Trade with these until I come.' But his citizens hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying: 'We do not want this man to reign over us.' And it happened that he returned, having received the kingdom, and he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to be called, so that he might know how much each had gained by trading. The first came, saying: 'Lord, your mina has earned ten minas.' And he said to him: 'Well done, good servant; because you have been faithful in a very little thing, you shall have power over ten cities.' And the second came, saying: 'Lord, your mina has made five minas.' And to him he said: 'And you be over five cities.' And another came, saying: 'Lord, here is your mina, which I have kept laid up in a cloth. For I feared you, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.' He said to him: 'By your own mouth I judge you, you wicked servant. You knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow. Why then did you not put my money in the bank, so that when I came, I might have collected it with interest?' And he said to those standing by: 'Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.' And they said to him: 'Lord, he has ten minas.' I tell you, that to everyone who has, more shall be given; but from him who has not, even what he has shall be taken away from him. But as for those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me." And having said these things, he went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.

# HERE BEGINS THE PROLOGUE TO THE SEVEN CANONICAL EPISTLES

The order of the seven epistles called "Canonical" <note>original: "canonicas"; referring to the "General" epistles intended for the whole church rather than a specific city</note> among the Greeks, who are fully wise and follow the right faith, is not the same as it is found in the Latin books. Because Peter is first in the number of the apostles, his epistles are also first in the order of the others. But just as we recently corrected the Evangelists <note>the four Gospel writers</note> to the line of truth, so we have restored these to their proper order, with God helping us. For the first of them is one by James, two by Peter, three by John, and one by Jude.

If these had been faithfully turned into the Latin language by translators as they were arranged by the apostles, they would not have created ambiguity for readers, nor would the variety of words conflict with one another. This is especially true in that place where we read about the unity of the Trinity in the First Epistle of John. In this matter, we find that the truth of the faith has been much distorted by unfaithful translators <note>This refers to the "Comma Johanneum," a disputed passage about the Father, Word, and Spirit that Jerome claims was omitted in some versions</note>, who placed only the names of three—the water, blood, and spirit—in their edition, and omitted the testimony of the Father, the Word, and the Spirit. It is in this testimony that the Catholic faith is most strengthened, and the single substance of the divinity of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is proven.

In the other epistles, I leave it to the prudence of the reader to see how much our edition differs from others. But you, Eustochium <note>a Roman noblewoman and student of Jerome</note>, virgin of Christ, while you earnestly seek the truth of Scripture from me, you expose my old age, in a way, to be gnawed at by the teeth of the envious, who proclaim me a falsifier and a corrupter of the sacred Scriptures. But in such a work, I neither fear my rivals' envy, nor will I deny the truth of the Scripture to those who ask for it.

# JAMES, SERVANT OF GOD AND OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST, TO THE TWELVE TRIBES

<margin>1.</margin> who are in the dispersion, greetings. Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience. But let patience have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing. If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing. For he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, moved and carried about by the wind. Therefore, let that man not think he will receive anything from the Lord. A man double-minded <note>original: "duplex animo"</note> is unstable in all his ways. Let the humble brother glory in his humility, and the rich man in his exaltation, because like the flower of the grass he will pass away. For the sun has risen with its heat and dried up the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished; so also will the rich man wither in his journeys. Blessed is the man who suffers temptation, for when he has been proven, he will receive the crown of life which God has promised to those who love him. Let no one say when he is tempted that he is tempted by God. For God is not a tempter of evils; he himself tempts no one. But everyone is tempted by his own desire, drawn away and enticed. Then, when desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is finished, generates death.

<margin>2.</margin> Do not err, therefore, my most beloved brothers. Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning. Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth, that we might be a kind of beginning of his creatures. You know this, my most beloved brothers. Let every man be quick to hear, but slow to speak, and slow to anger. For the anger of man does not work the righteousness of God. Therefore, casting away all uncleanness and abundance of malice, receive with meekness the implanted word which can save your souls. But be doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is compared to a man looking at the face of his birth in a mirror. For he looked at himself and went away, and immediately forgot what kind of man he was. But he who looks into the law of perfect liberty and remains in it, not being a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in his deed.

<margin>3.</margin> If anyone thinks himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue but deceiving his own heart, this man's religion is vain. Religion pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their tribulation, and to keep oneself unspotted from this world.

<margin>4.</margin> My brothers, do not have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ with respect of persons. For if there enters into your assembly a man having a gold ring and in white clothing, and there also enters a poor man in filthy clothing, and you pay attention to him who is clothed in fine clothing and say to him, "You sit here in a good place," but say to the poor man, "You stand there," or "Sit under the footstool of my feet," have you not made judgments within yourselves, and become judges of wicked thoughts? Listen, my most beloved brothers. Has not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which God promised to those who love him? But you have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you by power, and they themselves drag you to judgments? Do they not blaspheme the good name that is called upon you?

<margin>5.</margin> If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the Scriptures, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well. But if you show respect of persons, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors. For whoever keeps the whole law but offends in one point has become guilty of all. For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not kill." Now if you do not commit adultery but you do kill, you have become a transgressor of the law. So speak and so do as those beginning to be judged by the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to him who has not shown mercy. But mercy triumphs over judgment.

<meta>This page transitions from the final moral exhortations of the Epistle of James to the opening of the First Epistle of Peter. It continues the biblical sequence following the life of Christ and the early apostolic teachings discussed on the previous page.</meta>

...it is not becoming. Speak and act as those who are beginning to be judged by the law of liberty. For judgment is without mercy to him who has not shown mercy; but mercy triumphs over judgment.

What will it profit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith, but does not have works? Can faith save him? If a brother or sister is naked and lacks daily food, and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and filled," but you do not give them what is necessary for the body, what will it profit? So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead in itself.

But someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works." Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works. You believe that there is one God; you do well. Even the demons believe—and they shudder. But do you want to know, O empty man, that faith without works is useless? Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered his son Isaac upon the altar? Do you see that faith worked together with his works, and by works faith was made perfect? And the scripture was fulfilled which says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God. You see that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone. Similarly, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another way? For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.

My brothers, let not many of you become teachers, knowing that you will receive a greater judgment; for we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man; he is also able to lead the whole body with a bridle. If we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we guide their whole body as well. Look at ships also: though they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the will of the pilot directs. So also the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. See how small a fire sets a great forest ablaze! And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is placed among our members, staining the whole body and setting on fire the wheel of our birth <note>original: "rotam nativitatis nostrae"; a phrase likely referring to the whole course of human life or the cycle of nature</note>, being set on fire by hell <note>original: "gehenna"</note>. For every nature of beasts and birds and serpents and others is tamed and has been tamed by human nature, but no human being can tame the tongue—a restless evil, full of deadly poison. With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the likeness of God. From the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so. Does a spring pour forth both sweet and bitter water from the same opening? My brothers, can a fig tree produce grapes, or a grapevine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.

Who is wise and disciplined among you? Let him show by his good conduct his work in the meekness of wisdom. 

But if you have bitter zeal and there are contentions in your hearts, do not boast and be liars against the truth. For this is not the wisdom descending from above, but is earthly, animalistic, and devilish. For where there is zeal and contention, there is instability and every wicked work. But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, judging without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

Where do wars and quarrels among you come from? Is it not from your passions, which wage war in your members? You desire and do not have. You kill and are envious and cannot obtain. You quarrel and fight, and you do not have because you do not ask; you ask and do not receive because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your passions. Adulterers, do you not know that friendship with this world is enmity with God? 

Whoever, therefore, wants to be a friend of this world is constituted an enemy of God. Or do you think the scripture says in vain: "The spirit that dwells in you longs unto envy"? But he gives greater grace; for which reason it says: "God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble." Therefore, be subject to God; resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to the Lord, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded. Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow. Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you. Do not disparage one another, my brothers. He who disparages a brother or judges his brother disparages the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge. For there is one lawmaker and judge who is able to destroy and to set free. But who are you to judge your neighbor?

Look now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to that city, and we will spend a year there, and trade and make a profit"—you who do not know what tomorrow will bring. For what is your life? It is a vapor appearing for a moment, and then it shall vanish. Instead, you ought to say, "If the Lord wills, and if we live, we will do this or that." But now you exult in your pride. All such exultation is wicked. Therefore, to him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.

Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming upon you. Your riches are rotted, and your garments are eaten by moths. Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wrath for yourselves in the last days. Behold, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, which were defrauded by you, cry out; and their cry has entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth <note>original: "sabaoth"; a Hebrew term meaning "hosts" or "armies"</note>. You have feasted upon the earth, and in luxuries you have nourished your hearts for the day of slaughter. You have brought forth, you have killed the just man, and he does not resist you. Therefore, brothers, be patient until the coming of the Lord.

Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, bearing it patiently until he receives the early and the late rains. Be patient also, and strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near. Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge stands before the door. Brothers, take as an example of labor and patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord. Behold, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the suffering of Job, and you have seen the end intended by the Lord, because the Lord is merciful and compassionate. But above all, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath. But let your word be "yes, yes" and "no, no," so that you do not fall under judgment. Is any among you sad? Let him pray. Is he of good heart? Let him sing psalms. Is any among you sick? Let him bring in the priests <term>presbyteros: the elders or priests of the early church</term> of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will alleviate him; and if he is in sins, they will be forgiven him. Therefore, confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another so that you may be saved. For the persistent prayer of a righteous man is very powerful. Elijah was a man like us, subject to suffering, and he prayed with prayer that it might not rain upon the earth, and it did not rain for three years and six months. And he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth gave its fruit. My brothers, if anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone converts him, he ought to know that he who causes a sinner to be converted from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins. THE EPISTLE OF JAMES THE APOSTLE ENDS.

# THE FIRST EPISTLE OF PETER

<column-break/>

# PETER, AN APOSTLE OF JESUS CHRIST, TO THE ELECT

strangers of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has regenerated us into a living hope, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, into an inheritance incorruptible and uncontaminated and unfading, preserved in heaven for you, who are guarded by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time, in which you exult. Now for a little while, if it is necessary, you must be saddened by various temptations: so that the proof of your faith may be much more precious than gold which is tested by fire.

May it be found unto praise and glory and honor in the revelation of Jesus Christ, whom you love although you have not seen him. In whom also you now believe, though not seeing him: believing, you exult with joy unspeakable and glorified, bringing back the end of your faith, the salvation of souls. Concerning which salvation the prophets sought and searched, who prophesied about the grace to come to you. Searching into what or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ in them was signifying, foretelling the passions that are in Christ and the glories that follow. To whom it was revealed that they were ministering not to themselves, but to you, those things which have now been announced to you by those who have preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, into which things angels desire to look.

Therefore, having girded the loins of your mind, being sober and perfectly hoping in that grace which is offered to you in the revelation of Jesus Christ. Like children of obedience, not fashioned according to the former desires of your ignorance; but according to him who called you, the Holy One, be holy yourselves in all conduct, since it is written: "You shall be holy, because I am holy." And if you invoke as Father him who judges without respect of persons according to each one's work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourn. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things like gold or silver from your vain conduct of paternal tradition, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb uncontaminated and immaculate, foreknown indeed before the constitution of the world, but manifested in the last times for your sake, you who through him are faithful in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God. Purifying your souls by the obedience of charity in the love of brotherhood, love one another attentively from a simple heart: reborn not from corruptible seed but from incorruptible, through the word of the living God which remains forever. Because all flesh is as grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the grass. The grass has withered and its flower has fallen, but the word of the Lord remains forever.

And this is the word that was preached to you. Therefore, putting away all malice and all guile and hypocrisies and envies and all disparagements, like newborn infants, desire the rational milk without guile, so that in it you may grow into salvation, if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is sweet.

Approaching him as a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen and honored by God. And you yourselves, like living stones, are built up as a spiritual house: a holy priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. For which reason the scripture contains: "Behold, I place in Zion a chief cornerstone, chosen and precious, and he who believes in him shall not be confounded." Therefore, honor is to you who believe; but to those who do not believe, "the stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner," and "a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal," to those who stumble at the word and do not believe, in which they were also placed.

But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people: so that you may announce the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his admirable light, you who were once not a people, but are now the people of God; who had not obtained mercy, but have now obtained mercy.

Dearest ones, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims to abstain from carnal desires which wage war against the soul, having your conduct good among the Gentiles, so that in that which they disparage you as evildoers, they, considering you from your good works, may glorify God in the day of visitation. Be subject to every human creature for God’s sake, whether to the king as the one excelling, or to governors as sent by him for the vengeance of evildoers but the praise of the good. Because such is the will of God, that by doing good you may put to silence the ignorance of imprudent men. As free men, and not as having liberty as a veil for malice, but as servants of God. Honor everyone, love the brotherhood, fear God, honor the king. Servants, be subject to your masters in all fear, not only to the good and modest, but also to the difficult <note>original: "dyscolis"; meaning harsh, peevish, or difficult to please</note>. For this is grace, if for the sake of conscience toward God one sustains sorrows, suffering unjustly. For what glory is it if, when you sin and are buffeted, you endure it? But if when doing good you suffer patiently, this is grace with God. For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving an example so that you might follow his footsteps, who committed no sin, nor was guile found in his mouth. Who, when he was cursed, did not curse; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but delivered himself to him who judged him unjustly. He himself bore our sins in his body upon the wood <note>original: "lignum"; referring to the cross</note>, so that having died to sins, we might live to righteousness. By whose stripes you were healed. For you were like wandering sheep, but you have now turned to the shepherd and bishop <term>episcopum: overseer or guardian</term> of your souls.

Similarly, let wives be subject to their husbands, so that even if any do not believe the word, they may be won over without the word through the conduct of the wives, considering your chaste conduct in fear. Whose adornment should not be the outward braiding of hair, or the wearing of gold, or the putting on of robes; but let it be the hidden person of the heart in the incorruptibility of a quiet and modest spirit, which is rich in the sight of God. For so also formerly the holy women who hoped in God adorned themselves, being subject to their own husbands, just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters you are, doing good and not fearing any disturbance. Husbands, similarly, cohabiting according to knowledge, imparting honor to the woman as to a weaker vessel, as to co-heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered. Finally, all of you be of one mind, compassionate, lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, humble: not rendering evil for evil, nor curse for curse, but on the contrary, blessing, because to this you were called so that you might possess a blessing by inheritance. For he who wants to love life and see good days, let him restrain his tongue from evil and his lips that they speak no guile. Let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it, because the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayers, but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. And who is he who...

...so that you may humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in the time of visitation. Cast all your anxiety upon him, because he has a care for you. Be sober and watch, because your adversary the devil circles around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, standing firm in your faith, knowing that the same kind of suffering is experienced by your brotherhood throughout the world. But the God of all grace, who has called us into his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, will himself perfect, confirm, and establish you. To him be the dominion forever and ever. Amen. 

Through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother to you, I have written briefly, beseeching and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand. The church which is in Babylon <note>Babylon was often used as a code name for Rome in early Christian writing.</note>, chosen together with you, greets you, as does Mark my son. Greet one another with a holy kiss. Grace be to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.

### HERE ENDS THE FIRST EPISTLE OF PETER. <note>original: "EXPLICIT EPISTOLA PETRI PRIMA"</note>

## THE SECOND EPISTLE

<image-desc>A large, ornate drop-cap 'S' featuring interlaced vine-work and animal-like patterns in red, blue, and gold.</image-desc>

# SIMON PETER, SERVANT AND APOSTLE

of Jesus Christ: to those who have obtained a faith equal to ours in the justice of our God and Savior Jesus Christ. May grace and peace be fulfilled in you through the knowledge of our Lord. For all things of his divine power which pertain to life and godliness have been given to us through the recognition of him who called us by his own glory and virtue. Through him, he has given us the greatest and most precious promises, so that through these you may become sharers of the divine nature, escaping the corruption of lust that is in the world. 

And for this very reason, providing all care, minister virtue in your faith; and in virtue, knowledge; and in knowledge, abstinence <note>or self-control</note>; and in abstinence, patience; and in patience, godliness; and in godliness, love of the brotherhood; and in love of the brotherhood, charity. For if these things are present and abound in you, they will make you neither empty nor without fruit in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. For he who lacks these things is blind and groping with his hand, having forgotten the purging of his old sins. Therefore, brothers, be all the more eager to make your calling and election sure through good works. For by doing these things, you will never sin. For in this way, an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be abundantly provided for you. 

For this reason, I will begin to always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the present truth. I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle <note>The "tabernacle" refers to the physical body as a temporary dwelling for the soul.</note>, to stir you up by a reminder, knowing that the laying aside of my tabernacle is coming swiftly, according to what our Lord Jesus Christ has signified to me.

<column-break/>

Moreover, I will see to it that even after my death you may frequently have a means of remembering these things. For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his greatness. For he received honor and glory from God the Father, when a voice such as this came to him from the Magnificent Glory: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him." And we heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain. 

And we have a more reliable prophetic word, to which you do well to pay attention, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts. Understanding this first: that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation. For prophecy was never brought by human will, but holy men of God spoke as they were inspired by the Holy Spirit.

But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be lying teachers among you, who will introduce sects of perdition <note>or "destructive heresies"</note> and deny the Lord who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves. And many will follow their luxuries, by whom the way of truth will be blasphemed. In their greed, they will trade in you with fabricated words; for whom judgment has not ceased for a long time, and their destruction does not sleep. 

For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but delivered them to be tortured in hell, drawn down by the ropes of the infernal regions to be reserved for judgment; and if he did not spare the original world, but preserved Noah, the eighth person and a herald of justice, bringing a flood upon the world of the ungodly; and if he condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah by reducing them to ash, setting an example for those who would act impiously; and if he rescued the just man Lot, who was oppressed by the injustice and luxurious behavior of the wicked—for that just man, dwelling among them, was tortured in his just soul day after day by seeing and hearing their lawless deeds—then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from temptation and how to reserve the wicked to be tortured on the day of judgment. 

This is especially true for those who walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness and despise authority. Bold and self-pleasing, they do not fear to blaspheme against sects <note>or "glories/dignities"</note>. Whereas angels, though they are greater in strength and power, do not bring an execrable judgment against them. But these people, like irrational beasts naturally made to be captured and destroyed, blaspheming in things they do not understand, will perish in their own corruption, receiving the reward of injustice. They consider the delights of the day to be a pleasure; they are stains and blemishes, overflowing with delights, reveling in their banquets with you. They have eyes full of adultery and unceasing sin. They entice unstable souls; they have hearts trained in greed; they are children of a curse. Forsaking the right way, they have gone astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the reward of iniquity. But he received a rebuke for his madness: a mute beast of burden, speaking with a human voice, forbade the prophet's foolishness. 

These are fountains without water and clouds driven by whirlwinds, for whom the mist of darkness is reserved. For speaking proud words of vanity, they entice through the desires of the fleshly luxury those who have only recently escaped those living in error. They promise them liberty, while they themselves are slaves to corruption. For by whatever a person is overcome, to that he is a slave. For if, after escaping the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their latter state has become worse than the first. For it would have been better for them not to know the way of justice than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them. It has happened to them according to the true proverb: "The dog returns to his own vomit," and, "The sow that was washed returns to wallow in the mud."

Behold, beloved, I am now writing this second epistle to you, in which I stir up your sincere mind with a reminder, so that you may be mindful of the words I predicted from the holy prophets and the commandments of your apostles from the Lord and Savior. Knowing this first: that in the last days mockers will come with deception, walking according to their own lusts and saying: "Where is the promise of his coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation." For they willfully ignore this: that by the word of God the heavens existed long ago and the earth was formed out of water and through water, by which the world that then existed perished, being flooded with water. But the heavens and the earth that now exist are kept by the same word, reserved for fire until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly men. 

But do not let this one thing escape you, beloved: that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day. The Lord does not delay his promise as some think, but acts patiently for your sake, not wanting anyone to perish, but wanting all to return to repentance. But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with a great rush, and the elements will be dissolved by heat. 

Since all these things are to be dissolved, what kind of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of the Lord, by which the burning heavens will be dissolved and the elements will melt with the heat of fire? But we expect new heavens and a new earth according to his promises, in which justice dwells. Therefore, beloved, while you wait for these things, be diligent to be found by him in peace, immaculate and unviolated. And consider the long-suffering of our Lord to be salvation. Just as our dearest brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him; as he does in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things. In those letters are some things difficult to understand, which the unlearned and unstable distort, as they do the other Scriptures, to their own destruction. 

You therefore, brothers, knowing this beforehand, take guard; lest being led away by the error of the foolish, you fall from your own steadfastness. But grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

### HERE ENDS THE SECOND EPISTLE OF PETER.

...and we have looked upon and our hands have touched, concerning the word of life. And the life was made manifest, and we have seen it, and we testify and announce to you the eternal life which was with the Father and appeared to us. That which we have seen and heard we announce to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father and with his son Jesus Christ. And these things we write to you so that you may rejoice and your joy may be full. And this is the message <note>original: "adnuntiatio"</note> which we have heard from him and announce to you: that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all. If we say that we have fellowship with him and yet walk in darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth. But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his son cleanses us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all iniquity. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar and his word is not in us.

My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. But even if anyone does sin, we have an advocate <term>Advocate: from the Latin "advocatus," meaning one called to one's side, like a legal defender.</term> with the Father: Jesus Christ the just. And he is the propitiation <note>an offering that brings reconciliation</note> for our sins—not only for ours, however, but also for those of the whole world. And by this we know that we have come to know him: if we observe his commandments. He who says he knows him and does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him. But whoever keeps his word, truly in him the love <note>original: "caritas"</note> of God is perfected. By this we know that we are in him. He who says he abides in him ought himself to walk just as he walked.

Beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment which you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the word which you have heard. Again, I write a new commandment to you, which is true both in him and in you, because the darkness has passed away and the true light already shines. He who says he is in the light and hates his brother is in darkness even until now. He who loves his brother abides in the light, and there is no cause for stumbling in him. But he who hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.

I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven through his name. I write to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. I write to you, adolescents, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, infants, because you have known the Father. I write to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.

Do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him; because everything that is in the world—the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away, along with its lust; but he who does the will of God abides forever.

Little children, it is the last hour; and just as you heard that the Antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared; from this we know that it is the last hour. They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they certainly would have remained with us; but it was so that they might be made manifest that not all are of us. But you have an anointing <note>original: "unctionem"</note> from the Holy One and you know all things. I have not written to you as to those ignorant of the truth, but as to those who know it, and because every lie is not of the truth. Who is the liar but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father; he who confesses the Son has the Father as well.

As for you, let that which you heard from the beginning remain in you. If that which you heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and the Father. And this is the promise which he himself promised us: eternal life. I have written these things to you concerning those who seduce you. And as for you, let the anointing which you received from him remain in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you; but just as his anointing teaches you about all things and is true and is not a lie, so remain in him just as it taught you. And now, little children, remain in him so that when he appears we may have confidence and not be put to shame by him at his coming. If you know that he is just, know that everyone also who practices justice is born of him.

See what kind of love the Father has given to us, that we should be named—and should be—children of God. Because of this, the world does not know us, because it did not know him. Beloved, we are now children of God, and it has not yet appeared what we shall be. We know that when he appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him just as he is. And everyone who has this hope in him sanctifies himself, just as he is holy. Everyone who commits sin also commits iniquity, and sin is iniquity. And you know that he appeared so that he might take away sins, and there is no sin in him. Everyone who abides in him does not sin; and everyone who sins has not seen him nor known him. Little children, let no one seduce you. He who practices justice is just, just as he is just. He who commits sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the beginning. For this reason the Son of God appeared: to undo the works of the devil. Everyone who is born of God does not commit sin, because his seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. In this the children of God and the children of the devil are made manifest: everyone who is not just is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother. For this is the message you heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.

Not like Cain, who was of the evil one and killed his brother. And why did he kill him? Because his own works were evil, but his brother's were just. Do not wonder, brothers, if the world hates you. We know that we have been translated from death to life because we love the brothers. He who does not love remains in death. Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. And you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in himself. In this we have known the love of God: because he laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers. He who has the substance of this world and sees his brother in need and closes his heart <note>literally "bowels" or "viscera," a common idiom for the seat of compassion</note> against him, how does the love of God remain in him?

My little children, let us not love in word or tongue, but in deed and truth. In this we know that we are of the truth, and we persuade our hearts in his sight; because if our heart reproaches us, God is greater than our heart and knows all things. Beloved, if our heart does not reproach us, we have confidence toward God, and whatever we ask we shall receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do those things that are pleasing in his sight. And this is his commandment: that we should believe in the name of his son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he gave us the commandment. And he who keeps his commandments abides in him, and he in him. And by this we know that he abides in us: by the Spirit whom he gave to us.

Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see if they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. In this the Spirit of God is known: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God; and every spirit that separates <note>original: "solvit," or "dissolves"</note> Jesus is not from God, and this is the Antichrist of whom you have heard that he is coming, and now he is already in the world. You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world. They are of the world; therefore they speak of the world, and the world listens to them. We are of God; he who knows God listens to us; he who is not of God does not listen to us. In this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God. And everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. He who does not love does not know God, because God is love. In this the love of God appeared among us: because God sent his only-begotten Son into the world so that we might live through him. In this is love: not as though we had loved God, but because he first loved us and sent his Son as a propitiation for 

<column-break/>

<margin>
O
P
</margin>
our sins. Beloved, if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God abides in us and his love is perfected in us. By this we know that we abide in him and he in us: because he has given to us of his Spirit. And we have seen and testify that the Father sent the Son as the Savior of the world. Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him and he in God. And we have known and believed the love which God has for us.

God is love, and he who abides in love abides in God, and God in him. In this, love is perfected with us: so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, because as he is, so also are we in this world. There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment. He who fears is not perfected in love. We, therefore, love God, because God first loved us. If anyone says, "I love God," and hates his brother, he is a liar. For he who does not love his brother whom he sees, how can he love God whom he does not see? And we have this commandment from God: that he who loves God should also love his brother.

Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and everyone who loves him who begot, loves also him who was born of him. In this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and do his commandments. For this is the love of God: that we keep his commandments; and his commandments are not heavy, because everything that is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that overcomes the world: our faith. Who is it that overcomes the world but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? This is he who came through water and blood: Jesus Christ; not in water only, but in water and blood. And it is the Spirit who testifies, because Christ is the truth; for there are three who give testimony on earth: the spirit, the water, and the blood, and these three are one. If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater; for this is the testimony of God, which is greater because he has testified concerning his Son. He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God in himself. He who does not believe the Son makes him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony which God testified concerning his Son. And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He who has the Son has life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have life.

I write these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence we have toward him: that whatever we ask according to his will, he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we requested from him. If anyone knows his brother to be committing a sin that is not unto death, let him ask, and he will give life to him—to those sinning not unto death. There is a sin unto death; I do not say that one should pray for that. All iniquity is sin, and there is sin unto death. We know that everyone who is born of God does not sin, but the generation of God preserves him and the evil one does not touch him. We know that we are of God, and the whole world is seated in the evil one. And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know the true God and be in his true Son; this is the true God and eternal life. Little children, keep yourselves from idols. 

### HERE ENDS THE FIRST EPISTLE OF JOHN. <note>original: "Explicit epistola iohannis prima"</note>

### THE SECOND EPISTLE

# THE ELDER, TO THE BELOVED LADY AND HER CHILDREN

<image-desc>A large decorative letter 'S' containing a miniature portrait of a bearded saint, identified by tradition as St. John, holding a Gospel book. The background is vibrant blue and gold with leaf patterns.</image-desc>

whom I love in truth; and not I alone, but also all who have known the truth, because of the truth which remains in us and will be with us forever. May grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus the Son of the Father be with us in truth and love.

I rejoiced greatly because I found some of your children walking in truth, just as we received the commandment from the Father. And now I ask you, lady—not as though writing a new commandment to you, but that which we had from the beginning—that we love one another. And this is love: that we walk according to his commandments. For this is the commandment which you heard from the beginning: that you should walk in it. Because many seducers have gone out into the world, who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; such a one is a seducer and an antichrist. Look to yourselves, so that you do not lose what you have worked for, but that you may receive a full reward.

Everyone who withdraws and does not remain in the doctrine of Christ does not have God; he who remains in the doctrine has both the Son and the Father. If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your house nor say "hail" <note>original: "ave," a standard greeting</note> to him. For he who says "hail" to him shares in his evil works. Having more things to write to you, I did not want to do so through paper and ink. For I hope to be with you and to speak face to face, so that your joy may be full. The children of your elect sister greet you.

# THIRD EPISTLE OF JOHN THE APOSTLE.

# THE BEGINNING OF THE EPISTLE OF THE
# BLESSED APOSTLE JUDE.

# JUDE, SERVANT OF JESUS CHRIST, 
# BROTHER

of James: to those who are beloved in God the Father and kept and called in Jesus Christ: may mercy, peace, and love be fulfilled in you. Dearly beloved, while making every effort to write to you about our common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you: beseeching you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints. For certain men have slipped in: who long ago were designated for this judgment, impious men, turning the grace of our God into luxury, and denying our only Sovereign and Lord, Jesus Christ. However, I want to remind you, though you once knew all things, that Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe. And the angels who did not keep their own principality <term>Principality: or domain; the sphere of their original authority.</term> but left their own dwelling, he has reserved in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day: just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities, having given themselves over to fornication in like manner and gone after other flesh, were made an example, undergoing the judgment of eternal fire. Similarly, these men also defile the flesh: they despise authority, and they blaspheme majesty. When Michael the archangel, disputing with the devil, argued about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a judgment of blasphemy: but said, "May the Lord command you." But these men blaspheme whatever they do not know: and whatever things they know naturally, like mute animals, in these things they are corrupted. 2.
Woe to those who have gone in the way of Cain: and have abandoned themselves to the error of Balaam for reward: and have perished in the rebellion of Korah <note>original: "chore"</note>. These are stains in their feasts, banqueting without fear, feeding themselves: clouds without water which are carried about by winds: autumn trees, fruitless, twice dead, uprooted. Wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own confusion: wandering stars, for whom the storm of darkness is reserved forever. 2.
And Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about these, saying: "Behold, the Lord comes with his holy thousands, to execute judgment against all, and to convict all the impious of all their works of impiety which they have impiously committed, and of all the hard things which impious sinners have spoken against him." These are grumblers and complainers, walking according to their own desires: and their mouth speaks arrogant things, admiring persons for the sake of gain. But you, dearly beloved, be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ, who told you that in the last time there would come scoffers, walking according to their own desires in impieties: these are they who separate themselves, worldly men, not having the Spirit. But you, dearly beloved, building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit, keep yourselves in the love of God, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal salvation. And indeed, convict those who are judged: but save others by snatching them from the fire: and have mercy on others in fear, hating even the tunic stained by the flesh. 3.
Now to him who is able to keep you without sin and to set you before the presence of his glory spotless in exultation, to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory and magnificence, dominion and power, before all ages, both now and forever and ever, amen. 
Here ends the EPISTLE OF JUDE.

# APOCALYPSE.

# JOHN THE APOSTLE AND EVANGELIST,

chosen by the Lord Jesus Christ and loved among the others, held the privilege of a more abundant love: because after the beginning of the Gospel and the writing of the Acts, he is commended to his own mother <note>The author refers to Christ entrusting Mary to John at the Crucifixion.</note>. Indeed, when he was being plucked away into exile to the embrace of the troubling island, he even received from the same [Lord] for the writing [of this book], he being most white in virginity: this [lot] he obtained for a long time in Patmos and for the testimony of Jesus in the midst of the island of Patmos; there he described the Apocalypse shown to him. So that even as the incorruptible beginning is noted at the start of the canon in the book of Genesis, so also the incorruptible end should be returned through the virgin in the Apocalypse, saying: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end." This is John, who, knowing that the day of his release from the body had come upon him, having called his disciples together in Ephesus, descended into the dug-out place of his burial, and when his prayer was completed, he gave up his spirit, being as much a stranger to the pain of death as he is known to be alien to the corruption of the flesh. However, the arrangement of this scripture or the ordering of the book is not explained by us point by point for this reason: so that the desire for inquiring may be placed in those who do not know, and the fruit may be kept for those who seek, and the doctrine of mastery for God. 2.

And to the angel of the church of Ephesus write: These things says he who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands: I know your works and your labor and your patience, and that you cannot bear those who are evil: and you have tested those who say they are apostles and are not, and have found them liars: and you have patience and have endured for my name's sake, and have not fainted. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of my God.
And to the angel of the church of Smyrna write: These things says the first and the last, who was dead and lives: I know your tribulation and your poverty (but you are rich), and you are blasphemed by those who say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. And to the angel of the church of Pergamum write: These things says he who has the sharp two-edged sword: I know where you dwell, where Satan’s seat is: and you hold fast my name and have not denied my faith, even in the days in which Antipas was my faithful witness, who was killed among you where Satan dwells. But I have a few things against you, because you have there those holding the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit fornication. So you also have those holding the doctrine of the Nicolaitans likewise. Do penance. If not, I am coming to you quickly and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth. He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give hidden manna, and I will give him a white pebble, and in the pebble a new name written, which no one knows except him who receives it. 2.

And I gave her time to do penance, and she will not do penance for her fornication. Behold, I will cast her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her shall be in very great tribulation, unless they do penance for their deeds. And I will kill her children with death, and all the churches shall know that I am he who searches the reins and the hearts: and I will give to every one of you according to your works. But to you I say, to the rest who are in Thyatira: whosoever do not have this doctrine, who have not known the depths of Satan, as they say: I will not put upon you any other burden; but that which you have, hold fast until I come.
