### The Lord's Supper and Spiritual Gifts

Now I give you these instructions. I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better, but for the worse. First of all, when you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions <note>original: "scissuras"; referring to schisms or factions within the community.</note> among you, and to some extent I believe it. For there must also be factions among you, so that those who are proven may be made manifest among you. Therefore, when you meet together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper. For each one takes his own supper first to eat. And one is hungry, while another is drunk. Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Do I praise you? In this I do not praise you.

For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night he was betrayed, took bread, and giving thanks, he broke it and said: "Take and eat; this is my body, which shall be delivered for you; do this in remembrance of me." In the same way also the cup, after he had supped, saying: "This cup is the new covenant <note>original: "novum testamentum"</note> in my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me." For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you shall announce the death of the Lord until he comes. Therefore, whoever eats this bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of the cup. For he who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord. For this reason, many among you are weak and sickly, and many sleep <note>A common euphemism for death in the early Christian tradition.</note>. But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged. But while we are judged, we are corrected by the Lord, so that we may not be condemned with this world. Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another. If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together unto judgment. The rest I will set in order when I come.

Now concerning spiritual matters, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant. You know that when you were heathens, you were led away to dumb idols, however you were moved. Therefore, I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says "Jesus be cursed" <note>original: "anathema Iesu"</note>. And no one can say "Jesus is Lord" except by the Holy Spirit.

Now there are varieties of graces, but the same Spirit. And there are varieties of ministries, but the same Lord. And there are varieties of operations, but it is the same God who works all things in everyone. But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good. To one indeed is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit; to another faith in the same Spirit; to another the grace of healing in the one Spirit; to another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another the discerning of spirits; to another various kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of speeches. All these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, dividing to each one his own gifts as he wills.

For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though they are many, are yet one body, so also is Christ. For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Gentiles, whether slaves or free, and we were all made to drink in one Spirit. For the body is not one member, but many. If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," it is not therefore not of the body. And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," it is not therefore not of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be? But now God has placed the members, each one of them in the body, just as he willed. If they were all one member, where would the body be? But now there are indeed many members, yet one body. The eye cannot 

<column-break/>

say to the hand: "I do not need your work." Or again the head to the feet: "You are not necessary to me." But much more, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are more necessary; and those members of the body which we think to be less honorable, we surround with more abundant honor. And our unpresentable parts have more abundant modesty. But our presentable parts have no need. But God has tempered the body together, giving more abundant honor to that which lacked, so that there should be no schism in the body, but that the members should be mutually anxious for one another. And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; or if one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

Now you are the body of Christ, and members of a member. And God has placed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then the graces of healing, helps, governments, kinds of tongues, interpretations of speeches. Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracles? Do all have the grace of healing? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? But be zealous for the better gifts. And I show you a still more excellent way.

### The Hymn to Love

If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love <note>original: "charitatem"; although often translated as "charity" in older English, it refers to the highest form of Christian love (agape).</note>, I have become as sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal. And if I should have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I should have all faith so that I could move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I should deliver my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing.

Love is patient, it is kind. Love does not envy, it does not act wrongly, it is not puffed up, it is not ambitious, it does not seek its own, it is not provoked, it thinks no evil, it does not rejoice over iniquity, but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Love never fails. Whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect has come, that which is in part shall be made void. When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child. But when I became a man, I put away the things of a child. We see now through a glass darkly <note>original: "per speculum in ænigmate"; literally "through a mirror in a riddle."</note>, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know even as I am known. And now remain faith, hope, and love, these three; but the greatest of these is love.

### Order in the Church

Follow after love, be zealous for spiritual gifts, but especially that you may prophesy. For he who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men, but to God. For no one understands. But in the spirit he speaks mysteries. But he who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and exhortation, and consolation. He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church of God. I wish that you all spoke in tongues, but more so that you prophesied. For he who prophesies is greater than he who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive edification.

Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in doctrine? Even inanimate things that give sound, whether a pipe or a harp, unless they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped? For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself for battle? So you also, unless you utter a clear speech by the tongue, how shall it be known what is said? For you will be speaking into the air. There are, for instance, so many kinds of languages in this world, and nothing is without a voice. If then I do not know the power of the voice, I shall be a barbarian <note>original: "barbarus"; to the Greeks and Romans, a "barbarian" was anyone who spoke an unintelligible foreign language.</note> to him to whom I speak, and he who speaks will be a barbarian to me.

So also you, since you are zealous for spirits, seek that you may abound to the edification of the church. And therefore, let him who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret. For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is without fruit. What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray also with the mind. I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing also with the mind. Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how shall he who occupies the place of the unlearned <note>original: "idiotæ"; referring to a layperson or someone without specialized spiritual gifts.</note> say "Amen" to your blessing? For he does not know what you are saying. For you indeed give thanks well, but the other is not edified. I thank God that I speak in the tongues of all of you. But in the church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.

Brothers, do not become children in your senses, but be like infants in malice, and in your senses be perfect. In the law it is written: "In other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people, and even so they will not hear me, says the Lord." Therefore, tongues are for a sign, not to believers, but to unbelievers; but prophecies are not for unbelievers, but for believers. If therefore the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak in tongues, and there come in the unlearned or unbelievers, will they not say that you are mad? But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an unlearned person comes in, he is convinced by all, he is judged by all. The secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so falling on his face, he will adore God, pronouncing that God is truly among you.

What is it then, brothers? When you come together, each one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation; let all things be done for edification. If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two, or at most three, and in turn, and let one interpret. But if there is no interpreter, let him be silent in the church, and speak to himself and to God. Let two or three prophets speak, and let the rest judge. But if anything is revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent. For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be exhorted. And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets. For God is not a God of dissension, but of peace, as I teach in all the churches of the saints.

Let women keep silence in the churches. For it is not permitted to them to speak, but to be subject, as also the law says. If they want to learn anything, let them ask their husbands at home. For it is a shame for a woman to speak in the church. Did the word of God proceed from you? Or did it come to you alone? If anyone seems to be a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things I write to you are the commandments of the Lord. But if anyone is ignorant, he shall be ignored. Therefore, brothers, be zealous to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues. But let all things be done honestly and according to order among you.

### The Resurrection of Christ

Now I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I preached to you, which also you received, and in which you stand. By which also you are saved, if you hold fast the reason I preached to you, unless you have believed in vain. For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures; and that he was seen by Cephas <note>Cephas is the Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter.</note>, and after that by the eleven. Then he was seen by more than five hundred brothers at once, of whom many remain until now, but some have fallen asleep. Then he was seen by James, then by all the apostles. And last of all, as by one born out of time <note>original: "abortivo"; Paul describes himself as an "untimely birth" because he was called to be an apostle after the time of Jesus's earthly ministry.</note>, he was seen also by me.

For I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace in me was not in vain; but I labored more abundantly than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me. For whether it was I or they, so we preach, and so you have believed.

Now if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? For if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not risen. And if Christ has not risen, then our preaching is in vain, and your faith is also in vain. We are even found to be false witnesses of God, because we have given testimony against God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up if the dead do not rise again. For if the dead do not rise again, neither has Christ risen. And if Christ has not risen, your faith is vain, for you are still in your sins. Therefore, those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished. If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are more miserable than all men. But now Christ has risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep. For since by a man came death, by a man also comes the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all...

<meta>This page continues Paul’s first letter to the Corinthians, specifically the theological climax regarding the resurrection of the dead in chapter 15, and the practical concluding matters in chapter 16. It then transitions into the "Argument" (introduction) and the opening chapters of the second letter to the Corinthians.</meta>

... and this pure and incorruptible sacrifice <note>original: "victimam"; likely referring to the Eucharist mentioned on the previous page</note> continually until the coming of the Lord. Then there is the receiving and the eating of it by those who wait and eat. What is seen now will not be then. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> When he shall have abolished all principality and power and virtue. For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet. <margin>Psalm 109</margin> And afterwards, so that God may be all in all. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> All things will be present to those who are present. But when all things shall be subjected to him, it is without doubt except for him who subjected all things to him. But when all things have been subjected to him, then the Son himself shall be subject to him who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all. From the place where it is said, <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> What shall they do who are baptized for the dead, if the dead do not rise at all? <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Even to the point of "they are baptized for them." Up to here is the preaching on the resurrection. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Otherwise, it is said because of the temptation, brothers, which they endure here for Christ. And he says: If according to human standards I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me if the dead do not rise? <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die. Do not be led astray. Evil conversations corrupt good morals. Awake, you just, and do not sin; for some have an ignorance of God. I speak to your shame. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> So until that point: How do the dead rise? <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> With what kind of body do they come? Starting then with what is said: You fool, that which you sow is not brought to life unless it dies, and so forth, until it is said: and as we have carried the image of the earthly, let us also carry the image of the heavenly. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Paul shows the variety of the resurrection and the bringing to life through the comparison of seeds.

For he says that there is one kind of body for humans, another for cattle, another for birds, and for all living things. There are both heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the glory of the heavenly is one thing, and that of the earthly is another. There is one brightness of the sun, another brightness of the moon, and another brightness of the stars. For star differs from star in brightness; so also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it shall rise in incorruption. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> It is sown in dishonor, it shall rise in glory. It is sown in weakness, it shall rise in power. It is sown a natural body, it shall rise a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual one; so it is written: the first man Adam was made into a living soul, the last Adam into a life-giving spirit. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> But that which is spiritual was not first, but that which is natural, and afterward that which is spiritual. The first man was of the earth, earthly; the second man is from heaven, heavenly. Such as the earthly man was, such also are the earthly; and such as the heavenly man is, such also are the heavenly. Therefore, as we have carried the image of the earthly, let us carry also the image of the heavenly. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Now this I say, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God, nor shall corruption possess incorruption. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Behold, I tell you a mystery. We shall all indeed rise, but we shall not all be changed; in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall rise incorruptible, and we shall be changed. For it is necessary for this corruptible nature to put on incorruption, and this mortal nature to put on immortality. But when this mortal nature has put on immortality, then shall come to pass the word that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory. <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Where, O death, is your victory? <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> Where, O death, is your sting? <margin>1 Corinthians 15</margin> The sting of death is sin. And the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God, who has given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and unmovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord. Regarding the collections <note>original: "collectis"; the gathering of funds for the poor in Jerusalem.</note> that are made for the saints, as I have ordered the churches of Galatia, so also you should do on the first day of the week. <margin>1 Corinthians 16</margin> Let each one of you put aside by himself, storing up what shall please him, so that collections are not made when I come. And when I am present, whomever you shall approve by letters, these I will send to carry your grace to Jerusalem. And if it is worthy that I go also, they shall go with me. Finally, I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia. For I shall pass through Macedonia. But perhaps I will stay with you, or even winter there, so that you may lead me wherever I go. For I do not wish to see you now merely in passing. For I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord permits. But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost. For a great and evident door is opened to me, and there are many adversaries. Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear. For he works the work of the Lord, just as I do. Let no one despise him. But lead him forth in peace so that he may come to me. For I expect him with the brothers. Concerning our brother Apollos, I make it known to you that I urged him much to come to you with the brothers; and certainly it was not his will to come now. But he will come when he has the time. Watch, stand fast in the faith, act manfully and be strengthened; let all your things be done in charity. And I beseech you, brothers—you know the house of Stephanas and Fortunatus, who are the firstfruits of Achaia, and they have ordained themselves to the ministry of the saints—that you also be subject to such as these, and to everyone who cooperates and labors. I rejoice in the presence of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because they have supplied that which was lacking from you. For they have refreshed both my spirit and yours. Therefore, recognize those who are of this sort. The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, with their household church, with whom I am also a guest. All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. The greeting is by my own hand, Paul’s. If anyone does not love our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Our Lord comes! <note>original: "anathema maranatha"; Aramaic and Greek expressions used as a solemn warning and a prayer for the Lord's return.</note> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen. My charity is with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

### ARGUMENT
AFTER THE PENANCE, he writes a consoling letter to them from Corinth via Titus; and praising them, he exhorts them to better things, showing that though they were saddened, they were corrected.

## LIKEWISE THE SECOND [LETTER]
## OF THE APOSTLE
PAUL, AN APOSTLE
of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in all Achaia. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our tribulation, so that we also may be able to console those who are in any pressure through the exhortation by which we ourselves are exhorted by God; for as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ does our consolation abound. But whether we are troubled, it is for your exhortation and salvation; or whether we are consoled, it is for your consolation; or whether we are exhorted, it is for your exhortation and salvation, which works in the enduring of those same sufferings which we also suffer; so that our hope for you may be firm; knowing that as you are companions of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation.

For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of our suffering which happened in Asia, for we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond our strength, so that it wearied us even to live. But we had the response of death within ourselves, so that we should not be trusting in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead, who rescued us from such great dangers, and did deliver us; in whom we hope that he will yet rescue us, with you also helping <note>original: "adiuvantibus"; refers to the community supporting Paul through prayer.</note> in prayer for us, so that from many persons, thanks may be given by many on our behalf for the gift granted to us. For this is our glory, the testi- <column-break/> mony of our conscience, that in simplicity and the sincerity of God, and not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in this world, and more abundantly toward you. For we write no other things to you than what you have read and known. And I hope that you will know until the end, just as you have known us in part, that we are your glory, even as you are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ. And in this confidence, I wished to come to you before, so that you might have a second grace, and to pass through you into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you to be led forth into Judea. Therefore, when I wished this, did I use lightness? Or what I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, so that with me there is "yes" and "no"? But God is faithful, for our word which was with you is not "yes" and "no," but in him is "yes." For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me and Silvanus and Timothy—was not "yes" and "no," but in him was "yes." For however many promises of God there are, in him they are "yes." Therefore also through him is the "amen" to God for our glory. Now he who confirms us with you in Christ, and who has anointed us, is God, who also has sealed us, and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts. But I call God as a witness upon my soul, that to spare you I did not come again to Corinth; not because we lord it over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy; for by faith you stand. But I determined this within myself, that I would not come to you again in sadness; for if I make you sad, who is there to make me glad but the one who is made sad by me? And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come I might not have sadness upon sadness from those in whom I ought to rejoice, having confidence in all of you, that my joy is the joy of you all. For out of much tribulation and anguish of heart, I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made sad, but that you might know what more abundant charity I have for you. But if anyone has caused sadness, he has not saddened me, but in part, so that I do not burden you all. Sufficient for such a one is this rebuke which is given by many, so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and console him, lest perhaps such a one be swallowed up by more abundant sadness. Therefore I beseech you to confirm your charity toward him. For this reason also I wrote, that I might know your experience, whether you are obedient in all things. But to whom you have forgiven anything, I also. For what I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, I have done for your sakes in the person of Christ, so that we should not be circumvented by Satan. For we are not ignorant of his thoughts. Furthermore, when I had come to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door was opened to me in the Lord, I had no rest in my spirit because I did not find Titus my brother, but saying farewell to them, I went forth into Macedonia. But thanks be to God, who always triumphs over us in Christ Jesus, and manifests the odor of his knowledge through us in every place, because we are the good odor of Christ to God among those who are being saved, and among those who perish; to some indeed an odor of death unto death, to others an odor of life unto life. And who is so fit for these things? For we are not as many, adulterating the word of God, but out of sincerity—as from God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ. Do we begin again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some do, letters of commendation to you, or from you? You are our letter, written in our hearts, which is known and read by all men; being manifested that you are our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tables of stone but on the fleshly tables of the heart. And such confidence we have through Christ toward the Lord, not that we are sufficient to think anything of ourselves as if from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God, who also has made us fit ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life. But if the ministry of death, carved in stones, was in glory, so that the children of Israel could not look intently upon the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance which is being abolished, how shall the ministry of the Spirit not be more in glory? For if the ministry of condemnation is in glory, much more does the ministry of justice abound in glory. For even that which was clarified in this part was not glorified, because of the excellent glory. For if that which is abolished is through glory, much more that which remains is in glory. Having therefore such hope, we use great confidence, and not as Moses put a veil over his face, so that the children of Israel should not look intently upon his face, which is being abolished. But their senses were dulled. For even until this day, that same veil in the reading of the Old Testament remains unrevealed, because in Christ it is abolished. But even until this day, when Moses is read, a veil is placed over their hearts. But when he shall have turned to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit. And where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with revealed face, are transformed into the same image from brightness to brightness, as if by the Spirit of the Lord. Therefore, having this ministry, according as we have obtained mercy, we do not faint, but we renounce the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor adulterating the word of God, but in the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of men before God. But if our gospel is also hidden, it is hidden to those who perish, in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, so that the illumination of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine. For we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord, and ourselves your servants through Christ. For God, who said that light should shine out of darkness, has shined in our hearts, for the illumination of the knowledge of the brightness of God in the face of Christ Jesus. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels <note>term: "earthen vessels" (vasis fictilibus); a metaphor for the fragility and mortality of the human body containing the divine message.</note>, so that the excellence may be of the power of God, and not from us. In all things we suffer tribulation, but we are not distressed. We are perplexed, but not destitute. We suffer persecution, but we are not forsaken. We are cast down, but we do not perish; always carrying about in our body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our bodies. For we who live are always delivered unto death for Christ's sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh. So then death works in us, but life in you. But having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written: I believed, therefore have I spoken, we also believe, for which reason we also speak, knowing that he who raised up Jesus will also raise us up with Jesus, and will place us with you. For all things are for your sakes, so that the abundant grace through the thanksgiving of many may abound to the glory of God. For which reason we do not faint; but although our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. For that which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation, works in us beyond measure a sublimity of an eternal weight of glory, while we contemplate not the things which are seen, but the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal. For we know that if our earthly house of this habitation is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens. For in this also we groan, desiring to be clothed over with our habitation which is from heaven; if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked. For we who are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened, because we would not be unclothed but clothed over, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life. Now he who has fashioned us for this very thing is God, who has given us the pledge of the Spirit. Therefore, being always bold and knowing that while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord. For we walk by faith and not by sight. We are bold, I say, and have a good will rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Lord. And therefore we strive, whether absent or present, to please him. For we must all be manifested before the judgment seat of Christ, that every one may receive the proper things of the body, according as he has done, whether it be good or evil. Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are manifest to God. And I hope also that we are manifest in your consciences. We do not commend ourselves to you again, but we give you occasion to glory for...

<meta>This page continues the transition from the first letter to the Corinthians into a thematic commentary on the Second Letter to the Corinthians, specifically focusing on the qualities of a servant of God as described in Chapter 6.</meta>

**In all things let us exhibit ourselves as ministers <note>original: "ministros"; here meaning servants or attendants</note> of God in much patience, etc.**

In these words, four things are noted according to four types of people. First, he touches upon those who are in the **state of perfection**: *In all things let us exhibit ourselves as ministers of God.* Second, he touches upon those who are in the **state of tribulation** <note>a period of great suffering or distress</note>: *In much patience.* Third, he touches upon those who are in the **state of consolation**: *In chastity. In knowledge.* Fourth, he touches upon those who are in the **state of conduct** <note>original: "conversationis"; referring to one’s way of life and social dealings</note>: *In the word of truth. In the power of God.*

First, therefore, he addresses those who are in the **state of perfection**, who ought to exhibit themselves as ministers of God. In this, four things are noted: First, they ought to exhibit themselves as **ministers** of God. Second, as **friends** of God. Third, as **sons** of God. Fourth, as **heirs** of God.

Regarding the first, he says: *In all things let us exhibit ourselves as ministers of God.* In this, **humility** is noted, because a minister is one who serves another. Hence it is said in the Gospel: *He who is greater among you shall be your servant.* And again: *The Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve.*

Regarding the second, he says: *In much patience.* In this, **charity** <note>original: "caritas"; meaning selfless, divine love</note> is noted, because charity is patient. It is kind; it does not envy; it does not act wrongly; it is not puffed up; it is not ambitious; it does not seek its own; it is not provoked; it thinks no evil; it does not rejoice over iniquity, but rejoices in the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

Regarding the third, he says: *In chastity. In knowledge.* In this, **purity** is noted, because chastity is the cleanliness of body and soul. Hence it is said in the Book of Wisdom: *O how beautiful is the chaste generation with glory! For the memory of it is immortal, because it is known both with God and with men.*

Regarding the fourth, he says: *In the word of truth. In the power of God.* In this, **steadfastness** is noted, because truth is unchangeable, and the power of God is invincible. Hence it is said in the Psalm: *Your truth is from generation to generation.* And again: *The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation.*

<column-break/>

But note that these four things ought to be in **every Christian**. First, one ought to be a **minister** of God through obedience. Second, a **friend** of God through charity. Third, a **son** of God through adoption. Fourth, an **heir** of God through hope.

Regarding the first, he says: *In all things let us exhibit ourselves as ministers of God.* In this, **obedience** is noted, because a minister ought to obey his master. Hence it is said in the Gospel: *If anyone serves me, let him follow me.* And again: *Where I am, there also my minister shall be.*

Regarding the second, he says: *In much patience.* In this, **charity** is noted, because charity is patience. Hence it is said in the letter to the Corinthians: *Charity is patient, etc.* And again: *Greater love than this no man has, that a man lay down his life for his friends.*

Regarding the third, he says: *In chastity. In knowledge.* In this, **adoption** is noted, because the sons of God ought to be chaste and knowledgeable. Hence it is said in the letter to the Romans: *The Spirit himself gives testimony to our spirit that we are the sons of God. And if sons, then heirs; heirs indeed of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.*

Regarding the fourth, he says: *In the word of truth. In the power of God.* In this, **hope** is noted, because hope does not disappoint. Hence it is said in the Psalm: *In you, O Lord, I have hoped, let me not be confounded forever.* And again: *Hope in the Lord and do good; and dwell in the land, and you shall be fed with its riches.*

Likewise, note that these four things ought to be in **every preacher**. First, he ought to be a **minister** of God through humility. Second, a **friend** of God through charity. Third, a **son** of God through purity. Fourth, an **heir** of God through steadfastness.

Regarding the first, he says: *In all things let us exhibit ourselves as ministers of God.* In this, **humility** is noted, because a preacher ought to be humble. Hence it is said in the Gospel: *He who humbles himself shall be exalted.* And again: *Learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart.*

Regarding the second, he says: *In much patience.* In this, **charity** is noted, because a preacher ought to have charity toward his neighbor. Hence it is said in the letter to the Corinthians: *The charity of Christ urges us.* And again: *If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not charity, I am become as sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal.*

Regarding the third, he says: *In chastity. In knowledge.* In this, **purity** is noted, because a preacher ought to be chaste and knowledgeable. Hence it is said in the book of Leviticus: *Be holy, because I, the Lord your God, am holy.* And again: *The lips of the priest keep knowledge, and they seek the law from his mouth.*

Regarding the fourth, he says: *In the word of truth. In the power of God.* In this, **steadfastness** is noted, because a preacher ought to be firm in faith and in work. Hence it is said in the letter to the Corinthians: *Watch, stand fast in the faith, act manfully, and be strengthened.* And again: *Be firm and immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.*

For it is written that Abraham had two sons, the one by a slave-woman <note>original: "ancilla"; referring to Hagar</note>, and the other by a free-woman. But he who was of the slave-woman was born according to the flesh; but he of the free-woman was by promise. Which things are said through an allegory. For these are the two testaments <note>or covenants</note>; the one indeed from Mount Sinai, which brings forth children unto bondage, which is Hagar. For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, which corresponds to the Jerusalem that now is, and is in bondage with her children. But that Jerusalem which is above is free, which is our mother. For it is written: *Rejoice, you barren woman who does not bear; break forth and cry, you who do not travail; for the desolate has many more children than she who has a husband.* Now we, brothers, like Isaac, are the children of promise. But as then he who was born according to the flesh persecuted him who was born according to the spirit, so it is now also. But what says the scripture? *Cast out the slave-woman and her son; for the son of the slave-woman shall not be heir with the son of the free-woman.* Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave-woman, but of the free-woman: by which freedom Christ has made us free.

Stand fast therefore, and do not be held again under the yoke of bondage. Behold, I, Paul, say to you, that if you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing. And I testify again to every man who circumcises himself, that he is a debtor to perform the entire law. You are made void of Christ, you who are justified by the law: you are fallen from grace. For we through the Spirit wait for the hope of justice by faith. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision: but faith, which works by love. You were running well; who hindered you, that you should not obey the truth? This persuasion is not from him who calls you. A little leaven corrupts the whole lump. I have confidence in you in the Lord, that you will be of no other mind: but he who troubles you shall bear his judgment, whoever he may be.

But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why do I still suffer persecution? Then the scandal of the cross is made void. I wish that they who trouble you would even cut themselves off. For you, brothers, have been called unto liberty: only do not use liberty as an occasion for the flesh, but by charity serve one another. For all the law is fulfilled in one word: *You shall love your neighbor as yourself.* But if you bite and devour one another,

deeds: in distresses, for Christ Jesus' sake. Because when I am weak, then I am strong: I have become a fool; you have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For I am in no way inferior to those who are "super-apostles" <note>original: "supra modum apostoli"; Paul's sarcastic term for false teachers claiming higher authority</note>, even though I am nothing. Truly the signs of my apostleship were performed among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds. For what is there in which you were inferior to the other churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong.

For the children ought not to lay up treasures for the parents, but the parents for the children. Again, do you think that we excuse ourselves to you? We speak before God in Christ. But all things, dearly beloved, are for your edification. For I fear lest, perhaps, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found by you such as you would not: lest perhaps there be contentions, envies, wraths, dissensions, detractions, whisperings, swellings, seditions among you. Lest, when I come again, God will humble me among you, and that I shall bewail many who have sinned already, and have not practiced penance for the uncleanness, and fornication, and lasciviousness which they have committed.

Behold, this is the third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established. I told you before, and foretell as if I were present, and now being absent, to those who have sinned already, and to all others: that if I come again, I will not spare. Since you seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, who toward you is not weak, but is mighty in you. For although he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you. Examine yourselves, whether you be in the faith; prove your own selves. Do you not know your own selves, how that Christ Jesus is in you? Unless perhaps you are castaways. But I hope that you shall know that we are not castaways. Now we pray to God that you do no evil, not that we should appear approved, but that you should do that which is good, though we be as castaways. For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth. For we rejoice when we are weak, and you are strong: and this also we pray for, even your perfection. Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord has given me for edification and not for destruction.

Finally, brothers, rejoice, be perfect, take comfort, be of one mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace shall be with you. Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all. Amen.

**Here ends the second epistle to the Corinthians.**

## THE EPISTLE TO THE GALATIANS BEGINS.

# PAUL THE APOSTLE
not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead: and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia. Grace be to you and peace from God the Father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. I marvel that you are so soon turning away from him who called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: which is not another, but there are some who trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than that which we have preached to you, let him be accursed <note>original: "anathema"; a formal curse or excommunication</note>. As we said before, so say I now again: if any man preach any other gospel to you than that you have received, let him be accursed. For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.

But I certify to you, brothers, that the gospel which was preached by me is not according to man: for I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ. For you have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews' religion <note>original: "iudaismo"; Judaism</note>, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it, and profited in the Jews' religion above many of my equals in my own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers. But when it pleased him who separated me from my mother's womb, and called me by his grace, to reveal his Son in me, that I might preach him among the Gentiles; immediately I conferred not with flesh and blood, neither went I to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me: but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus. Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and stayed with him fifteen days. But of the other apostles I saw none, except James the Lord's brother. Now the things which I write to you, behold, before God, I lie not. Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia. And I was unknown by face unto the churches of Judea which were in Christ. But they had heard only, "He who persecuted us in times past now preaches the faith which once he destroyed": and they glorified God in me. Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles: but privately to those who seemed to be of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain. But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised: but that was because of false brothers unawares brought in, who came in privately to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: to whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you. But of those who seemed to be somewhat, whatsoever they were, it makes no matter to me, God accepts no man's person. For those who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me. But on the contrary, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to me, as the gospel of the circumcision was to Peter: (for he who worked in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles): and when James, Cephas <note>the Aramaic name for Peter</note>, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given to me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship: that we should go unto the Gentiles, and they unto the circumcision: only they would that we should remember the poor, the same which I also was forward to do.

But when Cephas was come to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he was to be blamed. For before certain men came from James, he ate with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him, so...

I tell you beforehand, as I have told you before, that those who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the spirit is charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, mildness, and continence. Against such things there is no law. And those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh with its vices and lusts. If we live by the spirit, let us also walk by the spirit. Let us not become desirous of empty glory, provoking one another, envying one another. Brothers, even if a person is overtaken in some fault, you who are spiritual should instruct such a person in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted.

Bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ. For if anyone thinks himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself. But let everyone prove his own work, and so he shall have glory in himself alone, and not in another. For everyone shall bear his own burden. And let him who is instructed in the word communicate to him who instructs him in all good things. Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. For whatever a man sows, those things he shall also reap. For he who sows in his flesh, from the flesh he shall also reap corruption; but he who sows in the spirit, from the spirit he shall reap eternal life. And in doing good, let us not fail; for in due time we shall reap, if we do not fail. Therefore, while we have time, let us work good to all, but especially to those who are of the household of faith. See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand. Whoever wishes to please in the flesh, they compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not suffer the persecution of the cross of Christ. For not even those who are circumcised keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may glory in your flesh. But God forbid that I should glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision counts for anything, nor the lack of it, but a new creature. And whoever follows this rule, peace be upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. For the rest, let no one be troublesome to me; for I bear the marks <note>original: "stigmata," referring to the physical scars of Paul's suffering</note> of the Lord Jesus in my body. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen. **Here ends the epistle to the Galatians.**

### PREFACE
The Ephesians are people of Asia. Having received the word of truth, they persisted in the faith. The Apostle praises them, writing to them from Rome while in prison, by way of Tychicus the deacon.

## HERE BEGINS THE EPISTLE TO THE EPHESIANS

**PAUL, AN APOSTLE**
of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus and to the faithful in Christ Jesus. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens in Christ, just as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and immaculate in his sight in charity. He predestined us to the adoption of sons through Jesus Christ in himself, according to the purpose of his will, to the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he has made us pleasing in his beloved Son. In him we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins according to the riches of his grace, which has superabounded in us in all wisdom and prudence; so that he might make known to us the mystery <note>original: "sacramentum," often translated in the early church as "mystery" or "sacred secret"</note> of his will according to his good pleasure, which he proposed in him, in the dispensation of the fullness of times, to restore all things in Christ—those which are in the heavens and those which are on the earth, in him. In him also we were called by lot, being predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will, so that we might be to the praise of his glory—we who first hoped in Christ. In him you also, when you had heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, in which also believing you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance, unto the redemption of acquisition, unto the praise of his glory.

Therefore I also, hearing of your faith which is in the Lord Jesus, and your love toward all the saints, do not cease giving thanks for you, making a memory of you in my prayers, so that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the spirit of wisdom and of revelation in the knowledge of him; that the eyes of your heart being enlightened, you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what are the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, and what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the operation of the might of his power, which he worked in Christ, raising him from the dead and setting him at his right hand in the heavens, above all principality and power, and virtue, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the future one. And he has subjected all things under his feet, and has given him as head over the entire church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all. And you, when you were dead in your offenses and sins, in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of this air, the spirit who now works in the sons of distrust, in which we all also once lived in the desires of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of our thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, just as the others.

But God, who is rich in mercy, because of his great charity with which he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, brought us to life together in Christ—by whose grace you are saved—and raised us up together, and made us sit together in the heavens in Christ Jesus, so that he might show in the coming ages the abundant riches of his grace in his goodness toward us in Christ Jesus. For by grace you are saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves; for it is the gift of God. Not of works, so that no one may glory. For we are his workmanship <note>original: "factura," implying something crafted or created</note>, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared so that we should walk in them.

For which reason, be mindful that you were once Gentiles in the flesh, who are called the "uncircumcision" by that which is called the "circumcision" made by hands in the flesh; because you were at that time without Christ, alienated from the community of Israel, and strangers to the testaments, having no hope of the promise, and without God in this world. But now in Christ Jesus, you who were once far off have been made near in the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who made both one, and breaking down the middle wall of the partition, the enmities in his flesh, making void the law of commandments in decrees, so that he might create in himself the two into one new man, making peace, and might reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, killing the enmities in himself. And coming, he preached peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near, because through him we both have access in one spirit to the Father. Therefore now you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are citizens of the saints,

<column-break/>

and members of God's household, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ himself being the chief cornerstone, in whom the whole building, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord, in whom you also are built together into a dwelling place for God in the spirit.

For this reason, I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles—if indeed you have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which was given to me toward you, because according to revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote above briefly, as you can understand by reading my insight into the mystery of Christ, which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the spirit: that the Gentiles are co-heirs and members of the same body and co-partners of his promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel, of which I was made a minister according to the gift of the grace of God, which was given to me according to the operation of his power. To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ, and to enlighten all as to what is the dispensation of the mystery hidden for ages in God who created all things, so that the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and powers in the heavens through the church, according to the eternal purpose which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord, in whom we have boldness and access with confidence through faith in him.

Therefore I ask that you do not fail in my tribulations for you, which is your glory. For this reason, I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom all fatherhood in heaven and on earth is named, that he may give you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell through faith in your hearts; being rooted and founded in charity, so that you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth, and length, and height, and depth; to know also the charity of Christ which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled unto all the fullness of God. Now to him who is able to do all things more abundantly than we ask or understand, according to the power that works in us, to him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus, unto all generations, world without end. Amen.

I, therefore, a prisoner in the Lord, beseech you that you walk worthily of the vocation by which you were called, with all humility and mildness, with patience supporting one another in charity, careful to keep the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace. One body and one spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism. One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in us all.

But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ. Therefore it says: "Ascending on high, he led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men." Now, that he "ascended," what is it but that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth? He who descended is the same who also ascended above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things. And he gave some to be apostles, and some prophets, and others evangelists, and others pastors and teachers, for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the building up of the body of Christ, until we all meet in the unity of faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ; so that we may no longer be children tossed to and fro, and carried about by every wind of doctrine in the wickedness of men, in craftiness toward the circumvention of error. But performing the truth in charity, let us grow in him through all things, who is the head, Christ, from whom the whole body, being compacted and connected through every joint of sub-ministration, according to the operation in the measure of every member, makes increase of the body unto the building up of itself in charity.

This, therefore, I say and testify in the Lord: that you no longer walk as the Gentiles walk in the vanity of their senses, having their understanding obscured in darkness, alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their hearts; who, despairing, have given themselves up to indecency, for the operation of all impurity in avarice. But you have not so learned Christ, if indeed you have heard him and were taught in him, as the truth is in Jesus: to put off, according to your former conversation, the old man who is corrupted according to the desires of error. And be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who according to God is created in justice and holiness of truth. Therefore, putting away lying, let each one speak the truth with his neighbor, since we are members of one another. Be angry, and do not sin. Let not the sun go down upon your anger. Do not give a place to the devil. Let him who stole, steal no longer; but rather let him labor, working with his hands what is good, so that he may have something to give to the one suffering need. Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth, but only what is good for the building up of opportunity, that it may give grace to the hearers. And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

Let all bitterness, and anger, and indignation, and clamor, and blasphemy be taken away from you, with all malice. And be kind to one another, merciful, forgiving one another, even as God in Christ has forgiven you. Be therefore imitators of God, as most dear children, and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and delivered himself up for us as an oblation and a victim to God for an odor of sweetness. But fornication, and all impurity, or avarice, let it not even be named among you, as becomes saints; or filthiness, or foolish talking, or scurrility, which are not to the purpose, but rather thanksgiving. For know and understand this: that no fornicator, or impure person, or avaricious person (which is the service of idols), has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

Let no one deceive you with empty words; for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of distrust. Do not, therefore, become partakers with them. For you were once darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk as children of light—for the fruit of the light is in all goodness, and justice, and truth—proving what is well-pleasing to God. And do not communicate with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather even reprove them. For the things that are done by them in secret, it is a shame even to speak of. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light. For everything that is made manifest is light. Therefore it says: "Rise, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall enlighten you."

See therefore, brothers, how cautiously you walk: not as unwise, but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not become imprudent, but understand what the will of God is. And do not be drunk with wine, in which there is luxury, but be filled with the Holy Spirit, speaking to yourselves in psalms, and hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord; giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God and the Father; being subject to one another in the fear of Christ. Let women be subject to their husbands as to the Lord, because the husband is the head of the woman, just as Christ is the head of the church, he being the savior of the body. But as the church is subject to Christ, so also let women be to their husbands in all things. Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and delivered himself up for her, so that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water in the word of life, that he might present the church to himself in glory, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing, but that she should be holy and immaculate. So also ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife, loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh...

[End of the] Epistle to the Ephesians. And so, all parts being fulfilled, 
that you may stand in the evil day and remain perfect in all things. Stand, therefore, having 
your loins girded with truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, 
and your feet shod in the preparation of the gospel of peace; in all things 
taking up the shield of faith, with which you may be able to extinguish all the 
fiery darts of the most wicked one. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit, which is 
the word of God. Through all prayer and supplication, praying at all 
times in the spirit: and watching in it with all instance and supplication 
for all the saints: and for me, that speech may be given to me in the opening of 
my mouth with confidence, to make known the mystery of the gospel: for which 
I act as an ambassador in chains <note>original: "cathena"</note>: so that in it I may dare to speak as I ought. 
But so that you also may know the things concerning me, and what I am doing, Tychicus, the beloved brother 
and faithful minister in the Lord, will make everything 
known to you. I have sent him to you for this very purpose: that you may know the things concerning us, 
and that he may comfort your hearts. Peace be to the brothers, and charity with faith from God 
the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace be with all who love 
our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen.

### THE PHILIPPIANS ARE MACEDONIANS. PREFACE.
The Philippians are Macedonians. Having received the word of truth, they stood fast 
in the faith. Nor did they receive false apostles. The apostle praises 
them, writing to them from Rome from prison via Epaphroditus.

## HERE BEGINS THE EPISTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS
Paulus and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ: to all the saints in Christ 
Jesus who are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons. Grace to you and peace 
from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I give thanks to my God in 
every memory of you, always in all my prayers making supplication 
for all of you with joy, because of your fellowship 
in the gospel from the first day until now. Being confident of this very thing: that he 
who began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Christ Jesus. As 
it is right for me to feel this for all of you, because I have you in 
my heart, and in my chains, and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel: 
that you are all sharers of my joy. For God is my witness, how 
I long for you all in the bowels <note>A common biblical expression for deep, heartfelt affection.</note> of Jesus Christ. And this I pray: that your charity 
may abound more and more in knowledge and in all understanding: that you may 
approve the better things: that you may be sincere and without offense until the day of Christ; filled 
with the fruit of righteousness through Jesus Christ unto the glory and praise of God.

Now I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me have come more to the 
advancement of the gospel, so that my chains became manifest in 
Christ in the whole praetorium <note>The headquarters of the Roman imperial guard.</note> and in all other places; and many of the brothers 
in the Lord, being confident in my chains, dare more abundantly to 
speak the word of God without fear. Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and contention, 
but some also out of good will. Some out of charity, 
knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel. 
But some announce Christ out of contention, not sincerely, 
thinking that they raise up affliction for my chains. What then? So long as in 
every way, whether by pretext or by truth, Christ is announced: 
and in this I rejoice, and will continue to rejoice. For I know that this will result 
for me unto salvation through your prayer and the supply of the spirit of Jesus 
Christ, according to my expectation and hope: that in nothing shall I be confounded. 
But in all confidence, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in 
my body, whether by life or by death. For to me, to live is Christ, 
and to die is gain. But if to live in the flesh is the fruit of labor, 
then what I shall choose, I do not know. For I am constrained between the two: having a desire 
to be dissolved and to be with Christ, which is much better. But to remain in the 
flesh is necessary for your sake. And being confident of this, I know that I shall remain 
and continue for all of you, for your advancement and joy of faith: that 
your rejoicing may abound in Christ Jesus in me, through my coming 
to you again. Only let your conduct be worthy of the gospel of Christ: so that 
whether I come and see you, or being absent hear of you, that you stand 
firm in one spirit, with one mind struggling together for the righteousness of faith, and in nothing be terrified 
by the adversaries: which is to them a cause of perdition, but to you of salvation.

<column-break/>

And this is from God: because it is given to you for Christ’s sake, not only to 
believe in him, but also to suffer for him: having the same struggle 
as you have seen in me, and now have heard of me. If there be therefore any consolation 
in Christ, if any comfort of charity, if any society of the spirit, if any 
bowels of mercy: fulfill my joy, that you may be of the same mind, 
having the same charity, being of one accord, feeling the same thing. Do nothing through 
contention, nor through empty glory. But in humility, let each 
esteem others better than themselves, not considering each one’s own interests, but 
those of others. For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus. Who, 
being in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal 
to God: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness 
of men, and found in habit as a man. He humbled himself, 
becoming obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Because of which 
God also has exalted him, and has given him a name which is above every name. 
That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and in 
hell: and that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the 
glory of God the Father. Therefore, my dearly beloved, as you have always obeyed, 
not as in my presence only, but much more now in my absence: 
work out your salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God who 
works in you both to will and to accomplish, according to his good will. And 
do all things without murmurings and hesitations: that you may be without blame 
and simple children of God, without reproach in the midst of a crooked and 
perverse nation. Among whom you shine like lights in the world, 
holding forth the word of life to my glory in the day of Christ: because I have not run in vain, 
nor labored in vain. But even if I am sacrificed upon the sacrifice and service 
of your faith, I rejoice and congratulate you all. And for the same 
reason, you also rejoice and congratulate me. But I hope in the Lord Jesus to 
send Timothy to you shortly, so that I also may be of good heart, knowing the things concerning 
you. For I have no one so like-minded who is sincerely 
solicitous for you with such affection. For all seek their own interests, not the things 
of Jesus Christ. But know the proof of him, that as a son to a father, 
so he has served with me in the gospel. Him, therefore, I hope to send to you, 
as soon as I see how things go with me. And I trust in the Lord that 
I myself shall also come to you shortly. But I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, 
my brother and co-worker and fellow-soldier, but your apostle <note>In this context, "apostle" means "messenger" or "envoy" sent by the Philippian church.</note> 
and the minister to my needs. For indeed he longed after you all, 
and was sad, because you had heard that he was sick. 
For indeed he was sick unto death, but God had mercy on him. And 
not only on him, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow. 
Therefore I sent him the more speedily, so that seeing him again you may rejoice, and I 
may be without sorrow. Receive him therefore with all joy in the Lord, and 
hold such as he is in honor. Because for the work of Christ he 
came close to death, delivering up his life, to fulfill that which was lacking on 
your part toward my service.

Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is 
indeed not tedious to me, but it is necessary for you. Beware of dogs, beware of evil 
workers, beware of the concision <note>A derogatory term for those who insisted on physical circumcision; literally "the mutilation."</note>. For we are the circumcision, who by the 
spirit serve God, and glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh; 
though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinks 
to have confidence in the flesh, I more so. Circumcised the eighth day, of the race of Israel, 
of the tribe of Benjamin. A Hebrew of Hebrews, according to the law a Pharisee; 
according to zeal, persecuting the church of God; according to the righteousness which 
is in the law, living without blame. But the things that were gain to me, these 
I have counted as loss for Christ. Furthermore, I count all things 
to be loss for the sake of the eminent knowledge of Jesus Christ my Lord: 
for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them as dung, that I may 
gain Christ, and be found in him, not having my own righteousness which is of the law, 
but that which is of the faith of Christ Jesus, the righteousness which is from God in 
faith; to know him and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship 
of his sufferings, being made conformable to his death: if by any means I may attain to the 
resurrection which is from the dead. Not as though I had already attained, or were 
already perfect. But I follow after, if by any means I may comprehend, in which 
I am also apprehended by Christ Jesus. Brothers, I do not count myself to have apprehended. 
But one thing: forgetting those things which are behind, and 
stretching myself forth to those things which are before, I pursue toward the mark, for the prize of the high calling 
of God in Christ Jesus. Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, feel this way. 
And if in anything you feel otherwise, this also God will reveal to you. Nevertheless, 
to that which we have attained, let us be of the same mind, and let us remain in the same rule. 
Be followers of me, brothers, and observe those who walk 
according to the pattern you have in us. For many walk, of whom I have often told you, 
and now tell you even weeping, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ: whose end is destruction, 
whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who 
mind earthly things. But our conversation <note>original: "conversatio," meaning citizenship or way of life.</note> is in heaven. From whence also we look for 
the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ, who will reform the body of 
our humility, made conformable to the body of his glory, according to the 
operation by which he is able even to subject all things to himself. Therefore, my brothers, 
dearly beloved and most longed for, my joy and my crown: so stand 
fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved. I beg Evodia and I beseech Syntyche, to be of the same mind in the Lord. 
And I ask you also, my sincere companion, help those women who have 
labored with me in the gospel with Clement and the rest of my fellow-workers, 
whose names are in the book of life. Rejoice in the Lord always; again 
I say, rejoice. Let your modesty be known to all men: the Lord is near. 
Be solicitous about nothing: but in every prayer and supplication with 
thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God. And the peace of God, 
which surpasses all understanding, keep your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus. 
Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever 
honest, whatever just, whatever holy, whatever lovely, 
whatever of good fame: if there be any virtue, if any praise of discipline: think 
on these things. The things which you have both learned and received and heard and seen in me, 
these do: and the God of peace shall be with you.

But I rejoiced in the Lord exceedingly, that now at last 
your care for me has flourished again, as you also were careful. But you were busy; 
I do not say this as if because of want. For I have learned in whatever state I am, to be 
sufficient. I know both how to be humbled, and I know how to abound; everywhere and in all things 
I am instructed: both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. 
I can do all things in him who strengthens me. Nevertheless, you have done well, sharing 
in my tribulation. And you also know, Philippians, that in the 
beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church 
communicated with me in the matter of giving and receiving, but you only. For even to 
Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my use. Not because I seek the gift, but 
I seek the fruit abounding to your account. But I have all things and 
abound. I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things which you sent, an 
odor of sweetness, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God. And may my God fulfill 
every desire of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ 
Jesus. Now to God and our Father be glory forever and ever. Amen. 
Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me salute you. 
All the saints salute you: especially those who are of Caesar’s household. 
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

### THE THESSALONIANS ARE MACEDONIANS. PREFACE.
The Thessalonians are Macedonians in Christ Jesus. Who, having received the word 
of truth, stood fast in the faith, even in the persecution of their fellow citizens. 
Moreover, they did not receive false apostles, nor those things which were said by false 
apostles. The apostle praises them, writing to them from Athens via Tychicus 
and Onesimus.

## HERE BEGINS THE FIRST EPISTLE TO THE THESSALONIANS.
Paulus and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father 
and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace. We give thanks to God always 
for all of you: making memory of you in our prayers 
without ceasing: mindful of the work of your faith and labor and charity 
and the enduring of the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ before God and our Father. 
Knowing, brothers beloved of God, your election: because our gospel 
was to you not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit.

<meta>This page continues the First Epistle to the Thessalonians, provides the complete Second Epistle to the Thessalonians, and begins the Epistle to the Colossians.
