Therefore, brothers, we were comforted in you in all our necessity and tribulation through your faith: because now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord. For what thanksgiving can we return to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God: praying more abundantly night and day that we may see your face and may complete those things which are lacking in your faith? Now may God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you. And may the Lord multiply you and make your charity abound toward one another and toward all, just as we also do toward you: to confirm your hearts without blame in holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints. Amen.

For the rest then, brothers, we ask you and beseech you in the Lord Jesus: that as you have received from us how you ought to walk and please God, so also you may walk that you may abound more. For you know what precepts we have given to you through the Lord Jesus. For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you should abstain from fornication; that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel <note>The "vessel" likely refers to one's own body or perhaps a spouse.</note> in sanctification and honor; and not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles who do not know God. And let no one overstep or circumvent his brother in business: because the Lord is the avenger of all these things, as we have also told you before and testified. For God has not called us to uncleanness, but to sanctification. Therefore, he who despises these things does not despise man, but God, who has also given his Holy Spirit in us. But concerning the charity of brotherhood, we have no need to write to you: for you yourselves have learned from God to love one another. For indeed you do that toward all the brothers in all of Macedonia. But we ask you, brothers, that you abound more, and that you strive to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; and that you may walk honestly toward those who are outside, and that you may desire nothing of anyone.

But we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who are sleeping <note>original: "dormientibus" — a common early Christian metaphor for the deceased</note>, so that you do not grieve like others who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with him those who have slept through Jesus. For this we say to you in the word of the Lord: that we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, shall not precede those who have slept. For the Lord himself, at a command and at the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God, shall descend from heaven; and the dead who are in Christ shall rise first. Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ in the air: and so we shall always be with the Lord. Therefore, comfort one another with these words.

But concerning the times and moments, brothers, you do not need us to write to you. For you yourselves know accurately that the day of the Lord shall come like a thief in the night. For when they shall say, "peace and security," then sudden destruction shall come upon them, like labor pains upon a woman with child, and they shall not escape. But you, brothers, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you like a thief. For you are all children of light and children of the day. We are not of the night nor of darkness. Therefore, let us not sleep like the others, but let us watch and be sober. For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who are drunk, are drunk at night. But let us, who are of the day, be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and charity, and for a helmet the hope of salvation. For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to the acquisition of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us: so that whether we watch or sleep, we may live together with him. Therefore, comfort one another and edify one another, just as you are doing.

And we ask you, brothers, to know those who labor among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you: that you hold them more abundantly in charity because of their work; have peace with them. And we ask you, brothers,

<column-break/>

admonish the restless, comfort the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all. See that no one renders evil for evil to anyone; but always follow that which is good toward one another and toward all. Always rejoice. Pray without ceasing. In all things give thanks. For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus in all of you. Do not extinguish the Spirit. Do not despise prophecies. But prove all things: hold fast that which is good. Abstain yourselves from every evil appearance. And may the Lord of peace himself sanctify you through all things: so that your whole spirit and soul and body may be preserved without blame at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. He who has called you is faithful, and he will also do it. Brothers, pray for us. Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. I adjure you by the Lord that this epistle be read to all the holy brothers. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

### HE WRITES THE SECOND [EPISTLE] TO THE THESSALONIANS

> The Thessalonians receive a second epistle concerning the last times and concerning the detraction <note>Referring to the deceptive claims of the adversary.</note> of the adversary. Paul and Onesimus write this epistle from Athens, and he exhorts them to perseverance in their practices.

### LIKEWISE TO THE THESSALONIANS

# PAUL AND SILVANUS

AND TIMOTHY TO THE CHURCH OF THE THESSALONIANS IN GOD OUR FATHER AND THE LORD JESUS CHRIST. GRACE TO YOU AND PEACE FROM GOD OUR FATHER AND THE LORD JESUS CHRIST.

We ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith is growing greatly, and the charity of every one of you toward each other abounds. So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God, for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations which you sustain as an example of the just judgment of God: that you may be held worthy in the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer. Seeing it is a just thing with God to repay tribulation to those who trouble you; and to you who are troubled, rest with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of his power, in a flame of fire giving vengeance to those who do not know God, and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. They shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he shall come to be glorified in his saints and to be made wonderful in all who have believed, because our testimony was believed by you in that day. In which also we pray always for you: that our God would deign you worthy of his calling and fulfill every desire of goodness and the work of faith in power in that day: so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

But we ask you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together unto him: that you be not easily moved from your sense nor terrified, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by epistle as if sent by us, as though the day of the Lord were near. Let no one deceive you in any way. For unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and is lifted up above all that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God. Do you not remember that when I was still with you, I told you these things? And now you know what withholds him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of iniquity is already at work: only let him who now holds, hold until he be taken out of the way. And then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming: him whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power and signs and lying wonders, and in all seduction of iniquity for those who perish: because they did not receive the love of the truth that they might be saved. Therefore God shall send them the operation of error, so that they believe a lie: that all may be judged who have not believed the truth but have consented to iniquity.

But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers beloved by God: because God has chosen us as firstfruits unto salvation in the sanctification of the Spirit and in the faith of the truth: into which he also called us through our gospel to the acquisition of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, brothers, stand fast and hold the traditions which you have learned, whether by word or by our epistle. Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who has loved us and given us eternal consolation and good hope in grace: exhort your hearts and confirm you in every good work and word.

For the rest, brothers, pray for us: that the word of God may run and be glorified, just as it is among you; and that we may be delivered from troublesome and evil men. For faith is not of all. But the Lord is faithful, who will confirm you and guard you from evil. And we have confidence concerning you in the Lord, that the things which we command, you both do and will do. And may the Lord direct your hearts in the charity of God and the patience of Christ. Now we denounce to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother walking inordinately <note>Walking "inordinately" refers to living in a disorderly way or not according to established rules.</note> and not according to the tradition which they received from us. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us: because we were not restless among you, nor did we eat any man's bread for free: but in labor and fatigue, working night and day, so that we might not be a burden to any of you. Not as though we had not the power, but that we might give ourselves as a pattern to you to imitate us. For also when we were with you, this we denounced to you: that if any man will not work, neither let him eat.

For we have heard that some among you walk restlessly, working at nothing but acting curiously. Now we denounce those who are such, and beseech them in the Lord Jesus Christ, that working with silence they eat their own bread. But you, brothers, do not fail in doing well. And if anyone does not obey our word through this epistle, note that man, and do not keep company with him, so that he may be ashamed. And do not count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother. Now may the Lord of peace himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with you all. The salutation of Paul with my own hand: which is the sign in every epistle; so I write. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

### THE COLOSSIANS ARE ASIANS LIKE THE LAODICEANS

> The Colossians are also Asians, just like the Laodiceans; and they had been reached first by false apostles. The apostle himself did not go to them, but he corrects them through an epistle. For they had heard the word from Archippus <note>original: "archi dilippo" — likely a scribal variant or error for Archippus, a companion of Paul mentioned in Colossians 4:17.</note> who had also received a ministry among them. Therefore the apostle, being already bound, writes to them from Ephesus through Tychicus the deacon.

### VII THE EPISTLE TO THE COLOSSIANS BEGINS

# PAUL THE APOSTLE

OF JESUS CHRIST BY THE WILL OF GOD, AND TIMOTHY THE BROTHER, TO THE HOLY AND FAITHFUL BROTHERS IN CHRIST JESUS WHO ARE AT COLOSSAE. GRACE TO YOU AND PEACE FROM GOD OUR FATHER.

We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you: hearing of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love which you have toward all the saints because of the hope which is laid up for you in heaven: which you heard before in the word of the truth of the gospel which has reached

For it is just in the sight of God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you; and to you who are troubled, to grant rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with the angels of his power, in a flame of fire, taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. They shall suffer the punishment of eternal destruction, away from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power, when he comes to be glorified among his saints and to be marveled at among all who have believed—because our testimony among you was believed—on that day. Toward this end, we also pray always for you: that our God may count you worthy of his calling and fulfill every desire for goodness and every work of faith in his power, so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

But we beseech you, brothers, regarding the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, that you not be quickly shaken in your mind or terrified—whether by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter allegedly sent by us—as though the day of the Lord were already at hand. Therefore, God will send them a working of error so that they believe a lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in iniquity may be judged. But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers beloved by God, because God chose you as the firstfruits for salvation through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth, to which he also called you through our gospel to obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, brothers, stand firm and hold to the traditions which you have learned, whether by our word or by our letter. Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal consolation and good hope through grace, comfort your hearts and confirm you in every good work and word.

Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of God may spread quickly and be glorified, just as it is among you, and that we may be delivered from troublesome and evil men; for not all have faith. But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one. We have confidence in you in the Lord, that you are doing and will continue to do the things we command. May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and the patience of Christ. Now we charge you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition they received from us. For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us; for we were not idle among you, nor did we eat anyone’s bread for free, but we worked in labor and toil night and day so as not to be a burden to any of you. This was not because we did not have the right, but to give ourselves as a model for you to imitate. For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is not willing to work, neither let him eat. For we hear that some among you walk in a disorderly way, doing no work at all, but acting as busybodies. To such persons we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ that they work in silence and eat their own bread. But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good. If anyone does not obey our word in this letter, take note of that person and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed; yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother. Now may the Lord of peace himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with you all. This greeting is by my own hand, Paul’s, which is the sign in every letter; this is how I write. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

## HERE BEGINS THE FIRST EPISTLE TO TIMOTHY.

<image-desc>Large illuminated initial 'P' containing a figure of St. Paul holding a sword and a book, set against a blue and gold background with foliate patterns.</image-desc>

**P**AUL, AN APOSTLE
of Christ Jesus according to the command of God our Savior, and of Christ Jesus our hope: to Timothy, my beloved son in the faith. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. As I asked you to remain at Ephesus when I went into Macedonia, so that you might charge certain people not to teach otherwise, nor to occupy themselves with myths and endless genealogies, which promote speculations rather than the divine training <note>original: *edificationem*; literally 'edification' or 'building up'</note> that is in faith. The goal of this command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith. Some, having strayed from these, have turned aside into vain talk, wanting to be teachers of the law but understanding neither what they say nor the things about which they make confident assertions. But we know that the law is good, if one uses it lawfully, knowing this: that the law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the impious and sinners, for the wicked and profane, for those who kill their fathers and mothers, for murderers, fornicators, those who practice homosexuality <note>original: *masculorum concubitoribus*; literally 'those who lie with males'</note>, kidnappers <note>original: *plagiariis*; referring to those who steal or sell human beings</note>, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine, which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which was entrusted to me. I thank him who strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he counted me faithful, appointing me to the ministry—I who was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an insolent man. But I obtained the mercy of God because I acted ignorantly in unbelief. And the grace of our Lord superabounded with the faith and love that is in Christ Jesus. This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptance: that Christ Jesus came into this world to save sinners, of whom I am the first. But for this reason I obtained mercy, so that in me first Christ Jesus might demonstrate all patience as a pattern <note>original: *deformationem*; here meaning an 'outline' or 'example'</note> for those who would believe in him for eternal life. Now to the King of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

This charge I commit to you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies previously made concerning you, that by them you may wage a good warfare, holding faith and a good conscience, which some, having rejected, have suffered shipwreck regarding the faith. Among these are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have delivered to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme. I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men: for kings and all who are in high positions, so that we may lead a quiet and tranquil life in all piety and purity. For this is good and acceptable before our Savior God, who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all, a testimony in its own time. For this I was appointed a preacher and an apostle (I am telling the truth and not lying), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth. I desire therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands without anger or contention. Similarly, women should adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefastness and sobriety, not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly attire, but with what is proper for women professing godliness through good works. Let a woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to have authority over a man, but to be in silence. For Adam was formed first, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived; but the woman, being deceived, was in the transgression. Yet she will be saved through the bearing of children, if they continue in faith, love, and sanctification with sobriety.

This is a faithful saying: If anyone desires the office of a bishop <note>original: *episcopatum*; the role of an overseer or church leader</note>, he desires a good work. It behooves a bishop, therefore, to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, of good behavior, chaste, hospitable, a teacher, not given to wine, not a striker <note>meaning not violent or prone to brawling</note> but modest, not quarrelsome, not greedy, but ruling his own house well, having his children in subjection with all purity. For if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the church of God? He should not be a neophyte <note>a new convert</note>, lest being puffed up with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil. Moreover, he must have a good testimony from those who are outside, so that he does not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. Deacons likewise must be chaste, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not seeking dishonest gain, holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be tested; and so let them minister, if they are found without crime. Women likewise should be chaste, not slanderers, sober, and faithful in all things. Let deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. For those who have ministered well will acquire for themselves a good standing and much confidence in the faith which is in Christ Jesus. I write these things to you, hoping to come to you quickly.

<meta>This page concludes the First Epistle to Timothy, covering instructions on the care of widows, the duties of elders (presbyters), and warnings against greed. It then transitions into the Second Epistle to Timothy, which is traditionally understood as Paul’s final letter, written from prison in Rome shortly before his death.</meta>

Beyond this life, he is slow to love himself, and yet very quick to the struggle <note>original: *agone*; referring to the spiritual contest or martyrdom</note>; or rather, where there is true confession and where he demonstrates firm truth. And so here he also commands that truth be commended by a certain manifestation, so that those who see it may know him, since he appears. He says: I charge you in the sight of God, who gives life to all things <note>original: *uiuificat ōia*</note>. This is an assumption, because here also he appears, and in the life to come he gives life to all things: showing indeed that those who suffer martyrdom and are victors do not die, but live in the Lord and in Christ Jesus, who gave testimony under Pontius Pilate, a good confession. And this again prepares one for martyrdom, so that they do not prefer life over death, and thus become victors. And they have that which they recognize for the sake of the gain of certain others, you have made a beginning: and they have what they wish to recognize. Because every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving. For it is sanctified by the word of God and by prayer. Setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and of good doctrine, which you have followed. But avoid foolish and old wives' fables; exercise yourself toward piety. For bodily exercise is useful for a little, but piety is useful for all things, having the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. A faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptance. For in this we labor and are reviled, because we hope in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, especially of those who believe.

Command these things and teach them. Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the faithful in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in chastity. Until I come, attend to reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine. Do not neglect the grace that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the priesthood <note>original: *psbiterii*; the body of elders or presbyters</note>. Meditate upon these things; be occupied in them, so that your progress may be manifest to all, both in your calling and in your doctrine. Persist in them; for in doing this, you will save both yourself and those who hear you. Do not rebuke an elder <note>original: *seniorem*</note>, but entreat him as a father; young men as brothers; old women as mothers; young women as sisters, in all chastity. Honor widows who are truly widows. But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let her learn first to govern her own house and to repay her parents; for this is acceptable before the Lord. But she who is truly a widow and desolate, let her hope in the Lord and persist in supplications and prayers night and day. For she who lives in delicacies is dead while she lives. And command this, that they may be irreproachable. But if anyone does not have care for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel. Let a widow be chosen not less than sixty years old, who has been the wife of one husband, having a testimony of good works: if she has raised children, if she has received strangers, if she has washed the feet of the saints <note>original: *scōrū*</note>, if she has ministered to those suffering tribulation, if she has followed every good work. But avoid the younger widows. For when they have grown wanton in Christ, they want to marry, having damnation because they have made void their first faith. At the same time, being idle, they learn to go about from house to house; not only idle, but also talkative and curious, speaking things which they ought not. I will, therefore, that the younger women marry, bear children, be mothers of families, and give no occasion to the adversary for the sake of evil speaking. For already some have turned back after Satan. If any faithful man has widows, let him minister to them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may suffice for those who are truly widows. Let the priests <note>original: *psbiteri*; the elders or leaders</note> who rule well be held worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in word and doctrine. For the Scripture says: You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the corn, and: The laborer is worthy of his reward. Against a priest, do not receive an accusation except under two or three witnesses. Rebuke those who sin in the presence of all, so that the others also may have fear. I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels, that you keep these things without prejudice, doing nothing by declining to one side or the other. Do not lay hands quickly on any man, nor communicate in the sins of others. Keep yourself chaste. Do not drink only water any longer, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent infirmities. The sins of some men are manifest, preceding them to judgment; but some they follow after. Likewise, good deeds are manifest, and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden. Whoever are servants under the yoke, let them count their masters worthy of all honor, lest the name of the Lord and his doctrine be blasphemed. But those who have faithful masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers, but rather serve them the more because they are faithful and beloved, partakers of the benefit. Teach and exhort these things. If anyone teaches otherwise and does not acquiesce to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to that doctrine which is according to piety, he knows nothing, but is sick concerning questions and strifes of words, from which arise envies, contentions, blasphemies, evil suspicions, and conflicts of men corrupted in mind, and who are deprived of the truth, thinking that piety is a source of gain. But piety with sufficiency is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. Having food and wherewith to be covered, let us be content with these. For those who want to become rich fall into temptation and the snare of the devil, and into many useless and hurtful desires, which drown men in destruction and perdition. For greed <note>original: *cupiditas*; the love of money</note> is the root of all evils, which some desiring have erred from the faith and entangled themselves in many sorrows. But you, O man of God, flee these things. Follow after justice, piety, faith, charity, patience, and mildness. Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life, to which you are called, and have confessed a good confession before many witnesses. I charge you before God, who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who gave testimony under Pontius Pilate, a good confession, that you keep the commandment without spot, irreproachable, until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, which he will show in his own time, who is the blessed and only powerful King of kings and Lord of lords. Who alone has immortality and inhabits inaccessible light, whom no man has seen nor can see; to whom be honor and everlasting empire. Amen.

Command the rich of this world not to be high-minded, nor to hope in the uncertainty of riches, but in the living God, who provides us all things abundantly to enjoy. To do good, to be rich in good works, to give easily, to communicate, to lay up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may lay hold on true life. O Timothy, guard the deposit, avoiding profane novelties of words and oppositions of knowledge falsely so named, which some promising have fallen away concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

## ALSO TO TIMOTHY

# PAUL THE APOSTLE

of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus, to Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my ancestors with a pure conscience, that without ceasing I have a memory of you in my prayers night and day, desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy; calling to mind that faith which is in you unfeigned, which also dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice, and I am certain that it is in you also. For which cause I admonish you that you stir up the grace of God which is in you by the imposition of my hands. For the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of sobriety. Be not, therefore, ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but labor with the gospel according to the power of God, who has delivered us and called us with his holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the times of the world. But it is now made manifest by the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has indeed destroyed death and illuminated life and incorruption through the gospel, in which I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles. For which cause I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is powerful to keep my deposit until that day. Hold the form of sound words which you have heard from me in faith and love in Christ Jesus. Guard the good deposit through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. You know this, that all who are in Asia are turned away from me, of whom are Phigelus and Hermogenes. May the Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain. But when he had come to Rome, he sought me out diligently and found me. May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And how many things he ministered to me at Ephesus, you know better than I.

You therefore, my son, be comforted in the grace which is in Christ Jesus. And the things which you have heard from me through many witnesses, commend these to faithful men who shall be fit to teach others also. Labor as a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No man warring for God entangles himself with secular businesses, so that he may please him to whom he has proved himself. For he also who strives in a contest <note>original: *agone*</note> is not crowned unless he has striven lawfully. The laboring husbandman must first partake of the fruits. Understand what I say; for the Lord will give you understanding in all things. Be mindful that the Lord Jesus Christ has risen again from the dead, of the seed of David, according to my gospel, in which I labor even unto chains, as an evil-doer; but the word of God is not bound. Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus, with heavenly glory. A faithful saying: for if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him; if we suffer, we shall also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us; if we do not believe, he remains faithful—he cannot deny himself. Admonish them of these things, testifying before the Lord. Contend not in words, for it is useful for nothing but the subversion of the hearers. Carefully study to present yourself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth. But avoid profane and vain babblings, for they grow much toward impiety, and their speech spreads like a cancer. Of whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus, who have fallen from the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past, and have subverted the faith of some.

But the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: The Lord knows who are his, and let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity. But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some indeed unto honor, but some unto contumely. If any man, therefore, shall cleanse himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honor, sanctified and useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work. Flee also youthful desires; follow justice, faith, charity, and peace with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart. But avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing that they beget strifes. But the servant of the Lord must not wrangle, but be mild toward all men, apt to teach, patient, with modesty admonishing those who resist the truth, if peradventure God may give them repentance to know the truth, and they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will. But know this, that in the last days dangerous times shall come. Men shall be lovers of themselves, covetous, haughty, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked, without affection, without peace, slanderers, incontinent, unmerciful, without kindness, traitors, stubborn, puffed up, and lovers of pleasures more than of God; having indeed an appearance of piety, but denying the power thereof. Avoid these. For of these are they who creep into houses and lead captive silly women laden with sins, who are led away with various desires: always learning, and never attaining to the knowledge of the truth. Now as Jannes and Mambres <note>Jannes and Jambres; the traditional names of the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses</note> resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth, men corrupted in mind, reprobate concerning the faith. But they shall proceed no further; for their folly shall be manifest to all, as theirs also was.

But you have followed my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, patience, persecutions, and afflictions, such as came upon me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra; what persecutions I endured, and out of them all the Lord delivered me. And all who will live piously in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. But evil men and seducers shall grow worse and worse, erring and driving into error. But continue in those things which you have learned and which have been committed to you, knowing of whom you have learned them; and because from your infancy you have known the holy scriptures, which can instruct you unto salvation through the faith which is in Christ Jesus. All scripture, inspired of God, is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in justice, so that the man of God may be perfect, furnished unto every good work. I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who shall judge the living and the dead, and by his coming and his kingdom: preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, entreat, rebuke in all patience and doctrine. For there shall be a time when they will not endure sound doctrine but, according to their own desires, they will heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears, and will indeed turn away their hearing from the truth, but will be turned unto fables. But watch in all things, labor, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. For I am even now ready to be sacrificed <note>original: *delibor*; literally poured out as a drink offering</note>, and the time of my dissolution is at hand. I have fought the good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith. As for the rest, there is laid up for me a crown of justice, which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day; and not only to me, but to them also who love his coming. Make haste to come to me quickly. For Demas has left me, loving this world, and is gone to Thessalonica; Crescens into Galatia, Titus into Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for the ministry. But Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus. The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when you come, bring with you, and the books, especially the parchments. Alexander the metalworker <note>original: *aerarius*; a coppersmith or worker in bronze</note> has done me much evil; the Lord will reward him according to his works: whom you also avoid, for he has greatly resisted our words. At my first defense no man stood with me, but all left me: may it not be imputed to them. But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching may be fulfilled, and all the Gentiles may hear; and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion. The Lord has delivered me from every evil work and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. Erastus remained at Corinth. And Trophimus I left sick at Miletus. Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers salute you. The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

It further details Christ's role as both High Priest and sacrificial victim, contrasting His perfect sacrifice with Old Testament rites.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from a general theological discussion on the Incarnation into the primary scriptural accounts of Christ’s arrival and the nature of Christian life. It moves from the narrative of the Gospel of Luke into a compilation of significant excerpts from the Epistles, concluding with the apocryphal Letter to the Laodiceans.</meta>

Since many have attempted to set in order a narrative of the events that have been fulfilled among us: just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word: it seemed good to me also, having followed all things diligently from the start, to write them down for you in an orderly way, most excellent Theophilus <note>original: "Theophile." The name means "Lover of God." It is unclear if this refers to a specific person or any devout reader.</note>: so that you may know the truth of those words in which you have been instructed.

In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the priestly division of Abijah: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth. Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. But they had no son because Elizabeth was barren: and both were advanced in their years. Now it happened that while he was performing his priestly service in the order of his division before God: according to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him by lot to enter the temple of the Lord to burn incense. And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense. Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him. But the angel said to him: "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard: and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John. And you will have joy and exultation: and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord: and he shall drink no wine or strong drink <term>strong drink: originally 'sicera,' referring to fermented beverages other than wine, such as cider or beer</term>: and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb. And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. And he himself will go before Him in the spirit and power of Elijah: to turn the hearts of the fathers toward the children and the unbelieving to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a perfect people."

And Zechariah said to the angel: "How shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is advanced in her years." And answering, the angel said to him: "I am Gabriel, who stands before God: and I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news. And behold, you will be silent and unable to speak until the day these things take place: because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their own time." And the people were waiting for Zechariah: and they wondered why he delayed so long in the temple. But when he came out, he could not speak to them: and they realized he had seen a vision in the temple. And he kept gesturing to them and remained mute. And it happened that when the days of his service were completed, he went to his house. After those days, Elizabeth his wife conceived: and she hid herself for five months, saying: "Because the Lord has done this for me in the days when He looked upon me to take away my reproach among men."

In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city of Galilee named Nazareth: to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David: and the virgin’s name was Mary. And entering to her, the angel said: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you: blessed are you among women." But when she heard this, she was troubled by his word: and she pondered what kind of greeting this might be. And the angel said to her: "Do not be afraid, Mary: for you have found grace with God. Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son: and you shall call his name Jesus. He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High: and the Lord God will give to him the throne of David his father: and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever: and of his kingdom there will be no end." But Mary said to the angel: "How shall this be, since I do not know a man?" And answering, the angel said to her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you: and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. And therefore that holy one which shall be born will be called the Son of God. And behold, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren: because no word shall be impossible with God." And Mary said: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord: let it be done to me according to your word." And the angel departed from her.

<column-break/>

Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Tribulation? Or distress? Or persecution? Or hunger? Or nakedness? Or danger? Or the sword? As it is written: "Because for your sake we are put to death all day long: we are counted as sheep for the slaughter." But in all these things we are more than conquerors because of Him who loved us. For I am certain that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor power, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

For just as we have many members in one body: and all the members do not have the same function: so we, being many, are one body in Christ: and individually members of one another. Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, according to the measure of faith: or ministry, in serving: or he who teaches, in doctrine: he who exhorts, in exhortation: he who gives, in simplicity: he who leads, with diligence: he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness. Let love be without pretense. Hating what is evil: clinging to what is good. Loving one another with brotherly affection: outdoing one another in honor. Not lagging in diligence: fervent in spirit: serving the Lord. Rejoicing in hope: patient in tribulation: constant in prayer. Sharing in the needs of the saints: pursuing hospitality. Bless those who persecute you: bless and do not curse. Rejoice with those who rejoice: weep with those who weep. Being of the same mind toward one another. Not setting your mind on high things, but consenting to the humble.

In many and various ways God spoke of old to the fathers through the prophets: most recently in these days He has spoken to us in His Son: whom He appointed heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages. Who, being the brightness of His glory and the image of His substance, and upholding all things by the word of His power, having made purification for sins, sits at the right hand of the Majesty on high. Having become so much better than the angels, as He has inherited a more excellent name than they. For to which of the angels did He ever say: "You are my Son, today I have begotten you"? And again: "I will be to Him a father, and He shall be to me a son"? And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says: "And let all the angels of God adore Him." And of the angels He says: "Who makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flame of fire." But to the Son: "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever: a scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom. You have loved justice and hated iniquity: therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions." And: "You, Lord, in the beginning founded the earth: and the heavens are the works of your hands. They shall perish, but you shall remain: and they all shall grow old like a garment. And like a cloak you will change them, and they shall be changed: but you are the same, and your years shall not fail." To which of the angels did He ever say: "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"? Are they not all ministering spirits, sent for ministry for the sake of those who shall inherit salvation?

### THE EPISTLE TO THE LAODICEANS <note>This is a non-canonical or "apocryphal" letter. Though widely circulated in medieval Latin Bibles, it was not ultimately accepted into the official New Testament canon.</note>

# PAUL THE APOSTLE

<margin>Prayers for them to the Lord</margin>

Paul, an apostle, not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, to the brothers who are at Laodicea: grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ. I give thanks to Christ in all my prayer, that you are remaining in Him and persevering in His works, expecting the promise on the day of judgment. Let the empty talk of certain people not unsettle you, who insinuate themselves to turn you away from the truth of the gospel which is preached by me. And now God will ensure that those who are from me serve toward the perfection of the truth of the gospel and perform the kindness of works which belong to the salvation of eternal life. And now my chains are public, which I suffer in Christ, in which I am glad and rejoice. And this is for my perpetual salvation, which was accomplished by your prayers and the administration of the Holy Spirit, whether through life or through death. For to me, to live is Christ and to die is joy. And He Himself will perform His mercy in you, that you may have the same love and be of one mind. Therefore, most beloved, as you have heard of the presence of the Lord, so hold fast and act in the fear of God, and there will be life for you forever. For it is God who works in you. And do whatever you do without hesitation. And what is best, most beloved, rejoice in the Lord Jesus Christ and beware of all filth in every gain. Let all your petitions be made public before God, and be firm in the mind of Christ. And whatever things are pure and true and modest and just and lovely, do these things. And what you have heard and received, keep in your heart, and peace shall be with you. Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen. Have this read to the Colossians, and that of the Colossians to you. The End.

->**THE CONFESSION OF VICES AND VIRTUES**<-

I WAS PROCEEDING IN THE LAWS <note>Original: "iurum." This likely refers to the outward observance of religious or legal rules.</note>, AND I DEEMED MYSELF HUMBLE AND CHASTE, BUT I WAS NOT FOR THAT REASON INNOCENT, SINCE I AM PUBLICLY <unclear>OFFENDED</unclear> BY MY OWN FAULTS; AND I HAVE SINNED, AND I HAVE SET THE INIQUITY OF ALL EVILS AGAINST MY OWN MERITS, JUST AS THE HOLY SCRIPTURE HAS TAUGHT ME. <note>The author is admitting that their outward "good behavior" was a mask for internal sin.</note> <unclear>FOR</unclear> WHILE FEARING GUILT, MY INIQUITY ABHORRED CHASTITY. I DID NOT OPPOSE THEM, NOR DID I KEEP THE CONTINENCE OF MY LIPS. I HAVE SINNED THROUGH **VAINGLORY** <note>original: "cenodoxia" — a Latinization of the Greek 'kenodoxia,' meaning empty pride or vanity.</note>, IN THE PRESUMPTION OF INIQUITIES, IN PERTINACITY <note>Meaning stubbornness or persistent wickedness.</note>, IN BOASTFULNESS, IN ARROGANCE, IN DISOBEDIENCE, IN TALKATIVENESS, AND IN HYPOCRISY; TO WHICH I DID NOT OPPOSE **COUNSEL**, **FEAR OF THE LORD**, **UNDERSTANDING**, **FORESIGHT**, **MEMORY**, **DOCILITY**, OR **SAGACITY**. I HAVE SINNED IN EXULTATION DURING ADVERSITY AND IN UNHAPPINESS DURING PROSPERITY; IN BITTERNESS, IN WHISPERING <note>Meaning gossip or backbiting.</note>, IN DETRACTION, IN HATRED, AND IN MALICE; TO WHICH I DID NOT RIGHTLY OPPOSE **CONSTANCY**, **TOLERANCE**, **MILDNESS**, **LOVE**, **GOODNESS**, OR **GENEROSITY**. I HAVE SINNED IN DECEIT, IN USURY, IN FRAUD, IN ROBBERY, IN PERJURY, IN VIOLENCE, AND IN THE **LOVE OF MONEY** <note>original: "philargiria" — from the Greek 'philargyria,' the root of "the love of money is the root of all evil."</note>; TO WHICH I DID NOT OPPOSE **COUNSEL**, **PATIENCE**, **SUFFICIENCY**, **CONTEMPLATION**, **REMORSE**, **MODESTY**, OR **FRUGALITY**. I HAVE SINNED IN PROSTITUTION, IN LUXURIES, IN SHAMEFULNESS, IN LASCIVIOUSNESS, IN PETULANCE, IN HESITATION, AND IN EVERY KIND OF FORNICATION <unclear>KIND</unclear>; [TO THESE] THEY DID NOT OPPOSE **TEMPERANCE**, **CHASTITY**, **PATIENCE**, <unclear>AND HUMILITY</unclear>.

<column-break/>

AND **GENTLENESS**. AND BEHOLD, I HAVE LISTENED [TO TEMPTATION] WITHOUT CAUSE, AND I HAVE SINNED IN STRIFE, IN CLAMOR, IN FURY, IN MOURNING, IN PERVERSITY, AND IN BLASPHEMY; TO WHICH I DID NOT OPPOSE **LAW**, **JUSTICE**, **TRUTH**, AND **RECTITUDE** IN TAKING OATHS, NOR DID I OBSERVE THE VISION OF **SEVERITY** OR **SPARINGNESS**. I HAVE SINNED IN IMPOSTURE AND IN DISCORD, IN INSULT, IN SLOTH, IN SECTARIANISM, AND IN ABANDONMENT; NOR DID I OPPOSE THESE WITH BENEVOLENCE, NOR DID I OPPOSE WRATH WITH CONCORD, NOR WITH ALACRITY, NOR WAS I MILD; BUT IN ALL THESE DREADFUL PRESCRIBED VICES, I HAVE LIVED AS IF IN DELIGHTS ALL THE DAYS [OF MY LIFE].

### Page 288.

->**THE CONFESSION OF THE PENITENT**<-

I THEREFORE CONFESS MY FAULTS <note>original: "inde confiteor meas culpas"</note> CONCERNING ALL THE SINS WHICH I HAVE COMMITTED SINCE I WAS BORN AND RECEIVED BAPTISM UNTIL THIS VERY HOUR. I CONFESS TO GOD AND TO YOU, PRIEST, WHETHER I HAVE REMEMBERED THEM OR NOT REMEMBERED THEM; WHETHER I SINNED KNOWINGLY OR UNKNOWINGLY; WHETHER WHILE AWAKE OR WHILE SLEEPING. FOR ALL MY SINS, I RECOGNIZE MYSELF AS A GUILTY SINNER. THEREFORE I CONFESS MY FAULTS TO ALMIGHTY GOD, AND TO HIS HOLY ANGELS, AND TO ALL HIS SAINTS, AND TO YOU, PRIEST; SO THAT I MAY ENTREAT YOU, BROTHER AND PRIEST, TO DEIGN TO PRAY FOR THE MERCY OF THE LORD FOR ME. FOR I AM A SINNER AND A FRAGILE MAN. INDEED, THERE IS NO SINNER UPON THE EARTH SUCH AS I, BECAUSE I DO NOT CEASE DAY AND NIGHT TO SIN IN WICKED THOUGHTS, IN IDLE WORDS, IN UNJUST DEEDS, IN THE WANDERING OF THE MIND, IN MANY IDLE PURSUITS, IN ANGER, IN **SLOTH** <note>original: "accidia" — a specific medieval term for spiritual apathy or a "sadness of the world" that prevents one from doing good.</note>, IN **VAINGLORY**, IN **PRIDE**, IN GREEDY DESIRES, IN FOOD AND DRINK, IN LUST, AND IN EVERY EVIL, IN IMPURITY OF THE MIND, IN FALSE ACCUSATIONS; AND BECAUSE MY CRIMES ARE MANY AND INNUMERABLE. AND I AM EXCEEDINGLY NEGLIGENT CONCERNING THE WORK OF GOD AND CONCERNING MY **ORDER** <note>original: "ordine meo" — this suggests the speaker is a member of the clergy or a monastic community with specific vows to keep.</note> WHICH I OUGHT TO HAVE GUARDED. I AM WORSE THAN ALL OTHERS; YET I AM BETTER IN MY TITLES THAN IN MY...

<column-break/>

...SINS, IN WHATEVER WAYS HUMAN FRAGILITY <note>The medieval understanding that humans are naturally weak and prone to error since the Fall of Adam.</note> CAN SIN AGAINST GOD AND THE CREATOR. IN ALL THESE THINGS I CONFESS THAT I AM GUILTY, AND I ACKNOWLEDGE MYSELF A SINNER. I BOTH BLUSH AND TREMBLE WHILE I BEHOLD MY SUFFERING STATE. THE **VIRTUES** ARE DESCRIBED TO WHICH I AM A STRANGER; THE **VICES** ARE THOSE WITH WHICH I AM FULL. WHAT MORE SHALL I SAY, EXCEPT THAT I REMEMBER MY LORD, AND THAT I AM NOT CONSUMED BECAUSE HIS MERCIES HAVE NOT FAILED? NOW, IN THE MULTITUDE OF YOUR MERCIES—AND BECAUSE IT IS SO—WHAT SHALL I SAY? I SHALL SAY: **WHY ARE YOU SAD, O MY SOUL, AND WHY DO YOU DISTURB ME? HOPE IN GOD, FOR I SHALL YET CONFESS TO HIM.** <note>A direct quotation from Psalm 42:5 (or 43:5 in modern numbering), used here to move from confession to hope.</note> THEREFORE I CONFESS TO YOU, LORD, HOLY FATHER, ALMIGHTY ETERNAL GOD, ALL MY SINS; FOR IT IS MY FAULT, FROM MY **ORIGIN** <note>original: "genesi" — likely referring to original sin or the state of being born into a sinful world.</note>, FROM MY INFANCY UNTIL THIS HOUR. WHATEVER I HAVE COMMITTED AGAINST THE PRECEPTS AND THE LAW OF GOD ALL THE DAYS OF MY LIFE, EITHER IN THOUGHT, IN DEED, OR IN REFLECTIONS UNTIL THE PRESENT DAY: AFTER MY SIN, YOU KNOW MY FRAGILITY. SPARE ME, AND FORGIVE, AND HAVE MERCY ON ME, BECAUSE AGAINST YOU ALONE HAVE I SINNED, AND MY SIN IS EVER BEFORE YOU. AND GRANT... TO ME, FOR I HAVE DONE INIQUITY. HELP ME, A SINNER, PIOUS GOD. I [CONFESS] THE FATHER AND THE SON AND THE HOLY SPIRIT, ONE GOD.

# Folio 289

->**The Purple Page**<-

<note>This page is a rare example of a "Codex Purpureus" (Purple Book). In the Middle Ages, dyeing <term>parchment</term> (animal skin) with expensive purple pigment was a way to signify the supreme importance of a text, often reserved for Gospels or royal prayer books. The text was usually written in gold or silver ink, which is prone to flaking or fading over a millennium.</note>

<meta>The text transitions from introductory matters to the start of the Chronicle of the Bohemians. The author, Cosmas of Prague, establishes his humility and his intent to record both the liberal arts and the history of his people.</meta>

# HERE BEGINS THE PREFACE TO PROVOST SEVERUS

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'D' in red and blue ink, featuring intricate knotwork and foliate patterns within the letter body.</image-desc>

To Lord Severus, Provost of the church of Mělník <note>original: "Milicensis"</note> and a praiseworthy scholar: Cosmas, though an unworthy priest and canon, sends greetings for desired health in Christ Jesus after the proper service of a devoted follower. Since you have urged me to write, and compelled me to undertake a difficult task that is not easily grasped by human senses, I truly confess that I wish to obey you, but my strength is not equal to it. For even if I possessed either the eloquence of Cicero <note>original: "Tullii facundia"</note> or the genius of Virgil <note>original: "Maronis ingenium"</note>, I would still hardly be sufficient for what you demand of me. Therefore, I ask you again and again that if you find anything in this work that is poorly said or inappropriately placed, you do not attribute it to me, but rather to your own persistence, which forced me to write this. Farewell, and remember me in your prayers.

# A LITTLE BOOK ON THE VARIOUS ARTS

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'Q' in red, blue, and green, containing a stylized dragon or hybrid creature forming the tail of the letter.</image-desc>

Since many authors, learned in all kinds of studies of wisdom, have written many excellent things about various arts and the different causes of things, I also—though the least of all and ignorant of all arts—have arranged to write something according to the measure of my own talent regarding those arts which they call "liberal" <note>The "Liberal Arts" were the foundation of medieval education, consisting of the Trivium (grammar, logic, rhetoric) and the Quadrivium (arithmetic, geometry, music, astronomy).</note>. I do this not so that I may seem to seek glory or praise for myself, but so that I may leave something for my successors concerning these things which I learned from my teachers. First, therefore, we must speak of grammar, which is the origin and foundation of all the arts. Grammar is the science of speaking correctly, and the origin and foundation of liberal letters. This is divided into eight parts, namely: the noun, pronoun, verb, adverb, participle, conjunction, preposition, and interjection. I will follow up on each of these as God grants me the ability.

# HERE BEGINS THE BOOK OF THE CHRONICLE OF THE BOHEMIANS BY COSMAS, DEAN OF PRAGUE

<image-desc>A very large, elongated decorative initial 'C' spanning the height of the lower heading, decorated with red and blue pigments and internal geometric patterns.</image-desc>

To all men who wish to be free from a malicious mind and to be built up in Christ Jesus: Cosmas, though an unworthy canon, sends greetings in the Lord. Since many before us have taken care to commit to writing various histories of events and the diverse occurrences of the times, I also—though the least and ignorant of all arts—have arranged to write something according to the measure of my talent concerning the deeds of the Bohemians and their origin.

<column-break/>

Thus begins the history of the Bohemians; and first, concerning the location of the land and the origin of the people. Bohemia, then, which is also called *Boiohemia* <note>Bohemia takes its name from the Boii, a Celtic tribe that inhabited the area in antiquity.</note>—named after the Boii who originally inhabited it—is a region situated in the middle of Germany, surrounded on all sides by mountains and forests. This land, as the authority of the ancients hands down, was first inhabited by giants who came into this land after the Flood and claimed it for themselves. After these, however, came the Boii, from whom it received its name. These Boii, since they were warlike men and vigorous in arms, subjugated many nations to themselves and expanded their borders. After them, however, came the Slavs, who inhabit it today. These Slavs, being peaceful men and devoted to agriculture, cultivated this land and dwelt in it.

<margin>Concerning the location of the land of Bohemia.</margin>
The land of Bohemia, as we have said, is surrounded on all sides by mountains and forests. In its center is a large and fertile plain, which is watered by many rivers and springs. Chief among these is the Elbe <note>original: "Albis"</note>, which rises in the Sudetes mountains and, flowing through the middle of Bohemia, goes out into the ocean. This land, as the authority of the ancients hands down, was first inhabited by giants who came into this land after the Flood and claimed it for themselves. After these, however, came the Boii, from whom it received its name. These Boii, since they were warlike men and vigorous in arms, subjugated many nations to themselves and expanded their borders. After them, however, came the Slavs, who inhabit it today. These Slavs, being peaceful men and devoted to agriculture, cultivated this land and dwelt in it.

<margin>Concerning the origin of the Slavic people.</margin>
The Slavs, as some believe, took their name from a certain "Sclavo," who was one of the sons of Japheth <note>In medieval genealogy, European peoples were often traced back to Japheth, one of the three sons of Noah.</note>. Others say they came from the region of Slavonia and took their name from there. But however it may be, this is certain: that the Slavs are an ancient people, spread through many parts of the world. These Slavs, being peaceful men and devoted to agriculture, cultivated this land and dwelt in it.

<margin>Concerning the first Duke of the Bohemians.</margin>
The first Duke of the Bohemians was a certain Čech <note>original: "Cechus"</note>, a noble man and vigorous in arms. He, coming from Slavonia with his brothers and his entire family, entered this land and claimed it for himself. This Čech, being a wise and just man, governed the people committed to him in peace and justice. After him, many other dukes succeeded, whose names and deeds will be set forth more fully in the following pages.

<meta>This page continues a systematic explanation of the Seven Sacraments, likely part of a late medieval theological manual or "Summa." The previous pages would have covered Baptism, Confirmation, and the Eucharist. This section focuses on Extreme Unction (Anointing of the Sick), Holy Orders, and Matrimony.</meta>

And if it is asked, what is the effect of this anointing? I respond first that it is the forgiveness of sins, if any remain in the soul after confession and the <term>Eucharist<note>The sacrament of Holy Communion.</note></term>. The second effect is that the soul may be strengthened against the temptations of the devil and against the fear of death, which usually attacks a person most severely at that time. The third is that, if it is beneficial for the salvation of the soul, the health of the body may be restored. And this is what is said in the Epistle of James: *And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up: and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him.* <note>original Latin: "Et oratio fidei salvabit infirmum, et alleviabit eum Dominus: et si in peccatis sit, remittentur ei."</note> From these things it is clear that this anointing ought not to be given except to the sick, and to those of whom it is feared that they are in danger of death. Therefore, it should not be given to children who do not yet have the use of reason, nor to the insane, unless they have <term>lucid intervals<note>Periods of temporary sanity or clarity.</note></term> in which they ask for it, or unless they had asked for it previously while they were healthy. Similarly, it should not be given to those condemned to death, because they are not in danger of death from sickness, but from the sentence of a judge. This anointing ought to be performed on those parts of the body in which the five senses flourish: namely, on the eyes, the ears, the nostrils, the mouth, the hands, and the feet. And for each sense, the anointing should be done with this form of words: *Through this holy anointing and His most tender mercy, may the Lord forgive you whatever sins you have committed by sight. Amen.* <note>original Latin: "Per istam sanctam unctionem, et suam piissimam misericordiam, indulgeat tibi Dominus quidquid per visum deliquisti. Amen."</note> And so on for the other senses, changing the name of the sense. This anointing must be performed by a priest, using oil blessed by a bishop. And if it is asked whether this anointing can be repeated? I respond that it can: in different illnesses, and even in the same illness if it lasts a long time and the sick person, after having recovered, falls back again into danger of death.

<column-break/>

I respond that <term>Order<note>The sacrament of Holy Orders, by which men are ordained as clergy.</note></term> is the sacrament through which spiritual power is handed over to the one being ordained. And it is called "Order" because through it some are placed above others in the Church according to certain ranks. There are seven orders, according to what is commonly said: namely, the doorkeeper, the reader, the exorcist, the acolyte, the subdeacon, the deacon, and the priest. Some, however, say that the office of bishop is an order, and thus there would be eight. But the more common opinion is that the bishopric is not an order, but a certain dignity above the priesthood. Now, some of these orders are called "sacred" or "major," such as the priesthood, the diaconate, and the subdiaconate. Others are called "non-sacred" or "minor," such as the other four. The <term>matter<note>The physical substance or outward sign used in a sacrament.</note></term> of this sacrament is that sensible object which is handed to the one being ordained as a sign of the power granted to him—just as the chalice with wine and the paten with the host are handed to a priest. To a deacon is handed the book of the Gospels. To a subdeacon, an empty chalice with a paten, and so on for the others. The <term>form<note>The specific words spoken to make the sacrament valid.</note></term>, however, is the prayer which the bishop says over the one being ordained. The minister of this sacrament is the bishop alone. The effect is an increase in grace, so that one may worthily minister in the office committed to him. And if it is asked whether a <term>character<note>A permanent spiritual "seal" or mark on the soul that signifies a change in status before God.</note></term> is imprinted in this sacrament? I respond that yes, it is in every order. Therefore, it ought not to be repeated.

Next, we must speak of Matrimony. Matrimony is the marital joining of a man and a woman, between legal persons, maintaining an inseparable way of life. This sacrament was instituted by the Lord before sin in Paradise, but after sin it was confirmed in the law of the Gospel. The "matter" of this sacrament is the consent of the parties expressed through <term>words of the present<note>Known as "verba de praesenti," these are vows that create an immediate marriage (e.g., "I take you"), as opposed to a promise to marry in the future.</note></term>. The "form" is the very words expressing consent, as when it is said: *I take you as mine*, and vice versa. The ministers of this sacrament are the contracting persons themselves. The effect is grace, through which the spouses may sustain the burdens of marriage and remain together in faith and love.

<summary>This page defines the theological requirements and spiritual effects of three sacraments: Extreme Unction for the dying, Holy Orders for the clergy, and Matrimony for the laity. It details the physical signs (matter), the necessary words (form), and the specific spiritual transformations intended for each.</summary>

## The Deeds of the Famous Hero

Finally, that most celebrated hero drew his sword in battle, but he made that victory as mournful and sad as any slaughter. That man—I say, that Christian soldier and warrior, that cultivator and lover of justice, that humble and pious leader and sinner—kept justice before his eyes, for he knew that the Lord had made him for his own justice, so that he might dispense justice among the people, not merely with words, but with all the strength of his deeds. And when the opposing armies recognized each other, as they were drawing themselves up in battle lines, he again sent messengers of peace to the people of the castle and the city of Wratislavia <note>Modern-day Wrocław</note>, announcing that he wished to grant the peace he had previously sought. But they, persevering in their malice and pride, rejected peace and chose war instead. Then this devoted soldier, seeing himself despised and knowing his cause was just, uttered this heroic voice, saying: "Let the judgment be of the righteous judgment of God."

Having spoken in this manner, as a leader familiar with his duty, he announced he would lead his army to aid his friends at Wratislavia. Passing by the places where damage had been promised, he moved by another route; he did this a second and third time so that, if possible, he might further avoid hatred. But when he gained nothing by this, he finally turned to vengeance. Then, by his command, they began to burn the countryside with fire, and only then did their tears flow. Then the poor, seeing this, lamented; and then finally the owners, who had compelled them to this by their pride, wished they could buy peace, but by then it was too late. Only then did they realize they deserved to lose their possessions for the sake of justice. 

There is a gap here in the narrative regarding the death of Mesico <note>Mieszko I Tanglefoot or Mieszko III the Old, depending on the specific lineage</note>, and I do not know where he is buried. Certainly, some say he was buried in Poznan, for little is known of some of these men. But since we know more about Mesico than others, it seems right that others should know what we know; if anyone wishes to know more, let them forgive us. As for the death of Mesico and his place of burial, since we do not know it, if anyone finds it, let it please them to write it down at this point.

And it is said: the generous justice of Mesico was of great worth, and his justice remains from age to age, and his justice is for eternity, and his justice remains forever and ever, because he instructed many in justice. As it is said, everything is for the sake of God's justice, with the greatest zeal for this. After Mesico, ten months later, Henry IV was born, and from then on their justice began to limp <note>original: "claudicare," meaning to falter or fail</note> little by little; therefore, his justice did not remain in them. From here, let the writer’s voice return to praising the justice of the righteous. Regarding what happened with these men, these things are briefly determined. They have spoken abundantly of good piety and the cause of justice, and it must be said that it should and can lead to blessing. And with certain modes of justice, as from no small law, and by his own pious and just judgment alone, all eleven princes came to him. They met in one counsel, speaking with one another of many other things and their friends, and he was always exceedingly mild. They made their journey with many services, and then they announced that they wished to return to peace and concord. And hastening more urgently toward this, singing thanks, they gave thanks to God with celebrations, and then they confirmed peace with one another. He offered to these same dukes the number of twelve thousand <note>likely silver marks or coins</note> for the justice and safety of the elders, but they did not receive this, and instead asked that there be offered to them a religious appearance of silver and gold. For these are the snares of desolation and shall perish like hay before the face of fire. Then they prepared great things, and then scarcely by analogy, since from them comes justice and justice, and then finally he was their castellan, and of this, enough is said.

After his death, in the Year of our Lord 1201, in the month of November, Casimir was elected king by King Wratislaus, with all the clergy and people favoring him. Then, with God's virtue having pacified the Emperor <note>Augustus</note>, just as with the Lombards—though they were not equals—he boldly managed his affairs. In the same year, after ten months, he fell asleep <note>died</note> in the palace. After this, there was a fire at the monastery of Saint Vincent in Wratislavia, where Walbert was then the first abbot. In the same year, King Wratislaus began to prevail over all their castellans; and then, as if he seemed more forgetful, they all acted on behalf of their faith for him, and an example is seen, and he prays. After they were expelled from the country, Henry brought his son Boleslaus, the king of the city of Olomouc and other cities. There, and after the time of the city's justice in just piety and death, he recognized it. And those three brothers—namely Jaromir and the two Conrads—were among them; then all were of one mind in the battle of justice, and the king wished to begin the journey. 

In the same year, the elected King Wratislaus sent messengers to the King of Poland, asking him to return the castles that his brother the king had invaded. After the sons of Conrad, after his death, were removed as a support to their father, he then led an army of enemies to expel them completely. <meta>This page continues the liturgical calendar for the month of March. Like the previous month, it combines a traditional church calendar of saints' feast days with a "necrology"—a list of names (mostly of Slavic origin) added in the margins and between lines to ensure they were remembered in daily prayers. The annotations from 1594 indicate the manuscript was still being used for scholarly or administrative reference in Prague during the Renaissance.</meta>
